name: analytical chemistry
definition: Scientific discipline that develops and applies strategies, instruments, and procedures to obtain information on the composition and nature of matter in space and time.

name: chemical analysis
definition: Application of analytical chemistry.

name: additive matrix effect
definition: Matrix effect that is independent of the measured quantity value of the measurand.

name: analytical run
definition: Set of measurements of the same quantity performed under repeatability conditions of measurement.

name: background indication
definition: Indication obtained from a phenomenon, body, or substance similar to the one under investigation but for which a quantity of interest is supposed not to be present or is not contributing to the indication.

name: blank correction
definition: Step in a measurement procedure in which the effect of a blank indication is removed from an indication.

name: blank indication
definition: Indication obtained from a sample of blank material under the measurement conditions for the measurand.

name: blank material
definition: Material which contains no, or as little as possible, of the analyte of interest used in measurement to establish a blank indication.

name: calibration certificate
definition: Document issued by a technically competent organization providing information about a calibration.

name: calibration interval
definition: Time period between calibrations over which the performance of the measuring system may be expected to meet specified requirements.

name: certified property value
definition: Property value of a reference material, accompanied by statements of associated uncertainty and traceability and identified as a certified property value in the reference material certificate.

name: chemical purity
definition: Mass (amount of substance or number of entities) of a specified component divided by the mass (amount of substance or number of entities, respectively) of the system.

name: consensus property value
definition: Property value derived from a collection of results.

name: conventional quantity value
definition: Quantity value attributed by agreement to a quantity for a given purpose.
synonyms: conventional value|conventional value of a quantity

name: critical value
definition: Measured quantity value for a quantity of a component in a material, above which the component is declared to be present.

name: determination
definition: Set of operations that are carried out on an object in order to provide qualitative or quantitative information about this object.

name: interferent
definition: Component of the matrix that embodies an influence quantity.

name: intermediate measurement precision
definition: Measurement precision under intermediate precision conditions of measurement.

name: laboratory bias
definition: Contribution to measurement bias that is attributed to systematic effects on measurement results made in a laboratory.

name: limit of quantification
definition: Smallest or largest measured quantity value, obtained by a given measurement procedure, which fulfils a requirement of fitness for purpose.

name: linearity of a measuring system
definition: Ability of a measuring system to provide measured quantity values that are directly proportional to the quantity value of the measurand.

name: linearity of calibration
definition: Closeness of agreement between indications obtained using calibrators in the first step of a calibration and indications predicted by the calibration function for the calibrators’ reference quantity values.

name: material homogeneity
definition: Uniform structure or composition of a material with respect to one or more specified properties.

name: material recovery
definition: Mass (volume, amount of substance) of a specified component isolated from a system divided by the mass (volume, amount of substance) of the system prior to isolation.

name: material stability
definition: Constancy of a property of a material over time.

name: measurement procedure
definition: Detailed description of a measurement according to one or more measurement principles and to a given measurement method, based on a measurement model and including any calculation to obtain a measurement result.

name: measurement procedure bias
definition: Contribution to measurement bias that is attributed to systematic effects on measurement results made according to a measurement procedure.

name: measurement procedure with standard addition
definition: Measurement procedure in which indications are obtained for an analytical sample as well as for analytical samples with addition(s) of a measurement standard.

name: measurement reproducibility
definition: Measurement precision under reproducibility conditions of measurement.

name: metrological compatibility of measurement results
definition: Property of a set of measurement results for a specified measurand, such that the absolute value of the difference of any pair of measured quantity values from two different measurement results is smaller than some chosen multiple of the standard measurement uncertainty of that difference.

name: metrological equivalence of measurement results
definition: Property of two or more measurement results for a given measurand which have metrological compatibility of measurement results, so that they are each acceptable for the same specified intended use.

name: minimum sample size
definition: Lower limit of sample size stipulated in documentation taken for chemical analysis.

name: multiplicative matrix effect
definition: Matrix effect that is proportional to the measured quantity value of the measurand.

name: non-certified property value
definition: Property value that is provided for information only but is not certified by a reference material producer.

name: object traceability
definition: Ability to trace the history, application, or location of an object.

name: property value assignment
definition: Determination of property values obtained in the course of the production of a reference material.

name: recovered quantity value ratio
definition: Measured quantity value relating a component to a system divided by a reference value.

name: repeatability condition of measurement
definition: Condition of measurement, out of a set of conditions that includes the same measurement procedure, same operators, same measuring system, same operating conditions, and same location, and replicate measurements on the same or similar objects over a short period of time.

name: run bias
definition: Contribution to measurement bias that is attributed to systematic effects on measurement results made in a single analytical run.

name: sample pre-treatment
definition: Collective noun for all procedures used for conditioning a sample to a defined state which allows subsequent chemical analysis or long-term storage (see material stability).

name: sampling
definition: Act of taking or constituting a sample.

name: sampling increment
definition: Individual portion of material collected by a single operation of a sampling device.

name: sampling target
definition: Portion of the material, at a particular time, that the sample is intended to represent.

name: shelf life
definition: Time interval during which a reference material producer warrants the material stability of the reference material.

name: spike
definition: Material with known quantity values added to an analytical sample.

name: systematic effect
definition: Recognized effect of an influence quantity on a measured quantity value.

name: testing
definition: Determination of one or more characteristics of an object of conformity assessment, according to a specified procedure.

name: unitary quantity
definition: Quantity with a magnitude expressed as a reference quantity multiplied by a number.

name: working interval
definition: Set of quantity values over which a measuring instrument or measuring system provides measurement results with acceptable measurement uncertainty under defined conditions.

name: acceptance interval
definition: Interval of permissible measured quantity values.

name: acceptance limit
definition: Specified upper or lower bound of permissible measured quantity values.

name: accreditation of a laboratory
definition: Third-party attestation related to a laboratory conveying formal demonstration of its competence to carry out specific conformity assessment tasks.

name: analytical selectivity
definition: Selectivity of a measuring system in analytical chemistry.

name: assessor
definition: Person, assigned by an accreditation body, with relevant professional expertise and experience who can determine the competence of a laboratory.

name: assigned value
definition: Value attributed to a particular property of an item and that serves as an agreed reference for comparison.

name: audit
definition: Systematic, independent, and documented process for obtaining objective evidence and evaluating it objectively to determine the extent to which the audit criteria are fulfilled.

name: candidate certified reference material
definition: Reference material subjected to a process of reference material certification.

name: candidate reference material
definition: Material subjected to the procedures necessary to show its fitness for intended use (see fitness for purpose).

name: capability
definition: Ability of an object to realize an output that will fulfil the requirements for that output.

name: cause-and-effect diagram
definition: Diagram indicating the causes of a specific event or condition.

name: certification
definition: Third-party attestation related to products, processes, systems, or persons.

name: commutability of a reference material
definition: Property of a reference material, demonstrated by the closeness of agreement between the relation among the measurement results for a stated quantity in this material, obtained according to two given measurement procedures, and the relation obtained among the measurement results for other specified materials.

name: competence
definition: Ability to apply knowledge and skills to achieve intended results.

name: conformance probability
definition: Probability that an item fulfils a specified requirement.

name: conformity assessment
definition: Activity to determine whether specified requirements relating to a product, process, system, person, or body are fulfilled.

name: control chart
definition: Chart with control limits on which some statistical measure related to a series of samples is plotted in a particular order to steer the process with respect to that measure.

name: control limit
definition: Value defining an intended level of stability for a process.

name: coordinator of an interlaboratory comparison
definition: Person(s) with responsibility for organizing and managing all of the activities involved in the operation of an interlaboratory comparison.

name: cumulative sum control chart
definition: Control chart where the cumulative sum of deviations of successive measured quantity values from a reference quantity value is plotted to detect shifts in the level of the measurand.

name: decision rule in conformity assessment
definition: Documented rule that describes how measurement uncertainty will be accounted for with regard to accepting or rejecting an item, given a specified requirement and a measured quantity value.

name: fitness for purpose
definition: Ability of a product, process, or service to serve a defined purpose under specific conditions.

name: good laboratory practice
definition: Quality system concerned with the organizational process, and conditions under which non-clinical health and environmental safety studies are planned, performed, monitored, recorded, archived, and reported.

name: good manufacturing practice
definition: Combination of manufacturing and quality procedures aimed at ensuring that products are consistently manufactured to their specified requirements and to avoid contamination of the product by internal or external sources.

name: guard band
definition: Interval between a tolerance limit and a corresponding acceptance limit. Figure 1: Guarded acceptance. Two-sided acceptance interval created by reducing the tolerance interval on either side by a guard band, thus reducing the probability of falsely accepting a non-conforming item.Figure 2: Guarded rejection. Two-sided acceptance interval created by increasing the tolerance interval on either side by a guard band, thus reducing the probability of falsely rejecting a conforming item.

name: Horwitz equation
definition: Empirical relationship providing a standard deviation under reproducibility conditions of measurement (\(s_{\rm{R,H}}\)) to be expected for typical measurements of the mass fraction (\(w\)) of a component in a material: \(s_{\rm{R,H}} = 0.02 w^{0.8495}\).
synonyms: Horwitz curve|Horwitz horn curve|Horwitz trumpet curve

name: Horwitz ratio
definition: Standard deviation of a mass fraction of a component under reproducibility conditions of measurement divided by the corresponding standard deviation calculated from the Horwitz equation. Figure 1: Horwitz curve (trumpet, horn). Expected relative standard deviation under reproducibility conditions of measurement, \(\pm s_{\rm{R,H}}/w\) plotted against logarithm of mass fraction, \(w\).

name: in-house reference material
definition: Reference material produced and used by an analytical laboratory.

name: inspection
definition: Examination of a product, process, service, or installation or their design and determination of conformity with specific requirements or on the basis of professional judgment, with general requirements.

name: interlaboratory comparison
definition: Organization, performance, and evaluation of measurements or tests on the same or similar items by two or more laboratories in accordance with predetermined conditions.

name: internal quality control
definition: Quality control within a specified laboratory.

name: intralaboratory comparison
definition: Organization, performance, and evaluation of measurements or tests on the same or similar items within the same laboratory in accordance with predetermined conditions.

name: laboratory information management system
definition: Information system which can provide services to one or more measuring systems.

name: material characterization study
definition: Intralaboratory comparison or interlaboratory comparison with the aim of assigning a reference quantity value to a quantity with stated measurement uncertainty or value to a reference nominal property value with stated examination uncertainty.

name: matrix reference material
definition: Reference material that is characteristic of a real sample.

name: measurement capability
definition: Ability to measure a quantity in a specified interval of quantity values, embodied in a specified material, as demonstrated by measurement uncertainty.

name: measurement precision control material
definition: Quality control material with or without reference quantity value used in quality control to assess measurement precision.

name: measurement trueness control material
definition: Quality control material with reference quantity value used in quality control to estimate a systematic measurement error.

name: method performance study
definition: Intra- or interlaboratory study of one or more performance characteristics of a measurement procedure.

name: organization
definition: Person or group of people that has its own functions with responsibilities, authorities, and relationships to achieve its objectives.

name: out-of-control criteria
definition: Set of decision rules for identifying the presence of special causes.

name: participant in an interlaboratory comparison
definition: Laboratory, organization, or person that receives test items and submits results for review by the coordinator of an interlaboratory comparison.

name: performance characteristic of a measurement procedure
definition: Aspect of a measurement procedure that may be quantitatively investigated and assessed as part of procedure validation.
synonyms: performance characteristic|performance characteristic of a measurement method

name: performance score
definition: Statistic, derived from a result reported by a participant in a proficiency testing scheme, used in interpretation of participant performance and to allow comparison with defined objectives.

name: precision limit
definition: Quantity value, less than or equal to what the absolute difference between two measured quantity values obtained under specified conditions of measurement is expected to be with a given probability.

name: procedure validation
definition: Process of defining an analytical requirement and confirming that the procedure under consideration has capabilities consistent with that requirement.

name: procedure verification
definition: Confirmation, through the provision of objective evidence, that the procedure fulfils specified requirements.

name: process in a state of statistical control
definition: Process subject only to random causes.

name: proficiency test item
definition: Sample, product, artefact, reference material, piece of equipment, measurement standard, data set, or other information used for proficiency testing.

name: proficiency testing
definition: Evaluation of the performance of a participant in an interlaboratory comparison against pre-established criteria.

name: proficiency testing provider
definition: Organization which takes responsibility for all tasks in the development and operation of a proficiency testing scheme.

name: proficiency testing round
definition: Single complete sequence from distribution of proficiency test items to reporting of the evaluation results to the participants.

name: proficiency testing scheme
definition: Proficiency testing designed and operated in one or more proficiency testing rounds for a specified area of testing, measurement, calibration, or inspection.

name: protocol for interlaboratory comparison
definition: Detailed set of instructions describing the objectives, design, conduct, and reporting of an interlaboratory comparison.

name: quality
definition: Degree to which a set of inherent characteristics of an object fulfils requirements.

name: quality control material
definition: Material used for the purposes of quality control and subjected to the same or part of the same measurement procedure as that used for analytical samples.

name: quality improvement
definition: Part of quality management focused on increasing the ability to fulfil requirements for quality.

name: quality management
definition: Coordinated activities to direct and control an organization with regard to quality.

name: quality management system
definition: Part of a set of interrelated or interacting elements of an organization to establish quality policies and quality objectives and processes to achieve those objectives.

name: quality manual
definition: Specification for the quality management system of an organization.

name: quality objective
definition: Result to be achieved related to quality.

name: quality plan
definition: Specification of the procedures and associated resources to be applied when and by whom to a specific object.

name: quality planning
definition: Part of quality management focused on setting quality objectives and specifying necessary operational processes and related resources to achieve the quality objectives.

name: quality policy
definition: Intentions and direction of a laboratory as formally expressed by its top management related to quality.

name: reference laboratory
definition: Laboratory that applies a reference measurement procedure, a reference examination procedure, or performs a calibration.

name: reference material certificate
definition: Document, issued by a reference material producer, containing the essential information for the use of a certified reference material and confirming that the necessary procedures have been carried out to ensure the validity and traceability of the stated property values.

name: reference material certification
definition: Process that formally establishes the certified property value(s) of a candidate certified reference material.

name: reference material certification report
definition: Document giving detailed information, in addition to that contained in a reference material certificate.

name: reference material producer
definition: Technically competent body that produces a reference material compliant with the appropriate guidance documents and issues the reference material documentation.

name: rejection interval
definition: Interval of non-permissible measured quantity values.

name: requirement
definition: Need or expectation that is stated, generally implied or obligatory.

name: ruggedness of a measurement procedure
definition: Ability of a measurement procedure to maintain acceptable performance under minor changes in operating conditions.

name: sensitivity of a measuring system
definition: Quotient of the change in an indication of a measuring system and the corresponding change in a quantity being measured.

name: Shewhart control chart
definition: Control chart with Shewhart control limits intended primarily to distinguish between the variation in the plotted measure due to random causes and that due to special causes.

name: Shewhart control limit
definition: Control limit determined statistically from the variation of the process due to random causes alone.

name: Shewhart means chart
definition: Shewhart control chart in which the means of measured quantity values are plotted against time. Figure 1: Shewhart means chart of the means of duplicate analyses of a quality control material, twice per day (d) over 20 days. Each point is the mean of the day’s four results (\(n = 4\)). Upper and lower warning limits (UWL and LWL) are at \(\bar{x} \pm 2s/\sqrt{n}\), where \(\bar{x}\) is the process mean, \(s\) is the standard deviation under repeatability conditions of measurement, and upper and lower action limits (UAL and LAL) are at \(\bar{x} \pm 3s/\sqrt{n}\). A simulated measurement bias of one standard deviation is applied after day 10.

name: Shewhart range chart
definition: Shewhart control chart in which the ranges of measured quantity values are plotted against time.

name: specified requirement
definition: Need or expectation that is stated.

name: standard deviation for proficiency assessment
definition: Measure of dispersion used in the evaluation of results of proficiency testing.

name: standard operating procedure
definition: Authorized, documented procedure or set of procedures with detailed instructions for specified activities.

name: statistical process control
definition: Activities focused on the use of statistical techniques to reduce variation, increase knowledge about the process, and steer the process in the desired way.

name: target measurement uncertainty
definition: Measurement uncertainty specified as an upper limit and decided on the basis of the intended use of measurement results.

name: tolerance
definition: Difference between upper and lower tolerance limits.

name: tolerance interval
definition: Interval of permissible quantity values.

name: tolerance limit
definition: Specified upper or lower bound of permissible quantity values of a property.

name: total quality management
definition: Organization-wide efforts to install a permanent climate in which an organization continuously improves its ability to deliver high-quality products and services to customers.

name: validation
definition: Confirmation, through the provision of objective evidence, that the requirements for a specific intended use or application have been fulfilled.

name: verification
definition: Confirmation, through the provision of objective evidence, that specified requirements have been fulfilled.

name: Youden plot
definition: Graphical technique for evaluating an interlaboratory comparison when each participant has made two measurements on the same sample or one measurement on each of two different samples.Figure 1: Youden plot of the \(z\) scores of samples #9 and #10 of Round 5 of U39 of the proficiency testing program held by the RCPA Australia for the analysis of creatinine in urine by 218 laboratories. (Reproduced with permission).

name: activated state
definition: In theories of unimolecular reactions an energized chemical species, often characterized by the superscript \(^{\ddagger}\), where the excitation is specific and the molecule is poised for reaction.

name: ambiphilic
definition: Both nucleophilic and electrophilic.

name: α
definition: 1) Designation applied to the carbon to which a functional group is attached. 2) In carbohydrate nomenclature, a stereochemical designation of the configuration at the anomeric carbon. 3) Parameter in a Brønsted relation expressing the sensitivity of the rate of protonation to acidity. 4) Parameter in Leffler’s relation expressing the sensitivity of changes in Gibbs activation energy to changes in overall Gibbs energy for an elementary reaction.

name: bidentate
definition: Feature of a ligand with two potential binding sites.

name: bifurcation
definition: Feature on a potential-energy surface whereby a minimum-energy reaction path (MERP) emanating from a saddle point (corresponding to a transition structure) splits in two and leads to alternative products without intervening minima or secondary barriers to overcome. A bifurcation arises when the curvature of the surface in a direction perpendicular to the MERP becomes zero and then negative; it implies the existence of a lower-energy transition structure with a transition vector orthogonal to the original MERP.

name: bond-dissociation enthalpy
definition: Standard molar enthalpy required to break a given bond of some specific molecular entity by homolysis.

name: bond enthalpy
definition: Average value of the gas-phase bond-dissociation enthalpies (usually at a temperature of \(\pu{298 K}\)) for all bonds of the same type within the same chemical species.

name: bond-stretch isomers
definition: Two (or more) molecules with the same spin multiplicity but with different lengths for one or more bonds.

name: β, βnuc, βlg
definition: Parameter in a Brønsted relation expressing the sensitivity of the rate of deprotonation to basicity.

name: β-elimination
definition: Transformation of the general type \[\ce{XABY -> A=B + XY (or X + Y, or X^{+} + Y^{-})}\] where the central atoms \(\ce{A}\) and \(\ce{B}\) are commonly, but not necessarily, carbon.

name: Catalán solvent parameters
definition: Quantitative measure of solvent polarity, based on the solvent’s hydrogen-bond-donor ability, hydrogen-bond-acceptor ability, polarizability, and dipolarity.

name: catalytic antibody
definition: Monoclonal antibody with enzymatic activity.

name: catalytic cycle
definition: Sequence of reaction steps in the form of a loop. One step is binding of a reactant to the active catalyst (sometimes formed from a precatalyst), and another step is the release of product and regeneration of the catalyst.

name: cation-π interaction
definition: Noncovalent attractive force between a positive ion (metal cation, protonated Brønsted base, etc.) and a \(\ce{\uppi\ electron}\) system.

name: chiral feature
definition: Structural characteristic rendering a molecule chiral.

name: chiral recognition
definition: Attraction between molecules through noncovalent interactions that exhibit complementarity only between partners with specific chirality.

name: coarctate
definition: Feature of a concerted transformation in which the primary changes in bonding occur within a cyclic array of atoms but in which two nonbonding atomic orbitals on an atom interchange roles with two bonding orbitals.

name: condensed formula
definition: Linear representation of the structure of a molecular entity in which bonds are omitted.

name: curly arrows
definition: Symbols for depicting the flow of electrons in a chemical reaction or to generate additional resonance forms.

name: dendrimer
definition: Large molecule constructed from a central core with repetitive branching and multiple functional groups at the periphery.

name: distortion interaction model
definition: Method for analyzing activation energy as the sum of the energies to distort the reactants into the geometries they have in transition states plus the energy of interaction between the two distorted reactants.

name: donicity
definition: Quantitative experimental measure of the Lewis basicity of a molecule \(\ce{B}\), expressed as the negative enthalpy of the formation of the 1:1 complex \(\ce{B.SbCl5}\).

name: dynamic NMR
definition: NMR spectroscopy of samples undergoing chemical reactions.

name: electron pushing
definition: Method using curly arrows for showing the formal movement of an electron pair (from a lone pair or a \(\upsigma\) or \(\ce{\uppi\ bond}\)) or of an unpaired electron, in order to generate additional resonance forms or to denote a chemical reaction.

name: electrophilic substitution
definition: Heterolytic reaction in which the entering group adds to a nucleophile and in which the leaving group, or electrofuge, relinquishes both electrons to its reaction partner, whereupon it becomes another potential electrophile.

name: NMR exchange spectroscopy
definition: Two-dimensional NMR technique producing cross peaks corresponding to site-to site chemical exchange. The cross-peak amplitudes carry information about exchange rates.

name: formal charge
definition: Quantity (omitted if zero) attached to each atom in a Lewis structure according to \[Z_{\rm{formal}} = N_{\rm{valence}} - N_{\rm{lonepairs}} - ½N_{\rm{bonds}}\]

name: frustrated Lewis acid-base pair
definition: Acid and base for which adduct formation is prevented by steric hindrance.

name: Gaussian orbital
definition: Function centered on an atom of the form \(\phi(r) \propto x^{i} y^{j} z^{k} \exp (-\zeta r^{2})\), used to approximate atomic orbitals in the LCAO-MO method.

name: graphene
definition: Allotrope of carbon, whose structure is a one-atom-thick planar sheet of \(\ce{sp^{2}{-}bonded}\) carbon atoms in a honeycomb (hexagonal) crystal lattice.

name: halogen bond
definition: Association between a Lewis-acidic halogen atom in a molecular entity and a Lewis-basic region in another, or the same, molecular entity, which acts as an electron-pair donor, such that the balance of forces of attraction and repulsion results in net stabilization.

name: hapticity
definition: Topological description for the number of contiguous atoms of a ligand that are bonded to a central metal atom.

name: HBA solvent
definition: Strongly or weakly basic solvent capable of acting as a hydrogen-bond acceptor (HBA) and forming strong intermolecular solute-solvent hydrogen bonds.

name: HBD solvent
definition: Solvent with a sizable permanent dipole moment that bears suitably acidic hydrogen atoms to form strong intermolecular solvent-solute hydrogen bonds.
synonyms: dipolar HBD solvent|hydrogen-bond donating solvent|protic solvent

name: high-throughput screening
definition: Automated method to quickly assay large libraries of chemical species for the affinity of small organic molecules toward a target of interest.

name: Huisgen reaction
definition: Cycloaddition of 1,3 dipolar compounds.

name: hydronation
definition: Attachment of the ion \(\ce{H^{+}}\) either in natural abundance or where it is not desired to distinguish between the isotopes.

name: ionic liquid
definition: Liquid that consists exclusively or almost exclusively of equivalent amounts of oppositely charged ions.

name: keto-enol tautomerization
definition: Interconversion of ketone and enol tautomers by hydron migration, accelerated by acid or base catalysis.

name: Laurence solvent parameters
definition: Quantitative measures of solvent polarity, based on the solvent’s dispersion/induction interactions, electrostatic interactions between permanent multipoles, solute Lewis base/solvent Lewis acid interactions, and solute HBD/solvent HBA interactions.

name: Leffler’s relation
definition: In a series of elementary reactions, the changes in Gibbs activation energies are often found to be proportional to the changes in Gibbs energies for the overall reaction.\[\updelta \Delta^{\ddagger} G = \alpha \Delta_{\rm{r}} G^{\circ}\] This relation was interpreted in terms of the simple assumption that a small change in any transition-state property \(P_{\ddagger}\) is a linear combination of changes in reactant- and product-state properties, \(P_{\ce{R}}\) and \(P_{\ce{P}}\). \[\updelta P_{\ddagger} = \alpha \updelta P_{\ce{P}} + (1-\alpha)\updelta P_{\ce{R}}\] Within the limits of this assumption, the parameter \(\alpha\) is an approximate measure of the fractional displacement of the transition state along the minimum-energy reaction path from reactants to products.

name: mass action, law of
definition: Statement that the velocity of a reaction depends on the active mass, i.e., the concentrations of the reactants.

name: Mayr–Patz equation
definition: Rate constants for the reactions of \(\ce{sp^{2}{-}hybridized}\) electrophiles with nucleophiles can be expressed by the correlation \[\lg [k/(\pu{dm3 mol-1 s-1})] = s_{\rm{N}}(E + N)\] where \(E\) is the nucleophile-independent electrophilicity parameter, \(N\) is the electrophile-independent nucleophilicity parameter, and \(s_{\rm{N}}\) is the electrophile-independent nucleophile-specific susceptibility parameter.

name: minimum structural change, principle of
definition: Principle that a chemical reaction is expected to occur with a minimum of bond changes or with a minimum redistribution of electrons (although more complex reaction cascades are also possible).

name: molecular recognition
definition: Attraction between specific molecules through noncovalent interactions that often exhibit electrostatic and stereochemical complementarity between the partners.

name: nanomaterial
definition: Substance whose particles are in the size range of 1 to \(\pu{100 nm}\).

name: non-Kekulé structure
definition: Compound with unpaired electrons for which no Lewis structures are possible with all bonding electrons paired in single or double bonds.

name: nucleophilic substitution
definition: Heterolytic reaction in which an entering group adds to the electrophilic part of the substrate and in which the leaving group, or nucleofuge, retains both electrons of the bond that is broken, whereupon it becomes another potential nucleophile.

name: octanol-water partition ratio
definition: Equilibrium concentration of a substance in octan-1-ol divided by its equilibrium concentration in water.

name: organocatalysis
definition: Catalysis by small organic molecules, as distinguished from catalysis by (transition) metals or enzymes.

name: parallel effect
definition: Change of the position of the transition state upon stabilization or destabilization of a structure (or structures) along the assumed minimum-energy reaction path.

name: polarity
definition: Characteristic of a bond between atoms of different electronegativity, such that the electrons in that bond are not shared equally.

name: potential of mean force
definition: Free energy as a function of a set of coordinates, the negative gradient of which gives the average force acting on that configuration averaged over all other coordinates and momenta within a statistical distribution. If the averaging is performed within a canonical ensemble (constant volume, temperature, and number of particles), the PMF is equivalent to the Helmholtz energy, but if it is performed within an isobaric-isothermal ensemble (constant pressure, temperature, and number of particles), the PMF is equivalent to the Gibbs energy.

name: protofugality
definition: Special case of nucleofugality, describing the relative rates of transfer of a proton (more generally: hydron) from a series of Brønsted acids \(\ce{H-X}\) to a common Brønsted base.

name: protonation
definition: Attachment of the ion \(\ce{^{1}H^{+}}\) of relative isotopic mass approximately equal to 1.

name: protophilicity
definition: Special case of nucleophilicity, describing the relative rates of reactions of a series of Lewis bases with a common Brønsted acid. This term has the advantage over the commonly used 'kinetic basicity' that philicity and fugality are associated with kinetics, while acidity and basicity are associated with thermodynamics.

name: push-pull conjugation
definition: Feature of an extended conjugated \(\ce{\uppi\ system}\) bearing an electron donor group at one end and an electron acceptor group at the other end.

name: π-electron donor
definition: Substituent capable of electron donation by resonance (e.g., \(\ce{OCH3}\)).

name: quantitative structure–property relationship
definition: Regression model to correlate chemical properties such as boiling point or chromatographic retention time with predictor parameters based on measured or calculated features of molecular structure.

name: resonance form
definition: One of at least two Lewis structures, with fixed single, double, and triple bonds, that is a contributing structure to the valence-bond wavefunction of a molecule that cannot be described by a single Lewis structure.

name: self-assembly
definition: Process whereby a system of single-molecule components spontaneously forms an organized structure, owing to molecular recognition.

name: shift reagent
definition: Paramagnetic substance that induces an additional change of the NMR resonance frequency of a nucleus near any site in a molecule to which the substance binds.

name: skeletal formula
definition: Two-dimensional representation of a molecular entity in which bonds are indicated as lines between vertices representing octet carbon atoms with attached hydrogens omitted and in which other atoms are represented by their chemical symbols.

name: solvatomers
definition: Isomers that differ in their solvation environment.

name: stereogenic center
definition: Atom within a molecule bearing groups such that interchanging any two of them leads to a stereoisomer of the original molecule.

name: superjacent orbital
definition: Second Lowest Unoccupied Molecular Orbital (SLUMO).

name: tautomers
definition: Constitutional isomers that can interconvert more or less rapidly, often by migration of a hydron.

name: through-conjugation
definition: Phenomenon whereby electrons can be delocalized from any of three (or more) groups to any other.

name: zero-point energy
definition: Extent, in consequence of Heisenberg’s Uncertainty Principle, by which a particle or a set of particles has an energy greater than that of the minimum on the potential-energy surface.

name: atomic spectroscopy
definition: Measurement principle of spectroscopy for the study of electromagnetic radiation absorbed and emitted by atoms.

name: molecular spectroscopy
definition: Measurement principle of spectroscopy for the study of rotational, vibrational, and electronic transitions of molecules.

name: nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy
definition: Measurement principle of spectroscopy to measure the precession of magnetic moments placed in a magnetic induction based on absorption of electromagnetic radiation of a specific frequency by an atomic nucleus.

name: absorption index
definition: Imaginary part of the complex refractive index describing absorption of electromagnetic radiation.

name: accidental degeneracy
definition: Condition that occurs when two or more normal transitions have the same energy as a matter of coincidence, as opposed to because of symmetry conditions.

name: angle of incidence
definition: Angle between a beam of electromagnetic radiation and a line normal to a surface.

name: anisotropic
definition: Having properties that depend on direction.

name: apodization
definition: Technical term for changing the shape of a mathematical function, electrical signal, or optical transmission to remove or smooth a discontinuity at the edges, literally meaning 'removing the foot'.

name: apodization function
definition: Mathematical function that effects apodization.

name: array detector
definition: Photoelectric detector in which a large number of pixels are distributed, usually in regularly spaced lines and usually over a rectangular area.

name: attenuated total reflection
definition: Internal reflection from an absorbing material at angles of incidence at or above the critical angle.

name: beam splitter
definition: Device to split a beam of electromagnetic radiation into two parts.

name: Cauchy function
definition: Function \(y = a/(b^{2} + x^{2})\) where \(a\) and \(b\) are constants.

name: charge coupled device
definition: Device that stores information in the form of charge packets in an array of closely spaced capacitors.

name: circular birefringence
definition: Difference between the refractive indices of an optically active medium for left, \(n^{\rm{L}}\), and right, \(n^{\rm{R}}\), circularly polarized radiation (\(n^{\rm{L}}-n^{\rm{R}}\)).

name: dephasing
definition: Loss of coherence between the upper and lower states of a transition.

name: detector gate width
definition: Time for signal integration after start of detection.

name: difference spectroscopy
definition: Measurement method of spectroscopy in which spectral subtraction is used to help the study and identification of individual species in a mixture.

name: diffuse reflectance
definition: Diffuse reflected (remitted) radiant power (\(P_{\rm{rem}}\)) divided by incident radiant power (\(P_{0}\)). \(R = P_{\rm{rem}}/P_{0}\).

name: diffuse reflection
definition: Reflection in which electromagnetic radiation incident on a scattering surface at a certain angle is reflected (remitted) over all angles.

name: diffuse transmission
definition: Process in which radiation is transmitted by a scattering sample and leaves the sample in directions other than that required by Snell’s law of refraction. The process is complicated and involves transmission, reflection, and scattering.

name: dipole coupling
definition: Coupling of different motions through dipole-dipole forces.

name: dispersive Fourier-transform spectroscopy
definition: Fourier-transform spectroscopy using a Michelson or other two-beam interferometer with the sample placed in one arm of the interferometer.

name: dispersive spectrometer
definition: Spectrometer in which electromagnetic radiation is separated spatially into its component wavenumbers by a dispersive element, such as a prism or a diffraction grating.

name: electromagnetic radiation
definition: Flow of energy through space propagated as synchronized sinusoidal waves of the electric field, \(\boldsymbol{E}\), and the magnetic field \(\boldsymbol{H}\).

name: electromagnetic transition
definition: Transition accompanied by the emission or absorption of a photon.

name: electron emission spectrometry
definition: Measurement principle of spectrometry for the study of electrons emitted by atoms.

name: electronic transition
definition: Transition in an atom, ion, or molecule from an electronic energy level \(E_{1}\) to another energy level \(E_{2}\).

name: energy level
definition: Set of one or more stationary quantum states of a free atom, ion, or molecule having a particular internal energy.

name: experimental absorbance
definition: Decadic absorbance as measured with no corrections for other processes.

name: folding
definition: The appearance of peaks at incorrect frequencies in a mathematically-processed spectrum due to insufficient density of datapoints in the time-domain spectrum or from peaks outside of the sampled frequency range.This process can be simulated by folding a spectrum that shows the correct wavenumbers back onto itself at \(\tilde{ u}_{\rm{M}}\) and its multiples.

name: free induction decay
definition: Indication from a pulsed spectroscopy experiment that takes the form of damped sine waves arising from the excited system returning to equilibrium.

name: Fresnel reflection
definition: Reflection of radiation from a surface that is smooth and large with respect to the wavelength of the radiation. A reflected beam, of intensity governed by the Fresnel equations, is produced at an angle of reflection equal to the angle of incidence.

name: Gaussian band
definition: Spectral band with the shape \(H_{\rm{G}} \exp[-4\ln 2{(\tilde{ u} - \tilde{ u}_{0})}^{2}/W^{2}]\), where \(H_{\rm{G}}\) is the band maximum (peak height), \(W\) is the full width at half maximum, and \(\tilde{ u}_{0}\) is the peak wavenumber.

name: Hadamard transform spectrometer
definition: Multiplexing spectrometer that uses the optical components of a dispersive spectrometer with a Hadamard encoding mask.

name: high-pass filter
definition: Optical filter that excludes radiation of wavenumber lower (wavelength higher) than a certain value and passes radiation of wavenumber above (wavelength lower) than this value. Electrical filter that blocks signal with a modulation frequency lower than a certain cut-on value and passes signals of frequency above this value.

name: Hilbert transforms
definition: Functions that interrelate the real part, \(f'\), and imaginary part, \(f''\), of the refractive index, \(\boldsymbol{\hat{n}} = n + {\rm{i}}k\), or relative permittivity, \(\boldsymbol{\hat{\epsilon}} = \epsilon' + \rm{i}\epsilon''\), through \[f'(\tilde{ u}_{\rm{a}}) - f_{\infty}' = \frac{1}{\pi} P \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \frac{f''(\tilde{ u})}{\tilde{ u} - \tilde{ u}_{\rm{a}}}\rm{d}\tilde{ u}\] \[f''(\tilde{ u}_{\rm{a}}) - f_{\infty}' = \frac{-1}{\pi} P \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \frac{f'(\tilde{ u}_{\rm{a}}) - f_{\infty}'}{\tilde{ u} - \tilde{ u}_{\rm{a}}}\rm{d}\tilde{ u}\] where \(P\) means that the principal part of the integral is taken at the singularity.

name: instrument line shape
definition: Idealized form of a feature in a spectrometer corresponding to a transition.

name: integrated intensity
definition: Area under a spectral band in an absorption spectrum where the absorption is linearly proportional to the amount of absorber in unit area.

name: integration range
definition: Frequency or wavenumber range over which the integrated intensity of an absorption band is measured by numerical integration of the area under the band.

name: intensified charge coupled device detector
definition: Charge coupled device with a prior amplification system to improve sensitivity.

name: internal absorbance
definition: Absorbance in the absence of reflection, scattering or luminescence.

name: Kramers–Kronig transforms
definition: Functions based on the physical principle of causality that interconvert the real and imaginary parts of complex optical quantities when they are known over a sufficiently wide (strictly infinite) wavenumber range. They are frequently used to interconvert the real part, \(f'\), and imaginary part, \(f''\), of the refractive index, \(\boldsymbol{\hat{n}} = n + {\rm{i}}k\), the dielectric constant (relative permittivity), \(\boldsymbol{\hat{\epsilon}_{r}} = \epsilon_{r}' + \rm{i}\epsilon_{r}''\), or the logarithm of the complex reflection coefficient \(re^{i\varphi}\) through \[f'(\tilde{ u}_{\rm{a}}) - f_{\infty}' = \frac{2}{\pi} P \int_{0}^{\infty} \frac{\tilde{ u} f''(\tilde  u)}{\tilde{ u}^{2} - \tilde{ u}_{\rm{a}}^{2}} {\rm{d}}\tilde{ u}\] \[f''(\tilde{ u}_{\rm{a}}) = \frac{-2\tilde{ u}_{\rm{a}}}{\pi} P \int_{0}^{\infty} \frac{f'(\tilde{ u}) - f_{\infty}'}{\tilde{ u}^2 - \tilde{ u}_{\rm{a}}^2} \rm{d}\tilde{ u}\] where \(P\) means that the principal part of the integral is taken at the singularity.

name: light
definition: Electromagnetic radiation visible to the human eye.

name: linear Napierian absorption coefficient
definition: Napierian absorbance (\(A_{\rm{e}}\)) divided by path-length (\(l\)). \(\alpha = A_{\rm{e}}/l\).

name: liquid crystal tunable filter
definition: Optical device based on polarization interference caused by transmission through a series of birefringent liquid crystal layers of different thicknesses that allow a narrow wavelength region to be selected and tuned over a broad spectral range.

name: lock-in amplifier
definition: Amplifier that amplifies only those signals that have, within a specified spectral bandwidth, the same frequency as, and a specified phase relation with, the selected reference signal.

name: low-pass filter
definition: Optical filter that excludes radiation of wavenumber greater (wavelength lower) than a certain value and passes radiation of wavenumber below (wavelength greater than) this value. Electrical filter that blocks signal with a modulation frequency above a certain cut-on value and passes signals of frequency below this value.

name: molar decadic absorption coefficient
definition: Decadic absorbance (\(A_{10}\)) divided by path-length (\(l\)) and amount concentration (\(c\)). \(\varepsilon = A_{10}/(cl)\).

name: molar Napierian absorption coefficient
definition: Napierian absorbance (\(A_{\rm{e}}\)) divided by path-length (\(l\)) and amount concentration (\(c\)). \(\kappa = A_{\rm{e}}/(cl)\).

name: multiple attenuated total reflection
definition: Process in which attenuated total reflection occurs sequentially several times with the same sample.
synonyms: MATR|frustrated multiple internal reflection (FMIR)|multiple internal reflection (MIR)

name: Napierian absorbance
definition: Absorbance calculated with logarithm base \(e\) (natural or Napierian logarithm).

name: net absorption cross-section
definition: Molar Napierian absorption coefficient divided by the Avogadro constant. \(\sigma_{\rm{net}} = \kappa/N_{\rm{A}}\).

name: nominal spectral resolution
definition: Spectral resolution setting on an instrument that a user sets to record a spectrum.

name: Nyquist criterion
definition: Result of information theory that a sine wave can be completely reconstructed if its ordinate is known at two or more points in a cycle.

name: Nyquist frequency
definition: Highest frequency or wavenumber that can be characterized by sampling at a given rate in order to be able to fully reconstruct the signal without artefacts.

name: optical throughput
definition: Volume in phase space, a function of the area of the emitting source (\(S\)) and the solid angle into which it propagates \((\mathit{\Omega}).{\rm{d}}^{2} G = {\rm{d}}S {\rm{d}}\mathit{\Omega}\).

name: path-length
definition: Length of the optical path through the sample.

name: radiofrequency
definition: Frequency or band of frequencies in the range \(\pu{E4}\) to \(\pu{E12 Hz}\).

name: received radiant flux density
definition: Radiant power incident on unit area.

name: reflection
definition: Process by which electromagnetic radiation is reflected by a sample. For non-scattering samples the term means Fresnel reflection; for scattering samples the term includes regular reflection and volume reflection or diffuse reflection.

name: signal-to-noise ratio
definition: Power of signal divided by power of noise.

name: single beam spectrum
definition: Output of a single beam spectrometer as a function of wavenumber or wavelength.

name: slit width
definition: Distance between the blades of the entrance or exit slits in a monochromator.

name: spectral band
definition: Region of the absorption/transmission spectrum in which the absorbance/transmission passes through a maximum/minimum.

name: spectral bandwidth
definition: Upper frequency minus lower frequency in a continuous band of frequencies.

name: spectral radiant energy density
definition: Radiant energy density in unit wavenumber (wavelength) interval at wavenumber \(\tilde{ u}\) (wavelength \(\lambda\)).

name: spectral range
definition: Wavelength range for which a spectrometer can be used.

name: spectral resolution
definition: Smallest difference between wavenumbers (or wavelengths or frequencies) at which different spectral properties may be distinguished, measured as the full width at half maximum.

name: spectral subtraction
definition: Ordinate of one spectrum minus ordinate of another spectrum.

name: spectrum
definition: Graph of a quantity derived from the radiant power at each wavelength (frequency or wavenumber) as ordinate plotted against the wavelength (frequency or wavenumber) of electromagnetic radiation as abscissa.

name: specular reflection
definition: Reflection of electromagnetic radiation from a surface such that each incident ray is reflected at the same angle to the surface normal as the incident ray, but on the opposing side of the surface normal in the plane formed by incident and reflected rays.

name: stray light
definition: Electromagnetic radiation that does not follow the usual path through a spectrometer and consequently appears in a spectrum at a frequency or wavenumber different from its initial value. The term is also used to refer to radiation that passes around the sample instead of through it, and consequently is not modified by the sample and seriously affects absolute and relative intensities.

name: transmission spectrum
definition: General term for the spectrum of transmitted electromagnetic radiation.

name: two-dimensional correlation spectroscopy
definition: Measurement principle of spectroscopy in which spectra are recorded at different magnitudes of an applied external perturbation of the sample and are processed to yield a 2-D correlation spectrum.

name: two-dimensional correlation spectrum
definition: Three-dimensional surface in which two of the dimensions show frequency axes (\( u_{1}\), \( u_{2}\)) and the third axis shows a correlation function of the spectral intensities observed at \( u_{1}\) and \( u_{2}\).

name: undersampling
definition: Sampling less frequently than is required by the Nyquist criterion.

name: Voigt function
definition: Convolution of Gaussian and Lorentzian (Cauchy) functions.

name: wavelength in medium
definition: Distance travelled by a wave of electromagnetic radiation in one cycle in a non-absorbing medium of real refractive index \(n\). \(\lambda = \lambda_{0}/n\).

name: wavelength in vacuum
definition: Distance travelled by a wave of electromagnetic radiation in one cycle in vacuum.

name: wavenumber in medium
definition: Reciprocal of wavelength of electromagnetic radiation. \(\sigma = 1/\lambda\).

name: wavenumber in vacuum
definition: Reciprocal of the vacuum wavelength of electromagnetic radiation. \(\tilde{ u} = 1/\lambda_{0}\).

name: working range
definition: Range of absorbance or intensity which a spectrometer can measure with accuracy and precision.

name: zero filling
definition: Addition of zeros to a free induction decay or interferogram to decrease the frequency or wavenumber spacing between points in the Fourier-transformed spectrum.

name: zero path difference
definition: In a Michelson interferometer or other two-beam interferometer, the position of the moving mirror at which the optical paths are equal.

name: <sup>13</sup>C-HMQC-NOESY
definition: Three-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy for the assignment of protein structure with one carbon and two hydrogen dimensions.

name: <sup>13</sup>C-NOESY-HSQC
definition: Three-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy for the assignment of protein structure with one carbon and two hydrogen dimensions.

name: <sup>15</sup>N-NOESY-HSQC
definition: Three-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy for the assignment of protein structure with one nitrogen and two hydrogen dimensions.

name: <sup>15</sup>N-TOCSY-HSQC
definition: Three-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy for the assignment of protein structure with one nitrogen and two hydrogen dimensions.

name: 180° pulse
definition: Pulsed radiofrequency signal in NMR that rotates the bulk magnetization vector (\(\boldsymbol{M}_{0}\)) of a nuclear spin to its opposing direction, effectively inverting the signal, (e.g., from the \(+z\) to \(-z\) axis).

name: 90° pulse
definition: Pulsed radiofrequency signal that rotates the bulk magnetization vector (\(\boldsymbol{M}_{0}\)) of a nuclear spin to its orthogonal plane.

name: acquisition time
definition: Duration of the digitization of a free induction decay.

name: adiabatic pulse
definition: Radiofrequency pulse that inverts spins by using a frequency sweep during the pulse.

name: Bloch equations
definition: Set of coupled differential equations which can be used to describe the behaviour of a magnetization vector under any conditions.

name: Bloch–Siegert shift
definition: Frequency difference seen for a nuclear magnetic resonance signal when a radiofrequency field is applied during the acquisition time.

name: Boltzmann distribution of nuclear spins
definition: Distribution of nuclear spins among their possible energy levels at thermal equilibrium.

name: CBCA(CO)NH/HN(CO)CACB
definition: Three-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy for the assignment of protein structure with nitrogen, carbon and hydrogen dimensions.

name: CBCANH/HNCACB
definition: Three-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy for the assignment of protein structure with nitrogen, carbon and hydrogen dimensions.

name: CC(CO)NH
definition: Three-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy for the assignment of protein structure with nitrogen, carbon and hydrogen dimensions.

name: chemical shift anisotropy
definition: Chemical shift difference between isotropic and anisotropic states in nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy.

name: combined rotation and multiple pulse spectroscopy
definition: Measurement method of nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy for obtaining high-resolution solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectra on nuclei with high gyromagnetic ratio such as \(\ce{^{1}H}\) and \(\ce{^{19}F}\).

name: constant time evolution
definition: Segment of a pulse sequence in nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy that allows evolution of chemical shift during a fixed time period rather than through the traditional symmetrical incremented delays.

name: correlation spectroscopy
definition: Homonuclear two-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy correlation experiment showing cross peaks representing spin-spin coupling between pairs of nuclei.

name: correlation spectroscopy through long-range coupling
definition: Heteronuclear (typically \(\ce{^{13}C}\)) detected long range 2D correlation experiment in nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy that has mostly been superseded by heteronuclear multiple bond correlation (HMBC) experiments and its variants.

name: correlation time
definition: Parameter related to the mean time during which a molecule maintains its spatial geometry.

name: cross polarization with magic angle spinning NMR
definition: Combined use of cross polarization with magic-angle spinning for solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy.

name: cross polarization
definition: Technique in solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy that enables polarization from abundant spins such as \(\ce{^{1}H}\) or \(\ce{^{19}F}\) to be transferred to dilute spins such as \(\ce{^{13}C}\) or \(\ce{^{15}N}\) to enhance signal-to-noise ratio.

name: decoupling in the presence of scalar interactions
definition: Pulse sequence in nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy often used for isotropic mixing in total correlation spectroscopy (TOCSY) experiments due to its efficiency over large spectral bandwidths.

name: diffusion ordered spectroscopy
definition: Pseudo-two-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy experiment that resolves NMR signals of a one-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectrum in a second dimension through the diffusion times of their corresponding molecules.

name: dipolar coupling
definition: Direct though-space interactions of nuclear magnetic moment vectors proportional to the inverse cube of internuclear distance.

name: distortionless enhancement by polarization transfer
definition: Measurement method of nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy used for determining the presence of primary, secondary and tertiary heteronuclei.

name: double pulsed-field gradient spin-echo excitation
definition: Pulse sequence in nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy in which pulsed-field gradients are applied to a doubled spin echo sequence to cleanly and precisely excite particular resonances.

name: double resonance
definition: Nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy experiment where excitation is applied independently to two distinct frequency ranges.

name: double-labelled protein
definition: Shorthand for a protein which has been uniformly \(\ce{^{15}N{-}}\) and \(\ce{^{13}C{-}labelled}\).

name: double-quantum filtered correlation spectroscopy
definition: Variant of the COSY experiment with a double quantum filter to remove, or at least reduce, impact of large singlet peaks on dynamic range and artefacts.

name: dwell time
definition: Time interval between sampled data points.

name: echo time
definition: In nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, time interval between the middle of the first radiofrequency pulse and the peak of the spin echo.

name: electronic reference to access in vivo concentrations
definition: Measurement method of nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy that generates an electronic signal in a nuclear magnetic resonance spectrometer which is detected simultaneously to the sample free induction decay during the acquisition.

name: Ernst angle
definition: When signal averaging in a single-pulse nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy experiment, flip angle giving the best signal-to-noise ratio for a given combination of spin-lattice relaxation time and repetition rate.

name: exchange spectroscopy
definition: Nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy experiment, which is the same as a NOESY, but for the purposes of observing nuclei exchanging chemical environments during the course of the experiment through conformational or chemical exchange.

name: excitation sculpting
definition: Robust method of generating selective excitation through combination of shaped pulses and pulsed-field gradients in nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy.

name: fast field cycling NMR relaxometry
definition: Relaxometry to measure the nuclear spin-lattice relaxation rate constant as a function of the applied magnetic field strength in nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy.

name: flip angle
definition: Rotation that the net magnetization experiences during the application of a radiofrequency pulse in nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy.

name: gated decoupling
definition: Application of spin decoupling only during selected time periods in a pulse experiment in nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy.

name: globally optimized alternating-phase rectangular pulses
definition: Spin decoupling pulse sequence in nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy used to provide decoupling over a large frequency range.

name: gradient-selected experiment
definition: Nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy experiment where pulsed-field gradients are employed to filter out unwanted resonances from a spectrum rather than the classic phase-cycling approach.

name: H(CCO)NH
definition: Three-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy for the assignment of protein structure with one nitrogen, and two hydrogen dimensions.

name: HBHA(CO)NH
definition: Three-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy for the assignment of protein structure with one nitrogen and two hydrogen dimensions.

name: HCCH-COSY
definition: Three-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy for the assignment of protein structure with one carbon and two hydrogen dimensions.

name: HCCH-TOCSY
definition: Three-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy for the assignment of protein structure with one carbon and two hydrogen dimensions.

name: heteronuclear decoupling
definition: Spin decoupling in nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy between two different nuclei (e.g., \(\ce{^{13}C}\) and \(\ce{^{1}H}\)) by appropriate excitation of the decoupled nucleus.

name: heteronuclear multiple bond correlation NMR
definition: Two-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy that gives correlations between carbons and protons that are separated by two, three, and, sometimes in conjugated systems, four bonds.

name: heteronuclear multiple-bond correlation over two bonds
definition: Variant of the heteronuclear single quantum correlation (HSQC) and heteronuclear multiple bond correlation (HMBC) experiment in nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy that almost exclusively correlates \(\ce{^{1}H}\) nuclei with heteronuclei separated by two covalent bonds.

name: heteronuclear multiple-quantum correlation NMR
definition: Simplest implementation of an inverse detected \(\ce{^{1}H}\) heteronuclear correlation nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy experiment.

name: heteronuclear multiple-quantum correlation with additional TOCSY transfer
definition: Variant of heteronuclear multiple bond correlation (HMBC) spectroscopy that shows correlations from a heteronucleus (e.g., \(\ce{^{13}C}\)) to not only its directly bound \(\ce{^{1}H}\) but also to all other \(\ce{^{1}H}\) nuclei within the spin system.

name: heteronuclear Overhauser effect spectroscopy
definition: Heteronuclear variant of nuclear Overhauser effect spectroscopy (NOSEY) showing through space interaction between \(\ce{^{1}H}\) and a heteronucleus, typically \(\ce{^{13}C}\).

name: heteronuclear shift correlation NMR
definition: Directly-observed one-bond heteronuclear correlation experiment in nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy.

name: heteronuclear single quantum correlation
definition: \(\ce{^{1}H}\) (inverse) detected two-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy heteronuclear experiment that correlates \(\ce{^{1}H}\) nuclei with their directly coupled nucleus through a single bond.

name: heteronuclear single quantum correlation with additional TOCSY transfer
definition: Variant of the heteronuclear single quantum correlation (HSQC) experiment that shows correlations from a heteronucleus (e.g., \(\ce{^{13}C}\)) to not only its directly bound \(\ce{^{1}H}\) but also to all other \(\ce{^{1}H}\) nuclei within the spin system.

name: heteronuclear single quantum multiple-bond correlation
definition: Variant of the heteronuclear single quantum correlation (HSQC) experiment that provides pure absorption, antiphase line shapes for precise, direct measurement of \(^{n}J(\ce{C,H})\) spin-spin coupling constants.

name: HN(CA)CO
definition: Three-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy for the assignment of protein structure with nitrogen, carbon and hydrogen dimensions.

name: HN(CO)CA
definition: Three-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy for the assignment of protein structure with nitrogen, carbon and hydrogen dimensions.

name: HNCA
definition: Three-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy for the assignment of protein structure with nitrogen, carbon and hydrogen dimensions.

name: HNCO
definition: Three-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy for the assignment of protein structure with nitrogen, carbon and hydrogen dimensions.

name: homonuclear decoupling
definition: Spin decoupling in nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy between two signals of the same nuclear isotope.

name: imaginary NMR spectrum
definition: In nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, one of two equally sized blocks of frequency data \(\pu{90\!^{\circ}}\) out of phase to each other produced by Fourier transformation of the time domain signal.

name: incredible natural-abundance double-quantum transfer experiment
definition: Nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy experiment designed to show homonuclear spin-spin coupling correlations between low natural abundance nuclei such as \(\ce{^{13}C}\).

name: insensitive nuclei enhanced by polarization transfer
definition: Pulse sequence in nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy that involves the transfer of nuclear spin polarization from spins with large Boltzmann population differences to nuclear spins of interest with low Boltzmann population differences.

name: inversion pulse
definition: Pulse in nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy that completely inverts the magnetization of a spin, e.g., \(+z\) to \(-z\).

name: inversion recovery sequence
definition: Spin echo sequence preceded by a \(\pu{180\!^{\circ}}\) inversion pulse used to determine spin-lattice relaxation times in nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy.

name: inversion time
definition: Time between the inversion pulse and the sampling pulse(s) in an inversion recovery sequence.

name: J-modulated spin-echo
definition: Nuclear magnetic resonance pulse sequence that refocuses spin vectors that have fanned out due to field inhomogeneity or chemical shift differences.

name: J-resolved spectroscopy
definition: Two-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy resolving chemical shift information in one dimension and spin-spin coupling in the second.

name: Knight shift
definition: Frequency shift in the nuclear magnetic resonance spectrum of a paramagnetic species that refers to the relative shift \(\boldsymbol{K}\) in NMR frequency for atoms in a metal (e.g., sodium) compared with the same atoms in a nonmetallic environment (e.g., as a salt).

name: Larmor angular frequency
definition: Frequency at which nuclei with a nuclear spin precess (Larmor precession) around the direction of an external magnetic induction \(\boldsymbol{B}_{0}\). \(\boldsymbol{\omega}_{\rm{L}} = -\gamma \boldsymbol{B}_{0}\), where \(\gamma\) is the magnetogyric ratio of the nucleus.

name: Larmor precession
definition: Precession of the magnetic moment (\(\boldsymbol{M}\)) of an object at an angular frequency, \(\boldsymbol{\omega}_{\rm{L}}\), about a static magnetic induction (\(\boldsymbol{B_{0}}\)), named after Joseph Larmor.

name: magic angle spinning
definition: Technique in solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy to remove or reduce the influence of anisotropic interactions by rapid sample rotation about the magic angle, where \(\boldsymbol{B_{0}}\) is external magnetic induction and \(\uptheta\) is the axis of rotation of the sample at an angle of approx. \(\pu{54.74\!^{\circ}}\) to the external magnetic induction.

name: multiple-quantum magic angle spinning NMR
definition: Measurement method of nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy used to obtain high-resolution NMR spectra of quadrupolar nuclei by removal of the anisotropy of the quadrupole interaction, involving creating a triple-quantum (or \(5{\rm{Q}}\)) coherence.

name: multiplet
definition: Feature in a nuclear magnetic resonance spectrum that is split but is too complex to easily interpret.

name: net dephasing time
definition: Measured time constant associated with spin-spin relaxation for loss of magnetization in the \(xy\) plane.

name: non-uniform sampling
definition: Technique employed within a high dimensionality nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy experiment that acquires only a subset of the data points traditionally acquired linearly thus enabling a reduction in experiment time or an increased resolution in the resultant spectra.

name: nuclear electric quadrupole moment
definition: Parameter that describes the effective shape of the ellipsoid of nuclear charge distribution.

name: nuclear magnetic resonance relaxometry
definition: Measurement method of nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy to measure nuclear relaxation variables.

name: nuclear magnetic resonance spectrum
definition: Representation of nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy data with at least one dimension a frequency domain.

name: nuclear Overhauser effect
definition: Change of intensity of one resonance when the spin transitions of another are somehow perturbed from their equilibrium populations.

name: nuclear Overhauser effect difference spectroscopy
definition: One dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy that yields, through subtraction of spectra generated with and without selective excitation of a specific resonance, the nuclear Overhauser enhancement of nuclei spatially close to a selectively excited nucleus.

name: nuclear Overhauser effect spectroscopy
definition: Measurement method of nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy based on the nuclear Overhauser effect to observe nuclei that are close to each other in space.

name: nuclear quadrupole resonance spectroscopy
definition: Measurement method of nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy where splitting of the nuclear spin states is determined by the electrostatic interaction of the nuclear charge density with the external electric potential of the surrounding electron cloud.

name: observation frequency
definition: Frequency corresponding to the centre of the spectrum window for a given nucleus under observation and the nominal frequency used to generate the hard, full spectrum pulses.

name: Pake doublet
definition: Characteristic line shape seen in solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy arising from dipolar coupling between two nuclei.

name: phase correction
definition: Linear combination of the real and imaginary parts of a 1-D nuclear magnetic resonance spectrum to produce peaks with pure absorption mode line shape.

name: phase cycling
definition: Component of nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy experiment that repeats a pulse sequence changing only the phases of the pulse(s) and the phase-sensitive detector reference.

name: powder pattern
definition: Very broad and distinctive line shape seen in a static solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy experiment with a typical magnitude of \(\pu{E2}\) to \(\pu{E5 Hz}\).

name: precession
definition: Classical description of the behaviour of nuclear magnetic moments, in which the vectors rotate about the \(\boldsymbol{B_{0}}\) axis at their Larmor angular frequencies.

name: presaturation
definition: Technique to suppress a particular nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy signal where a long low-power pulse is applied to that specific resonance prior to the main pulse sequence.

name: pulse sequence
definition: Timed series of radiofrequency pulses and magnetic field gradients that define a part or whole of a nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy experiment.

name: pulsed-field gradient
definition: Short, timed pulse in nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy that momentarily destroys the magnetic field homogeneity within the sample through a spatial-dependent field intensity.

name: pure shift yielded by chirp excitation
definition: Nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy experiment generating homonuclear spin-spin decoupled spectra.

name: quadrature detection
definition: Collection of time domain nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy data on both the \(x\) and \(y\ (\rm{g})\) axes of the rotating frame of reference to allow discrimination of positive and negative frequencies.

name: quadrupolar nuclide
definition: Nuclide with spin quantum number \(I \gt ½\) and a non-spherical distribution of charge in the nucleus giving rise to a nuclear electric quadrupole moment (\(eQ\)).

name: quadrupolar relaxation
definition: Relaxation mechanism in nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy arising from intramolecular quadrupolar interactions with electric field gradients.

name: radiation damping
definition: Line-broadening effect on intense signals in high field nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy.

name: radiofrequency coil
definition: In nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, an inductor-capacitor resonant circuit used to set up \(B_{1}\) magnetic inductions in a sample and to detect the signal from the sample.

name: real spectrum
definition: In nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, one of two equally sized blocks of frequency data \(\pu{90\!^{\circ}}\) out of phase to each other produced by Fourier transformation of the time domain signal.

name: relaxation reagent
definition: Paramagnetic species added to a sample in a nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy experiment to promote more rapid spin-lattice relaxation and allow a faster pulse repetition rate.

name: repetition time
definition: Time duration between repetitions of a nuclear magnetic resonance pulse sequence including the pulse sequence, acquisition time and relaxation delay.

name: residual dipolar coupling
definition: Dipolar coupling, but of a reduced magnitude to that seen in solids, observed in a liquid sample between spins in a molecule where there is incomplete averaging of spatially anisotropic dipolar couplings.

name: rotating-frame NOE spectroscopy
definition: Measurement method of nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy yielding through-space correlations via spin-spin relaxation.
synonyms: ROESY|cross-relaxation appropriate for minimolecules emulated by locked spins (CAMELPSIN)

name: rotational echo double resonance
definition: Measurement method of nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy allowing recoupling of heteronuclear dipolar coupling under magic angle spinning.

name: saturation transfer difference spectroscopy
definition: Measurement method of nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy that allows detection of transient binding of small molecule ligands to macromolecular receptors.

name: selective decoupling
definition: Spin decoupling of a specific resonance by selective irradiation.

name: selective excitation
definition: Application of a frequency selective radiofrequency pulse(s) to a single resonance or a discrete band of frequencies.

name: selective pulse
definition: Radiofrequency pulse with a narrow frequency spectral bandwidth (long, low-power pulse) to excite nuclei in a limited chemical shift range (see selective excitation).

name: single crystal nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy
definition: Solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy on a single crystal in a similar manner to that used in X-ray diffraction.

name: solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy
definition: Application of nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy to solids.

name: solvent suppression
definition: In nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy reduction or removal of large, unwanted resonances from solvents to improve spectrum quality and dynamic range through selective excitation and exploiting differences in relaxation times between solvent and analyte signals.

name: spectral width
definition: Frequency range that describes the width of the spectrum window of a specific nucleus in nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy.

name: spin
definition: Intrinsic angular momentum of a nucleus (or other sub-atomic particle).

name: spin decoupling
definition: Irradiation of a nucleus in nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy to prevent spin-spin coupling.

name: spin echo
definition: Refocusing of spin magnetization usually by two consecutive radiofrequency pulses.

name: spin system
definition: Group of magnetic nuclei that interact amongst themselves through spin-spin coupling but do not interact with any nuclei outside the spin system.

name: spin-lattice relaxation
definition: Mechanism in nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy by which the component of the magnetization vector along the direction of the static magnetic induction reaches thermodynamic equilibrium with its surroundings through loss of energy of the excited nuclear spins to the surrounding molecular lattice. The resultant exponential decay of signal is characterized by the spin-lattice relaxation time \(T_{1}\) (reciprocal of the rate constant of this mechanism).

name: spin-lattice relaxation time
definition: Reciprocal of the rate constant of longitudinal relaxation.

name: spinning sidebands
