definition: Satellite peaks in a nuclear magnetic resonance spectrum symetrically spaced either side of a main peak at a frequency offset related to the rate of spinning of the sample.

name: spin-spin relaxation
definition: Loss of magnetization in the \(xy\) plane (in the absence of \(\boldsymbol{B_{0}}\) inhomogeneities) through the interchange of energy between nuclear spins resulting in some precessing faster than the Larmor angular frequency and some slower.

name: spin-spin relaxation time
definition: Reciprocal of the rate constant of spin-spin relaxation.

name: static magnetic flux density
definition: Flux density of the magnetic field of a nuclear magnetic resonance spectrometer about whose direction the nuclear magnetic moment precesses.

name: symmetrization
definition: Method of removing artefacts from a two-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectrum that are symmetrical about the diagonal (e.g., HH COSY) or the \(\rm{f}1\) axis (e.g., tilted J-resolved spectra). Values equidistant from midline are compared and replaced the lower (or average) value of the two.

name: t1
definition: Time domain arising from the regular increments of the delay period in two-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy.

name: t2
definition: Time domain in two-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy arising from direct free induction decay detection.

name: t1 noise
definition: Streaks of spurious artefact signals in a two-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectrum parallel to the \(\rm{f}1\) axis at the \(\rm{f}2\) of a strong resonance.

name: three-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy
definition: Measurement method of nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy in which data are collected in three time domains.

name: time domain
definition: Condition in nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy where the independent variable of all functions is time.

name: time domain nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy
definition: Measurement method of nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy run at low magnetic field strengths where data analysis is performed directly on the free induction decay, often through the extraction of relaxation time constants

name: total correlation spectroscopy
definition: Two-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance homonuclear correlation experiment, which creates correlations between all protons within a given spin system, not just between geminal or vicinal protons as in COSY.

name: total suppression of spinning sidebands
definition: Technique to suppress spinning sidebands in solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy with cross polarization in magic angle spinning experiments.

name: transverse relaxation optimized spectroscopy
definition: Measurement method of nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, usually in protein NMR, that improves peak sharpness for molecules having a molecular mass of greater than \(\pu{100 kDa}\).

name: triple-resonance nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy
definition: Measurement method of nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy using three NMR-active nuclei.

name: two-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy
definition: Measurement method of nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy in which data are collected in two time domains: acquisition of the free induction decay (\(t_{2}\)) and a successively incremented delay (\(t_{1}\)).

name: wideband, alternating-phase, low-power technique for residual splitting
definition: Cluster of pulses applied repeatedly for heteronuclear decoupling.

name: Zeeman levels
definition: Energy levels of a nucleus arising from the interaction of its magnetic dipole with an external magnetic field.

name: zero-field nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy
definition: Measurement method of nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy in which nuclear magnetic resonance spectra are acquired in an environment carefully screened from magnetic fields, including from the Earth’s field allowing the direct detection of J-spectra in the absence of Zeeman interactions (see Zeeman levels).

name: ablation by sputtering
definition: Bombardment of a sample surface with ions resulting in the removal of atoms from their lattice sites, and thus an ongoing discharge process that causes continuous ablation of the sample.

name: ablation efficiency
definition: Mass of sample removed in laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy divided by the energy delivered by the laser beam.

name: ablation rate
definition: Depth of sample layer removed in the glow discharge process per unit time.

name: ablation threshold fluence
definition: Minimum fluence required to achieve ablation of the sample.

name: acid transient effects
definition: Increase in signal equilibration time or in wash out time caused by a modification in inorganic acid concentration.

name: additional gases
definition: Gases added to a combustion mixture.

name: aerosol transport phenomena
definition: Processes occurring inside the spray chamber or desolvation system responsible for the modification of the primary aerosol to finally yield the tertiary aerosol.

name: analyte transport rate
definition: Mass of analyte reaching the plasma per unit time.

name: atomic absorption spectroscopy
definition: Measurement method of atomic spectroscopy for measuring the amount of a chemical element based on the measurement of the absorption of characteristic electromagnetic radiation by atoms in the vapour phase.

name: atomic emission spectroscopy
definition: Measurement method of atomic spectroscopy for measuring the amount of a chemical element based on the measurement of the intensity of characteristic electromagnetic radiation emitted by atoms or molecules.

name: atomic excitation source
definition: Atomizer intended to convert free atoms to an excited state.

name: atomic fluorescence spectroscopy
definition: Measurement method of atomic spectroscopy for measuring the amount of a chemical element based on the measurement of the re-emission of characteristic electromagnetic radiation by atoms, following the absorption of radiation in the vapour phase.

name: atomic vapour
definition: Vapour containing free atoms of analyte.

name: atomization curve
definition: Graph of absorbance against atomization temperature.

name: axial viewing mode
definition: Inductively-coupled plasma optical emission spectrometer configuration in which the entrance slit is aligned with the main plasma axis.

name: background continuum emission
definition: Intense continuous background usually observed in laser-induced breakdown spectra.

name: background equivalent concentration
definition: Concentration of a given element measured at a given wavelength providing the same intensity as the background.

name: breakdown threshold fluence
definition: Minimum fluence required to achieve measurable emission signals

name: capacitive microwave plasma
definition: Plasma generated by a capacitor in presence of a microwave field.

name: characteristic line
definition: Spectral line of an atom used for the measurement of analyte concentration by atomic spectroscopy.

name: continuum source
definition: Source that emits electromagnetic radiation with relatively constant intensity over a broad spectral region.

name: depth-profiling
definition: Process by which the sample is sputtered 'atomic layer by layer' using suitable conditions.

name: direct current glow discharge optical emission spectroscopy
definition: Measurement method using optical emission spectroscopy in which atomization and excitation occur in a glow electric discharge sustained by a direct current electric field.

name: dispersion of a sample
definition: Conversion of the whole or part of a liquid or solid sample into a physical form sufficiently finely divided to allow it to be atomized (see atomization) upon introduction into the atomizer.

name: double-pulse laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy
definition: Measurement method of laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy in which reactions are induced by the interaction of the evolved plasma and the remaining part of the laser pulse, or with a following laser pulse provided from a second laser system.

name: dual viewing mode
definition: Inductively-coupled plasma spectrometer that allows axial viewing mode or radial viewing mode.

name: electric discharge
definition: Transmission of electrical current by a plasma in an applied electric field through a normally non-conducting medium.

name: electron number density
definition: Number of free electrons in vapour phase per volume unit.

name: electrothermal atomic absorption spectroscopy
definition: Measurement method of atomic absorption spectroscopy in which the sample is atomized by an electrothermal atomizer.

name: electrothermal vaporization
definition: Technique for sample introduction based on the use of a solid furnace heated at a controlled temperature to vaporize the sample prior to its introduction into an inductively-coupled plasma.

name: Esum
definition: Energy that must be supplied to an atom to transfer it from the ground atomic state to a given ionic excited state.

name: flame atomic spectrometer
definition: Spectrometer to make measurements by flame atomic spectroscopy.

name: flame atomic spectroscopy
definition: Measurement method of atomic spectroscopy that uses a flame to excite atoms.

name: flame
definition: Continuously flowing mixture of hot gases with a stationary position that derives its heat content from a strongly exothermic, irreversible chemical reaction between a fuel and an oxidant.

name: flow spoiler
definition: Component of a flame atomic spectrometer for creating turbulence in the stream of mist in the spray chamber and removing the largest droplets from this mist by deposition.

name: gate delay
definition: Time between the application of a laser pulse and the start of detection in laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy.
synonyms: time delay in laser induced breakdown spectroscopy

name: GD-OES spectrometers with simultaneous detection
definition: Spectrometers for glow discharge optical emission spectroscopy that allow simultaneous monitoring of selected spectral ranges or the whole emission spectra.

name: generator coupling efficiency
definition: Fraction of the energy generated being used for creating and maintaining the plasma in an inductively-coupled plasma spectrometer.

name: glow discharge source
definition: Component of an atomic emission spectrometer employing a glow electric discharge used in atomic emission spectroscopy for qualitative and quantitative analysis of solid materials.

name: glow electric discharge
definition: Electric discharge in gas at low pressure (\(\pu{100}\) to \(\pu{1000 Pa}\)).

name: glow-discharge optical emission spectroscopy
definition: Optical emission spectroscopy in which a glow electric discharge excites atoms at the surface of a sample, which is made the cathode of the discharge.

name: Grimm-type cathode
definition: Cathode for a glow electric discharge consisting of a flat sample, which is cooled during the discharge process so that thermal volatilization is suppressed and the sample material is removed by sputtering only.

name: hollow-cathode discharge source
definition: Glow discharge source with a graphite cathode, into which the sample is inserted in the form of drillings, a pressed pellet or a dry solution residue.

name: hollow-cathode lamp
definition: Glow discharge source of spectral lines of an atom in which the cathode is made of the desired element.

name: incident power
definition: Power supplied by a generator to the plasma.

name: inductively-coupled plasma
definition: Plasma produced by induction by means of a high-frequency (about \(\pu{2500 Hz}\)) electromagnetic field. The region of gas at high temperature and free from the field is taken as the region of observation.

name: inductively-coupled plasma spectrometry
definition: Measurement method of atomic spectroscopy that uses an inductively-coupled plasma to excite and ionize atoms.

name: inductively-coupled plasma mass spectrometry
definition: Measurement method of atomic spectrometry that uses an inductively-coupled plasma to excite and ionize atoms with measurement of the number and kind of ions in the plasma using mass spectrometry.

name: inductively-coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy
definition: Measurement method of atomic spectroscopy that uses an inductively-coupled plasma to excite and ionize atoms with measurement of the number and kind of ions in the plasma from their emission of electromagnetic radiation (see optical emission spectroscopy).

name: inductively-coupled plasma robustness
definition: Ability of an inductively-coupled plasma to withstand slight modification in the operating conditions and/or matrix composition with no significant changes in its fundamental characteristics (i.e., temperatures, electron number density) or the analytical figures of merit (i.e., sensitivity, detection limits or signal-to-noise ratio)

name: inductively-coupled plasma thermal pinch
definition: Decrease in the inductively-coupled plasma volume normally caused when an organic volatile solution is delivered to it. Organic vapours diffuse towards the outermost area of the plasma and its volume decreases.

name: inductively-coupled plasma torch
definition: Quartz component of an inductively-coupled plasma spectrometer where the plasma is generated and stabilized.

name: initial plasma radiation zone
definition: Inductively-coupled plasma volume in inductively-coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy where the analytically-relevant light emission begins to be observed.

name: interference curve
definition: Graph of absorbance or intensity plotted as a function of the concentration of an interfering element in an atomic spectroscopy experiment.

name: inverse Bremsstrahlung
definition: Absorption of photon energy by free electrons.

name: ionic cloud
definition: Gas phase containing free ions of analyte.

name: laser ablation
definition: Removal of material as an aerosol from a surface on irradiation by a laser beam.

name: laser induced breakdown spectroscopy
definition: Measurement method of atomic spectroscopy that uses a focused laser beam to ablate, atomize and excite atoms from a sample surface with subsequent measurement of the generated electromagnetic radiation.

name: laser-induced breakdown spectrum
definition: Emission spectrum generated as a consequence of the decay of the excited states generated in a laser-induced plasma that consists of a continuous background and element-specific atomic or ionic lines and molecular bands.

name: laser-induced plasma
definition: Local plasma formed by the interaction between a laser beam and a solid sample and initiated by the production of primary electrons by multiphoton ionization and thermionic photoemission mechanisms.

name: line-broadening
definition: Increase in the theoretical width of a spectral line owing to thermal motion of emitting atoms (Doppler effect), to electric field (Stark effect), to self-absorption and to pressure (Lorentz effect).

name: line profile
definition: Graph of the variation of emitted radiation intensity as a function of wavelength (emission line) or the variation of the absorption factor as a function of wavelength (absorption line).

name: low sample consumption system
definition: Liquid-sample introduction system to an inductively-coupled plasma spectrometer adapted to work at sample flow rates below \(\pu{100 \upmu L min-1}\).

name: measurement efficiency
definition: Number of detector events per atom in the sample.

name: microwave cavity
definition: Resonant cavity that permits focusing a microwave field inside a discharge tube thus giving rise to a standing wave.

name: microwave-induced plasma
definition: Plasma generated in a microwave cavity.

name: nebulization
definition: Conversion of a liquid into an aerosol consisting of droplets suspended in a gas stream.

name: nebulizer
definition: Device for producing nebulization.

name: non-specific emission or attenuation
definition: Electromagnetic radiation, within the bandpass filter used, emitted by, or absorption caused by, atoms, molecules and radicals that are subject to the atomizer by all components, apart from the analyte, that are present there during measurement.

name: normal plasma analytical zone
definition: Inductively-coupled plasma volume mainly responsible for emission of analytically-useful light because processes leading to excited species, such as droplet desolvation, element vaporization, atomization (or ionization) and excitation have been completed.

name: optical emission spectroscopy
definition: Measurement principle of atomic emission spectroscopy in which the emitted electromagnetic radiation is in the range of frequencies from the infrared, through visible, to the ultra-violet region.

name: overall efficiency of atomization
definition: In atomic spectroscopy, mass of analyte converted into free atoms in the atomizer divided by mass of analyte entering the dispersion device.

name: Penning excitation
definition: Collisional excitation and ionization mechanism of inductively-coupled plasma spectrometry involving analyte atoms and metastable argon atoms.

name: percentage transmission
definition: In atomic spectroscopy, flux of mass of sample divided by the flux of mass of solvent blank, measured under the same conditions, expressed as a percentage.

name: permanent modifier
definition: Substance added together with the sample or standards in electrothermal atomic absorption spectroscopy that is refractory, or forms a refractory species (e.g., a carbide), and thus does not need to be renewed for several atomization cycles.

name: plasma arc
definition: Plasma formed by an arc-discharge.

name: plasma excitation temperature
definition: Temperature governing the number density of atomic species in their ground state and excited states following a Boltzmann distribution.

name: plasma gases
definition: Gas streams used to maintain and stabilize the inductively-coupled plasma. The external stream is the main constituent of the plasma and confines the plasma avoiding melting of the torch walls; the intermediate gas stream keeps the plasma at a given height above the top of the torch and, the central stream carries the aerosol and promotes its injection in the plasma central channel.

name: plasma induction zone
definition: Inductively-coupled plasma volume where there is a maximum interaction between the electromagnetic field and the plasma gas (mostly argon). This is the plasma’s hottest area and has a toroidal configuration.

name: plasma ionization temperature
definition: Temperature associated with the energy level of plasma ions.

name: plasma local thermodynamic equilibrium
definition: Condition for which the temperatures estimated from different particles (atoms, molecules, ions, electrons) constituting a plasma are locally coincident.

name: plasma shielding
definition: Prevention of laser pulse energy from reaching a sample surface as a result of the presence of a laser-induced plasma.

name: plasma termination
definition: Extinction of the plasma after a laser pulse as a consequence of self-absorption (quenching) and recombination of electrons and ions.

name: platform atomization
definition: Sample support made of graphite that is inserted into the atomizer tube in electrothermal atomic absorption spectroscopy. The sample, a liquid or a solid, is deposited onto this platform, from which it undergoes all the transformations leading to atomization. The use of a platform delays atomization, until a more stabilized temperature in the gas phase is reached.

name: pneumatic nebulizers
definition: Nebulizers for which the aerosol generation principle is based on the exposure of the liquid sample to a high velocity gas stream.

name: preheating inductively-coupled plasma zone
definition: Inductively-coupled plasma volume where tertiary aerosols suffer from complete solvent evaporation, element salt vaporization and dissociation into atoms.

name: primary aerosol
definition: Aerosol generated by a nebulizer.

name: pulse energy
definition: Total optical energy content of a laser pulse. Integral of optical power over pulse duration.

name: pulsed laser
definition: Laser system that emits electromagnetic radiation in the form of pulses of a defined and constant duration.

name: pyrolysis curve
definition: Graph of absorbance against pyrolysis temperature in electrothermal atomic absorption spectroscopy.

name: quartz atomizer
definition: Atomizer that is used to atomize those elements that form volatile species (e.g., hydrides) at relatively low temperatures (e.g., \(\pu{1000^{\circ}C}\) or below).

name: radial viewing mode
definition: Inductively-coupled plasma optical emission spectrometer configuration in which the plasma and the entrance slit are perpendicular and from which the signal is taken perpendicularly to the main plasma axis.

name: radiofrequency generator
definition: Component of an inductively-coupled plasma spectrometer responsible for the generation of alternating current in the radiofrequency portion of the electromagnetic spectrum (see table).

name: radiofrequency glow discharge optical emission spectroscopy
definition: Optical emission spectroscopy in which a radiofrequency-powered glow discharge is operated with frequencies in the low megahertz range.

name: reference flux density
definition: Intensity transmitted by the reference medium in a double-beam spectrometer.

name: reflected power
definition: Incident power that is not absorbed by the plasma.

name: repetition rate
definition: Number of laser pulses emitted by a pulsed laser system per unit time.

name: resonant inelastic X-ray scattering
definition: Measurement method of inelastic X-ray spectroscopy that uses a hard or soft X-ray beam to excite transitions of core-level electrons into empty energy levels. The subsequent transition of an electron into the core state is accompanied by X-ray emission with characteristic momentum and energy.

name: Saha’s ionization equation
definition: Equation that relates the ionization state of an element present in a gas in thermal equilibrium to the temperature and the pressure of the medium.

name: sample flux density
definition: Intensity transmitted by the atomizer when the latter is supplied with the sample solution or a reference solution.

name: saturator
definition: Buffer containing interfering element(s) in sufficient quantity to reach the limit of enhancement or dispersion (i.e., saturation) of the interference curve.

name: sequential detection
definition: Sequential spectrometers use a dispersive element (grating) in combination with entrance and exit slits for selection of specific wavelengths. Geometric arrangements include the Czerny-Turner and the Ebert-geometry, both offering high resolution measurements. However, they do not permit simultaneous recording of different spectral lines, even for single emission line intensity, and adjacent spectral background has also to be measured sequentially.

name: solvent blank flux density
definition: Intensity transmitted by the atomizer when the latter is supplied with the solvent blank.

name: solvent nucleation
definition: Solvent condensation on solid particles or droplets contained in an aerosol.

name: solvent transport rate
definition: Mass of solvent, both in liquid and vapour forms, reaching an inductively-coupled plasma per unit of time.

name: spectral background
definition: Electromagnetic radiation, within the bandpass used, emitted by, and/or in the case of atomic absorption spectroscopy, absorbed in, the atomizer when nothing is supplied to the atomizer but the gases involved in its operation.

name: spectral line
definition: In atomic spectroscopy, a very narrow band of frequencies of electromagnetic radiation emitted or absorbed by atoms, which undergo a single electronic transition.

name: spray chamber
definition: Chamber of a nebulizer in which the sprayed liquid is converted to mist. Some of the droplets of this mist may evaporate, coalesce, or deposit in the chamber and subsequently drain away as waste.

name: sputter rate
definition: Mass of material removed from a sample surface in unit time.

name: stop-flow conditions
definition: Stoppage to the otherwise constant flow of argon gas to the atomizer in electrothermal atomic absorption spectroscopy, that can be programmed to occur during atomization, for the purpose of increasing the residence time of the analyte atoms and thus the associated signal.

name: synchrotron X-ray spectroscopy
definition: X-ray spectroscopy performed using a high intensity, continuous polychromatic synchrotron X-ray source.

name: tertiary aerosol
definition: Aerosol that reaches an inductively-coupled plasma.

name: thermal dispersion
definition: Procedures whereby an aerosol is produced at a high temperature, for example by sparks, arcs, furnaces, lasers, cathodic sputtering or electron-beam.

name: thermal volatilization
definition: Process in glow-discharge atomic emission spectroscopy in which sample volatilization occurs by heating due to sample bombardment with argon ions.

name: time-resolved laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy
definition: Measurement method of laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy in which the emitted radiation is monitored with time resolution sufficiently high to resolve different stages in the lifetime of the laser-induced plasma.

name: total sample consumption system
definition: Liquid-sample introduction system able to achieve \(\pu{100\%}\) transport efficiency.

name: transport efficiency
definition: Mass of analyte entering the atomizer of a flame atomic spectrometer or the plasma of an inductively-coupled plasma spectrometer divided by the mass of analyte entering the dispersion device.

name: ultrasonic nebulizers
definition: Nebulizers whose aerosol generation principle is based on the transfer of the energy from a vibrating transducer to the liquid sample.

name: wall atomization
definition: Electrothermal atomic absorption spectroscopy in which the sample is deposited directly onto the wall of the electrothermal atomizer tube, from which it undergoes all the transformations leading to atomization.

name: wash out time
definition: Time required for the output signal of an inductively-coupled plasma spectrometer for a given analyte to fall back to baseline levels from the end of sampling time and/or after introducing a blank solution.

name: X-ray emission spectrum
definition: Spectrum comprising the continuum Bremsstrahlung and the most energetic characteristic spectral lines defined by differences in binding energy between electron energy levels.

name: amorphous material transmitting infrared radiation
definition: Amorphous glasses made from elements of groups 4, 5 and 6 of the Periodic Table that transmit infrared radiation.

name: amplitude modulation
definition: Modulation of the amplitude of a beam of electromagnetic radiation; by the movement of a moving mirror in a rapid scan Fourier-transform spectrometer or by a mechanical chopper in other spectrometers.

name: anisotropic Raman scattering
definition: Raman scattering by the anisotropic part of the derived polarizability tensor.

name: anomalous dispersion
definition: Changes in real refractive index of a material in the vicinity of an absorption band in which real refractive index decreases markedly with decreasing wavenumber on the high wavenumber side of an absorption band, then increases rapidly through the band centre and decreases markedly on the low wavenumber side of the band, before resuming normal dispersion at wavenumbers far from the band.

name: anomalously polarized Raman band
definition: Raman band with a depolarization ratio greater than \(\pu{0.75}\), as is frequently observed in surface-enhanced resonance Raman spectroscopy.

name: anti-Stokes Raman scattering
definition: Raman scattering of electromagnetic radiation in which the scattered radiation has greater energy (greater wavenumber) than the exciting radiation.

name: asymmetric top
definition: Rotor whose three principal moments of inertia are all different.

name: atomic polar tensor
definition: 3 × 3 tensor that gives the change in the components of the molecular dipole moment when the atom is displaced in three-dimensional space.

name: attenuated total reflection spectroscopy
definition: Measurement method of vibrational spectroscopy based on internal reflection from an absorbing material at angles of incidence at or above the critical angle (attenuated total reflection).
synonyms: frustrated total internal reflection spectroscopy|internal reflection spectroscopy (IRS)

name: band shape
definition: Description of the profile of a spectral band.

name: Bragg filter
definition: Optical filter used, for example, to attenuate Rayleigh scattering while transmitting light subject to Raman shift.

name: centre burst
definition: Spectral region of an interferogram around zero-path-difference where intensity is greatest.

name: Christiansen effect
definition: Collections of solid particles that are transparent to electromagnetic radiation of a particular wavelength and are slightly larger than the wavelength of the radiation transmit poorly due to reflection and scattering from the interfaces. The transmission increases markedly at wavenumbers at which the refractive index of the particles is close to that of the surrounding medium.

name: Christiansen filter
definition: Optical filter based on the Christiansen effect.

name: coherent anti-Stokes Raman spectroscopy
definition: Measurement method of Raman spectroscopy that uses third-order susceptibility and is one of several four-wave mixing spectroscopies. The excitation is through lasers of wavenumber \(\tilde{ u}_{1}\) and \(\tilde{ u}_{2}\), which coincide spatially and temporally in the sample and produce an output laser of wavenumber \(\tilde{ u}_{3} = 2\tilde{ u}_{1} - \tilde{ u}_{2}\).

name: combination transition
definition: Transition in which more than one vibration changes its degree of excitation; i.e., in which more than one vibrational quantum number changes.

name: continuous scan interferometer
definition: Interferometer in which the optical path difference is continually changed.

name: Coriolis coupling
definition: Coupling between rotational and vibrational molecular motion caused by Coriolis forces.

name: Coriolis force
definition: In vibrational theory, the motion of a polyatomic molecule is usually initially regarded as the independent superposition of a rotation and a vibration, with the vibration considered in a coordinate system that rotates with the molecule. This initial treatment must be corrected for centrifugal forces and for Coriolis forces. The Coriolis force on an atom is given by \(F_{\rm{Coriolis}} = 2m v_{\rm{a}} \omega \sin \varphi\), where \(m\) is the mass of the atom, \(v_{\rm{a}}\) is its apparent velocity in the rotating coordinate system, \(\omega\) is the angular velocity of the coordinate system, and \(\varphi\) is the angle between the velocity vector and the axis of rotation.

name: critical angle
definition: Smallest angle of incidence at which total internal reflection occurs.

name: deformation vibration
definition: Vibration in which the dominant change from equilibrium is in one or more valence angles.

name: depolarization ratio
definition: Raman intensity with the electric vector of the scattered electromagnetic radiation perpendicular to that of the incident radiation divided by the Raman intensity with electric vectors parallel.

name: depolarized Raman band
definition: Raman band with depolarization ratio \(\rho = 0.75\) for linear polarized incident radiation in normal Raman spectroscopy.

name: difference transition
definition: Combination transition that does not start at the ground state and in which at least one vibration decreases and at least one vibration increases its degree of excitation; i.e., a transition in which more than one vibrational quantum number changes and at least one becomes smaller.

name: divided spinning cell
definition: Measuring instrument for Raman spectroscopy incorporating a dish-shaped cell that is divided by a vertical partition through its middle to allow different liquids in its two halves. It is rotated about a vertical axis through its centre and the Raman scattered radiation from each half is measured alternately. With a standard liquid in one half and a sample in the other it is used to determine Raman scattering intensities relative to the standard.

name: dynamic spectrum
definition: Spectrum of a material under the influence of an applied external perturbation represented by a variable \(\tau\), relative to a reference spectrum.

name: electrical anharmonicity
definition: Influence of terms that are of \(2^{\rm{nd}}\) and higher order in the normal coordinate \(Q\) in the expansion of the electric dipole moment.

name: electrical harmonicity
definition: Influence of the linear term, \(\Sigma_{k} (\partial \boldsymbol{\mu}/\partial Q_{k}) Q_{k}\), in the expansion of the electric dipole moment. \(Q\) is the normal coordinate.

name: electron energy loss spectroscopy
definition: Measurement method of vibrational spectroscopy in which a constant-energy beam of electrons passes through or is reflected from a sample and the energy distribution in the transmitted or reflected beam is analysed to give a spectrum of number of electrons against electron energy loss.

name: electro-optic parameter
definition: Characteristic quantity used in the analysis of absolute infrared intensity data chosen on the assumption that the electric dipole moment of the molecule can be described as the vector sum of bond dipole moments.

name: ellipticity
definition: Degree to which linearly polarized incident electromagnetic radiation becomes elliptically polarized in an absorbing optically active medium. \[\tan\;\psi = (E_{\rm{R}} - E_{\rm{L}})/(E_{\rm{R}} + E_{\rm{L}}) = \tanh (k^{\rm{L}} - k^{\rm{R}})\pi l/\lambda\] where \(E_{\rm{R}}\) and \(E_{\rm{L}}\) are the electric vectors of right and left circularly polarized radiation, \(k^{\rm{L}}\) and \(k^{\rm{R}}\) are the absorption indices of the sample for left and right circularly polarized radiation, \(\lambda\) is the wavelength of the radiation and \(l\) is the path-length through the medium.

name: evanescent wave
definition: Part of a standing-wave normal to a reflecting surface that extends beyond the reflecting surface when an electromagnetic wave undergoes total internal reflection.

name: Evans hole
definition: Unexpected minimum or hole in a broad absorption band due to a gap being created in a broad distribution of states by Fermi resonance.

name: excitation profile
definition: Graph of Raman intensity at the desired Raman shift against wavenumber of the excitation.

name: external reflection spectroscopy
definition: Measurement method of spectroscopy in which radiation is reflected from a sample of higher refractive index than that of the incident medium.

name: extraordinary wave
definition: In a uniaxial crystal electromagnetic radiation with electric vector oblique to the optic axis and which does not obey the normal laws of refraction.

name: Fermi resonance
definition: Cubic anharmonic resonance (see anharmonicity), i.e., any interaction caused by cubic terms in the vibrational potential energy.

name: finesse
definition: Free spectral range divided by resolution.

name: fingerprint bands
definition: Infrared and Raman bands that are characteristic of a particular molecule rather than a functional group.

name: fingerprint region
definition: Region of a spectrum that contains fingerprint bands as well as bands with characteristic group frequencies.

name: Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy
definition: Infrared spectroscopy in which a Fourier-transform spectrometer is used to separate the transmitted electromagnetic radiation into its component wavenumbers.

name: Fourier-transform Raman spectroscopy
definition: Raman spectroscopy in which a Fourier-transform spectrometer is used to separate the scattered electromagnetic radiation into its component wavenumbers.

name: free spectral range
definition: For a Fabry-Perot or laser cavity, wavenumber interval between successive longitudinal cavity modes of vibration; \(\Delta \tilde{ u} = 1/(2nl)\), where \(l\) is the cavity spacing and \(n\) is the refractive index of the material in the cavity.

name: grazing incidence
definition: Angle of incidence of a beam of electromagnetic radiation greater than \(\pu{70\!^{\circ}}\).

name: group frequency
definition: Frequency in vibrational spectroscopy that is characteristic of a particular chemical functional group.

name: harmonic constant
definition: Coefficient of (\( u + ½\)) in the vibrational term value, determined by the harmonic terms in the vibrational potential energy.

name: homogeneous line-broadening
definition: Line-broadening by mechanisms that affect every molecule of the same species in the sample in the same way.

name: hot transition
definition: Electronic transition between an excited state and a state in which all vibrational quantum numbers are the same or greater.

name: hyper-Raman spectroscopy
definition: Raman spectroscopy in which scattering occurs through hyperpolarizabilities. A two-photon technique in which an intense pulsed beam of electromagnetic radiation is focused onto the sample. When sufficient power is present in the pulse, two photons may interact with the one molecule to create a virtual state at double the frequency of the laser excitation. Raman scattering from this virtual state to an excited vibrational state of the ground state then occurs.

name: hyperspectral imaging
definition: Measurement method to obtain information about the spatial composition of a sample by obtaining a spectrum at each spatially resolved point of the sample.

name: improper rotation axis
definition: In spectroscopy, a rotation-reflection axis, which is a symmetry element such that rotation by \(2\pi/n\) about the axis followed by reflection through a plane perpendicular to the axis transforms an object into itself.

name: inelastic electron tunnelling spectroscopy
definition: Measurement method of vibrational spectroscopy to obtain spectra of molecules on metal oxide surfaces.

name: infrared radiation
definition: Electromagnetic radiation of wavelength between approximately \(\pu{780 nm}\) and \(\pu{1000 \upmu m}\) or of wavenumber between approximately \(\pu{13000 cm-1}\) and \(\pu{10 cm-1}\).

name: infrared spectroscopy
definition: Measurement principle of vibrational spectroscopy using infrared radiation.

name: inhomogeneous broadening
definition: Line-broadening by mechanisms that arise from an ensemble of spectroscopically non-equivalent molecules of the same species. Such molecules exist, for example, when molecules occupy non-equivalent sites in a condensed phase, and when gaseous molecules have different velocities and, thus, shift the observed wavenumber differently through the Doppler effect.

name: interference fringes
definition: Sinusoidal intensity variation due to interference of electromagnetic radiation that undergoes multiple reflection between two flat and parallel surfaces.

name: interference record
definition: Record of the signal from the detector of a two-beam interferometer as the optical path difference between the two beams is varied.

name: interferogram
definition: Pattern formed by wave interference produced by an interferometer, especially one represented on a screen or chart recorder.

name: internal reflection
definition: Reflection of electromagnetic radiation from a material of lesser refractive index than that of the incident medium.

name: internal reflection element
definition: Transparent or semi-transparent material of high refractive index that carries infrared radiation to a sample in internal reflection and attenuated total reflection measurements.

name: inverse Raman scattering
definition: Raman scattering showing absorption when Stokes Raman scattering exceeds anti-Stokes Raman scattering, in an experiment in which a sample is simultaneously illuminated by coincident beams from a continuum source and a pulse laser at \(\tilde{ u}_{0}\). Energy is absorbed from the continuum at \(\tilde{ u}_{0} + \tilde{ u}_{\rm{s}}\) where \(\tilde{ u}_{\rm{s}}\) is the wavenumber of a Raman-active vibration in the sample that is excited by this process, and this energy is emitted at \(\tilde{ u}_{0}\).

name: inverse spatially offset Raman spectroscopy
definition: Variant of spatially offset Raman spectroscopy in which a sample is illuminated with a ring of laser light and the Raman scattering is collected from the centre of the ring.

name: IRTRAN™
definition: Kinds of crystal transparent to infrared radiation used as windows and filters in infrared spectroscopy.

name: Jacquinot stop
definition: Aperture in the optics of a Fourier-transform spectrometer, typically between the source and the interferometer, designed to be the limiting aperture when no other optical element such as the detector serves this purpose.

name: kinetic coupling
definition: Coupling of vibrational displacements through terms in the vibrational kinetic energy.

name: KRS-5
definition: Eutectic (\(\pu{42 \% TlBr, 58 \% TlI}\)) mixture of thallium bromide and thallium iodide transparent to infrared radiation used as window in infrared spectroscopy.

name: Kubelka–Munk function
definition: \(f(R_{\infty}) = (1 – R_{\infty})^{2}/2R_{\infty}\), where \(R_{\infty}\) is the diffuse reflectance from a sample of infinite depth.

name: lifetime broadening
definition: Homogeneous line-broadening due to the limited lifetime of energy states involved in a transition.

name: local mode
definition: Mode of vibration localized in one type of bond.

name: local molar polarizability
definition: Defined under the assumption of the Lorentz local field by the Lorentz-Lorenz formula: \[\hat{\alpha}_{\rm{m}}(\tilde{ u}) = 3V_{\rm{m}}\epsilon_{0} \frac{\hat{\epsilon}(\tilde{ u}) - 1}{\hat{\epsilon}(\tilde{ u}) + 2} = 3V_{\rm{m}}{\epsilon}_{0}\,\frac{\hat{n}^{2}(\tilde{ u}) - 1}{\hat{n}^{2}(\tilde{ u}) + 2}\] where \(V_{\rm{m}}\) is the molar volume and \(\hat{\epsilon}\) and \(\boldsymbol{\hat{n}}\) are the complex dielectric constant and refractive index, respectively. To allow description of absorption, \(\hat{\alpha}_{\rm{m}}(\tilde{ u})\) is complex: \(\hat{\alpha}_{\rm{m}}(\tilde{ u}) = \alpha_{\rm{m}}'(\tilde{ u}) + \rm{i}\alpha_{\rm{m}}''(\tilde{ u})\).

name: mechanical anharmonicity
definition: Influence of cubic and higher-order terms in vibrational potential energy.

name: mechanical harmonicity
definition: Influence of quadratic terms in vibrational potential energy.

name: molar ellipticity
definition: Ellipticity divided by the amount concentration of the optically active absorbing material and by the path-length at temperature (\(t\)) and wavelength (\(\lambda\)).

name: multiplex advantage
definition: Decrease in measurement uncertainty obtained by measuring intensity at many different wavelengths simultaneously, as is done, for example, in Fourier-transform spectroscopy.

name: natural linewidth
definition: Line width of a molecular spectral band that arises from the probability of spontaneous emission in the absence of radiation fields and interaction with other molecules or entities.

name: near-infrared radiation
definition: Infrared radiation of which vacuum wavenumbers range from approximately \(\pu{12800 cm-1}\) to \(\pu{4800 cm-1}\) and wavelengths range from approximately \(\pu{780 nm}\) to \(\pu{2500 nm}\).

name: non-dispersive infrared spectroscopies
definition: Kinds of infrared spectroscopy in which the effect of the sample on the radiation from the source is measured as a whole without exploring the dependence on wavenumber.

name: normal coordinate
definition: Formal mathematical description of a normal vibration. When the potential energy, \(V\), is harmonic and the kinetic energy, \(T\), is calculated in the limit of infinitesimally small displacements, the normal coordinates are defined as independent entities such that '(for non-linear molecules)'\[V = ½\sum_{k=1}^{3N-6}\lambda_{k}Q_{k}^{2}\ {\rm{and}}\ T = ½\sum_{k=1}^{3N-6}\dot Q_{k}^{2}\]where \(\lambda_{k}\) is the \(k^{\rm{th}}\) eigenvalue and \(\dot {Q}\) is \(\partial Q/\partial t\). Normal coordinate \(Q_{k}\) is related to the internal displacement coordinates, \(R_{i}\), through the elements, \(L_{ik} = \partial R_{i}/\partial Q_{k}\) of the \(k^{\rm{th}}\) column of the eigenvector matrix \(\boldsymbol{L}\). Normal coordinates are not independent when the potential energy is anharmonic, or the displacements are not infinitesimal.

name: normal coordinate analysis
definition: Calculation of the normal modes of vibrations of a molecule or crystal under the assumptions that the potential energy is harmonic and the displacements from equilibrium are infinitesimal.

name: normal dispersion of the refractive index
definition: Slow decrease of real refractive index of a material in a non-absorbing spectral region far from regions of strong absorption as the wavenumber decreases.

name: normal incidence
definition: Incidence of a beam of electromagnetic radiation when the angle of incidence \(\theta = \pu{0\!^{\circ}}\), i.e., the incident radiation beam is normal to the surface.

name: normal mode
definition: One of the \(3N - 6\) (\(3N - 5\) for a linear molecule) modes of vibration that would add to give the total vibrational motion in a molecule if the interatomic potential were strictly quadratic in the displacements from equilibrium.

name: normalized tunnelling intensity
definition: Second differential of intensity with respect to bias voltage divided by first differential of intensity with respect to bias voltage.

name: optical absorption depth
definition: Depth in a sample at which the intensity of an incident beam is reduced to \(1/\rm{e}\) of its value at the surface of the sample.

name: optical constants
definition: Collective name for the real refractive index, \(n\) and the absorption index (imaginary refractive index), \(k\).

name: optical null double beam spectrometer
definition: Spectrometer in which the ratio of the radiant power in the two beams at each wavenumber is measured opto-mechanically by inserting a linear optical attenuator into the reference beam until the two signals measured by the detector are equal, then measuring the displacement of the optical attenuator.
synonyms: NTI double beam spectrometer|null-balance double beam spectrometer

name: optical path difference
definition: Path-length difference between the arms of a two-beam interferometer.

name: optical rotatory dispersion
definition: Wavelength dependence of the angle of rotation of the plane of linearly-polarized radiation when transmitted through optically active materials.

name: ordinary wave
definition: In a uniaxial crystal electromagnetic radiation with electric vector perpendicular to the optic axis and which obeys the normal laws of refraction.

name: overtone transition
definition: Transition between the ground state and a state in which a single mode of vibration is multiply excited.

name: pATR spectrum
definition: \(-\log_{10}\) of the spectrum obtained in attenuated total reflection spectroscopy.

name: photoacoustic saturation
definition: Condition in photoacoustic spectroscopy in which all bands with greater than a certain absorption intensity appear to have the same intensity.

name: photothermal spectroscopy
definition: Measurement method of spectroscopy in which the absorption of electromagnetic radiation by a sample is detected as a result of the heat generated by the absorption.

name: polarized Raman band
definition: Raman band with depolarization ratio \(\rho \le 0.75\) for linear polarized incident radiation in normal Raman spectroscopy.

name: potential coupling
definition: Coupling of vibrational displacements through terms in the vibrational potential energy. The second-order (quadratic) terms cause harmonic potential coupling while the cubic and higher terms cause anharmonic potential coupling.

name: p-polarization
definition: Polarization when electromagnetic radiation is incident upon a surface with its electric vector in the plane of incidence and, therefore, inclined to the reflecting surface unless the incidence is normal.

name: pressure broadening
definition: Increase in the line width of a spectral line of a gas due to molecular collisions and other intermolecular interactions that reduce the lifetime of an excited state.

name: quantum cascade laser
definition: Laser that emits mid-infrared radiation.

name: Raman band
definition: Spectral band in Raman spectroscopy.

name: Raman optical activity
definition: Phenomenon that vibrations in chiral molecules and materials Raman scattering right circularly polarized incident radiation to a different extent than left circularly polarized incident radiation.

name: Raman scattering
definition: Inelastic scattering of electromagnetic radiation by molecules that are excited to higher energy levels.

name: Raman shift
definition: Difference in wavenumber between the incident and scattered electromagnetic radiation in Raman spectroscopy.

name: Raman spectroscopy
definition: Measurement principle of vibrational spectroscopy based on Raman scattering.

name: Raman spectrum
definition: Graph of the intensity of scattered electromagnetic radiation in Raman spectroscopy against Raman shift.

name: Raman wavenumber shift
definition: Wavenumber of exciting electromagnetic radiation minus wavenumber of the scattered radiation.

name: rapid-scan Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy
definition: Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy in which the optical path difference is continually changed at a rate of \(\pu{0.05 cm s-1}\) or greater.

name: reflection-absorption at grazing incidence
definition: Reflection-absorption with very thin layers of an absorbing material on a metallic substrate and the angle of incidence between \(\pu{70\!^{\circ}}\) and \(\pu{90\!^{\circ}}\).

name: resonance Raman scattering
definition: Raman scattering that occurs through the polarizability of a molecule, (not the hyperpolarizabilities) and is excited by electromagnetic radiation that is in resonance with electronic transitions or vibronic transitions in the sample.

name: rotational branch
definition: Spectral lines in the rotation-vibration spectrum of a gas that derive from the same change in rotation quantum number, \(J\).

name: rotation-vibration spectrum
definition: Spectrum that shows absorption or emission of radiation during transitions between rotational-vibrational states of a molecule.

name: scattering geometry
definition: Relation between the propagation directions, \(k_{\rm{i}}\), \(k_{\rm{s}}\), and the polarization directions, \(p_{\rm{i}}\), \(p_{\rm{s}}\), of the incident and scattered radiation, usually expressed in terms of laboratory-fixed or crystal-fixed Cartesian axes.

name: site splitting
definition: Appearance of more than one band in the spectrum of a crystal when only one is seen in that of the gas, when this splitting is attributed to either the molecule lying on a crystal site of lower symmetry than that of the gaseous molecule or to molecules occupying more than one type of crystal site. See crystal field splitting.

name: spatially offset Raman spectroscopy
definition: Measurement method of Raman spectroscopy in which the sample is illuminated at one location, and the Raman signal is collected from a different location on the sample surface.

name: spherical top
definition: Molecule whose three principal moments of inertia are all the same. An isotropic molecule.

name: step-scan interferometer
definition: Interferometer (typically used for Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy) in which the optical path difference is changed by a certain amount, held constant, or modulated if phase modulation is desired, while the signal at the current path difference is recorded, then the process is repeated.

name: stimulated Raman scattering
definition: Two-photon Raman scattering occurs when a picosecond pump beam is used to create a virtual state and a probe beam of a frequency to match the frequency of Stokes Raman scattering from the virtual state to a specific vibrational level. The Stokes emission is stimulated thus depopulating the virtual state very quickly and increasing the scattering efficiency for the chosen vibration by orders of magnitude. SRS is a non-linear process, so sufficient photons from both the pump and probe beams must be present on the molecule at the one time.

name: Stokes–Raman scattering
definition: Raman scattering of electromagnetic radiation in which the scattered radiation has lesser energy (lesser wavenumber) than the exciting radiation.

name: sum band
definition: Band resulting from a sum transition.

name: sum transition
definition: Combination transition between the ground state and a state in which more than one vibration is excited; i.e., a transition from the ground state in which more than one quantum number increases.

name: sum-frequency spectroscopy
definition: Nonlinear optical technique in which pulsed lasers at frequencies \(\omega_{1}\) and \(\omega_{2}\) are overlapped at a surface and light emitted at the sum of the two frequencies, \(\omega_{1} + \omega_{2}\), is detected. One laser is normally in the mid-infrared and the other in the visible or near-infrared.

name: surface-enhanced hyper-Raman spectroscopy
definition: Measurement method of Raman spectroscopy by which the Raman spectrum is significantly enhanced simultaneously by both the hyper-Raman (see hyper-Raman spectroscopy) and surface-enhanced Raman (see surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy) effects.

name: surface-enhanced infrared absorption
definition: Measurement method of infrared spectroscopy by which the intensity of absorption bands of molecules within a few nanometers of the surface of metal particles is increased by interactions with surface plasmons (the collective resonance of electrons near the surface of metal islands).

name: surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy
definition: Measurement method of Raman spectroscopy by which the intensity of vibrational bands in the Raman spectra of molecules within a few nanometers of the surface of microscopically rough metals, metal colloids and metal nanoparticles is increased by several orders of magnitude.

name: surface-enhanced resonance Raman spectroscopy
definition: Measurement method of surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) by which the Raman spectrum is significantly enhanced when the conditions occur that whilst undergoing SERS the molecules are excited by radiation that is in resonance with electronic transitions in the sample.

name: surface-enhanced, spatially offset Raman spectroscopy
definition: Measurement method of Raman spectroscopy that combines spatially offset Raman spectroscopy and surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) enabling the detection of a SERS signal deep within diffusely scattering samples.

name: symmetric
definition: Term used in at least two senses in vibrational spectroscopy. In general usage, a symmetric molecule is a molecule with high symmetry. In more specific usage, a property is symmetric with respect to a symmetry element if it remains unchanged by the action of the corresponding symmetry operation.

name: symmetric top
definition: Molecule that has two equal principal moments of inertia with the third one different.

name: symmetry coordinate
definition: Each \(S_{i}\) is a linear combination of general coordinates, usually internal coordinates, constructed to take advantage of the molecular symmetry. The \(S_{i}\) are elements of the vector \(\boldsymbol{S}\). They have the same units as the general coordinates from which they were constructed.

name: symmorphic space group
definition: Space group that does not contain screw-axes and glide planes.

name: thermal diffusion depth
definition: In photoacoustic spectroscopy, \(L = \sqrt{(D/\pi f)}\), where \(D\) is thermal diffusivity and \(f\) is modulation frequency of the electromagnetic radiation.

name: thermal diffusivity
definition: Thermal conductivity divided by the product of the specific heat and the density.

name: thermal wave decay coefficient
definition: Reciprocal of the thermal diffusion depth (\(L\)). \(a_{\rm{s}} = 1/L\).

name: tip-enhanced Raman spectroscopy
definition: Measurement method of Raman spectroscopy combining surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy and scanning using an atomic force microscope or scanning tunnelling microscope to give complementary maps of a surface.

name: total internal reflection
definition: Internal reflection from a non-absorbing material at angles of incidence at or above the critical angle.

name: transflectance
definition: Spectral intensity of a transflected beam divided by spectral intensity of the incident beam in a transflection experiment.

name: transflection
definition: Reflection absorption at near-normal incidence when the thickness of the absorbing medium is large enough to yield an interpretable spectrum. The substrate is usually a mirror for mid-infrared measurements and a ceramic disk for near-infrared measurements. The angle of incidence is typically between \(\pu{0\!^{\circ}}\) and \(\pu{45\!^{\circ}}\).

name: transmission Raman spectroscopy
definition: Measurement method of Raman spectroscopy in which the sample is illuminated on one side and the Raman signal is collected from the opposite side.

name: vibrational circular dichroism
definition: Circular dichroism, \(k^{\rm{L}} – k^{\rm{R}}\), for vibrational transitions.

name: vibrational eigenvector
definition: Part of the solution of the matrix equation of normal coordinate analysis, \(\boldsymbol{G\!F\!L} = \boldsymbol{L \lambda}\). Each element \(L_{ik}\) of \(\boldsymbol{L}\) is a vibrational eigenvector, and gives the change in internal coordinate \(R_{i}\) during unit change in the normal coordinate \(Q_{k}\), as shown in matrix form by \(\boldsymbol{R} = \boldsymbol{LQ}\), i.e., \(L_{ik} = \partial R_{i}/\partial Q_{k}\). Eigenvectors are sometimes expressed in terms of symmetry coordinates or Cartesian coordinates.

name: vibrational kinetic energy
definition: Kinetic energy of the molecule as a function of the displacements of the atoms from equilibrium positions. For Cartesian displacement coordinates (\(x, y, z\)), \[T = \sum_{\alpha}½m_{\alpha}(\dot x_{\alpha}^{2} + \dot y_{\alpha}^{2} + \dot z_{\alpha}^{2})\] where the sum is over all atoms and \(\dot{x}_{\alpha}\), etc., are the displacement velocities. For internal coordinates \[T = ½\boldsymbol{P}^{t}\boldsymbol{GP} = ½\dot{\boldsymbol{R}}^{t}{\boldsymbol{G}}^{-1}\dot {\boldsymbol{R}} = ½\sum_{ij}G_{ij}^{-1}\dot R_{i}\dot R_{j}\] where \(\dot {\boldsymbol{R}}^{t}\) and \(\dot {\boldsymbol{R}}\) are the row and column vector, respectively, of the \(\partial R_{i}/\partial t\), \(\boldsymbol{P}^{t}\) and \(\boldsymbol{P}\) are the row and column vector, respectively, of the momenta conjugate to the \(R_{i}\), \(\boldsymbol{G}^{-1}\) is the inverse of the \(\boldsymbol{G}\) matrix and \(G_{ij}^{-1}\) is the \(ij^{\rm{th}}\) element of \(\boldsymbol{G}^{-1}\). The elements of the \(\boldsymbol{G}\) matrix are defined by \[G_{ij} = \sum_{\alpha} \frac{1}{m_{\alpha}} B_{i\alpha} B_{j\alpha}\] where \(B_{i\alpha}\) and \(B_{j\alpha}\) relate the \(i^{\rm{th}}\) and \(j^{\rm{th}}\) internal coordinate to the \(\alpha^{\rm{th}}\) Cartesian coordinate through the equation \(\boldsymbol{R} = \boldsymbol{BX}\) in which \(\boldsymbol{X}\) is the column vector of the Cartesian coordinates.

name: vibrational potential energy
definition: Potential energy of the molecule as a function of the displacements of the atoms from equilibrium positions. The harmonic terms are quadratic in the displacements and the anharmonic terms are of cubic, quartic and higher orders in the displacements. \(Q\) are normal coordinates \[2V = \sum\limits_{k}\lambda_{k}Q_{k}^{2} + \sum\limits_{ijk}k_{ijk}Q_{i}Q_{j}Q_{k} + higher\,order\,terms\] In terms of internal coordinates, \[2V = \sum\limits_{i} F_{ii} R_i^{2} + \sum\limits_{i,j e i} F_{ij} R_{i} R_{j} + \sum\limits_{i,j,k} F_{ijk} R_{i} R_{j} R_{k} + higher\,order\,terms\]

name: vibrational spectroscopy
definition: Measurement principle of spectroscopy to analyse molecular properties based on vibrations (bond stretching or deformation modes) in chemical species.

name: vibrational term value
definition: Vibrational energy, \(E\), expressed in wavenumber units. \(G = E/(hc)\), where \(h\) is the Planck constant and \(c\) is the speed of light in vacuum.

name: volume reflection
definition: Re-emergence of electromagnetic radiation from the surface of incidence after penetrating into a powdered sample.

name: absolute counting efficiency
definition: Number of particles or photons counted by a radiation detector divided by the number emitted by a radiation source.

name: accelerator mass spectrometry
definition: Mass spectrometry technique in which atoms and molecules from a sample are ionized, accelerated to mega-electron volt (\(\pu{1 MeV} = \pu{1.602176634E-13 J}\)) energies, and separated according to their momentum, charge, and energy, allowing high discrimination for the measurement of nuclide abundances.

name: activity growth curve
definition: Graph of the activity of a radioactive nuclide as a function of time and showing the increase of activity through the decay of the precursor or as a result of activation.

name: backscattering analysis
definition: Measurement principle in which the backscattering of nuclear radiation impinging on a sample is applied to measure the structure and composition of materials.

name: calibration, k0 method
definition: Calibration method of neutron activation analysis in which the \(k_{0}\) proportionality factors, together with a value of the neutron flux (as a function of the neutron energy) and with a value of the radiation detector's response for gamma radiation (as a function of the gamma-ray energy) are used for establishing a relationship between the number of counts measured and the corresponding amounts of elements in a material.

name: calibrator
definition: Measured amount of an element with stated measurement uncertainty that is simultaneously irradiated with the sample during activation analysis.

name: channeling effect
definition: Range- (traveling distance) increasing effect caused by the decrease in interaction cross sections of the incident particles with atoms in a single crystal when a highly collimated particle beam impinges on a crystal along its principal axis or principal plane.

name: channels ratio method
definition: Measurement method to obtain a quenching correction by counting the spectrum in two separate channels, the ratio of which gives the degree of quenching.

name: Compton scattering analysis
definition: Measurement principle in which wavelengths and angular distribution of Compton scattered electrons is applied in order to reconstruct X-ray and gamma-ray spectra.

name: cross reactivity
definition: Ability of substances other than the analyte to bind to the binding reagent and ability of substances other than the binding reagent to bind the analyte in competitive binding assays.

name: cross section
definition: Characteristic area related to the probability of a specified interaction or reaction between an incident nuclear radiation and a target particle or system of particles.

name: delayed-neutron activation analysis
definition: Neutron activation analysis where neutrons are counted after a delay to allow interfering species to decay.

name: directly-ionizing radiation
definition: Beam of particles capable of removing one or more orbital electrons in a single quantum event from a specified atom resulting in an ion.

name: external standardization for quenching correction
definition: Measurement method to obtain a quenching correction through the use of a gamma-radiation source to generate a spectrum of Compton electrons within the sample vial.

name: flux monitor
definition: Radiation detector to measure energy flux density.

name: flux perturbation
definition: Change of energy flux density or energy distribution of particles or photons in an object as a result of effects such as flux depression and/or self-shielding.

name: gamma-ray spectrometry
definition: Measurement principle of the quantitative study of the energy spectra of gamma-ray sources.

name: half-value thickness
definition: Thickness of a specified material that, when introduced into the path of a given beam of radiation, reduces the intensity of a specified radiation by one half.

name: indirectly-ionizing radiation
definition: Beam of electrically neutral particles that cause ionization by interacting with atoms in a material, producing electrically-charged particles that subsequently cause direct ionization in the material.

name: in-vivo neutron activation analysis
definition: Measurement method of neutron activation analysis in which a living organism is exposed to neutrons to measure the concentrations of elements in that living organism.

name: ion beam analysis
definition: Measurement principle in which elementary particles resulting from nuclear reactions of charged particles with nuclei in a material are applied in order to measure the amount and depth distribution of elements in materials.

name: isotopic label
definition: Radioactive or stable isotope of a specified element distinguishable by the observer but not by the system used to identify an isotopic tracer.

name: monoisotopic element
definition: Chemical element having only one stable nuclide.

name: Mössbauer spectrometry
definition: Measurement method in which recoil-less resonance gamma ray scattering and absorption in solids is applied to measure the nuclear environment of atoms of elements in a material.

name: muon induced X-ray emission analysis
definition: Measurement method of X-ray analysis in which characteristic X-radiation emitted upon irradiation of a material with a beam of muons of certain energy is used to measure the chemical composition and chemical state of an element.

name: near edge X-ray absorption fine structure
definition: Measurement method of X-ray absorption analysis similar to X-ray absorption near edge structure, but usually reserved for soft X-rays with photon energy less than \(\pu{1 keV}\).

name: neutron activation analysis
definition: Activation analysis using neutrons as the incident particles.

name: neutron depth profiling
definition: Measurement method of activation analysis for near-surface-depth light elements in which a thermal neutron or cold neutron (see: neutron energy) beam passes through a material with target nuclei that emit monoenergetic charged particles upon neutron absorption. The reduction of the energy of an emitted charged particle measures the depth of the target nuclei in a material.

name: neutron diffraction analysis
definition: Measurement method in which the diffraction of neutrons is applied to measure parameters of the atomic and/or magnetic structure of a material.

name: neutron energy
definition: Kinetic energy of a free neutron.

name: neutron scattering analysis
definition: Measurement method in which the elastic or inelastic scattering of neutrons by the target nuclei is applied to study the composition and structure of a material.

name: non-radiative quenching
definition: Deactivation of an electronically-excited state by interaction with the external environment through a non-radiative process.

name: nuclear capture
definition: Process in which an atomic nucleus acquires an additional particle.

name: nuclide precursor
definition: Radionuclide which precedes a nuclide in a decay chain.

name: particle flux density
definition: Number of particles (or photons) incident on a plane perpendicular to the incident radiation per unit time per unit area.

name: particle-induced gamma-ray-emission analysis
definition: Measurement principle in which the energies and intensities of characteristic prompt gamma-radiation emitted during nuclear reactions with charged particles other than electrons is used to measure the amounts of elements in a material.

name: perturbed angular correlation spectrometry
definition: Measurement method of gamma-ray spectrometry in which coincidence counting is used for the measurement of parameters describing hyperfine interactions, with internal or external electrical or magnetic field gradients, of the spin of an intermediate level between two gamma-ray transitions in cascade emitted in the decay of a radionuclide.

name: positron annihilation analysis
definition: Measurement principle in which the annihilation of positrons is applied to study the microscopic structure of materials.
synonyms: PAA|positron annihilation spectroscopy for chemical analysis (PASCA)

name: positron emission tomography
definition: Imaging method based on the detection of pairs of gamma rays emitted indirectly by a positron-emitting isotopic tracer.

name: positron lifetime spectrometry
definition: Measurement method of positron annihilation analysis in which the time interval between the emission of positrons from a radioactive source and the detection of gamma rays due to the annihilation of these positrons with electrons from the surrounding matter is the lifetime of the positron or positronium.

name: prompt gamma radiation
definition: Gamma radiation emitted during the de-excitation of a compound nucleus formed in a nuclear capture reaction.

name: prompt gamma-ray analysis
definition: Measurement principle in which gamma radiation emitted during the de-excitation of the compound nucleus formed by neutron capture is applied to measure the amounts of elements in a material.

name: pulse pile-up
definition: Processing by a radiation counter of pulses resulting from the simultaneous absorption of independent particles or photons in a radiation detector, resulting in them being counted as one single particle or photon with energy between the individual energies and the sum of these energies.

name: radiation filter
definition: Material interposed in the path of radiation to modify the energy distribution of the radiation.

name: radioactive steady state
definition: Among the radionuclides of a decay chain, the state that prevails when the ratios between the activities of successive radionuclides remain constant.

name: recovery time
definition: Period of time after the dead time of a radiation counter during which the output pulses are smaller than the original.

name: relative counting efficiency
definition: Absolute counting efficiency of a given radiation counter divided by the absolute counting efficiency of a reference radiation counter.

name: scanning proton microscopy
definition: Measurement method of X-ray fluorescence analysis in which protons are focused and collimated to form a micro beam to obtain an image of a surface.

name: selectively-labelled isotopic tracer
definition: An isotopically labelled compound is designated as selectively labelled when a mixture of isotopically substituted compounds is formally added to the analogous isotopically unmodified compound in such a way that the position(s), but not necessarily the number, of each labelling nuclide is defined.

name: specific activity (radionuclide)
definition: Activity of a specified radionuclide (\(\ce{R}\)) per unit mass of that nuclide.

name: synchrotron radiation induced X-ray fluorescence analysis
definition: Measurement method of X-ray fluorescence analysis in which synchrotron X-radiation is used to irradiate the substance.

name: total reflection X-ray fluorescence analysis
definition: Measurement method of X-ray fluorescence analysis in which a collimated X-ray flux impinges on a smooth surface under a grazing angle; rendering total reflection is used to excite atoms in the top layers of the material for measurement of the amounts of elements.

name: X-ray absorption analysis
definition: Measurement principle of X-ray analysis in which the absorption spectrum is used to measure the number of atoms, species, and other parameters of chemical elements.

name: X-ray absorption edge
definition: Increase in X-ray absorption observed at the energy at which a strongly bound electron is released.

name: X-ray absorption near edge structure
definition: Measurement method of X-ray absorption analysis in which the fine structure of the adsorption spectrum in the range \(\pu{30 eV}\) below to \(\pu{50 eV}\) above the absorption edge is used to measure parameters describing the chemical state, coordination environment, and local geometry distortion for the X-ray absorbing atom.
synonyms: X-ray absorption near edge fine structure|XANES

name: X-ray analysis
definition: Measurement principle in which characteristic X-radiation, produced upon irradiation of a material with elementary particles or photons, is applied to measure amounts of elements in a material.

name: X-ray computed micro-tomography
definition: Measurement method based on the transmission of X-rays to obtain three-dimensional images of a sample.

name: X-ray diffraction analysis
definition: Measurement method using diffraction of X-radiation to obtain the spatial arrangement of atoms in a crystalline sample.

name: X-ray fluorescence microscopy
definition: Measurement method of X-ray fluorescence to obtain quantitative and spatial information about elements in a sample.

name: actuator
definition: Transducer that converts the energy supplied or taken from the surroundings into some mechanical motion.

name: antisoliton
definition: Soliton with the negative amplitude or opposite spin with respect to a given soliton.

name: charge carrier
definition: Particle or quasiparticle capable of transporting an electric charge.

name: charge carrier concentration
definition: Number of charge carriers per unit volume.

name: charge carrier diffusion
definition: Purely random, thermally induced motion of charge carriers.

name: charge carrier generation
definition: Process whereby charge carriers are created.

name: charge carrier injection
definition: Process whereby charge carriers in excess of the thermodynamic equilibrium level are introduced into a conductor, a semiconductor or an insulator from another material.

name: charge carrier mobility
definition: Drift velocity (\(v_{\rm{d}}\)) of charge carriers divided by the electric field strength (\(E\)). \[\mu = v_{\rm{d}}/E \quad (\rm{unit}{:}\ \pu{m2 V-1 s-1})\]

name: charge carrier recombination
definition: Process whereby an electron in the conduction band (in LUMO level) loses its excess energy and re-occupies the energy state of a hole in the valence band (in HOMO level).

name: charge transfer
definition: Transfer of charge carriers between two sites of the same molecular entity (intramolecular CT) or between two molecular entities occurring in close proximity (intermolecular CT).

name: charge-transfer exciton
definition: Exciton formed by a charge-transfer transition.

name: conductor
definition: Material having the ability to transmit energy or charge carriers or both.

name: conjugated polymer
definition: A polymer composed of molecules whose backbone is a sequence of alternating single and multiple bonds:  where \(\ce{R^{1}}\) and \(\ce{R^{2}}\) are each hydrogen, alkyl, aryl or heteroaryl and Ar is arenediyl (formerly: arylene) or heteroarenediyl (formerly: heteroarylene).

name: π-conjugated system
definition: Molecule or a part of a molecule, of which structure may be represented as a system of alternating single and multiple bonds, in which, eventually, a multiple bond can be replaced by an atom with a pair of non-bonding electrons or an atom carrying a negative charge.

name: coulomb radius
definition: Distance between two oppositely charged charge carriers at which the energy of their Coulombic attraction is equal to \(kT\), where \(k\) is the Boltzmann constant and \(T\) the absolute temperature.

name: dark electric conductivity
definition: Electric conductivity of a material in the dark where the free charge-carrier photogeneration is excluded.

name: delocalization of electrons
definition: Redistribution of electron density in a molecular entity as compared with a model assuming individual atoms in the same valence states connected by localized bonds.

name: dielectric material
definition: Material which polarizes when exposed to an external electric field, because it creates its own internal electric field oriented against the external field.

name: dispersive transport
definition: Irregular charge transport in which charge carriers move with an ill-defined mean velocity owing to the high variety of dwell times spent at different transport sites.

name: double injection
definition: Simultaneous injection of both types of charge carriers (electrons and holes) into a material or a device.

name: drift current
definition: Electric current caused by electric drift.

name: drift velocity
definition: Average velocity that a charge carrier attains due to an applied electric field.

name: electret
definition: Dielectric material with a permanent or quasi-permanent electric dipole.

name: electric conductor
definition: Material that is able to transmit electric current.

name: electric drift
definition: Oriented flow of otherwise randomly moving charge carriers induced by an applied external electric field.

name: electrically conducting polymer composite
definition: Composite composed of a non-conducting polymer matrix in which irregular powdered or fibrous particles of an electrically conducting material are evenly dispersed in an amount exceeding the percolation threshold for electric conductivity and so the composite exhibits electric conductivity close to that of the conducting filler.

name: electrochromic polymer
definition: Polymer that exhibits electrochromism.

name: electrofluorescence
definition: Electroluminescence originated from singlet-state excitons.

name: electroinjection
definition: Process of charge carrier injection induced by an applied external electric field.

name: electromagnetic field
definition: Physical field composed of two interconnected, mutually orthogonal fields, an electric field and a magnetic field, which mediates interactions of charged, dipolar and multipolar objects.

name: electromagnetic field responsive polymer
definition: Polymer showing a noticeable response of its physical or chemical properties during or upon exposure to an electromagnetic field or one of its components: electric field and magnetic field.

name: electron-deficient molecule
definition: Molecule that has fewer valence electrons than required for forming normal two-center two-electron chemical bonds and thus contains multicenter chemical bonds.

name: electron-rich molecule
definition: Molecule that has more valence electrons than is needed to link its atoms by single covalent bonds.

name: electron tunneling
definition: Quantum mechanical effect of passing an electron through a potential energy barrier separating two energy equivalent regions.

name: electro-optic effect
definition: Change in the optical properties of a material in response to a change in an external electric field strength.

name: electrophosphorescence
definition: Electroluminescence originated from triplet-state excitons.

name: electrorheological effect
