definition: Reversible change in the apparent viscosity of a liquid system such as suspension of polar or good polarizable microparticles in an oil, upon exposure of an electric field.

name: energy band
definition: Quasi-continuous range of discrete energy levels that an electron is either allowed (an occupied band) or forbidden (forbidden band or band gap) to occupy in a molecule or solid.

name: energy band theory
definition: Theory describing the electronic structure of a solid in terms of energy intervals, called energy bands that are allowed or forbidden for occupation by electrons.

name: energy gap
definition: Energy interval in a lattice where no electronic state exists.

name: exciton annihilation
definition: Interaction of two excitons resulting in their decay and radiative emission of the stored excitation energy.

name: exciton diffusion
definition: Random movement of an exciton from one molecular entity to another or from one part of a molecular entity or a lattice to another part of the same kind.

name: exciton dissociation
definition: Fission of an exciton into independent, Coulombically unbound mobile charge carriers: an electron and a hole, or a negative and a positive polaron.

name: exciton mean free path
definition: Mean distance that an exciton travels from the site of its creation to the site where it radiatively or non-radiatively decays or dissociates into charge carriers.

name: exciton–phonon coupling
definition: Interaction in which a part of the exciton energy is converted into the lattice vibrational energy and vice versa.

name: extent of electron delocalization
definition: Magnitude of the region in a molecule over which a molecular orbital occupied with delocalized electrons is extended.

name: external quantum yield
definition: Quantum yield relating to the whole device or the overall process involved.

name: extrinsic semiconductor
definition: Semiconductor whose electric properties are largely determined by the dopant 'impurities' present.

name: field-effect transistor
definition: Transistor in which the flow of charge carriers from source to drain is controlled by the potential applied to the gate.

name: fill factor
definition: Ratio of the real maximum output power, \(P_{\rm{max}}\), that can be obtained with an actual solar cell to the product of the open-circuit potential, \(V_{\rm{oc}}\), and short-circuit photocurrent, \(I_{\rm{sc}}\): \[f_{\rm{FF}} = P_{\rm{max}}/V_{\rm{oc}}I_{\rm{sc}}\]

name: free charge-carrier photogeneration
definition: Generation of free charge carriers by photons.

name: head-tail isomerism
definition: Constitutional isomerism of polymeric (oligomeric) chains composed of identical non symmetric repeating units consisting in different orientations of the units.

name: heterojunction
definition: Interface between dissimilar crystalline or amorphous solid phases that have unequal bandgap levels.

name: hole
definition: Quasiparticle, a conceptual charge carrier opposite to electron, defined as the absence of electron at a position where it should be present if a lattice is in its ground state (valence band normally filled).

name: hole-transporting material
definition: Material, typically a semiconductor, in which holes are predominant mobile charge carriers.

name: homojunction
definition: Interface occurring between two similar semiconductors with equal bandgaps.

name: hopping transport
definition: Incoherent transport of charge carriers by hopping between adjacent energetically nearly equivalent localized sites.

name: hot electron
definition: Electron that is out of the thermal equilibrium with its environment and has enough kinetic energy to overcome potential barriers to travel between different regions of a molecule or lattice.

name: impact ionization
definition: Charge carrier generation by another charge carrier possessing a high kinetic energy, which knocks an electron out of the HOMO into the LUMO or still higher state so creating a new electron-hole pair.

name: internal quantum yield
definition: Quantum yield relating to a single component or a part of a device or a partial step of an overall process.

name: intrinsic semiconductor
definition: Semiconductor in which mobile charge carriers are generated solely by thermal excitation of electrons.

name: ion-conducting polymer
definition: Conducting polymer in which ionic species are mobile charge carriers.

name: lattice
definition: Periodic grid-like ideal structure consisting of regularly arranged elementary repeating units.

name: light emitting diode
definition: Transducer-type device that converts an electric current into luminescence light.

name: lowest unoccupied molecular orbital
definition: Lowest-energy molecular orbital that is unoccupied in the ground state but occupied by one or more electrons if the molecular entity occurs in its first electronically excited state.

name: luminescent material
definition: Material (polymer) that exhibits a luminescence.

name: magnetoresistance
definition: Change in the electric resistance of a material in response to an external magnetic field.

name: memristor
definition: Electric component that can be reversibly switched between stable low- and high-resistive states.

name: molecular orbital theory
definition: Theory of quantum mechanics in which electrons in a molecule (lattice) are not assigned to particular bonds between atoms but move under the influence of all atoms.

name: molecular switch
definition: Molecule that can be reversibly switched between two or more stable states in response to a change in, e.g., its microenvironment (pH, the presence of a ligand, temperature etc.), illumination or electric current.

name: occupied band
definition: Energy band occupied by electrons, typically the valence band.

name: ohmic contact
definition: Electric junction which exhibits linear and symmetric current-potential dependence.

name: optically nonlinear polymer
definition: Polymer that exhibits a nonlinear optical effect.

name: optoelectronics
definition: Branch of physics that deals with the optical-to-electric and electric-to-optical transducers.

name: percolation
definition: Formation of the long-range (infinite) functional connectivity in a disperse system composed of small active particles evenly dispersed in an inactive matrix, which makes the system penetrable for a fluid or current.

name: percolation threshold
definition: Minimal volume fraction of functionally active small particles evenly dispersed in a non-active matrix, at which the long-range (infinite) functional connectivity in the system is achieved.

name: photochromic polymer
definition: Polymer exhibiting photochromism.

name: photoconducting polymer
definition: Polymer exhibiting electrical conductivity or a clear increase in electrical conductivity under irradiation.

name: photodetrapping
definition: Removal of charge carriers from traps in the bandgap by irradiation.

name: photoinduced discharge
definition: Discharging of an electrically charged material by irradiation.

name: photoinjection
definition: Charge carrier injection by a process induced by irradiation.

name: photorefractive polymer
definition: Optically nonlinear polymer that changes refractive index when exposed to light.

name: photovoltaic effect
definition: Phenomenon consisting in converting light to electricity.

name: polarization density
definition: Change in electric dipole moment per unit volume of dielectric material in response to its exposure to an electric field.

name: poling
definition: Orientation of dipoles or dipolar domains inside a material by using a sufficiently strong electric field.

name: Poole–Frenkel effect
definition: Increase in the electric conductivity of a semiconductor or insulator by exposing it to an electric field.

name: protonic conductivity
definition: Ionic conductivity mediated by protons (more exactly by hydrogen cations properly called hydrons).

name: proton doping
definition: Transformation of a semiconducting or insulating material to conducting state by protonation (hydronation) of its molecules.

name: quantum confinement effect
definition: Effect occurring if at least one dimension of a structure is comparable to the de Broglie wavelength of the electron-hole pair and the motion of charge carriers is thus quantized by the structure boundary.

name: quantum tunneling polymer composite
definition: Electrically conducting polymer composite that, however, is conducting only when pressed due to thinning the insulating polymer matrix membranes so much that they allow electron tunneling through them.

name: quasiparticle
definition: Discrete disorder in a multi-particulate system that exhibits particle-specific behavior and properties.

name: radiative charge carrier recombination
definition: Charge carrier recombination in which the energy released is emitted as a photon of corresponding energy.

name: redox doping
definition: Doping of a parent polymer consisting in oxidation or reduction of its molecules.

name: regioirregular polymer
definition: Regular polymer or an irregular polymer whose macromolecules contain non-uniformly oriented simple asymmetric repeating units.

name: regiorandom polymer
definition: Regioirregular polymer with randomly oriented asymmetric constitutional repeating units in its chains.

name: regioregular polymer
definition: Regular polymer whose chains are composed of uniformly oriented asymmetric constitutional repeating units.

name: reticulate doped polymer
definition: Surface-conducting polymer composite obtained by crystallization of a low-molar-mass organic conductor on an insulating or semiconducting polymer support.

name: Schottky barrier
definition: Potential energy barrier at a semiconductor-metal junction with the current rectifying characteristics.

name: second harmonic generation
definition: Transformation of the input monochromatic radiation beam into a double frequency (half wavelength) beam.

name: sensor
definition: Transducer-type device that responds to a specific property of its surroundings or to a coming stimulus by a visually readable change in its state or by generation of a signal that can be read by an observer or instrument.

name: short circuit photocurrent
definition: Photocurrent flowing through a short circuited solar cell (if the electric potential across the cell is zero).

name: size effect
definition: Effect of size on properties of the material or device which incorporates it.

name: solar cell
definition: Device that directly transduces electromagnetic radiation into electricity based on the photovoltaic effect.

name: stimulated radiative charge carrier recombination
definition: Radiative charge carrier recombination induced by incident photons of appropriate wavelength, which synchronize emission of other photons as to their wavelength, phase, polarization and direction of travel.

name: thermal injection
definition: Charge carrier injection by a thermally activated processes.

name: valence bond theory
definition: Quantum mechanics theory of chemical bonding that treats electrons as being assigned to individual bonds between particular atoms.

name: work function
definition: Minimum thermodynamic work (energy) needed to remove an electron from a solid to a point in the vacuum nearby the solid surface.\[\mathit{\Phi} = -e{\mathit{\Psi}} - \mu\]where \(e\) is the elementary charge (\(-e\) is charge of electron), \(\mathit{\Psi}\) is the electric potential nearby the surface and \(\mu\) is the energy of Fermi level.

name: fluoropolymers
definition: Polymers whose macromolecules are rich in fluorocarbon groups (structure-based polymer class name).

name: metallo-supramolecular polymer
definition: Dynamic polymeric entity whose macromolecules are composed of alternating simple or oligomeric molecules with two or more chelate end-groups (so-called unimers) and metal ions (so-called ion couplers) that are linked to chains by reversible coordination bonds (structure-based polymer class name):

name: polyacetylenes
definition: Polymers prepared from acetylene (ethyne), a substituted acetylene, or both in admixture by a polymerization involving one or more triple bonds (source-based polymer class name).

name: polyanilines
definition: Polymers prepared exclusively from aniline, or substituted aniline, or both in admixture (source-based class name).

name: polyarylenes
definition: Polymers composed of macromolecules containing exclusively arenediyl (formerly arylene) or heteroarenediyl (formerly heteroarylene) units in the backbone:  where Ar is a divalent arenediyl or heteroarenediyl group (structure-based polymer class name).

name: polyarylenethynylenes
definition: Polymers composed of macromolecules containing exclusively alternating arenediyl or heterarenediyl (formerly arylene or heteroarylene, respectively) and ethynediyl (formerly ethynylene) constitutional repeating units in the backbone:  where Ar is a divalent arenediyl or heterarenediyl group (structure-based polymer class name).

name: polyarylenevinylenes
definition: Polymers composed of macromolecules containing exclusively alternating arenediyl or heteroarenediyl (formerly arylene or heteroarylene, respectively) and ethene-1,2-diyl (formerly vinylene) or substituted vinylene constitutional repeating units in the backbone:  where Ar is a divalent arenediyl or heteroarenediyl group and \(\ce{R^{1}}\) and \(\ce{R^{2}}\) are each hydrogen, or an alkyl, aryl or heteroaryl group (structure-based polymer class name).

name: polyazomethines
definition: Polymers composed of macromolecules containing azomethine (azanylylidenemethanylylidene) linkages in the backbone: \[\ce{-N=CR-}\] where \(\ce{R}\) is hydrogen, or an alkyl or aryl group (structure-based polymer class name).

name: polybenzimidazoles
definition: Polymers composed of macromolecules containing benzimidazole groups in the backbone, such as groups (structure-based polymer class name).

name: polydiacetylenes
definition: Polymer prepared from buta-1,3-diyne (diacetylene) or a substituted buta-1,3-diyne or both in admixture (source-based polymer class name).

name: poly(ethene-1,2-diyl)
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules exclusively consisting of ethene-1,2-diyl (formerly called vinylene) constitutional repeating units.

name: poly[3,4-(ethylenedioxy)thiophene]
definition: Polymer prepared from 3,4-(ethylenedioxy)thiophene (source-based polymer name).

name: polyfluorenes
definition: Polymers composed of macromolecules containing fluorenediyl or substituted fluorenediyl (mainly 2,7-diyl) constitutional repeating units in the backbone (structure-based polymer class name).

name: polyimides
definition: Polymers composed of macromolecules containing cyclic dicarboximide groupings in the backbone:  where \(\ce{R^{1}}\), \(\ce{R^{2}}\), \(\ce{R^{3}}\) and \(\ce{R^{4}}\) are groups with connectivity one, two, three, and four, respectively (structure-based polymer class name).

name: polyoxadiazoles
definition: Polymers composed of macromolecules containing exclusively oxadiazole rings in the backbone (structure-based polymer class name).

name: polyphenylenes
definition: Polymers composed of macromolecules containing exclusively \(\upsigma\)-bonded benzene or substituted benzene rings in the backbone:  where \(\ce{R^{1}}\), \(\ce{R^{2}}\), \(\ce{R^{3}}\) and \(\ce{R^{4}}\) are each hydrogen or an univalent group (structure-based polymer class name).

name: polyphenylenethynylenes
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing exclusively alternating phenylene or substituted phenylene and ethynediyl (formerly ethynylene) constitutional repeating units in the backbone:  where \(\ce{R^{1}}\), \(\ce{R^{2}}\), \(\ce{R^{3}}\) and \(\ce{R^{4}}\) are each hydrogen, alkyl, aryl, halogen, trialkylsilyl etc. (structure-based polymer class name).

name: polyphenylenevinylenes
definition: Polymers composed of macromolecules containing exclusively alternating phenylene or substituted phenylene and ethene-1,2-diyl (formerly vinylene) or substituted ethene-1,2-diyl constitutional repeating units in the backbone:  where \(\ce{R^{1}}\), \(\ce{R^{2}}\), \(\ce{R^{3}}\), \(\ce{R^{4}}\), \(\ce{R^{5}}\) and \(\ce{R^{6}}\) are each hydrogen, alkyl, aryl, heteroaryl, halogen, trialkylsilyl, etc. (structure-based polymer class name).

name: polypyrroles
definition: Polymers composed of macromolecules with backbones composed of pyrrole rings (structure-based polymer class name definition).

name: polysilanes
definition: Polymers composed of macromolecules containing exclusively silicon atoms in the backbone:  where \(\ce{R^{1}}\) and \(\ce{R^{2}}\) are each hydrogen or an alkyl, aryl or heteroaryl group (structure-based polymer class name).

name: polytetrazines
definition: Polymers composed of macromolecules containing tetrazine or hydrogenated tetrazine rings in the backbone (structure-based polymer class name):

name: polythiadiazoles
definition: Polymers composed of macromolecules containing thiadiazole rings in the backbone (structure-based polymer class name).

name: polythiazoles
definition: Polymers composed of macromolecules containing thiazole rings in the backbone:  where R is hydrogen, alkyl, aryl, heteroaryl, substituted alkyl, substituted aryl or substituted heteroaryl (structure-based polymer class name).

name: polythiophenes
definition: Polymers composed of macromolecules containing exclusively thiophene rings in the backbone (structure-based polymer class name).

name: polyvinylcarbazoles
definition: Polymers prepared from a vinylcarbazole or a substituted vinylcarbazole or both in admixture (source-based polymer class name).

name: polyvinylenes
definition: Polymers composed of macromolecules containing exclusively ethene-1,2-diyl (formerly vinylene) or substituted ethene-1,2-diyl constitutional repeating units in the backbone: \[\ce{-CR^{1}=CR^{2}-}\] where \(\ce{R^{1}}\) and \(\ce{R^{2}}\) are each hydrogen or an alkyl, aryl, or heteroaryl group (structure-based polymer class name).

name: polyzwitterions
definition: Polymers composed of macromolecules consisting of zwitterionic repeating units (structure-based polymer class name).

name: activated-monomer polymerization
definition: Chain polymerization in which propagation involves reaction between a growing-chain end and an activated monomer.

name: controlled polymerization
definition: Term indicating control of a certain kinetic feature of a polymerization or structural aspect of the polymer molecules formed, or both.

name: degenerative-transfer polymerization
definition: Reversible-deactivation polymerization in which the deactivation of the active species involves degenerative chain transfer.

name: group-transfer polymerization
definition: Chain polymerization in which a specific atom or group is intramolecularly transferred to remain associated with the active chain-end during the course of polymerization.

name: insertion polymerization
definition: Chain polymerization in which monomer units are sequentially inserted into a specific site within a polymer structure with retention of chain-end functionality.

name: reversible-deactivation polymerization
definition: Chain polymerization, propagated by chain carriers that are deactivated reversibly, bringing them into active-dormant equilibria of which there might be more than one.

name: controlled radical polymerization
definition: Term indicating control of a certain kinetic feature of a radical polymerization or structural aspect of the polymer molecules formed by radical polymerization, or both.

name: living radical polymerization
definition: Radical polymerization in which chain termination and irreversible chain transfer are absent.

name: radical ring-opening polymerization
definition: Radical polymerization in which a cyclic monomer yields a monomeric unit that is either acyclic or contains fewer rings than the cyclic monomer.

name: reversible-deactivation radical polymerization
definition: Chain polymerization, propagated by radicals that are deactivated reversibly, bringing them into active-dormant equilibria of which there might be more than one.

name: aminoxyl-mediated radical polymerization
definition: Stable-radical-mediated polymerization in which the deactivation of the radicals involves reversible coupling with aminoxyl radicals.

name: cobalt-mediated radical polymerization
definition: Reversible-deactivation radical polymerization mediated by a cobalt complex.

name: iniferter process
definition: Stable-radical-mediated polymerization where the initiator and dormant species are iniferters.

name: organometallic-mediated radical polymerization
definition: Reversible-deactivation radical polymerization mediated by an organometallic reagent.

name: stable-radical-mediated polymerization
definition: Reversible-deactivation radical polymerization in which the deactivation involves reversible coupling with stable (persistent) radicals.

name: reversible-addition-fragmentation radical polymerization
definition: Reversible-deactivation radical polymerization in which the dormant species is a stable (persistent) radical and the deactivation step involves reversible fragmentation.

name: carbonothioyl-mediated radical polymerization
definition: Reversible-addition-fragmentation radical polymerization mediated by a carbonothioyl compound.

name: atom-transfer radical polymerization
definition: Reversible-deactivation radical polymerization in which the deactivation of the radicals involves reversible atom-transfer or reversible group transfer to usually, though not exclusively, transition-metal complexes.

name: inner-sphere electron transfer atom-transfer radical polymerization
definition: Atom-transfer radical polymerization where the activation step involves direct atom or group transfer.

name: non-metal-mediated atom-transfer radical polymerization
definition: Atom-transfer radical polymerization in which the deactivation of the radicals involves reversible atom transfer or reversible group transfer to a non-metallic reagent.

name: outer-sphere electron transfer ATRP
definition: Atom-transfer radical polymerization where the activation step involves consecutive single electron transfer and atom or group transfer.

name: transition-metal-mediated radical polymerization
definition: Reversible-deactivation radical polymerization mediated by transition-metal complexes or organometallic compounds.

name: degenerative chain-transfer radical polymerization
definition: Reversible-deactivation radical polymerization in which the deactivation of the radicals involves degenerative transfer (DT) of a group (or atom).

name: iodine-transfer polymerization
definition: Reversible-deactivation radical polymerization mediated by an iodo-compound.

name: organobismuthane-mediated radical polymerization
definition: Reversible-deactivation radical polymerization mediated by an organobismuthane compound.

name: organostibane-mediated radical polymerization
definition: Reversible-deactivation radical polymerization mediated by an organostibane compound.

name: organotellurium-mediated radical polymerization
definition: Reversible-deactivation radical polymerization mediated by an organotellurium compound.

name: reverse iodine-transfer polymerization
definition: Iodine-transfer polymerization where the initial polymerization mixture comprises a conventional initiator (e.g., an azo-compound or a peroxide) and molecular iodine.

name: reversible-addition-fragmentation chain-transfer polymerization
definition: Degenerate-transfer radical polymerization in which chain activation and chain deactivation involve a degenerative chain-transfer process, which occurs by a two-step addition-fragmentation mechanism.

name: activated monomer
definition: Reactive species generated reversibly from a monomer.

name: addition-fragmentation chain transfer
definition: Chain-transfer process that proceeds by a propagating species adding to a chain-transfer agent to form an intermediate that then fragments to provide an initiating species.

name: catalyst precursor
definition: Coordination compound that by reaction with an activator or cocatalyst provides an active catalyst during initialization of coordination polymerization.

name: catalytic chain transfer
definition: Chain-transfer process involving transfer of an atom or group to a reagent (the catalyst) that in turn transfers that group to a monomer to reinitiate polymerization and regenerate the original reagent.

name: catalytic chain termination
definition: Chain termination process involving transfer of a group to a reagent (the catalyst) that in turn transfers that group to a propagating species to terminate a chain and regenerate the original reagent.

name: chain activation
definition: Unimolecular dissociation of a dormant species to form a mediating agent and a propagating species.

name: chain activation
definition: Reaction of an activator with a dormant species to form a deactivator and a propagating species.

name: chain deactivation
definition: Conversion of a chain carrier into an inactive species.

name: chain propagation
definition: Chemical reaction between a chain carrier and a monomer that results in the growth of a polymer chain and the regeneration of at least one chain carrier.

name: chain reactivation
definition: Conversion of an inactive chain into a chain carrier.

name: chain termination
definition: Chemical reaction in which a chain carrier is converted irreversibly into a non-propagating species without the formation of a new chain carrier.

name: chain-transfer agent
definition: Substance able to react with a chain carrier by a reaction in which the original chain carrier is deactivated and a new chain carrier is generated.

name: combination
definition: Chain termination, in a chain polymerization, between two propagating macromolecules that gives rise to a single macromolecule of molar mass equal to the sum of the molar masses of the two macromolecules.

name: deactivator
definition: Reagent that reacts reversibly with the initiating species or propagating species to form an initiator or a dormant chain, respectively, and an activator.

name: dead polymer chain
definition: Polymer chain which plays no active role in the polymerization.

name: degenerative chain transfer
definition: Chain-transfer reaction that generates a new chain carrier and a new chain-transfer agent with the same reactivity as the original chain carrier and chain-transfer agent.

name: dormant species
definition: Temporarily deactivated chain carrier.

name: inactive chain
definition: Dead chains or dormant chains.

name: inifer
definition: Substance that combines the properties of an initiator and a reversible chain-transfer agent.

name: iniferter
definition: Substance that combines the properties of an initiator, a reversible chain-transfer agent and a chain terminator or reversible deactivator.

name: initialization
definition: Process for converting a starting coordination complex or precatalyst into an active catalyst.

name: initializer
definition: Starting initiator or transfer agent in reversible-deactivation polymerization (RDP).

name: initialization efficiency
definition: Efficiency of conversion of a starting initiator or transfer agent into a macro-initiator or macro-chain-transfer agent.

name: initiating species
definition: Species to which monomer adds or becomes inserted to start a chain polymerization.

name: initiator efficiency
definition: Number of growing chains initiated divided by the number of active-centers generated from initiator molecules.

name: living polymer chain
definition: Polymer chains that possess the potential for chain growth under the polymerization conditions.

name: macro-chain-transfer agent
definition: Macromolecule containing chain-transfer-agent functionality.

name: macroinitiator
definition: Macromolecule containing initiator functionality.

name: mediating agent
definition: Species that mediates polymerization in reversible-deactivation polymerization.

name: primary species
definition: Species that is formed from an initiator or monomer molecule and that is capable of initiating polymerization.

name: propagating species
definition: Active species formed by addition to monomer that is capable of adding further monomer.
synonyms: active macromolecule (in RDP)|active polymer chain|growing chain

name: retardation
definition: Diminished rate of polymerization brought about by the action of a retarder.

name: reversible-addition-fragmentation chain-transfer agent
definition: Chain-transfer agent that provides chain transfer by a reversible-addition-fragmentation mechanism.

name: secondary species
definition: Species formed by the rearrangement or fragmentation of a primary species that is capable of initiating a polymerization.

name: stable radical
definition: Mediating agent in stable-radical-mediated radical polymerization with sufficient kinetic stability such that it is essentially unreactive towards addition to monomer under the conditions of the experiment.

name: unimer
definition: Species comprising only one monomer unit.

name: substitution chain transfer
definition: Chain-transfer process that proceeds by a one-step substitution reaction.

name: controlled ionic polymerization
definition: Term indicating control of a certain kinetic feature of an ionic polymerization or structural aspect of the polymer molecules formed by ionic polymerization, or both.

name: ionic ring-opening polymerization
definition: Ionic polymerization in which a cyclic monomer yields a monomeric unit that is either acyclic or contains fewer rings than the cyclic monomer.

name: living ionic polymerization
definition: Ionic polymerization in which chain termination and irreversible chain transfer are absent.

name: reversible-deactivation ionic polymerization
definition: Reversible-deactivation polymerization in which the kinetic-chain carriers are ions.

name: anionic group-transfer polymerization
definition: Anionic polymerization in which a specific atom or group is intramolecularly transferred to remain associated with the active chain-end during the course of polymerization.

name: anionic ring-opening polymerization
definition: Anionic polymerization in which a cyclic monomer yields a monomeric unit that is either acyclic or contains fewer rings than the cyclic monomer.

name: controlled anionic polymerization
definition: Term indicating control of a certain kinetic feature of an anionic polymerization or structural aspect of the polymer molecules formed by anionic polymerization, or both.

name: living anionic polymerization
definition: Anionic polymerization in which chain termination and irreversible chain transfer are absent.

name: reversible-deactivation anionic polymerization
definition: Reversible-deactivation polymerization in which the kinetic-chain carriers are anions.

name: nucleophilic chain polymerization
definition: Chain polymerization in which the active centres are nucleophilic species.

name: ring-opening nucleophilic chain polymerization
definition: Nucleophilic chain polymerization in which a cyclic monomer yields a monomeric unit that is either acyclic or contains fewer rings than the cyclic monomer.

name: cationic ring-opening polymerization
definition: Cationic polymerization in which a cyclic monomer yields a monomeric unit that is either acyclic or contains fewer rings than the cyclic monomer.

name: controlled cationic polymerization
definition: Term indicating control of a certain kinetic feature of a cationic polymerization or structural aspect of the polymer molecules formed by cationic polymerization, or both.

name: electrophilic chain polymerization
definition: Chain polymerization in which the active centres are electrophilic species.

name: living cationic polymerization
definition: Cationic polymerization in which chain termination and irreversible chain transfer are absent.

name: reversible-deactivation cationic polymerization
definition: Reversible-deactivation polymerization in which the chain carriers are cations.

name: anion-activated-monomer polymerization
definition: Activated-monomer polymerization where the propagating species is an electrophile and activating species is anionic.

name: cation-activated-monomer polymerization
definition: Activated-monomer polymerization where the propagating species is a nucleophile and the activating species is cationic.

name: living ring-opening metathesis polymerization
definition: Ring-opening metathesis polymerization in which chain termination and irreversible chain transfer are absent.

name: metathesis polymerization
definition: Polymerization in which unsaturated monomers are transformed into unsaturated polymers by a process of bond redistribution.

name: ring-opening metathesis polymerization
definition: Metathesis polymerization in which an unsaturated cyclic monomer is converted into an unsaturated monomeric unit that is either acyclic or contains fewer rings than the cyclic monomer.

name: electron-transfer ring-opening metathesis polymerization
definition: Ring-opening metathesis polymerization (ROMP) proceeding through one-electron redox processes in the absence of a metal carbene initiator.

name: coordination polymerization
definition: Chain polymerization that involves the preliminary coordination of a monomer molecule with a chain carrier.

name: coordination-addition polymerization
definition: Coordination polymerization of \(\ce{\upalpha\!,\!\upbeta\mbox{-}unsaturated}\) amides or esters that proceeds by sequential monomer coordination and Michael addition events.

name: coordination-insertion polymerization
definition: Coordination polymerization of olefins that proceeds by insertion of the olefin into a metal–carbon bond

name: living coordination polymerization
definition: Coordination polymerization in which chain termination and irreversible chain transfer are absent.

name: reversible-deactivation coordination polymerization
definition: Reversible-deactivation polymerization in which the chain carriers are coordination complexes.

name: coordination ring-opening polymerization
definition: Coordination polymerization in which a cyclic monomer yields a monomeric unit that is either acyclic or contains fewer rings than the cyclic monomer.

name: chain-shuttling polymerization
definition: Coordinative chain-transfer polymerization that involves two different catalysts showing different specificity, where chain propagation occurs sequentially on the two catalysts, allowing for the formation of segmented or multiblock copolymers.

name: chain-walking polymerization
definition: Coordination polymerization in which the chain carrier migrates along the formed polymer chain through a series of \(\ce{\upbeta\mbox{-}hydrogen}\) eliminations and reinsertions with inversion of stereochemistry.

name: coordinative chain-transfer polymerization
definition: Coordination polymerization in which a propagating chain is able to transfer reversibly between the catalyst and a chain-transfer agent, thereby converting the active species into a dormant species.

name: heterogeneous catalysis coordination polymerization
definition: Coordination polymerization making use of a heterogeneous catalyst.

name: homogeneous catalysis coordination polymerization
definition: Coordination polymerization making use of a homogeneous catalyst.

name: metallocene polymerization
definition: Coordination polymerization making use of a metallocene catalyst.

name: pseudo-ionic polymerization
definition: Polymerization proceeding by insertion of a monomer into a polar bond without the generation of ions.

name: rare-earth-metal-mediated coordination-addition polymerization
definition: Coordination-addition polymerization with propagation occurring within the coordination sphere of a rare-earth metal complex.
synonyms: lanthanide-mediated group-transfer polymerization|rare-earth-metal-mediated coordination polymerization|rare-earth-metal-mediated group-transfer polymerization

name: catalyst-transfer polymerization
definition: Catalysed condensative chain polymerization where the catalyst is transferred from reactant polymer to product polymer with high efficiency.

name: catalyst-transfer cross-coupling polymerization
definition: Catalyst-transfer polymerization where the propagation steps comprise cross-coupling reactions.

name: living condensative chain polymerization
definition: Condensative chain polymerization in which chain termination and irreversible chain transfer are absent.

name: brush polymer
definition: Polymer composed of brush macromolecules.

name: locant
definition: Numeral or letter or a combination of both that identifies position(s) in a structure.

name: senior constitutional repeating unit
definition: More (most) senior CRU of a structure of a macromolecule or oligomer molecule containing two or more different types of CRUs.

name: preferred constitutional repeating unit
definition: Constitutional repeating unit (CRU) written with the subunits in a linear series from the highest (higher) seniority to the lowest (lower) or as close as possible by the shortest path.

name: subunit
definition: Largest main-chain (backbone) segment of the constitutional repeating unit (CRU) that can be named a single unit under organic nomenclature rules. This may be a ring or a ring system, a heteroatom or a heteroatom chain, or an acyclic carbon chain.

name: dimensionless Henry’s law solubility constant
definition: Amount concentration \(c_{\rm{l}}\) of a species in the liquid phase divided by the amount concentration \(c_{\rm{g}}\) of that species in the gas phase under equilibrium conditions at infinite dilution: \[H_{\rm{s}}^{cc}: = \underset{c_{\rm{l}} \to 0}{\rm{lim}}\frac{c_{\rm{l}}}{c_{\rm{g}}}\]

name: dimensionless Henry’s law volatility constant
definition: Amount concentration \(c_{\rm{g}}\) of a species in the gas phase divided by the amount concentration \(c_{\rm{g}}\) of that species in the liquid phase under equilibrium conditions at infinite dilution: \[H_{\rm{v}}^{cc}: = \underset{c_{\rm{l}} \to 0}{\rm{lim}}\frac{c_{\rm{g}}}{c_{\rm{l}}}\]

name: Henry’s law constant
definition: Proportionality factor describing the equilibrium distribution of a chemical species between the gas phase and a liquid solution at infinite dilution of the solute according to Henry’s law. It is an umbrella term for the reciprocal quantities Henry’s law solubility constant and Henry’s law volatility constant. Because of its ambiguity, it is strongly recommended to specify whether a solubility or volatility constant is intended.

name: Henry’s law solubility constant
definition: Umbrella term for all variants of Henry’s law constants that are defined in such a way that the numerical value increases with increasing solubility of the solute. Variants include \(H_{\rm{s}}^{cp}\), \(H_{\rm{s}}^{xp}\), \(H_{\rm{s}}^{bp}\), and \(H_{\rm{s}}^{cc}\), as discussed elsewhere in this section.

name: Henry’s law volatility constant
definition: Umbrella term for all variants of Henry’s law constants that are defined in such a way that the numerical value increases with increasing volatility of the solute. Variants include \(H_{\rm{v}}^{pc}\), \(H_{\rm{v}}^{px}\), \(H_{\rm{v}}^{pw}\), and \(H_{\rm{v}}^{cc}\), as discussed elsewhere in this section.

name: Henry’s law volatility constant (via p and c)
definition: Partial pressure \(p\) of a species in the gas phase divided by the amount concentration \(c_{\rm{l}}\) of that species in the liquid phase under equilibrium conditions at infinite dilution: \[H_{\rm{v}}^{pc}: = \underset{c_{\rm{l}} \to 0}{\rm{lim}}\frac{p}{c_{\rm{l}}}\]

name: Henry’s law solubility constant (via c and p)
definition: Amount concentration \(c_{\rm{l}}\) of a species in the liquid phase divided by the partial pressure \(p\) of that species in the gas phase under equilibrium conditions at infinite dilution: \[H_{\rm{s}}^{cp}: = \underset{c_{\rm{l}} \to 0}{\rm{lim}}\frac{c_{\rm{l}}}{p}\]
synonyms: Henry solubility (defined via amount concentration and partial pressure)

name: Henry’s law solubility constant (via x and p)
definition: Amount fraction \(x\) of a species in the liquid phase divided by the partial pressure \(p\) of that species in the gas phase under equilibrium conditions at infinite dilution: \[H_{\rm{s}}^{xp}: = \underset{x \to 0}{\rm{lim}}\frac{x}{p}\]

name: Henry’s law solubility constant (via b and p)
definition: Molality \(b\) of a species divided by the partial pressure \(p\) of that species in the gas phase under equilibrium conditions at infinite dilution: \[H_{\rm{s}}^{bp}: = \underset{b \to 0}{\rm{lim}}\frac{b}{p}\]

name: Henry’s law volatility constant (via p and x)
definition: Partial pressure \(p\) of a species in the gas phase divided by the amount fraction \(x\) of that species in the liquid phase under equilibrium conditions at infinite dilution: \[H_{\rm{v}}^{px}: = \underset{x \to 0}{\rm{lim}}\frac{p}{x}\]
synonyms: Henry volatility (defined via partial pressure and liquid-phase amount fraction)

name: Henry’s law volatility constant (via p and w)
definition: Partial pressure \(p\) of a species in the gas phase divided by the mass fraction \(w\) of that species in the liquid phase under equilibrium conditions at infinite dilution: \[H_{\rm{v}}^{pw}: = \underset{w \to 0}{\rm{lim}}\frac{p}{w}\]

name: link
definition: Constitutive part of a conjugation that binds an active species to a substrate.

name: prodrug conjugate
definition: Conjugate in which at least one conjugation includes a bioactive active species to be released by cleavage of the link where its action is desired.

name: spacer arm
definition: Link used in a conjugation to distance the substrate from the active species that otherwise would have its activity affected by steric or other influences.

name: materials chemistry
definition: Materials chemistry is the scientific discipline that designs, synthesizes, and characterizes materials with particular interest on both their processing and the understanding of useful or potentially useful properties displayed by the materials designed and synthesized for specific applications.

name: pnictogen bond
definition: Weak attractive interaction between an electrophilic region on a pnictogen atom in a molecular entity (wherein the pnictogen is involved in other stronger bonds) and a nucleophilic region in another, or the same, molecular entity.

name: alkalinity
definition: Measure of the capacity of aqueous media to react with hydrogen ions.

name: back titration
definition: Titration of remaining reagent after addition of excess reagent to the titrand.

name: blank titration
definition: Titration performed with titrand containing no analyte.

name: cerimetric titration
definition: Redox titration using cerium(IV), in which an iron(II)-1,10-phenanthroline complex (ferroin) color change indicates the end-point.

name: composite alkalinity
definition: Measurement by titration to the phenolphthalein end-point (pH 8.3) of that portion of alkalinity arbitrarily attributed to all the hydroxyl content and half the carbonate content of a titrand.

name: conventional mass
definition: Mass of a body that is balanced by a standard mass under conventionally chosen conditions.

name: direct titration
definition: Titration in which titrant is added directly to titrand.

name: end-point error
definition: Difference in the volume or mass of titrant, or the corresponding difference in the volume or mass of titrand, between the end-point value and equivalence-point value.

name: equivalence-point
definition: Stage of a titration at which the titrant has completely reacted with the titrand according to the stoichiometry of the reaction.

name: gravimetric analysis
definition: Measurement principle of quantitative chemical analysis based on measurement of mass.

name: gravimetric factor
definition: Mass fraction of analyte in a precipitate (see precipitation) obtained in a gravimetric analysis.

name: homogeneous precipitation
definition: Precipitation in gravimetric analysis in which the precipitating agent is produced from a homogeneously dissolved precursor to minimise local excesses and supersaturation.

name: indicator consumption error
definition: Systematic measurement error from the reaction of a visual indicator with a reactant in a titration.

name: potentiometric titration
definition: Redox titration in which the course of the reaction is followed by potentiometry.

name: precipitation indicator
definition: Visual indicator precipitated, with concomitant color change, by reaction with excess titrant at the end-point of a titration.

name: redox indicator
definition: Visual indicator that reacts with excess titrant or titrand with a color change at the end-point of a redox titration.

name: stock solution
definition: Solution prepared by weighing an appropriate portion of a solid or by measuring out an appropriate volume of a liquid and dissolving it in the weighed mass of solvent or by adding solvent to a given volume.

name: titrand
definition: Reactant solution being titrated in a titration.

name: titrimetric analysis
definition: Methods of quantitative analysis employing titration.

name: transition potential
definition: Potential at the end-point of a redox titration.

name: universal indicator
definition: Visual indicator composed of a solution of several pH indicators (main components are thymol blue, methyl red, bromothymol blue and phenolphthalein) that changes color through a range of pH values, usually from 1 to 14.

name: volumetric titration
definition: Titration in which the titrant is added by volume.

name: von Weimarn ratio
definition: Difference between the concentration of the supersaturated solution (see supersaturation) required for nucleation (\(Q\)) and its solubility (\(S\)), divided by the solubility, \((Q − S)/S\).

name: net faradaic current
definition: Algebraic sum of faradaic currents flowing through an electrode.

name: electrochemical cell
definition: System that consists of at least two electron conductors (electrodes) in contact with ionic conductors (electrolytes).

name: electrochemical constants
definition: In May 2019, certain fundamental constants that had been measured in SI units have had their numerical values fixed, with no uncertainty, thus defining the units. Of importance to electroanalytical chemistry are the values of the Boltzmann constant, the elementary charge, and the Avogadro constant. These are given in the table below, with calculated values of the Faraday constant (\(F = e·N_{\rm{A}}\)) and gas constant (\(R = k\cdot\!N_{\rm{A}}\)).

name: electrode
definition: Electron conductor in an electrochemical cell connected to the external circuit.  Half-cell consisting of at least one electron conductor and at least one ionic conductor (electrolyte).

name: electrolyte
definition: Conducting medium in which the flow of electric current is accompanied by the movement of ions.  Substance that provides ions on dissolution in a solvent or on melting.

name: electrolytic cell
definition: Electrochemical cell in which electrical energy is converted into chemical energy.

name: electron number of an electrochemical reaction
definition: Number of electrons transferred in a charge transfer reaction between an electrode and a single entity (ion, radical-ion, or molecule) of an electroactive substance, whose identity must be specified.

name: equilibrium electrode potential
definition: Potential of an electrode when no electric current flows through the cell and all local charge transfer equilibria across phase boundaries that are represented in the cell diagram (except at possible electrolyte-electrolyte junctions) and local chemical equilibria are established.

name: formal electrode potential
definition: Equilibrium electrode potential under conditions of unit concentration of species involved in the electrode reaction. \[E_{\rm{eq}} = E^{\circ\prime} - (RT/zF) \mathop \sum \limits_{i}  u_{i} \ln(c_{i}/c^{\circ)\] where \(E_{\rm{eq}}\) is the equilibrium electrode potential, \(R\) the gas constant, \(T\) the thermodynamic temperature, \(F\) the Faraday constant, \(z\) the electron number of an electrochemical reaction, \( u_{\rm{i}}\) the stoichiometric coefficients (numbers of species) in the equation of the electrode reaction (positive for products and negative for reactants), and \(c_{\rm{i}}\) are the amount concentrations of the species involved (most usually ions).

name: galvanic cell
definition: Electrochemical cell in which chemical reactions occur spontaneously and chemical energy is converted into electrical energy.

name: line representation of electrochemical cells
definition: Notation giving electrodes, electroactive substances, and other relevant information for an electrochemical cell. The notation starts and finishes with an electrode. Phase boundaries are denoted with a solid vertical bar \(|\), boundaries between miscible liquids by a vertical dashed bar \(¦\), and a liquid junction by double vertical dashed bars \(¦¦\).

name: Nernst equation
definition: Fundamental equation in electrochemistry that describes the dependence of the equilibrium electrode potential on the composition of the contacting phases, written as a reduction: \[E_{\rm{eq}} = E^{\circ}\!-\!(RT/zF)\mathop \sum \limits_i  u_i \ln(a_i)\] where \(E_{\rm{eq}}\) is the equilibrium electrode potential, \(E^{\circ}\) the standard electrode potential of the reaction, \(R\) the gas constant, \(T\) the thermodynamic temperature, \(F\) the Faraday constant, \(z\) the electron number of an electrochemical reaction, and \( u_{\rm{i}}\) are the stoichiometric coefficients (numbers of species) in the equation of the electrode reaction, positive for products and negative for reactants, while \(a_{\rm{i}}\) represents the activities of the species involved (most usually ions).

name: Cottrell equation
definition: Equation for diffusion current \(I_{\rm{d}}\) at time \(t\) at a large planar electrode in contact with a semi-infinite layer of unstirred solution containing excess supporting (inert) electrolyte and an electroactive substance of bulk concentration \(c\) when, at the instant \(t = 0\), the potential of the electrode is suddenly changed to a value at which a mass-transport limited electrochemical reaction occurs and the concentration of the electroactive species at the electrode is zero, \[I_{\rm{d}} = zFA{D^{1/2}}c/(\pi^{1/2} t^{1/2})\] where \(z\) is the electron number of an electrochemical reaction in the charge transfer step of the species (being positive for an oxidation and negative for a reduction), \(F\) the Faraday constant, \(A\) the electrode surface area, and \(D\) the diffusion coefficient of the electroactive substance.

name: current-potential curve
definition: Plot of current versus applied potential (\(I\!{-}\!E\)) for a given system.

name: electrochemical biosensor
definition: Electrochemical sensor that has a biological recognition element.

name: electrochemical sensor
definition: Measuring system in which the response to an electrochemical reaction is converted, via a suitable transducer, into a measurable electrical signal.

name: electrode coverage density
definition: Amount of a chemical modifier at an electrode surface per unit area.

name: electrode surface area
definition: Area of electrode–solution interface.

name: Faraday’s laws of electrolysis
definition: Faraday’s First Law of electrolysis: Mass \(m\) of electrochemically-transformed substance is proportional to the charge \(Q\) passed, \(m\! \propto\! Q\). Faraday’s Second Law of electrolysis: When the same electric charge (quantity of electricity) \(Q\) is passed through several electrolytes, the mass \(m_{\rm{i}}\) of the substances deposited are proportional to their respective chemical equivalent molar mass, \(M_{\rm{i}}/z_{\rm{i}}\). \[m_{1}/m_{2} = (M_{1}/z_{1})/(M_{2}/z_{2})\]

name: galvanostat
definition: Instrument which controls the electric current between the working electrode and the auxiliary electrode.

name: open circuit potential
definition: Electrode potential of working electrode relative to the reference electrode when no potential or electric current is being applied to the electrochemical cell.

name: polarizable electrode
definition: Electrode whose potential changes with an applied potential.

name: potentiostat
definition: Measuring instrument for electric current that controls the potential difference between a working electrode and a reference electrode and measures the electric current between a working electrode and an auxiliary electrode.

name: salt bridge
definition: Means of making electrolytic connection between two half cells without introducing a significant liquid junction potential.

name: three-electrode cell
definition: Electrochemical cell with a working electrode, reference electrode, and auxiliary electrode.Schematic of a three-electrode cell. 1 - working electrode, 2 - reference electrode, 3 - auxiliary electrode. The potential between 1 and 2 is set while passing and measuring current between 1 and 3.

name: working potential range
definition: Range of electrode potentials of a given working electrode in a given electrolyte, where the electric current from reactions of the electrode or electrolyte is negligible compared with the current from reactions of the system under investigation.

name: macroelectrode
definition: Electrode with smallest dimension of order millimetre or greater.

name: microelectrode
definition: Electrode with smallest dimension of less than 1 millimetre and greater than 1 micrometre.

name: ultramicroelectrode
definition: Electrode with smallest dimension of less than 25 micrometre.

name: nanoelectrode
definition: Electrode with smallest dimension less than 1 micrometre

name: quasi-reference electrode
definition: Electrode that maintains a constant, but not generally well-defined, potential in an electrochemical cell.

name: glassy carbon electrode
definition: Electrode made of glassy carbon material with an intertwined graphitic ribbon structure, formed by pyrolysis of a resol precursor at temperatures up to \(\pu{3000^{\circ}C}\).

name: highly oriented pyrolytic graphite electrode
definition: Graphite electrode of material produced by high temperature deposition of carbon on a ceramic surface and subject to graphitization at \(\pu{3000^{\circ}C}\)

name: paraffin impregnated graphite electrode
definition: Graphite electrode based on a graphitic material impregnated with paraffin having a high melting point.

name: boron-doped diamond electrode
definition: Electrode composed of a boron-doped diamond film on an electron-conducting substrate.

name: biorecognition
definition: Detection principle for a chemically modified electrode (CME) in which the electrode is modified by a biological recognition element.

name: change of mass
definition: Detection principle for a chemically modified electrode (CME) in which the signal originates from accumulation and/or release of an analyte or reagent as well as other electrochemical processes which can result in changes in the mass of the CME.

name: electrocatalysis
definition: Detection principle for a chemically modified electrode (CME) in which a charge transfer reaction between a CME and analyte proceeds at a lower overpotential than at the bare electrode. Usually, the effect of electrocatalysis is also an increase of faradaic current.

name: redox mediation
definition: Detection principle for a chemically modified electrode (CME) in which an immobilized redox couple can shuttle electrons between the electrode and an analyte, for instance, one with difficult access to the electrode surface because of steric reasons.

name: carbon paste electrode
definition: Electrode of a composite of carbon powder and a pasting liquid (including mineral oil, Nujol, bromoform, bromonaphthalene).

name: carbon ink electrode
definition: Development of a carbon paste electrode that is screen printed using a carbon/polymer mixture of suitable composition.

name: solid amalgam electrode
definition: Electrode made of a solid amalgam of an appropriate metal.

name: gold electrode
definition: Foil, wire or disc electrode made of gold which is easily fabricated into a variety of electrode geometries.

name: platinum electrode
definition: Foil, wire, disc, or mesh electrode made of platinum, which is the most commonly used metallic working electrode in electrochemistry.

name: silver electrode
definition: Electrode in the form of foil, mesh, wire, rod, tube, powder, pellets, or single crystal of silver.

name: mercury electrode
definition: Liquid metal electrode used in polarography.

name: dropping mercury electrode
definition: Mercury electrode formed by sequence of mercury drops falling from a small aperture.

name: bimetallic electrode
definition: Electrode containing two different metals (e.g. platinum and ruthenium) on its surface (e.g. to modify its electrocatalytic properties).

name: chemically-sensitive field effect transistor
definition: Non-faradaic electrode system in which electric field variations in the semiconductor gate region control the magnitude of the source-drain current.

name: chemically-modified electrode
definition: Electrode coated with a thin layer of a substance that exhibits particular chemical, electrochemical, and/or optical properties.

name: enzyme-modified electrode
definition: Chemically-modified electrode in which the products of a reaction between enzymes in an immobilized enzyme layer and the enzyme reaction substrate are electrochemically active and are measured usually by amperometry or potentiometry.Schematic of the mediated oxidation of glucose to gluconolactone by glucose oxidase. The current passed to re-oxidise the mediator is proportional to the amount concentration of glucose.

name: homogeneous crystalline membrane electrodes
definition: ISE in which the membrane is a crystalline material prepared from either a single compound or a homogeneous mixture of compounds.

name: heterogeneous crystalline membrane electrodes
definition: ISE prepared of an active substance, or mixture of active substances, mixed with an inert matrix (such as silicone rubber or \(\ce{PVC}\)), or placed on hydrophobized graphite or conducting epoxy resin, to form a heterogeneous sensing membrane.

name: non-crystalline membrane
definition: Kind of ion-selective membranes used in an ISE which is a support matrix, containing an ion exchanger (either cationic or anionic), a plasticizer solvent, and possibly an uncharged, selectivity-enhancing species, form the ion-selective membrane which is usually interposed between two aqueous solutions. The matrix can be either macroporous (e.g., poly(propylene carbonate) filter, glass frit, etc.) or microporous (e.g., “thirsty” glass or polymeric material such as \(\ce{PVC}\)) yielding with the ion-exchanger and the solvent a “solidified” homogeneous mixture.

name: rigid membranes
definition: Kind of ion-selective membranes used in an ISE comprising synthetic cross-linked polymer with fixed sites or thin glass membrane.

name: membranes with mobile charged sites
definition: Kind of ion-selective membranes used in an ISE comprising:  Positively-charged, hydrophobic cations which, when dissolved in a suitable organic solvent and held in an inert support (e.g., poly(propylenecarbonate) filter or \(\ce{PVC}\)), provide membranes which are sensitive to changes in the activities of anions. Negatively-charged hydrophobic anions which, when dissolved in a suitable organic solvent and held in an inert support (e.g., poly(propylene carbonate) filter or \(\ce{PVC}\)), provide membranes which are sensitive to changes of cation activities. Uncharged “carrier” electrodes based on solutions of molecular complexing agents of cations and anions, which can be used for preparing ion exchanger membranes sensitive and selective to certain cations and anions. Hydrophobic ion-pair electrodes of plasticized polymers (e.g., \(\ce{PVC}\)) containing a dissolved hydrophobic ion-pair respond to the ion activities of those components, which are relevant to the ion-pairs incorporated in the membrane. The responses can be Nernstian.

name: combined electrode
definition: Ion-selective electrode cell in which the ion-selective electrode and reference electrode are combined in a single sensor assembly, thereby avoiding the need for a separate external reference electrode.

name: electrode array
definition: Assembly of linked electrodes (usually microelectrodes, ultramicroelectrodes or nanoelectrodes) acting as a single electrode.

name: glass pH-sensitive electrode
definition: pH-sensitive electrode, usually consisting of a bulb, or other suitable form, of special glass attached to a stem of high-resistance glass, complete with an internal reference electrode and internal filling solution system.

name: heterogeneous crystalline membrane ion-selective electrode
definition: Ion-selective electrode in which the ion-selective membrane is a crystalline material mixed with an inert matrix (such as silicone rubber or polyvinyl chloride), or placed on hydrophobized graphite or conducting epoxy resin, to form a heterogeneous sensing membrane.

name: homogeneous crystalline membrane ion-selective electrode
definition: Ion-selective electrode in which the ion-selective membrane is a crystalline material prepared from either a single compound or homogeneous mixture of compounds.

name: ion-selective field effect transistor
definition: Electrochemical sensor based on the principle of the field effect transistor (FET) in which the surface of the gate is modified in a way that makes the response ion-selective.

name: ion-selective membrane
definition: Membrane with controlled permeability to a particular ion covering an electrode, or separating two electrolyte solutions.

name: Nikolsky–Eisenman equation
definition: Equation describing the contribution of interfering ions, \(i\), to the electrode potential of an ion-selective electrode that is mainly dominated by the primary ion \(\ce{X}\). \[E = {\rm{const}} + \frac{RT}{z_{\rm{X}}F} \ln \left(a_{\ce{X}} + \sum\limits_i K_{{\ce{X}},i}^{\rm{pot}}a_{i}^{(z_{\ce{X}}/z_i)} \right)\] where \(E\) is the measured electrode potential of an ISE when the only variables are activities in the test solution. \(R\) is the gas constant, \(T\) the thermodynamic temperature, \(z_{\rm{X}}\) and \(z_{\rm{i}}\) are the numbers of electrons transferred by the analyte ion \(\ce{X}\) and \(i\), respectively, \(F\) is the Faraday constant, \(a_{\rm{X}}\) and \(a_{\rm{i}}\) the activity of \(\ce{X}\) and \(i\), respectively, and \(K_{\ce{X},i}^{\rm{pot}}\) is the potentiometric selectivity coefficient for interfering ion \(i\) with respect to the primary ion \(\ce{X}\).

name: pH-sensitive electrode
definition: Potentiometric electrochemical sensor that measures pH as a linear function of electrode potential.

name: potentiometric enzyme electrode
definition: Enzyme-modified electrode, or an electrode modified by a substrate, cofactor or inhibitor, in which the activity of a product of the enzyme reaction is measured by an ion-selective electrode.

name: potentiometric gas sensor
definition: Ion-selective electrode cell that is responsive to an analyte gas.

name: rotating disc electrode
definition: A disc electrode that is embedded in the centre of a cylinder which rotates in solution around the longitudinal cylinder axis.

name: wall-jet electrode
definition: A disc electrode with a thin circular jet of fluid impinging on its centre.

name: chronopotentiometry
definition: Potentiometry in which the potential is measured with time following a change in applied current.

name: potentiometry
definition: Electrochemical measurement principle where the potential difference between an indicator electrode and a reference electrode is measured.

name: amperometry
definition: Electrochemical measurement principle based on measurement of current at a controlled applied potential.

name: chronoamperometry
definition: Amperometry in which the current is measured as a function of time after a change in the applied potential.

name: AC voltammetry
definition: Voltammetry in which a sinusoidal alternating potential of small amplitude (\(\pu{10 to 50 mV}\)) of constant frequency (\(\pu{10 Hz to 100 kHz}\)) is superimposed on a slowly and linearly varying potential ramp. The resulting alternating current is plotted versus imposed DC potential. The obtained AC voltammogram is peak-shaped.Waveform for AC voltammetry. The applied potential as a function of time is a sinusoidal alternating potential superimposed on a linearly increasing ramp.

name: chronocoulometric constant
definition: Empirically-determined quantity defined by the equation \[{\cal Q} = (1/Ac)\Delta Q/\Delta (t^{1/2})\] where \(A\) is the electrode surface area, \(c\) is the bulk concentration of the electroactive substance, \(Q\) is the charge passed, and \(\Delta Q/\Delta(t^{1/2})\) is the slope of a plot of \(Q\) against \(t^{1/2}\).

name: chronopotentiometric constant
definition: Empirically-evaluated quantity defined by the equation \[{\cal T} = I\tau^{1/2}/(A c_{B}) = j\tau^{1/2}/c_{\ce{B}}\] where \(I\) is the electric current, \(\tau\) is the transition time, \(A\) is the electrode surface area, \(\ce{B}\) is the bulk concentration of the electroactive substance \(\ce{B}\), and \(j=I/A\) is the current density.

name: current sampling
definition: Measurement of electric current in voltammetry.

name: cyclic voltammetry
definition: Voltammetry in which the electric current is recorded as the electrode potential is varied with time cyclically between two potential limits, normally at a constant scan rate.Cyclic voltammetry. (a) Variation of applied potential with time. (b) Cyclic voltammogram of current against applied potential for a reversible redox couple.

name: DC polarography
definition: Linear scan voltammetry with slow scan rate in which a dropping mercury electrode is used as the working electrode. See figure.Electric current as a function of applied potential for DC polarography, showing oscillations of current as the dropping mercury electrode grows and is detached.

name: differential pulse voltammetry
definition: Voltammetry in which small potential pulses (constant height \(\pu{10 to 100 mV}\), constant width \(\pu{10 to 100 ms}\)) are superimposed onto a linearly varying potential or onto a staircase potential ramp. The current is sampled just before the onset of the pulse (e.g. \(\pu{10 to 20 ms}\)) and for the same sampling time just before the end of the pulse. The difference between the two sampled currents is plotted versus the potential applied before the pulse. Thus, a differential pulse voltammogram is peak-shaped.(a) Potential waveform for differential pulse voltammetry (not to scale). Typical values for pulse parameters are $\tau$=1 s, $t_{\rm{p}}$=50 ms, $E_{\tau}$=50 mV, $E_{\rm{p}}$=2 mV. Sampling interval indicated by horizontal curly brackets is typically 15 ms. (b) Differential pulse voltammogram. $I$ is the difference between currents sampled at ‘2’ and ‘1’.

name: Heyrovský–Ilkovič equation
definition: The relationship that describes the electrode potential as a function of the current of a reversible redox system (reversible electrode reaction) in the steady state in voltammetry \[E = E^{\circ\prime} - \frac{RT}{zF} \ln \left(\frac{D_{\rm{red}}}{D_{\rm{ox}}}\right)^{s} \pm \frac{RT}{zF} \ln\!\left(\frac{I_{\rm{d,lim}} - I}{I}\right)\] where \(E^{\circ\prime}\) is the formal electrode potential, \(z\) the electron number of an electrochemical reaction, \(D_{\rm{red}}\) and \(D_{\rm{ox}}\) the diffusion coefficients of the reduced and oxidized forms of the electroactive substance, respectively, \(I_{\rm{d,lim}}\) is the limiting diffusion current, and \(I\) is the current at the potential being applied. The value of the exponent \(s\) is ½ for a stationary or dropping mercury electrode, ⅔ for a hydrodynamic electrode (see hydrodynamic voltammetry), or 1 for a microelectrode. In the equation, the last term is added for reduction and subtracted for oxidation.

name: hydrodynamic voltammetry
definition: Voltammetry with forced flow of the solution towards the electrode surface.

name: Ilkovič equation
definition: Equation relating electric current at a dropping mercury electrode under purely diffusional control, \(I_{{\rm{d,}}t}\), the amount concentration of an electroactive substance at the drop surface \(c\), and the concentration in bulk solution \(c_{\rm{0}}\), \[I_{{\rm{d}},t} = -k\,z\,F\,D^{1/2}q_{\rm{m}}^{2/3} t^{1/6}(c - c_{0})\] where \(k\) is a numerical constant, $z$ the electron number of an electrochemical reaction, \(F\) the Faraday constant, \(D\) the diffusion coefficient of the electroactive substance, \(q_{\rm{m}}\) the mass flux of mercury at the dropping electrode, and \(t\) the time elapsed from the beginning of the drop.

name: Levich equation
definition: Equation relating limiting current at a rotating disc electrode (see hydrodynamic voltammetry) to the amount concentration of an electroactive substance in bulk solution \(c_{0}\), \[I_{\rm{lim}} = k\,z\,F\,A\,D^{2/3} \omega^{1/2}  u^{−1/6} c_{0}\] where \(k\) is a numerical factor, \(z\) the electron number of an electrochemical reaction, \(F\) the Faraday constant, \(A\) the electrode surface area, \(D\) the diffusion coefficient of the electroactive substance, \(\omega\) the angular velocity (rotation rate), and \( u\) the kinematic viscosity of the solution.

name: linear-scan voltammetry
definition: Voltammetry in which the electric current is recorded as the electrode potential is varied linearly with time. See figure.Linear scan voltammogram of current against applied potential for a reversible redox couple.

name: normal pulse voltammetry
definition: Voltammetry in which potential pulses of amplitude increasing by a constant increment and with a pulse width of \(\pu{2 to 200 ms}\) are superimposed on a constant initial potential. The current is sampled at the end of the pulse and then plotted versus the potential of the pulse. Sigmoidal wave-shaped voltammograms are obtained. See figure.(a) Waveform for normal pulse voltammetry (not to scale). Typical values for pulse parameters are \(\tau = \pu{1 s}\), \(t_{\rm{p}} = \pu{50 ms}\), \(E_{\rm{p}} = \pu{2 mV}\), \(E_{\rm{step}} = \pu{2 mV}\). Sampling interval indicated by horizontal curly brackets is typically \(\pu{15 ms}\). (b) Normal pulse voltammogram.

name: Randles–Ševčík equations
definition: Equations describing the peak current \(I_{\rm{p}}\) in linear scan voltammetry and cyclic voltammetry as a function of the amount concentration, \(c_{\rm{0}}\), of electroactive species in bulk solution. For a reversible charge transfer: \[I_{\rm{p,rev}} = k\,z\,F\,A\,c_0 (z\,F\,D u/RT)^{1/2}\] for irreversible charge transfer: \[I_{\rm{p,irrev}} = k^{\prime}(\alpha z^{\prime})^{1/2} zFA{c_0}(FD u/RT)^{1/2}\] where \(k\) and \(k^{\prime}\) are numerical constants, \(\alpha\) is the charge transfer coefficient (usually assumed to be close to 0.5), \(z\) the electron number of an electrochemical reaction, \(z^{\prime}\) the number of electrons transferred before the rate determining step, \(F\) the Faraday constant, \(R\) the gas constant, \(T\) the thermodynamic temperature, \(A\) the electrode surface area, \(D\) the diffusion coefficient, and \( u\) the scan rate.

name: rate of flow of liquid metal in polarography
definition: Mass of a drop of liquid metal in polarography at the instant when it is detached from the tip of the capillary divided by the drop time \(t_{\rm{d}}\).

name: sampled DC polarography
definition: DC polarography with current sampling at the end of each drop life mechanically enforced by a knocker at a preset drop time value. The current sampling and mechanical drop dislodge are synchronized.

name: scan rate
definition: The rate of change of applied potential with time.
synonyms: potential scan rate|potential sweep rate|sweep rate

name: square-wave voltammetry
definition: Voltammetry in which a square-wave potential waveform is superimposed on an underlying linearlyhyphen‐varying potential ramp or staircase ramp. The current is sampled just before the end of the forward-going pulse and of the backward-going pulse and the difference of the two sampled currents is plotted versus the applied potential of the potential or staircase ramp. The square-wave voltammogram is peak-shaped. See figure.(a) Waveform for square wave voltammetry (not to scale). Typical values for pulse parameters are \(\tau = \pu{10 ms}\), \(t_{\rm{p}} = \pu{5 ms}\), \(E_{\rm{\tau}} = \pu{25 mV}\), \(E_{\rm{step}} = \pu{4 mV}\). Sampling interval indicated by horizontal curly brackets is typically \(\pu{1 ms}\). (b) Square wave voltammogram of the difference between currents sampled at ‘2’ and ‘1’ against applied potential.

name: voltammetry
definition: Electrochemical measurement principle in which the electrode potential of a working electrode is controlled and the electric current measured.

name: voltammogram
definition: Current-potential curve in a voltammetry experiment.

name: accumulation in stripping voltammetry
definition: Transfer of an analyte from a test solution to an electrode surface as the first step in stripping voltammetry.

name: adsorptive stripping voltammetry
definition: Stripping voltammetry involving pre-concentration by adsorption of the analyte (in contrast to electrochemical accumulation).

name: anodic stripping voltammetry
definition: Stripping voltammetry in which material accumulated at the working electrode is electrochemically oxidized in the stripping step.

name: cathodic stripping voltammetry
definition: Stripping voltammetry in which material accumulated at the working electrode is electrochemically reduced in the stripping step. See figure.Applied potential against time during the accumulation and stripping steps in cathodic stripping voltammetry.

name: potentiometric stripping analysis
definition: Two-step electrochemical measurement in which 1) material is accumulated at an electrode and 2) the material is removed by chemical reaction or electrochemically at constant current with measurement of electrode potential. The time between changes in potential in step two is related to the concentration of analyte in the solution.

name: stripping voltammetry
definition: Two-step electrochemical measurement in which 1) material is accumulated at an electrode and 2) the amount of an accumulated species is measured by voltammetry. The measured electric current in step 2 is related to the concentration of analyte in the solution by calibration.

name: chronocoulometry
definition: Direct coulometry at controlled potential in which the electric charge passed after the application of a potential step perturbation is measured as a function of time (\(Q{-}t\) curve).

name: coulometer
definition: Measuring instrument to obtain the electrical charge passed in an experiment, or to produce a known amount of substance in a titration.

name: coulometry
definition: Electrochemical measurement principle in which the electric charge required to carry out a known electrochemical reaction is measured. By Faraday’s laws of electrolysis, the amount of substance is proportional to the charge.

name: direct coulometry at controlled current
definition: Coulometry at an imposed, constant electric current in the electrochemical cell.

name: direct coulometry at controlled potential
definition: Coulometry at a preselected constant potential of the working electrode.Electric current against time showing the representation of the electric charge in direct coulometry at controlled potential as the area under the graph.

name: electrochemical piezoelectric microgravimetry
definition: Electrogravimetry using an electrochemical quartz crystal microbalance.

name: electrochemical quartz crystal microbalance
definition: Electrochemical cell in which the working electrode is located on one surface of a piezoelectric quartz crystal, the oscillation frequency of which is measured.

name: electrogravimetry
definition: Gravimetry in which the material to be weighed is obtained by electrochemical reaction.

name: conductometric titration
definition: Titration in which the electric conductivity of a solution is measured as a function of the amount of titrant added.Conductimetric titration curve of conductance ($G$) against volume of titrant. The end-point of the titration is indicated by a change in slope of the graph.

name: conductometry
definition: Measurement principle in which the electric conductivity of a solution is measured.

name: dielectrometry
definition: Electrochemical measurement principle based on the measurement of the dielectric constant of a sample resulting from the orientation of particles (molecules or ions) that have a dipole moment in an electric field.

name: electrochemical impedance spectroscopy
definition: Electrochemical measurement method of the complex impedance of an electrochemical system as a function of the frequency of a small amplitude (normally \(\pu{5 to 10 mV}\)) sinusoidal voltage perturbation superimposed on a fixed value of applied potential or on the open circuit potential.

name: impedimetry
definition: Measurement principle in which the complex electric impedance of a system is measured, usually as a function of a small amplitude sinusoidal electrode potential.

name: electrochemical detection in flowing systems
definition: Electrochemical techniques (potentiometry, amperometry, voltammetry, coulometry, conductimetry) used for analyte detection in flowing systems.

name: spectroelectrochemistry
definition: Measurement methods combining spectrometric and electrochemical measurements.

name: Auger spectroscopy
definition: Measurement method of electron emission spectroscopy that utilizes Auger electrons emitted from the target following excitation with an electron beam or X-ray beam.

name: Auger photoelectron coincidence spectroscopy
definition: Detection of an Auger electron and a core-level photoelectron, emitted from a solid irradiated by mono-energetic X-rays, within a sufficiently short time that the Auger electron shall arise from the decay of the particular core-hole associated with the photoelectron.

name: elastic peak electron spectroscopy
definition: Measurement method in which an electron spectrometer is used to measure the energy, intensity, and/or energy broadening distribution of quasi-elastically scattered electrons from a solid or liquid surface.

name: direct recoil spectroscopy
definition: Measurement method to elucidate composition and structure of the outermost atomic layers of a solid material, in which principally monoenergetic neutral atoms or singly charged probe ions are used to sputter atoms or ions out of the solid surface, their energy being recorded at one or more angle of scattering.
synonyms: elastic recoil detection|elastic recoil detection analysis

name: low-energy ion scattering spectrometry
definition: Measurement method to elucidate the composition and structure of the very outermost atomic layers of a solid material, in which principally monoenergetic, singly-charged probe ions scattered from the surface are detected and recorded as a function of their energy, angle of scattering, or both.

name: medium-energy ion scattering spectrometry
