definition: Measurement method to elucidate the composition and structure of the outermost atomic layers of a solid material, in which principally monoenergetic, singly-charged probe ions scattered from the surface are detected and recorded as a function of their energy, angle of scattering, or both.

name: Rutherford backscattering spectrometry
definition: Measurement method to elucidate composition and structure of layers at the surface of a solid material, in which principally monoenergetic, singly charged probe ions scattered from the surface with a Rutherford cross section are detected and recorded as a function of their energy or angle of scattering, or both.

name: desorption atmospheric pressure chemical ionization mass spectrometry
definition: Measurement method in which a mass spectrometer is used to measure the ratio of mass to charge and the abundance of ionized entities emitted from a sample in air as a result of a nearby corona discharge in a humid carrier gas.

name: desorption atmospheric pressure photoionization mass spectrometry
definition: Measurement method in which a mass spectrometer is used to measure the ratio of mass to charge and the abundance of ionized entities emitted from a sample in air as a result of desorption by a jet of hot solvent vapour and ionization by ultraviolet light.

name: desorption electrospray ionization mass spectrometry
definition: Measurement method in which a mass spectrometer is used to measure the ratio of mass to charge and the abundance of ionized entities emitted from a sample in air as a result of the bombardment by ionized solvent droplets generated by pneumatically assisted electrospray ionization.

name: direct analysis in real time
definition: Measurement method in which a mass spectrometer is used to measure the ratio of mass to charge and the abundance of ionized entities emitted from a sample in air as a result of the interaction with a beam containing metastable, excited atoms heated to about \(\pu{500^{\circ}C}\).

name: dynamic secondary-ion mass spectrometry
definition: Secondary-ion mass spectrometry analysis with primary ion current density sufficiently high for use in the analysis of sample surface layers in the depth direction.

name: electrospray laser desorption ionization mass spectrometry
definition: Measurement method in which a mass spectrometer is used to measure the ratio of mass to charge quotient and the abundance of ionized entities emitted from a sample in air via ablation by a focused pulsed laser while simultaneously directing an electrospray jet through the desorbed plume to enhance sample ionization.

name: extractive electrospray ionization mass spectrometry
definition: Measurement method in which a mass spectrometer is used to measure the ratio of mass to charge and the abundance of ionized entities emitted from a sample in air as a result of an inert gas being passed over the sample to pick up the molecules, which are subsequently ionized by ionized solvent droplets generated by pneumatically assisted electrospray ionization.

name: G-SIMS
definition: Variant of static secondary-ion mass spectrometry in which the intensities for each mass in two spectra from the same area, recorded with different beam energies or different bombarding ions, are ratioed to each other and the result is used to scale one of the spectra to generate a new spectrum.

name: laser ablation electrospray ionization mass spectrometry
definition: Measurement method in which a mass spectrometer is used to measure the ratio of mass to charge and the abundance of ionized entities emitted from a sample in air as a result of laser ablation and electrospray ionization.

name: matrix-assisted laser desorption electrospray ionization mass spectrometry
definition: Measurement method in which a mass spectrometer is used to measure the ratio of mass to charge and the abundance of ionized entities from a sample that has been mixed with a matrix whose role is enhancing the ion yield produced by laser ablation and electrospray ionization.

name: matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry
definition: Measurement method in which a time-of-flight mass spectrometer is used to measure the ratio of mass to charge and the abundance of ions emitted, as a result of a short pulse of laser illumination, from a sample whose analyte is contained in a matrix that assists the formation of ions.

name: plasma assisted desorption ionization mass spectrometry
definition: Measurement method in which a mass spectrometer is used to measure the ratio of mass to charge and the abundance of ionized entities emitted from a sample in air as a result of the bombardment by a focused plasma.

name: reactive desorption electrospray ionization mass spectrometry
definition: Mode of desorption electrospray ionization mass spectrometry with reactive chemicals within the spray solution to enhance the analytical specificity.

name: secondary-ion mass spectrometry
definition: Measurement method in which a focused beam of primary ions produces secondary ions by sputtering from a solid surface. The secondary ions are analysed by mass spectrometry.

name: static secondary-ion mass spectrometry
definition: Method of secondary-ion mass spectrometry using low current densities for analysis of sample surface components, in contrast with dynamic secondary-ion mass spectrometry, which is used for analysis of components in the depth direction.

name: surface-assisted laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry
definition: Matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry using a combined liquid and particulate matrix.

name: attenuated total reflection infrared spectroscopy
definition: Attenuated total reflection spectroscopy in which the infrared absorption spectrum of a sample in contact with a prism is measured.

name: diffuse reflection-absorption infrared spectroscopy
definition: Measurement method in which the infrared absorption spectrum of light reflected and transmitted from powdered samples is measured.
synonyms: diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy

name: ellipsometry
definition: Measurement method for the thickness of transparent surface films and layers and for the refractive index of a reflecting material.

name: extended X-ray absorption fine structure spectroscopy
definition: X-ray absorption fine structure spectroscopy in the energy region from the core-level edge to an energy several hundred $\pu{eV}$ greater.

name: grazing-incidence small-angle X-ray scattering analysis
definition: Measurement method in which the elastically scattered intensity of X-rays from a reflecting surface is measured for small-angle deflections at grazing incidence.

name: off-specular X-ray reflectometry
definition: X-ray reflectometry in which significant scattered intensity arises from imperfections in the specimen, the scattered intensity falling outside the specular condition (see specular X-ray reflectometry).

name: reflection-absorption infrared spectroscopy
definition: Spectroscopy based on reflection-absorption.

name: scanning near-field optical microscopy
definition: Measurement method in microscopy in which spectroscopic data may be collected with the detector closer to the sample than the optical wavelength employed.
synonyms: SNOM|near-field optical microscopy|near-field scanning optical microscopy (NSOM)

name: small-angle X-ray scattering
definition: Measurement method in which the elastically scattered intensity of X-rays is measured for small-angle deflections.

name: specular X-ray reflectrometry
definition: Mode of X-ray reflectrometry in which the angle between the detected beam and the sample surface is equal to that of the incident beam and the sample surface.

name: sum frequency generation spectroscopy
definition: Measurement method from non-linear optics in which a structurally-ordered sample at an interface between two phases is irradiated by single frequency visible and variable frequency infrared pulses of light to generate a sum frequency vibrational spectrum of the interfacial species without any bulk phase contribution.

name: surface extended X-ray absorption fine structure spectroscopy
definition: Extended X-ray absorption fine structure spectroscopy in which, instead of measuring X-ray absorption, electron emission arising from that absorption is measured.

name: surface-enhanced infrared spectroscopy
definition: Measurement method giving enhanced infrared absorption in the measured infrared spectrum of a sample adsorbed on a roughened thin metal substrate. The metal substrate is deposited onto a prism and data is collected by total internal reflection.

name: surface-enhanced resonant Raman spectroscopy
definition: Measurement method of surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) by which the Raman spectrum is significantly enhanced under the conditions that, whilst undergoing SERS, the molecules are excited by radiation that is in resonance with electronic transitions in the sample.

name: tip enhanced raman spectroscopy
definition: Measurement method of Raman spectroscopy combining surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy and scanning using an atomic force microscope or scanning tunnelling microscope to produce maps of a surface.

name: total reflection X-ray fluorescence spectroscopy
definition: Measurement method in which an X-ray spectrometer is used to measure the energy distribution of fluorescence X-rays emitted from a surface irradiated by primary X-rays under the condition of total reflection.

name: X-ray absorption fine structure spectroscopy
definition: Measurement method to measure the absorption of X-rays at energies near and above (typically several hundred \(\pu{eV}\) greater) an absorption edge, over which fine structure (modulation of the X-ray absorption coefficient) can be detected.

name: X-ray absorption near-edge spectroscopy
definition: X-ray absorption fine structure spectroscopy in the energy region near (within approximately \(\pu{100 eV}\)) an absorption edge.
synonyms: XANES|near-edge extended X-ray absorption fine structure spectroscopy (NEXAFS)

name: X-ray reflectometry
definition: Measurement method for surface and interface roughness and density, layer thickness of thin layers, and electron density profile achieved by reflecting X-rays from a flat sample and analysing the reflected intensity as a function of angle.

name: X-ray standing waves
definition: Measurement method based on the interference of X-rays that occurs near the Bragg condition at the surface of a crystalline solid, which leads to intensity maxima in yields of photoelectrons as the Bragg condition is scanned by tilting the sample.

name: absolute elemental sensitivity factor
definition: Coefficient for an element by which the measured intensity for that element is divided to yield the atomic concentration or atomic fraction of the element present in the sample.

name: altered layer
definition: Surface region of a material under particle bombardment where the chemical state or physical structure is modified by the effects of the bombardment.

name: analysis area
definition: Two-dimensional region of a sample surface measured in the plane of that surface, from which the entire analytical signal or a specified fraction of that signal is detected.

name: analysis area
definition: Two-dimensional region of a sample surface at the analytical point, but set in the plane at right angles to the spectrometer axis, from which the entire analytical signal or a specified fraction of that signal is detected.

name: angle lapping
definition: Sample preparation in which a sample is mechanically polished at an angle to the original surface.

name: angle of emission
definition: Angle between the trajectory of a particle or photon, as it leaves a surface, and the local or average surface normal.

name: areic dose rate
definition: Areic dose introduced into a solid in time interval \(t\) divided by \(t\).

name: areic dose
definition: Number, \(N\), of energetic particles of a specified type introduced into a solid through a surface area \(A\) divided by \(A\). \(D = N/A\).

name: areic surface energy
definition: Energy required to increase a surface area at thermodynamic equilibrium divided by that increase in area.

name: atomic mixing
definition: Migration of sample atoms due to energy transfer with incident particles in the surface region.

name: Auger neutralization
definition: Process in which an electron, tunnelling from the conduction band of a solid, neutralizes an incoming ion and an electron is ejected from a surface atom.

name: average beam current
definition: Electric charge of specified polarity in a beam passing in time interval \(t\), divided by \(t\).

name: backscattering energy
definition: Energy of a particle from the primary beam after it has undergone a backscattering collision and escaped from the sample.

name: ball cratering
definition: Procedure in which the sample is abraded by a sphere in order to expose compositional changes in layers below the original surface, with the intent that the depth of those layers can be related to the lateral position in the crater created by the abrasion.

name: binary elastic scattering
definition: Collision between a moving particle and a second particle in which total kinetic energy and total momentum are conserved.

name: Bragg’s rule
definition: Empirical rule formulated by W.H. Bragg and R. Kleeman that states that the stopping cross section of a compound sample is equal to the sum of the products of the elemental stopping cross sections for each constituent and its atomic fraction. \[S_{\ce{AB}}(\varepsilon) = xS_{\ce{A}}(\varepsilon) + yS_{\ce{B}}(\varepsilon)\] where \(S_{\ce{AB}}(\varepsilon)\) is the stopping cross section of the compound \(\ce{A}_{x}\ce{B}_{y}\), and \(S_{\ce{A}}(\varepsilon)\) and \(S_{\ce{B}}(\varepsilon)\) are the stopping cross sections of elements \(\ce{A}\) and \(\ce{B}\), respectively.

name: cascade mixing
definition: Diffusion-like process in which atoms of material are moved randomly by energy deposited by incident particles slowing down in the sample surface region.

name: channeling
definition: Preferential motion of energetic particles along the crystal axes of a crystalline solid as the particles move through the sample.

name: charge neutralization
definition: Maintenance at a fixed potential, usually near neutrality, of the surface of a non-conducting or poorly conducting sample material under bombardment by primary particles or photons.

name: charging potential
definition: Electric potential of the surface region of an insulating sample, caused by irradiation.

name: chemical map
definition: Surface map using signals proportional to the amount of an element in a particular chemical state in the sample.

name: chromatic aberration
definition: Non-ideal focus of an electron or ion optical system for electrons or ions of different energies.

name: collision cascade
definition: Sequential energy transfer between atoms in a solid as a result of bombardment by an energetic species.

name: compositional depth profile
definition: Chemical composition measured as a function of distance normal to the surface.

name: crater depth
definition: Average depth of the region of a crater from which the measured signal is derived.

name: cross-sectioning
definition: Sample preparation in which the sample is cleaved, cut, or polished in a plane perpendicular to the interface under study, so that associated compositional differences or gradients can be observed in that plane.

name: damage limit
definition: Particle fluence above which significant changes in the spectrum or in a stated peak, arising from damage processes, are observed.

name: delta layer
definition: Layer of discrete composition, one atom thick, formed during the growth of material on a substrate.

name: depth profiling
definition: Monitoring of signal intensity as a function of a variable that can be related to distance normal to the surface.

name: depth resolution parameter
definition: Parameter that can be used as a coefficient in an analytic fit to a measured compositional depth profile or as a qualitative way of describing that profile.

name: elastic scattering cross section
definition: Cross section for binary elastic scattering.

name: electron flooding
definition: Irradiation of a sample with low-energy electrons in order to change or stabilize the charging potential.

name: elemental map
definition: Surface map using signals proportional to the amount of an element present in a sample.

name: erosion rate
definition: Change in the position of the surface as a result of particle or photon irradiation divided by time of irradiation.

name: field-induced migration
definition: Effect occurring in insulators or semi-conductors where internal electric fields cause the migration of sample atoms.

name: flux of a beam of particles
definition: \(\mathit{\Phi} = {\rm{d}}N/{\rm{d}}t\), where \(N\) is number of particles of a specified type and \(t\) is time.

name: focused ion beam system
definition: Ion beam system used for machining small regions with sub-micron precision.

name: fractional sputtering yield
definition: Number of atoms and ions of a particular species sputtered from a sample divided by the total number of atoms and ions sputtered from the sample.

name: image depth profile
definition: Three-dimensional representation of the spatial distribution of a particular elemental or molecular species, as indicated by emitted secondary ions or electrons, as a function of depth or material removed by sputtering.

name: impact energy
definition: Kinetic energy of particles on impact with a sample surface.

name: implanted areic dose
definition: Number, \(N_{\rm{imp}}\), of energetic particles of a specified type incident on a solid within a surface area \(A\) and stopped within the solid divided by \(A\). \(D_{\rm{imp}} = N_{\rm{imp}}/A\).

name: information depth
definition: Maximum depth, normal to the surface, from which useful information is obtained.

name: information radius
definition: Maximum radius of a circular region, in the plane of the surface, from which useful information is obtained.

name: instrumental depth resolution
definition: Depth resolution in a sample arising from parameters of the instrument.

name: ion beam
definition: Directed flux of charged atoms or molecules.

name: ion implantation
definition: Injection of ions into a sample.

name: line scan
definition: Plot of output signal intensity from a spectrometer, signal intensity from another detector, or processed intensity information from the available software along a line corresponding to a line on the sample surface.

name: matrix factor
definition: Factors, arising from the composition of the matrix, for multiplying the quotient of the measured intensity and the appropriate sensitivity factor in formulae to determine the composition using surface analytical techniques.

name: mean escape depth
definition: Average depth normal to the surface from which specified particles or radiations escape.

name: partial sputtering yield
definition: Number of atoms and ions of a particular species sputtered from a sample divided by the total number of incident particles.

name: peak energy
definition: Energy value corresponding to the intensity maximum in a direct spectrum or to the intensity minimum (i.e. the negative excursion) for a differential spectrum.

name: photoionization cross section
definition: Total ionization cross section for an incident photon of a given energy interacting with a material to produce one or more photoelectrons from all sub-shells that are energetically accessible.

name: plasmon
definition: Excitation of valence-band electrons in a solid in which collective oscillations are generated.

name: preferential sputtering
definition: Change in equilibrium surface composition of the sample, which can occur when sputtering multicomponent samples.

name: primary beam
definition: Directed flux of beam particles or photons incident on a sample.

name: projected range
definition: Distance from the surface at which an energetic ion or atom comes to rest in the sample, projected along the direction of the beam.

name: radial sectioning
definition: Sample preparation in which a sample is polished by a cylinder in order to expose compositional changes below the original sample surface, with the intent that the depth of these layers can be related to the position on the surface created by the cylinder.

name: range straggling
definition: Standard deviation of the projected ranges of energetic ions or atoms of a given energy.

name: raster
definition: Two-dimensional pattern generated by the deflection of a primary beam.

name: redeposition
definition: Deposition of sputtered sample material back onto the sample surface.

name: relative instrument spectral response function
definition: In Auger electron spectroscopy (AES), secondary-ion mass spectrometry, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, the spectrometer response function divided by the response function of a reference instrument, or the average for several such instruments, as a function of energy (AES, XPS, etc.) or mass (SIMS).

name: relative resolution
definition: Resolution of a spectrometer at a given energy, mass, or wavelength divided by that energy, mass, or wavelength.

name: relative sputtering rate
definition: Sputtering rate of a sample divided by the sputtering rate of a reference sample sputtered under the same conditions.

name: sample bias
definition: Electric potential applied to the whole or part of the sample, referenced to the electric potential of the sample holder.

name: sample charging
definition: Change in the electrical potential in the sample or on the sample surface caused by particle or photon bombardment.

name: sample voltage
definition: Electric potential difference of the sample referenced to ground.

name: solid angle of analyser
definition: Solid angle allowing particles or photons to be transmitted from a point on the sample to the detector.

name: spectrometer response function
definition: Number of particles detected with a spectrometer divided by the number of such particles per solid angle and per interval of the dispersing parameter available for measurement as a function of the dispersing parameter.

name: spectrometer transmission function
definition: Number of particles transmitted by the analyser divided by the number of such particles per solid angle and per interval of the dispersing parameter (e.g. energy, mass, or wavelength) available for measurement as a function of the dispersing parameter.

name: sputter depth profile
definition: Compositional depth profile obtained when the surface composition is measured while material is removed by sputtering.

name: sputtering rate
definition: Amount, mass, or number of entities of sample material removed, as a result of particle bombardment, per unit time.

name: sputtering yield
definition: Number of atoms and ions sputtered from a sample divided by the total number of incident primary particles.

name: standard vacuum level
definition: Electric potential \(\pu{4.500 eV}\) above the Fermi level.

name: steady-state sputtering
definition: State of the sputtering process in which important operational and analytical parameters are unchanging over a meaningful timescale.

name: steady-state surface composition sputtering
definition: Steady-state surface composition produced by sputtering a homogeneous sample under non-varying conditions.

name: stoichiometric sputtering
definition: State of the sputtering process in which the relative amounts of the elemental components sputtered from a sample are equal to their stoichiometry within the sample.

name: surface excess amount
definition: For an interface, the difference between the amount of component actually present in the system and that which would be present (in a reference system) if the bulk concentration in the adjoining phases were maintained up to a chosen geometrical dividing surface (Gibbs dividing surface).

name: surface map
definition: Two- or three-dimensional representation of the sample surface where the information at each point in the representation, given by a brightness or colour or as a length in a third dimension, is related to the output signal from a detector or processed intensity information from the available software.

name: surface plasmon
definition: Collective motion of electrons on an interface of two phases which have different permittivity, of which one must have electrical conductivity to sustain the collective motion.

name: surface segregation
definition: Partitioning of a species from the bulk of a material to the surface as a result of kinetic or thermodynamic effects.

name: take-off angle
definition: Angle between the trajectory of a particle as it leaves a surface and the local or average surface plane.

name: thermionic work function
definition: Parameter describing the apparent work function of a solid that controls the electronic current density, \(J\), emitted from a conductor at temperature \(T\). \(W = -kT\ln(J/AT^{2})\), where \(k\) is the Boltzmann constant and \(A\) is the Richardson constant.

name: topographic contrast
definition: Contrast in a surface map or image arising from the topography of the sample surface.

name: total ion yield
definition: Number of ions of both signs sputtered from a sample divided by the number of incident particles.

name: vacuum level
definition: Energy level of an electron positioned at rest just outside a solid, i.e. with zero kinetic energy with respect to the sample surface.

name: vacuum level at infinity
definition: Electric potential of the vacuum at a point in space.

name: volume yield
definition: Volume sputtered from a sample divided by number of incident particles.

name: X-ray linewidth
definition: Energy width of the principal characteristic X-ray line.

name: X-ray monochromator
definition: Device used to eliminate photons of energies other than those in a narrow energy or wavelength band.

name: adventitious carbon referencing
definition: In X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, measurement of the charging potential of a particular sample from a comparison of the experimentally measured \(\ce{C 1s}\) binding energy, arising from adsorbed hydrocarbons on the sample, with a standard binding energy value.

name: asymmetry parameter
definition: In X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy factor which characterizes the intensity distribution, \(L(\gamma)\), of photoelectrons ejected by X-rays from isolated atoms at an angle \(\gamma\) from the incident X-ray direction. In the dipole approximation, \(L(\gamma) = 1 + ½\beta [3(\sin^{2}\gamma)/2-1]\).

name: Auger electron spectrum
definition: Plot of intensity of Auger electrons as a function of the electron kinetic energy, usually as part of the energy distribution of detected electrons.

name: Auger parameter
definition: Kinetic energy of a narrow Auger electron peak in a spectrum minus the kinetic energy of the most intense X-ray photoelectron peak from the same element.

name: Auger vacancy satellite
definition: Emission of an Auger electron in which additional spectator holes are present in the initial state or the final state) for the transition.

name: average matrix relative sensitivity factor
definition: Coefficient, proportional to the intensity, calculated for an element in an average matrix, by which the measured intensity for that element is divided in calculations to yield the atomic concentration or atomic fraction of the element present in the sample.

name: backscattered electron
definition: Electron, originating in the incident beam, which is emitted after interaction with the sample.

name: backscattering correction factor
definition: In Auger electron spectroscopy, factor equal to the total Auger-electron current arising from ionizations in the sample caused by both primary electrons and backscattered electrons divided by the Auger-electron current arising directly from the primary electrons.

name: backscattering fraction
definition: In Auger electron spectroscopy, Auger-electron current arising from ionizations in the sample caused by backscattered electrons divided by Auger-electron current arising directly from the primary electrons.

name: backscattering yield
definition: Number of electrons emitted from the sample with energies greater than \(\pu{50 eV}\) divided by the number of electrons incident at a given energy and angle of incidence.

name: characteristic electron energy losses
definition: Inelastic scattering of electrons in solids that produces a non-uniform energy loss spectrum determined by the characteristics of the material.

name: charge referencing
definition: Measurement of charging potential of a sample in order to correct the measured energies so that those energies correspond to a sample with no surface charge.

name: chemical state
definition: State of an atom arising from its chemical interaction with neighbouring atoms in a molecule, compound, solid, liquid, or gas that leads to a characteristic energy or feature observable in electron spectroscopy.

name: chemical state plot
definition: In X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, plot of the measured kinetic energy of a sharp Auger electron peak versus the binding energy of a photoelectron peak for the same element.

name: differential spectrum
definition: Differential of a direct spectrum with respect to energy by an analogue electrode modulation method or by the numerical differentiation of that spectrum.

name: direct spectrum
definition: Spectrum of intensity of electrons transmitted and detected by a spectrometer with a dispersing energy analyser as a function of energy, \(E\).

name: dynamic emittance matching
definition: Electron or ion optical method of steering a spectrometer axis to align with the impact area of the primary beam at all points of a raster scan on the sample surface.

name: effective attenuation length
definition: Parameter that, when introduced in place of the electron inelastic mean free path into an expression derived for Auger electron spectroscopy and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy on the assumption that elastic scattering effects are negligible for a given quantitative application, will correct that expression for elastic scattering effects.

name: Einstein photoelectric equation
definition: Equation relating the kinetic energy of an electron, emitted from a conductor illuminated by monochromatic photons, and the photon energy and work function of the surface from which the photoelectron is emitted. \(½m_{\rm{e}}  u_{\rm{max}}^{2} = h u - \phi_{0}\), where \(m_{\rm{e}}\) is the mass of an electron, \( u_{\rm{max}}\) the maximum velocity of the emitted electron, \(h\) the Planck constant, \( u\) the frequency of the illuminating photons, and \(\phi_{0}\) the photoelectric work function of the surface.

name: elastic peak
definition: Peak in the electron spectrum, produced by quasi-elastically scattered electrons detected by an electron spectrometer.

name: electron energy analyser
definition: Measuring instrument for measuring the number of electrons, or an intensity proportional to that number, as a function of the electron kinetic energy.

name: electron energy loss spectrum
definition: Energy spectrum of electrons from a nominally monoenergetic source emitted after inelastic interactions with the sample, often exhibiting peaks due to specific inelastic loss processes (see characteristic electron energy losses and plasmon).

name: electron inelastic mean free path
definition: Average distance that an electron with a given energy travels between successive inelastic collisions.

name: electron retardation
definition: In Auger electron spectroscopy and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, measurement method for kinetic energy distribution by retarding the emitted electrons before or within the electron energy analyser.

name: electron spectrometer
definition: Measuring system, the essential part of which is an electron energy analyser.

name: elemental relative sensitivity factor
definition: In dynamic secondary-ion mass spectrometry, coefficient for an element by which the measured intensity of a mass peak for that element, divided by the measured intensity of a mass peak for the matrix, is multiplied to yield the atomic concentration of the element present in the sample.

name: extrinsic plasmon
definition: Plasmon excited as an electron travels through a condensed medium.

name: Fermi level referencing
definition: Process for establishing the binding energy scale for a particular sample by assigning the kinetic energy corresponding to the Fermi level, as determined by analysis of the spectrum obtained from X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy or ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy, as the point of zero binding energy.

name: final energy state
definition: Energy state of an atom after a particular Auger, X-ray, or photoemission process.

name: inelastic electron scattering background
definition: Intensity distribution in a spectrum for particles originally at one energy but which are emitted at lower energies due to one or more inelastic scattering processes.

name: inelastic electron scattering background subtraction
definition: Subtraction of a chosen inelastic electron scattering background from a measured spectrum in Auger electron spectroscopy and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy.

name: inelastic scattering cross section
definition: Cross section for inelastic scattering by an electron traversing a material.

name: initial energy state
definition: Core-hole excited state of an atom prior to Auger transition or to X-ray emission.

name: initial energy state
definition: Ground state of an atom prior to photoelectron emission.

name: initial-state Auger parameter
definition: \(\beta = 3E_{\rm{B}} + E_{\rm{K}}\), where \(E_{\rm{B}}\) and \(E_{\rm{K}}\) are, respectively, the binding energy of a photoelectron peak and the Fermi level referenced (see Fermi level referencing) kinetic energy of an Auger electron peak, each involving the same initial core level of the same element.

name: interatomic Auger process
definition: Auger transition in which at least one of the final electron vacancies is localized in valence levels or molecular orbitals of atoms adjacent to the atom in which the initial vacancy occurred.

name: interface core-level shift
definition: Energy shift observed in core-level photoelectron spectroscopy arising from the changed bonding and/or from the displacements of atoms from their bulk positions near an interface between two materials.

name: intrinsic plasmon
definition: Plasmon excited at the same time as the excitation of a core-level photoelectron or an Auger electron associated with the same locality as the excitation of the photoelectron or Auger electron.

name: modified Auger parameter
definition: Sum of the Fermi level referenced (see Fermi level referencing) kinetic energy of a narrow Auger electron peak in the spectrum and the binding energy of the most intense photoelectron peak from the same element.

name: pass energy
definition: Mean kinetic energy of detected particles in the energy-dispersive portion of an electron energy analyser.

name: photoelectric work function
definition: Minimum photon energy required to liberate an electron from the surface of a conducting solid by absorption of that photon.

name: photoelectron X-ray satellite peaks
definition: Photoelectron peaks in a spectrum resulting from photoemission induced by characteristic minor X-ray lines associated with the X-ray spectrum of the anode material.

name: photoelectron X-ray satellite subtraction
definition: Removal of photoelectron X-ray satellite peaks from a spectrum.

name: photoemission
definition: Emission of electrons from atoms or molecules caused by the photoelectric effect.

name: pure-element relative sensitivity factor
definition: In electron spectroscopy, coefficient, proportional to the intensity measured for a pure sample of an element, by which the measured intensity for that element is divided in calculations to yield the atomic concentration or atomic fraction of the element present in the sample.

name: relaxation energy
definition: Energy associated with intra-atomic or extra-atomic electronic readjustment to the removal of an atomic electron, so as to minimize the energy of the final state of the system.

name: selected-area aperture
definition: Aperture in the electron or ion optical system restricting the detected signal to a small area of the sample surface.

name: shakeoff
definition: Multi-electron process in which two or more electrons are emitted, partitioning between them the excess kinetic energy.

name: shakeup
definition: Multi-electron process in which an atom is left in an excited state following a photoionization or Auger electron process, so that the outgoing electron has a characteristic kinetic energy slightly less than that of the parent photoelectron.

name: Shirley background
definition: In Auger electron spectroscopy and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, background calculated to fit the measured spectrum at points at greater and lesser kinetic energy than the peak or peaks of interest, such that the background contribution at a given kinetic energy is in a fixed proportion to the total peak area above that background for greater kinetic energies.

name: spectator hole
definition: Electronic configuration of an atom containing an electronic vacancy that can be present during processes, such as Auger electron and X-ray photoelectron emission, but is not created or destroyed in the process.

name: sub-shell photoionization cross section
definition: Cross section for an incident photon interacting with a material to produce one or more photoelectrons from a given sub-shell.

name: surface core-level shift
definition: Energy shift observed in core-level photoelectron spectroscopy arising from the reduced coordination of the surface or near-surface atoms compared to bulk atoms.

name: total secondary-electron yield
definition: Total number of electrons emitted from a sample divided by the total number of electrons incident at a given energy and angle of incidence. \(\sigma = \delta + \eta\), where \(\delta\) is the secondary-electron yield and \(\eta\) is the backscattering coefficient.

name: Tougaard background
definition: In Auger electron spectroscopy and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, intensity distribution of the background due to inelastic scattering obtained from the differential inelastic scattering cross section with respect to energy loss and the three-dimensional distribution of the emitting atoms in the surface region.

name: vacuum level referencing
definition: Method of establishing the kinetic energy scale in which the zero point corresponds to an electron at rest at the vacuum level.

name: valence-band spectrum
definition: X-ray photoelectron energy distribution arising from the excitation of electrons from the valence band of the sample material.

name: aligned incidence spectrum
definition: Backscattering spectrum recorded with the analysing beam aligned with crystallographic axes or planes of the sample that produce channelling.

name: backscattering spectrum
definition: Plot of backscattering yield versus backscattering energy.

name: beam chopper
definition: Electrostatic or electromagnetic device used to generate pulses of ions from a continuous ion beam.

name: binary elastic scattering peak
definition: In ion-scattering spectrometry, increase in the spectrometer detection system response above the background signal, which can be attributed to the binary elastic scattering of an incident ion by a surface atom of a particular mass.

name: blocking geometry
definition: Experimental arrangement wherein the atom rows or planes of a single-crystal target are aligned parallel to a vector from the sample to the detector.

name: electronic stopping cross section
definition: Stopping cross section arising from energy transfer to the electrons of the sample.

name: energy edge
definition: Values of the backscattering energy for an element, or for an isotope, that is located at the surface of a sample.

name: surface approximation energy
definition: Simplification of calculations involving the energy of an ion passing through a solid sample, where the energy of the ion at the surface is used in place of a properly averaged energy.

name: enhanced elastic cross section
definition: Cross section of an atom for elastic scattering that is greater than the Rutherford cross section due to partial penetration of a nucleus in the sample by the incident particle.

name: experimental scattered-ion intensity
definition: Measured response of the energy filtering and detection system as a consequence of bombarding the sample material with an ion beam, usually presented as the ordinate of an ion-scattering spectrum.

name: ion-scattering spectrum
definition: Plot of the intensities of ions, scattered from a sample, as a function of the scattered-ion energy divided by the incident-ion energy.

name: kinematic factor
definition: Particle energy after an elastic collision divided by the energy before the collision, in the laboratory frame of reference.

name: nuclear reaction cross section
definition: Cross section at a given beam energy and emission direction of the detected product for a particular nuclear reaction per atom.

name: nuclear stopping cross section
definition: Stopping cross section arising from energy transfer to atomic nuclei of the sample.

name: pileup
definition: Counts in a backscattering spectrum arising from two or more separate events that occur so closely in time that the signals are not resolved by the detection system and cause counts to be recorded in erroneous channels.

name: probe ion
definition: Ion intentionally produced by an ion source and directed onto the sample surface at a known angle of incidence and a known energy.

name: random incidence spectrum
definition: Backscattering spectrum recorded with the analysing beam incident on the sample in a direction such as to produce no channelling.

name: resonance reaction
definition: Nuclear reaction that has a narrow peak in the nuclear reaction cross section as a function of energy, the nuclear reaction cross section at the peak being so much larger than the nuclear reaction cross sections at adjacent energies on either side of the peak that essentially all the particles detected from the reaction are due to the peak.

name: Rutherford cross section
definition: Elastic scattering cross section calculated using classical mechanics and a Coulomb potential.

name: scattered-ion energy
definition: Kinetic energy of a primary ion after a collision.

name: scattered-ion energy ratio
definition: Scattered-ion energy divided by energy of the incident probe ion prior to a collision.

name: screening
definition: Response arising from electrons in an atom causing an apparent reduction in the coulomb potential of the nucleus.

name: screening function
definition: Factor by which the Rutherford cross section is reduced as a result of screening in a given experiment.

name: stopping cross section factor
definition: Energy loss of a particle scattered at a given depth in the sample, and detected at a given angle, by the product of the atomic density of the sample atoms and the depth of scattering.

name: stopping cross section
definition: Rate of energy loss of a particle with distance along its trajectory in a sample divided by the atomic density of sample atoms for a sample of infinitesimal thickness.

name: swift ion
definition: Ion moving with a velocity exceeding the Bohr speed of \(c/137\), where \(c\) is the velocity of light.

name: system resolution
definition: Energy resolution or depth resolution measured in a backscattering spectrum for a monoenergetic incident-ion beam.

name: theoretical scattered-ion intensity
definition: Calculated intensity for probe ions scattered into a specified solid angle at a given direction.

name: thin target
definition: In energetic-ion analysis and Rutherford backscattering spectrometry, sample whose thickness is sufficiently small that the variation in energy of particles backscattered from atoms of each constitutive element is small with respect to the system resolution.

name: analyser blanking
definition: Action to prevent secondary ions from travelling through the mass spectrometer and being detected.

name: beam bunching
definition: Reduction in the spread of arrival times of an ion pulse by reduction in the speed of the leading ions or acceleration of those at the trailing edge of the pulse.

name: buncher
definition: Device to shorten the time length of a pulse of ions so that they arrive at a point over a reduced time interval.

name: dilute limit
definition: Atomic fraction or concentration of impurity species in a homogeneous matrix below which the secondary-ion mass spectrometry can safely be assumed to be linear with composition.

name: disappearance cross section
definition: Cross section for the loss of intensity of an ion signal observed as a result of the bombardment by primary ions.

name: dual-beam profiling
definition: In secondary-ion mass spectrometry, sputter depth profiling involving two ion guns.

name: extraction field
definition: In secondary-ion mass spectrometry, electric field above a sample, operational during ion emission from the sample.

name: extractor voltage
definition: Electric potential, referenced to the sample, of the electrode defining the field above the sample and used to facilitate introduction of emitted ions into the mass spectrometer.

name: fast-atom bombardment secondary ion mass spectrometry
definition: Secondary ion mass spectrometry in which the primary-ion beam is replaced by a fast-atom beam.

name: fractional ion yield
definition: Number of ions of a particular species sputtered from a sample divided by number of particles of that species sputtered from that sample.

name: g index
definition: Power for the ratio of mass intensities in two mass spectra measured for two different primary ion conditions, used to generate the G-SIMS spectrum.

name: G-SIMS with fragmentation pathway mapping
definition: Development of G-SIMS in which the g index is varied in order to deduce the linkages between product ions and precursor ion.

name: ion beam ratio
definition: Intensity of analyte ion divided by intensity of matrix ion, both corrected for isotopic abundance.

name: liquid-metal ion gun
definition: Ion gun utilizing a liquid-metal Taylor cone as the source of the primary ions.

name: mass accuracy
definition: Measured mass minus reference value for that mass.

name: metastable background
definition: Intensity in a mass spectrum arising from ions that spontaneously fragment between emission and detection.

name: molecular fragment
definition: Ion or neutral particle that was part of a larger molecular structure and contains information about that structure.

name: molecular image
definition: Image of a surface formed from ions characteristic of a particular molecule.

name: negative-ion yield
definition: Number of negatively-charged secondary ions sputtered from a sample divided by total number of incident primary particles.

name: partial ion yield
definition: Number of ions of a particular species sputtered from a sample divided by the number of incident particles.

name: polyatomic fragment
definition: Ion or neutral particle composed of three or more atoms.

name: positive-ion yield
definition: Number of positively-charged secondary ions sputtered from a sample divided by the total number of incident primary particles.

name: primary ion
definition: Ion extracted from a source and directed at a sample.

name: pulse rate
definition: Number of ion pulse cycles per second in secondary ion mass spectrometry.

name: pulse width
definition: Full width at half maximum of the time distribution of the pulse of ions generated by a beam chopper and, optionally, the use of beam bunching in secondary ion mass spectrometry.

name: pulsed extraction field
definition: Extraction field around the sample that is pulsed to the working value for extracting ions for the time necessary for operation of a time-of-flight mass spectrometer, but is otherwise at a low value.

name: reflector voltage
definition: Electric potential set on the reflector electrode of a reflectron mass spectrometer with the zero referenced, such that an ion emitted from the sample with an energy numerically equal to the reflector voltage would just be on the point of reflection or transmission by the reflector electrode.

name: relative isotopic sensitivity factor
definition: In dynamic secondary-ion mass spectrometry, coefficient for an element by which the measured intensity for an isotope of that element, divided by the measured intensity for a matrix ion, is multiplied to yield the atomic concentration of that isotope of the element present in the sample.

name: relative mass accuracy
definition: Mass accuracy divided by reference mass.

name: secondary ion
definition: Ion ejected from a sample surface as a result of energy and momentum transfer from a primary ion.

name: secondary-ion angular distribution
definition: Number of secondary ions as a function of angle of emission.

name: secondary-ion energy distribution
definition: Number of secondary ions as a function of kinetic energy at a specified collection angle.

name: secondary-ion yield
definition: Number of ions sputtered from a sample divided by the number of ions incident with a given mass, energy, charge, and angle of incidence.

name: shots per pixel
definition: Number of ion pulses incident at each pixel in an image for one raster frame in secondary ion mass spectrometry.

name: SIMS ion image
definition: Two-dimensional surface map of the spatial distribution of the amount of a particular secondary ion emitted from within a specific area of the sample in secondary ion mass spectrometry.

name: static limit
definition: Ion fluence above which any significant changes in the spectrum, arising from beam damage, are observed in secondary ion mass spectrometry.

name: stop event
definition: Registration of a particle by a time-to-digital converter in secondary ion mass spectrometry.

name: transformation probability
definition: Probability of a defined charged or neutral species being produced, by consumption of a defined parent atomic or molecular configuration at a surface, as a result of sputtering in secondary ion mass spectrometry.

name: ultra-shallow depth profile
definition: Depth profile in secondary-ion mass spectrometry where the depth over which significant changes occur is less than \(\pu{10 nm}\).

name: useful ion yield
definition: In secondary ion mass spectrometry, number of ions of a particular isotope detected divided by the number of atoms of the same element sputtered from the sample.

name: useful spatial resolution
definition: Image resolution in secondary ion mass spectrometry obtained in practice.

name: absorption length
definition: Distance over which the transmitted X-ray intensity falls by \(1/e\), where \(e\) is the base of the natural logarithm.

name: beam footprint
definition: Area on the specimen irradiated by X-rays in X-ray reflectrometry.

name: beam spill-off
definition: Fraction of the incident X-ray beam in X-ray reflectrometry missing the specimen.

name: delayed onset
definition: X-ray energy at which there is a significant increase of absorption and for which the increased absorption occurs at a greater energy than a core-level binding energy.

name: dispersion plane
definition: Plane containing the source, detector, incident, and specularly reflected X–ray beams in X-ray reflectrometry.

name: total reflection of X-rays
definition: Condition where the glancing angle for the incident X-rays is at or less than the critical angle and the X-rays are either reflected or absorbed in a region very close to the surface.

name: wave vector
definition: Vector in reciprocal space describing the direction of propagation of X-rays and equal in magnitude to \(2\uppi/\lambda\), where \(\lambda\) is the wavelength of the X-rays.

name: X-ray jump ratio
definition: X-ray absorption coefficient at an energy just above an absorption edge divided by that at an energy just below the edge.

name: observed interface width
definition: In secondary-ion mass spectrometry, Auger electron spectroscopy, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, distance over which a change in signal intensity from \(\pu{16\%}\) to \(\pu{84\%}\), or from \(\pu{84\%}\) to \(\pu{16\%}\), is measured at the junction of two dissimilar matrices, the thicknesses of which are more than six times that distance

name: surface plasmon resonance
definition: Resonant interaction between the natural frequency of a surface plasmon and incident light of the same frequency.

name: adhesion promoter
definition: Interfacial agent comprised of molecules possessing two or more functional groups, each of which exhibits preferential interactions with the various types of phase domains in a composite.

name: aerial image
definition: Image of a mask pattern that is projected onto the photoresist coated wafer by an optical system.

name: annealing
definition: Thermal treatment of a solid polymer material at a fixed or changing temperature that leads to desired changes in its physical structure and properties without involving complete melting or dissolution.

name: solvent vapor annealing
definition: Annealing via the exposure of a substrate to solvent vapor.

name: thermal annealing
definition: Annealing in which a heating step is used to activate chemical processes in a resist that depend on diffusion.

name: anti-reflective coating
definition: Material used in lithography or in other technologies that is applied to a surface in order to reduce reflection.

name: aspect ratio
definition: Proportional relationship between the width and height of an image produced by exposing a resist.

name: atomic force microscopy
definition: High-resolution scanning probe microscopy that maps a surface with a demonstrated resolution of the order of fractions of a nanometer.

name: base quencher
definition: Base added to a chemical amplification resist to neutralize low levels of acid that might diffuse into nominally unexposed regions and cause blur.

name: block copolymer lithography
definition: Process in which a thin film of block copolymer is formed into a regular nanoscale pattern.

name: bottom anti-reflective coating
definition: Layer placed between a photoresist and a substrate to prevent reflection from the latter resulting in a reduction in photoresist pattern quality, as characterized by resolution, line edge roughness, etc.

name: bottom-up lithography
definition: Pattern formation using self-assembly processes.

name: basting solvent
definition: Solvent in which a resist or additional thin-film component (typically a BARC) is dissolved for the coating process.

name: clearance dose
definition: Dose of radiation required to completely remove a positive-tone resist from a large area.

name: contact hole
definition: Hole in a layer of a semiconductor device enabling contact with an underlying semiconductor layer.

name: contrast
definition: Maximum of the absolute value of the gradient of a contrast curve taken as a measure of the ability of a resist to differentiate the regions that have been exposed to radiation from those that have not.

name: contrast curve
definition: Plot of the fraction of the original thickness that remains after the development of a uniformly irradiated resist versus the logarithm of the incident exposure dose.

name: critical dimension
definition: Length of the smallest geometrical features that can be formed in a lithographic process.

name: dark loss
definition: Unwanted change in the solubility of a resist that takes place in the absence of exposure.

name: defect
definition: Imperfection introduced during pattern formation.

name: defect-free pattern
definition: Imaged resist without imperfections in pattern.

name: deprotection
definition: Removal of a protecting group which leads to a change in the solubility of a polymeric resist.

name: depth of focus
definition: Tolerance of the placement of the image plane in relation to image quality.

name: development
definition: Process in which a developer is used to generate an image by removing the soluble portion of the latent pattern of an exposed resist.

name: dip-pen nanolithography
definition: Direct write, tip-based patterning method that uses the tip of an AFM probe to act as a pen and deposit molecules on a surface.

name: directed self-assembly
definition: Process in which a thin film of block copolymer is formed into a regular nanoscale pattern on chemically or topographically nanopatterned surfaces (or a combination thereof).

name: dislocation
definition: Defect, or irregularity, within an ordered structure.

name: dissolution inhibitor
definition: Compound that, when included in a resist formulation, slows the rate of dissolution.

name: dissolution promoter
definition: Compound that, when included in a resist formulation, increases the rate of dissolution.

name: dissolution rate
definition: Rate at which resist is removed during development.

name: doctor blading
definition: Coating of solution or slurry drawn to uniform film by use of a knife edge or doctor blade.

name: doping (p- and n-type)
definition: Process that increases the thermal-equilibrium concentration of free charge carriers in a material to augment its electrical conductivity using chemical agents or additives (i.e. dopants).

name: double exposure
definition: Lithographic process requiring two exposures to radiation for a single resist layer to form a finished pattern.

name: double patterning
definition: Printing of two distinct lines at the edges of a single resist line pattern by means of a deposit-etch process.

name: dry deposition
definition: Assembly of a layer on a substrate by the use of a solvent-free process, such as vapor deposition.

name: dry development
definition: Process in which a portion of a latent pattern in an exposed resist is removed to form the image without the use of a liquid developer.

name: dry-etch resistance
definition: Facility of an exposed resist to withstand etching conditions, usually a plasma, determined in comparison to a reference standard.

name: dual-tone resist
definition: Photoresist capable of being processed in either positive tone (aqueous base development) or negative tone (organic solvent development).

name: edge acuity
definition: Degree to which the edge of an image appears sharp and precise.

name: embossing
definition: Creating a pattern by pressing a master die into a malleable material.

name: epitaxial crystallization
definition: Growth of crystals on other crystals involving a precisely defined mutual orientation of their lattices.

name: epitaxy
definition: Deposition of a crystalline over layer on a crystalline substrate.

name: etch
definition: Treatment to remove substrate to a requisite depth from those areas of a surface no longer protected following the exposure and development of an overlaid resist.

name: dry etching
definition: Process of removal of material, typically of a masked pattern on a semiconductor, by exposing it to a bombardment of ions.

name: etch rate
definition: Rate of material removal using either a wet or a dry-etch process.

name: wet etching
definition: Process of removal of material, typically of a masked pattern on a semiconductor, by exposing it to a corrosive liquid.

name: exposure latitude
definition: Extent to which a light- or radiation-sensitive material can be overexposed or underexposed and still achieve acceptable imaging.

name: focused ion beam
definition: Technique used for the site-specific analysis, deposition, ablation, and micromachining of materials down to dimensions of \(\pu{10}\) to \(\pu{15 nm}\).

name: hard bake
definition: High temperature annealing to solidify any resist material remaining after development in order to provide a durable protective layer for etching.

name: image
definition: Pattern produced in or on a substrate during a lithographic process.

name: developed image
definition: Visible image produced by an effect of radiation on a substrate followed by subsequent lithographic development.

name: image blur
definition: Broadening during the development of a lithographic image.

name: immersion fluid
definition: High refractive index liquid medium used in immersion lithography that replaces the air gap between the lens and the resist surface in conventional photolithography.

name: lift-off process
definition: Method whereby a film, usually metallic, deposited on a patterned substrate after etch processing, is removed during resist strip, which leaves only that portion of the film that is deposited directly onto the exposed regions of the substrate.

name: line edge roughness
definition: Variations along one edge of a linear resist feature over an extended length.

name: line width roughness
definition: Variations in the width of a linear resist feature over an extended length.

name: line-space patterning
definition: Developed lithographic pattern comprising alternating lines with spaces between.

name: lithography
definition: Process whereby an image is created on an apparently planar surface.

name: direct-write lithography
definition: Pattern created without recourse to irradiation through a mask of the image.

name: electron beam lithography
definition: Lithography performed by exposing a resist to a beam of electrons.

name: electron-beam direct-write lithography
definition: Electron beam lithography whereby the pattern is written directly onto the photoresist without the use of a mask.

name: extreme ultraviolet lithography
definition: Photolithography performed by exposing a resist to extreme ultraviolet (\(\pu{13 nm}\)) radiation.

name: immersion lithography
definition: Photolithography that provides resolution enhancement by immersing a resist-coated substrate in a fluid during the exposure process.

name: imprint lithography
definition: Patterns created by mechanical deformation of an imprint resist and a subsequent curing process.

name: nanoimprint lithography
definition: Subset of imprint lithography that allows for the fabrication of nanometer scale patterns.

name: interference lithography
definition: Technique for patterning regular arrays of fine features without the use of complex optical systems or photomasks.

name: magnetolithography
definition: Lithography for direct patterning of surfaces based on the application of a magnetic field to the substrate using paramagnetic metal masks.

name: maskless lithography
definition: Lithography that does not need a mask of the image to make a pattern.

name: microlithography
definition: Lithography or pattern formation at a resolution of the order of microns.

name: nanolithography
definition: Umbrella term that is used to describe all lithographic techniques that allow for the fabrication of nanometer scale patterns.

name: nanosphere lithography
definition: Lithography in which material is deposited into the interstices of a 2D array of nanospheres that are subsequently removed to form a pattern.

name: photolithography
definition: Lithography performed by exposing a resist to an intense parallel light beam through an image mask.

name: scanning-probe lithography
definition: Lithographic method in which a microscopic or nanoscopic stylus is moved mechanically across a surface to form a pattern.

name: soft lithography
definition: Family of techniques for fabricating or replicating structures using elastomeric stamps, molds, and conformable photomasks.

name: X-ray lithography
definition: Lithography performed by exposing a resist to X-radiation through an image mask.

name: 3D lithography
definition: Lithography performed in three dimensions, typically carried out using nanoimprint patterning or 2-photon lithography.

name: 2-photon lithography
definition: Photolithography within a thick photoresist film, within which the photochemically-induced solubility change results from the simultaneous absorption of two photons.

name: mask
definition: Transparent substrate pre-patterned with the desired image that is inserted into the incident beam in photo- and X-ray lithography.

name: magnetic mask
definition: Mask with a pattern defined by a paramagnetic metal.

name: mask error enhancement factor
definition: Increase in error of pattern edge location during pattern formation when the wavelength of light used to expose a resist is greater than the feature size.

name: microcontact printing
definition: Form of soft lithography that uses micron-scale and smaller relief patterns on a master elastomer stamp to form images on the surface of a substrate through conformal contact.

name: microfabrication
definition: Process whereby structures of micrometre scale and smaller are fabricated.

name: microfluidics
definition: Multi-disciplinary subject concerned with the behavior, precise control, and manipulation of fluids that are geometrically constrained within a small, typically sub-millimeter, scale channel.

name: micromolding
definition: Form of soft lithography that uses the relief patterns in a master template to make 3-dimensional structures.

name: molecular glass
definition: Assembly of small molecules that vitrify, rather than crystallize, when cooled.

name: molecular logic gate
definition: Molecule that acts as a device performing a logical operation based on one or more physical or chemical inputs and a single output.

name: molecular template
definition: Molecular structure that transfers a pattern to or organizes another molecular scale structure.

name: molecular wires
definition: Molecular-scale objects that conduct electrical current.

name: Moore’s law
definition: Empirical observation by Gordon E. Moore, co-founder of Intel, that, over the history of computing hardware, the number of transistors on integrated circuits doubles approximately every two years.

name: nanodevice
definition: Device in which the manufactured size is between \(\pu{1}\) and \(\pu{100 nm}\).

name: nanoelectromechanical systems
definition: Devices that integrate electrical and mechanical functionality at the nanoscale. A miniaturization of microelectromechanical systems (MEMS).

name: nanoelectronics
definition: Application of nanotechnology to microelectronics.

name: nanoparticle
definition: Particle of any shape with an equivalent diameter of approximately \(\pu{1}\) to \(\pu{100 nm}\).

name: nanopattern
definition: Patterns on a substrate with lesser dimensions of between \(\pu{1}\) to \(\pu{100 nm}\).

name: nanophotonics
definition: Study of the interaction of light with particles or substances on a scale less than the wavelength of the light.

name: nanostructure
definition: Structure or feature of size between \(\pu{1}\) and \(\pu{100 nm}\).

name: nanotechnology
definition: Manipulation of matter on an atomic and molecular scale.

name: near-field scanning optical microscopy
definition: Microscopy applied to the investigation of nanostructures that breaks the farfield resolution limit by exploiting the properties of evanescent waves.

name: negative-tone development
definition: Process for revealing the latent image in a resist in which the exposed regions are less soluble in the developer than the unexposed regions.

name: normalized image log slope
definition: Measure of the information content of the aerial image and represents an energy (intensity) gradient at the position of the nominal line edge.

name: pattern collapse
definition: Destruction of pattern during and after development caused by the surface tension of the development solvent.

name: pattern transfer
definition: Transfer of the pattern of a developed lithographic image to an underlying substrate by processes such as etching.

name: photoacid generator
definition: Compound that on exposure to radiation gives rise to a proton.

name: photoactive compound
definition: Compound that on exposure to radiation will release an active ionic or radical species.

name: photonic crystal
definition: Periodic structures consisting of a dielectric material that shows strong interaction with light.

name: photonics
definition: Science and technology of the production, transmission, absorption, sensing, and direction of light.

name: pitch division
definition: Method for making a lithographic pattern smaller than that deemed possible given the wavelength of the imaging radiation.

name: planarising layer
definition: Coating used to create a level surface during lithographic processing.

name: plasma enhanced chemical vapor deposition
definition: Process to deposit a solid film on a substrate resulting from plasma-induced reactions of precursor compounds, either in the gaseous state or on the film surface.

name: plasma etch
definition: Plasma processing used in the fabrication of integrated circuits that generates volatile products from the elements of the material etched and the reactive species generated by the plasma.

name: positive-tone development
definition: Process for revealing the latent image in a resist in which the exposed regions are more soluble in the developer than are the unexposed regions.

name: post-apply bake
definition: Thermal annealing step following the coating of a substrate with a resist material.

name: post-exposure bake
definition: Thermal annealing step following the exposure of a resist to imaging radiation.

name: post-exposure delay
definition: Pause between successive patterning steps in lithographic processing.

name: protecting group
definition: Non-reactive group temporarily used to transform a reactive group into one that does not react under conditions where the non-protected group reacts.

name: proximity effect
definition: Widening of the exposure dose distribution, and hence the developed pattern, caused by the scattering of the primary beam electrons within the resist and substrate.

name: raster scan
definition: Rectangular pattern of line-by-line scanning for image capture used in electron beam and ion-beam lithography.

name: reactive ion etching
definition: Etching technology used in microfabrication that uses chemically reactive plasma to remove material from a substrate.

name: resist
definition: Material, usually a polymer, that when irradiated either undergoes a marked change in solubility in a given solvent or is ablated.

name: chemically amplified resist
definition: Resist that undergoes solubility change upon exposure of photoacid generator, followed by thermally activated acid catalyzed deprotection.

name: electron beam resist
definition: Resist optimized for use under electron beam irradiation.

name: ion beam resist
definition: Resist optimized for use under ion beam irradiation.

name: multi-component resist
definition: Resist comprising more than one active component.

name: X-ray resist
definition: Resist optimized for use under X-ray irradiation.

name: resist profile
definition: Topography of a resist pattern in cross section.

name: resist strip
definition: Subsequent removal of the remaining resist that covers the protected regions of a substrate during development and etch processing.

name: shot noise
definition: Noise which originates from the discrete nature of elementary charge.

name: silylation
definition: Introduction of a substituted silyl group (\(\ce{R3Si}\)) to an alcohol, carboxylic acid, amine, thiol, or phosphate, commonly as a protecting group.

name: soft bake
definition: Short, low temperature annealing step following the coating of a wafer with a photoresist.

name: stamp
definition: Three-dimensional template comprising the negative pattern used to leave an impression on the surface of a malleable material.

name: supramolecular assembly
definition: Molecular system comprising two or more self-assembled molecular, or molecular and ionic, entities held together by means of non-covalent intermolecular binding interactions.

name: surface roughness
definition: Measure of the texture of a surface that is quantified by vertical deviations from its ideal location.

name: swing curve
definition: Sinusoidal variation in the lithographic clearance dose arising from changes in the phase difference between incoming and outgoing radiation that is induced by variations in resist thickness.

name: topcoat
definition: Protective layer spun directly on top of a resist.

name: top-down patterning
definition: Pattern formation using lithographic (also embossing) methods.

name: top-surface imaging
definition: Lithographic process in which the exposed region of resist is silylated and the image then formed through reactive oxygen etch.

name: vapor deposition
definition: Growth of solid materials on a substrate by deposition from the gas phase.

name: vector scan
definition: Pattern formation using a directed electron beam or ion beam that skips from region to region requiring exposure but is otherwise turned off.

name: rotated Fischer projection
definition: Projection formula for macromolecules in which horizontal lines denote polymer backbone bonds. At each individual backbone carbon atom, horizontal lines represent bonds directed below the projection plane and vertical lines represent bonds directed above that plane.

name: m diad
definition: Pair of adjacent constitutionally equivalent stereogenic units that are of like configuration.

name: r diad
definition: Pair of adjacent constitutionally equivalent stereogenic units that are of unlike configuration. Figure 2: Diagrammatic representations of the configurational repeating unit or stereorepeating unit (upper), and the diad sequence (lower) for isotactic poly(oxypropylene), both as a rotated Fischer projections (left) and as a zigzag projection (right). name: heterotactic macromolecule
definition: Regular macromolecule having a configurational repeating unit comprising four configurational base units, the first two stereogenic units of which are identical and enantiomorphic to the last two.

name: asymmetric enantiomer-differentiating polymerization
definition: Asymmetric polymerization in which, starting from a mixture of enantiomeric monomer molecules, only one enantiomer is polymerized.

name: asymmetric polymerization
definition: Polymerization that proceeds in an unsymmetrical manner in terms of chirality under the influence of chiral features present in one or more components of the reaction system.

name: Bernoullian distribution
definition: The Bernoullian distribution is a discrete distribution having two possible outcomes labelled by \(n = 0\) and \(n = 1\), in which \(n = 1\) ('success') occurs with probability $p$ and \(n = 0\) ('failure') occurs with probability \(q = 1 - p\), where $0 \lt p \lt 1$. It is a special case of a binomial distribution corresponding to a random distribution.

name: bioassimilation
definition: Conversion of a substance into biomass by biochemical processes.

name: biobased
definition: Composed of or derived from, in whole or in part, biological products derived from the biomass (including plant, animal, and marine or forestry materials).

name: biodegradable
definition: Qualifier for a substance or device that undergoes biodegradation.

name: bioerosion
definition: Surface degradation resulting from the action of cells.

name: biorelated
definition: Qualifier for actions or substances that are connected to living systems.

name: bioresorbable
definition: Qualifier used to indicate that a compound or a device is bioresorbed, i.e., totally eliminated or bioassimilated by an animal or a human body.

name: composting
definition: Process of biological decomposition of organic matter performed by microorganisms, mostly bacteria and fungi.

name: degradable
definition: Qualifier to a substance that can undergo physical and/or chemical deleterious changes of some properties, especially of integrity, under stress conditions.

name: heterogeneous degradation
definition: Degradation or biodegradation occurring at different rates depending on the location within a matrix.

name: homogeneous degradation
definition: Degradation that occurs at the same rate regardless of the location within a polymeric item.

name: stereocopolymer
definition: Copolymer formed of constitutional repeating units that are constitutionally identical but configurationally different.

name: branch constitutional repeating unit
definition: Constitutional repeating unit of connectivity three or more connected at least to three other constitutional repeating units.

name: core unit
definition: Constitutional unit in a dendrimer molecule, from which the dendron(s) emanate(s).

name: degree of branching
definition: Parameter characterizing the branched architecture of a hyperbranched polymer, which is equal to unity for a polymer that contains no linear or semi-dendritic constitutional repeating unit and is equal to 0 for a polymer that contains no dendritic or semi-dendritic constitutional repeating unit.

name: dendrimer molecule
definition: Molecule consisting of one or more dendrons emanating from a single constitutional unit.

name: dendritic block macromolecule
definition: Block macromolecule in which at least one block is a dendron.

name: dendritic constitutional repeating unit
definition: Constitutional repeating unit of connectivity $c \ge 3$ connected to $c$ other constitutional repeating units.

name: dendritic graft macromolecule
definition: Graft macromolecule in which at least one of the grafts contains a dendron.

name: dendritic macromolecule
definition: Macromolecule containing at least one dendron.

name: dendritic polymer
definition: Substance composed of dendritic macromolecules.

name: dendron
definition: Part of a molecule with only one free valence, comprising exclusively dendritic and terminal constitutional repeating units and in which each path from the free valence to any end-group comprises the same number of constitutional repeating units.

name: dendron direction
definition: For a constitutional repeating unit of a dendron, the direction from the free valence to the end-groups.

name: focal unit
definition: Core unit of a dendrimer molecule that comprises only one dendron

name: generation
definition: Set of constitutional repeating units separated from the free valence of a dendron by the same number of constitutional repeating units.

name: hyperbranched macromolecule
definition: Highly branched macromolecule, the constitutional repeating units of which are in substantial part branch constitutional repeating units and terminal constitutional repeating units.

name: hyperbranched oligomer
definition: Substance composed of hyperbranched oligomer molecules.

name: hyperbranched oligomer molecule
definition: Highly branched oligomer molecule, the constitutional repeating units of which are in substantial part branch constitutional repeating units and terminal constitutional repeating units.

name: hyperbranched polymer
definition: Substance composed of hyperbranched macromolecules.

name: irregular dendrimer
definition: Substance composed of irregular dendrimer molecules.

name: irregular dendrimer molecule
definition: Dendrimer molecule that contains either different types of regular dendrons or at least one irregular dendron.

name: irregular dendron
definition: Dendron composed of either different types of constitutional units, different types of end-groups or any combination of these.

name: linear constitutional repeating unit
