definition: Constitutional repeating unit connected to exactly two other constitutional repeating units.

name: number of generations
definition: Number of constitutional repeating units on the path from the free valence to any end-group of a dendron.

name: number of generations
definition: Number of generation of the dendrons of a regular dendrimer molecule.

name: number of pseudo-generations
definition: Number of generations of the hypothetical dendrimer molecule that would present the same ratio of constitutional repeating units to core unit.

name: regular dendrimer
definition: Substance composed of regular dendrimer molecules.

name: regular dendrimer molecule
definition: Dendrimer molecule comprising only identical regular dendrons.

name: regular dendron
definition: Dendron composed of only one type of constitutional repeating units and of only one type of end-groups.

name: semi-dendritic constitutional repeating unit
definition: Constitutional repeating unit of connectivity \(c \ge 4\) connected to more than two but less than \(c\) other constitutional repeating units.Example of a hyperbranched macromolecule part with a semi-dendritic constitutional repeating unit of connectivity \(c = 4\) (circled), connected to three other constitutional repeating units and to one hydroxymethyl end-group. The preferred constitutional repeating unit is chosen such that the branch points are at its end in the dendron direction.

name: terminal constitutional repeating unit
definition: Constitutional repeating unit connected to only one other constitutional repeating unit.

name: chalcogen bond
definition: Net attractive interaction between an electrophilic region associated with a chalcogen atom in a molecular entity and a nucleophilic region in another, or the same, molecular entity.

name: bioanalytical chemistry
definition: Sub-field of analytical chemistry dealing with analysis of biomolecules.

name: biomolecule
definition: Molecule of biological origin.

name: biomacromolecule
definition: Macromolecule (including proteins, nucleic acids, and polysaccharides) formed by living organisms.

name: amniotic fluid
definition: Fluid that surrounds the foetus in the amniotic sac.

name: blood
definition: Fluid that circulates through the heart, arteries, capillaries, and veins.

name: blood cell
definition: Any cellular element of the blood, including erythrocytes, leucocytes, and platelets.

name: blood cell count
definition: Number of red blood cells and white blood cells per unit volume in a specimen of venous blood.

name: blood group
definition: Red cell phenotypes classified by their antigenic structural characteristics, which are under the control of various allelic genes.

name: body fluids
definition: Liquids originating from the bodies of living or dead humans, animals, and other organisms.

name: cerebrospinal fluid
definition: Clear, colourless fluid that fills spaces within and around the central nervous system.

name: cord blood
definition: Blood contained in the vessels of the umbilical cord at the time of birth.

name: lymph
definition: Yellowish, slightly basic fluid circulating through the lymphatic system.

name: occult blood
definition: Blood present in such small amounts that its presence can be ascertained only by chemical analysis or by spectroscopic or microscopic examination; particularly the blood found in stools.

name: peripheral blood
definition: Blood obtained from parts of the body that are located at some distance from the heart.

name: protein-free filtrate
definition: Sample of blood, serum, or plasma from which all proteins have been removed by chemical or physical denaturation, dialysis, ultrafiltration, or solvent extraction.

name: saliva
definition: Clear, viscous secretion from the parotid, submaxillary, sublingual, and smaller mucous glands in the cavity of the mouth.

name: skin
definition: Soft outer covering of vertebrates.

name: sperm
definition: Seminal fluid containing male reproductive cells.

name: sweat
definition: Fluid excreted by the sweat glands in the skin of mammals during perspiration.

name: tears
definition: Clear salty liquid that is secreted by the lachrymal gland of the eye to lubricate the surface between the eyeball and eyelid and to wash away irritants.

name: tissue
definition: Group of biological cells that perform a specific function.

name: urine
definition: Fluid containing metabolic products that is excreted by the kidneys, stored in the bladder, and normally discharged by way of the urethra.

name: bioinformatics
definition: Discipline encompassing the development and utilisation of computational tools to store, analyse, and interpret biological data.

name: biological recognition element
definition: Component of biological origin that translates information from the biochemical domain into a physical or chemical domain with a defined selectivity.

name: enzymatic decomposition
definition: Decomposition of organic materials (e.g. starch, sugars, proteins, lignin, hemicelluloses, etc.) with specific enzymes or microbes in which the enzyme converts a high relative molecular mass compound into lower relative molecular mass species.

name: lysis
definition: Breaking down of a cell.

name: microarray
definition: Two-dimensional arrangement of a device for analysis of sub-microlitre sample volume.

name: sample quality control
definition: Test of the purity of the sample that will be subjected to detailed biochemical analysis.

name: affinity
definition: Strength of association between a single antibody and a single epitope of antigen.

name: agglutination inhibition
definition: Type of agglutination in which particulate and soluble antigen compete for soluble antibody.

name: antigenic determinant
definition: Part of the structure of an antigen molecule that is responsible for specific interaction with antibody molecules evoked by the same or a similar antigen.

name: avidity
definition: Net affinity of all binding sites of all antibodies in the antiserum under specified physicochemical reaction conditions.

name: binding capacity
definition: Amount of a ligand that binds to a receptor expressed in operational units.

name: blocking
definition: Coating of an immunospecific surface (e.g. serum, tissues, cells, biological macromolecules, biosensor surface) to form an active cover with selectivity or an inert layer.

name: bound/free ratio
definition: Amount of analyte bound by a label divided by amount of unbound (free) analyte

name: complement
definition: Array of serum proteins (some of which are enzymes) that become sequentially activated after the first member of the series is activated by either antigen-antibody complexes or microbial products.

name: enzyme conjugate
definition: Conjugate that has an enzyme bound covalently.

name: hemagglutination
definition: Agglutination reactions in which the particles used are erythrocytes.

name: immunoblotting
definition: Technique that uses antibodies (or other specific ligands in related techniques) to identify target proteins among a number of unrelated protein species.

name: immunochemical specificity
definition: The extent to which the immunoassay responds only to (all subsets of) a specific analyte and not to other substances of similar structure that are present in the sample.

name: immunocomplex
definition: Product of an antigen-antibody reaction that may also contain components of the complement.

name: immunoglobulin class
definition: Classification of immunoglobulins based on antigenic and structural differences of the heavy peptide chain.

name: immunoprecipitation
definition: Isolation and concentration of an antigen by forming a precipitate with an antibody.

name: immunoreactivity
definition: Kinetic property of the immune response caused by an antigen.

name: immunosensor
definition: Biosensor where one of the immunointeracting partners (an antibody or an antigen as the analyte) is immobilised on the surface of a physicochemical transducer.

name: indirect agglutination
definition: Agglutination in which antigen is first immobilised artificially onto the particulate surfaces, either by physical adsorption or by chemical and/or immunochemical linkers.

name: lateral flow test
definition: Migration of the sample zone driven by capillary forces in a porous carrier strip.

name: monoclonal
definition: Arising from a single clone of cells.

name: monospecificity
definition: Immunoreactivity of an antiserum with its designated antigen.

name: polyclonal
definition: Arising from multiple, different clones.

name: reverse passive agglutination
definition: Modification of the indirect agglutination assay, where the particles are coated with antibody.

name: sandwich immunoassay
definition: Immunoassay using chemical or immunochemical binding of analyte to a solid phase carrying antibody and the immunochemical binding of a second (labelled) reagent to the analyte.

name: amplification of deoxyribonucleic acid
definition: Process of producing multiple copies of a deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) sequence by the repeated copying of a DNA segment.

name: base pair
definition: Pair of two nucleobases, consisting of one purine and one pyrimidine base, held together by hydrogen bonds.

name: base sequence analysis
definition: Method for determining the nucleotide sequence.

name: basic local alignment search tool
definition: Computer algorithm that finds regions of local similarity between deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) or protein sequences.

name: cloning
definition: Specialised deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) technology for the production of multiple exact copies of a single gene or another segment of DNA.

name: cloning vector
definition: Deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) molecule into which another DNA fragment of appropriate size can be integrated without the loss of its capacity for self-replication.

name: complementary sequence
definition: Nucleotide sequence that can form a double-stranded structure with another deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) sequence by following base-pairing (see base pair) rules.

name: complete genome sequence
definition: High-quality, low-error, gap-free deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) sequence of an entire genome of an organism.

name: damage to deoxyribonucleic acid
definition: Alteration in the deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) chemical structure resulting from interactions with physical or chemical agents occurring in the environment, generated in the organisms as by-products of metabolism, or used as therapeutics.

name: deletion
definition: Loss of a part (one or more base pairs) of deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA).

name: deoxyribose
definition: Type of pentose sugar that is incorporated in the structure of deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA).

name: deoxyribonucleic acid fragmentation
definition: Breaking and/or separation of large deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) molecules into smaller pieces (fragments).

name: deoxyribonucleic acid fragmentation index
definition: Fraction of deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) having fragmented DNA.

name: deoxyribonucleic acid integrity index
definition: Ratio of longer fragments to shorter deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA).

name: deoxyribonucleic acid mismatch
definition: Defect in the double stranded deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) structure in which the DNA double helix contains one (or more) non-standard base pairs.
synonyms: DNA mismatch|mismatch in DNA|multi-base mismatch|single mismatch

name: deoxyribonucleic acid profiling
definition: Identification of individuals by matching characteristics of their genome deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) sequence.

name: deoxyribonucleic acid replication
definition: Synthesis of new deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) strands using existing DNA as a template.

name: deoxyribonucleic acid sequencing
definition: Determination of nucleotide sequence (the deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) primary structure).

name: double helix
definition: The twisted shape of two complementary strands of deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA).

name: endonuclease
definition: Enzyme that cleaves nucleic acids by hydrolysing phosphodiester bonds between nucleotides within a nucleic acid molecule.

name: exogenous deoxyribonucleic acid
definition: Deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) molecule of foreign origin that has been introduced into an organism.

name: exonuclease
definition: Enzyme that cleaves nucleotides from free ends of a linear nucleic acid molecule.

name: gene expression
definition: Process for converting a gene’s coded information into biomolecules present and operating in the cell.

name: Northern blot
definition: Technique involving hybridization of nucleic acids  used to study gene expression at the level of ribonucleic acid (RNA).

name: nucleic acid aptamers
definition: Single stranded (ss) oligonucleotides (mainly deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) or ribonucleic acid (RNA)) originating from in vitro selection, which, starting from random sequence libraries, optimise the nucleic acids for high-affinity binding to a given target.

name: nucleobase
definition: Purine or pyrimidine nitrogenous base occurring in deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) or ribonucleic acid (RNA).

name: nucleobase lesion
definition: Product of chemical modification of a nucleobase.

name: nucleotide sequence
definition: Order of nucleotides in a deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) or ribonucleic acid (RNA) molecule.

name: open reading frame
definition: Sequence of deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) or ribonucleic acid (RNA) nucleotides, located between the start-code sequence (initiation codon) and the stop-code sequence (termination codon), which is transcribed and translated to generate a protein.

name: peptide nucleic acid
definition: Synthetic deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) mimic, which contains 2-aminoethylglycine linkages instead of the negatively charged phosphodiesteric backbone of oligonucleotides.

name: polymerase
definition: Enzyme that catalyses the synthesis of nucleic acids on pre-existing nucleic acid templates.

name: primer
definition: Short pre-existing polynucleotide chain attached to a complementary stretch in template deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) to which new deoxyribonucleotides can be added by DNA polymerase.

name: purine
definition: Nitrogen-containing, double-ring, basic compound that occurs in nucleic acids.

name: pyrimidine
definition: Nitrogen-containing, single-ring, basic compound that occurs in nucleic acids.

name: quantitative polymerase chain reaction
definition: Polymerase chain reaction to quantify target nucleotide sequences of interest.

name: real-time polymerase chain reaction
definition: Polymerase chain reaction where data are collected and monitored in real-time as the reaction proceeds.

name: recombinant deoxyribonucleic acid
definition: Deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) molecules joined together using recombinant deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) technology.

name: recombination
definition: Process by which genetic material is broken and joined to other genetic material, which can lead to a rearrangement of genetic sequences.

name: restriction fragment length polymorphism
definition: Variation between individuals in deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) fragment sizes cut by specific restriction enzymes.

name: reverse transcriptase
definition: Enzyme used to form a complementary deoxyribonucleic acid sequence (cDNA) from a ribonucleic acid (RNA) template.

name: Sanger sequencing
definition: Method for determining a nucleotide sequence of deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) based on incorporating chain-terminating dideoxynucleotides.

name: shotgun method
definition: Method used for determining the order of bases in long DNA using sequencing of deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) broken up randomly into numerous small segments.

name: single nucleotide polymorphism
definition: Variant of nucleotide sequence of deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) in which the purine or pyrimidine base of a single nucleotide is replaced by another such base.

name: Southern blot
definition: Technique based on deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) hybridization used for the detection of a DNA fragment of specific nucleotide sequence.

name: strand break
definition: Interruption of the sugar-phosphate backbone of a polynucleotide chain.

name: tandem repeat sequence
definition: Multiple consecutive copies of the same nucleotide sequence on a chromosome.

name: telomerase
definition: Enzyme that directs the replication of telomeres.

name: telomere
definition: Repetitive nucleotide sequences present at the ends of a chromosome that protect the chromosome from deterioration.

name: yeast artificial chromosome
definition: Vector used to clone large deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) fragments.

name: alternative splicing
definition: Process occurring during gene expression that allows the generation of multiple protein molecules from one gene. It generally involves the processing of messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA) via elimination of introns.

name: bottom-up proteomics
definition: Approach to identify proteins and characterise their amino acid sequences or post-translational modifications by sequential combination of proteolysis (enzymatic proteolysis and chemical proteolysis) prior to mass spectrometric analysis of the resulting proteolytic peptides.

name: C-terminal analysis
definition: Chemical method for C-terminal sequencing of proteins and peptides starting at their C-terminus.

name: C-terminus
definition: End of an amino acid chain (protein or polypeptide), terminated by a carboxylic group.

name: database searching
definition: Bioinformatics analysis of proteomic mass spectrometric data used in order to identify a protein or its post-translational modification. It results in a list of candidates presented mostly in order of the decreasing statistical significance of the hit.

name: difference gel electrophoresis
definition: Measurement method of two-dimensional gel electrophoresis used to study protein expression regulation by the differential staining of multiple gels representing different states of a proteome, preferably with fluorescent dyes (e.g. \(\ce{Cy{3}}\), \(\ce{Cy{5}}\), \(\ce{Cy{2}}\)).

name: disulfide bond cleavage
definition: Chemical reduction of protein disulfide bonds.

name: Edman degradation
definition: Method of N-terminal analysis in which the N-terminal amino acid residue is labelled and cleaved from the peptide without affecting other peptide bonds in the peptide chain.

name: electron-transfer dissociation
definition: Ion fragmentation technique in mass spectrometry-driven proteomics based on the transfer of low energy electrons to the molecules selected for fragmentation.

name: electron-transfer/higher-energy collision dissociation
definition: Ion fragmentation technique in mass spectrometry-driven proteomics that is a combination of electron-transfer dissociation (ETD) and higher-energy collision dissociation (HCD) in Kingdon trap instruments (Orbitrap™).

name: electrospray ionisation
definition: Soft ionisation technique in mass spectrometry-driven proteomics.

name: expression proteomics
definition: Field of study in proteomics that deals with the determination of changes in protein expression and regulation in response to different stimuli, internal or external. It also includes the analysis of post-translational modifications (e.g. phosphorylation, glycosylation, etc.), their identification, and their localisation.

name: functional proteomics
definition: Field of study in proteomics studying protein interactions on different levels: protein-protein interactions (interactomics), the formation of protein complexes, and the interaction of proteins with other biomolecules.

name: gel electrophoresis
definition: Separation technique used to separate or fractionate proteins and larger peptides according to their relative molecular mass using an electric field in polyacrylamide gel (PAGE).

name: higher-energy collision dissociation
definition: Ion fragmentation technique in mass spectrometry-driven proteomics used mostly in Kingdon trap (Orbitrap™) instruments. It does not have low mass cut-off of collision-induced dissociation (CID) and therefore is used for the tandem mass tag of stable isotope labels.

name: isoelectric focusing
definition: Separation technique used to separate or fractionate proteins and peptides in a gel (or similar type of media) according to their isoelectric point.

name: mass fingerprinting
definition: Protein analysis where an unknown protein is chemically or enzymatically cleaved into peptide fragments whose masses are determined by mass spectrometry. The peptide masses are compared to peptide masses calculated for known proteins in a database and analysed statistically to determine the best match.

name: MS/MS data based identification
definition: Mass spectrometric method used for protein/peptide identification based on protein sequencing.

name: multidimensional protein identification technology
definition: Non-gel step-wise multidimensional technique for separating and identifying individual components of complex protein and peptide mixtures. It combines fractionation of proteolytic peptides in steps on a strong cation exchanger (SAX) using ion exchange chromatography (IEC); each step uses higher elution force. Then, each fraction is separated on reversed phase liquid chromatography and analysed using mass spectrometry.

name: N-terminal analysis
definition: Chemical method for N-terminal sequencing of proteins and peptides starting at their N-terminus.

name: N-terminus
definition: The end of an amino acid chain (protein or polypeptide), terminating in a free primary amine group.

name: off-gel isoelectric focusing
definition: Separation technique used to fractionate proteins and peptides into discrete liquid fractions according to their isoelectric point.

name: off peptide product ions
definition: Protein/peptide sequencing approach using overlapping complementary information on a sequence acquired using proteolysis in bottom-up proteomic analysis by at least two different proteolytic approaches.

name: peptide de novo sequencing
definition: Analytical process that derives an amino acid sequence of a peptide from its tandem mass spectrum without the assistance of a sequence database.

name: peptide fragment ion
definition: Product ion which originates in a peptide precursor ion fragmentation process.

name: peptide fragmentation technique
definition: Mass spectrometric technique that serves to generate peptide fragment ions through the fragmentation of peptide precursor ions via different physicochemical processes in an ion source.

name: peptide precursor ion
definition: Peptide ion generated during the ionisation of peptides in an ion source or during tandem mass spectrometry of an intact protein in top-down proteomic analysis, selected for further analysis by means of tandem mass spectrometry.

name: peptidomics
definition: Study of the set of peptides in an organism, its peptidome.

name: protein complex
definition: Ensemble of two or more different associated proteins, each with a specific function, linked by non-covalent protein-protein interactions.

name: protein complex purification
definition: Set of methods serving to purify the intact protein complex for further analysis.

name: protein database
definition: Collection of protein sequences from several sources, including translations from annotated genetic coding regions, as well as original protein and peptide sequences.

name: protein folding
definition: Physicochemical process by which a polypeptide folds into its characteristic and functional three-dimensional structure from a random coil.

name: protein fractionation
definition: Methodical approach to simplify a complex mixture of proteomic sample.

name: protein fragmentation
definition: Process which happens during tandem mass spectrometry of intact proteins.

name: protein identification
definition: Analytical approach leading to the identity of a protein.

name: protein machine
definition: Supramolecular interacting system, such as a metabolic circuit, intracellular signal transduction, or cell-to-cell communication.

name: protein purification
definition: Series of processes conducted to isolate either the whole proteome or a subset from a biological sample.

name: protein quantification
definition: Analytical methods and related techniques to measure the protein content.

name: protein sequencer
definition: Equipment designed for the automatic determination of amino acid sequences of peptides using a method of N-terminal analysis.

name: protein staining
definition: Technique used to visualise proteins separated on electrophoretic slab gels.

name: proteoform
definition: All of the different molecular forms in which the protein product of a single gene can be found, including changes due to genetic variations, alternatively spliced ribonucleic acid (RNA) transcripts, and post-translational modifications.

name: proteogenomics
definition: Field of biological research in-between proteomics and genomics using proteomic information (mostly derived from mass spectrometry) to improve gene annotations.

name: proteolysis
definition: Protein cleavage to generate proteolytic peptides for bottom-up proteomic analysis, either enzymatic or chemical.

name: proteolytic digestion
definition: Exposure of a sample to proteolytic reactions.

name: proteolytic enzyme
definition: Group of enzymes that cleave the polypeptide into shorter oligopeptides (peptides) and amino acids.

name: proteolytic peptide
definition: Peptide generated via proteolysis.

name: proteomics
definition: Complex and comprehensive study of proteomes, particularly proteins, and the way they are expressed, modified, involved in metabolism, as well as of their interactions.

name: relative quantification
definition: Type of protein/peptide quantification, where the relative amounts of one protein in different samples is determined, i.e. the ratio of the content of a protein/peptide in sample 1 to sample 2.

name: stable isotope labelling
definition: Techniques which serve to quantify protein content by means of mass spectrometry. The principle lies in the introduction of a mass tag to an internal standard protein/peptide containing different stable isotopes than the protein/peptide in the sample. Mass resolved signals originating in the internal standard and the sample are read individually and evaluated.

name: structural proteomics
definition: Field in proteomics which focuses on higher orders of the protein structure, mainly tertiary or quaternary.

name: targeted proteomics
definition: Approach in proteomics focused on the selected proteins of a sample.

name: tertiary structure of a protein
definition: Arrangement of all atoms of a protein molecule or a subunit of a protein molecule in space, without regard to its relationship with neighbouring molecules or subunits.

name: top-down proteomics
definition: Approach to identify proteins and characterise their amino acid sequences or post-translational modifications either by direct mass spectrometric analysis of an ionised protein molecule or by sequential combination of protein/peptide fragmentation in the ion source or mass analyser with ion trapping mass spectrometers.

name: trypsin
definition: Serine protease with highly specific primary endoproteolytic activity that serves to generate proteolytic peptides in bottom-up proteomics analysis.

name: two-dimensional gel electrophoresis
definition: Technique used to separate proteins using isoelectric focusing in a gel. The proteins are then further separated in the second dimension using denaturing PAGE.

name: Western blot
definition: Immunoanalytical technique for the identification of polypeptides separated using gel electrophoresis. The polypeptide is transferred by blotting to a membrane, where it undergoes specific interaction with primary antibody that is specific to the protein of interest. The peptides are detected as complexes by a label and/or enzymatic reaction, which may be conjugated to the primary antibody directly or via a separate (secondary) antibody.

name: cultivation
definition: Sample pretreatment to degrade complex metabolites in the presence of oxygen; a method for amplifying the concentration of native metabolites in solution.

name: design of experiment
definition: Metabolomic workflow composed of sampling, metabolism quenching, metabolite extraction, metabolite analyses, data analysis, and interpretation.

name: endometabolome
definition: Complete set of metabolites inside a cell (intracellular metabolites).

name: excretion
definition: Process removing compounds and their metabolites from the body, usually through the kidneys (via urine) or in the feces. Unless excretion is complete, the accumulation of foreign substances can adversely affect normal metabolism.

name: exometabolome
definition: Complete set of metabolites outside the cell (extracellular environment).

name: fingerprinting
definition: Qualitative analysis of the endometabolome.

name: fluxomics
definition: In vivo measurements of metabolic fluxes and integration of the results into stoichiometric network models.

name: footprinting
definition: Qualitative analysis of the exometabolome.

name: glucuronide
definition: Glycoside of glucuronic acid.

name: metabolic pathway
definition: All metabolic products of the main compound (e.g. phase 1 and phase 2 metabolites) with the routes of metabolism and the excreted metabolites in body fluids, e.g. in urine or blood.

name: metabolism quenching
definition: Physical or chemical methodology used for rapidly breaking all biochemical processes in metabolomic samples.

name: metabolite fingerprinting and footprinting
definition: Unique pattern characterizing the metabolism in a given living phase that does not attempt to identify or quantify all the metabolites.

name: metabolite profiling
definition: Strategy to identify and quantify a particular set of metabolites belonging to a specific metabolic pathway or class of compounds.

name: metabolome
definition: Complete set (from \(\pu{50}\) to \(\pu{1000}\) metabolites) of organic or inorganic compounds of low relative molecular mass, present in the cell or organism and which participate in the metabolic reactions required for growth, maintenance, and normal functioning.

name: metabolomics
definition: Complex and comprehensive study of metabolome; identification and quantification of the small molecule metabolic products of a biological system (cell, tissue, organ, biological fluid, or organism) at a specific point in time.

name: metabonomics
definition: Measurement of the dynamic multiparametric metabolic response of a living system to pathophysiological stimuli or genetic modification.

name: primary metabolite
definition: Metabolite directly involved in the normal life processes of each cell.

name: activated nucleotide sugar
definition: Activated form of monosaccharide linked to a nucleotide to be available in a high-energy state for glycosyl transfer.

name: anomeric hydroxy group
definition: Hydroxy group that originates from the aldehydic or ketonic group of a monosaccharide after ring closure.

name: carbohydrate
definition: Monosaccharide, oligosaccharide and polysaccharide substances, as well as substances derived from a monosaccharide by reduction of the carbonyl group (alditol), by oxidation, including the oxidation of one or more terminal groups of a carboxylic acid, or by replacement of one or more hydroxy groups by a hydrogen atom, an amino group, a thiol group, or by similar heteroatomic groups. This term also includes derivatives of these of these compounds.

name: comparative glycoproteomics
definition: Field of glycoproteomics that studies that the changes in the structures and expression levels of glycoproteins under different conditions.

name: comparative proteoglycomics
definition: Field of proteoglycomics that studies the changes in the structures and expression levels of proteoglycans under different conditions.

name: glycan microarray
definition: Glycans attached to a surface of a microarray.

name: glycan profiling
definition: Determination of the diversity of glycan structures expressed on glycoconjugates or cells.

name: glycan-binding protein
definition: Protein that recognises and binds to specific glycans and mediates their biological function.

name: glycoform
definition: Specific form of a glycoprotein containing a distinct glycan structure per glycosylation site.

name: glycogene
definition: Gene encoding an enzyme or other functional protein for glycan synthesis.

name: glycolipid
definition: Compound containing a glycan covalently linked to a lipid aglycon.

name: glycome
definition: Complete set of glycans and glycoconjugates produced by a species, tissue, or cell in a specified time, space, and environment.

name: glycomics
definition: Complex and comprehensive study of the glycome.

name: glycone
definition: Carbohydrate part of a glycoconjugate or a glycoside.

name: glycoprotein
definition: Protein with one or more covalently bound glycans.

name: glycoproteomics
definition: Comprehensive analysis of glycoproteins.

name: glycosidase
definition: Enzyme that catalyses the hydrolysis of glycosidic linkages.

name: glycoside
definition: Mixed acetal formally arising by the elimination of water between the hemiacetal or hemiketal hydroxy group of a sugar and a hydroxy group of a second compound. Glycan containing at least one glycosidic linkage to another glycan or an aglycon.

name: glycosidic linkage
definition: Linkage of a monosaccharide to another residue via the anomeric hydroxy group.

name: glycosyl
definition: Monosaccharide ring without the anomeric oxygen.

name: glycosylation
definition: Covalent attachment of a saccharide to a protein, lipid, polynucleotide, saccharide, or other organic compound, generally catalysed by enzymes glycosyltransferases.

name: glycosyltransferase
definition: Enzyme that catalyses the transfer of a saccharide from a nucleotide di(mono)phosphate-activated sugar to an acceptor molecule.

name: hemiacetal
definition: Compound having the general formula \(\ce{RCH(OH)(OR^{\prime})}\) (\(\ce{R^{\prime}}  eq \ce{H}\)).

name: hemiketal
definition: Compound having the general formula \(\ce{R2C(OH)OR^{\prime}}\) (\(\ce{R^{\prime}}  eq \ce{H}\)).

name: lectin
definition: Saccharide binding protein of non-immune origin.

name: lectin microarray
definition: Lectins with distinct saccharide-binding specificity arranged on a microarray platform.

name: proteoglycomics
definition: Systematic study of the structure, expression, and function of proteoglycans.

name: sugar
definition: Term frequently applied to monosaccharides and lower oligosaccharides.

name: alkaline degradation
definition: Treatment with alkaline solution (e.g. hydrazine, \(\ce{KOH}\), \(\ce{NaOH}\)) useful for the cleavage of fatty acids.

name: core oligosaccharide
definition: Intermediate structural region between the O-polysaccharide and lipid A moiety of lipopolysaccharides (LPS).

name: fatty acyls
definition: Diverse group of lipid molecules synthesised by chain elongation of an acetyl-CoA primer with malonyl-CoA (or methylmalonyl-CoA) groups.

name: glycerolipids
definition: Esters, ethers, and other O-derivatives of glycerol with alkyls or alkenyls, including mono-, di-, and tri-substituted glycerols.

name: glycerophospholipids
definition: Lipids with glycerol backbone esterified with one or two fatty acids in position \(\ce{C-1}\) and/or \(\ce{C-2}\) and with phosphoric acid at position \(\ce{C-3}\). The phosphate group is usually esterified with an alcohol (choline, ethanolamine, serine, inositol, glycerol) to form the 'lipid head group'.

name: lipid A
definition: Glycolipid component of lipopolysaccharides (LPSs) that is integrated into the bacterial cell wall and is responsible for the beneficial (immunostimulatory) or toxic (immunopathological) effects of the molecule.

name: lipid droplets
definition: Round-shaped intracellular inclusions consisting of hydrophobic cores (mainly triacylglycerols, sterol esters, occasionally free fatty acids or squalene) covered by a phospholipid monolayer containing a specific set of proteins.

name: lipid extraction
definition: Isolation of lipids in their native state from samples of different origin.

name: lipid profiling
definition: Lipidomics technique conferring unbiased information about total lipids within a particular cell type, tissue, or body fluid.

name: lipid remodelling
definition: Changes in the lipid molecules composition after completion of their biosynthesis.

name: lipidome
definition: Complete set of lipid species and their metabolites present within a particular cell type, tissue, or body fluid.

name: lipidomics
definition: Systematic and comprehensive study aimed at the identification, profiling, and quantification of lipidome.

name: lipooligosaccharide
definition: Lipopolysaccharide produced by specific wild-type bacteria that give a smooth-colony appearance when cultured on agar plates.

name: lipopolysaccharidomics
definition: Study of the structure-activity relationship of bacterial lipopolysaccharides.

name: membrane bilayer
definition: Planar structure spontaneously formed by amphipathic lipids in a polar (aqueous) environment.

name: membrane rafts
definition: Dynamic, nanometre-sized, highly ordered, membrane domains enriched in sterols and sphingolipids. They contain specific sets of membrane proteins that are sorted into rafts by their specific physical properties and specific lipid-protein interactions.

name: molecular shape of lipids
definition: Specific structure of lipid molecules (glycerophospholipids) in aqueous environments and membranes as a function of the ratio between the cross-sections of their polar heads and hydrophobic tails.

name: O-polysaccharide
definition: Part of a lipopolysaccharide that consists of a polysaccharide chain extending outwards from the bacterial cell surface.

name: plasma lipoproteins
definition: Assemblies of lipids and proteins in blood plasma transporting lipids between tissues.

name: polyunsaturated fatty acids
definition: Fatty acids with more than one double bond.

name: prenol lipids
definition: Lipids containing a linear chain of isoprenoid groups.

name: proteolipids
definition: Proteins with covalently linked lipids, e.g. fatty acid or glycophosphatidylinositol (GPI).

name: saccharolipids
definition: Biomolecules where fatty acids are directly bound to a saccharide backbone, thus forming structures similar to glycerolipids or glycerophospholipids, with saccharide substituting for the glycerol.

name: shotgun lipidomics
definition: Methodological approach based on the direct analysis of the total lipid extracts from cells or tissues without an online chromatographic separation.

name: signalling lipids
definition: Lipid molecules involved in intracellular signalling and the regulation of cell death, immune response, or inflammation.

name: sphingolipids
definition: Complex family of lipids that contain a sphingoid base backbone and a fatty acyl chain.

name: sterol lipids
definition: Structural derivatives of tetracyclic alcohols with a hydroxyl group in the position \(\ce{C-3}\) and an aliphatic side chain in the position \(\ce{C-17}\).

name: structural lipids
definition: Lipids (mainly glycerophospholipids, sterols and sphingolipids) involved in the formation of biological membranes.

name: targeted lipidomics
definition: Analytical technique focusing on the quantification of specific lipids of interest.

name: unsaturation index
definition: Measure of the number of double bonds in fatty acids moieties of phospholipids, calculated as the fraction of each unsaturated fatty acid multiplied by the number of double bonds within that fatty acid.

name: capture probe
definition: Specifically-designed single-stranded nucleic acid with a defined (known) nucleotide sequence immobilised on a surface.

name: chromatin immunoprecipitation
definition: Method for studying deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA)–protein and/or protein–protein interactions in the context of chromatin, suitable for the identification of binding sites of proteins in genome DNA, etc. This method combines chemical cross-linking, the isolation of specific protein conjugates by immunoprecipitation, and polymerase chain reaction (PCR) amplification of co-precipitated DNA.

name: cross-linking
definition: Formation of a covalent bridge between two biomacromolecules or between two segments of the same biomacromolecule using reactive substances (e.g. formaldehyde, bifunctional aldehydes such as glutaraldehyde, or cisplatin) or photochemical processes.

name: fluorescent in situ hybridization
definition: Cytogenetic technique used to detect and localise the presence or absence of specific deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) sequences on chromosomes. It uses fluorescent probes that only bind to those parts of the chromosome with which they show a high degree of sequence complementarity.

name: groove binding
definition: Process in which molecules are bound within a minor or major groove of the deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) double helix.

name: hybridization assay
definition: Assay with specifically designed single-stranded deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) probe with a defined (known) nucleotide sequence usually immobilised on a surface (in such a case, the nucleic acid probe is called the capture probe).

name: interactome
definition: Virtual map depicting protein–protein interactions.

name: interactomics
definition: Complex and comprehensive study of the interactions between various proteins and between protein and other molecules within a cell, such as nucleic acids and metabolites, as well as the consequences of these interactions.

name: intermolecular interactions
definition: Interactions between (parts of) two biomolecule chains (e.g. base pairing in deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) double helix, or the interactions between two polypeptide chains, or between a DNA and a protein molecule).

name: intramolecular interactions
definition: Interactions between (neighbouring or distant) segments within the same biomolecule chain (e.g. base pairing in hairpin or monomolecular tetraplex structures of deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) or ribonucleic acid (RNA), the interactions stabilizing the secondary or tertiary structures of proteins, etc.).

name: non-covalent interactions
definition: Interactions between biomolecules or within a biomolecule (e.g. hydrogen bonds, electrostatic interactions, and van der Waals forces) taking part in the stabilization of proper biomolecule structure and intermolecular interactions.

name: non-specific binding
definition: Binding of a protein to deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) independent of the nucleotide sequence or the conformation of the DNA, often with a strong contribution of electrostatic interaction between the negatively charged sugar-phosphate backbone of the DNA and basic amino acid residues of the protein.

name: nucleic acid–protein interaction
definition: Formation of specific or non-specific complexes between deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) or ribonucleic acid (RNA) and proteins, mediated and stabilised by a network of non-covalent interactions.

name: protein–protein interaction
definition: Association of one protein with one or more other proteins to form either homo- or heteromeric proteins or protein complexes.

name: pull-down assay
definition: Approach used for studying protein–protein interactions analogous to immunoprecipitation, using (instead of antibody) one of the interacting proteins (the 'bait') immobilised at a surface to capture the other protein (the 'prey').

name: reporter probe
definition: Specifically designed single-stranded deoxyribonucleic acid (ssDNA) (alternatively, ribonucleic acid (RNA) or a synthetic nucleic acid analogue such as locked nucleic acid (LNA) or peptide nucleic acid (PNA)) with a defined (known) nucleotide sequence used to detect complementary DNA or RNA sequence in a sample.

name: specific binding
definition: Binding of proteins to specific sites in deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) based on the precise recognition of nucleotide sequence and/or conformation of the DNA.

name: stacking interactions
definition: Attractive interaction between planar aromatic rings, in nucleic acids being one of the critical forces stabilizing double- and multistranded structures.

name: Tunel test
definition: Method for the determination of strand breaks and DNA fragmentation in cells based on labelling and quantification of free 3′-OH ends of deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA).

name: two hybrid system
definition: Molecular biology method for studying protein–protein or protein–deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) interactions in cellular (yeast or bacterial) milieu.

name: chromatographic bed
definition: Form in which the stationary phase is used.

name: immobilized stationary phase
definition: Stationary phase which has been immobilized on the support particles or on the inner wall of the column, e.g. by a physical attraction (coated stationary phase), by chemical bonding (bonded stationary phase), or by in situ polymerisation (cross-linked stationary phase) after coating.

name: countercurrent chromatography
definition: Partition chromatography which uses two immiscible liquid phases and no solid support. One liquid acts as the stationary phase and the other as the mobile phase.

name: enantioselective chromatography
definition: Separation of enantiomeric species due to the enantioselectivity of their interaction with the chiral selector(s) of a chromatographic (electrophoretic) system.

name: hydrodynamic chromatography
definition: Liquid chromatography for the separation of macromolecules and particles based on the difference in the speed of the mobile phase flow between the column axis and column wall and the specific size-dependent distribution of particles across the column cross-section.

name: hydrophilic-interaction liquid chromatography
definition: Liquid chromatography in which the molecules are partitioned between a water-enriched layer, which is immobilised on a hydrophilic (polar) stationary phase, and a less-polar mobile phase, containing water and organic solvent.

name: hydrophobic-interaction chromatography
definition: Chromatography in which molecules are separated by interactions between their hydrophobic moieties and hydrophobic sites on the surface of the stationary phase.

name: ion-exclusion chromatography
definition: Exclusion chromatography in which ionized compounds are excluded from the pores of the support and elute first, while weakly ionized and non-ionic compounds elute later.

name: ion-pair chromatography
definition: Liquid chromatography in which the mobile liquid phase contains an ionized additive (an ion-pair reagent) that can form an ion pair with an analyte molecule.

name: ligand exchange chromatography
definition: Chromatography based on the different ability of substances to form complexes with metal ions.

name: micellar chromatography
definition: Reversed-phase liquid chromatography which uses a mobile phase containing a surfactant above its critical micellar concentration (cmc).

name: isocratic elution
definition: Chromatography in which the composition of the mobile phase remains constant during elution.

name: column diameter
definition: Inner diameter of the column tubing.

name: column length
definition: Length of that part of the column tube that contains the stationary phase.

name: cross-sectional area of the column
definition: Cross-sectional area of the empty tube: \(A_{\rm{c}} = \pi r_{\rm{c}}^{2} = \pi (d_{\rm{c}}/2)^{2}\), where \(d_{\rm{c}}\) is the column diameter.

name: liquid-phase film thickness
definition: Average thickness of the liquid stationary phase film coated on the inside wall of the column tubing of an open-tubular column.

name: monolithic column
definition: Column packed with a single piece of solid material (monolith) composed of interconnected skeletons (forming macropores) and interconnected flow paths (mesopores) as a stationary phase material.

name: asymmetry factor
definition: Width of a peak (\(f + b\)) divided by twice the width of the front of the peak (\(f\)), measured at \(\pu{10\%}\) of the peak height (see figure). \[A_{\rm{s}} = \frac{(f + b)}{2f}\] Peak asymmetry (schematic). \(R_{\rm{D}}\) is the response of the detector.Peak asymmetry (schematic). \(R_{\rm{D}}\) is the response of the detector.

name: peak width at base
definition: Peak width at peak base intercepted by tangents to the chromatogram drawn at the inflection points on either side of the peak. Represented by the line AB in the peak height figure.

name: peak width at half height
definition: Peak width at \(\pu{50\%}\) of the peak height that terminates at the intersections with the peak.

name: tailing factor
definition: Width of the back of a peak (\(b\)) divided by the width of the front (\(f\)) of the peak measured at \(\pu{10\%}\) of the peak height. See figure in asymmetry factor.

name: effective plate height
definition: Column length (\(L\)) divided by effective plate number (\(N_{\rm{eff}}\)): \[H_{\rm{eff}} = \frac{L}{N_{\rm{eff}}}\]
synonyms: height equivalent to one effective plate

name: effective plate number
definition: Number indicative of column performance, calculated from the ratios of measures of adjusted retention and peak width: \[\eqalign{& N_{\rm{eff}} = \left(\frac{V_{\rm{R}}^{\prime}}{\sigma} \right)^{2} = \left(\frac{t_{\rm{R}}^{\prime}}{\sigma} \right)^{2} \cr & N_{\rm{eff}} = 16 \left(\frac{V_{\rm{R}}^{\prime}}{w_{\rm{b}}} \right)^{2} = 16 \left(\frac{t_{\rm{R}}^{\prime}}{w_{\rm{b}}} \right)^{2} \cr & N_{\rm{eff}} \approx 5.545 \left(\frac{V_{\rm{R}}^{\prime}}{w_{\rm{h}}} \right)^{2} \approx 5.545 \left(\frac{t_{\rm{R}}^{\prime}}{w_{\rm{h}}} \right)^{2}}\]

name: reduced plate height
definition: In liquid chromatography plate height divided by average particle diameter. \[h = H/d_{\rm{p}}\]

name: detector
definition: Sensor that responds to components in the effluent.

name: capillary affinity electrophoresis
definition: Capillary electrophoresis in which the background electrolyte contains substances capable of specific, often biospecific, interactions with the analytes.

name: capillary electrochromatography
definition: Liquid chromatography, where the movement of the mobile phase through a capillary, filled, packed, or coated with a stationary phase, is achieved by electroosmotic flow (which may be assisted by pressure).

name: capillary electrophoresis
definition: Separation method based solely on the differences in the electrophoretic mobilities of charged species in capillaries.

name: capillary gel electrophoresis
definition: Capillary sieving electrophoresis in which the capillary is filled with a gel.

name: capillary isoelectric focusing
definition: Electrophoretic technique for the separation of analytes according to their isoelectric points by an electric field along a pH gradient formed in a capillary.

name: capillary isotachophoresis
definition: Electrophoretic separation technique in a discontinuous buffer system in which analytes migrate according to their electrophoretic mobilities, forming a chain of adjacent zones moving with equal speed (velocity) between two solutions, leading and terminating electrolytes, bracketing the mobility range of the analytes.

name: capillary sieving electrophoresis
definition: Electrophoretic separation technique, which takes place in a capillary containing a medium in the background electrolyte that retains molecules and particles based on their size and shape.

name: effective length of the capillary
definition: Length of the capillary from the sample introduction point to the detection point.

name: electrokinetic chromatography
definition: Separation method based on a combination of electrophoresis and interactions of the analytes with additives (e.g. surfactants), which form a dispersed phase moving at a different speed (velocity). In order to achieve separation, either the analytes or this secondary phase should be charged.

name: electrokinetic injection
definition: Injection of the analytical sample by applying a potential across the sample and capillary and using the electroosmotic flow to draw an aliquot into the end of the capillary tube. The sample is then replaced by the running electrolyte for the separation to take place.

name: electroosmosis
definition: Motion of a liquid through a capillary (or membrane or plug) because of the application of an electric field across the capillary (or membrane or plug).

name: electroosmotic velocity
definition: Effective length of the capillary (\(L_{\rm{eff}}\)) divided by the electroosmotic hold-up time (\(t_{\rm{eo}}\)). \[\boldsymbol{v}_{\rm{eo}} = L_{\rm{eff}}/t_{\rm{eo}}\]

name: electroosmotic volume flow rate
definition: Volume flow rate divided by electric field strength through the whole plug or capillary.

name: electrostacking
definition: Methods that use differences in migration behaviour in spatially defined regions of the capillary of different field strengths (conductivities).

name: hydrodynamic injection
definition: Introduction of the analytical sample into a capillary by a pressure difference between the ends of the capillary.

name: immunoelectrophoresis
definition: Biochemical methods for separation and characterization of proteins based on electrophoresis and reaction with antibodies.

name: micellar electrokinetic chromatography
definition: Electrokinetic chromatography, in which the secondary phase is a micellar dispersed phase in the capillary.

name: microemulsion electrokinetic chromatography
definition: Electrokinetic chromatography, where a microemulsion is employed as the dispersed phase.

name: non-aqueous capillary electrophoresis
definition: Capillary electrophoresis, which uses water-free organic solutions and modifiers to produce ions in solution.

name: sample introduction
definition: In isotachophoresis a sample is introduced between a zone of fast leading electrolyte and a zone of slow terminating electrolyte.

name: asymmetrical flow field-flow fractionation
definition: Flow field-flow fractionation in which only one channel wall is permeable, meaning there is one channel inlet for the flow during the run and some of the channel flow is directed through the accumulation wall.

name: Brownian field-flow fractionation mode
definition: Mechanism of field-flow fractionation of sub-micron particles that relies on Brownian motion.
synonyms: BFFF|BFFF mode|NFFF mode|normal FFF|normal FFF mode (NFFF)

name: coiled-tube field-flow fractionation
definition: Field-flow fractionation in a long (usually \(\pu{10 m}\) or more) rotating coiled column under the action of asymmetrical centrifugal field.

name: field-flow fractionation
definition: Separation based on the retention and elution of macromolecular, colloidal, and particulate matter achieved by the combined action of the non-uniform flow speed (velocity) profile of a carrier fluid (mobile phase) and a physical force field (e.g. gravitational, centrifugal, electrical) applied at right angles to a thin (\(\pu{0.05 mm}\) to \(\pu{0.5 mm}\)) channel (see figure). Basic principle of field-flow fractionation.Basic principle of field-flow fractionation.

name: flow field-flow fractionation
definition: Field-flow fractionation in which the physical force field is a nonspecific hydrodynamic force field across the channel, generated by a secondary mobile phase cross-flow in addition to the normal channel flow.

name: gravitational field-flow fractionation
definition: Field-flow fractionation in which the physical force field is the Earth’s gravitational field.

name: hyperlayer focusing field-flow fractionation
definition: Mechanism of field-flow fractionation of particles greater than \(\pu{1 \upmu m}\) in diameter relying on hydrodynamic lift forces near the channel wall to move particles into faster flowing streams.
synonyms: HyFFF|hyperlayer field-flow fractionation mode|lift-hyperlayer field-flow fractionation mode

name: sedimentation field-flow fractionation
definition: Field-flow fractionation in which the physical force field is a centrifugal force field.

name: split-flow thin-cell fractionation
definition: Separation in which laminar flow conditions are established between a liquid containing suspended sample and a carrier liquid, with a physical force field applied across the streams.

name: steric field-flow fractionation
definition: Mechanism of field-flow fractionation of particles greater than \(\pu{1 \upmu m}\) in diameter relying on proximity to the accumulation wall.

name: symmetrical flow field-flow fractionation
definition: Flow field-flow fractionation in which the speed of mobile phase is constant along the length of the channel due to constant channel width.

name: thermal field-flow fractionation
definition: Field-flow fractionation in which the physical force field is created by a temperature difference across the channel.

name: elution mode
definition: Method of introduction of the mobile phase (upper or lower) into the rotating coil (from the head or the tail). Of four combinations, only two elution modes should be used in high-speed counter-current chromatography, i.e. either the lower phase from the head toward the tail or the upper phase from the tail toward the head.

name: high-speed counter-current chromatography
definition: Counter-current chromatography system using a multilayer coil separation column, which undergoes a type-J synchronous planetary motion (see figure).Type-J planetary motion of a multilayer coil separation column. The column holder rotates about its own axis and revolves around the centrifuge axis at the same angular velocity (ω) in the same direction. This planetary motion prevents twisting of the bundle of flow tubes, allowing continuous elution through a rotating column without risk of leakage and contamination.

name: mobile-phase volume
definition: Volume of the liquid mobile phase contained in the column in counter-current chromatography \[V_{\rm{M}} = V_{\rm{C}} - V_{\rm{S}}\] where \(V_{\rm{C}}\) is the total volume of the column and \(V_{\rm{S}}\) is the volume of the liquid stationary phase in the column.

name: multilayer coil
definition: Separation column used for high-speed counter-current chromatography.

name: pH-zone-refining counter-current chromatography
definition: Counter-current chromatography that produces a train of fused rectangular solute peaks called pH-zones, each with its specific pH. Each zone contains highly concentrated solute, often near saturation level, and is separated from the neighbouring zone by a narrow strip called a mixing zone, which contains a mixture of impurities.

name: retainer and eluter
definition: Most important reagents in pH-zone-refining counter-current chromatography. A retainer is added to the stationary organic phase to retain the analytes and the eluter added to the mobile aqueous phase to elute the analytes.

name: retention volume of the stationary phase
definition: Volume of the stationary phase, which stays permanently within the column in counter-current chromatography.

name: type-J coil planet centrifuge
definition: Centrifuge that provides type-J synchronous planetary motion to the column holder, the axis of which is parallel to the centrifuge axis (see figure in high-speed counter-current chromatography).

name: type-J synchronous planetary motion
definition: Unique type of planetary motion (so named because the flow tubes form a letter J figure, as shown in the figure in high-speed counter-current chromatography) of the column holder, which rotates around its own axis once during one revolution around the central axis of the centrifuge in the same direction.

name: chiral additive
definition: Chiral selector that has been added as a component of a mobile phase or electrophoretic medium.

name: comprehensive two-dimensional chromatography
definition: Type of two-dimensional chromatography in which all the effluent from the first separation step is transferred in fractions to a second separation step.

name: heart-cut separations
definition: Type of two-dimensional chromatography in which selected fractions from the first separation step are transferred to a second separation step.

name: modulation frequency
definition: Number of modulations in a given time interval.

name: modulation number
definition: Number of modulations for a given first-dimension peak.

name: modulation period
definition: Duration of a complete cycle of modulation in a system for comprehensive two-dimensional chromatography.

name: modulator
definition: Interface device between the two columns in a system for comprehensive two-dimensional chromatography that accumulates or samples narrow bands from the effluent of the first column for fast re-injection into the second column.

name: multi-dimensional chromatography
definition: Chromatography in which parts or all of the separated sample components are subjected to additional separation steps.

name: wrap-around
definition: Occurrence of second dimension peaks in subsequent elution sequences, caused by second-dimension retention times that exceed the modulation time in comprehensive two-dimensional chromatography.

name: retention volume of an unretained compound
definition: Retention volume of a sample component the molecules of which are larger than the largest pores of the particles of the stationary phase.

name: retention volume
definition: Retention volume of a sample component, the molecules of which are smaller than the largest pores of the particles of the stationary phase but larger than the smallest pores.

name: total mobile phase volume
definition: Retention volume of a sample component, the molecules of which are smaller than the smallest pores of the particles of the stationary phase.

name: relative molecular-mass exclusion limit
definition: Maximum value of the relative molecular masses of components in a specific polymer solvent system that can enter into the pores of the porous non-adsorbing material used in size-exclusion chromatography.

name: specific resolution
definition: Peak resolution also considering the molar masses (\(M_{1}\), \(M_{2}\)) of the two test compounds: \[R_{\rm{sp}} = \left[\frac{V_{\rm{R1}} - V_{\rm{R2}}}{(w_{\rm{b1}} + w_{\rm{b2}})/2} \right] \cdot \left[ \frac{1}{\log (M_{2}/M_{1})} \right]\]

name: flavans
definition: Flavans are compounds with a 2-phenyl-3,4-dihydro-2\(H\)-1-benzopyran skeleton (1 in flavonoids), that may be substituted, and include flavan-3-ols (compounds derived from 2-phenyl-3,4-dihydro-2\(H\)-1-benzopyran-3-ol skeleton 2) and flavan-4-ones (compounds derived from 2-phenyl-2,3-dihydro-4\(H\)-1-benzopyran-4-one skeleton 3), which are generically designated as flavanols and flavanones, respectively. Compounds derived from 2-phenyl-3,4-dihydro-2\(H\)-1-benzopyran-3,4-diol skeleton 4 are flavan-3,4-diols, designated leukoanthocyanidins because these colourless compounds have their structure derived from that of an anthocyanidin, specifically they are dehydronated 3,4-dihydroxy-1,2,3,4-tetrahydroanthocyanidins.

name: flavones
definition: Flavones and 3-hydroxyflavones (flavonols) are compounds with a 2-phenyl-4\(H\)-1-benzopyran-4-one (2-phenyl-4\(H\)-chromen-4-one) skeleton 5.

name: isoflavans
definition: Isoflavans are compounds with a 3-phenyl-3,4-dihydro-2\(H\)-1-benzopyran skeleton (see isoflavonoids). They may be substituted.

name: isoflavones
definition: Isoflavones are compounds with a 3-phenyl-4$H$-1-benzopyran-4-one (3-phenyl-4$H$-chromen-4-one) skeleton 9. They may be substituted.

name: neoflavans
definition: Neoflavans are compounds with a 4-phenyl-3,4-dihydro-2$H$-1-benzopyran skeleton (see neoflavonoids). They may be substituted.

name: neoflavones
definition: Neoflavones are compounds with a 4-phenyl-2$H$-1-benzopyran-2-one (4-phenyl-2$H$-chromen-2-one) skeleton 11. They may be substituted.

name: aurones
definition: Aurones are compounds derived from (2$Z$)-2-benzylidene-1-benzofuran-3(2$H$)-one [alternative name: (2$Z$)-2-(phenylmethylidene)-1-benzofuran-3(2$H$)-one] (aurone, compound 14).

name: pterocarpans
definition: Pterocarpans are compounds derived from (6a$R$,11a$R$)-6a,11a-dihydro-6$H$-[1]benzofuro[3,2-$c$][1]benzopyran (15), and their 6a,11a-didehydro derivatives 16 are named coumestans. They are numbered systematically following the numbering rules for fused ring systems.

name: flavonolignans
definition: Flavonolignans have structures based on flavonoids condensed with \(\ce{C6{-}C3}\) lignan precursors.

name: biflavonoids
definition: Biflavonoid and other flavonoid oligomers, which occur widely in nature, are exemplified and named in this recommendation (Flv-3.8).

name: nominal property
definition: Property of a phenomenon, body, or substance, where the property has no size.

name: kind-of-nominal-property
definition: Defining aspect, common to mutually comparable nominal properties.

name: category
definition: Kind-of-nominal-property indicating a class among nominal properties ordered according to nominal property values of a specified nominal property value set without relation to size.

name: taxon
definition: Category indicating a class of organisms within a recognized hierarchically structured nominal property value set.

name: dedicated kind-of-nominal-property
definition: Kind-of-nominal-property with a sort of system and any pertinent sort(s) of component(s).

name: examination
definition: Process of experimentally obtaining one or more nominal property values that can reasonably be attributed to a nominal property.

name: examinand
definition: Nominal property intended to be examined.

name: examining system
definition: Set of one or more devices, including any reagent and supply, assembled and adapted to give information used to generate examined values from a nominal property value set.

name: influence nominal property
definition: Nominal property that, in an examination, does not affect the nominal property that is actually examined, but affects the relation between the nominal indication on the examining system and the examination result.

name: examination principle
definition: Phenomenon serving as a basis of an examination.

name: examination method
definition: Generic description of a logical organization of operations used in an examination.

name: examination procedure
definition: Detailed description of an examination according to one or more examination principles and to a given examination method and any decision algorithm necessary to obtain an examination result.

name: nominal indication
definition: Nominal property value provided by an examining system.

name: blank nominal indication
definition: Nominal indication obtained from an object similar to the one under investigation, except that the nominal property of interest is supposed not to be present, or is not contributing to the nominal indication.

name: repeatability condition
definition: Condition of examination out of a set of conditions that includes the same examination procedure, same operators, same examining system, same operating conditions, same location, and replicate examinations on the same or similar objects over a short period of time.

name: intermediate precision condition
definition: Condition of examination out of a set of conditions that includes the same examination procedure, same location, and replicate examinations on the same or similar objects over an extended period of time, but may include other conditions involving changes.

name: reproducibility condition
definition: Condition of examination out of a set of conditions that includes different locations, operators, examining systems, and replicate examinations on the same or similar objects.

name: nominal property value
definition: Feature common to equivalent individual nominal properties.

name: nominal property value set
definition: Set of possible nominal property values for nominal properties of a given kind-of-nominal-property.

name: reference nominal property value
definition: Nominal property value used as a basis for comparison with nominal property values of nominal properties of the same kind-of-nominal-property.

name: examination result
definition: Set of nominal property values being attributed to an examinand together with any other available relevant information.

name: examined value
definition: Nominal property value representing an examination result.

name: true nominal property value
definition: Nominal property value consistent with the definition of a nominal property.

name: conventional nominal property value
definition: Nominal property value attributed by agreement to a nominal property for a given purpose.

name: examination trueness
definition: Fraction of examined values identical to one or more reference nominal property values among all the examined values provided.

name: examination uncertainty
definition: Fraction of examined values that is different from a reference nominal property value among all the examined values provided.

name: examination error
definition: Disagreement between an examined value and a reference nominal property value.

name: examination accuracy
definition: Closeness of agreement between an examined value and a true nominal property value of an examinand.

name: examination precision
definition: Closeness of agreement between nominal indications on an examining system or examined values obtained by replicate examinations on the same or similar objects under specified examination conditions.

name: examination repeatability
definition: Examination precision under repeatability condition of examination.

name: intermediate examination precision
definition: Examination precision under intermediate precision condition of examination.

name: examination reproducibility
definition: Examination precision under reproducibility condition of examination.

name: systematic examination error
definition: Fraction of examined values with examination error that in replicate examinations remains constant or varies in a predictable manner.

name: examination bias
definition: Estimate of a systematic examination error.

name: target examination uncertainty
definition: Examination uncertainty specified as an acceptable fraction and decided on the basis of the intended use of examination results.

name: nominal property value coverage set
definition: Subset of the nominal property value set containing the true nominal property value(s) of an examinand with a stated probability, based on the information available.

name: nominal property value coverage probability
definition: Probability that the set of true nominal property values of an examinand is contained within a specified nominal property value coverage set.

name: examination traceability
definition: Property of an examination result whereby it can be related to a reference through a documented unbroken chain of examination calibrations, each contributing to the examination uncertainty.

name: examinational comparability
definition: Comparability of examination results, for nominal properties of a given kind-of-nominal-property, that are examined and traceable to the same reference.

name: examinational compatibility
definition: Property of a set of examination results for a specified examinand of a given kind-of-nominal-property that have overlapping nominal property value sets.

name: examination standard
definition: Realization of the definition of a given nominal property (2.1), with stated nominal property value (3.1) and associated examination uncertainty (3.9), used as a reference.

name: nominal reference material
definition: Material, sufficiently homogeneous and stable with reference to a specified nominal property, that has been established to be fit for its intended use in an examination.

name: examination calibration
definition: Process that confers to one or more persons or to a device the capacity to provide nominal property values from specified examinations after having examined one or more examination standards.

name: reference examination procedure
definition: Examination procedure accepted as providing examination results fit for their intended use in assessing examination trueness of examined values) obtained from other examination procedures for nominal properties of the same kind-of-nominal-property, in examination calibration, or in characterizing nominal reference materials.

name: primary reference examination procedure
definition: Reference examination procedure used to obtain an examination result without relation to an examination standard for a nominal property of the same kind-of-nominal-property.

name: international examination standard
definition: Examination standard recognized by signatories to an international agreement and intended to serve worldwide.

name: national examination standard
definition: Examination standard recognized by national authority to serve in a state or economy as the basis for assigning nominal property values to other examination standards for the same kind-of-nominal-property.

name: primary examination standard
definition: Examination standard established using a primary reference examination procedure, or created as an artefact, chosen by convention.

name: secondary examination standard
definition: Examination standard established through examination calibration with respect to a primary examination standard for a nominal property of the same kind-of-nominal-property.

name: reference examination standard
definition: Examination standard designated for the examination calibration of other examination standards for nominal properties of a given kind-of-nominal-property in a given organization or at a given location.

name: working examination standard
definition: Examination standard that is used routinely to calibrate or verify examining systems.

name: travelling examination standard
definition: Examination standard, sometimes of special construction, intended for transport between different locations.

name: transfer examination device
definition: Device used as an intermediary to compare examination standards.

name: intrinsic examination standard
definition: Examination standard based on a reproducible nominal property of a phenomenon or substance.

name: conservation
definition: Set of operations necessary to preserve the examinational properties of an examination standard within stated limits.

name: examination calibrator
definition: Examination standard used in examination calibration.

name: certified nominal reference material
definition: Nominal reference material accompanied by documentation issued by an authoritative body and providing one or more specified nominal property values with examination uncertainty and examination traceability, using valid examination procedures.

name: mobile-phase speed
definition: Linear velocity of the mobile phase across the average cross-section of the column.

name: adjusted retention time
definition: Total retention time (\(t_{\rm{R}}\)) minus hold-up time (\(t_{\rm{M}}\)). \(t_{\rm{R}}^{\prime} = t_{\rm{R}} - t_{\rm{M}}\)

name: hold-up time
definition: Time required to elute a component which is not retained by the stationary phase.

name: total retention time
definition: Time between sample injection and the emergence of the peak maximum of the sample component of interest.

name: retention time of an unretained compound
definition: Retention time of a sample component the molecules of which are larger than the largest pores of the particles of the stationary phase.

name: response
definition: Measured or observed quantity in an experimental design.

name: autocorrelation
definition: Correlation of a variable with itself over a successive time or space intervals (lags).

name: autoscaling
definition: Variance scaling of mean-centered data.

name: categorical data
definition: Data, values of which are one of a fixed number of nominal categories.

name: contingency table
definition: Type of table in a matrix format that displays the multivariate frequency distribution of variables.

name: data matrix
definition: Measurement results on a system arranged in a \(m \times n\) matrix, with \(m\) objects and \(n\) variables.

name: data pre-processing
definition: Manipulation of raw data prior to a specified data analysis treatment.

name: dynamic time warping
definition: Process of synchronizing a data matrix so that it represents the same time shifts.

name: evaluation data
definition: Data used to validate a model.

name: explanatory variable
definition: Variable that influences the value of a response variable, and is used to build models of the response variable.

name: exploratory data analysis
definition: Summary of the main characteristics of data, often using graphical methods.

name: mean centering
definition: Data pre-processing in which the mean value of a variable is subtracted from data across all objects. \[a_{i,j}^{\ast} = a_{i,j} - \frac{1}{n} \sum \limits_{i\,=\,1}^{n} a_{i,j}\]

name: multiplicative scatter correction
definition: Data pre-processing in which a constant and a multiple of a reference data set is subtracted from data.

name: multivariate data
definition: Data having two or more variables per object.

name: multi-way data
definition: Multivariate data having two or more kinds of explanatory variable per object.

name: random sampling
definition: Sampling in which the sample locations are selected randomly from the whole population.

name: raw data
definition: Data not yet subjected to analysis.

name: sampling unit
definition: Defined quantity of material having a boundary which may be physical or temporal.

name: scaling
definition: Element-wise division of a data matrix by a scaling matrix.

name: smoothing
definition: Transformation using an approximating function to capture important patterns in data, while removing noise or other fine-scale structures.

name: systematic sampling
definition: Sampling in which individual samples are taken at equal intervals in location.

name: take-it-or-leave-it data
definition: Happenstance data that must be processed, or not processed, as is.

name: variance scaling
definition: Scaling in which the scaling matrix is the standard deviation of each variable across the objects. \[a_{i,j}^{\ast} = \frac{a_{i,j}}{s_{j}}\]

name: alias structure
definition: List of combinations of effects that are aliased (confounded).

name: aliased effects
definition: In a fractional-factorial design, effects for which the information obtained are identical.

name: coded experimental design
definition: Matrix of runs by factor levels in which each level is denoted by a code that represents the relative magnitude of the level.

name: effect of a factor
definition: Coefficient of a term in a response model.

name: design matrix
definition: Matrix with rows representing individual experimental treatments (possibly transformed according to the assumed model) which can be extended by deduced levels of other functions of factor levels.

name: dummy factor
definition: Factor that is known to have no effect on the response, used in an experimental design, to estimate repeatability standard deviation.

name: experimental design
definition: Efficient procedure for planning combinations of values of factors in experiments so that the data obtained can be analyzed to yield valid and objective conclusions.

name: factor level
definition: Value of a factor in an experimental design.

name: fractional-factorial design
definition: Experimental design obtained from a full-factorial design in which experiments are systematically removed to fulfill stated statistical requirements.

name: full-factorial design
