definition: Experimental design with all possible combinations of factor levels.

name: interaction effect
definition: Effect of a factor where the term is the product of two or more factors.

name: main effect
definition: Effect of a factor where the term is a single factor.

name: model
definition: Equation describing the response as a function of values of the factors.

name: nth-order effect
definition: Effect of a factor where the term is a factor raised to the power \(n\).

name: optimization
definition: Minimization or maximization of a real function by systematically choosing the values of real or integer variables from within an allowed set.

name: Plackett−Burman design
definition: Incomplete experimental design to estimate main effects for which each combination of factor levels for any pair of factors appears the same number of times.

name: resolution of a design
definition: One more than the smallest nth-order interaction effect that some main effect is aliased with.

name: response surface methodology
definition: Experimental design in which the response is modelled in terms of one or more factor levels.

name: alternating least squares regression
definition: Solution to the multivariate decomposition of a data matrix in which iteratively a solution of one output matrix is used to compute the second matrix, after the application of constraints.

name: autoregression
definition: Stochastic process in which future values are estimated based on a weighted sum of past values.

name: biplot
definition: Combination plot of a scores plot as points and loadings plot as vectors for common factors.

name: bootstrapping
definition: Estimation of parameters by multiple re-sampling from measured data to approximate its distribution.

name: canonical variables
definition: Linear combinations of data with the greatest correlation.

name: canonical variate analysis
definition: Multivariate technique which finds linear combinations of two sets of data that are most highly correlated.

name: common factor analysis
definition: Factor analysis in which latent variables are calculated that maximise the correlation with observed variables.

name: core consistency diagnostic
definition: Method to assess the appropriateness of a PARAFAC model.

name: correspondence factor analysis
definition: Factor analysis applied to categorical data in which orthogonal factors are obtained from a contingency table.

name: evolving factor analysis
definition: Factor analysis that follows the change or evolution of the rank of the data matrix as a function of an ordered variable.

name: factor analysis
definition: Matrix decomposition of a data matrix (\(\boldsymbol{X}\)) into the product of a scores matrix (\(\boldsymbol{T}\)) and the transpose of the loadings matrix (\(\boldsymbol{P}^{\rm{T}}\)).

name: G-fold cross validation
definition: Cross validation of a data set of \(N\) objects in which \(N/G\) objects are removed at each iteration of the procedure.

name: latent variable
definition: Variable that is inferred through a mathematical model from other variables that are observed.

name: loadings
definition: Projection of a factor onto the variables.

name: loadings plot
definition: Plot of one loading against variable number, or two or three loadings against each other.

name: maximum likelihood principal component analysis
definition: Principal-component analysis that incorporates information about measurement uncertainty to develop models that are optimal in a maximum likelihood sense.

name: mean squared error of prediction
definition: In multivariate calibration the average of the squared deviation of estimated values from the values of evaluation data. For \(N\) evaluation data where \(c_{i}\) is an observed value and \(\hat c_{i}\) is the predicted value. \[E_{\rm{MSEP}} = \frac{\sum\limits_{i\,=\,1}^{i\,=\,N} (\hat c_{i}\,-\, c_{i})^2}{N}\]

name: multivariate curve resolution
definition: Factor analysis for the decomposition of multicomponent data into a linear sum of chemically-meaningful components when little or no prior information about the composition is available.

name: non-linear iterative partial least squares
definition: Iterative decomposition of a data matrix to give principal components.

name: nonlinear mapping
definition: Projection of objects defined in a multivariate space onto two- or three-dimensional space so that the distances between objects are preserved as well as possible.

name: parallel factors analysis
definition: Decomposition of a three-way data matrix into the sum of sets of two-way loadings matrices.

name: prediction error sum of squares
definition: In multivariate calibration for a prediction set of \(N\) data where \(c_{i}\) is an observed value and \(\hat c_{i}\) is the predicted value. \[E_{\rm{PRESS}} = \sum\limits_{i\,=\,1}^{i\,=\,N} (\hat c_{i} - c_{i})^2\]
synonyms: residual sum of squares|sum of squared errors of prediction|sum of squared residuals

name: principal component-discriminant analysis
definition: Discriminant analysis on a multivariate data set that has been subject to principal-component analysis.

name: principal-component analysis
definition: Factor analysis in which factors are calculated that successively capture the greatest variance in the data set.

name: principal-component factor
definition: Orthogonal factors obtained in a principal-component analysis.

name: Procrustes analysis
definition: Comparison of shapes of multi-dimensional objects by a series of geometrical transformations to minimise the sum of squared distances between the transformed and target structures while maintaining the internal structure of the objects.

name: root mean square error of cross validation
definition: Root mean square error of prediction when the predicted data is obtained by cross validation.

name: root mean squared error of prediction
definition: In multivariate calibration or classification for \(N\) evaluation data where \(c_{i}\) is an observed value and \(\hat c_{i}\) is the predicted value \[E_{\rm{RMSEP}} = \sqrt {\frac{\sum\limits_{i\,=\,1}^{i\,=\,N} (\hat c_{i}\,-\,c_{i})^2}{N}}\]
synonyms: root mean squared error of estimation|standard error of estimation|standard error of prediction

name: simple-to-use interactive self-modelling mixture analysis
definition: Interactive method to obtain concentrations and pure spectra from spectra of mixtures using directly-measured variables.

name: score
definition: Factor analysis projection of an object onto a factor.

name: scores plot
definition: Plot of one score against object number, or two or three scores against each other.

name: simulated annealing
definition: Generic probabilistic meta-heuristic to locate a good approximation to the global optimum of a given function in a large search space, in which there is a slow decrease in the probability of accepting worse solutions as the solution space is explored.

name: singular value decomposition
definition: A factorization of an \(m \times n\) matrix (\(\boldsymbol{M}\)) such that \(\boldsymbol{M} = \boldsymbol{U}\boldsymbol{\Sigma} \boldsymbol{V}^{T}\), where \(\boldsymbol{U}\) is an \(m \times m\) matrix, \(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}\) is a \(m \times n\) matrix and \(\boldsymbol{V}^{\rm{T}}\) is a \(n \times n\) matrix.

name: Tucker tri-linear analysis
definition: Decomposition of a three-way data matrix into a three-way core matrix, and three, two-way loadings matrices.

name: backward chaining
definition: Inference method from hypothesis to data that supports the hypothesis

name: backward propagation
definition: Supervised classification method for an artificial neural network in which weights of connections between nodes are calculated from the known output layer back to the input layer.

name: backward stepwise linear discriminant analysis
definition: Linear discriminant analysis in which variables to build the discriminant functions are removed one at a time to minimise the loss of discrimination, until there is a significant loss.

name: city-block distance
definition: Distance (\(d_{i,j}\)) between two objects (\(i\) and \(j\)) calculated as the sum of the absolute difference between \(k\) variables (\(x\)) that describe the objects. \[d_{i,j} = \sum\limits_{k\,=\,1}^{k\,=\,N} \vert x_{i,k} - x_{j,k}\vert\]

name: complete linkage
definition: Linkage criterion in hierarchical clustering in which the distance between two clusters is the distance between those two objects (one from each cluster) that are farthest apart.

name: dendrogram
definition: Tree diagram used to illustrate the arrangement of clusters produced by hierarchical clustering.

name: disjoint principal component analysis
definition: Principal-component analysis (PCA) independently performed on each class as a step in classification.

name: Euclidean distance
definition: Distance (\(d_{i,j}\)) between two objects (\(i\) and \(j\)) calculated as the square root of the sum of the squared differences between \(k\) variables (\(x\)) that describe the objects. \[d_{i,j} = \sqrt {\sum\limits_{k\,=\,1}^{k\,=\,N} (x_{i,k} - x_{j,k})^2}\]

name: forward chaining
definition: Inference method from data to hypothesis.

name: forward stepwise linear discriminant analysis
definition: Linear discriminant analysis in which variables to build the discriminant functions are introduced one at a time to maximise the discrimination, until there is no significant improvement.

name: fuzzy clustering
definition: Classification in which membership of an object in each possible class is given a weight between zero and one.

name: hidden layer
definition: Group of nodes in an artificial neural network between input layer and output layer.

name: hierarchical clustering
definition: Pattern recognition in which objects are linked together by use of an appropriate measure of distance between pairs of objects, and a linkage criterion, which specifies the dissimilarity of sets as a function of the pairwise distances between objects.

name: k-means clustering
definition: Unsupervised classification method which partitions objects into \(k\) groups, in which each object belongs to the group with the nearest mean.

name: k-nearest neighbour
definition: Non-parametric supervised classification method for objects based on the closest training examples in the variable space.

name: Kohonen network
definition: Type of self-organising map with low dimensional grid.

name: linear discriminant analysis
definition: Discriminant analysis in which the criterion function is based on the pooled covariance matrix.

name: Mahalanobis distance
definition: Distance (\(d_{i,j}\)) between an object characterised by vector of variables \(\boldsymbol{x}_{i}\) and the centroid of a class \(\boldsymbol{\mu}_{j}\) with covariance matrix \(\boldsymbol{S}\) calculated as \[d_{i,j} = \sqrt {(\boldsymbol{x}_{i} - \boldsymbol{\mu}_{j})^T \boldsymbol{S}^{-1}(\boldsymbol{x}_{i} - \boldsymbol{\mu}_{j})}\] where \(\boldsymbol{S}\) is the covariance matrix of the variables.

name: misclassification rate
definition: Fraction of objects incorrectly assigned to a group in supervised classification.

name: one-class classification
definition: Classification identifying objects of a specific class amongst all objects, by learning from training data containing only objects of the specific class.

name: node
definition: Locations in an artificial neural network that carry values that are calculated from values of connected nodes and weights by a transfer.

name: partial least squares discriminant analysis
definition: Linear classification in which the criterion function is obtained by partial least squares analysis.

name: quadratic discriminant analysis
definition: Discriminant analysis in which the criterion function is based on the individual within-group covariance matrix.

name: regularized discriminant analysis
definition: Discriminant analysis in which the criterion function is based on a combination of pooled covariance matrix and the individual within-group covariance matrix.

name: similarity index
definition: Quantity that describes the equivalence of two objects characterised by multivariate data.

name: single linkage
definition: Linkage criterion in hierarchical clustering in which the distance between two clusters is the distance between those two objects (one from each cluster) that are closest together.

name: soft independent modelling of class analogy
definition: Supervised classification that performs a principal-component analysis on each class, and then an unknown is assigned to the class with which it has the lowest residual variance.

name: supervised classification
definition: Classification in which, in a first step, a model is built using data from objects of known classes, and in a second step, the model is applied to new data to assign a class to unknown objects.

name: Tanimoto similarity index
definition: Fraction of variables that are considered to agree between two objects.

name: unsupervised classification
definition: Classification in which no prior information about membership of groups is known.

name: unweighted pair group method with arithmetic mean
definition: Linkage criterion in hierarchical clustering in which the distance between two clusters is the average of all distances between pairs of objects.

name: Ward’s minimum variance method
definition: Linkage criterion in hierarchical clustering in which the within-cluster variance is minimized.

name: least squares regression
definition: Regression that minimizes the sum of squared differences between observed values of a variable and the values predicted by a model.

name: errors-in-variables regression
definition: Least squares regression in which both the response variable and predictor variable have measurement error.

name: mean squared error of calibration
definition: In calibration for \(N\) calibration data where \(c_{i}\) is an observed value and \(\hat c_{i}\) is the value predicted by the calibration function. \[E_{\rm{MSEC}} = \frac{\sum\limits_{i\,=\,1}^{i\,=\,N} (\hat c_{i} - c_{i})^2}{N}\]

name: multilinear least squares regression
definition: Multivariate calibration in which the coefficients of the regression are calculated directly from the indications and values of standards.

name: multivariate calibration
definition: Calibration in which the indications are multivariate data.

name: ordinary least squares regression
definition: Least squares regression that minimizes the sum of squared differences between the known values of dependent variable and values predicted by a linear model.

name: partial least squares regression
definition: Multivariate calibration which finds factors that maximise covariance between two blocks of data.

name: principal components regression
definition: Multivariate calibration in which a dependent variable is regressed against the scores of a chosen number of factors obtained from principal-component analysis of the predictor variable.

name: root mean squared error of calibration
definition: In calibration for \(N\) calibration data where \(c_{i}\) is an observed value and \(\hat c_{i}\) is the value predicted by the calibration function. \[E_{\rm{RMSEC}} = \sqrt \frac{\sum\limits_{i\,=\,1}^{i,=\,N} (\hat c_{i} - c_{i})^2}{N}\]

name: underfitting of a calibration model
definition: Condition in which a model fails to describe the data adequately.

name: weighted least squares regression
definition: Least squares regression in which a nonnegative constant is associated with each value of the dependent variable.

name: boundary layer thickness
definition: Distance from the interface beyond which mass transfer is determined by convection.

name: breakthrough volume
definition: Sample volume at which a defined amount of an analyte pumped continuously through an extraction device will begin to be eluted. Typical breakthrough curve indicating the breakthrough volume \(V_{\rm{B}}\) and the sample volume corresponding to the saturation capacity of the sorbent \(V_{\rm{C}}\) (\(V_{\rm{R}}\) corresponds to the chromatographic elution volume and \(\upsigma_{\rm{v}}\) the standard deviation of the derivative of the curve).Typical breakthrough curve indicating the breakthrough volume \(V_{\rm{B}}\) and the sample volume corresponding to the saturation capacity of the sorbent \(V_{\rm{C}}\) (\(V_{\rm{R}}\) corresponds to the chromatographic elution volume and \(\upsigma_{\rm{v}}\) the standard deviation of the derivative of the curve).

name: ion-pair extraction
definition: Transfer of ions from an aqueous phase to an immiscible liquid (or solid) phase by adding an ion of complementary charge to the aqueous phase.

name: sorbent
definition: Condensed phase where extraction of analytes can occur at the surface and in the bulk.

name: acceptor phase
definition: Component of a multi-phase system into which the target analytes are extracted.

name: active sampling
definition: Continuous extraction with movement of the sample matrix with respect to the extraction phase.

name: batch extraction
definition: Extraction in which the extraction phase and the sample are confined in an extraction vessel and processed according to a defined procedure.

name: calibrant in extraction phase
definition: Internal standard that is incorporated in the extraction phase for calibration.

name: charcoal tube
definition: Tube filled with charcoal typically used to adsorb analytes from the gas or liquid phase.

name: continuous extraction
definition: Extraction in which the sample is continuously introduced into the extraction device.

name: countercurrent extraction
definition: Extraction in which both phases are continuously added (or changed) and flow (or move) in opposite directions as the extraction progresses.

name: donor phase
definition: In extraction, the sample or sample solution.

name: dynamic extraction
definition: Extraction in which clean (or recycled) extraction phase is continuously passed through the sample.

name: exhaustive extraction
definition: Type of extraction where the intent is a complete extraction of the analytes.

name: external calibration
definition: Calibration employing a simplified sample matrix spiked with target analyte embodying a reference value of the measurand.

name: extraction phase
definition: Liquid, solid, or gas phase in contact with the sample for the purpose of removal of analytes from the sample matrix.

name: extraction rate
definition: Rate at which analytes are transferred from the sample to the extraction phase.

name: feed
definition: Solution or gas containing analyte introduced into an extraction.

name: fluorous extraction
definition: Extraction in a biphasic system in which the main component of one phase is a highly fluorinated solvent (liquid-liquid extraction) or highly fluorinated sorbent (solid-phase extraction).

name: leaching
definition: Dissolution of sample components from a solid with a liquid in which the solid phase is not wholly soluble.

name: matrix-matched calibration
definition: Calibration employing external calibration in which standard solutions of target are prepared in a solution of analyte-free matrix.

name: multiwell sample plate
definition: Plate with multiple wells for individual samples.

name: optimisation of extraction
definition: Adjustment of extraction parameters to achieve a defined goal.

name: passive sampling
definition: Extraction process driven by diffusion of analytes towards the extraction phase.

name: salting in
definition: Addition of an electrolyte to an aqueous phase to decrease the distribution ratio of the analyte(s) or matrix.

name: sequential extraction
definition: Extraction wherein extractants of increasing strength or different chemical character are used in order to extract analytes of interest.

name: static extraction
definition: Batch extraction in which the extraction phase attains a constant composition before phase separation.

name: steady state extraction
definition: State of a continuous process operating in such a way that the concentration of solutes in exit streams remains constant with respect to time for constant feed concentrations, even though the two phases are not necessarily in thermodynamic equilibrium in any part of the process.

name: time-weighted average sampling
definition: A passive sampling or active sampling strategy over a relatively long time, during which the amount of analyte(s) extracted is proportional to its average (mean) concentration over that time.

name: chemical hydride generation
definition: Type of chemical vapour generation wherein volatile hydrides are generated by reaction with (usually) borane complexes in aqueous solution.

name: closed-loop extraction
definition: Extraction by a fixed volume of gas continuously recycled through the sample and a sorbent trap by a pump in a closed-circuit arrangement.Typical apparatus for closed-loop stripping analysis.

name: cryogenic trap
definition: Device used to concentrate volatile analytes from the gas phase by condensation on a cold surface.

name: denuder
definition: Apparatus for the extraction of volatile analytes from a flowing gas stream by diffusion to the wall of a collection vessel, where they are retained by chemisorption or strong physisorption by the wall coating.

name: dynamic headspace analysis
definition: Continuous removal of headspace above a sample by a flow of inert gas over or through the sample until all or a significant portion of the analytes have been removed from the sample. Sample vapours are typically transferred to a sorbent trap or cryogenic trap for collection.Typical apparatus for analysis by dynamic headspace (purge and trap). The gas flow (sparging gas) enters at the bottom of the sample container transporting volatile compounds through the headspace and purge head to the desorption tube for collection.

name: extractive distillation
definition: Separation of close-boiling liquids by fractional distillation in the presence of a low-volatility solvent or salt that selectively interacts with one or more components of the mixture, increasing the difference in vapour pressure of the sample components.

name: flash desorption
definition: Thermal desorption where the temperature of a packed tube or cryogenic trap is rapidly increased to transfer condensed or sorbed compounds to the gas phase.

name: full-evaporation headspace analysis
definition: Small volume of sample in a headspace vessel maintained at a temperature sufficient to cause complete evaporation of analytes.

name: headspace
definition: Volume of gas phase above a sample in a closed container.

name: multiple headspace extraction
definition: Dynamic gas extraction carried out stepwise, with sequential analysis of a number of headspace samples taken from the same vial.

name: simultaneous steam distillation-solvent extraction
definition: Extraction in which a sample dispersed in water and a water immiscible organic solvent (extraction phase) in separate flasks are heated simultaneously and their vapours co-condensed and separated into two streams in which water is returned to the sample flask and the extraction phase to the organic solvent flask.Apparatus for simultaneous steam distillation-solvent extraction with a lighter-than-water extraction phase. A = aqueous sample solution or slurry; B = immiscible organic solvent and receiving flask for extracted compounds; C = bowl for phase separation; D, E, F, and G are solvent or vapour transfer arms; and H = entry port for additional solvent or alternative sample introduction position for continuous liquid–liquid extraction. Switching the position of flasks A and B allows extraction with a heavier-than-water extraction solvent.

name: sorbent trap
definition: Tube filled with porous sorbent typically used to extract analytes from the gas phase.

name: static headspace analysis
definition: Method of analysis, in which a small aliquot of the gas phase in contact with the sample in a closed container is withdrawn for analysis.

name: thermal extraction
definition: Release of volatile compounds from a sample by heat.

name: thin-layer headspace analysis
definition: Dynamic headspace analysis of a flowing sample solution in the form of a thin film on the surface of a heated tube.

name: biphasic system
definition: Equilibrium system containing two or more solvents forming two phases with a single interface.

name: chelation solvent extraction
definition: Extraction method wherein charged analytes are extracted from an aqueous phase into an organic phase, assisted by a chelating agent.

name: cloud point extraction
definition: Coacervative extraction at a temperature above the cloud point temperature.

name: coacervative extraction
definition: Extraction by a surfactant-rich, water-immiscible phase formed by adding a dehydrating agent to a colloidal solution of the sample and a surfactant above its critical micelle concentration.

name: continuous liquid-liquid extraction
definition: Extraction in which a water-immiscible extraction solvent is continuously percolated through an aqueous solution and returned to the extraction solvent reservoir.Apparatus for continuous liquid–liquid extraction with a lighter-than-water extraction solvent (left) and a heavier-than-water extraction solvent (right). In each case the extraction solvent is contained in the round bottom flask and the aqueous sample in the vertical glass column.

name: Craig countercurrent distribution apparatus
definition: Apparatus for extraction based on a multistage countercurrent distribution.

name: crosscurrent extraction
definition: Extraction comprising a cascading series of states where the raffinate is brought into a subsequent stage and contacted with fresh solvent.

name: differential contactor
definition: Type of continuous multistage extraction equipment in which there is only one interface at which phase separation by settling occurs.

name: dispersing solvent
definition: Solvent used to disperse the extraction solvent as fine droplets throughout the sample solution in dispersive liquid–liquid microextraction.

name: dispersive liquid-liquid microextraction
definition: Extraction of analyte(s) from an aqueous solution by fine droplets of extraction phase dispersed throughout the solution.

name: liquid-ion exchange
definition: Liquid-liquid distribution process that involves the transfer of ionic species from the extractant to the aqueous phase in exchange for ions from the aqueous phase.

name: liquid-phase microextraction
definition: Microextraction technique using a liquid as the extraction phase.

name: multistage countercurrent distribution
definition: Multistage countercurrent separation based on a discontinuous, differential migration process employing stepwise extraction.

name: single-drop microextraction
definition: Extraction of analytes from the gas phase or solution by a single drop of extraction solvent.Typical experimental arrangement for single-drop microextraction.

name: solidified floating organic drop
definition: Droplet of organic solvent recovered from the surface of the sample solution by solidification induced by cooling.

name: solidified floating organic drop microextraction
definition: Microextraction employing a solidified floating organic drop.

name: stage
definition: Physically distinct part of an extraction process in which transfer of analyte(s) occurs, followed by phase separation.

name: stagewise contactor
definition: Type of continuous multi-stage liquid-liquid distribution equipment in which each stage has a physically distinct cycle of interphase contact and separation.

name: two-phase aqueous partition
definition: Distribution in a biphasic system formed by two aqueous solutions containing structurally incompatible components (two polymers or a polymer and a salt) above a critical concentration.

name: matrix-solid phase dispersion
definition: Extraction in which samples are blended with an abrasive solid sorbent, forming a free flowing powder from which target analytes are recovered by solvent elution.Typical work flow scheme for solid-phase matrix dispersion. (i) Sample is blended with an abrasive sorbent, (ii) free flowing powder containing sample is packed in a short column, and (iii) target analytes are recovered by elution.

name: microwave-assisted extraction
definition: Leaching using microwave energy to heat the solvent in contact with the sample or the sample directly.

name: pressurized hot-water extraction
definition: Extraction by water below its critical point (\(\pu{374.15^{\circ}C}\) and \(\pu{22.064 MPa}\)).

name: pressurized-liquid extraction
definition: Leaching performed at elevated temperature and pressure.Schematic diagram of a typical apparatus for pressurized-liquid extraction. Gas flow is used to displace the extraction solvent from the sample chamber.

name: Soxhlet extraction
definition: Leaching with fresh solvent cycled multiple times through a fine solid sample contained in a porous thimble.Typical apparatus for classical Soxhlet extraction.

name: supercritical fluid extraction
definition: Use of a supercritical fluid to extract analytes from a solid or supported liquid sample.

name: QuEChERS (quick, easy, cheap, effective, rugged and safe) extraction
definition: Streamlined multiresidue method for extraction and clean-up of analytes in complex matrices.

name: ultrasound-assisted extraction
definition: Extraction in which ultrasound energy is used to increase the extraction rate by enhancing the contact area between the sample and solvent and by promoting efficient agitation.

name: acid digestion
definition: Process in which the sample (analyte and matrix) is dissolved by an acid.

name: closed-vessel acid digestion
definition: Type of acid digestion performed in a closed vessel at elevated pressure.

name: digestion
definition: Sample dissolution with simultaneous matrix simplification.

name: microwave acid digestion
definition: Type of bomb acid digestion with microwave radiation used for sample heating.

name: open-vessel acid digestion
definition: Type of acid digestion performed at ambient pressure wherein the digestion temperature is limited by the boiling point of the acid.

name: UV photochemical digestion
definition: Formation of free metal ions in aqueous solution by oxidation under the influence of UV light and possibly an oxidizing agent (e.g. hydrogen peroxide or peroxodisulfate) in order to break down dissolved organic matter and metal complexes.

name: cartridge
definition: Short disposable column containing a bed of porous particles immobilized between two porous frits.

name: conditioning solvent
definition: Small volume of solvent used to prepare the sorbent for efficient sample processing.

name: elution solvent
definition: Small volume of strong solvent used to displace target analytes from the sorbent bed.

name: foamed polyurethane sorbent
definition: Sorbent consisting of spherical, micron-sized, agglomerated particles bound together in a rigid and highly porous structure used for the extraction of semi-volatile organic compounds from air in high-volume samplers.

name: immunosorbents
definition: Porous material with surface bound monoclonal or polyclonal antibodies capable of selective extraction of target analytes by formation of reversible antibody-antigen (compound) binding complexes.

name: inorganic oxide adsorbent
definition: Adsorbent with site-specific polar and ion exchange functional groups that extract analytes from a gas or liquid phase by their complementary interactions with the surface.

name: ion-exchange sorbent
definition: Porous sorbent material  containing fixed ionic sites with a complementary charge to that of the target analyte(s).

name: low-specificity sorbents
definition: Sorbent with a non-selective surface used almost exclusively to extract analytes from an aqueous solution. The sorbent has a largely passive role in the extraction, with the driving force being the expulsion of the organic contaminants from waterto minimize disruption of the water structure.

name: magnetic nanoparticle sorbent
definition: Sorbent consisting of nanometre-sized, spherical particles with a magnetic or magnetisable core surrounded by a sorbent shell.

name: mixed-mode sorbent
definition: Porous sorbent material with surface co-bonded ion exchange and alkyl functional groups.

name: molecularly imprinted polymer sorbent
definition: Porous polymer sorbent with synthetic recognition sites with a high specificity for the sorption of a targeted compound or group of structurally-related compounds.

name: multiwell extraction plate
definition: Regular array of wells in a single moulded body with a short sorbent bed or disc embedded at the base of each well.Multiwell extraction plate.

name: needle trap
definition: Gas-tight syringe with a sorbent-filled needle.

name: particle-embedded glass fibre disc
definition: Suspension of micron-sized sorbent particles woven into a glass fibre matrix.

name: particle-loaded membrane disc
definition: Suspension of micron-sized sorbent particles distributed throughout a web of poly(tetrafluroethylene) microfibrils formed into a thin disc of various diameters.

name: restricted-access sorbent
definition: Porous material with a biocompatible outer surface and a retentive interior surface.

name: rinse solvent
definition: Weak solvent used to displace matrix components from a sorbent without displacing the target analyte(s).

name: solid-phase extraction
definition: Extraction of analytes from a gas, liquid, or fluid by transfer to a solid sorbent.

name: solvent desorption
definition: Use of a solvent, typically combined with agitation, to remove target analytes from a sorbent.

name: sorbent-containing pipette tip
definition: Disposable pipette tip with a small packed bed, disc, or monolithic plug of sorbent at its narrow end.Sorbent containing pipette tips in an array for use with a multiwall sample plate.

name: sorptive-tape extraction
definition: Extraction from the surface of a solid by sorbent or polymer film in the form of a tape in direct contact with, or in the headspace above, the sample.

name: stir bar sorptive extraction
definition: Extraction of compounds from solution by a sorbent coated magnetic stir bar by rapid stirring (direct immersion) or by exposure to the headspace above a sample (headspace extraction).

name: surface-bound macrocyclic sorbent
definition: Porous sorbent with surface-bound macrocyclic ligands designed for the extraction of metal ions and some anions from aqueous solution.

name: surface-bound phenylboronic acid sorbent
definition: Porous sorbent with surface-bound phenylboronic acid groups for the selective extraction of bifunctional compounds by reversible formation of 5- or 6-membered covalent cyclic boronic acid complexes.

name: biocompatible solid-phase microextraction
definition: Extraction by a matrix-compatible immersion solid-phase microextraction device where the extraction phase and support are chosen to eliminate matrix interferences.

name: blade format
definition: Solid-phase microextraction device where the extraction phase (sorbent) is dispersed in the form of a thin coating on the surface of a blade.

name: coated-vessel format
definition: Sample vessel with sorbent-coated walls.

name: cold fibre solid-phase microextraction
definition: Solid-phase microextraction in the fibre format with a sorbent temperature maintained below that of the sample matrix during extraction.

name: fibre format
definition: Extraction phase in the form of a thin layer supported on a fibre made of inert material, such as fused silica, stainless steel, or nickel-titanium alloy.

name: headspace solid-phase microextraction
definition: Solid-phase microextraction where the extraction phase is placed in the headspace above the sample.

name: immersion solid-phase microextraction
definition: Solid-phase microextraction where the extraction phase is immersed directly into the sample.

name: in-needle capillary adsorption trap
definition: In-tube format device with a sorbent-coated capillary placed inside a needle.

name: in-tube solid-phase microextraction
definition: Extraction utilizing a coated open tubular or packed capillary tube as the extraction phase in a flow system.

name: matrix-compatible solid-phase microextraction
definition: Immersion solid-phase microextraction where the extraction phase is designed to minimize sorption of particles or macromolecules present in the sample matrix.

name: membrane-protected solid-phase microextraction
definition: Immersion solid-phase microextraction in which the extraction phase is surrounded by a permeable membrane that allows access of analytes to the extraction phase while shielding the extraction phase from matrix components with a potential to interfere in the extraction or subsequent analysis.

name: particle sorbent
definition: Extraction phase in the form of sorbent particles.

name: rotating disk sorptive extraction
definition: Sorbent-coated disc consisting of a polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) base with an integrated magnet and a sorbent film attached to one side.

name: solid-phase dynamic extraction
definition: Solid-phase microextraction in which the extraction phase is coated on the internal surface of a needle.

name: solid-phase microextraction
definition: Microextraction where the extraction phase is a solid.

name: thin film format
definition: Solid-phase microextraction where the sorbent is in the form of a thin film on a support or self supported membrane.

name: electromembrane extraction
definition: Hollow-fibre liquid-phase microextraction in which the extraction is driven by an electrical potential sustained between the sample solution and the acceptor phase, separated by a supported liquid membrane.Typical experimental arrangement for electromembrane extraction of cations (anions extracted by reversing the polarity). SLM, supported liquid membrane in the form of a porous hollow fiber with solvent-filled pores.

name: hollow fibre
definition: Narrow cylindrical tube prepared from a porous polymer.

name: hollow-fibre liquid-phase microextraction
definition: Liquid-phase microextraction of analytes from a liquid (or gaseous) sample by a supported liquid membrane in the form of a porous hollow fibre with solvent-filled pores. The analytes are transferred to an acceptor phase contained in the cavity of the hollow fibre.Typical experimental arrangement for hollow-fiber supported liquid membrane (SLM) for liquid-phase microextraction.

name: membrane extraction
definition: Extraction of analytes from a sample by permeation through a membrane.

name: membrane extraction with sorbent interface
definition: Membrane extraction with a sorbent trap for concentration of the permeate.

name: microdialysis
definition: Dialysis by a short length of hollow-fibre membrane used for sampling.

name: non-porous membrane
definition: Membrane in which permeation occurs by processes other than flow through pores.

name: parallel artificial liquid membrane extraction
definition: Extraction of analytes from aqueous samples in a multiwell plate with a porous membrane at the base of each well by migration through the solvent-filled membrane pores into an acceptor phase located in each well.

name: perfusate
definition: Stream of extraction phase entering a dialysis module.

name: permeation
definition: Process by which mass transfer occurs through a membrane.

name: porous membrane
definition: Membrane in which permeation occurs through its porous structure.

name: retentate stream
definition: Sample left over in membrane separations after initial contact with the membrane.

name: semipermeable membrane device
definition: Membrane extraction in which the membrane fully encloses an acceptor phase.

name: stream
definition: The sample in membrane separations prior to contact with the membrane.

name: stripping phase
definition: Extraction phase in a membrane separation.

name: supported liquid membrane
definition: Porous membrane with solvent-filled pores.

name: at-line extraction
definition: Flow system with extraction device employing a local detector.

name: automated extraction
definition: Extraction in a mechanical device regulated by feed-back of information without human intervention.

name: automatic extraction
definition: Extraction according to manually preselected conditions without further human intervention.

name: bead injection
definition: Fully renewable (disposable) packed sorbent bed for solid-phase extraction in a flow manifold or mesofluidic platform using programmable flow extraction.Bead-injection protocols for automated solid phase microextraction with sorbent renewal for each assay [Reproduced from  https://www.flowinjectiontutorial.com].a) Injection of a metered amount of particles or beads with reactive surfaces in the flow system followed by mechanical trapping or capture with the aid of external energy sources; b) Injection of a metered volume of sample; c) Interaction of analyte(s) with sorptive surfaces; d) Preconcentration of analyte(s) followed by detection of native species or derivatization products; e) Automatic removal of sorptive surfaces.

name: bioaccessibility
definition: Fraction of analytes desorbed from a sample potentially available to organisms.

name: dynamic bioaccessibility
definition: Leaching of analytes from a solid or semi-solid sample in a flow-through device to evaluate their bioaccessibility.

name: flow-through extraction
definition: Extraction by flow of sample through or over the extraction phase, or vice versa, to enhance the extraction rate.

name: flow-through solid-phase spectrometry
definition: Continuous optical interrogation of a packed-sorbent bed in a flow system at any stage of the extraction process prior to analyte elution and sorbent regeneration.

name: in-line extraction
definition: Coupling of a flow system with extraction device to a detector without flow interruption.

name: in-syringe microextraction
definition: Batch-type extraction in which the barrel of a syringe pump is used as the device for liquid-phase microextraction or dispersive solid-phase microextraction.

name: lab-at-valve liquid-phase microextraction
definition: Automatic batch-type liquid-phase microextraction by sequential injection analysis using an external extraction container (e.g. pipette tip) connected to a multiposition rotary valve.

name: lab-on-a-chip extraction
definition: Microfluidic platform containing microconduits to facilitate extraction processes with pressure-driven or electroosmotic flow.

name: lab-on-valve extraction
definition: Mesofluidic platform containing microconduits for extraction processes mounted on a multi-position rotary valve.

name: mechanized extraction
definition: Extraction using a device with at least one movable part that replaces or supplements human effort in any (or all) steps of the process.

name: mesofluidic extraction device
definition: Extraction device with channel widths from \(\pu{10 \upmu m}\) to \(\pu{2 mm}\) integrated into a flow platform.

name: microflow injection analysis extraction device
definition: Miniaturized flow injection analysis device for extraction with conduits of a diameter greater than \(\pu{0.1 mm}\).

name: microfluidic extraction device
definition: Extraction device with channel widths from \(\pu{100 nm}\) to \(\pu{10 \upmu m}\) integrated into a flow platform.

name: multicommutation flow extraction
definition: Programmable flow extraction device with microsolenoid valves for processing microliter sample volumes.

name: on-line extraction
definition: Coupling of a flow system with an extraction device to a detector via a discontinuous interface.

name: programmable flow extraction
definition: Multi-bidirectional flow (including stopped flow) of sample and/or extractant through an extraction device controlled by a pump.

name: segmented flow analysis
definition: Continuous-flow system attaining steady-state extraction/reaction conditions facilitated by injection of air bubbles. This might be extended to immiscible liquids injected as droplets in the flow system. Related term: segmented flow extraction.

name: segmented flow extraction
definition: Extraction by insertion of the sample solution as equal-size droplets (segments) in a flowing stream of immiscible extraction phase.Typical segmented flow extraction manifold. C, carrier or liquid phase for sample; R, reagent (optional); P, propulsion unit; S, sample; IV, injection valve; MC, mixing coil; DB, displacement bottle (functions as a constant volume pump); ORG, organic solvent; SG, segmenter; EC, extraction coil; PS, phase separator; D, detector (optional); RC, restriction coil; and W, waste.

name: sequential injection analysis extraction device
definition: Automatic programmable flow extraction through a multi-position rotary valve housing a mesofluidic extraction device.

name: A/D ratio
definition: Ratio of the adult toxic dose to the developmentally toxic dose.

name: abdominal cavity
definition: Body cavity between the diaphragm and pelvis that contains the abdominal organs.

name: ablepharia
definition: Congenital absence of the eyelids.

name: abortion
definition: Premature termination of pregnancy with the death of the embryo or fetus.

name: induced abortion
definition: Intentional termination of a pregnancy with death of the embryo or fetus.

name: spontaneous abortion
definition: Non-intentional termination of pregnancy before the embryo or fetus has developed to the stage of independent viability, or in humans before the 20th week of gestation.

name: accessory rib
definition: Rib arising from a cervical vertebra (cervical rib), or supernumerary rib arising from a thoracic or lumbar vertebra.

name: accessory sex gland
definition: Any gland, other than a gonad, associated with the genital tract, such as the bulbourethral gland and prostate.

name: accessory sex organ
definition: Organ or structure other than the gonads that matures at puberty and assists indirectly in sexual reproduction by nurturing and transporting gametes.

name: β-N-acetylhexosaminidase
definition: Hydrolytic enzyme (EC 3.2.1.52) that acts on ganglioside \(\rm{G}_{\rm{M2}}\), producing N-acetyl-D-galactosamine and ganglioside \(\rm{G}_{\rm{M3}}\).

name: achondroplasia
definition: Inherited disorder where ossification of cartilage is retarded, especially affecting growth of long bones, resulting in very short limbs and a comparatively large head. Type of dwarfism.

name: acinus
definition: Small sac-like cavity in a gland, surrounded by secretory cells. Terminal region of the airways of the lung where gas exchange occurs.

name: acoustic meatus
definition: Either of two passages in the ear, one leading to the tympanic membrane (external acoustic meatus), and one for passage of nerves and blood vessels (internal acoustic meatus).

name: acrania
definition: Rare congenital disorder that occurs in the human fetus, in which the flat bones in the cranium are either completely or partially absent.

name: acrocephaly
definition: Type of cephalic disorder where the top of the skull is pointed or conical due to premature closure of the coronal suture plus any other suture.

name: acromegaly
definition: Abnormal enlargement of the hands, feet, and face in adults, caused by overproduction of growth hormone by the pituitary gland.

name: acrosome
definition: Organelle that develops over the anterior half of the head in the spermatozoon.

name: acrosome reaction
definition: Process that occurs in the acrosome of the sperm as it contacts the egg, leading to structural changes that facilitate fusion.

name: activin
definition: Growth factor of the transforming growth factor \(\upbeta\) (TGF-\(\upbeta\)) superfamily, originally identified as a gonadal factor that stimulated secretion of follicle-stimulating hormone, also involved in many aspects of development including mesodermal induction (see mesenchyme), hematopoiesis, and neuronal differentiation.

name: acyclicity
definition: Irregular or absent estrous cycles.

name: adactyly
definition: Congenital absence of fingers or toes.

name: adenocarcinoma
definition: Malignant tumor formed from glandular epithelial tissue or formed in a glandular pattern.

name: adermia
definition: Congenital absence of skin.

name: adhesion factor
definition: Substance contributing to selective cell-cell and cell-matrix binding.

name: aditus
definition: Entrance or opening to some interior space or cavity.

name: adolescence
definition: Stage of human development beginning with puberty and ending with adulthood.

name: adrenal 4 binding protein
definition: Transcription factor that regulates the expression of the enzymes of steroid synthesis and is expressed primarily in steroidogenic cells.

name: adrenal gland
definition: Either of two small endocrine glands, one located above each kidney, consisting of a cortex, which secretes several steroid hormones, and a medulla, which secretes adrenaline and noradrenaline.

name: adrenaline
definition: Catecholamine hormone secreted by the adrenal glands that increases heart rate, breathing rate, blood pressure, and carbohydrate metabolism.

name: adrenocortocotropic hormone
definition: Hormone secreted by the pituitary gland and stimulating the adrenal cortex (see adrenal gland).

name: adult
definition: Person or animal that is fully grown, developed and sexually mature.

name: adulthood
definition: State of being adult.

name: agenesis
definition: Absence or partial development of an organ or body part observed at birth.

name: age-specific birth rate
definition: Mean number of offspring born to a female in a specific age class in a given year, expressed per \(\pu{1000}\) females in that age class.

name: aggregation chimera
definition: Organism made by combining cells from two embryos of different genotypes.

name: agnathia
definition: Congenital absence or partial absence of the lower jaw.

name: alar plate
definition: Part of the dorsal side of neural tube in the embryo, involved in general somatic and visceral sensory communication.

name: albinism
definition: Congenital disorder characterized by the complete or partial absence of pigment in the skin, hair and eyes, due to an absence of or defect in tyrosinase, a copper-containing enzyme involved in the production of melanin.

name: alcohol-related neurodevelopmental disabilities
definition: Spectrum of functional neurologic (behavioral) defects resulting from exposure in utero to alcohol.

name: allantois
definition: Extra-embryonic membrane formed early in development as an outpouching of the yolk sac into the area of the future umbilical cord.

name: alopecia
definition: Hairlessness; absence or thinning of hair from areas of skin where it is usually present.

name: alpha-fetoprotein
definition: Protein coded by the AFP gene and produced by fetal tissues, an abnormally high amount of which in the amniotic fluid or maternal serum may indicate a neural tube defect, or some other loss of structural integrity in the fetus.

name: alveolus
definition: Any of the many terminal air sacs of the airways in the lungs necessary for rapid gaseous exchange with the blood.

name: amastia
definition: Congenital absence of one or both mammary glands.

name: ambisexual
definition: Pertaining to or characterized by hermaphroditism. Denoting sexual characteristics common to both sexes, e.g., pubic hair.

name: amelia
definition: Lacking one or more limbs or having a shrunken or deformed limb as a birth defect.

name: ameloblast
definition: Epithelial cell that deposits enamel during tooth development.

name: amelogenesis imperfecta
definition: Hereditary yellow, brown, or grey tooth enamel. Developmental disorder of the teeth in which they are covered with thin, abnormal enamel resulting from defective structure or processing of enamel proteins.

name: amenorrhea
definition: Absence or abnormal stoppage of menstruation.

name: amniocentesis
definition: Transabdominal procedure in which amniotic fluid is sampled by means of a needle inserted into the amniotic sac.

name: amniochorionic membrane
definition: Composite membrane, formed by fusion of the amnion, interiorly, with the outer chorion that surrounds the developing fetus.

name: amnion
definition: Membrane that lines the amniotic cavity (amniotic sac) and encloses the embryo of a mammal, bird, or reptile.

name: amniote
definition: Any vertebrate animal, such as a reptile, bird, or mammal, that possesses an amnion, chorion, and allantois during embryonic development.

name: amniotic cavity
definition: Fluid-filled space that surrounds the developing embryo of a mammal, bird, or reptile, bounded by the amniotic sac.

name: amniotic sac
definition: Membranous structure in amniotes, within which the embryo and fetus develop.

name: amphibian metamorphosis assay
definition: Procedure in which a frog (often _027793_) is exposed to a substance starting at the tadpole stage, and the growth and development of the animals is studied.

name: ampulla
definition: Flask-like dilatation of a canal or duct.

name: anal canal
definition: Terminal part of the large intestine between the rectum and anus.

name: anal membrane
definition: In the embryo, dorsal part of the cloacal membrane after its division of the urorectal septum.

name: anamniote
definition: Any vertebrate animal, such as a fish or amphibian, that lacks an amnion, chorion, and allantois during embryonic development.

name: anaphase
definition: Stage of mitosis and meiosis in which the chromosomes move from the equatorial plate toward opposite ends of the nuclear spindle.

name: anaphase lag
definition: Slowing or stopping of normal migration of chromosomes during anaphase, resulting in chromosomes being excluded from one of the daughter cells causing aneuploidy.

name: anasarca
definition: Generalized edema in the subcutaneous connective tissue.

name: anastomosis
definition: Connection creating continuity between two tubular body structures, e.g. blood vessels or loops of bowel.

name: fetal anatomic position
definition: Usual positioning of the developing fetus with the back curved forward, head bent forward, and limbs drawn in towards the body.

name: anchoring villus
definition: Chorionic villus that is attached to the region of the endometrium (see also decidua) that interacts with the trophoblast during development of the placenta.

name: androblastoma
definition: Rare benign tumor of the testis histologically resembling the fetal testis: the epithelium contains Sertoli cells that may produce estrogen and cause feminization.

name: androgen
definition: Substance, such as a naturally occurring steroid hormone, that binds to androgen receptors to activate the male accessory sex organs and induce male secondary sexual characteristics.

name: androgenic
definition: Producing masculine characteristics.

name: androgen receptor
definition: Nuclear receptor that is activated by binding of testosterone or dihydrotestosterone.

name: androstenedione
definition: Steroid hormone produced in the adrenal glands and gonads as a common precursor of male (testosterone) and female (estrogen) sex hormones.

name: anemia
definition: Decrease in the number of erythrocytes or total hemoglobin in the blood that results in a decrease in the oxygen-carrying capacity of the blood, sometimes inducing pallor and fatigue.

name: anencephalus
definition: Fetus lacking all or most of the neural tissues of brain.

name: anencephaly
definition: Congenital absence of a major portion of the brain and its meninges, skull, and scalp that results from abnormal embryonic development.

name: anestrus
definition: Interval of sexual inactivity between two periods of estrus.

name: aneugen
definition: Agent inducing aneuploidy.

name: aneuploid
definition: Referring to a cell or organism with missing or extra chromosomes or parts of chromosomes, and thus an abnormal number of chromosomes that is not an exact multiple of the haploid number.

name: aneuploidy
definition: State of being aneuploid.

name: aneurysm
definition: Abnormal bulging of the wall of an artery or a chamber of the heart.

name: angioblast
definition: Cell taking part in blood vessel formation. Primordial mesenchymal tissue from which embryonic blood cells and vascular endothelium are differentiated.

name: angiogenesis
definition: Development of new blood vessels in the embryo or from pre-existing vessels; formation of capillary networks.

name: angiotensin converting enzyme
definition: Enzyme (EC 3.4.15.1) that converts angiotensin I to angiotensin II, causing blood vessels to constrict thus increasing blood pressure.

name: ankyloglossia
definition: Congenital oral anomaly, in which the lingual frenulum (the membrane connecting the underside of the tongue to the floor of the mouth) is unusually short and thick.

name: anodontia
definition: Congenital absence of all primary or permanent teeth.

name: anogenital distance
definition: Distance along the perineum between the anus and the base of the vagina or penis, or in the fetus between the anus and the base of the genital tubercle.

name: developmental anomaly
definition: Deviation in structure or function arising in the embryo or fetus, due to genetic or other causes.

name: anonychia
definition: Absence of nails.

name: anophthalmia
definition: Congenital absence of one or both eyeballs.

name: anorchism
definition: Congenital absence of one or both testes.

name: anorectal
definition: Relating to the anus and rectum.

name: anotia
definition: Congenital absence of the (outer ear) pinna, often with narrowing or absence of the ear canal.

name: anovulation
definition: Failure of the ovaries to produce, to facilitate maturation of, or to release ova.

name: anoxia
definition: Total absence of dioxygen.

name: antemortem
definition: Before death.

name: antepartum
definition: Before birth.

name: antimitotic
definition: Referring to inhibition of cell division by mitosis.

name: anti-Müllerian hormone
definition: Protein that inhibits the development of the Müllerian ducts (paramesonephric ducts) in the male embryo.

name: antrum
definition: Cavity or chamber, often in bone, with specific meanings in some hollow organs (e.g., the pyloric end or gastric antrum of the stomach).

name: anus
definition: External opening of the rectum to the body surface, controlled by the anal sphincter.

name: aorta
definition: Great artery arising from the left ventricle, being the main trunk from which the systemic arterial system proceeds

name: aorta-gonad-mesonephros region
definition: Region of the vertebrate embryonic mesoderm that gives rise to the genitourinary tract and its blood supply.

name: aortic arch
definition: Curved portion of the aorta between its ascending portion exiting the heart and its descending portion that proceeds to the arteries of the thoracic and abdominal cavities and the lower body.

name: aortopulmonary septum
definition: Spiral septum that, during development, separates the truncus arteriosus into a ventral pulmonary trunk and the ascending aorta dorsally.

name: aphakia
definition: Absence of the lens of the eye, occurring as a congenital defect or as a result of trauma or surgery.

name: appendicular skeleton
definition: Bones and cartilage that support the appendages, including the bones of the shoulders, upper limbs, pelvis, and lower limbs.

name: appendix
definition: Tube-shaped sac ('vermiform appendix') attached to and opening into the upper end of the large intestine (cecum) in humans and some other mammals. Appendage, blind sac, or diverticulum.

name: arachnodactyly
definition: Extreme length and slenderness of the fingers or toes.

name: arachnoid membrane
definition: Web like membrane that lies between the outer (and much thicker) dura mater and the deeper pia mater, and which covers the brain.

name: arachnoid villus
definition: Small projection of the arachnoid membrane into some of the venous sinuses of the dura mater.

name: areola
definition: A circular area of different color surrounding a central point, such as that surrounding the nipple of the breast, the part of the iris surrounding the pupil of the eye, or an area surrounding a vesicle. Any minute space or interstice in a tissue.

name: Arnold–Chiari malformation
definition: Congenital herniation of the brainstem and lower cerebellum through the foramen magnum into the cervical vertebral canal.

name: aromatase
definition: Enzyme (EC 1.14.14.1) of the cytochrome P450 superfamily that converts testosterone to 17\(\upbeta\)-estradiol and androstenedione to estrone.

name: arteriogenesis
definition: Increase in the diameter of arterial vessels that leads to the formation of large conductance arteries from pre-existing arterioles.

name: arteriovenous shunt
definition: Connection between the arterial and venous sides of the circulation that bypasses the capillary beds.

name: artificial insemination
definition: Introduction of semen into the cervix, uterus or Fallopian tubes by means other than the natural one.

name: aryl hydrocarbon receptor
definition: Ligand-activated transcription factor involved in the regulation of biological responses to planar aromatic hydrocarbons.

name: aryl hydrocarbon receptor nucleotide translocator protein
definition: Protein coded for by a gene on chromosome 1q21 that forms a complex with ligand-bound aryl hydrocarbon receptor, resulting in translocation of the ligand-binding subunit to the nucleus.

name: atelectasis
definition: Total or partial collapse of the lung. Congenital condition characterized by the incomplete expansion of the lungs at birth.

name: athelia
definition: Congenital absence of one or both nipples.

name: athymia
definition: Congenital absence of functioning thymus tissue.

name: atresia
definition: Congenital absence or abnormal narrowing of a normal opening or normally patent lumen.

name: atrial-septal defect
definition: Defect in the septum between the atria of the heart, due to failure of normal closure of the foramen ovale in the perinatal period.

name: atrichia congenita
definition: Congenital baldness caused by an abnormality of the hairless gene.

name: atrioventricular
definition: Relating to the atrial and ventricular chambers of the heart.

name: atrium
definition: Each of the two upper chambers of the heart from which blood is passed to the ventricles.

name: atrophy
definition: Wasting away of the body or of an organ or tissue, involving a decrease in size and (or) numbers of cells.

name: auditory tube
definition: Narrow channel connecting the middle ear and the nasopharynx.

name: auricle
definition: An appendage to the atrium of the heart.

name: autopsy
definition: Postmortem examination of the human organs and body tissue to determine cause of death or pathological condition.

name: autosite
definition: Independent twin of a pair of conjoined twins; the other twin is a parasitic twin.

name: autosomal dominant mutation
definition: Change in an autosomal gene capable of expression when carried by only one of a pair of homologous chromosomes.

name: autosomal recessive mutation
definition: Change in an autosomal gene that produces an effect in the organism only when it is homozygous.

name: autosome
definition: Any chromosome that is not a sex chromosome.

name: avascularity
definition: Absence of a blood supply.

name: axial skeleton
definition: Bones of the body axis, including the skull, spinal column, ribs and sternum.

name: azoospermia
definition: Absence of viable spermatozoa in the semen.

name: basal ganglia
definition: Complex structure at the base of the brain consisting of several groups of neurons, the caudate nucleus, the putamen, the globus pallidus, and the substantia nigra.

name: basement membrane
definition: Thin layer of connective tissue underlying an attached epithelial cell layer.

name: bell stage
definition: Period in which the developing tooth takes on a bell shape in cross section, immediately preceding the 'advanced bell stage', in which the hard tissues (dentin and enamel) form the crown of the tooth.

name: bicornate uterus
definition: Uterus that is divided into two lateral horns as a result of imperfect fusion of the paired embryonic tubes from which the uterus is formed.

name: bilaminar embryo
definition: Early blastula having only two of the three primary germ layers that it will ultimately have; the two layers present are the cells of the epiblast that will give rise to the ectoderm and those of the hypoblast that will become the endoderm during gastrulation - both attached to a basement membrane before the mesoderm has formed.

name: birth
definition: Start of life as a physically separate being, e.g., the emergence of a baby from the body of its mother, or the hatching of an egg.

name: birth defect
definition: Physical or biochemical abnormality that is present at birth, and that may either be inherited or be the result of environmental influence.

name: blastema
definition: Mass of cells from which an organ or a body part develops, either in normal development or in the regeneration of a lost body part.

name: blastocoel
definition: Fluid-filled cavity in the blastula of a developing embryo.

name: blastocyst
definition: Modified blastula that is characteristic of placental mammals.

name: blastomere
definition: Any of the cells formed by cleavage of a fertilized egg.

name: blastula
definition: Hollow mass of cells formed after a zygote has undergone approximately six cell divisions.

name: blastulation
definition: Process by which the early embryo transforms from the morula into the blastula.

name: blood–testis barrier
definition: Occluding barrier, formed by the Sertoli cells of the seminiferous tubules, that separates the more mature cells of spermatogenesis from blood-borne products.

name: bone age
definition: Average age at which children reach a given stage of bone maturation, denoting the stage of skeletal development of an individual fetus or child.

name: bone morphogenetic protein
definition: Any of a family of growth factors involved in bone and cartilage formation and, more generally, in orchestrating tissue architecture through morphogenetic signals.

name: bone morphogenetic protein-4
definition: Bone morphogenetic protein member of the transforming growth factor \(\upbeta\) (TGF-\(\upbeta\)) superfamily.

name: brachydactyly
definition: Congenital abnormal shortness of fingers and toes.

name: branchial
definition: Of, relating to, or resembling the gills of a fish or the homologous embryonic structures and their derivatives in higher animals.

name: branchial arch
definition: In embryology, one of several arches, resembling the gill arches of a fish, found in the embryo of a higher vertebrate; these arches develop into structures of the ear and neck. In biology, one of several bony or cartilaginous arches located on either side of the pharynx and supporting the gills in fish and amphibians.

name: congenital branchial cyst
definition: Congenital cyst arising in the lateral aspect of the neck, from epithelial remnants of a pharyngeal groove.

name: brevicollis
definition: Shortness of the neck.

name: bronchopulmonary segment
definition: Largest subdivision of a lobe of the lung with its air supply from a major branch of the bronchus and having its own arterial blood supply.

name: buccopharyngeal membrane
definition: Membrane present in fetal life that separates the nasal cavities from the pharynx.

name: bud
definition: Small protuberance resembling the bud of a plant and having the potential for growth and differentiation.

name: olfactory bulb
definition: Region of the frontal lobe of the brain, receiving input from neurons of the nasal mucosa and involved in the sense of smell.

name: bulbourethral gland
definition: One of two small glands located on each side of, and inferior to, the prostate, draining to the urethra. Bulbourethral glands secrete a fluid component of the seminal fluid

name: bulbus cordis
definition: Outflow tract of the embryonic heart between the primitive ventricle and the aorta.

name: bundle of His
definition: Band of specialized cardiac muscle fibers connecting the atria with the ventricles of the heart.

name: bursa
definition: Padlike fluid-filled sac or sac-like cavity, especially one reducing friction at a joint.

name: Caesarian section
definition: Surgical operation for delivering a child by opening the mother’s abdominal wall and uterus.

name: canal
definition: In biology and medicine, a relatively narrow tubular passage or channel.

name: cancer
definition: Disease resulting from the development of a malignant tumor.

name: capacitation
definition: Sum of biochemical changes undergone by mammalian spermatozoa in the female genital tract that enables them to penetrate and fertilize (see fertilization) an egg.

name: caput epididymis
definition: Upper and larger extremity of the epididymis.

name: carcinogenesis
definition: Induction, by chemical, physical, or biological agents, of malignant neoplasms and thus of cancer.

name: cardiac
definition: Pertaining to the heart.

name: cardiac jelly
definition: Gelatinous substance, present between the endothelium and myocardium of the heart in early embryos, that develops into the connective tissue of the endocardium.

name: cardiogenesis
definition: Development of the heart in the embryo.

name: cardiogenic
definition: Originating in the heart; describing anything caused by normal or abnormal function of the heart. Pertaining to cardiogenesis.

name: cardiovascular
definition: Pertaining to the heart and blood vessels.

name: cartilage
definition: Specialized, fibrous connective tissue present in adults, forming the temporary skeleton in the embryo, providing a model in which the bones develop, and constituting a part of the organism’s growth mechanism.

name: castration
definition: Removal of the testicles or ovaries.

name: cataract
definition: Partial or complete opacity (clouding) of the lens of the eye.

name: cauda epididymis
definition: Tail of the epididymis that opens into the ductus deferens; part of the reservoir of spermatozoa.

name: caudal
definition: Situated more toward the cauda, or tail, than some specified reference point; toward the inferior (in humans) or posterior (in animals) end of the body.

name: cavitation
definition: Formation of a cavity, as in formation of the amnion in mammalian development.

name: cecum
definition: Pouch connected to the junction of the small and large intestines.

name: central nervous system
definition: Part of an animal’s nervous system that exerts control over the rest of the nervous system; in vertebrates, the brain and spinal cord protected within the dorsal body cavity (cranial and spinal cavities).

name: centromere
definition: Constricted region of a chromosome that joins the two chromatids to each other and attaches to spindle fibers in mitosis and meiosis.

name: acrocentric centromere
definition: Having the centromere very close to one end.

name: cerebral hemisphere
definition: Right or left half of the brain in sagittal section.

name: cerebral palsy
definition: Condition marked by lack of muscle control, resulting from brain damage before, at, or shortly after birth.

name: cervical rib
definition: Supernumerary rib arising from a cervical vertebra.

name: cervix
definition: Narrow lower end of the uterus that opens into the vagina.

name: checkpoint pathway
definition: Type of pathway used in intracellular signaling, activated in response to a cell’s own internal imbalance or to errors in its synthetic activities.

name: Chernoff–Kavlock assay
definition: Group of testing methods for assessing parturition, postnatal growth, and viability of prenatally exposed litters of test animals.

name: chimera
definition: Animal consisting of genetically different cells derived from two (or more) different zygotes. Substance, such as an antibody, created from the proteins or genes of two different species.

name: chondrification
definition: Formation of cartilage; transformation into cartilage.

name: chondroblast
definition: Cartilage-producing mesenchymal progenitor cell, capable of proliferating and maturing into a chondrocyte or osteoblast.

name: chondrocyte
definition: Any one of the cells embedded in the lacunae of the cartilage matrix.

name: chordin
definition: Secreted protein that dorsalizes early vertebrate embryonic tissues by binding to ventralizing transforming growth factor \(\upbeta\) (TGF-\(\upbeta\))-like bone morphogenetic proteins, sequestering them in latent complexes.

name: chorioallantoic placenta
definition: Placenta developed from the allantois and chorion, establishing a nutritive and excretory connection between the blood of the fetus and that of the mother.

name: chorion
definition: In human embryology, the cellular, outermost extra-embryonicmembrane, composed of trophoblast lined with mesoderm. Note: The chorion develops villi, becomes vascularized by allantoic vessels, and forms the fetal part of the placenta.  In mammalian embryology, the cellular, outer extra embryonic membrane, not necessarily developing villi. In biology, the noncellular membrane covering eggs of various animals, e.g., fish and insects.

name: chorionic gonadotropin
definition: Hormone secreted by the chorionic villi of the placenta in mammals, especially human chorionic gonadotropin.

name: chorionic sac
definition: Outermost membranous sac that encloses the embryo in higher vertebrates (reptiles, birds, and mammals), lined by chorion.

name: chorionic villus
definition: Any of the tiny extensions from the chorion that contain fetal blood vessels and combine with the uterine tissue to form the placenta.

name: chorioretinitis
definition: Inflammation of the choroid layer behind the retina of the eye.

name: choroid plexus
definition: Infoldings of blood vessels of the pia mater, projecting into the cerebral ventricles, covered with ependymal cells, and secreting cerebrospinal fluid.

name: chromaffin cell
definition: Cell of the adrenal medulla that secretes epinephrine and norepinephrine, and contains granules that are readily stained with chromate salts.

name: chromatid
definition: One of a pair of chromosomes arising by duplication during mitosis or by pairing during meiosis, and joined together at the centromere.

name: chromosomal abnormality
definition: Abnormality in the number or structure of chromosomes.

name: chromosome deletion
definition: Loss of a chromosome or part of a chromosome.

name: chromosome ring
definition: Abnormal chromosome in which both ends have been lost and the two broken ends have reunited to form a ring-shaped structure.

name: clastogen
definition: Agent causing chromosome breakage and (or) the consequent gain, loss, or rearrangement of pieces of chromosomes.

name: cleavage
definition: First few divisions of a fertilized egg.

name: meroblastic cleavage
definition: Partial cleavage of the egg, occurring in some animals, such as reptiles and birds, whose eggs have a large amount of yolk, resulting in unequal blastomeres and only part of the egg progressing to further cell division; the yolk mass remains and has nutritive value.

name: holoblastic cleavage
definition: Cleavage producing separate, equal blastomeres.

name: cleft
definition: Gap in soft tissue, bone, or both.

name: cleft
definition: Split, divided, or partly divided into two.

name: cleft lip
definition: Congenital malformation consisting of one or more clefts in the upper lip, the result of failed closure in the embryo of the maxillary and median nasal processes.

name: cleft palate
definition: Congenital fissure along the midline of the hard palate, that may extend into the soft palate.

name: cleft sternum
definition: Rare congenital malformation resulting from defective fusion in the embryo of paired mesodermal bands in the ventral midline.

name: clitoris
definition: Erectile body in the female genitalia, homologous with the penis in the male.

name: cloaca
definition: Common cavity at the end of the digestive tract in vertebrates (apart from most mammals) into which are released both excretory and genital products.

name: cloacal membrane
definition: Membrane that covers the embryonic cloaca during the development of urinary and reproductive organs in those vertebrates where the cloaca occurs.

name: clover disease
definition: Condition caused by the continued ingestion of low but toxic levels of estrogens.

name: clubfoot
definition: Deformed foot that is twisted out of shape or position, usually congenital (congenital talipes equinovarus (CTEV)).

name: coarctation
definition: Narrowing or constriction of a short section of a blood vessel, commonly of the aorta.

name: cochlea
definition: Spiral cavity of the inner ear containing the organ of Corti that transduces sound into nerve impulses.

name: coelom
definition: Body cavity, found in many animals, lined with mesodermal epithelium and containing the digestive tract and other visceral organs

name: collagenous
definition: Rich in the fibrous connective tissue protein, collagen.

name: collembolan reproduction test
definition: Procedure in which collembolans (small soil-inhabiting insects) are exposed to soil that has been treated with a test substance, and adult mortality and reproductive output are studied.

name: coloboma
definition: Any defect resulting from incomplete closure of the retinal fissure.

name: combined repeated dose toxicity study
definition: Procedure to evaluate both general systemic toxicity, with an emphasis on neurological endpoints, and notably reproductive effects and developmental progression in rodents. Groups of males and females are administered a test substance in graded doses prior to mating, during the mating period, and subsequently (up to two weeks post-mating in males and four days post-delivery in females).

name: compaction
definition: Complication of labor in twin births in which there is attempted simultaneous expulsion of both twins, so that the lower part of the mother’s pelvis is filled and further descent through the birth canal is prevented. In embryology, process during which blastomeres change their shape and align themselves tightly against each other to form the compact morula.

name: conal growth hypothesis
definition: Hypothesis that explains transposition of the great arteries of the heart by failure of the aortopulmonary septum to follow a spiral course during partitioning of the bulbus cordis and truncus arteriosus in the process of forming the aorta and pulmonary trunk.

name: conception
definition: Formation of a viable zygote by the union of a spermatozoon and an ovum.

name: conceptus
definition: Embryo and associated membranes in the uterus, especially during the early stages of pregnancy.

name: congenital
definition: Present from birth, as of a disease or physical abnormality.

name: congenital adrenal hyperplasia
definition: Group of disorders caused by hyperplasia of the adrenal cortex or by malignant tumors, resulting in excess secretion of adrenocortical androgenic hormones, and characterized by masculinization of women, feminization of men, or precocious puberty in the male.

name: congenital malformation
definition: Malformation existing at birth, or developing during the first month of life, regardless of the cause.

name: conjoined twin
definition: One of a pair of identical twins fused together with varying degrees of union and of residual duplication of organs.

name: connective tissue
definition: Extracellular matrix of fibrous proteins and glycoproteins, with associated cells such as fibroblasts, that fills the spaces between and within organs and tissues.
