definition: Autosomal recessive disorder resulting from mutations that impair the function of the enzyme phenylalanine 4-monooxygenase (EC 1.14.16.1).

name: philtrum
definition: Groove in the midline of the upper lip below the nose.

name: phocomelia
definition: Congenital abnormality in which one or more of the hands or feet is attached to an underdeveloped limb, and therefore too close to the body.

name: phytoestrogen
definition: Non-steroidal natural product from a plant that, because of a structural similarity to 17\(\upbeta\)-estradiol can exert mild estrogenic effects, or antagonize them.

name: piebaldism
definition: Patchy absence of pigmentation of the hair or skin or, depending on the species, of feathers, scales, or other body surfaces.

name: pineal gland
definition: Pea-sized conical mass of tissue behind the third ventricle of the brain, secreting the hormone-like substance melatonin in some mammals.

name: pinna
definition: Externally visible portion of the ear.See also: auricle Feather or fin.

name: pituitary
definition: Small endocrine gland sitting in a bony cavity (the sella turcica) at the base of the brain and connected to the hypothalamus.

name: placenta
definition: Organ of exchange of nutrients and waste products between mother and fetus, having parts derived from both.

name: placental barrier
definition: Multilayered membrane of fetal tissue within the placenta that separates the maternal blood from the fetal blood and allows selective passage of substances between the two.

name: placental circulation
definition: Circulation of blood through the placenta during intrauterine life, serving the needs of the fetus for oxygenation, nutrition, and elimination of waste.

name: placental insufficiency
definition: Inadequate blood flow through the placenta to maintain the needs of the fetus for oxygenation and metabolic balance.

name: placental transfer
definition: Delivery of substances from the maternal circulation to the fetus, across the placental barrier.

name: pleiotropism
definition: Having more than one effect. Relating to a gene, expression of which gives rise to multiple phenotypic traits.

name: pleura
definition: Each of a pair of serous membranes lining the thorax and enveloping the lungs in humans and other mammals.

name: pleural cavity
definition: Potential space between the pleural membranes lining the chest cavity (parietal pleura) and covering the lungs (visceral pleura).

name: pluripotent
definition: Able to differentiate into a variety of cell types.

name: polycystic
definition: Composed of many cysts.

name: polydactyly
definition: Congenital occurrence of supernumerary fingers or toes.

name: polymorphism
definition: Occurrence of a gene in more than one distinct nucleotide sequence in a population, resulting from mutation(s) and potentially producing gene products with different levels of function. Note: It is sometimes considered that the least frequent of polymorphic gene sequences should be present in at least \(\pu{1\%}\) of the population; otherwise the variant is a mutation rather than a polymorphism. Occurrence of different phenotypes of a single trait.

name: polyploidy
definition: Occurrence of more than two complete sets of chromosomes.

name: porencephaly
definition: Occurrence of a cyst in the substance of the brain that usually communicates with one of the lateral ventricles.

name: post-implantation
definition: Occurring after the early embryo embeds in the lining of the uterus.

name: postmortem
definition: After death.

name: postnatal
definition: Referring to events in the life of the mother or fetus following birth.

name: postpartum
definition: Period following the birth of an infant, often considered to be about six weeks in the human.

name: predatory mite test
definition: Procedure in which adult females of the predatory mite (_027814_ considered representative of soil fauna) are exposed to a test substance in artificial soil and the number of surviving females and of juveniles is determined.

name: pre-eclampsia
definition: Pathological condition in pregnancy with symptoms of high blood pressure, kidney dysfunction and edema.

name: pre-embryo
definition: Fertilized ovum up to \(\pu{14 days}\) of age and before implantation.

name: pregnancy
definition: State of a female between conception and the termination of gestation.

name: pre-implantation
definition: Occurring before the early embryo embeds in the lining of the uterus.

name: premature birth
definition: Delivery before the expected length of gestation for the species; in humans taken as birth before a gestational age of \(\pu{37 weeks}\).

name: prenatal
definition: Referring to events in the life of the mother or fetus preceding birth.

name: prenatal development study
definition: Procedure in which a substance is administered to pregnant animals (usually rodents or rabbits) from the time of implantation until closure of the hard palate. The animals are killed one to two days before a scheduled delivery, whereupon uterine contents and the fetuses are evaluated for abnormalities.

name: preoptic area
definition: Region of the anterior hypothalamus primarily involved in regulating body temperature.

name: prepubertal
definition: Stage of human development before the onset of puberty.

name: prepubescence
definition: Period before pubescence.

name: prepuce
definition: Skin protecting the glans penis in the male (foreskin) or the clitoris in the female (clitoral hood).

name: preputial separation
definition: Separation of the prepuce from the glans penis.

name: primary sex organ
definition: Gonads, which form gametes; ovaries in the female and testes in the male.

name: primitive axis
definition: Thickening of the embryonic tissue extending forward from the primitive streak.

name: primitive groove
definition: Shallow depression in the primitive streak that extends anteriorly to communicate with the yolk sac.

name: primitive node
definition: Group of cells at the anterior end of the primitive streak, involved in secreting chemical signals that regulate differentiation of the germ layers during gastrulation.

name: primitive pit
definition: Depression in the primitive node contiguous with the notochord.

name: primitive streak
definition: Structure forming in the blastula during early embryogenesis that establishes bilateral symmetry and determines the site of gastrulation and germ layer formation.

name: primordial follicle
definition: Early stage of the oocyte in which it is surrounded by a single layer of follicular cells.

name: primordial germ cell
definition: Germ cell in the earliest stages of development.

name: primordium
definition: Organ or tissue at its earliest recognizable stage of development.

name: proctodeum
definition: Ectodermal depression of the caudal end of the embryo, where later the anus is formed.

name: progesterone
definition: Steroidal hormone produced in the ovary by the corpus luteum.

name: progestin
definition: Synthetic variant of progesterone, often used in oral contraceptive pills or to suppress hyperplasia of the endometrium.

name: progestogen
definition: Member of a family of hormones, based on the 21-carbon pregnane skeleton, involved in maintaining gestation and regulating the ovarian cycle.

name: prolactin
definition: Hormone released from the anterior pituitary gland that stimulates milk production after childbirth.

name: prolapse
definition: Falling or slipping out of place of an organ or other body part.

name: pronephros
definition: Collection of cells in the vertebrate embryo that represent the earliest stage of development of the kidney.

name: pronucleus
definition: Haploid nucleus formed by either the head of the sperm or the nucleus of the oocyte after fertilization but before their nuclei fuse to form the diploid zygotic nucleus.

name: prophase
definition: First phase of meiosis or mitosis in which thickening and orientation of the chromosomes occurs.

name: prosencephalon
definition: Most forward part of the brain that includes most of the cerebral cortex, the thalamus and hypothalamus, and the basal ganglia.

name: prostate
definition: Male exocrine gland whose secretion contributes alkaline fluid to the ejaculate (see ejaculation).

name: protamine
definition: Small, basic (arginine-rich) protein involved in sperm maturation and DNA packaging during spermatogenesis.

name: protein kinase
definition: Any enzyme catalyzing protein phosphorylation, often for the purpose of signal transduction.

name: proximal
definition: Nearer to an anatomical point of origin or attachment, or the midline of the body.

name: pseudohermaphrodite
definition: Organism possessing either male (testes) or female (ovaries) gonads, but with ambiguous external genitalia.

name: pseudopregnancy
definition: Development of signs of pregnancy in the absence of an embryo.

name: psychomotor retardation
definition: Delayed development of both cognitive and motor function.

name: puberty
definition: Process in which an individual undergoes sexual development, including the onset of gametogenesis, changes in hormonal secretions, secondary sexual characteristics, and reproductive competence.

name: pubescent
definition: Being in the early stage of puberty.

name: pubic
definition: Relating to the region of the most ventral bone of the pelvis (the pubic bone), and thus the region around the genital area, normally showing hair growth (pubic hair) in the adult.

name: pubic symphysis
definition: Cartilaginous joint between the pubic bones forming the front of the pelvis.

name: pulmonary
definition: Pertaining to the lungs.

name: pulmonary artery
definition: Large vessel that transports blood from the heart to the lungs.

name: pulmonary valve stenosis
definition: Condition in which the flow of blood from the heart to the lungs is slowed by a deformity on or near the pulmonary valve that controls the blood flow from the right heart to the lungs.

name: pup
definition: (n) Young or newborn dog, rat or seal. (v) Give birth to a pup.

name: pyloric stenosis
definition: Narrowing of the sphincter (the pylorus) between the stomach and duodenum.

name: quickening
definition: Initial awareness of fetal movement by the pregnant mother, usually occurring early in the second trimester.

name: rachischisis
definition: Failure of the neural tube to close in utero, resulting in a birth defect that leaves a fissure in the vertebral column with part of the spinal cord exposed.

name: nuclear receptor
definition: Receptor that encounters its ligand in the cytosol and translocates to the nucleus, where it binds DNA and acts as a factor regulating gene transcription.

name: recessive
definition: In genetics, relating to or denoting heritable characteristics controlled by genes which are expressed in offspring only when inherited from both parents.

name: reciprocal mesenchymal-epithelial interaction
definition: Process in tissue or organ development in which epithelium induces changes in the mesenchyme and the mesenchyme also induces changes in the epithelium, through paracrine signaling.

name: reciprocal translocation
definition: Chromosomal translocation in which crossing over between two non-homologous chromosomes leads to each carrying genetic material from the other.

name: genetic recombination
definition: Referring to new gene sequences, and thus to new heritable information, caused by gene crossovers, occurring naturally in either meiosis or mitosis, or constructed artificially for the purpose of introducing a new trait into an organism or cell line. In immunology, random scrambling of specific gene sequences to produce the vast array of possible immunoglobulin and T cell receptor sequences required to recognize, potentially, all possible antigens.

name: rectum
definition: Terminal part of the large intestine, ending at the anus.

name: 5α-reductase
definition: Enzyme (EC 1.3.99.5) that converts testosterone to 5\(\upalpha\)-dihydrotestosterone in peripheral tissues.

name: 5α-reductase deficiency
definition: Condition caused by a mutation of the $\ce{5\upalpha\!\mbox{-}reductase}$ type II gene, with autosomal recessive inheritance.

name: renal
definition: Pertaining to the kidneys.

name: reproductive senescence
definition: Progressive decline in reproductive capacity with age, marked by menopause in females.

name: reproductive toxicant
definition: Agent that interferes with reproductive function, including sexual performance, fertility, and development of the fetus and embryo.

name: reproductive toxicity test
definition: Procedure based on specific guidelines in which adverse effects of a substance on reproduction and development are studied either in animals or by use of in vitro assays.

name: resorption
definition: Removal of mineralized tissue by natural processes, as in the breakdown of bone by osteoclasts or the disappearance of a tooth.  Disintegration and assimilation of an embryo or fetus through a natural process involving lysis and removal of all the products of conception by cells of the maternal immune system.  In multigestational pregnancies, death of one fetus followed by absorption of its tissue by another, sometimes referred to as a 'vanishing twin'.

name: restriction site
definition: Short DNA nucleotide sequence that is recognized by a sequence-specific enzyme (restriction enzyme) that cleaves the double stranded DNA.

name: rete
definition: Fibrous mesh or network.

name: rete testis
definition: Rete in the testis that carries sperm from the seminiferous tubules.

name: retina
definition: Multicell-layer membrane in the back of the eye that is sensitive to light and transduces incoming optical information into signals that are necessary for vision.

name: retinoic acid
definition: Acidic metabolite of vitamin A.

name: retinopathy
definition: Noninflammatory degenerative disease of the retina.

name: congenital retinoschisis
definition: Congenital splitting of the retina into two layers.

name: retroperitoneal
definition: Outside of and posterior to the peritoneum.

name: reverse genetics
definition: Approach to elucidating the function of a gene by studying the effects on phenotype of expressed variations in a known DNA sequence.

name: rhesus factor
definition: Antigen that occurs on the red blood cells of about 85 per cent of humans and can cause hemolytic disease of the newborn (erythroblastosis fetalis) and hemolytic transfusion reactions.

name: rhombencephalon
definition: Posterior portion of the brain that includes the cerebellum, pons, and medulla.

name: RNA interference
definition: Effect of small, often double-stranded RNA targeting a specific messenger RNA (mRNA), blocking its translation, and thereby silencing expression of the corresponding gene.

name: Robertsonian translocation
definition: Chromosomal translocation in which chromosomes with acrocentric centromeres break the centromere to fuse the long arms into a new large chromosome and the short arms into another small one that may be lost, leaving a karyotype in the human of \(\pu{45}\) chromosomes.

name: rostral
definition: Pertaining to, resembling, or having a rostrum or beak. Situated toward the beak (thus, oral and nasal region), which may mean superior (in relationships of areas of the spinal cord) or anterior or ventral (in relationships of brain areas). Closer to the head.

name: runt
definition: Smallest and weakest animal of a litter.

name: sacral agenesis
definition: Absence or significant underdevelopment of the lower part of the spine and the lower limbs.

name: sagittal
definition: Vertical (longitudinal) plane dividing the body into right and left sections.

name: salpingectomy
definition: Surgical removal of the Fallopian tubes.

name: saturation mutagenesis
definition: Mutagenesis screening in which a large number of mutations are introduced in a target area of the genome with the aim of identifying all the genes or their functions that are associated with that area.

name: scaphocephaly
definition: Elongated and narrow head with decrease of the parietal regions and conspicuous frontal and occipital protrusions; a type of craniosynostosis.

name: scoliosis
definition: Abnormal lateral and rotational curvature of the vertebral spinal column.

name: scrotum
definition: Pouch of skin containing the testicles and their accessory tissues.

name: secondary sexual characteristic
definition: Feature of the adult animal, appearing during puberty in humans and distinct between the sexes, although not part of the reproductive system.

name: seizure
definition: Sudden change in neural activity, leading to convulsions and (or) changes in consciousness of varying degrees of severity.

name: selector gene
definition: Member of a group of genes that codes factors driving differentiation and regional patterning during development.

name: sella turcica
definition: Depression on the upper surface of the sphenoid bone, accommodating the pituitary gland.

name: semen
definition: Fluid, containing spermatozoa, that is expelled from the penis during ejaculation.

name: seminal vesicle
definition: One of a pair of glands of the male reproductive system that together produce a significant portion of the semen.

name: seminiferous tubule
definition: One of numerous coiled tubes, found in the testis, in the walls of which spermatogenesis occurs.

name: sensitized strain
definition: Model organism containing a mutation in a pathway (e.g., metabolic or signal transducing) that does not itself cause a change in phenotype, but makes the organism more sensitive to another change elsewhere in the pathway.

name: septum
definition: In anatomy, thin wall dividing two cavities or masses of softer tissue.

name: serous
definition: Containing, resembling, or secreting serum.

name: Sertoli cell
definition: Somatic cell in the seminiferous tubule that supports spermatogenesis.

name: Sertoli–Leydig cell tumor
definition: Ovarian tumor composed of both Sertoli and Leydig cells.

name: sex chromatin
definition: Condensed mass of one inactivated X chromosome seen inside the nuclear membrane of an interphase cell.

name: sex chromosome
definition: One of the pair of chromosomes determining sex; in humans designated an X chromosome and a Y chromosome, with females having an XX genotype and males an XY genotype.

name: sex-determining region Y protein
definition: Transcription factor coded by a gene on the Y chromosome that initiates development of the male sex organs (i.e., testicular differentiation) in the embryo.

name: sexual dimorphism
definition: Phenotypic difference between the sexes of a species.

name: sexually dimorphic nucleus
definition: Compact area of large cells in the anterior hypothalamus, larger in men than women, and believed to influence sexual behaviour.

name: sexual maturation
definition: Process of reaching the age or stage when an organism can reproduce sexually.

name: sexual maturity
definition: Age or stage when an organism can reproduce sexually.

name: sexual reproduction
definition: Creation of a new organism requiring combination of the genetic material from two different sexes.

name: sibling
definition: One of two or more individuals with a common pair of parents.

name: signal transduction
definition: Process whereby a signal arising outside the cell is converted through a series of intermediate chemical reactions inside the cell to produce a functional change in the cell.

name: sinoatrial node
definition: Mass of specialized cardiac muscle cells ('pacemaker cells') that spontaneously depolarize to initiate rhythmic contraction of the heart.

name: sinus
definition: Hollow or cavity. Channel for the passage of fluid, lacking the usual lining of a blood or lymphatic vessel; especially a dilatation for the passage of venous blood.

name: sinus venosus
definition: Cavity at the caudal end of the developing embryonic heart where intra- and extra-embryonic veins meet.

name: sister chromatid exchange
definition: Reciprocal exchange of chromatin between two replicated chromosomes that remain attached to each other until anaphase of mitosis.

name: situs inversus
definition: Developmental anomaly in which major visceral organs are found in a mirrored position to their normal location.

name: small interfering RNA molecule
definition: Short interfering RNA.

name: somatic
definition: Pertaining to the body or describing cells that form the body other than germ line cells or undifferentiated stem cells.

name: somatic hypermutation
definition: Programmed process of mutation affecting the variable (V) regions of immunoglobulin (Ig) genes. SHM affects only individual immune cells, and the mutations are not transmitted to offspring.

name: human chorionic somatomammotropin
definition: Placental hormone that affects maternal metabolism and supports fetal growth by making more glucose and fatty acids available to the fetus.

name: somatomedin
definition: Any of a group of peptide growth factors produced by the liver following stimulation by somatotropin.

name: somatotropin
definition: Hormone produced in the pituitary gland that stimulates the liver to produce somatomedin.

name: somite
definition: One of bilaterally paired, segmented masses of mesodermal tissue lying along the notochord that gives rise to the vertebrae and associated muscle and connective tissue.

name: sonic hedgehog
definition: Protein morphogen produced in the notochord that plays a critical role in early development, including vertebrate organogenesis, brain development and limb formation.

name: spawn
definition: (v) Release gametes. (Of mature adult fish, frogs, molluscs, crustacea, etc.). (n) Fertilized eggs of mature adult fish, etc.

name: spawning
definition: (n) Release of gametes (eggs or sperm) from mature adult fish, frogs, molluscs, crustacea, etc. (adj) Describing behavior related to the readiness of mature adult fish, etc. to release gametes.

name: Spemann organizer
definition: Group of cells in the amphibian embryo that is important in orientation of surrounding cells and facilitates development of the central nervous system.

name: sperm banking
definition: Storage of frozen donor sperm for use in artificial insemination.

name: spermatid
definition: Haploid cell in the late stage of developing into a spermatozoon, derived from the secondary spermatocyte.

name: spermatocide
definition: Agent that kills spermatozoa.

name: spermatocyte
definition: Parent cell of a spermatid, derived by mitotic division from a spermatogonium.

name: spermatogenesis
definition: Entire process by which spermatogonial stem cells divide and differentiate into spermatozoa.

name: spermatogonial chromosome aberration test
definition: Procedure in which rodents are exposed to a test substance and chromosome aberrations are then studied microscopically in germ cells.

name: spermatogonium
definition: Primitive cell derived from mitosis of the germ cell that becomes the diploid primary spermatocyte.

name: spermatozoon
definition: Mature male gamete.

name: spermiation
definition: Release of mature spermatozoa from the Sertoli cells.

name: spermiogenesis
definition: Maturation of an immature spermatid into a spermatozoon.

name: sphenoid bone
definition: Irregular wing-shaped bone at the anterior base of the skull, forming part of the orbit, serving as an attachment site for muscles of mastication, and containing foramina for nerves and vessels of the head and neck.

name: sphincter
definition: Ringlike muscle that maintains closure of a body passage or orifice by contracting, and opens it by relaxing.

name: spina bifida
definition: Failure of the neural tube to close, resulting in the absence of part of the vertebral arch at the midline of the spinal column and exposure of the spinal cord and its covering membranes.

name: spinal column
definition: Backbone.

name: spinal cord
definition: Portion of the central nervous system outside the brain and inside the vertebral column.

name: spiral arteriole
definition: One of the corkscrew-like arterioles in premenstrual or progestational endometrium.
synonyms: coiled artery of the uterus|corkscrew-like artery|spiral artery|spiral endometrial artery

name: splanchnic
definition: Relating to the visceral organs, especially those of the abdomen.

name: spongioblast
definition: Embryonic epithelial cell that develops into a neuroglial cell.

name: stalk
definition: In anatomy, narrow connection with an organ or other structure.

name: allantoic stalk
definition: Narrow connecting tube between the intra- and extra-embryonic parts of the allantois.

name: stenosis
definition: Abnormal narrowing of a passage or opening in the body.

name: sterility
definition: Infertility. Asepsis.

name: sterilization
definition: Process that makes an organism incapable of fertilization or reproduction, e.g., castration, vasectomy, or salpingectomy. Process that makes an object aseptic.

name: steroid
definition: Naturally occurring compounds and synthetic analogues, based on the cyclopenta[a]phenanthrene carbon skeleton, partially or completely hydrogenated; there are usually methyl groups at \(\ce{C-10}\) and \(\ce{C-13}\), and often an alkyl group at \(\ce{C-17}\). By extension, one or more bond scissions, ring expansions, and/or ring contractions of the skeleton may have occurred.

name: steroid 21-monooxygenase
definition: Member (EC 1.14.14.16) of the cytochrome P450 family of enzymes required for the synthesis of some steroid hormones including aldosterone and cortisol.

name: steroidogenesis assay
definition: Procedure in which the effect of a test substance on steroid synthesis is studied, usually in a human adrenocortical carcinoma cell line.

name: stillbirth
definition: Birth of a baby without any signs of life, at a time variously taken as \(\pu{20\!{-}\! 28 weeks}\) of pregnancy.

name: stress-response pathway
definition: Signaling events induced when normal cell function or development is disrupted by environmental (physical or chemical) factors.

name: stromal cell
definition: Cell producing the connective tissue framework of an organ or other anatomical structure.

name: subthalamus
definition: Part of the diencephalon, of which the major part is the subthalamic nucleus, and which connects to the globus pallidus, part of the telencephalon.

name: sulcus
definition: Any long, narrow groove, furrow or shallow depression, specifically referring to one of the fissures on the surface of the brain.

name: superfecundation
definition: Fertilization of two or more ova released in the same period of ovulation, either by different males or by the same male in separate acts of intercourse.

name: superfetation
definition: Presence of two fetuses in the uterus at different stages of development, resulting from fertilization of ova released in two successive periods of ovulation.

name: supernumerary
definition: Exceeding the usual number; thus, in anatomy, anomalies such as a sixth finger on one hand or a third nipple (in a human).

name: pulmonary surfactant
definition: Surface-active layer of phospholipids and proteins coating the pulmonary alveoli that increases lung compliance, facilitates lung expansion, and stabilizes alveolar volume.

name: synapsis
definition: Point-wise pairing of homologous chromosomes during the prophase of meiosis.

name: synaptonemal complex
definition: Structure of filamentous proteins that forms between homologous chromosomes when they pair during meiosis; it may contribute to synapsis and genetic recombination.

name: syncephalus
definition: Conjoined twins with two bodies and a fused head.

name: syncytiotrophoblast
definition: Outer syncytial layer of trophoblast cells that invades the endometrium during implantation.

name: syncytium
definition: Referring to a large multinucleated mass of cellular contents that arises from the fusion of originally individual cells.

name: syndactyly
definition: Congenital occurrence of fusion or webbing of the fingers or toes.

name: syndrome
definition: Group of signs and symptoms occurring together, having a common cause and defining a disease.

name: synophthalmia
definition: Congenital fusion of the orbits in the midline, which then contains one eyeball.

name: synotia
definition: Congenital malformation characterized by the union or approximation of the ears in front of the neck, often accompanied by the absence or defective development of the lower jaw.

name: tail bud
definition: In the vertebrate embryo, mass of proliferating cells at the caudal end that arises from the primitive node.

name: Tay–Sachs disease
definition: Autosomal recessive inheritance of hexosaminidase A deficiency leading to a lysosomal storage disease characterized by central and peripheral neuronal involvement and early death.

name: tegmentum
definition: Floor of the midbrain.

name: telencephalon
definition: Embryonic structure that develops into the cerebrum.

name: telophase
definition: Final phase of both meiosis and mitosis in which distinct nuclei form in each daughter cell.

name: teratocarcinoma
definition: Malignant teratoma, occurring most often in the testis.

name: teratogen
definition: Chemical, physical, or biological agent that, when administered to a parent either prior to conception or before birth of the child, induces permanent structural malformations or birth defects in the offspring.

name: teratogenesis
definition: Process of development of malformations or birth defects.

name: teratogenetics
definition: Study of how genes and teratogens interact to cause birth defects.

name: teratogenic index
definition: Mortality of eggs expressed as a lethal concentration divided by the threshold concentration for production of abnormal embryos with nonheritable permanent structural malformations or defects following exposure to a teratogen.

name: teratogenicity
definition: Inherent ability to act as a teratogen.

name: teratology
definition: Study of the causes, mechanisms, and manifestations of developmental deviation of either structure or function.

name: teratoma
definition: Benign germ cell-derived tumor containing embryonic elements of the three primary germ layers, such as skin, hair, and muscle, occurring most frequently in the ovary.

name: Tessier classification
definition: Classification of bony and soft tissue facial clefts based on their anatomic location.

name: testicular feminization
definition: Type of male pseudohermaphroditism in which the individual has a male karyotype and testes present within the abdominal cavity, but develops external female genitalia and female secondary sexual characteristics.

name: testis
definition: Gonad of a male animal, involved in the secretion of androgens and the site of sperm production.

name: testosterone
definition: Androgenic steroid hormone produced primarily in the testis, responsible for the development of the male sexual organs and male secondary sexual characteristics.

name: tetralogy of Fallot
definition: Set of four congenital cardiac defects involving an opening in the wall that should separate the right and left ventricles (ventricular septal defect), allowing the aorta to receive venous as well as arterial blood: including stenosis of the pulmonary artery, hypertrophy of the right ventricle, and displacement of the aorta. Right ventricular hypertrophy is the fourth part of the tetralogy, although it may also be a consequence of the other defects.

name: thalamus
definition: Either of two masses of grey matter, the largest part of the diencephalon, lying between the cerebral hemispheres on either side of the third ventricle, relaying sensory information and acting as a centre for pain perception.

name: thalidomide
definition: Teratogenic indole-based drug with sedative and anti-angiogenic properties.

name: theca
definition: Bilayer covering of the ovarian follicle (thus theca interna and externa), of which the theca interna is involved in production of androstenedione.

name: thoracic duct
definition: Largest of the lymphatic vessels; it conducts lymph from its origin in the abdomen to the venous circulation at the junction of the left subclavian and jugular veins.

name: thrombocytopenia
definition: Abnormally low concentration of platelets (thrombocytes) in the blood.

name: thymus
definition: Pyramid-shaped organ in the thoracic or cervical region of mammals, composed of lymphatic tissue in which minute concentric bodies (thymic corpuscles, the remnants of epithelial structures) are found.

name: thyroglossal duct
definition: Connection in the embryo between the site of initiation of development of the thyroid gland and its final location in the neck.

name: thyroid gland
definition: Bilobar endocrine gland, located below the prominence of cartilage surrounding the larynx (the Adam’s apple), that produces and secretes the hormones triiodothyronine (T3), thyroxin (T4), and calcitonin.

name: accessory thyroid tissue
definition: Ectopic thyroid tissue arising from remnants of the thyroglossal duct.

name: thyroid stimulating hormone
definition: Pituitary hormone that stimulates the thyroid gland to produce thyroxine (T4), and then triiodothyronine (T3).

name: tonsil
definition: Small, rounded mass of tissue, especially of lymphoid tissue; generally used to designate one of the paired palatine tonsils.

name: toxoplasmosis
definition: Infection with the parasite Toxoplasma gondii that, when acquired by the fetus, can lead to a variety of congenital abnormalities that may include hydrocephalus or microcephaly, mental retardation, and problems with vision and hearing.

name: trachea
definition: Thin-walled, cartilaginous tube descending from the larynx to the bronchi and carrying air to the lungs.

name: transcription factor
definition: DNA-binding protein that is involved in regulating gene expression.

name: transgenic
definition: Describing an organism that is genetically changed by the addition or deletion of genetic material or whose existing genes are altered by gene targeting.

name: chromosomal translocation
definition: Rearrangement involving transfer or exchange of genetic material between non-homologous chromosomes that may occur during gametogenesis or in somatic cells, potentially leading to birth defects.

name: transplacental carcinogen
definition: Substance that crosses the placenta and subsequently causes cancer in the child or young adult.

name: transposition of the great arteries
definition: Congenital cardiovascular malformation in which the position of the chief blood vessels of the heart (aorta and pulmonary artery) is reversed.

name: Treacher Collins syndrome
definition: Congenital deformity characterized by structural abnormalities of the head and face.

name: trilaminar embryo
definition: Disc-like embryonic stage in which differentiation into three layers (endoderm, mesoderm, and ectoderm) has occurred.

name: trimester
definition: In pregnancy, one of three equal timed divisions of the normal human gestation period, each lasting approximately three months.

name: triple screen
definition: Measurement of maternal serum levels of alpha-fetoprotein, human chorionic gonadotropin, and estriol, usually in the second trimester of pregnancy, that can serve as an indicator of risk for certain fetal chromosomal abnormalities and neural tube defects.

name: triploidy
definition: Presence of three haploid sets of chromosomes in the cell.

name: trisomy
definition: Condition of having three homologous chromosomes in each somatic cell instead of the normal pair.

name: trisomy 8
definition: Presence of an extra chromosome 8.

name: trisomy 13
definition: Presence of part or all of an extra chromosome 13 from nondisjunction during meiosis.

name: trisomy 18
definition: Presence of part or all of an extra chromosome 18 from nondisjunction during meiosis.

name: trisomy 21
definition: Presence of an extra chromosome 21.

name: trophectoderm
definition: Outer layer of the blastocyst that contacts the endometrium, establishes nutrition for the embryo, and differentiates into the trophoblast.

name: trophoblast
definition: Outer layer of the blastocyst that invades the endometrium and establishes nutrition for the embryo.

name: truncus arteriosus
definition: Arterial trunk, opening from the fetal heart and developing into the aorta and pulmonary artery.

name: tuberoinfundibular pathway
definition: Group of dopaminergic neurons in the hypothalamus involved in regulating prolactin secretion from the anterior pituitary gland.

name: tumor
definition: Any abnormal swelling or growth of tissue, whether benign or malignant.

name: tunica albuginea
definition: Dense, collagenous fibrous coat surrounding an anatomical structure, and in particular surrounding the ovaries, testicles, and corpora cavernosa of the penis.

name: tunica vaginalis
definition: Membranous sheath, derived from the peritoneum, surrounding the testis and epididymis.

name: turner syndrome
definition: Phenotypic female lacking one X chromosome, the genotype being designated XO.

name: two-generation reprotox study
definition: Procedure in rodents wherein parents (P0 generation) and their offspring (F1 generation) are both exposed to a test substance and the second generation (F2) is examined for possible toxic effects.

name: tympanic
definition: In anatomy, relating to the resonant cavity and membrane of the inner ear.

name: ultrasonography
definition: Imaging technique that creates a picture of internal body structures from differentially reflected ultrasound waves.

name: ultrasound
definition: Sound waves of frequency higher than the range audible to the human ear. Imaging technique that uses such sound waves to create a picture of internal body structures.

name: umbilical artery
definition: Paired artery that, in the fetus, returns deoxygenated blood from each half of the fetal body to the placenta, via the umbilical cord.

name: umbilical cord
definition: Cord-like structure connecting the fetus with the placenta and housing the umbilical artery and umbilical vein that carry nutrients from the mother and remove wastes from the fetus.

name: umbilical hernia
definition: Protrusion of bowel or omentum through the abdominal wall at the umbilicus.

name: umbilical vein
definition: Vessel within the umbilical cord, entering the fetus at the umbilicus and carrying oxygenated blood from the placenta.

name: undescended testis
definition: Testis that has failed to descend completely from its developmental origin in the lower abdominal cavity into the scrotum.

name: urethra
definition: Duct by which urine is conveyed out of the body from the bladder, and which in male vertebrates also conveys semen.

name: urogenital
definition: Concerning the urinary and genital organs.

name: urogenital sinus
definition: Embryonic structure that forms in the ventral part of the cloaca when it separates from the anal canal to give rise to the genitourinary organs.

name: uterine crypt
definition: Chamber on the interior surface of the uterus that serves as a site of embryo homing and implantation.

name: uterine cycle
definition: Regular, periodic changes that occur in the uterus and, together with the ovarian cycle constitute the menstrual cycle necessary for female fertility.

name: uterotrophic
definition: Having an effect on the uterus.

name: uterotrophic assay
definition: Procedure in which immature female rodents are treated for three days with a test substance. A resultant increase in uterine wet weight suggests an estrogenic activity of the substance.

name: uterus
definition: Hollow muscular organ of the female reproductive system that receives the fertilized ovum (see implantation) and supports the subsequent development of the fetus.

name: uvula
definition: Muscular projection from the posterior edge of the soft palate.

name: vagina
definition: Fibromuscular canal passing between the uterine cervix and the opening to the vulva.

name: vaginal cornification
definition: Conversion of the normal epithelium of the vagina to a keratinized squamous (flattened) epithelium.

name: vaginal patency
definition: Referring to the opening of the vagina that usually occurs at sexual maturity and is maintained by hormonal influences pre-menopausally.

name: vaginal smear
definition: Examination by light microscopy of a sample of a vaginal discharge, used in the diagnosis of a vaginal infection.

name: developmental variation
definition: Anatomical deviation that is not life-threatening.

name: vasculogenesis
definition: De novo development of blood vessel endothelium in absence of preexisting vessels, e.g., during fetal development or in connection with tissue repair, initiated by migration of mesodermal precursor cells.

name: vas deferens
definition: Secretory duct of the testis running between the epididymis and the ejaculatory duct.

name: vasectomy
definition: Surgical removal of all or part of each vas deferens, typically as a means of sterilization.

name: vasopressin
definition: Pituitary hormone that acts to promote the retention of water by the kidneys and to increase blood pressure.

name: velopharyngeal insufficiency
definition: Inability to achieve closure of the velopharyngeal sphincter (closure of the muscle of the soft palate) during speech, owing to muscular dysfunction, cleft palate, or other disorders.

name: vena cava
definition: Large vein returning deoxygenated blood to the right heart.

name: ventral
definition: Situated to the anterior side of the trunk; in humans, to the front of the body.

name: ventricular septum
definition: Dividing wall between the two lower chambers (ventricles) of the heart.

name: ventricular septal defect
definition: Congenital defect with an opening in the wall separating the right and left ventricles of the heart (see ventricular septum).

name: vertebra
definition: One of the bony segments that together make up the bony column surrounding the spinal cord.

name: vertebrate
definition: Denoting an animal that has as part of its nervous system a spinal cord that is surrounded by a bony vertebral column.

name: vesicle
definition: Small fluid-filled sac, bladder-like structure, or blister.

name: vestigial
definition: In anatomy, pertaining to a remnant of an embryonic or fetal structure persisting in the adult.

name: viability
definition: Ability to continue living.

name: villus
definition: Projection from the surface, typically of a mucous membrane. Elongated projection of the dermis into an epidermal space.

name: vimentin
definition: Intermediate filament protein that is expressed in mesenchymal cells, e.g., fibroblasts, leukocytes, and blood vessel endothelial cells.

name: virilization
definition: Possession or acquisition of characteristics of a male body, especially by a female or prepubescent male.

name: viscera
definition: Soft and hollow organs of the body, in vertebrates particularly those found in the thoracic and abdominal cavities.

name: vitellogenin
definition: Protein that forms part of the yolk of egg-laying vertebrates.

name: vulva
definition: External genitalia of the female.

name: wean
definition: Accustomize a young mammal to independence from its mother’s milk as a source of nutrition.

name: web
definition: Tissue or membrane present between adjacent structures where it is not usually found, e.g., between fingers or toes, or between the neck and shoulder, representing a congenital abnormality.

name: Wharton’s jelly
definition: Gelatinous substance that embeds the vessels of the umbilical cord.

name: white matter
definition: Portion of the brain and spinal cord consisting mainly of myelinated axons (see myelination) and glial cells.

name: whole embryo culture
definition: Technique, used prior to embryo transfer during in vitro fertilization, in which embryos undergoing organogenesis are maintained in formulated medium outside the body.

name: wild type
definition: Of an allele or phenotype, the naturally occurring, unaltered, or most frequent; if several alleles occur, the most frequent one is considered to be the wild type.

name: Williams syndrome
definition: Congenital disorder with characteristic facies (described as elf-like), short stature, outgoing personality and mild mental retardation; associated with contiguous gene deletions on chromosome 7.

name: Wnt
definition: Family of genes important in development, the proteins they encode, or the signal transduction pathways they determine.

name: X chromosome
definition: Chromosome determining female sex in the absence of a Y chromosome.

name: X-linked
definition: Carried by a gene located on the X chromosome.

name: Y chromosome
definition: Chromosome determining male sex.

name: yolk
definition: Nutritive material stored in the ovum for the nourishment of the embryo.

name: yolk sac
definition: Fluid-filled, membrane-bound pouch on the ventral side of the early embryo that provides nourishment until the circulatory system develops.

name: yolk stalk
definition: Narrow tubular support that connects the yolk sac to the middle of the digestive tract of an embryo.

name: zinc finger
definition: Small tertiary protein structure in which parts of the protein, typically with cysteine and histidine residues, link to a divalent zinc ion, forming a loop or 'finger' that attaches proteins to DNA.

name: zona pellucida
definition: Acellular glycoprotein-rich membrane surrounding the mature ovum.

name: zygosis
definition: Sexual union of two cells with fusion of their nuclei.

name: zygote intrafallopian transfer
definition: Introduction of a zygote fertilized in vitro into one of the Fallopian tubes.

name: 1D property descriptor
definition: An observed or calculated property of the whole molecule.

name: 1D structure
definition: The structure of a molecule encoded into a string such as SMILES or InChI.

name: 2D property
definition: A molecular property that is calculated from the structure diagram of the molecule.

name: 2D structure
definition: The structure of a molecule presented as a drawing or a file that contains a description of the topology, stereochemistry, and atomic symbol of its atoms and the bonds connecting them, but no explicit information about its three-dimensional structure.

name: 2D quantitative structure-activity relationships
definition: A computational model of the quantitative relationship between the observed independent 1D property of a set of compounds and their dependent 1D properties or 2D properties.

name: 3D property
definition: A property that is observed or calculated from a 3D representation of a molecule, which may depend on one or more conformations of the molecule.

name: 3D searching
definition: A virtual screening method that processes a chemical database to discover those compounds that match a query that either contains a 3D pharmacophore, a molecular shape or field, the 3D structure, or a combination of these.

name: 3D structure
definition: The structure of the conformation of a molecule presented as a drawing or a file that describes atomic symbols of its atoms and the bonds connecting them as well as their coordinates in three-dimensional space.

name: 3D structure generation
definition: A method to generate one or more 3D structures, conformations, of a molecule from its topological molecular graph.

name: 4D quantitative structure-activity relationships
definition: A computational model of the quantitative relationship between the target observed independent 1D properties for a set of compounds and the 3D properties of  several of their conformations.

name: algorithm
definition: A step-by-step procedure for solving a problem or performing a function, usually by a computer.

name: applicability domain
definition: The property or structure space for which the predictions of a computational model are considered to be reliable.

name: area under the curve
definition: The area under a graph curve, such as the number of actives identified by an algorithm as a function of the number of compounds tested, commonly used as a  measure of the discriminating ability of an algorithm to correctly classify a test molecule.

name: autocorrelation vector
definition: A vector that describes a molecular structure in which each element corresponds to a distance (number of bonds in a 2D structure or a binned interatomic  distance in a 3D structure) between atoms of a particular type and the count of the number of times that distance is found in the structure.

name: basis set superposition error
definition: An artifactual increase in calculated stability of the supersystem (the system formed by noncovalent interaction between two or more molecular entities, e.g. hydrogen bond system) resulting from the basis set of the supersystem being larger than for the component subsystems. The BSSE arises from a lowering of the quantum mechanical energy when the electron density of each subsystem spreads into the basis functions provided by the other subsystems.

name: Bayesian regularized neural network
definition: A feed-forward neural network that uses Bayesian statistics to optimize the complexity and predictive power of the model.

name: Bayesian statistics
definition: A branch of statistics in which the evidence of the state of a system is expressed in terms of degrees of belief (probabilities).

name: Bayes’s theorem
definition: A method for calculating prior probability estimates of an event that can be revised in accordance with new observations.

name: belief theory
definition: A method to combine probability estimate states that given two or more probabilities \(P_{i}\) that a particular event is true, the combined probability of the event is given by: \[P = 1 - \Pi (1 - {P_{i}})\]

name: bilinear equation
definition: A QSAR equation that describes the non-linear dependence of the relative biological potency (\(\log 1/C\)) of a molecule on log P by the following form: \[log(1/{C_i}) = a\log P_{i} - b \log (\beta P_{i} + 1) + c\]

name: bit string
definition: A description of a molecule in a fixed length vector, each element of which is set from corresponding structural keys or calculated by hashing a molecular  fingerprint.

name: Boltzmann enhanced discrimination of receiver operating characteristic
definition: A generalization of the area under the ROC curve to weight more heavily the early recognition of active compounds.

name: bootstrap resampling
definition: A procedure to evaluate the accuracy of the statistics of a model, such as the overall R2 or the contribution of particular properties, by systematically recomputing the statistics generated from many models developed using sample sets that contain the same number of observations as the original set, but for which certain observations are randomly omitted and other observations are included more than once.

name: calculated molar refractivity
definition: The calculated molar refractivity of a molecule or substituent used as a measure of size and polarizability in 2D-QSAR.

name: canonical structure representation
definition: A unique representation of the chemical structure of a molecule that is independent of the sequence in which the atoms were ordered in the original input file  but is dependent on the algorithm used for the canonicalization.

name: chance correlation
definition: An artificial correlation that can arise when too many properties are screened relative to the number of available observations.

name: cheminformatics
definition: The science of handling, indexing, archiving, searching, and evaluating information that is specific to chemical structures and is used in data mining,  information retrieval, information extraction, and machine learning.

name: circular fingerprints
definition: Hashed molecular fingerprints that describe, either by atom type or properties, each atom in the molecule; the atoms connected to it (for path length 2); the  atoms connected to them (for path length 4); and the atoms connected to them (for path length 6); etc..

name: clog P
definition: Calculated log of the octan-1-ol/water partition coefficient.

name: cluster centroid
definition: The geometric center of a cluster, often exemplified as the object that is closest to the center.

name: collinearity
definition: A linear relationship between two or more of the descriptors in a model, which can lead to difficulties in interpreting the relative importance of these  descriptors.

name: comparative molecular similarity analysis
definition: A 3D-QSAR method similar to CoMFA that instead uses Gaussian-type functions to calculate the 3D properties of the molecules by the similarity of each molecule  to each probe at each lattice position surrounding the molecules.

name: concordance
definition: The ability of a two-group classification model to correctly classify all molecules.

name: confusion matrix
definition: A table layout that shows the results of a two-class/binary classifier in which columns correspond to the predicted classifications from the model and rows correspond to the observed classifications.

name: continuum
definition: The computational representation of a solvent as a continuous medium instead of individual explicit solvent molecules.

name: counterpoise correction
definition: A method to correct for basis set superposition error.

name: data mining
definition: The extraction of useful information from large sets of observations.

name: Daylight fingerprints
definition: Path fingerprints that are generated from a structure where atoms are described by atomic number and aromaticity; bonds are described as single, double,  triple, or aromatic; and the results are hashed into a bit string of fixed length.

name: de novo design
definition: The process whereby a computer algorithm designs new molecules to meet certain single or multiple criteria, defined by an objective function, for example predicted affinity for a binding site or predicted affinity plus appropriate lipophilicity.

name: decision tree
definition: The result of a recursive partitioning classification method that shows at each branching point the value of the property responsible for the split and the resulting classifications after the split.

name: density functional theory
definition: A quantum mechanical modeling method used to investigate the electronic structure of molecules using functionals that describe the spatially dependent electron density, rather than the wavefunction as in ab initio and semi-empirical quantum chemical methods.

name: descriptor
definition: A qualitative or quantitative property of a molecule or a part of a molecule.

name: docking
definition: Computational methods that optimize the placement of a ligand in a macromolecular binding site of known or proposed 3D structure and provide a score as to the quality of the fit.

name: drug-likeness
definition: An estimate of the probability that a chemical structure is similar to known drugs based on chemical or physical properties.

name: energy of the highest occupied molecular orbital
definition: The energy of the highest energy level in the ground state of a molecule that contains electrons, sometimes used as a measure of nucleophilicity in QSAR  models.

name: energy of the lowest unoccupied molecular orbital
definition: The energy of the lowest energy level of a molecule that contains no electrons in the ground state, sometimes used as a measure of electrophilicity in QSAR  models.

name: expert system
definition: A system that predicts properties or activities of chemicals from rules devised by domain experts.

name: explicit solvent
definition: Individual solvent molecules that are included in a computation, in contrast to those implied by a continuum approximation.

name: extended connectivity fingerprints
definition: Hashed circular fingerprints that encode each atom according to its atomic symbol and hybridization for path length 2, ECFP2; path length 4, ECFP4; and path  length 6, ECFP6.

name: false negative
definition: A model prediction of a negative result, such as no biological activity, when the true result is positive, i.e. activity.

name: false positive
definition: A model prediction of a positive result, such as biological activity, when the true result is negative, i.e. inactivity.

name: force field
definition: A set of mathematical functions and their associated parameters used in a molecular mechanics or dynamics calculation of conformations, flexibility, and interactions of molecules.

name: fragment keys
definition: Description of the structure of a molecule as the presence or absence of each of a pre-determined set of molecular substructures, usually associated with a  particular location in a bit string.

name: free energy perturbation
definition: A method that uses molecular dynamics or Metropolis Monte Carlo simulations to compute the relative free energy differences between two conditions, typically the solution and bound states of a ligand-protein system.

name: functional class fingerprints
definition: Hashed circular fingerprints that encode each atom according to its property (hydrophobic, hydrogen bond donor, hydrogen bond acceptor, negatively charged, or  positively charged) for path length 2, FCFP2; path length 4, FCFP4; and path length 6, FCFP6.

name: global model
definition: A computational model designed to cover all of chemistry space although it typically includes a measure of if the molecule for which the properties are to be  predicted is within or outside the applicability domain of the model.

name: graph-based method
definition: A computational method that converts the problem to be solved into a graph characterized by the character of the objects, such the atoms of a molecule or molecules in a database, and the distances between them.

name: Hansch equation
definition: A QSAR equation that describes the relationship between the logarithm of the relative biological potency of a molecule (\(\log (1/C_{i})\)) and its electronic and hydrophobic properties: \[\log (1/C_{i}) = \rho \sigma_{i} + b\,\log P_{i} - c\,(\log P_{i})^{2}\] in which fitting to the square term provides a parabola with an associated optimum log P.

name: Hansch–Fujita π-constant
definition: A constant that describes the contribution of a substituent to the octan-1-ol-water log P of a compound.]

name: hashing
definition: An algorithm that maps data of variable length, such as the raw descriptors of path or circular fingerprints or InChIs, to a smaller fixed length vector.

name: InChIKey
definition: A fixed length (character) condensed digital representation of the InChI that is not human-understandable.

name: International Chemical Identifier
definition: A non-proprietary canonical identifier of chemical substances that can be used in printed and electronic data sources to enable easier linking of diverse data  compilations.

name: ISIS keys
definition: Predefined fragment keys that are used in 2D substructure and similarity searching with the ISIS software but are also generated by many other software  programs and used for 2D-QSAR or cluster analysis of molecules.

name: jackknifing
definition: A procedure to evaluate the accuracy of the statistics of a model, such as the overall R2 or the contribution of particular properties, by systematically recomputing the statistics generated from models developed by leaving out one or more observations at a time from the sample set.

name: kappa shape descriptor
definition: A type of topological index.

name: kernel method
definition: Algorithms for pattern analysis that use functions such as Gaussians to enable them to operate in a high-dimensional descriptor space without ever computing  the coordinates of the data in that space.

name: leave-some-out cross-validation
definition: A form of cross-validation in which more than one observation is left out at each run. Typically many runs with random samplings are performed.

name: leverage
definition: The influence of an observation on the coefficients of a fitted equation.

name: ligand efficiency
definition: Measure of the free energy of binding per heavy atom count (i.e. non-hydrogen) of a molecule.

name: linear interaction energy
definition: A method that forecasts ligand binding free energies using force field estimations of the receptor-ligand interactions and thermal conformational sampling .

name: lipophilic ligand efficiency
definition: A measure of the efficiency of ligand binding that is corrected for binding driven by lipophilicity.

name: loading of a property
definition: The contribution of the property to a principal component or partial least squares latent variable.

name: local model
definition: A computational model that applies to only a subset of molecules, typically a closely related series.

name: log D
definition: The logarithm of the ratio of the total concentration (neutral and charged species) of a compound in a nonpolar phase, traditionally water-saturated octan-1-ol, to that in water at a given \(\pu{pH}\).

name: log P
definition: The logarithm of the ratio of the concentration of the uncharged form of a compound in a nonpolar phase, traditionally water-saturated octan-1-ol, to that in  water.

name: machine learning
definition: A computer algorithm that generates empirical models, such as a model of biological potency as a function of the properties of the molecules, that is derived  from the analysis of a training set for which all the necessary data are available.

name: macromolecular crystallographic information file
definition: A file that describes in detail the features of a macromolecular structure and the X‑ray diffraction experiment that was used to derive that structure.

name: Markush structure
definition: A structure diagram that describes a set of related molecules with the structure of the common core and the structures of the substituents at each position.

name: molecular diversity
definition: A measure of the spread of various properties or chemotypes within a set of compounds.

name: molecular fingerprints
definition: Descriptions of the structure of a molecule calculated from the properties of each of its atoms and bonds that are then usually condensed into a fixed-length string by a hashing algorithm.

name: molecular similarity
definition: The degree to which two molecules resemble one another as calculated from their respective 2D or 3D properties, molecular fingerprints, fragment keys, or superimposed 3D structures that usually ranges from 1 (identical) to 0 (dissimilar).

name: multidimensional scaling
definition: A visualization method that converts a dataset of distances between molecules in property space into coordinates in lower dimension space with emphasis on  preserving the relative distances between dissimilar molecules.

name: multiobjective optimization
definition: The search for those combinations of properties that produces the best compromise between the various objectives of the search, for example properties of  compounds that are the best trade-off between potency, bioavailability, and selectivity.

name: orthogonal projections to latent structures
definition: A preprocessing method for partial least squares calculations that filters out variation that is not correlated to the property to be fit and so results in  improved interpretability of a PLS model while maintaining its predictivity.

name: overtraining
definition: Training a machine learning model for so long that the original input data is memorized with the result that model predictivity is degraded.

name: Pareto front
definition: The various combinations of predictor properties that lead to optimum predicted compromises in multiple target properties.

name: Pareto optimization
definition: The search for solutions to functions that provide a compromise between several desirable outcomes, such as potency, lack of toxicity, and good absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME) properties.

name: partial atomic charges
definition: Charges assigned to atoms, arising from the uneven distribution of electrons in bonds, that are used to calculate intermolecular interaction energy or to  characterize the charge distribution of a molecule.

name: path fingerprints
definition: Vectors of Boolean arrays generated from the properties of the atoms and bonds in linear paths, typically two to seven bonds long, hashed into an integer of  fixed determined length.

name: protein data bank file
definition: A text file that stores the atomic coordinates of a macromolecule, usually a protein or nucleic acid with associated ligands, solvent molecules and ions.

name: pharmacophore
definition: A proposal for the ensemble of steric and electronic features that define the optimal supermolecular intermolecular interaction of a ligand with a specific  biological target structure with the result that it triggers or blocks its biological response.

name: pipelining programs
definition: Visual programming of the computational execution of sequential operations on a dataset, with each node specifying an operation with options, and the nodes processed sequentially.

name: PLS latent variable
definition: One of the vectors of a linear combination of the input descriptors that a partial least squares calculation extracts from a dataset.

name: PLS loading
definition: The contribution of a particular property to a PLS latent variable.

name: Poisson–Boltzmann equation
definition: A differential equation that uses a mean-field, continuum model to describe the electrostatic interactions in ionic solutions where both ions and solvent are  treated implicitly, resulting in less computational effort to describe biomolecules in ionic aqueous solutions.

name: polar surface area
definition: Surface area over all polar atoms (usually oxygen and nitrogen), including any attached hydrogen atoms, of a molecule.

name: pose diagram
definition: A 2D diagram that shows the interactions between a ligand and a protein in the 3D structure of the complex.

name: posterior probability
definition: The conditional probability that is assigned to a quantity after relevant evidence is taken into account. The prior and posterior probabilities are linked by  the (normalized) likelihood function (Bayes's theorem).

name: prediction set
definition: Molecules that have been set aside from model development to test the reliability of the derived model.

name: principal component loading
definition: The contribution, scaled between \(\pu{-1.0}\) and \(\pu{1.0}\), of an original variable to a particular principal component.

name: principal component score
definition: A property of a molecule calculated from a principal components analysis of the original properties and the value of these properties for the molecule.

name: prior probability
definition: The conditional probability that is assigned to a quantity before relevant evidence is taken into account, for example, the prior probability of an active  compound would be the fraction of the compounds in the dataset that are active.

name: protein data bank
definition: An archive of freely available macromolecular structural data of proteins, nucleic acids, and complex assemblies.

name: q2
definition: The square of the leave-one-out cross-validation regression coefficient calculated from the variance of the observed versus predicted values of the target  property, usually potency, of each compound when eliminated during cross-validation.

name: r2
definition: The ratio of the sum of squares explained by a regression model (SSR) to the 'total' sum of squares around the mean (SST), or, because SST equals SSR plus the sum of squares of the error or residuals from the fit (SSE): \[R^{2} = \frac{{\rm{SSR}}}{{\rm{SST}}} = 1 - \frac{{\rm{SSE}}}{{\rm{SST}}}\]

name: random forest method
definition: A classification method that produces many recursive partitioning models, each with a random selection of predictor properties, and then combines the models  for predictions.

name: recall
definition: The fraction of the total number of actives, in the top-scoring docking hits, such as the fraction of true actives that are retrieved in the top \(\pu{1\%}\) scoring molecules.

name: receiver-operator characteristic curve
definition: A plot that shows the result of a test of the performance of a binary classifier by plotting the fraction of true positives identified versus the fraction of  false positives as the discrimination threshold is varied.

name: recursive partitioning
definition: A classification method that uses predictor properties to successively divide the data set into subsets such that each resulting subset is enriched in  molecules that are in one class.

name: regularization
definition: Introducing additional information in order to solve an ill-posed problem or to prevent overfitting, usually taking the form of a penalty for complexity of the  model.

name: response scrambling
definition: Evaluation of the robustness of a QSAR or classification model by repeatedly randomizing the target property of compounds, developing models based on this  randomized property, and comparing the statistics of fit of the scrambled models with those of the true model, which should be superior.

name: R-group decomposition
definition: The process whereby the molecules in a dataset are partitioned into the core ('scaffold'), usually user-specified, and the specific substituents ('R-groups')  found at each specific position.

name: rule of five
definition: The rule of five states that molecules that violate two or more of the following rules are likely to have permeability problems; (1) CLOGP calculated octan-1-ol-water log P greater than 5.0; (2) molecular weight greater than 500; (3) more than five hydrogen bond donors; and (4) the sum of oxygen and nitrogen atoms is greater than 10.

name: scoring
definition: A mathematical formula that estimates the binding affinity of a ligand to a macromolecular target based on the structure of the complex.

name: structure-data format file
definition: A computer text file that follows a specified format in which each molecule is described by 2D or 3D coordinates, atom type, and connectivity to other atoms  and also specific user-definable fields that contain other information such as name and biological or chemical properties.

name: sensitivity analysis
definition: Analysis, often by finding approximate derivatives of the output with respect to each input, that determines which of the descriptors in a model has the  greatest influence on the output.

name: similarity ensemble approach
definition: A method that predicts the probability that a molecule or set of molecules will be active against a particular target by considering its pairwise similarities  to all known ligands for that target.

name: similarity searching
definition: A virtual screening method that calculates the molecular similarity of an input 2D or 3D structure to each of the molecules in a database to identify a  requested number of most similar molecules or those above some similarity threshold.

name: SMARTS
definition: An expansion of the SMILES language that describes a particular specific or generalized substructure.

name: SMIRKS
definition: A derivative of the SMILES language that describes the transformation in a chemical reaction.

name: specificity
definition: The ability of a two-class model to detect known inactive or non-toxic molecules.

name: standard error of estimates
definition: The standard error of the errors or residuals, observed minus calculated, from a computational model: \[{\rm{SEE}} = \sqrt \frac{\sum (Y_{o} - Y_{c})^{2}}{n}\] in which \(Y_{o}\) is the observed value of \(Y\), \(Y_{c}\) is the calculated value of \(Y\), and \(n\) is the number of observations.

name: standard error of prediction
definition: The standard deviation of the errors or residuals, observed minus calculated, from a computational model: \[{\rm{SEP}} = \sqrt \frac{\sum (Y_{o} - Y_{p})^{2}}{n - k}\] in which \(Y_{o}\) is the observed value of \(Y\), \(Y_{p}\) is the predicted value of \(Y\), \(n\) is the number of observations, and \(k\) is the number of terms in the model.

name: structural keys
definition: A pre-established set of substructures the presence or absence of which are used to describe a molecule and are used during substructure searching as a filter  to eliminate molecules that cannot match a query, for clustering or similarity searching, or for developing classification or regression models.

name: structure diagram
definition: A 2D drawing that shows the atoms of a molecular structure and the bonds that connect them.

name: substructure searching
definition: A virtual screening method that uses a graph-based method to discover which molecules in a chemical structure database contain the substructure specified in  the query.

name: supervised learning
definition: A machine learning method that aims to discover a relationship between the predictor and the response values, such as exists in a QSAR or recursive  partitioning model.

name: Tanimoto similarity
definition: A scale that ranges from \(\pu{0.0}\) to \(\pu{1.0}\) when calculated as the ratio of the fingerprint bits or structural keys that both molecules have set divided by the number of bits or keys set in both molecules plus those set either molecule.

name: test set
definition: The set of molecules not used in any way to devise a computational model but instead are used to test its predictivity.

name: topological index
definition: A numerical value associated with chemical constitution for correlation of chemical structure with various physical properties, chemical reactivity or biological activity. The numerical basis for topological indices is provided (depending on how a molecular graph is converted into a numerical value) by either the adjacency matrix or the topological distance matrix. In the latter the topological distance between two vertices is the number of edges in the shortest path between these.

name: topological polar surface area
definition: An approximation to polar surface area that is calculated from the 2D structure.

name: true negative
definition: A model prediction of a negative result, such as no biological activity, when the true result is also negative.

name: true positive
definition: A model prediction of a positive result, such as biological activity, when the true result is also positive.

name: Tversky similarity
definition: An asymmetric measure in which a target structure is compared to a reference structure with user-selectable weighting of the relative importance of the fingerprint bits or structural keys that are present only in the reference versus the fingerprint bits or structural keys that are only in the target, weightings for which the Tanimoto coefficient uses \(\pu{1.0}\).

name: underdetermined system
definition: A system in which the number of descriptors is much larger than the number of observations.

name: validation set
definition: The molecules not used to devise a computational model but instead are used during model development to test for possible over-fitting as seen when additional  properties are added to a model but the predicted potencies of the validation set become less accurate.

name: virtual reaction
definition: The computer encoding of a possible chemical reaction between two explicit or Markush structures or substructures, often with a mapping between the atoms in  the starting material and those in the product.

name: virtual screening
definition: Computational methods that rank the molecules in a database by their forecast continuous or categorical biological or chemical properties.

name: workflow
definition: The sequence of steps used to perform a certain task.

name: apparent monomer
definition: Monomer which from the name of a polymer appears to have been used in the synthesis of the latter when it has actually been prepared from different precursor(s).

name: block homopolymer
definition: Homopolymer that is composed of macromolecules comprising blocks that have at least one constitutional or configurational feature which is not present in the adjacent portions.

name: graft homopolymer
definition: Homopolymer composed of macromolecules with one or more species of block connected to the main chain as side chains, these side chains having constitutional or configurational features that differ from those in the main chain.

name: standardization
definition: Measurement of the concentration of a component of a solution with a reference measurement standard for the preparation of a secondary measurement standard

name: controlled release
definition: Detection principle for a chemically modified electrode (CME) in which an analyte or reagent accumulated at a CME undergoes quantitative release (egress, stripping, expulsion, or microdosing) to the test solution, under electrochemical or chemical control.

name: all-solid-state ion-selective electrode
definition: Ion-selective electrode in which the ion-selective membrane contacts the electronic conductor without internal electrolyte solution.

name: self-assembled monolayer
definition: Film, one molecule thick, in an ordered assembly on a surface.

name: cationized molecule
definition: Ion formed by the association of a cation with a molecule \(\ce{M}\).

name: nominal mass
definition: Mass of a molecular ion or molecule calculated using the isotope mass of the most abundant constituent element isotope of each element rounded to the nearest integer value and multiplied by the number of atoms of each element.

name: reflectron
definition: Component of a time-of-flight mass spectrometer that uses a static electric field to reverse the direction of travel of the ions and improves mass resolution by assuring that ions of the same m/z but different translational energy arrive at the detector at the same time.

name: adhesion
definition: Attachment of interfaces between phases or components that is maintained by intermolecular forces, chain entanglements, or both.

name: Michaelis–Menten equation
definition: The relationship between the initial rate (velocity) of an enzyme-catalysed reaction \(v_{0}\) and the initial substrate concentration \([\ce{S}]_{0}\) in the form \[v_{0} = V[\ce{S}]_{0}/(K_{\rm{M}} + [\ce{S}]_{0})\] where \(V\) (the limiting rate) and \(K_{\rm{M}}\) (the Michaelis constant) are independent of the initial substrate concentration and constant at a given temperature and a given enzyme concentration. The reaction is then said to display Michaelis–Menten kinetics.

name: protein sequencing
definition: Determination of the primary structure of a protein.

name: zone pH
definition: pH of the solute zone in pH-zone-refining counter-current chromatography. \[{\rm{pH}}_{\rm{zone}} = \pu{p}K_{\rm{a}} + \log[(K_{\rm{DS}}/K_{\rm{S}}) - 1]\], where \(K_{\rm{DS}}\) is the partition ratio of solute $\ce{S}$ (an indicator for solute hydrophobicity) and \(K_{\rm{S}}\), the dissociation constant of the solute.

name: intraparticle volume of the column
definition: Volume of the mobile phase within the pores of the particles in the stationary phase.
synonyms: intrastitial volume of the column|stationary mobile-phase volume

name: distribution constant (exclusion)
definition: Fraction of the intraparticle volume (the volume of the pores) available to the molecules of a particular sample component for diffusion: \[K_{0} = \frac{V_{\rm{R}} - V_0}{V_{\rm{i}}}\]

name: distribution constant calibration
definition: Calibration for extraction when close to equilibrium conditions, using a known for the distribution constant for the analyte.

name: microextraction (methology)
definition: Extraction method characterized by a low phase ratio, so that at equilibrium the fraction extracted is low (i.e. the extraction is not exhaustive).
