definition: Behavioral test wherein a rodent stranger is placed in the cage of a domestic rodent and intensities and duration of interactions (e.g., sniffing, aggression, avoidance) between the socially unacquainted animals are observed.

name: soporific
definition: Substance producing sleep.

name: spasm
definition: Sudden involuntary contraction of one or more muscles; includes cramps and contractures.

name: spasmolytic
definition: Agent that relieves smooth muscle spasms.

name: spastic
definition: Relating to spasticity.

name: spasticity
definition: Increased muscle tone at rest, characterized by resistance to passive stretch.

name: sphingolipid
definition: Member of a class of lipids containing the aliphatic amino alcohol sphingosine, or related structures, thus including ceramide.

name: sphingomyelin
definition: One of a family of phospholipids found especially in the central nervous system, containing 1-phosphocholine bound to a ceramide.

name: sphingosine
definition: Major lipid component of cell membranes.

name: startle reaction
definition: Rapid physiological and psychological response to a sudden, unexpected stimulus that includes muscle contraction and avoidance posturing, with an increase in heart rate, respiration, skin conductance, and a negative affect.

name: startle reflex
definition: The earliest brainstem-mediated part of the reflex reaction to a stimulus perceived as threatening.

name: acoustic startle response test
definition: Neurophysiological examination in which an animal is exposed to a brief (e.g., \(\pu{40 ms}\)) acoustic stimulus, followed by measurement of the animal’s motor reaction.

name: status epilepticus
definition: Repeated or prolonged seizure lasting more than \(\pu{30 min}\).

name: stereology
definition: Three dimensional interpretation of two dimensional cross sections of tissue and other materials.

name: unbiased stereology
definition: Stereological method that uses systematic analysis of defined spatial fractions of a sample to estimate numbers of neuronal nuclei independent of changes in size and shape that may occur during tissue processing.

name: stimulant
definition: Agent that rouses or increases mental or physical activity.

name: stimulus
definition: Anything that produces a reaction in an organism. That which causes a response in an excitable tissue such as a nerve, muscle or gland.

name: conditioned stimulus
definition: Stimulus that comes to evoke a response after repetitive pairing with another stimulus that automatically elicits that response.

name: unconditioned stimulus
definition: Stimulus that automatically elicits a paired response, such as food eliciting salivation in a hungry animal.

name: striatum
definition: Subcortical structure of striations of gray matter and white matter in the forebrain that serves as the major input to the basal ganglia, specifically the caudate nucleus, the putamen and the striated structure linking them.

name: stroke
definition: Acute impairment of circulation to a part of the brain, lasting more than \(\pu{24 h}\).

name: stupor
definition: State of impaired consciousness showing diminution in response to environmental stimulation.

name: subarachnoid
definition: Underneath the arachnoid membrane.

name: subarachnoid hemorrhage
definition: Loss of blood into the space between the arachnoid membrane and the pia mater.

name: subdural
definition: Between the dura mater and the arachnoid membrane.

name: substantia nigra
definition: Component of the basal ganglia involved in production of the neurotransmitterdopamine.

name: supratentorial
definition: Intracranial contents located above the tentorium of the cerebellum, notably the white matter of the cerebrum, often describing functional symptoms of diseases of the white matter that lead to physical and mental disability.

name: supratentorial herniation
definition: Abnormal protrusion of brain structures into compartments above the tentorium, or over the edge of the tentorium, due to increased intracranial pressure.

name: swimming test
definition: Procedure in which a test animal (rodent) is forced to swim to avoid drowning.
synonyms: Porsolt forced swimming test|behavioral despair test|forced swimming test

name: sympathetic nervous system
definition: Part of the autonomic nervous system originating in the thoracic and lumbar regions of the spinal cord that tends to inhibit or oppose the physiological effects of the parasympathetic nervous system, as in tending to reduce digestive secretions, increase the heart rate, and contract blood vessels.

name: sympathomimetic
definition: n., Substance that produces effects resembling those of impulses transmitted by the postganglionic fibers of the sympathetic nervous system. adj., Having the property of producing such effects.

name: synapse
definition: Functional junction between two neurons, where a nerve impulse is transmitted from one neuron to another, by neurotransmitters.

name: synaptic cleft
definition: Narrow gap between the presynaptic and postsynaptic regions of two communicating neurons, into which neurotransmitters are secreted.

name: synaptic inhibition
definition: Suppression of synaptic transmission.

name: synaptic plasticity
definition: Ability of synapses to form and reform continually, including to allow learning. Malleability of signal strength arising at the level of synaptic transmission.

name: synaptic stripping
definition: Removal of dysfunctional synapses.

name: synaptic transmission
definition: Neurotransmitter release, diffusion, and receptor binding, propagating an impulse across a synapse.

name: syringomyelia
definition: Cyst occurring within the spinal cord as a result of accumulation of cerebrospinal fluid.

name: T-maze
definition: Simple type of test apparatus with three arms shaped like the letter 'T.' After placing a rodent in the middle, it is recorded how often the animal enters each arm.

name: tachycardia
definition: Abnormally fast heartbeat.

name: tail flick test
definition: Procedure in which the tail of a rodent is heated and the time taken for the animal to flick its tail (latency) is taken as a measure of the relative degree of antinociception.

name: tail immersion test
definition: Procedure in which the tail of a rodent is placed in a hot water bath (typically between \(\pu{54^{\circ}C}\) and \(\pu{58^{\circ}C}\)) and the time it takes the animal to remove the tail from the water is interpreted as a measurement of the relative degree of antinociception.

name: tail suspension test
definition: Procedure in which a mouse is suspended by its tail and the time spent attempting to right itself is observed.

name: tauopathy
definition: One of a class of neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer disease, associated with abnormal aggregation of tau proteins.

name: tau protein
definition: One of a class of proteins that stabilizes microtubules, particularly in neurons, astrocytes, and oligodendrocytes of the central nervous system.

name: TDP-43 transcription factor
definition: Cleavage product (\(\pu{43 kDa}\)) of the transactive response (TAR) DNA binding protein (TARDBP) that targets TAR DNA and transcriptionally represses HIV-1.

name: temperature sensitivity
definition: Adverse responsiveness to heat or cold. Note: It is associated with a number of medical conditions, some physiologically well-defined (as in cold intolerance in hypothyroidism) and others less so (as in reported chronic fatigue syndrome). Phenotype arising from engineered or selected gene mutations in experimental organisms characterized by an altered temperature permissive for optimal growth or survival.

name: temporal lobe
definition: One of the four major lobes of each cerebral hemisphere, situated at the base of the brain.

name: tentorium
definition: Fold of the dura mater separating the cerebrum from the cerebellum.

name: tetanic
definition: Pertaining to tetanus, characterized by tonic muscle spasm.

name: tetanus
definition: Sustained muscle contraction. Disease caused by tetanus toxin and characterized by painful, sustained muscle contraction with spasticity and paralysis.

name: tetanus toxin
definition: Neurotoxin produced by the bacterium Clostridium tetani growing in anaerobic conditions, producing the disease tetanus.

name: tetanus toxin-binding ganglioside
definition: Ganglioside that binds tetanus toxin, facilitating its internalization at the presynapticneuronal membrane.

name: tetany
definition: Neurological syndrome characterized by muscle twitches, cramps, and spasms; and in severe forms, by spasm of the muscles of the larynx (laryngospasm) and seizures.

name: tetrad test
definition: Battery of tests typically for the effects of cannabinoids in rodents that includes hypomotility assessed by an open field test, catalepsy assessed by the bar test, hypothermia measured by rectal temperature, and analgesia measured by avoidance of heat, e.g., in the tail immersion test.

name: tetrodotoxin
definition: Neurotoxin that inhibits action potentials by blocking sodium ion channels.

name: tetrodotoxin-insensitive
definition: Denoting a class of sodium ion channels, found mainly in the heart, that is not blocked by tetrodotoxin.

name: thigmotaxis
definition: Movement of an organism toward or away from a mechanical stimulus, physical contact, or spatial discontinuity, as in movement away from touch by a physical stimulus or exploring close to a wall.

name: thoracic spine
definition: Portion of the vertebral column of the upper back, between the cervical spine and lumbar spine, in humans consisting of 12 vertebrae designated T1 to T12.

name: threshold potential
definition: Level of depolarization that must be reached to trigger an action potential in an excitable cell.

name: thrombus
definition: Clot in the cardiovasculature formed from components of the blood, which may be attached to the vessel wall and (or) occlusive.

name: tingling
definition: Pricking type of paresthesia.

name: tinnitus
definition: Continual noise in an ear, such as ringing, buzzing, roaring, or clicking.

name: tomography
definition: Construction of an image of a three-dimensional structure from a series of planar sections obtained with penetrating waves.

name: torticollis
definition: Spasmodic contraction of neck muscles drawing the head to one side with the chin pointing to the other side.

name: toxic substance
definition: Substance causing injury to living organisms as a result of physicochemical interactions.

name: tranquilizer
definition: Drug that calms and pacifies with minimal sedating or depressant effects.

name: transcutaneous electronic nerve stimulation
definition: Electrical stimulus applied across the skin to excite nerves for therapeutic purposes.

name: transsynaptic
definition: Referring to an event, such as transmission of a nerve impulse, across a synapse.

name: transtentorial herniation
definition: Bulging of brain tissue from the cerebrum through the notch of the tentorium, caused by increased intracranial pressure.

name: treadmill test
definition: Procedure used to assess limb function and strength, often to evaluate models of peripheral neuropathy, in which a rodent is placed in an enclosed lane upon a surface that can be made to move at variable speed in a retrograde manner, thus allowing observation of the animal’s gait dimension during sustained attempt at forward motion.

name: tremor
definition: Repetitive, often regular and usually involuntary oscillatory movement caused by alternating contractions of opposing muscle groups.

name: trigeminal nerve
definition: Fifth cranial nerve, supplying sensation to the face and controlling motor activity of mastication.

name: trigeminal neuralgia
definition: Severe, paroxysmal bursts of pain in one or more branches of the trigeminal nerve, often induced by touching trigger points in or about the mouth.

name: triptan
definition: Member of a class of drugs based on tryptamine that act as serotonin receptor agonists.

name: unconscious
definition: Not in a conscious state. In psychoanalytic theory, describing feelings and motivations of which one is unaware that nevertheless shape behavior.

name: uncus
definition: Anterior projection of the gray matter surrounding the hippocampus, covered by a region of the temporal lobe, involved in olfaction.

name: upper motor neuron
definition: Neuron whose cell body lies in the cerebral cortex or brainstem and whose axon carries impulses to a lower motor neuron.

name: vagus nerve
definition: Tenth cranial nerve, arising from the medulla oblongata.

name: vasoconstriction
definition: Decrease in the diameter of the lumen of a blood vessel (especially in the arteries and arterioles) as a result of contraction of smooth muscles in the vessel walls.

name: vasodilator
definition: Agent that induces vasorelaxation.

name: vasopressor
definition: Agent that induces vasoconstriction.

name: vasorelaxation
definition: Increase in the diameter of the lumen of the blood vessels as a result of relaxation of smooth muscles in the vessel walls.

name: vasospasm
definition: Contraction of the muscular wall of blood vessels with sustained vasoconstriction possibly leading to tissue ischemia.

name: venom
definition: Animal toxin generally used for self-defense or predation and usually delivered by a bite or sting.

name: ventricle
definition: Normal cavity within an organ, as in the brain or heart.

name: ventriculo-atrial shunt
definition: Surgical shunt draining cerebrospinal fluid into a cardiac atrium, to relieve pressure in hydrocephalus.

name: ventriculogram
definition: Radiographic image of the cerebralventricles.

name: ventriculomegaly
definition: Enlargement of the cerebralventricles.

name: ventriculo-peritoneal shunt
definition: Surgical shunt draining cerebrospinal fluid into the peritoneum of the abdominal cavity, to relieve pressure in hydrocephalus.

name: vermis
definition: Narrow central part of the cerebellum between the two cerebellar hemispheres.

name: vertebral column
definition: Bony structure consisting of the vertebrae and enclosing the spinal cord.

name: vertigo
definition: Dizziness; an illusion of movement as if the external world were revolving around one’s self or as if one’s self were revolving in space.

name: vigilance
definition: Ability to maintain concentration or sustain attention over prolonged periods of time.

name: vigilance decrement
definition: Decreased vigilance measured as a decline in the ability to maintain an accurate voluntary response to signals with time.

name: visual cortex
definition: Part of the cerebral cortex located in the occipital lobe, responsible for processing the images of sight.

name: voltage-gated ion channel
definition: Ion channel that opens and closes in response to changes in membrane potential.

name: water maze test
definition: Procedure in which a rat or mouse is placed in a pool of water and observed to swim, using visual environmental clues, to an invisible submerged platform that allows escape from the water.
synonyms: Morris water maze test|water navigation test

name: Wernicke aphasia
definition: Type of aphasia associated with damage to Wernicke’s area or alternatively the medial temporal lobe of the brain, characterized by preservation of speech but with loss of meaningful language and language comprehension.

name: Wernicke’s area
definition: Region of the brain in superior temporal gyrus of the dominant hemisphere, associated with comprehension of written and spoken language.

name: Wernicke–Korsakoff syndrome
definition: Co-existence of Wernicke encephalopathy (with gait, ocular and mental disturbances) and Korsakoff psychosis (severe memory loss, often with aphasia, apraxia or agnosia) caused by vitamin B1 deficiency in the context of chronic alcohol abuse.

name: Western Pacific amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and parkinsonism–dementia complex
definition: Neurodegenerative disease observed in the islands of Guam, Indonesia, Japan and Papua New Guinea, showing combinations of characteristics of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, atypical parkinsonism with dementia, or dementia alone that may present sequentially during life.

name: Wisconsin card sorting test
definition: Procedure in which cards, depicting different arrangements, numbers, and colors of symbols, are presented to the test subject, who is asked to make the most appropriate match of a test card without further instructions.

name: withdrawal
definition: Cessation of exposure to a substance, being characterized by adverse symptoms.

name: withdrawal effect
definition: Adverse event following withdrawal from a person or animal of a drug to which they have been chronically exposed or on which they have become dependent.

name: Wolfgram protein
definition: Acidic proteolipid protein component of central nervous systemmyelin.

name: wrist drop
definition: Inability to extend the wrist as a result of peripheral nerve damage, causing drooping of the hand.

name: zebrafish
definition: Tropical fish (Danio rerio) about \(\pu{4 cm}\) long, commonly used as a model organism in developmental biology.

name: chain segment
definition: Group of contiguous skeletal atoms in a chain, including their side groups, if any, such that the chain itself can be represented as a chain of segments.

name: rotational isomeric state
definition: Rotamer defined by a relative rotation about a skeletal bond of a single-strand chain.

name: chain conformation
definition: Conformation of a chain as defined by its sequence of bond-conformational states.

name: unperturbed conformational state
definition: Chain conformation corresponding to unperturbed dimensions.

name: unperturbed radius of gyration
definition: Radius of gyration of a macromolecule in an unperturbed conformational state.

name: root-mean-square radius of gyration
definition: For a flexible macromolecule composed of \(n\) mass elements, of masses \(m_{i}\), \(i = 1, 2, \ldots, n\), located at statistical-mechanical mean-square distances \(\lt\!s_{i}^{2}\!\gt\) from the centre of mass, the root-mean-square radius of gyration is the square-root of the mass average of \(\lt\!s_{i}^{2}\!\gt\) over all mass elements, i.e., \[\lt\!s^{2}\!\gt^{1/2}\;= \left(\sum\limits_{i=1}^{n} m_{i} \lt\!s_{i}^{2}\!\gt\!/\sum\limits_{i=1}^{n} m_{i} \right)^{1/2}\]

name: mean-square radius of gyration
definition: For a flexible macromolecule composed of \(n\) mass elements, of masses \(m_{i}\) , \(i = 1, 2, \ldots, n\), located at statistical-mechanical mean-square distances \(\lt\!s_{i}^{2}\!\gt\) from the centre of mass, the mean-square radius of gyration is the mass average of \(\lt\!s_{i}^{2}\!\gt\) over all mass elements, i.e., \[\lt\!s^{2}\!\gt = \left(\sum\limits_{i=1}^{n} m_{i} \lt\!s_{i}^{2}\!\gt\!/\sum\limits_{i=1}^{n} m_{i} \right)\]

name: root-mean-square unperturbed radius of gyration
definition: Root-mean-square radius of gyration of a macromolecule having unperturbed dimensions.

name: mean-square unperturbed radius of gyration
definition: Mean-square radius of gyration of a macromolecule having unperturbed dimensions.

name: unperturbed end-to-end vector
definition: Vector connecting the two ends of a linear chain in a particular conformation, with the chain having unperturbed dimensions.

name: unperturbed end-to-end distance
definition: Magnitude of the unperturbed end-to-end vector.

name: mean-square end-to-end distance
definition: Statistical-mechanical mean-square end-to-end distance of a linear chain averaged over all chain conformations.

name: root-mean-square unperturbed end-to-end distance
definition: Root-mean-square end-to-end distance of a chain having unperturbed dimensions.

name: mean-square unperturbed end-to-end distance
definition: Mean-square end-to-end distance of a chain having unperturbed dimensions.

name: root-mean-square end-to-end distance of a freely rotating chain
definition: Root-mean-square end-to-end distance of a linear freely rotating chain.

name: mean-square end-to-end distance of a freely rotating chain
definition: Mean-square end-to-end distance of a linear freely rotating chain.

name: effective bond length
definition: Square root of the ratio of the unperturbed mean-square end-to-end distance of a linear chain to its number of skeletal bonds, i.e., \[b = (\lt\!r_{\rm{o}}^{2}\!\gt\!/n)^{1/2}\]

name: equivalent freely jointed chain
definition: Hypothetical freely jointed chain with the same mean-square end-to-end distance and contour length as an actual linear chain having unperturbed dimensions.

name: Kuhn segment
definition: Segment or link of an equivalent freely jointed chain.

name: Kuhn segment length
definition: Length of a Kuhn segment.
synonyms: freely jointed link length|statistical segment length

name: self-avoiding random-walk chain
definition: Freely jointed chain subject to the condition that the segments cannot intersect one another.

name: macromolecular coil
definition: Depiction of a macromolecule in which its segments are distributed about some point in space.

name: chain stiffness
definition: Parameter describing the end-to-end distance of a linear, single-strand macromolecular chain having unperturbed dimensions relative to that of a model macromolecular chain not subject to short-range interactions.

name: g-factor
definition: Ratio of the mean-square radius of gyration of a branched molecule, \(\lt\!s_{\rm{b}}^{2}\!\gt\), to that of an otherwise identical linear molecule, \(\lt\!s_{\rm{l}}^{2}\!\gt\), of the same relative molecular mass in the same solvent at the same temperature, i.e., \(g = \lt\!s_{\rm{b}}^{2}\!\gt\!/\!\lt\!s_{\rm{l}}^{2}\!\gt\).
synonyms: contraction factor|geometric contraction factor|radius of gyration contraction factor

name: g′-factor
definition: Ratio of the intrinsic viscosity of a branched molecule, \([\eta_{\rm{b}}]\), to that of an otherwise identical linear molecule, \([\eta_{\rm{l}}]\), of the same relative molecular mass in the same solvent at the same temperature, i.e., \(g^{\prime} = [\eta_{\rm{b}}]/[\eta_{\rm{l}}]\).

name: molar mass
definition: Mass divided by amount of substance.

name: molar-mass average
definition: Any average of the molar mass, molecular weight, relative molar mass, or relative molecular mass for a non-uniform polymer, with the symbol \(\rm{k}\) specifying the type of average.

name: number-average molar mass
definition: The equation for number-average molar mass is \[M_{\rm{n}} = \frac{1}{\sum\limits_{M} (w_{M}/M)}\] The equation for number-average molecular weight  is \[M_{\rm{r,n}} = \frac{1}{\sum\limits_{M_{\rm{r}}}(w_{M_{\rm{r}}}/M_{\rm{r}})}\]

name: mass-average molar mass
definition: The equation for mass-average molar mass is \[M_{\rm{m}} \equiv M_{\rm{w}} = \sum\limits_{M} w_{M}M\] The equation for mass-average molecular weight  is \[M_{\rm{r,m}} \equiv {M_{\rm{r,w}}} = \sum\limits_{M_{\rm{r}}} w_{M_{\rm{r}}} M_{\rm{r}}\]

name: z-average molar mass
definition: The equation for z-average molar mass is \[M_{\rm{z}} = \frac{\sum\limits_{M} w_{M}M^{2}}{\sum\limits_{M} w_{M}M}\] The equation for z-average molecular weight is \[M_{\rm{r,z}} = \frac{\sum\limits_{M_{\rm{r}}} w_{M_{\rm{r}}}M_{\rm{r}}^{2}}{\sum\limits_{M_{\rm{r}}} w_{M_{\rm{r}}}M_{\rm{r}}}\]

name: (z + 1)-average molar mass
definition: The equation for (z + 1)-average molar mass is \[M_{\rm{z+1}} = \frac{\sum\limits_{M} w_{M}M^{3}}{\sum\limits_M w_{M}M^{2}}\] The equation for (z + 1)-average molecular weight is \[M_{\rm{r,z+1}} = \frac{\sum\limits_{M_{\rm{r}}} w_{M_{\rm{r}}}M^{3}}{\sum\limits_{M_{\rm{r}}} w_{M_{\rm{r}}}M^{2}}\]

name: viscosity-average molar mass
definition: The equation for viscosity-average molar mass is \[M_{\rm{v}} = \left[\sum\limits_{M} w_{M}M^{a} \right]^{1/a}\] The equation for viscosity-average molecular weight is \[M_{\rm{r,v}} = \left[\sum\limits_{M_{\rm{r}}} w_{M_{\rm{r}}}M_{\rm{r}}^{a} \right]^{1/a}\] where \(a\) is the exponent in the Mark–Houwink equation, \([\eta] = KM^{a}\)

name: apparent molar mass
definition: Molar mass, molecular weight, relative molar mass, or relative molecular mass calculated from experimental data without the application of appropriate corrections.

name: cumulative number-distribution function
definition: Cumulative distribution function in which the relative amount of a portion of a substance with values of the random variable or variables less than or equal to a given value or given values is expressed in terms of mole fraction.
synonyms: cumulative number distribution|integral number distribution|integral number-distribution function

name: cumulative mass-distribution function
definition: Cumulative distribution function in which the relative amount of a portion of a substance with values of the random variable or variables less than or equal to a given value or given values is expressed in terms of mass fraction.
synonyms: cumulative mass distribution|integral mass distribution|integral mass-distribution function

name: molar-mass dispersity
definition: Ratio of the mass-average molar mass, \(M_{\rm{m}}\), molecular weight, relative molar mass, or relative molecular mass, \(M_{\rm{r,m}}\), to the number-average molar mass, \(M_{\rm{n}}\), molecular weight, relative molar mass, or relative molecular mass, \(M_{\rm{r,n}}\). \[Ð\!_{\rm{M}} = M_{\rm{m}}/M_{\rm{n}} = M_{\rm{r,m}}/M_{\rm{r,n}}\]

name: degree-of-polymerisation dispersity
definition: Ratio of the mass-average degree of polymerisation, \(X_{\rm{m}}\), to the number-average degree of polymerisation, \(X_{\rm{n}}\). \[Ð\!_{\rm{X}} = X_{\rm{m}}/X_{\rm{n}}\]

name: dispersity
definition: Ratio of \(M_{\rm{m}}\) to \(M_{\rm{n}}\), or the ratio of \(X_{\rm{m}}\) to \(X_{\rm{n}}\) for a homopolymer or an alternating copolymer of sufficiently large molar mass, such that the effects of the distinct structures of the end-groups of the constituent macromolecules can be neglected, giving \(X_{\rm{n}}\) directly proportional to \(M_{\rm{n}}\), \(X_{\rm{m}}\) directly proportional to \(M_{\rm{m}}\) and \(Ð\!_{\rm{M}} = Ð\!_{\rm{X}} = Ð\).

name: semi-dilute solution
definition: Polymer solution in the concentration range at which the domains occupied by the dissolved macromolecules or entities start to overlap.

name: concentrated solution
definition: Polymer solution in the concentration range at which the domains occupied by the dissolved macromolecules or entities overlap to such an extent that it is not possible to distinguish the individual domains from one another.

name: entanglement
definition: Entanglement, involving one or more macromolecular chains, of duration at least equal to the period of observation.

name: mesh size
definition: Average distance between two adjacent entanglements on a given macromolecule in a semi-dilute solution, a concentrated solution, or bulk amorphous polymer.

name: blob
definition: Hypothetical spherical volume element occupied by a subchain of a macromolecule between two neighbouring entanglements on the same macromolecule.

name: scaling law
definition: Equation of the type \(y = k x^{a}\), relating two physical quantities, \(x\) and \(y\ (\rm{g})\), in which the value of the exponent \(a\) can be predicted by theory.

name: free volume
definition: Difference between specific volume of an amorphous polymer and that of its perfect crystalline form.

name: mean-field theory
definition: Theory reducing the difficult exact evaluation of interactions in a multi-body system to a simpler but approximate evaluation of an average effective interaction of one body with its surroundings.

name: co-nonsolvency
definition: Decrease in solubility of a polymer in a solvent comprising more than one component, each component of which by itself is a solvent for the polymer.

name: osmometer
definition: Apparatus for measuring osmotic pressure.

name: osmometry
definition: Measurement of the osmotic pressure of a solution using an osmometer.

name: osmotic virial coefficient
definition: Coefficient in the expansion of the chemical potential of the solvent, \(\mu_{\rm{s}}\), in powers of the mass concentration, \(c\), of the solute, i.e., \[\mu_{\rm{s}} - \mu_{\rm{s}}^{\circ} = -\mathit{\Pi} V_{s}^{\prime} = -RT V_{s}^{\prime} (A_{1}c + A_{2}c^{2} + A_{3}c^{3} + \ldots)\] where \(\mu_{\rm{s}}^{\circ}\) is the chemical potential of the solvent in the reference state at the temperature of the system and ambient pressure, \(\mathit{\Pi}\) is the osmotic pressure and \(V_{s}^{\prime}\) is the partial molar volume of the solvent. In solvents comprising more than one component, the definition applies to any solvent component.
synonyms: virial coefficient of the chemical potential

name: binodal
definition: Curve in the isobaric temperature-composition plane for a mixture defining the region of composition and temperature across which a transition occurs from miscibility of the components to conditions where single-phase mixtures are metastable or unstable.

name: cloud point
definition: Point in the isobaric temperature-composition plane of a binary or multicomponent mixture at which a decrease in transparency is observed due to the turbidity caused by phase separation.

name: cloud-point curve
definition: Curve of temperature vs. composition defined by the cloud points over range of compositions of two substances.

name: cloud-point temperature
definition: Temperature at a cloud point.

name: lower critical solution temperature
definition: Critical temperature below which a mixture is miscible at any composition.

name: translational diffusion
definition: Process by which the equilibrium statistical distribution of positions of molecules or entities in space is maintained or restored due to their translational Brownian motion.

name: translational frictional coefficient
definition: Frictional force, \(F\), per unit velocity, \(u\), experienced by an isolated spherical body moving unidirectionally in a viscous isotropic fluid, i.e., \(F = fu\).

name: translational diffusion coefficient
definition: Proportionality constant relating the flux per unit area, \(J_{n}\), in unidirectional flow of amount, \(n\), of entities \(\ce{B}\) to their concentration gradient in the direction (\(x\)) of flow, \({\rm{d}}c_{\ce{B}}/{\rm{d}}x\), i.e., \(J_{n} = -D{\rm{d}} c_{\ce{B}}/{\rm{d}}x\).

name: rotational frictional coefficient
definition: Torque, \(T\), per unit angular velocity, \(\omega\), required for rotation of a body about a given axis in a viscous isotropic fluid, i.e., \(T = \zeta\omega\).

name: equilibrium sedimentation method
definition: Experimental method by which the distribution of the concentration of the solute or dispersed component in a dilute solution or dispersion along the centrifuge cell is measured at sedimentation equilibrium, and the results are interpreted in terms of the molar masses of the solute species or their distribution functions, or both.

name: equilibrium sedimentation in a density gradient
definition: Equilibrium sedimentation method using a multicomponent solvent forming a density gradient in a centrifugal field.
synonyms: sedimentation equilibrium in a density gradient

name: Kraemer equation
definition: Equation describing the dependence of the inherent viscosity, \(\eta_{\rm{inh}}\), of a dilute solution on the mass concentration of the solute, \(c\), with \[\eta_{\rm{inh}} = (\ln \eta_{\rm{r}})/c = [\eta] + k_{\rm{K}}[\eta]^{2} c\] where \(k_{\rm{K}}\) is the Kraemer coefficient and \([\eta]\) is the intrinsic viscosity.

name: Kraemer coefficient
definition: Parameter in the Kraemer equation.

name: hydrodynamic interaction
definition: In a solution or dispersion, the perturbation of the flow of the solvent continuum or dispersing medium continuum around a solute molecule, a segment of a dissolved macromolecule or dispersed entity caused by the presence of the other solute molecules, segments, or dispersed entities.

name: free-draining
definition: Adjective describing the undisturbed flow of solvent through the domain of a dissolved macromolecule.

name: impermeable
definition: Adjective describing the flow behaviour of a macromolecule in solution or a dispersed entity when, due to hydrodynamic interaction, the solvent or dispersion medium within the domain of the macromolecule or dispersed entity is essentially immobilised and moves with the dissolved macromolecule or dispersed entity.

name: partial free-draining
definition: Adjective describing the flow behaviour of a macromolecule in solution or a dispersed entity when, due to hydrodynamic interaction, the solvent within the domain of the macromolecule or a dispersed entity becomes progressively more immobilised with respect to the macromolecule or a dispersed entity in the direction from its outer fringes inward.

name: equivalent hydrodynamic volume
definition: Volume of the hydrodynamically equivalent sphere.

name: equivalent hydrodynamic radius
definition: Radius of the hydrodynamically equivalent sphere.

name: Stokes equation
definition: For an isolated dissolved molecule or dispersed entity, an equation relating the translational frictional coefficient, \(f\), to the equivalent hydrodynamic radius in translational diffusive flow, \(r_{D}\), and to the viscosity of the solvent continuum or the dispersion medium continuum, \(η_{0}\), with \[f = 6\uppi \eta_{0}r_{D}\]

name: Stokes–Einstein equation
definition: For an isolated dissolved molecule or dispersed entity, an equation relating the translational diffusion coefficient, \(D\), to the equivalent hydrodynamic radius in translational diffusive flow, \(r_{D}\) , and to the viscosity of the solvent continuum or the dispersion medium continuum, \(\eta_{0}\), with \[D = kT/(6\uppi \eta_{0}r_{D})\] where \(k\) is the Boltzmann constant, and \(T\) the thermodynamic temperature.

name: Perrin equation
definition: For an isolated dissolved molecule or dispersed entity, an equation relating the rotational diffusion coefficient, \(\mathit{\Theta}\), to the equivalent hydrodynamic radius in rotational diffusive flow, \(r_{\mathit{\Theta}}\), and to the viscosity of the solvent continuum or the dispersion medium continuum, \(\eta_{0}\), with \[D = kT/(6\pi \eta_{\rm{0}} r_{\mathit{\Theta}}^3)\] where \(k\) is the Boltzmann constant and \(T\) the thermodynamic temperature.

name: pearl-necklace model
definition: Model describing the flow behaviour of a dissolved chain macromolecule in terms of a freely jointed sequence of beads, each of which offers hydrodynamic resistance to the flow of the surrounding solvent continuum and is connected to the next bead by a rigid rod that offers no hydrodynamic resistance.

name: Kirkwood–Riseman theory
definition: Theory, based on the pearl-necklace model, that describes the translational diffusive and viscous flows of an isolated linear macromolecule in solution in the theta state and accounts for the gradual change from free-draining behaviour at lower molecular weights to impermeable behaviour at higher molecular weights.

name: Flory–Fox assumption
definition: Assumption that the Kirkwood–Riseman theory can be applied to linear isolated macromolecules in solution, independent of whether they are in the theta state.

name: Flory–Fox equation
definition: Equation relating intrinsic viscosity, \(\eta\), and molar mass, \(M\), to the mean-square radius of gyration, with \[[\eta]M = \mathit{\Phi}^{\prime}\!\lt\!s^{2}\!\gt^{3/2}\] where \(\mathit{\Phi}^{\prime}\) is a parameter the value of which depends on the molar-mass distribution, macromolecular constitution, and chain expansion.

name: Rouse theory
definition: Molecular theory for treating polymer chain dynamics based on the bead-spring model assuming the beads (segments) have zero excluded volume and there is no hydrodynamic interaction between the beads.

name: Rouse chain
definition: Hypothetical polymer chain satisfying the assumptions made in the Rouse theory.

name: reptation
definition: Snake-like movement of a polymer chain in a semi-dilute or concentrated solution or bulk amorphous polymer through the hypothetical tube created by neighbouring chains.

name: tube model
definition: Model to describe the motion of a polymer chain confined in the hypothetical tube created by neighbouring chains.

name: tube renewal
definition: Dynamic renewal of tubes by the disentanglement and re-entanglement of polymer chains.

name: primitive chain
definition: Polymer chain allowed to undergo reptation along the tube created by neighbouring chains.

name: uniform dispersion
definition: Dispersion of particles of identical size, shape, and constitution.

name: non-uniform dispersion
definition: Dispersion of particles not identical with respect to size, shape, or constitution.

name: static light scattering
definition: Experimental method based on the measurement of the time-averaged intensity of light scattered from a polymer solutions or a dispersion of particles at various angles with respect to the incident beam.

name: dynamic light scattering
definition: Experimental method based on the measurement of the time autocorrelation function of the intensity of light scattered from a polymer solution or a dispersion of particles.

name: small molecule
definition: Molecule much smaller than the wavelength of the radiation in the solvent used.

name: large molecule
definition: Molecule of size similar to or larger than the wavelength of the radiation in the solvent used.

name: excess scattering
definition: Difference between the scattering intensity for a dilute solution or a dilute dispersion and that for the pure solvent or the dispersion medium at the same scattering angle.

name: static structure factor
definition: Function describing the dependence of relative scattering intensity on the magnitude of the scattering vector, \(q\), for a polymer solution or a dispersion.

name: dynamic structure factor
definition: Function describing the temporal dependence of relative scattering intensity on the magnitude of the scattering vector, \(q\).

name: elution time
definition: Time elapsed from the injection of the sample into a chromatography bed to the recording of a specified signal of the detector due to the sample having passed through the bed.

name: elution volume
definition: Volume of solvent that has passed through a chromatography bed from the injection of the sample to the recording of a specified signal of the detector due to the sample having passed through the bed.

name: transfer coefficient
definition: The anodic transfer coefficient \(\alpha_{\rm{a}}\) and the cathodic transfer coefficient \(\alpha_{\rm{c}}\) are defined by the following equations: \[\alpha_{\rm{a}} = (RT/F)({\rm{d}}\ln\! j_{\rm{a}}/{\rm{d}}E); \quad \alpha_{\rm{c}} = -(RT/F)({\rm{d}}\ln\!\vert {j_{\rm{c}}} \vert /{\rm{d}}E)\] In these equations, \(j_{\rm{a}}\) and \(j_{\rm{c}}\) are the anodic and cathodic current densities, respectively, corrected for any changes in the reactant concentration at the electrode surface with respect to its bulk value; incidentally, the symbols \(\ln\! j_{\rm{a}}\) and \(\ln\!\vert j_{\rm{c}}\vert\) imply that the argument of the logarithm is of dimension one, obtained by division with the corresponding unit, e.g., \(\ln\! j_{\rm{a}}\) meaning \(\ln(j_{\rm{a}}/\pu{A m^{-2}})\), and similarly for the other quantities \(\vert j_{\rm{c}}\vert\), \(k_{\rm{a}}\) and \(k_{\rm{c}}\). \(E\) is the applied electric potential, \(R\) is the gas constant, \(T\) is the thermodynamic temperature, and \(F\) is the Faraday constant. In practice, \(\alpha_{\rm{a}}\) and \(\alpha_{\rm{c}}\) are defined as the reciprocal of the corresponding Tafel slopes, \({\rm{d}}E/{\rm{d}}\ln\! j_{\rm{a}}\) and \(-{\rm{d}}E/{\rm{d}} \ln\! \vert j_{\rm{c}} \vert\), made dimensionless by the multiplying factor \(RT/F\). Both the transfer coefficient and the Tafel slope are determined at constant temperature and pressure.

name: combined technique
definition: Application of two or more techniques to different samples at the same time. This can include thermal and nonthermal analytical techniques.

name: controlled-rate thermal analysis
definition: Sample-controlled method where the feedback used to control the heating is the rate of transformation.

name: controlled temperature program
definition: Temperature history imposed on the sample during the course of the thermal analysis experiment.

name: cooling curve
definition: Experimental result of measuring the temperature of the sample as a function of time during cooling. Heating curves are obtained for temperature-time experiments during heating.

name: derivative technique
definition: Pertaining to the \(1^{\rm{st}}\) derivative (mathematical) of any curve with respect to temperature or time.

name: dielectric thermal analysis
definition: Technique where dielectric properties are measured.

name: differential technique
definition: Pertaining to a difference in measured or measurable quantities usually between a sample and a reference or standard material.

name: heat-flow differential scanning calorimetry
definition: Technique where the difference between the heat-flow rates into a sample and a reference material is measured.

name: power compensation differential scanning calorimetry
definition: Technique where the difference between the electrical powers into a sample and a reference material is measured.

name: dynamic technique
definition: Indicates, especially in the mechanical analysis of materials, that a parameter changes continuously during the experiment.

name: dynamic mechanical analysis
definition: Technique where storage and loss viscoelastic moduli are determined with the help of a periodical stress.

name: gas flow
definition: Passage of gas from one part of the system to another. The gas may be either inert (carrier gas) or reactive, either introduced into the system or evolving from the sample.

name: isothermal technique
definition: Applied to a technique to indicate that the temperature is maintained constant throughout the experiment.

name: material
definition: The substance which is studied and from which the sample is taken.

name: micro- technique
definition: Prefix used to denote that the technique measures small quantities, either with respect to the amount of sample studied, or with respect to the change in the properties measured.

name: modulated technique
definition: Indicates that a parameter changes in a periodic manner during the experiment.

name: modulated temperature technique
definition: Applied to the technique name to indicate that a temperature modulation has been applied to the temperature program.

name: photo- technique
definition: Indicates that the experiment involves the illumination of the sample or measures the amount of light emitted from a sample. Where possible, the wavelength range of the light should be specified.

name: sample controlled technique
definition: Applied to the technique to indicate that a property of the sample is used either continuously or discontinuously to control the sample heating. Without this term, it is assumed that the experiment is following a controlled-temperature program.

name: scan
definition: A term used to describe the data produced from a thermal analysis experiment. More correct usage is a thermal analysis curve, or, for a specific technique thermogravimetric curve, etc.

name: scanning technique
definition: Indicates that a specified experimental parameter, if not temperature, is changed in a controlled manner.

name: scanning calorimetry
definition: Techniques where heat is measured as a function of temperature.

name: simultaneous technique
definition: Indicates the measurement of two or more properties of a single sample at the same time.

name: static technique
definition: Indicates, especially in the mechanical analysis of materials, a constant parameter during the experiment.

name: stepwise technique
definition: Indicates discrete, discontinuous changes in an experimental parameter, e.g., force, temperature, etc.

name: tan $\delta$
definition: The dimensionless ratio of energy lost to energy returned during one cycle of a periodic process.

name: temperature-programmed desorption
definition: EGA using an inert atmosphere or vacuum, in the absence of sample decomposition.

name: temperature-programmed oxidation
definition: Experiment using an oxidising atmosphere, usually oxygen. Oxidation is monitored by any appropriate technique (EGA, TGA, gas sorption, etc.).

name: temperature-programmed reduction
definition: Experiment using a reducing atmosphere, usually hydrogen. Reduction is monitored by any appropriate technique (EGA, TGA, gas sorption, etc.).

name: thermal curve
definition: Any graph of any combination of property, time, temperature derived from a thermal analysis technique.

name: thermally stimulated current
definition: Electrical current observed during heating and caused by the thermally initiated relaxation of the frozen-in electrical polarization of a sample.

name: thermally stimulated depolarisation
definition: Relaxation of frozen-in electrical polarization caused by a temperature increase.

name: thermo- technique
definition: Indicating the use of changing temperature during the experiment, when in the name of a thermal analysis technique.

name: thermoanalytical
definition: Of, or pertaining to, thermal analysis.

name: thermodiffractometry
definition: A technique where the X-ray diffraction of the sample is measured.

name: thermogravimetric analysis
definition: A technique where the mass of the sample is measured, also known as thermogravimetry.

name: thermomanometry
definition: A technique where the gas pressure is measured.

name: thermomechanical analysis
definition: A technique where the deformation of the sample is measured under constant load.

name: thermomicroscopy
definition: A technique where the optical properties of the sample are observed and measured through a microscope.

name: thermospectrometry
definition: A group of techniques where a spectrum of the sample is measured.

name: absolute quantitation of proteins
definition: Method for absolute quantitation of proteins via measurements on constituent proteolytic peptides using chemically synthesized isotope-labeled peptides as surrogate internal standards for mass spectrometry.

name: accelerating potential
definition: Electrical potential difference used to impart translational energy to ions.

name: accurate mass
definition: Experimentally determined mass of an ion of known charge.

name: accurate mass tag
definition: Value of the mass of a peptide from a protein that has been chemically or enzymatically cleaved into fragments. The mass is recorded with sufficiently high accuracy and precision that it can be used in identification of the protein.

name: a-ion
definition: Fragment ion containing the peptide \(\ce{N}\)-terminus formed upon dissociation of a peptide ion at the peptide backbone \(\ce{C-C}\) bond.

name: alkyl cation
definition: Even-electron positively charged saturated hydrocarbon ion containing no aromatic groups, a special case of carbenium ions.

name: all-glass heated inlet system
definition: All-glass inlet system for ion sources operating under vacuum that can be heated to about \(\pu{500^{\circ}C}\) and allows low vapor pressure materials to be introduced into the mass spectrometer without breaking vacuum.

name: allyl cation
definition: Even-electron ion formulated as \(\ce{R^{1}R^{2}C=CR^{3}C+R^{4}R^{5}}\) and its resonance forms.

name: ambient ionization
definition: Desorption of molecules and formation of ions outside the mass spectrometer directly from samples in their native environment with no or minimal sample preparation.

name: ambient mass spectrometry
definition: Mass spectrometry analysis performed using an ambient ionization technique.

name: angle resolved mass spectrometry
definition: Technique used to investigate details of the collisional excitation process by studying trends relating scattering angle of the precursor ion, internal energy transferred, and the masses of the ion and its collision partner.

name: anionized molecule
definition: Ion formed by the association of an anion with a molecule, \(\ce{M}\).

name: atmospheric pressure chemical ionization
definition: Chemical ionization of a sample that is a gas or nebulized liquid, using an atmospheric pressure corona discharge or beta emitter such as \(\ce{^{63}Ni}\).

name: atmospheric pressure matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization
definition: Matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization in which the sample target is at atmospheric pressure.

name: atmospheric pressure photoionization
definition: Direct ionization of molecules at atmospheric pressure by electron detachment induced by photons forming \(\ce{M^{+.}}\), or atmospheric pressure chemical ionization in which the reactant ions are generated by photoionization of suitable dopant species and subsequent ion/molecule reactions of their molecular ions.

name: autodetachment
definition: Process whereby a negative ion in a discrete state with energy greater than the detachment threshold loses an electron spontaneously without further interaction with an energy source.

name: auxiliary gas
definition: Gas used in a spray ion source in addition to the nebulizing gas to aid in solvent removal.

name: average mass
definition: Mass of an ion or molecule weighted for its isotopic composition.

name: axial ejection
definition: Ejection of an ion from an ion trap in a direction parallel to the longitudinal axis of the trap.

name: axialization
definition: Technique used in Fourier-transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometers to limit the translational motion of the trapped ions so that they occupy a small volume near the trap center, thus optimizing performance criteria including resolving power.

name: base peak chromatogram
definition: Chromatogram obtained by plotting the signal of the ions represented by the base peak detected in each of a series of mass spectra recorded as a function of retention time.

name: beam mass spectrometer
definition: Mass spectrometer in which an ion beam accelerated from the ion source is transmitted through a m/z analyzer, or analyzers, to the detector.

name: benzyl ion
definition: Even-electron ion \(\ce{C7H7^{+}}\) with the same carbon skeleton as toluene that has lost a hydrogen atom from the methyl side-chain that carries the positive charge.

name: b-ion
definition: Fragment ion containing the peptide \(\ce{N}\)-terminus formed upon dissociation of a peptide ion at the peptide backbone \(\ce{C-N}\) bond.

name: blackbody infrared radiative dissociation
definition: Special case of infrared multiphoton dissociation wherein excitation of the reactant ion is caused by absorption of infrared photons radiating from heated blackbody surroundings, which are usually the walls of a vacuum chamber.

name: Brubaker lens
definition: Additional set of four short, cylindrical electrodes, mounted co-linearly with a transmission quadrupole mass spectrometer that is excited with some fraction of the AC potential but not the DC potential applied to the main quadrupole. The Brubaker lens thus acts as a high-pass filter for ion m/z, but the resulting delay in application of the DC potential component also results in a reduction in defocusing by fringe fields and thus significantly improves overall ion transmission efficiency at a given mass resolution.

name: buffer gas
definition: Inert gas used for collisional reduction of the internal or translational energy of ions, such as in ion traps.

name: centroid acquisition
definition: Procedure of recording mass spectra in which an automated computer-based system detects peaks, calculates the centroid based on the average m/z value weighted by the intensity, and assigns m/z values based on a calibration file. Only the centroid m/z value and the peak magnitude are stored.

name: charged residue model
definition: Theoretical model for production of highly charged macromolecules by electrospray ionization in which the excess charges on electrosprayed droplets are transferred to and remain on molecules enclosed within the droplets after solvent evaporation.

name: charge inversion reaction
definition: Reaction of an ion with a neutral, surface, or ion of opposite polarity, in which the charge on the product ion is reversed in sign with respect to the reactant ion.

name: charge-mediated fragmentation
definition: Fragmentation of an ion in which the cleavage of one of its bonds is induced by the charge site. The cleaved bond is adjacent to the apparent charge site, and its cleavage involves movement of the electron pair forming that bond to the original charge site and thus migration of the charge to the released fragment.

name: charge remote fragmentation
definition: Fragmentation of an ion in which the cleaved bond is isolated from the apparent charge site by a distance of several bond lengths.

name: charge site derivatization
definition: Chemical derivatization of molecules to introduce a fixed charge site, thus improving ionization efficiency by electrospray ionization or matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization and directing subsequent ion fragmentation in a manner that facilitates structure identification.

name: c-ion
definition: Fragment ion containing the peptide \(\ce{N}\)-terminus formed upon dissociation of a peptide ion at the peptide backbone \(\ce{N-C}\) bond.

name: coaxial reflectron
definition: Reflectron that is arranged such that its main axis is coaxial with the ion source and first stage of the time-of-flight analyzer.

name: collector slit
definition: Slit installed in a magnetic sector mass spectrometer to allow only those m/z separated ions with a specific m/z into the detector system.

name: collisional focusing
definition: Effect where collisions with a buffer gas in a radio-frequency ion trap or transmission quadrupole causes ions to lose translational energy and concentrate at the center of the trap or axis of the linear quadrupole. The effect increases with gas pressure up to a point where ion scattering becomes the dominant process.

name: collision cell
definition: Chamber in the ion path between m/z separation elements, or between ion source acceleration region and the first analyzer, in tandem mass spectrometry in space configurations.

name: collision gas
definition: Inert gas used for collisional excitation or a reactive gas used for ion/molecule reactions.

name: collision quadrupole
definition: Transmission quadrupole to which an oscillating radio frequency potential is applied so as to focus a beam of ions through a collision gas or buffer gas with no m/z separation other than low m/z cut-off.

name: collision reaction cell
definition: Collision cell for removal of interfering ions by ion/neutral reactions in inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry.

name: concentric nebulizer
definition: Pneumatic nebulizer in which the liquid flows through a central capillary and dispersion gas flows through a surrounding outer tube.

name: consecutive reaction monitoring
definition: Multiple-stage mass spectrometry experiment with three or more stages of m/z separation in which products of sequential fragmentation or bimolecular reactions are selected for detection.

name: constant neutral mass gain spectrum
definition: Spectrum formed of all precursor ions that have undergone a selected m/z increase corresponding to the mass of a particular neutral species divided by the charge number of the precursor. The ions detected are the product ions produced by gain of a preselected neutral species mass following ion/molecule reactions of the precursor ions with a reactant gas in a collision cell.
synonyms: fixed neutral gain spectrum|fixed neutral mass gain spectrum

name: constant neutral mass loss spectrum
definition: Spectrum of all precursor ions that have undergone a selected m/z decrement corresponding to the mass of a particular neutral divided by the charge number of the precursor. The ions detected are the product ions produced by loss of a preselected neutral mass following collision-induced dissociation of the precursor ions in a collision cell.
synonyms: fixed neutral loss spectrum|fixed neutral mass loss spectrum

name: continuous dynode particle multiplier
definition: Ion-to-electron detector in which the ion strikes the inner surface of a continuous tube device and induces the production of secondary electrons that, in turn, impinge on the inner surfaces of the device to produce more secondary electrons. This avalanche effect produces an increase in the final measured current pulse.

name: continuous-flow fast atom bombardment
definition: Variant of fast atom bombardment in which the mixture of analyte and liquid matrix is continuously supplied to the sample probe tip.

name: continuous-flow matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization
definition: Variant of matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization in which the analyte is dissolved in a liquid matrix that is continuously supplied to the sample probe tip.

name: conversion dynode
definition: Surface that is held at high potential so that ions striking the surface produce secondary charged particles that are subsequently detected.

name: corona discharge
definition: Electric discharge generated in a gas, usually at atmospheric pressure, surrounding a conductor carrying a sufficiently high potential that the electric field around it ionizes the gas so as to form a plasma in the immediate vicinity of the conductor without causing complete electric breakdown or arcing.

name: corona discharge ionization
definition: Formation of ions in a corona discharge.

name: counter-current gas
definition: Stream of inert gas, often heated, that is used in an electrospray or other spray ionization source to aid in the evaporation of solvent from the sprayed particles. The flow of the gas is in the direction opposite to that of the spray.

name: counter electrode
definition: Counter electrode in an electrospray ionization ion source is one of two electrodes between which the high electric potential is applied, the other electrode being the electrospray needle.

name: cross-flow nebulizer
definition: Pneumatic nebulizer in which the dispersion gas flows at an angle, usually \(\pu{90\!^{\circ}}\), with respect to the column of liquid emerging from a capillary.

name: curved field reflectron
definition: Reflectron designed to provide a decelerating field strength that varies with depth of ion penetration and thus with ion translational energy, permitting energy focusing of ions with a range of translational energies such as those formed as product ions from post-source decay of metastable ions.

name: cyclotron motion
definition: Circular motion of a charged particle moving perpendicularly to the direction of a magnetic field that results from the Lorentz force.

name: Daly detector
definition: Detector consisting of an off-axis conversion dynode, scintillator, and photomultiplier. The dynode at high potential emits secondary electrons when ions impinge on the surface. The secondary electrons are accelerated onto the scintillator that produces light that is then detected by the photomultiplier detector, which can be outside the vacuum system.

name: data-dependent acquisition
definition: Mode of data collection in tandem mass spectrometry in which a fixed number of precursor ions whose m/z values were recorded in a survey scan are selected using predetermined rules and are subjected to a second stage of mass selection in an MS/MS analysis.

name: deconvoluted mass spectrum
definition: Mass spectrum processed with an algorithm designed to extract a desired signal or signals from raw experimental data in which the desired signals have been complicated (convolved) by some interferences or in some other way.

name: delayed extraction
definition: Application of the accelerating voltage pulse after a time delay in desorption ionization from a surface.

name: deprotonated molecule
definition: Ion formed by the removal of a proton from a molecule \(\ce{M}\) to produce an anion represented as \(\ce{[M - H]^{-}}\).

name: desorption chemical ionization
definition: Formation of gas-phase ions by chemical ionization of gaseous molecules produced by the rapid heating and desorption of a solid or low vapour pressure liquid.

name: desorption ionization
definition: Formation of gas phase ions from a solid or liquid sample surface upon activation by heat, strong electric field, particles, droplets, or photon bombardment.

name: desorption ionization on silicon
definition: Soft ionization alternative to matrix-assisted desorption/ionization involving laser desorption ionization of a sample deposited on a porous silicon surface.

name: diagnostic ion
definition: Product ion whose formation reveals structural or compositional information about its precursor ion.

name: dielectric barrier discharge ionization
definition: Atmospheric pressure chemical ionization in which the low-temperature plasma is not generated by a corona discharge but by a device consisting of two electrodes with at least one dielectric layer that separates the electrode from the plasma.

name: d-ion
definition: High-energy fragment ion of a protonated peptide, formally equivalent to a fragment ion formed by homolytic cleavage of a peptide \(\ce{C-N}\) bond together with the part of the \(\ce{C}\)-terminal side-chain starting at the \(\ce{\upgamma\mbox{-}carbon}\) (if any).

name: direct exposure probe
definition: Device based on a modification of a direct insertion probe for exposing an involatile sample directly to the electron beam (in an electron ionization source) or to a chemical ionization plasma as in desorption chemical ionization.

name: direct infusion
definition: Method of liquid sample introduction in which the sample is continuously flowed into a mass spectrometer ion source.

name: direct insertion probe
definition: Device for introducing a single sample of a solid or liquid, usually contained in a quartz or other nonreactive sample holder, into a mass spectrometer ion source.

name: direct liquid introduction
definition: Direct delivery of a liquid sample at a low solvent flow rate into the chemical ionization ion source of a mass spectrometer. The solvent vapour can act as the reagent gas.

name: discrete dynode particle multiplier
definition: Ion-to-electron detector in which the ion strikes the surface of an electrode and induces the production of secondary electrons. In turn, these impinge in sequence on dynodes at a more positive electric potential to produce more secondary electrons. This avalanche effect produces an amplification of several orders of magnitude in the final measured current pulse.

name: dissociative electron capture
definition: Ionization mechanism in which capture of a low-energy electron by a molecule leads directly to a dissociative state of the nascent anion, an example of dissociative ionization.

name: drift tube
definition: Cylindrical chamber containing a buffer gas. Ions introduced at one end are caused to move to the other end by either a flow of the buffer gas or by a uniform longitudinal electric field.

name: drying gas
definition: Inert gas that is used to promote the removal of solvent from aerosol particles in spray ionization.

name: dynamic exclusion
definition: Software method used to minimize repeat selections of identical precursor ions for collision-induced dissociation in replicate chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry analyses of complex mixtures.

name: einzel lens
definition: Three-element charged particle lens in which the first and third elements are maintained at the same electric potential. Such a lens produces focusing without changing the translational energy of the particle.

name: electrohydrodynamic ionization
definition: Ionization process that produces charged droplets and gas-phase ions from a liquid under vacuum with the application of an electric field.

name: electron capture dissociation
definition: Process in which multiply protonated molecules interact with low-energy electrons followed by fragmentation. The capture of an electron by the even-electron cation \(\ce{[M + nH]^{n+}}\) liberates energy and reduces its charge state, thus producing the corresponding \(\ce{[M + nH]^{(n - 1)+.}}\) odd-electron ion, which readily fragments.

name: electron capture ionization
definition: Ionization of a gas-phase atom or molecule by attachment of a free electron to form molecular ions of the \(\ce{M^{-.}}\) type.

name: electrospray needle
definition: Narrow bore tube from which highly charged droplets are emitted in electrospray ionization.

name: electrostatic energy analyser
definition: Device consisting of pairs of parallel conducting plates, concentric cylinders, or concentric spheres that separate charged particles according to their ratio of translational energy to charge by means of a potential difference applied between the pair.

name: even-electron rule
definition: Rule that states that even-electron ions tend to form even-electron fragment ions whereas odd-electron ions tend to dissociate to form either odd- or even-electron ions.

name: exact mass
definition: Calculated mass of an ion or molecule with specified isotopic composition.

name: extracted ion chromatogram
definition: Chromatogram created by plotting the intensity of the signal observed at a chosen m/z value or set of values in a series of mass spectra recorded as a function of retention time.

name: extracted ion electropherogram
definition: Electropherogram created by plotting the intensity of the signal observed at a chosen m/z value or set of values in a series of mass spectra recorded as a function of electrophoresis time.

name: extracted ion profile
definition: Any plot of signal intensity observed at a chosen m/z value or set of values in a series of mass spectra recorded as a function of time, including extracted ion chromatogram, extracted ion electropherogram, or from flow injection analysis or any other time-dependent sampling.

name: fast ion bombardment
definition: Ionization of any species by the interaction of a focused beam of ions, with a translational energy of several thousand \(\pu{eV}\), with a solid or liquid sample.

name: field-free region
definition: Section of a mass spectrometer in which there are no electric or magnetic fields.

name: first stability region
definition: Stability region of a Mathieu stability diagram closest to the origin.

name: fixed precursor ion spectrum
definition: Spectrum obtained when data are acquired that determine the m/z values of product ions produced by the reaction of a selected precursor ion with a user-specified m/z value.

name: flow injection mass spectrometry
definition: Method of flow injection analysis in which an aliquot of sample is injected, without chromatographic separation, into a liquid carrier stream for on-line mass spectrometry.

name: focal plane detector
definition: Detector for m/z spatially dispersed ion beams in which all ions simultaneously impinge on the detector plane to produce spatially defined signals.

name: forward geometry
definition: Double-focusing mass spectrometer configuration in which the ion beam traverses the electric sector before the magnetic sector.

name: forward library search
definition: Procedure of comparing a mass spectrum of an unknown compound with a mass spectral library so that the unknown spectrum is compared in turn with the library spectra, considering only the m/z peaks that have intensities greater than a specific threshold in the unknown.

name: Fourier-transform mass spectrometry
definition: Mass spectrometry technique in which m/z values are represented by frequencies of ion motion and mass spectra are generated by Fourier transform mathematical operations from time domain transients produced by image current detection.

name: fringe field
definition: Electric or magnetic field that extends from the edge of an electric sector, magnetic sector, lens, or other ion optics element.

name: gas chromatography-mass spectrometry
definition: Technique by which a mixture is separated into individual components by gas chromatography, followed by detection with a mass spectrometer.

name: glow discharge ionization
definition: Formation of ions from gaseous atoms or molecules or from the vapor of a solid sample at the cathode by applying a potential difference between two electrodes immersed in a low-pressure inert gas environment.

name: gridless reflectron
definition: Reflectron design in which the decelerating/accelerating field is produced without the use of wire-mesh grids.

name: hard ionization
definition: Formation of gas-phase ions accompanied by extensive fragmentation.

name: high-field asymmetric waveform ion mobility spectrometry
definition: Separation of ions at atmospheric pressure between two electrodes due to simultaneous application of a high potential asymmetric waveform, whereby ions migrate towards one of the two electrodes depending on the ratio of the high- to low-field mobility of the ion. A variable compensating DC potential is used to selectively transmit ions of interest.

name: hybrid mass spectrometer
definition: Mass spectrometer that combines m/z analyzers of different types to perform tandem mass spectrometry or higher-order \({\rm{MS}}^{n}\) experiment.

name: hydrogen/deuterium exchange
definition: Exchange of hydrogen atoms with deuterium atoms in a chemical species in solution prior to introduction into a mass spectrometer, or by ion/molecule reaction with a neutral gas inside a mass spectrometer.

name: hydrogen shifts
definition: Sigmatropic reactions of ions in which the \(\ce{\upsigma\mbox{-}bonds}\) broken and formed involve hydrogen atoms, and are subject to the Woodward–Hofmann rules resulting from orbital symmetry considerations.

name: hyphenated mass spectrometry technique
definition: Analytical technique in which mass spectrometry is interfaced with a pretreatment step, most often chromatographic separation but many other combinations are possible.

name: image current detection
definition: Method of ion detection by measuring the current that results from the image charge induced by a coherent motion of ions passing near a conductor.

name: imaging mass spectrometry
definition: Procedure used to form chemically selective images of an object based on the mass spectrometric detection of ions desorbed from its surface.

name: iminium ion
definition: Cation with the structure \(\ce{R2C=N^{+}R2}\).

name: infrared multiphoton dissociation
definition: Dissociation of a reactant ion as a result of the absorption of multiple infrared photons.

name: in-source collision-induced dissociation
definition: Dissociation of an ion as a result of collisional excitation during ion transfer from an atmospheric pressure ion source to the vacuum chamber of the mass spectrometer.

name: internal fragment
definition: Fragment ion of a peptide ion precursor formed by a double backbone cleavage that contains neither the original \(\ce{C}\)- or \(\ce{N}\)-terminal residues. Typically a combination of b- and y-type cleavages or occasionally an a- and y-type combination.

name: ion desolvation
definition: Removal of solvent molecules clustered around a gas-phase ion by means of heating and/or collisions with gas molecules.

name: ion enhancement
definition: Phenomenon in which the ionization efficiency of a compound is increased by the presence of another compound.

name: ion evaporation model
definition: Mechanism for production of gas-phase ions from highly charged fine liquid droplets as in electrospray ionization that involves direct ejection of the ions from the droplet surface.

name: ion funnel
definition: Series of stacked ring electrodes with progressively decreasing inner diameter to which a combined radio frequency and fixed potential is applied. The resulting field focuses ions travelling along the central axis.

name: ion gate
definition: Set of plates or grid of wires in an ion mobility spectrometer, time-of-flight mass spectrometer, or other mass spectrometer that is used to apply a pulsed electric field with the purpose of selectively deflecting charged particles.

name: ion/ion reaction
definition: Reaction between two ions, generally of opposite polarity.

name: ion mobility spectrometry
definition: Separation of ions according to their velocity through a buffer gas under the influence of an electric field.

name: ion/neutral complex
definition: Weakly bound species formed from an ion and neutral.

name: ion optics
definition: Devices designed to control the formation, focusing, and deflection of charged particle beams in a vacuum under the influence of electric and magnetic fields.

name: ion suppression
definition: Phenomenon in which the ionization efficiency of a species is lowered by the presence of a different species.

name: ion-to-photon detector
definition: Detector in which ions strike a conversion dynode to produce electrons that in turn strike a phosphor and the resulting photons are detected by a photomultiplier.

name: ion trap
definition: Device for spatially confining ions using electric and magnetic fields alone or in combination.

name: isobaric tag for relative and absolute quantitation
definition: Chemical labeling reagents used for relative or absolute quantitation in proteomics, based on covalent labeling of the \(\ce{N}\)-terminus and side-chain amines of peptides from protein digestions with tags of varying mass.

name: isotope cluster
definition: Group of peaks representing ions of the same elemental composition, but different isotopic compositions.

name: isotope coded affinity tag
definition: Chemical labeling reagents used for relative quantitation in proteomics, consisting of a reactive group capable of labeling a defined amino acid side-chain, an isotopically coded linker, and a tag for the affinity isolation of labeled proteins and peptides.

name: isotope dilution mass spectrometry
definition: Quantitative mass spectrometry technique in which an isotopically enriched compound is used as a surrogate internal standard.

name: isotope ratio
definition: Ratio of the number of atoms of one isotope to the number of atoms of another isotope of the same chemical element in the same system.

name: isotope ratio mass spectrometry
definition: Measurement and study of the relative abundances of the different isotopes of an element in a material using a mass spectrometer.

name: isotopolog ions
definition: Ions that differ only in the isotopic composition of one or more of the constituent atoms.

name: isotopomeric ion
definition: Isomeric ions having the same numbers of each isotopic atom but differing in their positions within the ion.

name: jet separator
definition: Gas chromatograph-to-mass spectrometer interface where the gas chromatography effluent expands into a lower-pressure region and then through a downstream orifice. The low mass carrier gas molecules diffuse from the jet axis, leaving the sample stream enriched in the heavier analyte molecules.

name: kinetic energy release
definition: Translational energy of fragments resulting from dissociation of a metastable ion measured relative to the center-of-mass.

name: kinetic energy release distribution
definition: Distribution of values of translational energies in the center-of-mass reference for an ensemble of metastable ions undergoing a specific dissociation reaction.

name: kinetic shift
definition: Excess energy above the thermochemical threshold required to observe dissociation of a precursor ion within the timeframe of a particular mass spectrometry experiment.

name: Kingdon trap
definition: Ion trapping device that consists of an outer barrel-like electrode and a coaxial inner spindle-like electrode that form an electrostatic field with a quadro-logarithmic potential distribution.

name: label-free quantitation
definition: Method for determining the concentration of proteins through a combination of protein digestion and liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) without relying on stable isotope labeling. Protein quantification is achieved by measuring the signal intensity of peptide ions corresponding to a protein or by counting and comparing the number of fragment mass spectra identifying peptides of a given protein.

name: laser desorption
definition: Formation of gas-phase species from a solid or liquid sample surface upon activation using a short pulse of photons from a laser.

name: laser desorption ionization
definition: Formation of gas-phase ions by the interaction of a laser with a solid or liquid material.

name: laser microprobe mass spectrometry
definition: Laser desorption ionization mass spectrometry, particularly emphasizing spatially resolved composition information.

name: linear ion trap
definition: Two-dimensional Paul ion trap in which ions are confined in the axial dimension by means of a static electric potential.

name: liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry
definition: Technique by which a mixture of analytes is separated into individual components by liquid chromatography (typically high-performance liquid chromatography), followed by detection with a mass spectrometer.

name: liquid ion evaporation
definition: Spray ionization interface in which droplets are dispersed from a pneumatic nebulizer toward a high potential electrode that produces a static charge on the droplets leading to ion formation after solvent evaporation.

name: liquid junction interface
definition: Means of coupling capillary electrophoresis to a mass spectrometer in which a liquid reservoir surrounds the separation capillary and transfer capillary to the mass spectrometer and provides electric contact for the capillary electrophoresis.

name: liquid secondary ionization
definition: Ionization of any species by the interaction of a focused beam of ions or atoms with a sample that is dissolved in a solvent matrix.

name: liquid sheath
definition: Flow of make-up liquid in a sheath flow interface.

name: lock mass
definition: Mass of an ion of known m/z value, derived from a suitable standard compound introduced into an ion source together with the sample to be analyzed, which permits real-time recalibration by correction of m/z shifts arising from instrumental drift.

name: low-energy collision-induced dissociation
definition: Collision-induced dissociation process wherein the precursor ion has laboratory-frame translational energy lower than a given value, often taken to be \(\pu{1 keV}\).

name: magnetic sector
definition: Device that produces a magnetic field perpendicular to a charged particle beam that deflects the beam to an extent that is proportional to the ratio of particle momentum and charge.

name: magnetron motion
definition: Slow rotation of the center of cyclotron motion around the central axis of a Penning ion trap that results from a drift of the cyclotron centre along the electric equipotential lines perpendicular to the magnetic field direction.

name: make-up liquid
definition: Solvent that is mixed with the sample flow in a liquid introduction mass spectrometry interface in order to adjust the flow rate or solvent characteristics of the system, for example, to promote ionization efficiency.

name: mass-analyzed ion kinetic energy spectrometry
definition: Procedure by which translational energy spectra are obtained from a sector mass spectrometer that incorporates at least one magnetic sector plus one electric sector in reverse geometry (a magnetic sector followed by an electric sector).

name: mass calibration
definition: Means of determining m/z values of ions from experimentally detected signals using a theoretical or empirical relational equation.

name: mass defect
