definition: Difference between the nominal mass and the monoisotopic mass of an atom, molecule, or ion.

name: mass discrimination
definition: Differences in overall detection sensitivities for ions of different m/z values in a mass spectrum, caused by variations in ionization efficiency, transmission efficiency through the interface between the ion source and the analyzer vacuum system, analyzer, and detector response.

name: mass gate
definition: Ion gate used to transmit ions in a given m/z range.

name: mass limit
definition: Value of m/z above or below which ions cannot be detected in a mass spectrometer.

name: mass selective axial ejection
definition: Use of mass selective instability to eject ions of selected m/z values from an ion trap along the trap axis.

name: mass selective instability
definition: Unstable trajectories in an ion trap for ions within a particular range of m/z values caused by an appropriate combination of oscillating electric fields.

name: mass spectral library
definition: Collection of mass spectra of different compounds, usually represented as arrays of signal intensity vs. the m/z values.

name: mass spectrometry/mass spectrometry
definition: Acquisition and study of the spectra of the product ions or precursor ions of m/z selected ions, or of precursor ions of a selected neutral mass loss.

name: Mathieu stability diagram
definition: Graphical representation expressed in terms of dimensionless reduced coordinates that describes the stability or instability of charged particle motion in a transmission quadrupole mass spectrometer or Paul ion trap, based on an appropriate form of the Mathieu differential equation.

name: membrane introduction mass spectrometry
definition: Mass spectrometry measurement that uses a semi-permeable membrane separator that permits the passage of analytes directly from solutions or ambient air to the mass spectrometer ion source.
synonyms: MIMS|membrane inlet mass spectrometry|membrane interface mass spectrometry

name: membrane separator
definition: GC-MS interface with a polymer membrane that selectively passes analyte molecules in preference to the carrier gas thereby enriching the analyte in the gas stream.

name: microchannel plate
definition: Thin plate that contains a closely spaced array of channels each of which acts as a continuous dynode particle multiplier. A fast charged or neutral particle, or a photon, that strikes the plate causes a cascade of secondary electrons that ultimately exits the opposite side of the plate.

name: microelectrospray
definition: Electrospray ionization at a low solvent flow rate, typically several microliters per minute (\(\pu{\upmu L min-1}\)) or lower, where a pump is used to provide the sample flow.

name: molecular beam mass spectrometry
definition: Mass spectrometry measurement in which the sample is introduced into the ion source of the mass spectrometer as a collimated beam of molecules with a narrow velocity distribution.

name: molecular effusion separator
definition: GC-MS interface that subjects the GC effluent to effusive flow through a porous glass tube. The lighter carrier gas passes out of the tube, leaving the gas within the tube enriched in analyte.

name: momentum separator
definition: Mass spectrometer interface to inlets including chromatography and spray-based ion sources that enriches the sample by selecting the central part of the effluent or spray using an orifice or skimmer. Particles with a higher forward momentum diverge less from the spray axis for a given radial momentum.

name: monodisperse aerosol generating interface for chromatography
definition: Particle beam interface that incorporates a monodisperse aerosol generator.

name: monoisotopic mass
definition: Exact mass of an ion or molecule calculated using the mass of the most abundant isotope of each element.

name: moving belt interface
definition: Liquid sample mass spectrometer interface that uses two or more pulleys and a continuous loop of material. Samples are sprayed or deposited from solution onto the belt where they are transported into the vacuum system for vaporization or desorption and ionization.

name: MS/MS spectrum
definition: Mass spectrum obtained using tandem mass spectrometry.

name: MSn
definition: Symbol for multiple-stage mass spectrometry experiments designed to record product ion spectra where \(n\) is the number of product ion stages (nth-generation product ions).

name: multicollector mass spectrometer
definition: Mass spectrograph based on a double-focusing magnetic analyzer that spatially disperses ions of different m/z values on to an array of Faraday cup detectors, generally used with inductively coupled plasma ion sources for isotopic composition measurements.

name: multiple reaction monitoring
definition: Application of selected reaction monitoring to multiple product ions from one or more precursor ions.

name: multiple-stage mass spectrometry
definition: Multiple stages of precursor ion m/z selection followed by product ion detection for successive nth-generation product ions.

name: nanoelectrospray
definition: Electrospray ionization at a very low solvent flow rate, typically hundreds of nanoliters per minute of sample solution or lower, often without the use of an external solvent delivery system.

name: negative ion chemical ionization
definition: Chemical ionization that results in the formation of negative ions.

name: neutralization-reionization mass spectrometry
definition: Procedure by which neutral species are formed from m/z selected ions by charge transfer to a collision gas or by dissociation. The neutral species are separated from the remaining ions and ionized through collisions with a second gas.

name: neutral loss
definition: Loss of an uncharged species from an ion during dissociation.

name: neutral loss scan
definition: Scan used to generate a constant neutral loss spectrum.

name: nitrogen rule
definition: Rule stating that a neutral organic molecule containing one or more atoms of the elements \(\ce{C}\), \(\ce{H}\), \(\ce{O}\), \(\ce{N}\), \(\ce{S}\), \(\ce{P}\), or any halogen has an odd nominal mass if it contains an odd number of nitrogen atoms.

name: nozzle-skimmer dissociation
definition: Collisionally activated dissociation that is caused by collisions in the region between the nozzle and skimmer of an atmospheric pressure ionization source such as electrospray or atmospheric pressure chemical ionization.

name: nozzle-skimmer voltage
definition: Electric potential difference applied between the electrospray needle and the skimmer, which is typically held at the same potential as the counter electrode.

name: nth-generation product ion
definition: Serial product ions from dissociation or bimolecular reaction of selected precursor ions where \(n\) refers to the number of stages of dissociation or bimolecular reaction in a series of consecutive reactions that involve successive product ions.

name: nth-generation product ion spectrum
definition: Mass spectrum recorded from any mass spectrometer in which the appropriate scan function can be set to record the appropriate generation product ion or ions of m/z selected precursor ions.

name: orthogonal electrospray
definition: Configuration for electrospray ionization in which the axis of the spray is at a right angle to the axis of the sampling cone.

name: orthogonal extraction
definition: Pulsed acceleration of ions perpendicular to their original direction of travel into a mass spectrometer, typically time-of-flight.

name: partial isotopic scrambling
definition: Partial random mixing of isotopes among specified atom positions in an ion or neutral species.

name: particle beam interface
definition: Method for coupling liquid chromatography to mass spectrometry in which the effluent is passed through a heated capillary to form an expanding jet of vapour and aerosol particles. After passing through a skimmer that acts as a momentum separator, the beam impinges on a heated surface to form ions through chemical ionization at the surface or ionization of the resulting vapour in a chemical ionization or electron ionization source.

name: Paul ion trap
definition: Ion trapping device that depends on the application of radio frequency potentials between a ring electrode and two end-cap electrodes to confine the ion motion to a cyclic path described by an appropriate form of the Mathieu equation. The choice of these potentials determines the m/z value below which ions are not trapped.
synonyms: quadrupole ion storage trap|quadrupole ion trap

name: peak matching
definition: Procedure for measuring the accurate mass of an ion using scanning mass spectrometers, in which the peak corresponding to the unknown ion and that for a reference ion of known m/z are displayed alternately and caused to overlap by adjusting appropriate electric fields.

name: peak parking
definition: Method used to extend the amount of time available for mass spectrometric analysis of the components in a narrow chromatographic peak. The eluent flow rate is reduced to an ultra-low level at the leading edge of the peak and held at this low flow rate for the duration of compound elution, thus enabling collection of sufficient data for reliable statistical analysis.

name: peak stripping
definition: Data analysis technique used in elemental mass spectrometry to correct the intensity of an unresolved multiplet peak monitored for a specific element for contributions from a multi-isotopic contaminant. The correction is calculated from the measured intensity of a different isotopic peak of the contaminant and the known natural isotopic abundance ratio.

name: Penning ionization
definition: Ionization via electron removal that occurs through the energy transfer from a neutral species \(\ce{N}\) internally excited to a metastable state (such as a high Rydberg state) to a neutral species \(\ce{M}\) with lower ionization energy, as represented by the following reaction: \(\ce{N^{\ast} + M -> N + M^{+.} + \textit{e}^{-}}\).

name: Penning ion trap
definition: Ion trapping device using a static magnetic field and a static electric potential well. The magnetic field confines the ion motion to circular orbits around the magnetic force line direction, which aligns with the direction of the trap axis, whereas the electric potential well confines the ion motion axially.

name: peptide mass fingerprinting
definition: Method for protein analysis where an unknown protein is chemically or enzymatically cleaved into peptide fragments whose masses are determined by mass spectrometry. The peptide masses are compared to peptide masses calculated for known proteins in a database and analyzed statistically to determine the best match.

name: peptide sequence tag
definition: Sequence of peptide ion fragment masses that can be used to aid in the identification of the amino acid sequence.

name: photodissociation
definition: Process wherein the reactant ion or molecule is dissociated as a result of absorption of one or more photons.

name: photographic plate recording
definition: Recording of ion currents by allowing them to strike a photographic plate, which is subsequently developed.

name: $\boldsymbol{\pi}$/n rad magnetic sector
definition: Arrangement in which an ion beam is deflected magnetically through \(\pi/n\ \rm{rad}\), where \(n \gt 1\).

name: pneumatically assisted electrospray ionization
definition: Electrospray ionization in which the nebulization of the liquid stream is assisted by a concentric stream of gas.

name: point detector
definition: Detector in which the ion beam is focused onto a small area, for example, defined by a collector slit, rather than dispersed by m/z spatially across a focal plane.

name: post-acceleration detector
definition: Detector in which a high potential is applied after m/z separation to accelerate the ions and produce an improved signal.

name: post-source decay
definition: Technique specific to reflectron time-of-flight mass spectrometers where product ions of metastable transitions or collision-induced dissociations generated in the flight tube prior to entering the reflectron are separated according to m/z to yield product ion spectra.

name: precursor ion spectrum
definition: Mass spectrum in which the appropriate m/z separation function records the precursor ions of selected product ions or specified neutral loss.

name: pre-ionization state
definition: Electronic state capable of undergoing autoionization.

name: probability-based matching
definition: Automated system for computer examination of the mass spectrum of an unknown mixture for the presence of a specific compound for which a standard spectrum is available in a library. The probability that the compound is present is given by a confidence index \(K\) such that \(2^{K}\) is the average number of randomly selected compounds whose mass spectra would have to be examined to find data which match the target spectrum to the same degree as does the unknown.

name: product ion analysis
definition: Process whereby a precursor ion of a particular m/z is selected by m/z, fragmentation is induced, and the mass spectrum of the resulting product ions is recorded.

name: product ion spectrum
definition: Mass spectrum in which the appropriate m/z separation analysis function is set to record the product ions of a selected precursor ion selected by m/z.

name: profile mode
definition: Method for acquiring a mass spectrum where each peak is displayed as a curve, with the data points defining the curve corresponding to the signal intensities at each particular m/z value.

name: proton-bound dimer
definition: Dimeric ion consisting of two similar or dissimilar molecules bound together by hydrogen bonding with a shared proton.

name: pyrolysis mass spectrometry
definition: Mass spectrometry technique in which the sample is heated to the point of decomposition and the gas-phase decomposition products are characterized by mass spectrometry.

name: quadratic field reflectron
definition: Reflectron in which the electric field varies with the square of the distance from the entrance and compensates for kinetic energy spread to all orders.

name: quadrupolar axialization
definition: Technique for axialization in Fourier transform-ion cyclotron resonance-mass spectrometers in which magnetron motion is converted into cyclotron motion by subjecting the trapped ions to a quadrupolar excitation field while they undergo collisions.

name: quadrupole time-of-flight
definition: Hybrid mass spectrometer consisting of a transmission quadrupole mass spectrometer coupled to an orthogonal acceleration time-of-flight mass spectrometer. A collision quadrupole is typically inserted between the two mass spectrometers.

name: quantitation by concatenated tryptic peptides
definition: Method for absolute quantitation of a protein or proteins in a multiplexed fashion using isotope-labeled peptides as surrogate internal standards. The labeled peptides are produced by synthesizing a gene coding for all desired peptides, expressing this gene in E. coli culture containing appropriately labeled substrate, and digesting with trypsin the expressed protein composed of the desired concatenated peptides.

name: quasi-equilibrium theory
definition: Statistical theory of unimolecular reaction rates (isomerization or fragmentation) of molecular species that assumes that reaction occurs from the ground electronic state of the reactant regardless of its mode of formation, at a rate determined by the free statistical redistribution of internal energy into those vibrational and rotational modes that must be activated sufficiently to reach the appropriate transition state for the specified reaction to occur.

name: radial ejection
definition: Ejection of an ion from an ion trap in a direction perpendicular to the longitudinal axis of the trap.

name: Rayleigh limit
definition: Limiting droplet size at which self-fragmentation will occur for charged droplets generated in electrospray or other ionization processes. Self-fragmentation occurs when the electrostatic repulsion force generated by the excess charge exceeds the surface tension that maintains the integrity of the droplet.

name: reagent gas
definition: Gas that reacts with ions to produce product ions through ion/molecule reactions; for example, a gas such as methane, ammonia, or isobutane used in chemical ionization to create reagent ions or a gas used in ion traps or collision cells to perform gas-phase ion/molecule reactions.

name: reagent ion
definition: Ion that reacts with a neutral to produce an ionized form of such species through an ion/molecule reaction, for example, as in chemical ionization.

name: recombination energy
definition: Energy released when an electron is added to an ionized molecule or atom.

name: rectilinear ion trap
definition: Quadrupole ion trap whose electrodes form a rectilinear polygon, the simplest form of which consists of two pairs of rectangular electrodes supplied with radio frequency (RF) potentials and a pair of electrodes to which a DC potential is applied. Slits or apertures in the electrodes allow injection and ejection of charged particles.

name: reference ion
definition: Stable ion whose structure or elemental formula is known with certainty. These ions are formed by direct ionization of a molecule of known structure or elemental formula, and are used to verify by comparison the structure or thermochemistry of an unknown ion or to calibrate the m/z scale of the mass spectrometer.

name: relative isotope-ratio difference
definition: Measure of an isotope ratio in a sample of interest relative to a reference defined by the relation \[\delta = (R_{\rm{sample}} - R_{\rm{standard}})/R_{\rm{standard}}\] where \(R\) is the isotope ratio of the element.
synonyms: delta notation|isotope delta|relative difference of isotope ratios

name: residual gas analyser
definition: Mass spectrometer used to measure the composition and pressure of gases in an evacuated chamber and to test for leaks in pressurized systems.

name: resolution: 10 per cent valley definition
definition: Value of \((m/z)/\Delta(m/z)\) measured for two peaks of equal height in a mass spectrum at m/z and \(m/z \pm \Delta(m/z)\) that are separated by a valley which at its lowest point is \(\pu{10\%}\) of the height of either peak. For peaks of similar height separated by a valley, let the height of the valley at its lowest point be \(\pu{10\%}\) of the lower peak. Then the resolution (\(\pu{10\%}\) valley definition) is \((m/z)/\Delta(m/z)\) and should be given for a number of values of m/z.

name: resolution: peak width definition
definition: For a single peak corresponding to singly charged ions at mass \(m\) in a mass spectrum, the resolution may be expressed as \((m/z)/\Delta(m/z)\), where \(\Delta(m/z)\) is the width of the peak at a height which is a specified fraction of the maximum peak height. It is recommended that one of three values 50, 5, or \(\pu{0.5\%}\) should always be used.

name: resonance-enhanced multiphoton ionization
definition: Multiphoton ionization in which the ionization cross section is significantly enhanced because the energy of the incident photons is resonant with an intermediate excited state of the neutral.

name: resonance ion ejection
definition: Mode of ion ejection in an ion trap that relies on an auxiliary radio frequency potential that is applied to the end-cap or trapping electrodes. The potential is tuned to the classical oscillation frequency of a particular ion to eject it.

name: retro Diels–Alder reaction
definition: Ion fragmentation mechanism in which the molecular ion \(\ce{M^{+.}}\) of a cyclic alkene fragments to form a neutral diene and an alkene radical cation or a diene radical cation and an alkene. The reaction is the reverse of the Diels–Alder reaction of organic synthesis.

name: reverse geometry
definition: Double-focusing mass spectrometer configuration in which the ion beam traverses the magnetic sector prior to the electric sector.

name: reverse library search
definition: Process of comparing a subset of the peaks in the mass spectrum of an unknown compound with peaks present in the library mass spectrum. Any peaks in the mass spectrum of the unknown compound that are not in the library spectrum are disregarded.

name: RF-only quadrupole
definition: Transmission quadrupole device in which a sinusoidal radio frequency (RF) potential is applied between the connected pairs of opposite rod electrodes in a linear quadrupole, providing a transmission device for all ions with m/z values above a cut-off value.

name: ring and double bond equivalent
definition: Conventional measure of the degree of unsaturation of an organic molecule given by \(X - Y/2 + Z/2 + 1\) where \(X\) is the number of carbon atoms, \(Y\) is the number of hydrogen or halogen atoms and \(Z\) is the number of nitrogen and phosphorus atoms.

name: saddle field gun
definition: Compact ion and fast atom sources for use when small size and high beam intensity are required, as in fast atom bombardment mass spectrometry. The discharge is produced by electrons oscillating between two cold cathodes in an electric field that possesses a single saddle point. To produce and intensify the plasma the electrons must have long path lengths, achieved by allowing the electrons to have an oscillatory motion in the saddle-shaped electric field between the cathodes separated by the anode.

name: sampling cone
definition: Component of a spray ionization interface that consists of a cone with a small orifice through which the spray passes into a differentially pumped chamber

name: scan cycle time
definition: Time required to obtain a mass spectrum (or other mass spectrometric data quantity) such as in a separation coupled to mass spectrometry.

name: secondary neutral mass spectrometry
definition: Mass spectrometry technique in which neutral species ejected from a sample surface as a result of bombardment by a primary beam of atoms or ions are ionized, most often by photoionization, prior to analysis.

name: sector mass spectrometer
definition: Mass spectrometer consisting of one or more magnetic sectors for recording a mass spectrum of a monoenergetic beam of ions. Such instruments may also have one or more electric sectors for energy dispersion that can be arranged for velocity-focusing by compensating for dispersion by the magnetic sector if the beam is not truly monoenergetic. Such a combination provides double focusing of ions of the same m/z, i.e., focusing with respect to both direction and speed.

name: selected ion flow tube
definition: Device in which m/z selected ions are entrained in an inert carrier gas and subsequently undergo ion/molecule reactions with molecules introduced into the gas flow.

name: selected reaction monitoring
definition: Data acquired from one or more specific product ions corresponding to m/z selected precursor ions recorded via two or more stages of mass spectrometry.

name: self-chemical ionization
definition: Chemical ionization of an analyte where the reagent ion is an ionized form of the analyte or one of its product ions.

name: sheath flow interface
definition: Capillary electrophoresis to electrospray ionization interface that uses a coaxial flow of make-up liquid that is introduced through a tube that is concentric with the separation capillary.

name: sheath gas
definition: Gas introduced through a tube that is coaxial with the electrospray emitter to pneumatically assist the formation of the sprayed droplets.

name: sheath liquid
definition: Make-up liquid in a sheath flow interface

name: shotgun proteomics
definition: Protein identification using a combination of high-performance liquid chromatography and mass spectrometry in which the proteins in a mixture are digested, usually by a specific enzyme, and the resulting peptides are separated by liquid chromatography and identified by tandem mass spectrometry.

name: skimmer
definition: Cone with a central orifice that intercepts the center of a spray or jet expansion to sample the central portion of the expansion, for example, as in a momentum separator.

name: soft ionization
definition: Formation of gas-phase ions without extensive fragmentation.

name: sonic spray ionization
definition: Process in which both anions and cations are produced at atmospheric pressure from an ionic solution due to a statistically unbalanced charge distribution in the minute droplets formed by the action of a sonic atomizer.

name: space charge effect
definition: Result of mutual repulsion of particles of like charge (ions, electrons, etc.) that can limit the current in a charged-particle beam and can also cause some motion of ions in a beam or packet in addition to that caused by external fields.

name: spectral skewing
definition: Deviation of the peak intensities in a mass spectrum from their expected values that occurs when the relative concentration of the various analytes change during acquisition of the mass spectrum.

name: spray ionization
definition: General term used to describe a range of ionization techniques for analytes in solution that involve dispersing the liquid into fine droplets as a component step.

name: stable isotope ratio analysis of amino acids in cell culture
definition: Proteomics technique that detects differences in protein abundance between cultured cell samples using stable isotopic labeling achieved with labeled amino acids in one cell culture and unlabeled ones in a separate culture.

name: stable isotope standards and capture by anti-peptide antibodies
definition: Method for absolute quantitation of a protein or proteins in a multiplexed fashion using isotope-labeled peptides as surrogate internal standards. The labeled peptides are produced by synthesizing a gene coding for each desired peptide, cell-free transcription, and translation of this gene in a medium containing \(\ce{^{13}C6}\)-labeled lysine, and digesting with trypsin the expressed protein composed of the desired concatenated peptides. For low-abundance proteins the sensitivity is increased by selective enrichment of the target peptides by antibody capture.

name: static field
definition: Electric or magnetic field that does not change in time.

name: Stevenson’s rule
definition: Rule stating that in competing fragmentations the product ion formed from its neutral species counterpart with the lower ionization energy will usually be the more abundant.

name: stored waveform inverse fourier transform
definition: Technique to create excitation waveforms for ions in Fourier transform-ion cyclotron resonance-mass spectrometers or Paul ion traps. An excitation waveform in the time-domain is generated by taking the inverse Fourier transform of an appropriate frequency-domain programmed excitation spectrum, in which the resonance frequencies of ions to be excited are included.

name: supercritical fluid chromatography-mass spectrometry
definition: Combined technique in which a mixture of analytes is separated into solutions of individual components by chromatography that uses a supercritical fluid as mobile phase, followed by the ionization of the separation effluent in the ion source of a mass spectrometer.

name: surface-enhanced laser desorption/ionization
definition: Variant of matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization (MALDI) in which the matrix is replaced by a surface coating of a chromatographic stationary phase designed to selectively retain different subsets of proteins or peptides from a mixture depending on their physico-chemical properties or biochemical affinity characteristics.

name: surface-induced dissociation
definition: Fragmentation that results from the collision of an ion with a surface.

name: surface-induced reaction
definition: Process wherein a reactant ion interacts with a surface to produce either chemically different species or a change in the internal energy of the reactant ion.

name: surrogate internal standard
definition: Compound added in accurately known amounts to a sample to be analyzed for a specified analyte. The surrogate internal standard is chemically similar to the analyte so that losses in the analytical procedure are the same for both and thus the analyte concentration can be determined relative to that of the standard.

name: sustained off-resonance irradiation
definition: Procedure associated with Fourier transform-ion cyclotron resonance-mass spectrometers to facilitate ion/neutral reactions such as low-energy collision-induced dissociation in which a radio-frequency electric field, slightly off-resonance with respect to the cyclotron frequency of the reactant ion, cyclically accelerates and decelerates the reactant ion that is confined in the Penning ion trap. As a consequence, the orbit does not exceed the dimensions of the ion trap but maintains a high average translational energy for an extended time that activates an ion/neutral process.

name: tandem mass spectrometry in space
definition: Tandem mass spectrometry procedure in which product ion spectra are recorded for ion beams in m/z analyzers separated in space. Specific m/z separation functions are designed so that in one section of the instrument ions are selected, dissociated in an intermediate region, and the product ions are then transmitted to another analyzer for m/z separation and data acquisition.

name: tandem mass spectrometry in time
definition: Tandem mass spectrometry procedure in which product ion spectra are recorded in a single m/z analyzer (such as a Paul ion trap, linear ion trap, or Fourier transform-ion cyclotron resonance-mass spectrometer) in discrete steps over time. Ions in a specific m/z range are selected, dissociated, and the product ions analyzed sequentially in time.

name: Taylor cone
definition: Conical shape of the liquid emanating from a capillary under high potential, as in electrospray or other electrohydrodynamic spray processes.

name: thermospray ionization
definition: Spray ionization in which a liquid is flowed through a heated capillary to produce a spray of droplets and solvent vapor. Ions are formed due to the statistical imbalance of charges in the droplets or by a heated filament.

name: thin layer chromatography-mass spectrometry
definition: Technique by which a mixture of analytes is separated into individual components by liquid chromatography, followed by the ionization of the separated species by an ion source of a mass spectrometer.

name: time-lag focusing
definition: Energy focusing of ions formed in the gas phase in a time-of-flight mass spectrometer that is accomplished by introducing a time delay between the formation of the ions and the application of the accelerating potential pulse.

name: tolyl ion
definition: Even-electron \(\ce{C7H7^{+}}\) ion with the same carbon skeleton as toluene that has lost a hydrogen atom from one of the ring carbons that carries the positive charge.

name: toroidal ion trap
definition: Ion trapping device based on the three-dimensional structure formed by rotating the cross-section of a quadrupole ion trap about the edge perpendicular to the plane of the ring electrode. The resulting trapping region is toroidal.

name: total ion current electropherogram
definition: Plot of the total ion current in each of a series of mass spectra that are recorded as a function of electrophoresis time.

name: total ion current profile
definition: Any plot of total ion current in a series of mass spectra recorded as a function of time, including total ion current chromatogram, total ion current electropherogram, flow injection mass spectrometry, or any other time dependent sampling.

name: transmission efficiency
definition: Ratio of the number of ions leaving a region of a mass spectrometer to the number entering that region.

name: transmission quadrupole mass spectrometer
definition: Mass spectrometer that consists of an array of four parallel rod electrodes whose centers form the corners of a square and whose opposing electrode pairs are connected. The electric potential applied between the connected pairs of rods is a superposition of a static potential and a sinusoidal radio frequency potential. The motion of an ion in the \(x\mbox{-}y\) plane perpendicular to the length direction of the rod electrodes is described by the Mathieu equation whose solutions show that ions in a particular m/z range can be transmitted along the \(z\mbox{-}\rm{axis}\).
synonyms: quadrupole mass analyzer|quadrupole mass filter|quadrupole mass spectrometer

name: transport region
definition: Region in a mass spectrometer in which an ion beam is transported from the ion source to the ion optics or from one ion optical element to the next.

name: triple quadrupole mass spectrometer
definition: Tandem mass spectrometer comprising two transmission quadrupole mass spectrometers in series, with a (non-selecting) RF-only quadrupole (or other multipole) between them to act as a collision cell.

name: unimolecular dissociation
definition: Fragmentation reaction in which the molecularity of the reaction system is unity. The dissociation may arise from the extra energy acquired by a metastable ion produced in the ion source or that provided by collisional excitation of a stable ion.

name: unit mass resolution
definition: Mass resolution such that it is possible to clearly distinguish a peak corresponding to a singly charged ion from its neighbors \(\pu{1 u}\) away, usually with no more than \(\pu{5\!-\! 10\%}\) overlap.

name: v-ion
definition: High-energy product ion of a protonated peptide formally equivalent to a y-ion with the ionizing proton on the \(\ce{N}\)-terminus, but with elimination of \(\ce{HR}\) from the \(\ce{N}\)-terminus where \(\ce{R}\) is the side-chain on the \(\ce{C}\)-atom of the \(\ce{N}\)-terminal residue, to give a (\(\ce{H2N^{+}=CH-CO\bond{-}}\)) structure.

name: volumetric internal standard
definition: Compound added in a fixed reproducible amount to a solution to be analyzed by gas chromatography to permit corrections for uncontrolled variations in injected volumes.

name: Wahrhaftig diagram
definition: Diagram illustrating the relative contributions in unimolecular dissociation of an ion, for example, by homolytic cleavage of a single bond, and fragmentation following rearrangement. The diagram is in two parts with a common horizontal axis representing the internal energy of the ion. The vertical axis in one part of the diagram shows the two types of rate constant on a logarithmic scale, and that for the other portion of the diagram indicates the distribution function for internal energy of the ion.

name: Wien filter
definition: Mass spectrometer in which m/z separation is achieved using crossed electric and magnetic fields.

name: w-ion
definition: High-energy product ion of a protonated peptide formally equivalent to a z-ion that has lost the part of the \(\ce{N}\)-terminal side-chain starting at the \(\ce{\upgamma\mbox{-}carbon}\) (if any).

name: x-ion
definition: Fragment ion containing the peptide \(\ce{C}\)-terminus formed upon dissociation of a peptide ion at the peptide backbone \(\ce{C-C}\) bond.

name: y-ion
definition: Fragment ion containing the peptide \(\ce{C}\)-terminus formed upon dissociation of a peptide ion at the peptide backbone \(\ce{C-N}\) bond.

name: z-ion
definition: Fragment ion containing the peptide \(\ce{C}\)-terminus formed upon dissociation of a peptide ion at the peptide backbone \(\ce{N-C}\) bond.

name: ADMET
definition: Acronym referring to the absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity profile or processes for a xenobiotic upon its administration in vivo.

name: allosteric antagonist
definition: Compound that binds to a receptor at a site separate from, but actively coupled to, that of the endogenous agonist to reduce actively receptor signals.

name: alpha-helix
definition: Secondary 3D structure of a protein or peptide containing a right-handed coiled or spiral conformation, in which every backbone \(\ce{N-H}\) group donates a hydrogen bond to the backbone \(\ce{C=O}\) group of the amino acid four residues earlier.

name: analogue
definition: Chemical compound having structural similarity to a reference compound.

name: analogue-based drug discovery
definition: Strategy for drug discovery and/or optimization in which structural modification of an existing drug provides a new drug with improved chemical and/or biological properties.

name: ATP binding cassette protein
definition: Large gene family of transporter proteins that bind ATP and use the energy to transport substrates (e.g., sugars, amino acids, metal ions, peptides, proteins, and a large number of hydrophobic compounds and metabolites) across lipid membranes.

name: attrition rate
definition: Rate of loss of drug candidates during progression through the optimisation and developmental stages while on route to the marketplace.

name: autoinduction
definition: Capacity of a drug to induce enzymes that mediate its own metabolism.

name: back-up compound
definition: Molecule selected as a replacement for the lead drug candidate should this subsequently fail during further preclinical evaluation or in clinical studies.

name: best-in-class
definition: Drug acting on a specific molecular target that provides the best balance between efficacy and adverse effects.

name: beta-barrel
definition: Secondary 3D protein structure containing a large beta-sheet that twists and coils to form a closed structure in which the first-strand hydrogen bonds to the last.

name: beta-sheet
definition: Secondary 3D structure of a protein that takes on a flat, pleated appearance.

name: beta-sheet breaker
definition: Compound that on binding to a protein disrupts beta-sheet formation.

name: biological agent
definition: Biopolymer-based pharmaceutical, such as a protein, applicable to the prevention, treatment, or cure of diseases or injuries to man.

name: blockbuster drug
definition: Drug that generates annual sales of USD 1 billion (\(\$\pu{E9}\)) or more.

name: carcinogen
definition: Agent (chemical, physical, or biological) that is capable of increasing the incidence of malignant neoplasms, thus causing cancer.

name: chemical biology
definition: Application of chemistry to the study of molecular events in biological systems, often using tool compounds.

name: chemical database
definition: Specific electronic repository for storage and retrieval of chemical information.

name: chemical library
definition: Collection of samples (e.g., chemical compounds, natural products, over-expression library of a microbe) available for biological screening. Set of compounds produced through combinatorial chemistry or other means that expands around a single core structure or scaffold.

name: chemical space
definition: Set of all possible stable molecules based on a specific chemical entity that interacts at one or more specific molecular targets.

name: chemogenomics
definition: Systematic screening of chemical libraries of congeneric compounds against members of a target family of proteins.

name: chemokine
definition: Member of a superfamily of proteins with the primary function to control leukocyte activity and trafficking through tissues.

name: co-drug
definition: Two chemically linked synergistic drugs designed to improve the drug delivery properties of one or both drugs.

name: constitutive activity
definition: Receptor or enzymatic function displayed in the absence of an agonist or activator.

name: contract research organisation
definition: Commercial organisation that can be engaged to undertake specifically defined chemical, biological, safety, or clinical studies.

name: covalent drug
definition: Ligand that binds irreversibly to its molecular target through the formation of a new chemical bond.

name: designed multiple ligands
definition: Compounds conceived and synthesised to act on two or more molecular targets.

name: diversity
definition: Unrelatedness of a set of molecules (e.g., building blocks or members of a compound library), as measured by properties such as atom connectivity, physical properties, or computationally generated descriptors.

name: diversity-oriented synthesis
definition: Efficient production of a range of structures and templates with skeletal and stereochemical diversity as opposed to the synthesis of a specific target molecule.

name: drug cocktail
definition: ­(in drug therapy) Administration of two or more distinct pharmacological agents to achieve a combination of their individual effects. Note 1: The combined effect may be additive, synergistic, or designed to reduce side-effects. Note 2: This term is often used synonymously with that of 'drug combination' but is preferred in order to avoid confusion with medications in which different drugs are included in a single formulation. (in drug testing) Administration of two or more distinct compounds to test simultaneously their individual behaviours (e.g., pharmacological effects in high-throughput screens or drug metabolism).

name: drug delivery
definition: Process by which a drug is administered to its intended recipient.

name: drug distribution
definition: Measured amounts of an administered compound in various parts of the organism to which it is given.

name: druggability
definition: Capacity of a molecular target to be modulated in a favourable manner by a small-molecule drug.

name: drug repurposing
definition: Strategy that seeks to discover new applications for an existing drug that were not previously referenced and not currently prescribed or investigated.

name: drug safety
definition: Assessment of the nontolerable biological effects of a drug.

name: dual binding site
definition: Presence of two distinct ligand binding sites on the same molecular target.

name: effective concentration
definition: Concentration of a substance that produces a defined magnitude of response in a given system.

name: effective dose
definition: Dose of a substance that causes a defined magnitude of response in a given system.

name: efflux pump
definition: Transporter protein located in the membrane of cells that utilizes active transport to move a compound from the internal to the external environment.

name: equilibrium solubility
definition: Analytical composition of a mixture or solution that is saturated with one of the components in the designated mixture or solution.

name: fast follower
definition: Compound selected as a rapid successor to a lead drug candidate.

name: fingerprint
definition: Representation of a compound or chemical library by attributes (descriptors) such as atom connectivities, 3D structure, or physical properties.

name: first-in-class
definition: First drug acting on a hitherto unaddressed molecular target to reach the market.

name: follow-on drug
definition: Drug having a similar mechanism of action to an existing drug.

name: fragment
definition: Low-molar-mass ligand (typically smaller than \(\pu{200 Da}\)) that binds to a target with low affinity but high ligand efficiency.

name: fragment-based lead discovery
definition: Screening libraries of low-molar-mass compounds (typically \(\pu{120\!{-}\! 250 Da}\)) using sensitive biophysical techniques capable of detecting weakly binding lead compounds.

name: frequent hitter
definition: Structural feature that regularly results in a positive response in a variety of high-throughput or primary screens.

name: G protein
definition: Member of a family of membrane-associated proteins which on activation by cellular receptors lead to signal transduction.

name: green chemistry
definition: Invention, design, and application of chemical products and processes to reduce or eliminate the use and generation of hazardous substances.

name: hit
definition: Molecule that produces reproducible activity above a defined threshold in a biological assay and whose structural identity has been established.

name: hit expansion
definition: Generation of additional compound sets that contain chemical motifs and scaffolds that have activity in the primary screen.

name: hit-to-lead chemistry
definition: Process by which a proven molecule or series derived from high-throughput screening or primary screens is chemically optimised to a viable lead or series.

name: homology model
definition: Computational representation of a protein built from the 3D structure of a similar protein or proteins using alignment techniques and homology arguments.

name: hydrophobic fragmental constant
definition: Representation of the lipophilicity contribution of a constituent part of a structure to the total lipophilicity.

name: inhibitory concentration at 50%
definition: The concentration of an enzyme inhibitor or receptor antagonist that reduces the enzyme activity or agonist response by \(\pu{50\%}\).

name: inhibition constant
definition: Equilibrium dissociation constant of an enzyme-inhibitor complex: \(K_{\rm{i}} = [\ce{E}][\ce{I}]/[\ce{EI}]\). The equilibrium dissociation constant of a receptor-ligand complex.

name: intrinsic solubility
definition: Equilibrium solubility of the uncharged form of an ionisable compound at a pH where it is fully unionised. \[\ce{HA(s)  HA(aq)} \quad (1)\] \[\ce{HA(aq)  H^{+}(aq) + A^{-}(aq)} \quad (2)\]

name: investigational new drug
definition: Drug not yet approved for general use by the national authority, such as the Food and Drug Administration of the United States of America, but undergoing clinical investigation to assess its safety and efficacy.

name: ionotropic receptor
definition: Transmembrane ion channel that opens or closes in response to the binding of a ligand.

name: kinase
definition: Enzyme that transfers a phosphate group from high-energy donor molecules, such as ATP, to specific target molecules.

name: kinetic solubility
definition: Composition of a solution with respect to a compound when its induced precipitate first appears.

name: lead
definition: Compound (or compound series) that satisfies predefined minimum criteria for further structure and activity optimization.

name: lead validation
definition: Process by which a lead compound is authenticated by the confirmation of its expected pharmacological properties.

name: ligand-based drug design
definition: Method of drug discovery and/or optimization in which the pursuit of new structures and/or structural modifications is based upon one or more ligands known to interact with the molecular target of interest.

name: metabotropic receptor
definition: Receptor that modulates electric potential-gated channels via G-proteins.

name: me-too drug
definition: Term applied to drug analogues that offer no significant advantage over the prototype compound.

name: microRNA
definition: Small single-stranded RNA molecules that play a significant role in the post-transcriptional regulation of gene expression.

name: molecular descriptor
definition: Parameter that characterizes a specific structural or physicochemical aspect of a molecule.

name: molecular target
definition: Protein (e.g., receptor, enzyme, or ion channel), RNA, or DNA that is implicated in a clinical disorder or the propagation of any untoward event.

name: multidrug resistance
definition: Characteristic of cells that confers resistance to the effects of several different classes of drugs.

name: multiparameter optimisation
definition: Drug-likeness penetrability algorithm derived from CLOGP, clogD, molar mass, topological polar surface area, number of hydrogen-bond donors, and \(\pu{p}K_{\rm{a}}\).

name: multitarget-directed ligand
definition: Ligand acting on more than one distinct molecular target. Targets may be of the same or different mechanistic classes.

name: multitarget drug discovery
definition: Deliberate design of compounds that act on more than one molecular target.

name: Murcko assembly
definition: Core scaffold of a molecule that remains after all chain substituents that do not terminate in a ring are removed. Single atoms connected by a double bond are typically also retained.

name: neglected disease
definition: Term used to emphasise an imbalance between therapeutic needs and resource allocation.

name: neutral antagonist
definition: Ligand that blocks the responses of a receptor to both agonists and inverse agonists with the same intensity. It binds to the receptor without evoking any change of conformation or change to the ratio of activated to inactivated conformations.

name: new chemical entity
definition: Drug that contains no active moiety previously approved for use by the national authority, such as the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.

name: new molecular entity
definition: Active ingredient that has never before been approved in any form by the national authority, such as the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.

name: noncompetitive antagonist
definition: Functional antagonist that either binds irreversibly to a receptor or to a site distinct from that of the natural agonist.

name: nuclear hormone receptor
definition: Ligand-activated transcription factor that regulates gene expression by interacting with specific DNA sequences upstream of its target gene(s).

name: obviousness
definition: Term associated with intellectual property wherein the latter’s patentability is assessed relative to the combination of more than one item of 'prior art'.

name: off-target effect
definition: Pharmacological action induced by any molecule at molecular/biological sites distinct from that for which it was designed.

name: orphan disease
definition: Disease for which drug research, development, and marketing is economically unfavourable.

name: orphan drug
definition: Pharmaceutical agent that has been approved specifically to treat a rare and commercially unfavourable medical condition.

name: orphan receptor
definition: Receptor for which an endogenous ligand has yet to be identified.

name: parallel synthesis
definition: Simultaneous preparation of sets of discrete compounds in arrays of physically separate reaction vessels or microcompartments without interchange of intermediates during the assembly process.

name: patentability
definition: Set of criteria that must be satisfied in order to achieve commercial exclusivity for an invention.

name: peptoid
definition: Peptide-like oligomer consisting of repeating \(N\)-substituted glycine units  where \(\ce{R1}\) to \(\ce{R4}\) are typically alkyl or aryl and may be the same or different.

name: P-glycoprotein
definition: ATP-binding cassette transporter responsible for the efflux of small molecules from cells.

name: pharmacogenetics
definition: Study of inherited differences (variation) in drug metabolism and response.

name: pharmacogenomics
definition: General study of all of the many different genes that determine drug behaviour.

name: phase 0 clinical studies
definition: Exploratory first-in-human trials that involve microdosing of drug to allow the assessment of pharmacokinetic parameters with limited drug exposure.

name: phase I clinical studies
definition: Initial introduction of an investigational new drug into humans.

name: phase II clinical studies
definition: Controlled clinical studies conducted in a limited number of individuals to obtain some preliminary data on the effectiveness of an investigational new drug for a particular indication or indications in patients with the disease or condition.

name: phase III clinical studies
definition: Expanded controlled and uncontrolled trials in humans.

name: phase IV clinical studies
definition: Extended post-marketing studies in humans.

name: phenotypic screening
definition: Evaluation of compounds (small molecules, peptides, siRNA, etc.) in cells, tissues, or organisms for their ability to modify the system in a measurable manner.

name: pipeline
definition: Discovery and development compound portfolio of a pharmaceutical company or research organization.

name: pivotal study
definition: Experiment that provides strong support for or against the drug or molecular target under investigation.

name: potential genotoxic impurity
definition: Confirmed or suspected presence of one or more known genotoxic materials in an active pharmaceutical ingredient.

name: preclinical candidate
definition: Optimised lead compound successfully passing key screening, selectivity, and physicochemical criteria sufficient to warrant further detailed pharmacological and pharmacokinetic evaluation in animal models.

name: privileged structure
definition: Substructural feature that confers desirable (often drug-like) properties on compounds containing that feature. They often consist of a semi-rigid scaffold that presents multiple hydrophobic residues without undergoing hydrophobic collapse.

name: proof of concept
definition: Procedure by which a specific therapeutic mechanism or treatment/diagnostic paradigm is shown to be beneficial.

name: proteinase
definition: Enzyme that catalyses the hydrolysis of proteins.

name: prototype drug
definition: Early compound that has biological properties suitable for target validation but may not necessarily be adequate for clinical studies.

name: QTc interval
definition: Time between the start of the Q wave and the end of the T wave in the heart’s electrical cycle. When corrected for individual heart rate it becomes known as the corrected QT, or QTc interval.

name: retrosynthesis
definition: Process of conceptually deconstructing complex molecules into simpler fragments capable of chemical manipulation to reform the parent compound.

name: rule of three
definition: Set of molecular descriptors used to assess the quality of hit or lead molecules.

name: scaffold
definition: Core portion of a molecule common to all members of a chemical library or compound series.

name: scaffold hopping
definition: Exchange of one scaffold for another while maintaining molecular features that are important for biological properties.

name: site-directed mutagenesis
definition: Molecular biology technique in which mutations are created at one or more defined sites in a DNA molecule.

name: small inhibitory double-stranded RNA
definition: Small RNA fragments that can combine with specific genes to silence their expression.

name: spare receptor
definition: Residual binding site still available to an endogenous ligand after sufficient sites have already been filled to elicit the maximal response possible for that particular biological system.

name: structural alert
definition: Chemical features present in a hit or lead molecule indicative of potential toxicity.

name: supersaturated solution
definition: Solution that has a greater composition of a solute than one that is in equilibrium with undissolved solute at specified values of temperature and pressure.

name: systems biology
definition: Integration of high-throughput biology measurements with computational models that study the projection of the mechanistic characteristics of metabolic and signalling pathways onto physiological and pathological phenotypes.

name: targeted drug delivery
definition: Approach to target a drug to a specific tissue or molecular target using a prodrug or antibody recognition systems.

name: target validation
definition: Process by which a protein, RNA, or DNA is implicated in a biological pathway thought to be of relevance to a disease or adverse pathology.

name: tautomer
definition: Structural isomer that can readily convert to another form that differs only by the attachment position of a hydrogen atom and the location of double bond(s).

name: therapeutic index
definition: Ratio of the exposure/concentration of a therapeutic agent that causes beneficial effects to that which causes the first observed adverse effect.

name: unmet medical need
definition: Term used for diseases or other disorders for which no optimal therapeutic options exist.

name: virtual chemical library
definition: Collection of chemical structures constructed solely in electronic form or on paper.

name: volume of distribution
definition: Apparent (hypothetical) volume of fluid required to contain the total amount of a substance in the body at the same concentration as that present in the plasma assuming equilibrium has been attained.

name: wild-type receptor
definition: Receptor that occurs naturally in human and other species.

name: alpha relaxation
definition: Highest-temperature or lowest-frequency relaxation in the loss curve of a polymer.

name: alpha relaxation peak
definition: Highest-temperature peak or lowest-frequency peak in the loss curve of a polymer.

name: amorphous polymer
definition: Polymer in the amorphous state.

name: amorphous state
definition: State of matter characterised by the absence of long-range molecular order.

name: beta relaxation
definition: Second-highest-temperature or second-lowest-frequency relaxation in the loss curve of a polymer.

name: beta relaxation peak
definition: Second-highest-temperature or second-lowest-frequency peak in the loss curve of a polymer.

name: characteristic temperatures
definition: Temperatures obtained from a differential scanning calorimeter (DSC) experiment or a differential thermal analysis (DTA) experiment that characterise the physical processes occurring.

name: clearing temperature
definition: Temperature at which the transition between the mesophase with the highest temperature range and the isotropic phase occurs.

name: cold crystallisation
definition: Polymer crystallisation brought about from a glass, from a liquid-crystalline state, or a state displaying a low degree of crystallinity at temperatures a little above the glass-transition temperature.

name: conformational enthalpy
definition: Enthalpy change associated with conformational changes.

name: conformational entropy
definition: Entropy change associated with conformational changes.

name: conformational melting
definition: Step-like increase in the conformational entropy of macromolecules, or parts of macromolecules.

name: conformational transition
definition: Transition between two conformational states.

name: constant oscillation-amplitude method
definition: Forced-resonance method to determine the viscoelastic properties of a material.

name: crystalline state
definition: State of matter ideally characterised by three-dimensional, long-range order on an atomic scale.

name: crystallisable polymer
definition: Polymer that is able to partially crystallise.

name: damping curve
definition: Decrease in the deformation amplitude of a material specimen plotted vs. time when the specimen is subjected to a free oscillation.

name: devitrification
definition: Formation of a polymer melt from a polymer glass.

name: differential scanning calorimeter
definition: Apparatus for conducting a differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) experiment.

name: differential thermal analyser
definition: Apparatus for conducting a differential thermal analysis experiment.

name: dilatometer
definition: Apparatus for conducting a dilatometry experiment.

name: dilatometry
definition: The measurement of changes with time in the volume, length, width, or thickness of a material sample caused by temperature changes under negligible load or by chemical reaction.

name: dynamic-load thermomechanical analysis
definition: Thermomechanical analysis carried out using a sinusoidal stress.

name: dynamic mechanical analyser
definition: Apparatus for conducting a dynamic mechanical analysis experiment.

name: dynamic viscometer
definition: Apparatus that uses a forced, non-resonance method to determine the viscoelastic properties of a material sample.

name: enthalpy relaxation
definition: Enthalpy change observed near the glass transition when a sample is heated at a rate different from that at which it was cooled down, or observed after annealing in the glassy state below the glass-transition temperature.

name: equilibrium melting temperature
definition: Temperature at which perfect polymer crystals of infinite thickness melt under equilibrium conditions.

name: forced sinusoidal oscillation
definition: Deformation of a material by the application of a small sinusoidal strain (\(\gamma\)) such that \[\gamma = \gamma_{0} \cos \omega t\] where \(\gamma_{0}\) and \(\omega\) are positive constants.

name: fragile glass
definition: Glass characterised by a large value of the fragility index (m).

name: fragility index
definition: Quantity characterising the fragility or the strength of a glass at a given temperature \[m = \left (\frac{\rm{d} \log_{10} \tau}{{\rm{d}} (T_{\rm{g}}/T)} \right)_{T = T_{\rm{g}}}\] \(\tau\) = relaxation time [\(\pu{s}\)]; \(T_{\rm{g}}\) = glass-transition temperature [\(\pu{K}\)]; \(T\) = temperature [\(\pu{K}\)].

name: free oscillation
definition: Oscillatory deformation of a material specimen with the motion generated without the continuous application of an external force.

name: gamma relaxation
definition: Third-highest-temperature or third-lowest-frequency relaxation in the loss curve of a polymer.

name: gamma relaxation peak
definition: Third-highest-temperature or third-lowest-frequency peak in the loss curve of a polymer.

name: glass
definition: Amorphous matter in the glassy state, i.e., below its glass-transition temperature.

name: glassy state
definition: State of amorphous matter below its glass-transition temperature.

name: Hoffman–Weeks plot
definition: Plot of melting temperature, \(T_{\rm{m}}\), vs. crystallisation temperature, \(T_{\rm{cr}}\).

name: isotropisation temperature
definition: Temperature at which a transition from any anisotropic state to an isotropic liquid occurs.

name: Kauzmann temperature
definition: Temperature at which the extrapolation of the entropy of a super-cooled liquid is equal to the entropy of its crystalline state.

name: Kohlrausch–Williams–Watts equation
definition: Equation describing the enthalpy relaxation, \(\Delta H\) which is observed during the annealing of polymers in the glassy state at a temperature, \(T_{\rm{a}}\), lower than \(T_{\rm{g}}\) \[\Delta H(t_{\rm{a}}) = \Delta c_{p}(T_{\rm{g}} - T_{\rm{a}}) \exp\!\left[- \left (\frac{t_{\rm{a}}}{\tau} \right)^{\beta} \right]\] \(\Delta H\) = difference of the enthalpy in the initial, glassy state, and the enthalpy of the glassy state after annealing; \(t_{\rm{a}}\) = time of annealing; \(\Delta c_{p}\) = difference in heat capacity at the glass-transition temperature, \(T_{\rm{g}}\), and the starting temperature of the annealing process, \(T_{\rm{a}}\); \(\tau\) = relaxation time at \(T_{\rm{a}}\); \(\beta\) = exponential factor.

name: linear thermodilatometry
definition: Technique in which one dimension of a substance under negligible load is measured as a function of temperature while the substance is subjected to a controlled temperature program.

name: logarithmic decrement
definition: Natural logarithm of the ratio of the displacement of a damping curve separated by one period of the displacement.

name: loss curve
definition: Plot of loss tangent (\(\tan \delta\)) vs. the temperature or the frequency of the forced sinusoidal oscillation.

name: loss modulus
definition: Ratio of the amplitude of the stress \(\pu{90\!^{\circ}}\) out of phase with the strain (\(\sigma_{0} \sin \delta\)) to the amplitude of the strain (\(\gamma_{0}\)) in the forced sinusoidal oscillation of a material. \[M^{\prime\prime} = \frac{\sigma_{0} \sin \delta}{\gamma_{0}}\]

name: loss tangent
definition: Tangent of the phase angle (\(\delta\)) between stress and strain during a forced sinusoidal oscillation.

name: master curve
definition: Viscoelastic spectrum of a polymer or polymer material constructed using the time–temperature superposition (TTS) principle, so that the spectrum covers a wide range of lengths of time or frequencies of measurement.

name: mechanical melting
definition: Mechanically induced transition of matter in the crystalline or glassy state to its melt.

name: melt
definition: Matter in the amorphous state above its glass-transition temperature.

name: melt flow index
definition: Mass of a polymer in grams that flows through a calibrated orifice at constant temperature under a specified load over a \(\pu{10\!{-}min}\) period.
synonyms: MFI|MFR|melt flow rate|melt mass flow rate|melt volume flow

name: melting temperature
definition: Temperature at which the last trace of crystallinity disappears upon heating.

name: modulated heat flow
definition: Heat flow in a modulated-temperature DSC experiment.

name: modulated-temperature DSC
definition: DSC experiment in which a small sinusoidal modulation overlays the change in temperature with time.

name: multiplexing
definition: Technique used in dynamic mechanical analysis in which a specimen is subjected to the superposition of a number of forced sinusoidal oscillations of different frequencies.

name: non-reversing heat flow
definition: In modulated-temperature DSC, the component of the total heat flow that is out-of-phase with the temperature modulation.

name: polymer glass
definition: Amorphous polymer at temperatures below its glass-transition temperature.

name: polymer melt
definition: Polymer in the amorphous state above its glass-transition temperature.

name: relaxation map
definition: Plot of the logarithm of the relaxation time vs. the reciprocal temperature.

name: relaxation spectrum
definition: Range of relaxation times describing stress relaxation in a polymer.

name: reversing heat flow
definition: In modulated-temperature DSC the heat-capacity component of the total heat flow that is in-phase with the temperature modulation.

name: secondary relaxation
definition: Second-, third-, fourth-, … highest-temperature or second-, third-, fourth-, … lowest-frequency relaxation in the loss curve of a polymer.

name: secondary relaxation peak
definition: Any peak in a loss curve either at a lower temperature than the temperature of the alpha relaxation peak or at a higher frequency than the frequency of the alpha relaxation peak.

name: secondary relaxation temperature
definition: Temperature characterising a secondary relaxation peak identified as the temperature at which the loss modulus (or loss tangent), measured by DMA or DETA, exhibits a maximum at the measurement frequency, due to the occurrence of localised motions involving only short segments of the polymer chains, or side groups of the polymer chains.

name: shift factor
definition: Multiplier used to change the interval of time or the range frequencies of measurement of a viscoelastic property at a given temperature, \(T_{1}\), so that the values of the property superimpose on the values measured at a reference temperature, \(T_{0}\).

name: storage modulus
definition: Ratio of the amplitude of the stress in phase with the strain (\(\sigma_{0} \cos \delta\)) to the amplitude of the strain (\(\gamma_{0}\)) in the forced sinusoidal oscillation of a material. \[M^{\prime} = \frac{\sigma_{0} \cos \delta}{\gamma_{0}}\]

name: stress relaxation
definition: Change in stress with time after the instantaneous application of a constant strain.

name: strong glass
definition: Glass characterised by a small value of the fragility index (\(m\)).

name: supercooled polymer melt
definition: Metastable melt of a crystallisable polymer at temperatures below its equilibrium melting temperature.

name: Tammann’s 2/3rd rule
definition: Empirical rule that states that in a partially crystalline polymer the glass-transition temperature can be reasonably approximated by a value equal to two-thirds of the melting temperature, \(T_{\rm{m}}\)/\(\pu{K}\).

name: thermal history
definition: Thermal treatment a polymer material has experienced before its characterisation or measurement of its properties.

name: thermal lag
definition: Delay of the response of a system to a change in temperature.

name: thermogravimetric analyser
definition: Apparatus for conducting thermogravimetric analysis.

name: thermoluminescence analysis
definition: Technique that monitors the light that is emitted from a sample against time or temperature while the temperature of the sample, in a specified atmosphere, is heated in a controlled manner.

name: thermomechanical analyser
definition: Apparatus for conducting thermomechanical analysis.

name: thermomechanical properties
definition: The temperature dependence of deformability or mechanical properties of a polymer sample.

name: time–temperature superposition principle
definition: Principle stating that the value of a viscoelastic property measured at a given temperature, after a given length of time or at a given frequency, is equal to the value of the property at a different temperature after a length of time or at a frequency equal to the given length of time or given frequency multiplied by a shift factor, \(a_{T}\) , with the value of the shift factor being independent of length of the time or frequency.

name: torsion pendulum
definition: Device consisting of a disc or other body of large moment of inertia mounted on one end of a torsionally flexible elastic rod or wire, the other end of which is fixed.

name: torsional pendulum analysis
definition: Dynamic mechanical analysis performed using a torsion pendulum.

name: Vicat softening temperature
definition: Temperature at which a thermoplastic polymer reaches a specific degree of softness as measured by a standard test.

name: viscoelastic spectrum
definition: Double logarithmic plot of a viscoelastic property vs. frequency of measurement or interval of time of measurement at constant temperature.

name: vitrification
definition: Formation of a polymer glass from a polymer melt.

name: Vogel–Fulcher–Tammann equation
definition: Equation describing the time-dependence of a relaxation time that deviates from an Arrhenius-type temperature dependence. \[\tau = \tau_{0} \exp\!\left({\frac{B}{T - T_{0}}}\right)\] \(\tau\)/\(\pu{s}\) = relaxation time; \(\tau_{0}\)/\(\pu{s}\) = relaxation time at the Kauzmann temperature, \(B\)/\(\pu{K}\) = constant; \(T\)/\(\pu{K}\) = temperature; \(T_{0}\)/\(\pu{K}\) = Kauzmann temperature.

name: volume thermodilatometry
definition: Technique in which the volume of a substance under negligible load is measured as a function of temperature while the substance is heated or cooled in a controlled programme.

name: Williams–Landel–Ferry equation
definition: Equation describing the temperature dependence of the shift factor, \(a_{T}\), for time–temperature superposition \[\log_{10}a_{\rm{T}} = \frac{-C_{1}(T_{1} - T_{0})}{C_{2} + (T_{1} - T_{0})}\] \(C_{1}\) and \(C_{2}\) are empirical constants, \(T\) is the temperature of measurement, and \(T_{0}\) is the reference temperature.

name: coordination polymer
definition: A coordination compound with repeating coordination entities extending in 1, 2, or 3 dimensions.

name: coordination network
definition: A coordination compound extending, through repeating coordination entities, in one dimension, but with cross-links between two or more individual chains, loops, or spiro-links, or a coordination compound extending through repeating coordination entities in two or three dimensions.

name: metal-organic framework
definition: A metal-organic framework, abbreviated to MOF, is a coordination network with organic ligands containing potential voids.

name: α:β T-cell receptor
definition: T-cell receptor (TCR) consisting of a heterodimer of two different glycoprotein chains, designated \(\upalpha\) and \(\upbeta\), assembled into an \(\upalpha{:}\upbeta\) heterodimer.

name: α:β T cell
definition: Lymphocyte whose T-cell receptor (TCR) is a heterodimer of an \(\upalpha\) chain and a \(\upbeta\) chain.

name: ABL oncogene
definition: Gene resulting from a chromosomal translocation (9;22) that fuses sequences from the BCR (breakpoint cluster region) gene with the ABL gene.

name: ABO blood group system
definition: System of antigens expressed on erythrocytes and used for typing human blood for transfusion.

name: abzyme
definition: Antibody or antibody construct with catalytic activity.

name: accessory cell
definition: Cell that assists in the adaptive immune response but does not directly mediate specific antigen recognition.

name: accessory molecule
definition: Molecule other than immunoglobulin (Ig), T-cell receptor (TCR), or major histocompatibility complex (MHC) molecule that participates in T lymphocyte recognition and response to antigen.

name: acquired immunity
definition: State of protection against pathogen-induced injury, with rapid immune elimination of pathogenic invaders owing to previous immunization or vaccination.

name: acquired immunodeficiency syndrome
definition: Disease caused by infection with the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), assuming clinical relevance when an infected patient has lost most of his/her CD4+ T cells, so that infections with opportunistic pathogens occur.

name: activation-induced cell death
definition: Process by which immune responses end in the death of most of the responding lymphocytes, leaving only a small number of resting memory cells.

name: active immunization
definition: Immunization with antigen, as distinct from the transfer of antibody to an unimmunized individual, which is called passive immunization.

name: active systemic anaphylaxis test
definition: Test for determining whether a drug can cause anaphylactic reactions in an animal following immunization with the drug.

name: acute lymphoblastic leukemia
definition: Highly aggressive, undifferentiated form of lymphoid malignancy derived from a progenitor cell that is thought to be able to give rise to both T- and B-cell lineages.

name: acute myelogenous leukemia
definition: Cancer characterized by rapid growth of abnormal granulocytes that accumulate in the bone marrow.

name: acute-phase protein
definition: Serum protein, mostly produced in the liver, which rapidly changes in concentration (some acute-phase proteins increase, some decrease) during the initiation of an inflammatory response.

name: acute-phase response
definition: Physiological response stimulated by cytokines including interleukin-1, interleukin-6, interferons, and tumor necrosis factor (TNF), characterized by increased vascular permeability, fever, and increased levels of proteins (thus called acute-phase proteins) such as C-reactive protein (CRP), occurring within a few hours of initiation.

name: acute rejection
definition: Rejection of a tissue or organ graft from a genetically unrelated donor, typically occurring within 10 to 13 days of transplantation.

name: acute respiratory distress syndrome
definition: Acute lung failure characterized by alveolar and interstitial edema, perivascular pulmonary edema, and hyaline membrane formation, resulting from a variety of underlying diseases that result in increased pulmonary vascular permeability.

name: adaptive immune response
definition: Immune response based on the principle of clonal recognition, such that upon first exposure to an antigen, primed lymphocytes either differentiate into immune effector cells or form an expanded pool of memory cells that respond to secondary exposure to the same antigen by mounting an amplified and more rapid response.

name: adaptive immune system
definition: Part of the immune system responsible for the adaptive immune response.

name: Addison disease
definition: Adrenocortical hypofunction characterized by hypotension, weight loss, anorexia, and weakness. The most common form is idiopathic Addison disease, mediated by autoimmune mechanisms. Autoantibodies specific to the adrenal cortex are specific diagnostic markers of this form.
synonyms: Addison autoimmune disease|Addison's autoimmune disease|Addison's disease

name: addressin
definition: Extracellular protein of the venular endothelium serving as a ligand to a homing receptor for lymphocytes.

name: adenosine deaminase deficiency
definition: Lack of the enzyme adenosine deaminase (ADA), which catalyzes the deamination of adenosine and deoxyadenosine to produce inosine and deoxyinosine, respectively. Affected individuals have a form of severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID).

name: adhesion molecule
definition: Molecule belonging mainly to the immunoglobulins, integrin superfamily (e.g., LFA-1, ICAM-1) or selectins, expressed on the cell membrane of various cells including those of the immune system. Interaction of adhesion molecules with each other as receptor and corresponding ligand facilitates cooperation (cross-talk) of cells, signal transduction, and information transfer between cells.

name: adjuvant arthritis
definition: Experimental model of immunopathology with features of rheumatoid arthritis (RA), induced in rats by injection with bacterial products, which may be used to study anti-inflammatory therapies.

name: adoptive transfer
definition: Transfer, by transplantation of immunocompetent cells, of the capacity to mount an immune response.

name: adverse drug reaction
definition: Appreciably harmful or unpleasant reaction resulting from an intervention related to the administration of a pharmaceutical product.

name: adverse immunostimulation
definition: Antigen-non-specific, inappropriate, or unintended activation of a component of the immune system.

name: aeroallergen
definition: Any airborne particle, such as a pollen grain or spore, that triggers an allergic reaction in sensitive individuals.

name: affinity maturation
definition: Increase in antibody affinity for an antigen observed as the humoral immune response progresses.

name: agranulocytosis
definition: Failure of the bone marrow to make sufficient granulocytes, especially neutrophils.

name: allelic exclusion
definition: Phenomenon whereby, following successful rearrangement of one allele of an antigen receptor gene, rearrangement of the other parental allele is suppressed, thereby ensuring each lymphocyte expresses only a single specificity of antigen receptor.

name: allergen
definition: Immunostimulant antigenic substance that may or may not cause a clinically significant effect but which is capable of producing an immune reaction, often immediate-type hypersensitivity.

name: allergic
definition: Immunologically hypersensitive.

name: allergy
definition: Symptoms or signs occurring in sensitized individuals following exposure to a previously encountered substance (allergen) that would otherwise not cause such symptoms or signs in non-sensitized individuals. The most common forms of allergy are rhinitis, urticaria, asthma, and contact dermatitis.

name: alloantibody
definition: Antibody produced against an antigen from another member of the same species.

name: alloantigen
definition: Antigen, present in some but not all individuals of a particular species, that arises from polymorphisms at the major histocompatibility complex (MHC) loci and stimulates intense reactions to allograft tissues from other individuals of the same species that do not produce it.

name: allogeneic
definition: Genetically different, referring to individuals of the same species.

name: allograft
definition: Tissue or organ graft between allogeneic individuals.

name: allotype
definition: Allelic variant of an antigen that, because it is not present in all individuals, may be immunogenic in members of the same species that have a different version of the allele.

name: alloreactivity
definition: Reactivity of an antibody with an alloantigen.

name: alternative pathway
definition: Activation pathway involving complement components C3, Factor B, Factor D, and properdin that, in the presence of a stabilizing activator surface such as microbial polysaccharide, generates the alternative pathway C3 convertase C3bBb.

name: alveolar macrophage
definition: Macrophage found in the lung alveoli; it may remove and sometimes retain inhaled particulate matter.
