name: alveolitis
definition: 1) Inflammation of alveoli. 2) Inflammation of a tooth socket.

name: amyloid
definition: Fibrous protein secreted into the extracellular space where it forms amorphous deposits in multiple organs in some pathological states.

name: anamnestic
definition: Describing immunological memory that gives rise to a rapid increase in immunological response after reexposure to antigen.

name: anaphylactic shock
definition: Immediate overreaction of the immune system to a drug or other agent in an individual who has previously encountered the agent and has produced antibodies to that agent.

name: anaphylactoid
definition: Of or resembling anaphylaxis.

name: anaphylatoxin
definition: Complement-derived protein fragment (e.g., C3a, C4a, or C5a) capable of directly triggering mast cell degranulation, chemotaxis, smooth muscle contraction, and inflammation.

name: anaphylaxis
definition: Life-threatening type I hypersensitivity allergic reaction occurring in a person or animal exposed to an antigen or hapten to which they have previously been sensitized.

name: anergy
definition: Lack of an immune response, usually taken as lack of response to common recall antigens.

name: angioedema
definition: Swelling that occurs in the tissue just below the surface of the skin, most often around the lips and eyes, the mucous membranes and occasionally the viscera.

name: ankylosing spondylitis
definition: Chronic inflammatory disease affecting the spine, sacroiliac joints, and large peripheral joints, having a major genetic predisposition.

name: therapeutic antibody
definition: Antibody administered with the aim of treating a disease.

name: antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity
definition: Cytotoxic reaction in which an antibody-coated target cell is directly killed by an Fc receptor-bearing leukocyte, e.g., NK cell, macrophage, neutrophil, or eosinophil.

name: antibody-forming cell assay
definition: Assay that measures the humoral immune response mediated by the concerted actions of antigen-presenting cells, T lymphocytes, and B lymphocytes, generally by determination of murine primary IgM or IgG antibodies directed against the T-cell-dependent sheep red blood cell (SRBC) surface antigens after in vivo sensitization.
synonyms: AFC|AFC assay|Jerne plaque assay|hemolytic plaque assay|plaque-forming cell (PFC) assay

name: antibody therapy
definition: Use of an antibody to target specific cells (often tumor cells) or signal transduction pathways (often via chemokines/cytokines) in the treatment of disease.

name: lupus anticoagulant
definition: Autoantibody that binds to phospholipids and/or proteins of the cell membrane in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), and can interfere with blood clotting and tests of clotting function.

name: anti-DNA antibody
definition: Antibody directed against single-stranded or double-stranded DNA.

name: anti-erythrocyte antibody
definition: Antibody against molecules of the red blood cell, usually against membrane proteins, causing lysis of the red blood cells.

name: antigenic
definition: Capable of stimulating lymphocytes to produce antibodies.

name: antigenicity
definition: Ability of an antigen to bind to a specific antibody or T-cell receptor (TCR); often a measure of its ability to produce immunity.

name: antigen presentation
definition: Display of antigen as peptide fragments bound to major histocompatibility complex (MHC) molecules on the surface of a cell.

name: antigen-presenting cell
definition: Cell, such as a dendritic cell or macrophage, that is responsible for making antigens accessible to lymphocytes and other immune effector and regulatory cells, making possible specific recognition by receptors on the cell surface.

name: antigen-presenting groove
definition: 1) Pocket in a major histocompatibility complex (MHC) molecule that binds antigen for antigen presentation. 2) Hydrophobic binding region in the CD1 protein that anchors lipid-containing antigens causing exposure of the peptide or carbohydrate moiety in a position enabling T-cell receptor (TCR) contact.

name: antigen processing
definition: Cleavage of protein antigens in antigen-presenting cells (APCs).

name: antigen receptor
definition: Specific antigen-binding receptor on T or B lymphocytes that is transcribed and translated following rearrangements and translocation of V, D, and J genes.

name: antigen recognition
definition: Ability of highly specialized proteins of the immune system to recognize antigens and specifically bind to them.

name: anti-idiotypic antibody
definition: Antibody raised against antigenic determinants unique to the variable region of a single antibody.

name: anti-isotypic antibody
definition: Antibody against universal features of a given constant (C) region isotype (such as $\upgamma\!$ or $\upmu\!$) of one species that is made by immunizing a member of another species with that isotype.

name: antimitochondrial antibody
definition: Autoantibody producing a mitochondrial staining pattern on sections of various tissues and on tumor cell monolayers.

name: antineutrophil cytoplasmic autoantibody
definition: Antibody against antigens in the cytoplasm of neutrophils.

name: antineutrophil cytoplasmic autoantibody associated vasculitis
definition: One of a group of autoimmune systemic vasculitides associated with antineutrophil cytoplasmic autoantibodies (ANCAs), e.g., Wegener granulomatosis (WG), microscopic polyangiitis, and Churg–Strauss syndrome.

name: antinuclear antibody
definition: Antibody, detectable in the blood, that has the capability of binding to a substance, e.g., DNA, within the nucleus of the cells.

name: antiphospholipid syndrome
definition: One of the most common autoimmune diseases, characterized by thrombosis, recurrent spontaneous abortions, and the presence of antiphospholipid antibodies.

name: anti-sheep red blood cell IgM response assay
definition: Test to determine T-cell-dependent antibody response, usually by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Sheep red blood cells (SRBCs) are used as an antigen. Often referred to as the plaque assay.

name: antitoxin
definition: Antibody specific for exotoxins produced by certain microorganisms such as the causative agents of diphtheria and tetanus.

name: aplastic anemia
definition: Greatly decreased formation of erythrocytes and hemoglobin, usually associated with pronounced granulocytopenia and thrombocytopenia, as a result of hypoplastic or aplastic bone marrow.

name: arthritis
definition: Inflammation of a joint or joints.

name: Arthus reaction
definition: Local antibody-mediated hypersensitivity reaction in which antigen-antibody complexes which fix complement are deposited in the walls of small vessels, often in the skin, causing acute inflammation with an infiltration of neutrophils.
synonyms: Gell and Coombs Type III reaction

name: asthma
definition: Chronic respiratory disease characterized by bronchoconstriction, excessive mucus secretion, and edema of the pulmonary alveoli, resulting in difficulty in exhaling, wheezing, and cough.

name: ataxia telangiectasia
definition: Disease characterized by staggering gait, multiple disorganized blood vessels, and an immunodeficiency, associated with a protein called ataxia telangiectasia-mutated (ATM), a protein kinase thought to be important in detection of double-stranded DNA breaks.

name: atopic allergy
definition: Immunoglobulin E (IgE)-mediated hypersensitivity, including asthma, eczema, hay fever, and food allergy.

name: atopic dermatitis
definition: Inflammation of the skin in atopic individuals.

name: atopic eczema
definition: Chronic skin disease, often localized on flexural surfaces, in individuals with propensity to develop immunoglobulin E (IgE)-mediated allergy.

name: atopy
definition: Of, relating to, or caused by a hereditary predisposition toward developing certain hypersensitivity reactions, such as hay fever, asthma, or chronic urticaria, upon exposure to specific antigens.

name: attenuated vaccine
definition: Vaccine made from a live organism that targets cells of the immune system but has been engineered or weakened so as not to cause disease.

name: atypical interstitial pneumonia
definition: Acute or chronic respiratory distress in cattle, in the absence of toxemia or other systemic signs that are characteristic of other pneumonias.

name: autoantibody
definition: Immunoglobulin (Ig) antibody that is directed against the organism’s own antigen(s).

name: autoantigen
definition: Antigenic component of an individual’s tissues which may be a target of autoimmune responses by autoreactive B cells (autoantibodies) or T cells, including proteins (e.g., enzymes, structural proteins), glycoproteins (e.g., 2-glycoprotein I), nucleic acids, (e.g., double-stranded DNA), phospholipids (e.g., cardiolipin), and glycosphingolipids (e.g., gangliosides).

name: autochthonous
definition: Pertaining to self.

name: autocrine
definition: Type of signaling in which a cell secretes a chemical messenger that binds to receptors on the same cell, leading to changes in the cell.

name: autograft
definition: Tissue transplant from one site to another in an individual.

name: autoimmune
definition: Of or relating to an immune response by the body against one of its own cells or tissues.

name: autoimmune disease
definition: Pathological condition resulting when an organism produces antibodies or specific cells that bind to constituents of its own tissues (autoantigens) and cause tissue injury.

name: autoimmune hemolytic anemia
definition: Autoimmune disease in which antibodies initiate complement lysis of erythrocytes.

name: autoimmune hepatitis
definition: Chronic autoimmune-mediated hepatic inflammation usually characterized by antinuclear (ANA), smooth muscle (SMA)/anti-F-actin, liver-kidney microsomal (LKM), and/or soluble liver antigen (SLA) antibodies.

name: autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome
definition: Disease characterized by lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, autoimmune cytopenias, and hypergammaglobulinemia.

name: autoimmune polyendocrine syndrome type 1 or 2
definition: Heterogeneous group of rare diseases characterized by autoimmune activity against more than one endocrine organ, although non-endocrine organs can also be affected.

name: autoimmune regulator
definition: DNA-binding protein involved in immunoregulation (probably in the establishment and maintenance of tolerance).

name: autoimmunity
definition: Immune response to 'self' tissues or components.

name: autoinflammatory disease
definition: Unregulated inflammation without significant levels of autoantibodies or autoactivated T cells, or evidence of infection, but rather caused by genetic disturbance of the mechanisms that initiate and control inflammation.

name: autologous
definition: From the same individual.

name: autologous antibody
definition: Antibody derived from a specific individual, acting within that individual.

name: autophagy
definition: Digestion and breakdown in lysosomes of a cell’s own proteins and/or organelles.

name: autoreactivity
definition: Immune response directed at self-antigens.

name: β2-microglobulin
definition: Small (\(\pu{12 kDa}\)) protein forming part of the structure of major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class I-encoded molecules.

name: B-1/B-2 cells
definition: Two major subpopulations of B lymphocytes.

name: B7 molecule
definition: Co-stimulatory molecule on the surface of T-cell-activating antigen-presenting cells (APCs), allowing full activation of T cells that are bound to major histocompatibility complex (MHC)-peptide complexes.

name: B-cell linker protein
definition: Adaptor protein operating in B cells that, upon phosphorylation, recruits signaling molecules to membrane lipid rafts.

name: B-cell stimulatory factor
definition: Generic name given to B-cell-specific growth and differentiation factors involved in the T-cell-dependent activation of B cells. Many are now identified as specific interleukins (ILs).

name: B-cell receptor
definition: Receptor on the surface of a B cell consisting of transmembrane immunoglobulin (Ig) that recognizes a specific antigen.

name: B lymphocyte
definition: Bone marrow-derived lymphocyte, expressing an antigen-receptor complex composed of membrane-bound immunoglobulin (Ig) and associated molecular chains.

name: B-lymphocyte chemokine
definition: Chemokine that attracts B cells and activated T cells into the follicles of peripheral lymphoid tissues.

name: B-lymphocyte-induced maturation protein 1
definition: Transcriptional repressor in B cells, that switches off genes required for B cell proliferation in the germinal center, and for class switching and affinity maturation.

name: bacille Calmette–Guérin
definition: Attenuated Mycobacterium tuberculosis used both as a specific vaccine for tuberculosis and as an adjuvant.

name: BALB/c mouse
definition: Inbred albino mouse strain, substrains of which produce plasmacytomas on injection with mineral oil, useful for the production of monoclonal antibodies.

name: bare lymphocyte syndrome
definition: Rare, recessive genetic condition in which the products of one or more genes required to switch on major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class I or MHC class II genes are defective or absent. As a consequence, MHC class I (BLS1) or MHC class II (BLS2) genes are not expressed, leading to severe immunodeficiency.

name: basophil
definition: Type of granulocyte found in the blood and resembling the tissue mast cell.

name: basophilic degranulation
definition: Loss of granules in basophilic cells, associated with the release of active substances from the cells, characteristic of type I immediate hypersensitivity.

name: Bcl-2
definition: Member of the Bcl protein family that protects cells from apoptosis by binding to the mitochondrial membrane.

name: Behcet disease
definition: Chronic vasculitis of unknown origin, characterized by ulcerations and skin rash and treated by immunosuppression.

name: Bence–Jones protein
definition: Excess circulating kappa ($\kappa$)-light chain found in the urine of patients with multiple myeloma.

name: benign monoclonal gammopathy
definition: Nonmalignant overproduction of $\ce{\upgamma\!\mbox{-}globulin}$ by a single clone of lymphocytes.

name: biolistics
definition: Use of small particles, e.g., colloidal gold, as a vehicle for carrying agents (drugs, nucleic acid, etc.) into a cell.

name: biopanning
definition: Technique for selection of peptides with high affinity binding to a chosen target.

name: bispecific antibody
definition: Artificially produced hybrid antibody in which each of the two antigen-binding arms is specific for a different antigenic epitope. Such antibodies, which can be produced either by chemical cross-linkage or by recombinant DNA techniques, can be used to link together two different antigens or cells, e.g., a cytotoxic T lymphocyte and a tumor cell.

name: blast
definition: Immature stage in cell development, before the appearance of the definitive characteristics of the cell; used also as a word termination, as in erythroblast, etc.

name: Blau syndrome
definition: Rare familial inflammatory disease characterized by arthritis, dermatitis, and uveitis.

name: blocking antibody
definition: Antibody that prevents other antibodies from combining with a specific antigen but does not itself produce an immunological response when combined with that antigen.

name: blood dyscrasia
definition: Presence of abnormal material in the blood, usually applied to diseases affecting blood cells or platelets.

name: blood group antigen
definition: Surface antigen on erythrocytes, detectable with a specific antibody from other individuals.

name: blood–placenta barrier
definition: Physiological interface between maternal and fetal blood circulations that filters out some substances that could harm the fetus while favoring the passage of others such as nutrients.

name: Bloom syndrome
definition: Disease caused by mutations in a DNA helicase and characterized by low T cell numbers, reduced antibody levels, and an increased susceptibility to respiratory infections, cancer, and radiation damage.

name: bone marrow
definition: Soft fatty vascular substance in the cavity of bone where blood cells are formed.

name: bone marrow transplantation
definition: Transfer of bone marrow from a donor to a recipient whose bone marrow has been ablated.

name: booster
definition: Portion of an immunizing agent given at a later time to stimulate the effects of a previous dose of the same agent.

name: bradykinin
definition: Vasoactive peptide and inflammatory mediator produced at sites of tissue damage.

name: bronchial provocation test
definition: Test of alteration of lung function induced by inhalation of an allergen or airway-constricting agent, providing information on bronchial responsiveness.

name: Buehler assay
definition: Skin sensitization test for contact allergic dermatitis in which a test substance is applied to the shaved flank of a guinea pig in an occlusive patch for 6 h at 0, 1, and 2 weeks, followed by challenge of the untreated flank at 4 weeks.

name: autoimmune bullous skin disease
definition: Any of several autoimmune diseases characterized by intraepidermal or subepidermal blisters (e.g., pemphigus vulgaris, bullous pemphigoid) and highly specific autoantibodies against components of the desmosome or hemidesmosome (e.g., desmoglein 3, BP180).

name: Burkitt lymphoma
definition: Lymphoma caused by Epstein–Barr virus (EBV), occurring mainly in sub-Saharan Africa.

name: bursa of Fabricius
definition: Primary lymphoid organ in avian species, located at the cloacal-hind gut junction; it is the site of B-cell maturation.

name: bystander effect
definition: Positive or negative effect on the immune system seen after exposure to certain drugs, radiation, and other agents, induced by non-immune mechanisms.

name: bystander suppression
definition: Suppression of an immune response to an antigen due to tolerance to an unrelated (hence bystander) antigen.

name: C1 inhibitor
definition: Plasma glycoprotein secreted primarily by the liver and acting as a serine proteinase inhibitor (serpin), inhibiting C1 components of the complement system.

name: CD1
definition: Cell surface protein of antigen-presenting cells (APCs) involved in presentation of lipopeptide or glycolipid antigens.

name: CD3
definition: Molecule composed of five polypeptide chains associated with the heterodimer T-cell receptor (TCR), forming the T-cell receptor complex (TCR/CD3); CD3 transduces the activating signals when antigen binds to the TCR.

name: CD4
definition: Cell surface antigen belonging to the immunoglobulin (Ig) superfamily of molecules and a marker of T helper cells.

name: CD4+/CD25+ T cell
definition: Subtype of CD4+ regulatory T cell (Treg) with potential role in the regulation of immune homeostasis.

name: CD5+ B lymphocyte
definition: Lymphocyte of type B-1a, which is predominant in fetal lymphoid organs and in neonatal cord blood.

name: CD8
definition: Cell surface molecule belonging to the immunoglobulin (Ig) superfamily of molecules found, among others, on cytotoxic T cells, which binds to major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class I molecules.

name: CD8+ T suppressor cell
definition: Outdated term for CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL, Tc). The term 'suppressor T cell' is nowadays reserved for regulatory T cell (Treg).

name: CD16
definition: Low-affinity $\ce{Fc\mbox{-}\upgamma\! receptor}$ ($\ce{Fc\mbox{-}\upgamma\!\mbox{-}RIII}$) expressed mainly on natural killer (NK) cells, granulocytes, and macrophages, mediating antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC).

name: CD23
definition: Low-affinity ${\rm{Fc\mbox{-}}}\upvarepsilon\!$ receptor induced by interleukin-4 (IL-4) and expressed on see activated B cells and macrophages.

name: CD25
definition: \(\ce{\upalpha\mbox{-}chain}\) of the interleukin-2 (IL-2) receptor.

name: CD40 ligand
definition: Essential molecule for normal switching signaling through binding to CD40 on B cells. The interaction of CD40L and CD40 is also critical for optimal T cell function.

name: C-reactive protein
definition: Serum protein produced by liver cells as part of the acute-phase response, which acts as a stimulus of the classical pathway of complement activation.

name: C-type lectin
definition: Any of a large family of \(\ce{Ca^{2+}}\)-dependent lectins; members of this family share primary structural homology in their carbohydrate-recognition domains and include many endocytic receptors, many proteoglycans, and all known collectins and selectins.

name: cadherin
definition: Calcium-dependent, transmembrane glycoprotein occurring in cell-cell contacts (desmosomes) and functioning as an adhesion molecule.

name: calcineurin inhibitor
definition: Any member of a group of immunomodulating drugs that bind to the cytosolic protein cyclophilin of T lymphocytes, thus inhibiting the phosphatase calcineurin, an inducer of interleukin-2 (IL-2) formation.

name: candidiasis
definition: Infection with a fungus of the genus Candida, especially C. albicans, that usually occurs in the skin and mucous membranes of the mouth, respiratory tract, or vagina but may invade the bloodstream, especially in immunocompromised individuals.

name: capping
definition: Active process whereby cross-linking of cell surface molecules (e.g., by antibody) leads to aggregation and subsequent migration of the molecules to one pole of the cell.

name: carcinoembryonic antigen
definition: Membrane glycoprotein epitope normally present in the fetal gastrointestinal tract and elevated in many patients with various carcinomas.

name: cardiolipin
definition: 1,3-Bis(sn-3-phosphatidyl)-sn-glycerol, the main target of antiphospholipid antibodies.

name: caspase
definition: Any member of a family of intracellular cysteine proteinases that cleave proteins at specific aspartic acid residues to initiate or promote apoptosis.

name: caveola
definition: Invagination on the cell surface (plasma membrane), enriched in caveolin proteins, cholesterol, and glycosphingolipids, important in various processes including pinocytosis and signal transduction.

name: celiac disease
definition: Autoimmune disorder occurring in genetically predisposed individuals, characterized by immune intolerance to the \(\ce{\upalpha\mbox{-}gliadin}\) component of gluten, a protein found in wheat, barley, and rye. Resultant inflammation of the mucosa of the upper small intestine is associated with malabsorption of nutrients and a wasting illness follows from this.

name: cell-mediated cytotoxicity
definition: Lysis of a target cell initiated by a T lymphocyte binding to surface antibodies or antigen-bound major histocompatibility complex (MHC) molecules.

name: cell-mediated immune response
definition: Specific immune response in which T lymphocytes mediate the effects, either through the release of cytokines or through cytotoxicity.

name: cell-mediated immunity
definition: Immune response mediated by antigen-specific T lymphocytes, either through the release of cytokines or through cytotoxicity, in contrast with humoral immunity, which is antibody-mediated.

name: central tolerance
definition: Specific immunological tolerance due to the induction of lymphocyte apoptosis or anergy within the primary lymphoid organs (bone marrow in the case of B cell tolerance and the thymus for T cells).

name: challenge
definition: Induction or evaluation of an immune response in an organism by administration of a specific antigen to which it has been sensitized.

name: chaperone-mediated autophagy
definition: Type of autophagy targeting only those proteins that are recognized by the binding of an hsc70-containing chaperone/co-chaperone complex.

name: chemotactic factor
definition: Biologically active substance, such as a chemokine or anaphylatoxin, that induces a concentration gradient-dependent movement of cells.

name: chemotaxis
definition: 1) General. Movement of an organism or cell along a concentration gradient of a chemical. 2) In immunology. Movement of cells up a concentration gradient of a chemical attractant (chemotactic factor), such as a chemokine or other cytokine.

name: chemotype
definition: Character of a plant or microorganism based on a metabolite distinct from that found in other members of the same species.

name: chloracne
definition: Acne-like eruption caused by exposure to certain chlorinated organic substances such as polychlorinated biphenyls or 2,3,7,8-tetrachlorodibenzo[1,4]dioxin [2,3,7,8-tetrachlorooxanthrene] and other polychlorinated dibenzodioxins and furans.

name: chromate uptake assay
definition: Method used in immunotoxicology to quantify the toxic effect of a substance on leukocytes by measuring uptake of \(\ce{^{51}Cr{-}labeled}\) chromate.

name: chromium release assay
definition: Immunotoxicity assay that can be used to assess either natural killer (NK) cell or cytotoxic T cell activity or macrophage activity. When incubated with \(\ce{^{51}Cr{-}labeled}\) chicken red blood cells (cRBCs), NK and cytotoxic T cells lyse the cRBC and thus induce the release of \(\ce{^{51}Cr}\) into the medium. In contrast, macrophages phagocytose cRBC, and are then lysed to assess the amount of \(\ce{^{51}Cr}\) they have taken up.

name: chronic allergic inflammation
definition: Disease of airways, skin, eyes and other organs, resulting from repeated or continuous exposure to an allergen and involving immunoglobulin E (IgE) formation, IgE-induced histamine-release from mast cells, liberation of mediators such as cytokines and prostaglandins, and local inflammation characterized by infiltrating leucocytes; it results in augmented susceptibility to the allergen.

name: chronic granulomatous disease
definition: Immunodeficiency disease in which multiple granulomas form as a result of defective elimination of bacteria by phagocytes.

name: chronic lymphocytic leukemia
definition: B cell tumor found in the blood.

name: chronic myelogenous leukemia
definition: Cancer characterized by overgrowth of the bone marrow with malignant white blood cells, usually exhibiting a chromosomal abnormality (Philadelphia chromosome), which causes uncontrolled proliferation of cells that are released into peripheral blood.

name: chronic rejection
definition: Immunologically triggered reaction occurring in a transplanted organ or tissue, leading to progressive destruction and finally failure of the transplanted organ occurring two months to many years after transplantation.

name: class switching
definition: Process by which a B cell changes the class but not specificity of a given antibody it produces, e.g., switching from an immunoglobulin M (IgM) to an immunoglobulin G (IgG) antibody.

name: classical pathway
definition: Activation pathway involving complement components C1, C2, and C4 which, following fixation of C1q, e.g., by antigen-antibody complexes, produces the classical pathway C3 convertase C4b2a.

name: clonal anergy
definition: Form of self-tolerance developing as a consequence of negative selection during thymic selection processes. Clones of thymocytes whose antigen receptors [T-cell receptors (TCRs)] bind with high affinity to self-antigens in association with major histocompatibility complex (MHC) molecules are inactivated.

name: clonal deletion
definition: Process by which contact with antigen (e.g., self-antigen) at an early stage of lymphocyte differentiation leads to cell death by apoptosis.

name: clonal expansion
definition: Proliferation of B lymphocytes and T lymphocytes activated by clonal selection in order to produce a clone of identical cells.

name: clonal indifference
definition: Failure of B or T cells expressing anti-self-receptors to interact with antigen (e.g., by low valency, low concentration, or sequestration of antigens; low receptor avidity; or lack of co-stimulatory molecules).

name: clonal selection
definition: Selection and activation by antigen of a lymphocyte, bearing a complementary receptor, which then proliferates to form an expanded clone.

name: cluster determinant
definition: Cluster of antigens representing a cell surface marker with which antibodies react. Not to be confused with cluster of differentiation (CD) antigen.

name: cluster of differentiation antigen
definition: Any of a family of molecular markers on cell surfaces that may be used operationally to define phenotype, origin, and activation state of the cell.

name: coagulation system
definition: Proteolytic cascade of plasma enzymes that triggers blood clotting when blood vessels are damaged.

name: cognate T cell
definition: Helper T lymphocyte (Th) primed by the same antigen as the B cell to which it gives help.

name: cold autoantibody type
definition: Autoantibody that reacts optimally at low temperatures (\(\pu{{0}{-}{5} ^{\circ}C}\)) with surface antigens of erythrocytes.

name: collagen arthritis
definition: Autoimmune model of rheumatoid arthritis (RA), arising from combined cellular immunity and humoral immunity against collagen type II, and characterized by rapid and severe erosions of cartilage and bone.

name: collectin
definition: Any member of a structurally related family of calcium-dependent carbohydrate-binding proteins or lectins containing collagen-like sequences, e.g., mannose-binding lectin (MBL).

name: colony-stimulating factor
definition: Factor that permits the proliferation and differentiation of hematopoietic cells.

name: combinatorial diversity
definition: Component of antibody and T-cell receptor (TCR) diversity that is generated by the recombination of variable (V), diversity (\(D\), for immunoglobulin heavy chains, and for TCR \(\upbeta\) and \(\ce{\updelta\ chains}\)), and joining (J) gene segments.

name: combinatorial joining
definition: Merging of DNA segments generating new genetic information.

name: common variable immunodeficiency
definition: Relatively common deficiency in antibody production, of unknown pathogenesis but strongly associated with genes mapping within the major histocompatibility complex (MHC).

name: competitive inhibition assay
definition: Method of measuring an antigen in a sample using a labeled species of the antigen as a competitive inhibitor of its binding in a specific antigen–antibody reaction.

name: complementarity-determining region
definition: Hypervariable amino acid sequence within antibody and T-cell receptor (TCR) variable (V) regions, which interacts with complementary amino acids on the antigen or major histocompatibility complex (MHC)–peptide complex.

name: complement deficiency
definition: Congenital deficiency in any of the various components of the complement system.

name: complement reaction
definition: Physiological reaction to the presence of a foreign microorganism in which a cascade of enzymatic reactions, triggered by molecular features of the microorganism, result in lysis or phagocytosis of the foreign material.

name: complement receptor
definition: Cell-surface protein that recognizes and binds complement proteins that have bound an antigen.

name: complement system
definition: Group of serum proteins with the capacity to interact with each other when activated in a chain reaction which results in formation of a lytic complex and the release of several biologically active peptides of low relative molecular mass (anaphylatoxins).

name: concanavalin A
definition: Hemagglutinin, isolated from jack bean (Canavalia ensiformis) meal, which reacts with polyglucosans in the blood of mammals, causing agglutination.

name: conformational epitope
definition: Epitope on a protein antigen formed from several separate regions in the primary sequence of a protein brought together by protein folding.

name: congenic
definition: Differing at a single genetic locus.

name: allergic conjunctivitis
definition: Irritation of the ocular conjunctiva, resulting from the activation of conjunctival mast cells by airborne allergens such as pollens or house dust.

name: constant gene
definition: Gene that encodes the constant (C) region of immunoglobulin (Ig) chains or T-cell receptor (TCR) chains.

name: constant region
definition: Part of an immunoglobulin (Ig) or T-cell receptor (TCR) that is relatively constant in amino acid sequence among different Ig or TCR molecules.

name: contact allergen
definition: Substance that causes a skin hypersensitivity reaction by direct contact.

name: contact dermatitis
definition: Skin inflammation that occurs when the skin’s surface comes in contact with a substance originating outside the body.

name: contact hypersensitivity
definition: Immune response following skin contact with an antigen.

name: contact sensitivity
definition: State of immunological sensitization in which an eczematous epidermal reaction may occur when a hapten is applied to the skin of a sensitized individual.

name: contact urticaria
definition: Urticaria provoked by contact with inducing agents.

name: conventional dendritic cell
definition: Predominant type of dendritic cell active in antigen presentation to and activation of naïve T cells.

name: convergent evolution
definition: Independent evolution of similarity between molecules or between species.

name: convertase
definition: Enzyme activity that converts complement protein into its reactive form by cleaving it.

name: Coombs test
definition: Diagnostic test using anti-immunoglobulin (Ig) to agglutinate antibody-coated erythrocytes.
synonyms: direct Coombs test|direct antiglobulin test (DAT)|indirect Coombs test|indirect antiglobulin test (IAT)

name: coreceptor
definition: Cell surface protein receptor that recognizes a substance bound to a primary receptor, and binds to a signaling molecule that thereby enhances the activity of another receptor.

name: corticosteroid
definition: Any of the family of steroid molecules that are produced in the adrenal cortex, or their synthetic analogs.

name: co-stimulation
definition: Delivery of a second signal, in addition to that of antigen binding or antigen presentation, that is required for lymphocyte proliferation.

name: counter-regulation hypothesis
definition: Hypothesis that all types of infection early in childhood may protect against the development of atopy by driving the production of cytokines such as interleukin-10 (IL-10) and transforming growth factor $\ce{\upbeta\!}$ ($\ce{TGF\mbox{-}\upbeta\!}$), which downregulate both Th1 and Th2 responses.

name: Crohn disease
definition: Chronic inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) thought to result from an abnormal overresponsiveness to commensal gut flora.

name: cross-matching
definition: 1) Test for determining the compatibility between the blood of a donor and that of a recipient before transfusion; the clumping of erythrocytes indicates incompatibility. 2) Test for determining tissue compatibility between a transplant donor and the recipient before transplantation, in which the recipient’s serum is tested for antibodies that may react with the lymphocytes or other cells of the donor. 3) Process of performing one of these tests.

name: cross-presentation
definition: Activation of CD8+ lymphocytes by the presentation of exogenous antigens in association with major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class I molecules.

name: cross-reacting antibody
definition: Antibody that is able to react with an antigen that did not specifically stimulate its production.

name: cross-reacting antigen
definition: Antigen that is able to react with an antibody induced by a different antigen. Note: The two antigens may share the same antigenic determinants or carry determinants that are sufficiently alike stereochemically to enable the antibody to react with both. Antigen that has an identical structure in two strains of microorganism, so that antibody raised against one strain will react with the other strain.

name: cross sensitivity
definition: State of immunological hypersensitivity to one substance that predisposes an individual to sensitivity to other substances that are related in chemical structure (cross-reacting antigens).

name: cross-tolerance
definition: State of immunological tolerance to one substance produced by priming an animal with another substance that bears a cross-reacting antigen.

name: cryoglobulin
definition: Immunoglobulin (Ig) that forms insoluble aggregates at temperatures below body temperature.

name: cryoglobulinemic vasculitis
definition: Cutaneous or systemic vasculitis caused by cold-labile proteins (cryoglobulins, cryofibrinogen) that leads to increased viscosity, protein precipitation or gelatinification, complement activation, and endothelial cell damage, especially in the cold.

name: cryptic epitope
definition: Epitope that cannot be recognized by a lymphocyte receptor until the antigen has been broken down and processed or modified by hapten binding.

name: cutaneous lymphocyte antigen
definition: Cell-surface molecule that is involved in lymphocyte homing to the skin in humans.

name: cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
definition: Malignant growth of T cells that home to the skin.

name: cytokine
definition: Any of a group of soluble small proteins released from a variety of cells, typically of the immune system, that affect cell behavior in an autocrine or paracrine fashion.

name: cytokine capture assay
definition: Method to detect cytokine release by injecting an animal with a neutralizing biotinylated antibody to the cytokine, which inhibits its utilization and allows its accumulation in the blood. Recovered cytokineantibody complexes are then measured in an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) with an antibody to a second epitope on the cytokine.

name: cytokine profile
definition: Characteristic pattern of cytokine production associated with a defined immunological state.

name: cytokine release assay
definition: Method of quantifying cytokines released by viable cells, using cytokine-specific antibodies.

name: immune cytolysis
definition: 1) Cell lysis caused by a lesion produced by the action of complement proteins on the antibody-coated plasma membrane of a cell. 2) Cell lysis following plasma membrane reaction with perforins released by natural killer (NK) cells.

name: cytopenia
definition: Decrease in the number of one or more types of blood cells.

name: cytotoxic
definition: Causing damage to cell structure or function.

name: cytotoxic T lymphocyte
definition: Any of a subset of T lymphocytes bearing the CD8 surface marker and able to kill target cells [infected somatic or tumor cells, recognized by the antigen receptor complex (TCR/CD3)] after induction of a specific immune response to the antigens bound to major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class I molecules.
synonyms: CD8+ T cell|cytolytic T cell|cytotoxic T cell|killer T cell

name: cytotoxic T lymphocyte antigen 4
definition: High affinity receptor for B7 molecules expressed on T cells, binding of which inhibits T cell activation.

name: cytotoxic T lymphocyte assay
definition: Assay based on quantitation of cell death caused by sensitized lymphocytes or splenocytes cultured with a fixed number of tumor or other target cells that have been prelabeled with \(\ce{^{51}Cr}\). The \(\ce{^{51}Cr}\) is taken up and reversibly binds to cytosolic proteins. When these target cells are incubated with sensitized lymphocytes, the target cells are killed and the \(\ce{^{51}Cr}\) is released.

name: cytotoxin
definition: Substance with a specific toxic effect on certain cells.

name: DEC-205
definition: Surface antigen characteristic of dendritic cells.

name: DNA vaccination
definition: Injection of DNA into muscle, followed by its transcription and translation into a protein or proteins that elicit antibody and T-cell responses.

name: DP, DQ, and DR molecules
definition: Major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class II molecules occurring on human B lymphocytes and antigen-presenting cells (APCs).

name: danger hypothesis
definition: Hypothesis that suggests it is not foreignness of a molecule per se but rather its ability to cause cell damage or stress that induces an immune response. Often implicated in causation of idiosyncratic drug reactions.

name: death receptor
definition: Cell-surface receptor whose binding to extracellular ligands stimulates apoptosis in the receptor-bearing cell through the extrinsic pathway.

name: death domain
definition: Protein-interaction domain originally discovered in proteins involved in programmed cell death or apoptosis.

name: decay-accelerating factor
definition: Cell-surface molecule that protects cells from lysis by complement.

name: defensin
definition: Any member of a family of oligopeptides made within the body, notably by neutrophils and macrophages, and having potent antimicrobial properties.

name: degranulation
definition: Cell reaction that releases antimicrobial cytotoxic molecules and other substances (e.g., histamine) from secretory vesicles called granules found inside some cells.

name: delayed-type hypersensitivity
definition: Form of T cell-mediated immunity in which the ultimate effector cell is the activated mononuclear phagocyte (macrophage); the response of DTH appears fully over \(\pu{24}\) to \(\pu{48 h}\). Previous exposure is required.
synonyms: DTH|Gell and Coombs Type IV reaction

name: delayed-type hypersensitivity assay
definition: In vivo assay of cell-mediated immune response, elicited by antigen in the skin and mediated by CD4+ Th1 cells.

name: dendritic cell
definition: Ameboid cell that is major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class II-positive, Fc receptor-negative, and presents processed antigens to T cells in the T-cell areas of secondary lymphoid tissues.

name: immune complex deposition
definition: Precipitation of immune complex in organs and tissues, often causing local inflammation.

name: dermatitis
definition: Inflammation of the skin showing redness, swelling, infiltration, scaling, and sometimes vesicles and blisters: contact dermatitis is due to local exposure and may be caused by irritation, allergy, or photocontact dermatitis.

name: dermatomyositis
definition: Disease characterized by the presence of inflammation of the skin and muscles.

name: desensitization
definition: Generally transient state of specific non-reactivity in a previously sensitized individual, resulting from repeated antigen exposures.

name: diabetes mellitus type 1
definition: Disease in which the \(\ce{\upbeta\ cells}\) of the pancreatic islets of Langerhans are destroyed with the result that no insulin is produced.

name: diapedesis
definition: Movement of blood cells, particularly leukocytes, from the blood across blood vessel walls into tissues.

name: differential
definition: Reported blood count that distinguishes the percentages of the different blood cells present.

name: differential splicing
definition: Utilization and splicing of different exons from a primary RNA transcript in order to generate different mRNA sequences.

name: differentiation antigen
definition: Cell surface molecule expressed at a particular stage of development or on cells of a given lineage.

name: disintegrin and metalloproteinase domain-containing protein 33
definition: Member of the ADAM (A Disintegrin And Metalloproteinase domain) family of transmembrane proteins, possibly related to asthma susceptibility.

name: diversity gene
definition: Small segment of immunoglobulin (Ig) heavy-chain or T-cell receptor DNA between the variable (V) gene and joining (J) gene segments, coding for the third hypervariable region of the receptors.

name: domain
definition: Structural element of a polypeptide.

name: dot plot
definition: Two-dimensional graphical representation of individual data points.

name: double-negative cell
definition: Immature T cell in the thymus that lacks expression of the two coreceptors, CD4 and CD8.

name: double-positive cell
definition: Immature T cell in the thymus that is characterized by expression of both CD4 and CD8 coreceptor proteins.

name: draining lymph node
definition: Lymph node that is downstream of a site of infection and thus receives antigens and microbes from the site via the lymphatic system.

name: Draize test
definition: Context: ocular; Test for potential to cause irritation to the eye in which the test substance is applied directly to the eye of restrained rabbits. Note: Widely criticized as unethical. Now often replaced with an acute eye irritation test using cadaveric chicken eyes. Context: skin; Test for the potential of a material to cause irritation or corrosion following local dermal application. Generally performed with rabbits.

name: drug-induced autoimmunity
definition: Immune-mediated idiosyncratic drug reaction against self-antigens.

name: drug-induced lupus
definition: Idiosyncratic drug reaction similar in character to systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and having antinuclear antibodies (ANA), but generally milder in nature and resolving when drug exposure is discontinued.

name: eczema
definition: Acute or chronic skin inflammation with erythema, papules, vesicles, pustules, scales, crusts, or scabs, alone or in combination, of varied etiology.

name: effector cell
definition: Cell that carries out an immune function, e.g., cytokine release, cytotoxicity.

name: elicitation
definition: Production of a cell-mediated or antibody-mediated allergic response by exposure of a sensitized individual to an allergen.

name: endogenous
definition: Produced within or caused by factors within an organism.

name: endosome
definition: Intracellular smooth surfaced vesicle in which endocytosed material passes on its way to the lysosomes.

name: endotoxin
definition: Pathogenic cell wall-associated lipopolysaccharides of Gram-negative bacteria.

name: enhancing antibody
definition: Antibody that binds to an antibody-antigen complex or idiotypic-anti-idiotypic antibody complex and strengthens the interaction.

name: enterotoxin
definition: Toxin affecting intestinal cells and thus causing food poisoning.

name: enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay
definition: Procedure for detection or quantitation of an antibody or antigen using a ligand (e.g., an anti-immunoglobulin) conjugated to an enzyme that changes the color of a substrate.

name: enzyme-linked immunospot assay
definition: Adaptation of enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) in which cells are placed over antibodies or antigens attached to a plastic surface. The antigen or antibody traps the cells’ secreted products, which can then be detected using an enzyme-coupled antibody that cleaves a colorless substrate to make a localized colored spot. This allows quantitation of the number of cells producing a given product such as a cytokine.

name: eosinophil
definition: Circulating granular leukocyte (granulocyte) having prominent granules that stain specifically by eosin and containing numerous lysosomes.

name: eosinophil chemotactic factor of anaphylaxis
definition: Cytokine that facilitates anaphylaxis and attracts eosinophils during substrate release by mast cells.

name: eotaxin
definition: CC chemokine that acts predominantly on eosinophils.

name: epitope retrieval
definition: Treatment of denatured antigen with heat or other agents in order to regenerate (unmask) lost antibody-binding capacity.

name: epitope spreading
definition: Increase in the number of epitopes targeted by autoantibodies and/or T cells. The epitopes may be on the same autoantigen (intramolecular epitope spreading) and/or on other autoantigens (intermolecular epitope spreading).

name: Epstein–Barr virus
definition: Virus responsible for infectious mononucleosis and Burkitt’s lymphoma. This virus is used to immortalize human B lymphocytes in vitro.

name: equivalence
definition: Ratio of antibody to antigen at which immunoprecipitation of the reactants is virtually complete.

name: equivalence zone
definition: Range of concentrations of antigen and antibody in which neither is in significant excess in a precipitin reaction.

name: erythema
definition: Redness of the skin produced by congestion of the capillaries.

name: erythroblastosis fetalis
definition: Two potentially disabling or fatal blood disorders in infants: Rhesus (Rh) factor incompatibility disease and ABO blood group incompatibility disease.

name: erythrocyte
definition: Red blood cell.

name: erythropoiesis
definition: Erythrocyte production.

name: erythropoietin
definition: Glycoprotein hormone that stimulates the production of erythrocytes by stem cells in bone marrow.

name: euglobulin
definition: Member of a class of proteins insoluble in water but soluble in saline solutions.

name: exocytosis
definition: Release of the content of an intracellular vesicle to the exterior of the cell.

name: exotoxin
definition: Pathogenic protein secreted by bacteria.

name: extravasation
definition: Movement of cells or fluid from within blood vessels to the surrounding tissues.

name: exudate
definition: Extravascular fluid containing proteins and cellular debris that accumulates during inflammation.

name: Fab fragment
definition: Monovalent antigen-binding (‘ab’) fragment obtained following papain digestion of immunoglobulin (Ig). It consists of an intact light chain and the N-terminal VH and C H1 domains of the heavy chain.

name: F(ab')2 fragment
definition: Bivalent antigen-binding fragment obtained following pepsin digestion of immunoglobulin. Consists of both light chains and the N-terminal part of both heavy chains linked by disulfide bonds.

name: Fc fragment
definition: Crystallizable, non-antigen-binding fragment of an immunoglobulin (Ig) molecule obtained following papain digestion. Consists of the C-terminal portion of both heavy chains, responsible for binding to Fc receptors and complement factor C1q.

name: Fc receptor
definition: Receptors expressed on a wide range of cells, interacting with the Fc portion of immunoglobulins (Ig) belonging to various isotypes.

name: Fd fragment
definition: Heavy chain portion of an immunoglobulin (Ig) N-terminal to the papain hydrolysis site, after reduction and separation of the light chain portion.

name: fMLP peptide
definition: Formyl-methionyl-leucyl-phenylalanine, a chemoattractant (see chemotactic factor, chemotaxis) derived from degradation of bacterial or mitochondrial proteins. It causes neutrophil activation.

name: Foxp3
definition: Transcription repressor that is specifically expressed in CD4+CD25+ T cells.

name: Fv fragment
definition: Variable (V) region fragment of an antibody heavy chain or light chain.

name: familial cold autoinflammatory syndrome
definition: Episodic autoinflammatory disease, induced by exposure to cold, and caused by mutations in the gene CSA1, encoding cryopyrin.

name: familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis
definition: Progressive and potentially lethal inflammatory disease caused by an inherited deficiency of perforin.

name: farmer’s lung
definition: Hypersensitivity disease caused by the interaction of immunoglobulin G (IgG) antibodies with large amounts of an inhaled allergen in the alveolar wall of the lung, causing alveolar wall inflammation and compromising gas exchange.

name: Fas
definition: Member of the tumor necrosis factor (TNF) receptor gene family. Engagement of Fas on the surface of the cell by the Fas ligand (CD178) present on cytotoxic cells can trigger apoptosis in the Fas-bearing target cell.

name: fetal antigens
definition: Human cancer cell antigens, which cross-react serologically with antigens normally expressed by embryonic tissue, e.g., carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA), or $\ce{\upalpha\!\mbox{-}fetoprotein}$ (AFP).

name: fetal tolerance
definition: Lack of rejection of a fetal allograft carrying paternal major histocompatibility complex (MHC) and minor histocompatibility antigens that differ from those of the mother.

name: fibrinolysis
definition: Enzymatic lysis of a fibrin clot.

name: fibrinolytic
definition: Pertaining to, characterized by, or causing the breakdown of fibrin (fibrinolysis), usually by the action of plasmin.

name: first line of defence
definition: Surface tissues, notably the skin, respiratory tract, and gastrointestinal tract.

name: flow cytometry
definition: Method of sorting and measuring types of cells by fluorescent labeling of markers on the surface of the cells. It is sometimes referred to as fluorescence-assisted (or activated) cell sorting (FACS) analysis.

name: fluorescein isothiocyanate
definition: Green fluorescent dye used to 'tag' antibodies for use in immunofluorescence.

name: fluorescence-activated cell sorting
definition: Fluorescence-assisted cell sorting.

name: fluorescent antibody
definition: Antibody conjugated to a fluorescent dye such as fluorescein isothiocyanate (FITC).

name: follicular dendritic cell
definition: Major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class II-negative Fc receptor-positive dendritic cell which bears immune complexes on its surface and is probably involved in the generation of antibody-secreting cells and maintenance of B-cell memory (see memory cell) in germinal centers.

name: footpad test
definition: Test for allergic contact dermatitis in which the test substance is injected into the front footpad of a guinea pig and challenge is performed seven days later.

name: Forssman antigen
definition: Glycolipid heterophile antigen (globopentosylceramide) expressed on cell surfaces during embryonic and adult life in rodents and other mammals, and found in many pathogens, but probably not in humans.

name: framework region
definition: One of several relatively conserved amino acid sequences that flank the hypervariable regions in immunoglobulin (Ig) and T-cell receptor (TCR) variable (V) regions and maintain a common overall structure for all V region domains.

name: Freund’s adjuvant
definition: Complete Freund’s adjuvant is an emulsion of aqueous antigen in mineral oil that contains heat-killed Mycobacteria.

name: γ:δ T cell
definition: Lymphocyte whose T-cell receptor (TCR) is a heterodimer of a \(\ce{\upgamma\mbox{-}chain}\) and a \(\ce{\updelta\mbox{-}chain}\).

name: γ:δ T-cell receptor
definition: T-cell receptor (TCR) composed of two different glycoprotein chains, designated \(\upgamma\) and \(\updelta\), assembled in a \(\ce{\upgamma\mbox{:}\updelta\ heterodimer}\).

name: γ-interferon
definition: Member of a group of cytokines, the interferons, which has as its primary action the activation of macrophages and can induce cells to resist viral replication.

name: gp120
definition: Viral glycoprotein, non-covalently associated with gp41 in the viral envelope of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV).

name: gammaglobulin
definition: One of a group of serum proteins, mostly immunoglobulins (Ig), which have the greatest mobility towards the cathode during electrophoresis.

name: autoimmune gastritis
definition: Autoimmune-mediated destruction of the gastric mucosa that may result in the development of pernicious anemia.

name: Gell and Coombs classification
definition: Classification of immune mechanisms of tissue injury into four types: type I, immediate-type hypersensitivity reactions, mediated by interaction of immunoglobulin E (IgE) antibody and antigen causing the release of histamine and other mediators; type II, antibody-mediated hypersensitivity reactions, due to antibody–antigen interactions on cell surfaces; type III, immune complex, local or general inflammatory responses due to formation of circulating immune complexes and their deposition in tissues; and type IV cell-mediated hypersensitivity reactions, initiated by sensitized T lymphocytes either by release of lymphokines or by T-cell-mediated cytotoxicity [see cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL)].

name: gene knockout
definition: Method of disabling a specific gene by homologous recombination with an introduced DNA construct designed for that purpose.

name: gene rearrangement
definition: Structural alteration in a chromosome that changes the order of its genetic loci, occurring by DNA recombination, e.g., during development or in some cancers.

name: germ-free
definition: Descriptor applied to animals (usually mice) raised in the complete absence of intestinal and other microorganisms.

name: germ line
definition: Referring to genes in their unrearranged state rather than those rearranged for production of immunoglobulin (Ig) or T-cell receptor (TCR) molecules.

name: germinal center
definition: Discrete area within lymph nodes and spleen where B-cell maturation and memory development occur.

name: giant cell
definition: Large multinucleate cell derived from fused macrophages and often present in granulomas.

name: glomerulonephritis
definition: Any of a group of kidney diseases involving inflammation of the renal glomeruli, often as a result of antibody–antigen complexes that localize in the kidney.

name: glomerulonephropathy
definition: Disease of the renal glomeruli, which may show either thickening of the glomerular basement membrane due to the accretion of proteins or a minimal change disease, in which there is functional damage but little structural change by light microscopy.

name: glutamic acid decarboxylase
definition: Main autoantigen in diabetes mellitus type 1 and stiff-person syndrome (a neurological autoimmune disease).

name: gluten
definition: 1) Any of the prolamins found in cereal grains, especially the prolamins in wheat, rye, barley, and possibly oats, which cause digestive disorders, notably celiac disease. 2) In wheat, mixture of water-insoluble proteins, including gliadins, that give wheat dough its elastic texture.

name: Goodpasture syndrome
definition: Autoimmune disease of humans in which glomerulonephritis and pulmonary hemorrhage are produced by complement-mediated tissue damage caused by antibodies directed against the renal glomerular and alveolar basement membranes.

name: graft rejection
definition: Destruction of grafted tissue by host lymphocytes following an adaptive immune response.

name: graft-versus-host disease
definition: Disease that occurs following bone marrow transplantation between genetically non-identical people and in which mature T cells in the transplanted bone marrow attack and destroy the recipients tissues.

name: graft-versus-host reaction
definition: Reaction occurring when T lymphocytes present in a graft recognize and attack host cells.

name: granulocyte colony-stimulating factor
definition: Hematopoietic (see hematopoiesis) factor augmenting the production of neutrophils in the bone marrow.

name: granulocyte–macrophage colony-stimulating factor
definition: Cytokine that stimulates production of granulocytes and monocytes from stem cells.

name: granulocytopenia
definition: Decreased circulating granulocytes.

name: granuloma
definition: Mass or nodule of granulation tissue, with actively growing fibroblasts and capillary buds, characterized by the presence of aggregates of modified macrophages resembling epithelial cells (epithelioid histiocytes), and lymphocytes, surrounded by a rim of giant multinucleate cells, either of the Langerhans or foreign body type.

name: granzyme
definition: Member of a family of serine esterases present in the granules of cytotoxic T lymphocytes and natural killer (NK) cells. They induce apoptosis in the target cell that they enter through perforin channels inserted into the target cell membrane by the cytotoxic lymphocyte.

name: Graves disease
definition: Hyperthyroidism associated with diffuse hyperplastic goitre resulting from production of a thyroid-stimulating hormone receptor (TSHR)-binding autoantibody.

name: guinea pig maximization test
definition: Skin sensitization test for allergic contact dermatitis in which shaved guinea pig skin is exposed to intradermal injections of a test agent together with complete Freund’s adjuvant, followed by an occlusive patch for boosting for \(\pu{48 h}\) beginning on day 7, and challenged on day 21.

name: gut-associated lymphoid tissue
definition: Lymphoid cells and tissues lining the mucosa that seem to serve as the first point of antigen contact via this route, including Peyer’s patches, the appendix, tonsils, adenoids, and mesenteric lymph nodes.

name: H-2
definition: Region of mouse chromosome 17 coding the major histocompatibility complex (MHC).

name: H-2 complex
definition: Mouse major histocompatibility complex (MHC) coded by H-2.

name: hairy cell leukemia
definition: B-cell neoplasm, usually occurring during middle age, constituting about \(\pu{2\%}\) of all leukemias and responding well to chemotherapy. The neoplastic cells have fine, hairlike surfaces.

name: haplotype
definition: Set of allelic variants present at a given genetic region.

name: haptenic
definition: Able to act as a hapten.

name: Hashimoto thyroiditis
definition: Autoimmune disease where the body’s own antibodies attack the cells of the thyroid.

name: hay fever
definition: Allergic condition affecting the mucous membranes of the upper respiratory tract and the eyes, characterized by nasal discharge, sneezing, and itchy, watery eyes; and usually caused by an abnormal sensitivity to airborne pollen.

name: heat shock proteins
definition: Evolutionarily conserved proteins, found in many organisms, that are induced upon exposure of cells to various types of stress, including heat, oxidative or hypoxic stress, and deprivation of nutrients or essential ions.

name: heavy chain
definition: Larger of the two types of polypeptide chain found in immunoglobulin (Ig) molecules.

name: helper T lymphocyte
definition: Member of a subclass of T lymphocytes that provides help (in the form of cytokines and/or cognate interactions) necessary for the expression of effector function by other cells in the immune system.
synonyms: T helper cell|Th|helper T cell|helper cell

name: hemagglutinin
definition: Any molecule that agglutinates erythrocytes.

name: hematopoietic stem cell
definition: Self-renewing stem cell that is capable of giving rise to all of the formed elements of the blood (i.e., leukocytes, erythrocytes, and platelets).

name: hemolytic anemia
definition: Anemia resulting from the lysis of erythrocytes.

name: heparin-induced thrombocytopenia
definition: Most frequent antibody-mediated drug-induced thrombocytopenia, which occurs in \(\pu{1-}\pu{2\%}\) of patients treated with heparin intravenously for longer than four days.

name: hereditary angioneurotic edema
definition: Clinical name for a genetic deficiency of the C1 inhibitor of the complement system.

name: heteroantigen
definition: Identical or similar cross-reacting antigen shared by several species (e.g., Forssman antigen).Antibodies produced against one of these antigens will also react with the other antigens of the set even though these are derived from a different species; such antibodies are also called heterophile antibodies.

name: heterologous antibody
definition: Antibody derived from another individual of the same species or another species.

name: heterologous antigen
definition: Antigen that reacts with an antibody other than the one whose formation it induced.

name: heterophagy
definition: Digestion of exogenous material taken up by a cell by phagocytosis or pinocytosis, following fusion of the phagocytic or pinocytic vacuole with a lysosome.

name: heterophile antibody
definition: Antibody raised against an antigen from one species, which also reacts against antigens from other species.

name: heterophile antigen
definition: Antigen that stimulates production in a vertebrate of antibodies capable of reacting with tissue components having related antigens in a wide range of other species.

name: heterozygous
definition: Possessing different alleles at a given locus on the two homologous chromosomes.

name: high endothelial venule
definition: Specialized venule in lymphoid tissues that has walls permeable to migrating lymphocytes, allowing them to move from blood into the lymphoid tissues.

name: highly active antiretroviral therapy
definition: Approach to the treatment of acquired immune deficiency syndrome (AIDS) patients involving a combination of nucleoside analogs, which prevent reverse transcription, with drugs that inhibit responses to the virus.

name: high-mobility group box protein
definition: Any of a group of universal sensors of nucleic acids, required for the induction of transmembrane and cytoplasmic receptor-mediated innate immune responses.

name: hinge region
definition: Amino acids between the Fab and Fc regions of immunoglobulin (Ig) that permit flexibility of the molecule.

name: histaminosis
definition: Histamine intolerance, which may contribute to food intolerance as part of a pseudoallergic reaction.

name: histocompatibility
definition: Relationship between a tissue or organ donor and a recipient who have sufficient similarity in major histocompatibility complex (MHC) antigens to avoid rejection of a graft.

name: histoincompatibility
definition: Relationship between a tissue or organ donor and a recipient who have sufficient differences in major histocompatibility complex (MHC) antigens to cause rejection of a graft.

name: hives
definition: Vascular reaction pattern of the skin marked by the transient appearance of smooth, slightly elevated patches (wheals) that are either more red or more pale than the surrounding skin and are accompanied by severe itching.

name: Hodgkin disease
definition: Immune system tumor characterized by large cells called Reed–Sternberg cells that derive from mutated B-lineage cells.

name: homing
definition: Movement of leukocytes to specific locations in the body.

name: homing receptor
definition: Cell surface molecule that directs leukocytes to specific locations in the body.

name: homocytotropic antibody
definition: Antibody that binds preferentially to cells from the same species rather than to cells from other species.

name: homozygous
definition: Possessing the same allele at a given locus on the two homologous chromosomes.

name: horror autotoxicus
definition: Term (Latin: dread of self-poisoning) to describe the body’s innate aversion to immunological self destruction.

name: host defense
definition: Ability of an individual to resist invasion by opportunistic agents and production of disease associated with exposure to microorganisms, foreign tissue, and particulates, as well as certain types of neoplasia. Host defense may be either nonspecific (innate or natural immunity) or specific (adaptive or acquired immunity) in nature.

name: host-resistance assay
definition: Evaluation of host resistance in rodents to in vivo challenge with an infectious organism under normal conditions and after pharmacological and nutritional alterations of the immune system.

name: human immunodeficiency virus
definition: Causative agent of acquired immune deficiency syndrome (AIDS).

name: humanized antibody
definition: Genetically engineered monoclonal antibody of non-human origin in which all but the antigen-binding complementarity-determining region (CDR) sequences have been replaced with sequences derived from human antibodies.

name: human leukocyte antigen
definition: Antigen coded by genes of the human major histocompatibility complex (MHC).

name: human leukocyte antigen polymorphism
definition: Discontinuous genetic variation in the major histocompatibility complex (MHC) that results in the occurrence of several different forms of MHC molecules among people.

name: human leukocyte antigen type I
definition: Molecules that enable the body to recognize infected cells and tumor cells and destroy them with cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTLs).

name: human leukocyte antigen type II
definition: Molecules that enable CD4+ lymphocytes to recognize epitopes of exogenous antigens and discriminate self from non-self.

name: humoral
definition: Pertaining to extracellular fluid such as plasma and lymph.

name: humoral immune response
definition: Immune response in which specific antibodies induce the effector functions (such as phagocytosis and activation of the complement system).

name: humoral immunity
definition: Specific immune response that is mediated primarily by humoral factors circulating in solution in the blood plasma and lymph (i.e., antibodies and complement).

name: hypergammaglobulinemia
definition: Increase of gammaglobulins in the blood by paraproteinemia or increased production of immunoglobulins (Ig).

name: hyperimmunoglobulin E syndrome
definition: Rare primary immunodeficiency syndrome characterized by recurrent severe staphylococcal skin abscesses (hence Job syndrome), lung infections, and markedly elevated serum immunoglobulin E (IgE) levels.

name: hyperimmunoglobulin M syndrome
definition: Primary T cell defect due to mutations in the CD40 ligand (CD40L), characterized by recurrent (opportunistic) infections and very low levels of immunoglobulin G (IgG) and immunoglobulin A (IgA).

name: hyperreactivity
definition: Abnormally increased response to a stimulus.

name: hypersensitivity
definition: State in which an individual reacts with allergic effects following exposure to a certain substance (allergen) after having been exposed previously to the same substance. It is sometimes used loosely for any increased response.

name: hypersensitivity pneumonitis
definition: Immune-mediated inflammatory disease of the lung parenchyma caused by exposure to an inhaled chemical allergen or organic dust.

name: hypersensitization
definition: Development of excessive immune reactivity to an antigen.

name: hypersusceptibility
definition: Adverse immunological effects in an individual occurring under conditions of exposure to an allergen that result in no effects in the great majority of the population, or an individual exhibiting exaggerated effects in comparison with the great majority of those showing some adverse effects.

name: hypervariable region
definition: Amino acid sequence within the immunoglobulin (Ig) and T-cell receptor (TCR) variable (V) regions that shows the greatest variability and contributes most to the antigen or peptide-major histocompatibility complex (MHC) molecule binding site.

name: hypogammaglobulinemia
definition: Immunodeficiency state marked by abnormally low levels of all classes of immunoglobulins (Ig), associated with increased susceptibility to infectious diseases.

name: hyposensitization therapy
definition: Dermal application of a selected allergen to an allergic person in stepwise increasing dosage, with the aim of reducing the immune system’s tendency for the corresponding allergic reaction.

name: Ia antigen
definition: Isoantigen encoded by the Ia region of the mouse major histocompatibility complex (H-2 complex).

name: idiopathic
definition: Term that describes a 'primary' symptom or disease in which no underlying cause or associated disorder can be found.

name: idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura
definition: Thrombocytopenia of unknown cause, probably related to the production of anti-platelet antibodies, and leading to bruising (purpura).

name: idiosyncratic drug reaction
definition: Rare and unpredictable adverse drug reaction occurring only in susceptible individuals.

name: idiotype
definition: The combined antigenic determinants (idiotopes) expressed in the variable (V) region of immunoglobulins (Ig) of an individual that determine antibody specificity to a particular antigen.

name: idiotype network
definition: Regulatory network based on interactions of anti-idiotypic antibodies and idiotypes present on antibodies and T-cell receptors (TCRs), resulting in feedback inhibition of ongoing B cell or T cell responses.

name: immature
definition: Describing cells that are not fully developed and unable to participate immediately in an immune response.

name: immediate-type hypersensitivity
definition: Reaction provoked by re-exposure to an antigen (allergen) that causes plasma cells to secrete immunoglobulin E (IgE) which binds to Fc receptors on the surface of tissue mast cells and blood basophils, sensitizing them, so that later exposure to the same allergen cross-links the bound IgE, leading to degranulation and the secretion of pharmacologically active mediators such as histamine, leukotriene, and prostaglandin that act immediately on the surrounding tissues.

name: immune adherence
definition: Attachment of particulate antigen coated with C3b (see complement) to cells expressing C3b receptors, which results in enhanced phagocytosis of bacteria by macrophages.

name: immune complex
definition: Product of an antigen–antibody reaction, which may also contain components of the complement system.

name: immune complex disease
definition: Illness resulting from deposition of antigen–antibody complexes in tissues.

name: immune deviation
definition: Regulatory mechanism of the preferential activation of one aspect (cellular or humoral) of the adaptive immune system at the expense of the other.

name: immune elimination
definition: Removal of pathogens or tumor cells by the immune system; the first step of immunoediting of tumors.

name: immune enhancement
definition: Therapeutic stimulation of the immune response, especially in tumor therapy.

name: immune equilibrium
definition: State in carcinogenesis where there is an equilibrium between elimination of tumor cells by the immune system and growth of non-immunogenic tumor cells; the second step in immunoediting.

name: immune escape
definition: Biological feature of an infectious agent or of a tumor cell that prevents its elimination by the immune system. Such a feature can be acquired by a selection process. Immune escape is the third step in immunoediting of tumors.

name: immune evasion
definition: Property of a pathogen that results in avoidance of attack by the immune system, e.g., because of reduced phagocytosis, lack of recognition by the innate immune system, or suppression of the immune response.

name: immune modulation
definition: Alteration of the immune response to alleviate harmful effects of the immune system or to promote its activity by changes in regulatory factors; often part of deliberate therapeutic intervention.

name: immune regulation
definition: Capacity of the immune system to regulate itself so that an immune response does not become excessive and cause tissue damage, autoimmune reactions, or allergic reactions.

name: immune reserve hypothesis
definition: Hypothesis that the immune response involves multiple redundancies that are capable of compensating for acute reductions in certain immune functions.

name: immune response-associated protein
definition: Protein found in antigen-presenting cells (APCs) and B lymphocytes in mice.

name: immune response genes
definition: Genes, including those within the major histocompatibility complex (MHC), that together determine the overall level of immune response to a given antigen.

name: immune surveillance
definition: Recognition, and in some cases elimination, of tumor cells by the immune system before they become clinically detectable.

name: immune system
definition: Integrated network of organs, glands, and tissues that has evolved to protect the body from foreign substances, including bacteria, viruses, and other infection-causing parasites and pathogens.

name: immunity
definition: Inherited, acquired, or induced resistance to infection by a specific pathogen.

name: immunoactivation
definition: Activation of the immune system as a whole to react more rapidly to antigens.

name: immunoactivator
definition: Substance that activates the immune system as a whole to react more rapidly to antigens.

name: immunoadsorption
definition: Method for removal of antibody or antigen by allowing it to bind to a corresponding antigen or antibody immobilized in the solid phase.

name: immunoblot
definition: Supporting substrate [often a nitrocellulose, nylon, or poly(vinylidene fluoride) membrane] onto which proteins that have been separated by gel electrophoresis are transferred and then identified by the binding of specific antibodies.

name: immunocompetence
definition: Having the ability to exhibit an immune response.

name: immunocompromised
definition: Unable to mount a full or effective immune response.

name: immunoconjugate
definition: Antibody or antibody fragment to which a functional molecule, such as a drug, has been chemically linked.

name: immunocytokine
definition: Antibody or antibody fragment to which a cytokine has been chemically linked.

name: immunodeficiency
definition: Inability to produce a normal repertoire of antibodies or immunologically sensitized T lymphocytes, especially in response to specific antigens.

name: immunodominant epitope
definition: Epitope in an antigen that is preferentially recognized by T cells, which then come to dominate the immune response.

name: immunodysregulation–polyendocrinopathy–enteropathy, X-linked
definition: X-linked syndrome characterized by immunodysregulation, polyendocrinopathy (diabetes mellitus type 1, thyroiditis), hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, dermatitis, and enteropathy, caused by mutations in the gene encoding Foxp3.

name: immunoediting
definition: Process of continuing immunosuppression of immunogenic tumor cells, which may finally result in the selection of non-immunogenic tumor cells. It consists of the steps immune elimination, immune equilibrium, and immune escape.

name: immunofluorescence
definition: Technique for detection of cell- or tissue-associated antigens by the use of a fluorescently tagged ligand, e.g., an anti-immunoglobulin (Ig) conjugated to fluorescein isothiocyanate (FITC).

name: immunoglobulin A
definition: Class of immunoglobulin (Ig) characterized by $\ce{\upalpha\!}$ heavy chains.

name: immunoglobulin D
definition: Class of immunoglobulin (Ig) characterized by $\updelta\!$ heavy chains.

name: immunoglobulin E
definition: Class of immunoglobulin (Ig) characterized by $\upvarepsilon\!$ heavy chains.

name: immunoglobulin Y
definition: Immunoglobulin (Ig) found in chickens.

name: immunoglobulin E-binding Fc receptors
definition: High-affinity IgE-binding ${\rm{Fc\mbox{-}}}\upvarepsilon\!{\rm{\mbox{-}R}}$ type I receptors are expressed on mast cells and basophils and interact with IgE antibodies with high affinity.

name: immunoglobulin E-mediated hypersensitivity
definition: State in which an individual reacts with allergic effects caused fundamentally by the reaction of antigen-specific immunoglobulin E (IgE) following exposure to a certain substance (allergen) after having been exposed previously to the same substance.

name: immunoglobulin G
definition: Class of immunoglobulin (Ig) characterized by \(\upgamma\) heavy chains.

name: immunoglobulin M
definition: Class of immunoglobulin (Ig) characterized by \(\upmu\) heavy chains.

name: immunoglobulin gene superfamily
definition: Genes encoding proteins containing one or more immunoglobulin (Ig) domains (homology units) that are homologous to either Ig variable (V) region or constant (C) region domains. Cell surface and soluble molecules mediating recognition, adhesion, or binding functions in and outside the immune system, derived from the same precursor, belong to this family of molecules (e.g., immunoglobulin, T-cell receptor (TCR), major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class I and class II molecules, CD4, CD8, and $\ce{Fc\upgamma\!R}$).

name: immunoglobulin superfamily
definition: Large family of proteins characterized by possession of 'immunoglobulin-type' domains of approximately 110 amino acids folded into two \(\ce{\upbeta\mbox{-}pleated sheets}\). Members include immunoglobulins \(A\), \(E\), \(G\), \(M\) (IgA, IgE, IgG, and IgM), T-cell receptors (TCRs), and human leukocyte antigen (HLA) major histocompatibility complex (MHC) molecules.

name: immunohistochemistry
