definition: Detection of cell-associated molecules in the light microscope with antibodies labeled with enzymes that change a substrate into a colored precipitate.

name: immunological ignorance
definition: Absence of a pathogenic autoimmune response in spite of the concomitant presence in the host of the autoantigen and T cells bearing the specific autoreactive T-cell receptor (TCR).

name: immunological incompetence
definition: Inability of the immune system to function in a normal fashion.

name: immunologically privileged site
definition: Any of various sites in the body where foreign tissue grafts do not induce an immune reaction.

name: immunological memory
definition: Ability of the immune system to respond faster and more effectively to subsequent exposures to an antigen following a primary immune response to the same antigen.

name: immunological synapse
definition: Contact point between the T cell and antigen-presenting cell (APC) that is generated by reorganization and clustering of cell surface molecules in lipid rafts. The synapse facilitates interactions between T-cell receptor (TCR) and major histocompatibility complex (MHC) molecules, and between adhesion molecules, thereby potentiating a TCR-mediated activation signal.

name: immunological tolerance
definition: Persistent specific immunological unresponsiveness toward a substance that would normally be expected to elicit an immune response, resulting from previous non-sensitizing exposure to an antigen.

name: immunology
definition: Science that deals with the immune system including cell-mediated immunity (CMI) and humoral aspects of immunity and immune responses.

name: immunomagnetic separation
definition: Method of separating specific cell types or macromolecules with the aid of cell-specific antibodies coupled to paramagnetic beads.

name: immunomodulation
definition: Modification of the functioning of the immune system by the action of a substance that increases or reduces the ability to produce an immune response.

name: immunopathology
definition: 1) Study of diseases of the immune system. 2) The occurrence of such diseases.

name: immunopathy
definition: Disease of the immune system.

name: immunopharmacology
definition: 1) Study of the immune system using drugs as diagnostic tools. 2) Use of pharmaceutical molecules to support and stimulate the immune system in patients with immunodeficiency, or to suppress or specifically influence the reactivity of the immune system in order to control a pathological immune reaction or disease.

name: immunophenotyping
definition: Use of a panel of antibodies to determine a subset of proteins expressed on the surface of a cell or heterogeneous group of cells, often for diagnostic purposes, e.g., identifying the presence of leukemia cells in a population of lymphocytes.

name: immunophilin
definition: Any of a group of cytoplasmic proteins in T cells that are targets of the immunosuppressant drugs cyclosporin A, tacrolimus (fujimycin), rapamycin, and related compounds.

name: immunopotentiation
definition: Enhancement of the capacity of the immune system to produce an effective response.

name: immunoprecipitate
definition: Precipitate formed in an antigen–antibody reaction.

name: immunoreceptor tyrosine-based activation motif
definition: Consensus sequence for src-family tyrosine kinases, found in the cytoplasmic domains of several signaling molecules including the signal transduction units of lymphocyte antigen receptors and of Fc receptors.

name: immunoreceptor tyrosine-based inhibitory motif
definition: Consensus sequence present in the cytoplasmic domains of certain cell surface molecules [e.g., Fc \(\upgamma\) RIIB, inhibitory natural killer (NK) cell receptors] and which mediates inhibitory signals.

name: immunosensitivity
definition: Reactivity to antigens.

name: immunosensitizer
definition: Substance that makes the immune system more reactive to antigens.

name: immunostimulating complex
definition: Immunological adjuvant composed of saponin, cholesterol, phospholipid, and an immunogen, usually protein.

name: immunostimulation
definition: Increase in immune function, e.g., by use of bacille Calmette–Guérin (BCG) vaccine or drugs.

name: immunosuppressant
definition: Substance that depresses the function of the immune system.

name: immunosuppressive
definition: Causing depression of the normal function of the immune system.

name: immunosurveillance
definition: Mechanisms by which the immune system is able to recognize and destroy malignant cells before the formation of an overt tumor.

name: immunotherapy
definition: Treatment or prevention of a disease using agents that can modify the immune response.

name: immunotoxic
definition: Harmful to the immune system.

name: immunotoxicant
definition: Substance that is harmful to the immune system.

name: immunotoxicology
definition: Discipline applying cardinal principals of both immunology and toxicology to study the ability of certain substances to alter the immune response.

name: immunotoxin
definition: Biochemical conjugate, or recombinant fusion protein, consisting of an immune targeting molecule such as an antibody or antibody fragment together with a cytotoxic molecule.

name: inactivated vaccine
definition: Vaccine formulated from the whole microorganism that has been rendered unable to reproduce or cause disease, often by mutation or heat denaturation.

name: indirect immunofluorescence
definition: Method of visualizing an antigen in which an unlabeled antibody against the antigen is reacted with it first, and then is detected by staining with a second fluorescently tagged immunoglobulin G (IgG) directed against the first antibody.

name: indolamine-2,3-dioxygenase
definition: Enzyme catalyzing the initial rate-limiting step of tryptophan degradation.

name: inducible co-stimulatory protein
definition: Highly specific receptor for the protein B7H/B7RP-1 that is expressed on the surface of B cells and macrophages, and also appears on the surface of T cells during the process of T-cell activation.

name: infectious tolerance
definition: Continuing state of tolerance that can be transferred by T lymphocytes from a tolerant animal.

name: autoimmune infertility
definition: Infertility caused by sperm antibodies, autoimmune ovarian inflammation (oophoritis), or autoimmune orchitis.

name: inflammasome
definition: High-molecular-weight complex that activates inflammatory caspases and the cytokines interleukin-1$\ce{\upbeta\!}$ ($\ce{IL\mbox{-}1\upbeta\!}$) and IL-18.

name: inflammatory bowel disease
definition: Group of chronic inflammatory conditions resulting in the inappropriate and persistent activation of the mucosal immune system of the bowel.

name: innate immunity
definition: Immunity that is not intrinsically affected by prior contact with antigen, i.e., all aspects of immunity not directly mediated by lymphocytes.

name: intercellular adhesion molecule
definition: Member of the immunoglobulin superfamily that interacts with integrins and is found on the surface of several cell types, including antigen-presenting cells (APCs) and T cells.

name: interclonal competition
definition: Process which favors survival of foreign-specific lymphocytes at the expense of self-specific lymphocytes and is a secondary mechanism involved in the induction and maintenance of self-tolerance.

name: interleukin
definition: Member of a group of immunoregulatory glycoproteins, also called lymphokines, monokines, or cytokines.

name: internal image
definition: Epitope on an anti-idiotype that binds in a way that structurally and functionally mimics the antigen.

name: intolerance
definition: Extreme sensitivity or allergy to a drug, food, or other substance.

name: intradermal test
definition: Diagnostic test for a possible cause of hypersensitivity in an individual in which a small drop of antigen is placed on a scarified skin surface or injected intradermally.

name: intra-epithelial lymphocyte
definition: Lymphocyte found in the epithelial layer of mammalian mucosal linings, such as those of the gastrointestinal and reproductive tracts.

name: invariant chain
definition: Protein (\(\pu{31 kDa}\)) of the endoplasmic reticulum lumen that binds to newly formed major histocompatibility complex (MHC) heterodimeric proteins, preventing binding of endogenous peptides to their groove.

name: islet cell antibodies
definition: Autoantibodies reacting with endocrine (pancreatic islet) cells and detectable by indirect immunofluorescence on pancreatic cryostat sections.

name: isograft
definition: Tissue transplanted (see graft) between two genetically identical individuals.

name: isohemagglutinin
definition: Naturally occurring immunoglobulin M (IgM) antibody specific for the erythrocyte antigens of the ABO blood groups, thought to result from immunization by bacteria in the gastrointestinal and respiratory tracts.

name: isotype
definition: Class of antibody that differs from others in the constant region of the heavy chain (Fc portion).

name: isotype control
definition: Antibody exhibiting the non-specific characteristics of the antibody-isotype but lacking any specificity for the antigen in question; used as a negative control in antibody-antigen detection assays, notably in flow cytometry.

name: isotype switch
definition: Process by which a B cell switches from making antibody of one isotype to another without altering the specificity of the antibody, producing an isotype with the same variable (V) regions but a different heavy chain constant (C) region.

name: JAK/STAT signaling pathway
definition: Mechanism that transmits information from chemical signals outside the cell to gene promoters on the DNA in the cell nucleus. The mechanism is activated by the binding of Janus-family tyrosine kinase (JAK) to the nonpolypeptide portion of occupied receptors for some interleukins (IL). JAK phosphorylates signal transducer and activator of transcription (STAT) proteins apart from STAT 5a and 5b.

name: JAM test
definition: Method which uses labeled nucleotide precursors to estimate DNA fragmentation during cell-mediated cytotoxicity or apoptosis.

name: Janus-family tyrosine kinase
definition: Tyrosine kinase activated by cytokines binding to cell receptors.

name: joining chain
definition: Polypeptide that forms part of the polymeric structure of pentameric immunoglobulin M (IgM) and dimeric immunoglobulin A (IgA).

name: joining gene
definition: Gene coding for a joining segment that connects variable (V) regions and constant (C) regions of immunoglobulin (Ig) or T-cell receptor (TCR) chains that, upon gene rearrangement, encodes part of the third hypervariable region of the antigen receptors.

name: junctional diversity
definition: Diversity of the splice junctions in the recombined variable (V) gene, diversity (D) gene [for immunoglobulin (Ig) heavy chains, and for TCR b and d chains], and joining (J) gene segments of antibody and T-cell receptor (TCR) genes.

name: kallikrein
definition: Any of a group of enzymes found in the blood and body fluids that acts on certain plasma globulins to produce bradykinins.

name: Kaposi sarcoma
definition: Form of skin cancer that can involve internal organs. It is most often found in patients with acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS) and can be fatal.

name: kappa-light chain
definition: Smaller of the two types of light chain found in human immunoglobulins (Ig), the other type being a lambda ($\uplambda\!$)-light chain.

name: keratinocyte
definition: Epidermal cell that produces keratin.

name: killer activatory receptor
definition: Receptor found on natural killer (NK) cells, and some $\ce{\upgamma\!{:}\updelta\!}$ and $\ce{\upalpha\!{:}\upbeta\! T cells}$.

name: killer cell
definition: Cell that displays cell-mediated cytotoxicity, including cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTL, Tc), natural killer (NK) cells, and natural killer T (NKT) cells. Some also consider activated macrophages, monocytes, and interferon (IFN)-activated neutrophils to be killer cells.

name: killer cell immunoglobulin-like receptor
definition: Receptor expressed on natural killer (NK) cells that binds to major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class I molecules on target cells; binding MHC class I inhibits the signaling that would otherwise lead to target cell killing.

name: killer lectin-like receptor
definition: Killer cell receptor that binds to major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class I molecules and, like the C-type lectin receptors also found on these cells, can either inhibit or activate the killer cells.

name: kinin
definition: Any of a family of polypeptides that is released during inflammatory responses and that increases vascular permeability and smooth muscle contraction.

name: knockout
definition: Use of homologous genetic recombination in embryonic stem cells to replace a functional gene with a defective copy of the gene.

name: knockout mouse
definition: Mouse produced from embryonic cells containing DNA that has been genetically engineered so that it does not express a particular gene or group of genes.

name: Kupffer cell
definition: Fixed tissue macrophage found lining the blood sinuses in the liver.

name: Kveim reaction
definition: Test for sarcoidosis, eliciting a granuloma at the site of intrradermal injection of a lymph node extract from a person with active disease. Generally considered non-specific.

name: L-selectin
definition: Any of a group of leukocyte surface adhesion molecules; they are classed as CD62 in the cluster of differentiation (CD) antigen marker system. All have lectin family carbohydrate binding domains and epidermal growth factor (EGF) repeats.

name: Ly-6
definition: Family of multi-gene-encoded, small, generally glycosylphosphatidyl inositol-anchored membrane proteins thought to be involved in cell adhesion and signaling, and in antigen-independent activation of lymphocytes.

name: Lambert–Eaton myasthenic syndrome
definition: Paraneoplastic neurological disorder associated with small-cell lung cancer and caused by autoantibodies against voltage-gated calcium channels.

name: lambda (λ)-light chain
definition: One of the two types of light chain of human immunoglobulins (Ig), the other type being the kappa ($\kappa$)-light chain.

name: Langerhans cell
definition: Immature, phagocytic dendritic cell of the mammalian skin, characterized by the presence of Fc receptors, major histocompatibility (MHC) class II molecules, and epidermal dendritic cell marker CD1. It contains a cytoplasmic organelle called the Birbeck granule.

name: large granular lymphocyte
definition: Lymphocyte of greater than normal size that contains cytoplasmic granules and functions as a natural killer (NK) cell or killer (K) cell. Activated CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTL, Tc) also assume an LGL morphology.

name: late phase reaction
definition: Immunoglobulin E (IgE)-mediated immune response occurring \(\pu{5}\) to \(\pu{8 h}\) after exposure to antigen, after the 'wheal and flare' reaction of immediate hypersensitivity has diminished, with inflammation peaking around \(\pu{24 h}\), and then subsiding.

name: latex agglutination test
definition: Use of latex beads coated with antibodies to detect antigen in biological samples.

name: latex allergen
definition: Allergen found in natural rubber latex (NRL).

name: leukemia
definition: Progressive, malignant disease of the blood-forming organs, characterized by excessive proliferation and development of leucocytes and their precursors in the bone marrow and blood.

name: leukocyte
definition: White blood cell.

name: leukocyte common antigen
definition: Antigen common to both T lymphocytes and B lymphocytes.

name: leukocyte functional antigen
definition: Any of a group of cell-surface antigens involved in intercellular adhesion.

name: leukocytopenia
definition: Amount of leukocytes below normal values that is a characteristic feature of systemic autoimmune diseases [e.g., Felty syndrome, systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), Sjögren syndrome, mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD)].

name: leukocytosis
definition: Abnormal increase in the number of leukocytes.

name: leukotriene
definition: Metabolic product of arachidonic acid that promotes inflammatory processes (e.g., chemotaxis, increased vascular permeability) and is produced by a variety of cell types including mast cells, basophils, and macrophages.

name: ligand of inducible co-stimulatory protein
definition: Protein involved, after binding to inducible co-stimulatory protein (ICOS), in several harmful immune responses, such as autoimmunity, allergy, or graft-versus-host (GVH) reaction.

name: light chain
definition: Small polypeptide subunit of an antibody or immunoglobulin (Ig).

name: Limulus test
definition: Method of detecting bacterial endotoxins based on gelation of a blood cell lysate from the horseshoe crab, Limulus polyphemus.

name: linear epitope
definition: Antigenic determinant that is contiguous in the amino acid sequence of a protein and therefore does not require the protein to be folded into its native conformation for antibody to bind.

name: linked recognition
definition: Requirement for a helper T lymphocyte (Th) and B lymphocyte to interact with separate but physically linked epitopes in the same antigen, in order for an immune response to a thymus-dependent (TD) antigen.

name: lipid raft
definition: Cholesterol- and glycosphingolipid-rich membrane subdomain in which molecules involved in cellular activation become concentrated.

name: live attenuated vaccine
definition: Vaccine prepared from living attenuated organisms or from viruses that have been attenuated but can still replicate in the cells of the host organism.

name: liver-kidney microsomal antibodies
definition: Autoantibodies directed against cytochrome P450 and uridine diphosphate (UDP)-glucuronosyltransferase (UGT) antigens typically found in patients with immune-mediated hepatitis.

name: lymphadenopathy
definition: Enlarged lymph nodes.

name: lymphangion
definition: Morphological or functional unit of lymphatic vessels consisting of the region between adjacent lymphatic valves.

name: lymphatic system
definition: Describing vessels whose special function is the collection of lymph and its ultimate conveyance to the blood circulation and thoracic duct.

name: lymphatic tissue
definition: Tissue involved in the collection, production, and handling of lymph, including the lymphatic vessels and lymph nodes.

name: lymph node
definition: Any of the small rounded gland-like structures of the lymphatic system, which occur along the lymphatic vessels and which are responsible for removing bacteria, viruses, and foreign molecules from the lymph stream and for producing lymphocytes and antibodies.

name: lymphoblast
definition: Abnormal cell with a large nucleus and scanty cytoplasm, thought to be the precursor of the lymphocyte, found in blood and blood-forming organs in patients with lymphoblastic leukemia.

name: lymphocyte
definition: Small leucocyte found in the blood, lymph, and lymphoid tissues that has a single round nucleus and little or no granulation in the cytoplasm.

name: lymphocyte-activating factor
definition: Interleukin-1 (IL-1)

name: lymphocyte activation
definition: Sum of the biochemical processes necessary to stimulate a resting lymphocyte to become an immune effector cell, requiring antigen and co-stimulatory molecules.

name: lymphocyte function-associated antigen-1
definition: Adhesion molecule found on lymphocytes, macrophages, and neutrophils, involved in adhesion of lymphocytes to antigen-presenting cells (APCs).

name: lymphocyte homing
definition: Process that directs lymphocyte subsets to specialized microenvironments that control their differentiation, regulate their survival, and target immune effector cells to sites of antigenic or microbial invasion.

name: lymphocyte homing receptor
definition: Cell surface glycoprotein on lymphocytes and other leukocytes that mediates adhesion to specialized blood vessels, the high endothelial venules.

name: lymphocyte proliferation test
definition: Test of immune sensitization in which white blood cells are exposed in vitro to an antigen and multiply if already sensitized to that antigen.

name: immunoglobulin or T-cell receptor lymphocyte repertoire
definition: Profile of immunoglobulins (Ig) or T-cell receptors (TCRs) available within a specified group of cells.

name: lymphocyte subpopulation
definition: Population forming part of the whole population of lymphocytes, usually characterized by sensitivity to a given antigen.

name: lymphocyte transformation test
definition: Test for increased DNA synthesis followed by cell division and differentiation of lymphocytes in response to antigens or mitogens; an in vitro test of lymphocyte function.

name: lymphocytopenia
definition: Deficiency of lymphocytes in the blood compared with normal values.

name: lymphocytosis
definition: Condition characterized by an abnormal increase in the number of lymphocytes in blood, usually a result of infection or inflammation.

name: lymphocytotoxicity
definition: Capability of lysing lymphocytes.

name: lymphoid follicle
definition: Region of clustered B cells, allowing the selection of antigen-binding B cells by dendritic cells during adaptive immune responses.

name: lymphoid stem cell
definition: Stem cell giving rise to the lineage of lymphocytes.

name: lymphoid tissue
definition: Vertebrate tissue that is made up predominantly of lymphocytes, e.g., lymph, lymph nodes, spleen, thymus, Peyer’s patches, adenoids, pharyngeal tonsils, and, in birds, bursa of Fabricius and cecal tonsils.

name: lymphokine
definition: Cytokine produced by lymphocytes.

name: lymphokine-activated killer cell
definition: Killer (K) cell or natural killer (NK) cell activated in vitro by interleukin (IL)-2 to give enhanced killing of target cells.

name: lymphoma
definition: Neoplasm, usually malignant, of the lymphatic tissues.

name: lymphopoiesis
definition: Production of lymphocytes.

name: lymphoproliferation
definition: Proliferation of lymphocytes in response to stimulation with cellular activators, including antigens or mitogens.

name: lymphosum
definition: Sum of B cells + T cells + natural killer (NK) cells determined separately (by flow cytometry), compared to the total number of lymphocytes.

name: lymphotoxin
definition: T-cell-derived cytokine that is cytotoxic for certain tumor cells and also has immunoregulatory functions.

name: lysosome
definition: Cytoplasmic granule containing hydrolytic enzymes involved in the digestion of phagocytosed material.

name: macroautophagy
definition: Sequestration and breakdown of organelles and long-lived proteins in a double-membrane vesicle, called an autophagosome or autophagic vacuole, inside the cell.

name: macrophage
definition: Large (\(\pu{10\!{-}\! 20 \upmu m}\) diameter) ameboid and phagocytic cell found in many tissues, especially in areas of inflammation, derived from blood monocytes and playing an important role in host defense mechanisms.

name: residential macrophage
definition: Macrophage stationed at a point where microbial invasion or accumulation of dust is likely to occur.

name: macrophage function test
definition: Any assay suitable to characterize the effect of substances on macrophage function in in vivo or in vitro.

name: macrophage mannose receptor
definition: Receptor involved in pathogen recognition, in clearance of endogenous serum glycoproteins, and in antigen presentation.

name: macropinocytosis
definition: 'High-volume' pinocytosis by which dendritic cells engulf relatively large volumes of fluid from their surroundings, enabling them to take in many antigens nonspecifically.

name: major basic protein
definition: Small basic arginine-rich peptide (\(\pu{pI 10.9}\), molecular mass of \(\pu{13.8 kDa}\)) in the granules of eosinophils that kills helminths and protozoa.

name: major histocompatibility complex
definition: Cluster of genes encoding cell surface molecules involved in antigen presentation to T cells. In humans, they are found on chromosome 6 and in mice on chromosome 17. They are polymorphic and code for antigens that lead to rapid graft rejection between members of a single species that differ at these loci.

name: major histocompatibility complex class I molecule
definition: Surface protein encoded by the major histocompatibility complex (MHC) expressed on all nucleated cells, presenting antigen-derived peptides.
synonyms: MHC class I molecule|class I MHC gene product

name: major histocompatibility complex class II molecule
definition: Surface protein encoded by the major histocompatibility complex (MHC) expressed on antigen-presenting cells (APCs), presenting antigen-derived peptides.
synonyms: MHC class II molecule|class II MHC gene product

name: major histocompatibility complex class III molecule
definition: Antigen encoded by the major histocompatibility complex (MHC) including several complement factors, tumor necrosis factor (TNF) $\ce{\upalpha\!}$, and lymphotoxin.
synonyms: MHC class III molecule|class III MHC gene product

name: major histocompatibility complex molecule
definition: Any of the cell-surface glycoprotein alloantigens encoded by the major histocompatibility complex (MHC) that are involved in the regulation of immune responses and can cause the rejection of grafted tissues, cells, and tumors bearing them.

name: major histocompatibility complex restriction
definition: Necessity that T cells recognize processed antigen only when presented by major histocompatibility complex (MHC) molecules of the original haplotype associated with T-cell priming.

name: mammalian target of rapamycin
definition: Intracellular signaling molecule (phosphoinositide-3-kinase) involved in control of cell growth, whose activity is negatively influenced by the immunosuppressive drug rapamycin.

name: mannan-binding lectin-associated serine peptidase-1 and -2
definition: Complement-dependent bactericidal factors that bind to the Ra and R2 polysaccharides expressed by certain enterobacterium strains, such as Ra chemotype strains of Salmonella.

name: mannose-binding protein
definition: Member of the collectin family of calcium-dependent lectins, and an acute-phase protein.

name: mantle zone
definition: Outer ring of small lymphocytes surrounding the center of a lymphatic nodule (lymphoid follicle). It contains transient lymphocytes and is the location of the lymphoma in mantle cell lymphoma.

name: marginal zone
definition: Outer area of the splenic periarteriolar lymphoid sheath (PALS) that is rich in B cells, particularly those responding to thymus-independent antigens.

name: margination
definition: Leukocyte adhesion to the endothelium of blood vessels in the early phase of an acute inflammatory response.

name: mast cell
definition: Large connective tissue cell that contains inflammatory substances such as histamine, proteases (including tryptases, chymases, and carboxypeptidase A), heparin and chondroitin sulfate proteoglycans, and eicosanoid lipid mediators (the precursors of leukotrienes and prostaglandins). These substances are released in allergic reactions or in response to injury or inflammation.

name: mast cell activation disorder
definition: Disorder or syndrome in which there is evidence of systemic, inappropriate release of mast cell mediators.

name: mast cell stabilizer
definition: Non-steroidal medication that reduces the release of substances from mast cells, e.g., sodium cromoglycate.

name: mastocytoma
definition: Nodule of mast cells that can involve the skin, subcutaneous tissue, and sometimes muscle.

name: mastocytosis
definition: Rare disease characterized by the presence of too many mast cells in various organs and tissues. The condition can be a chronic, long-term illness or it can develop suddenly.

name: maturation
definition: Process by which B cells produce antibodies with increased affinity for antigen during the course of an immune response.

name: mature B cell
definition: B cell with immunoglobulin M (IgM) and immunoglobulin D (IgD) on its surface.

name: megakaryocyte
definition: Bone marrow precursor of platelets.

name: membrane attack complex
definition: Complex of complement components C5b–C9 that inserts as a pore into the membrane of target cells leading to cell lysis.

name: memory
definition: Characteristic of the acquired immune response (see acquired immunity) of lymphocytes whereby a second encounter with a given antigen produces a secondary immune response that is faster, greater, and longer lasting than the primary immune response.

name: memory cell
definition: Clonally expanded T cell or B cell produced during a primary immune response and which is primed to mediate a secondary immune response to the original antigen.

name: memory lymphocyte immunostimulation assay
definition: Patented modification of the lymphocyte transformation test (LTT) based on the enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) principle.

name: mesenteric lymph node
definition: Lymph node lying between layers of the mesentery.

name: metabolic activation
definition: Formation of one or more chemically reactive intermediate(s) as a result of modification of a molecule by the xenobiotic-metabolizing enzymes of liver and other organs.

name: microautophagy
definition: Process in which lysosomes directly engulf cytoplasm by invagination, protrusion, and/or septation of the lysosomal limiting membrane.

name: microfold cell
definition: Cell found in the follicle-associated epithelium of the Peyer’s patch that has the unique ability to sample antigen from the lumen of the small intestine and deliver it via transcytosis to antigen-presenting cells (APCs) and lymphocytes located in a unique pocket-like structure on their basolateral side.

name: microglobulin
definition: Any small globular protein found on the surface of many cells, including lymphocytes, and in the blood plasma distinct from albumin.

name: microscopic polyangiitis
definition: ANCA-associated necrotizing, pauci-immune vasculitis of the small vessels (capillaries, venules, arterioles) frequently associated with rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis and/or hemorrhagic alveolitis as well as autoantibodies against myeloperoxidase.

name: minor histocompatibility antigen
definition: Non-major histocompatibility complex (MHC)-encoded cell surface processed peptide which, in association with MHC-encoded molecules, contributes to graft rejection, albeit not usually as severe as that due to MHC mismatch.

name: mitogen
definition: Substance that induces lymphocyte transformation or, more generally, mitosis and cell proliferation.

name: mitogen-activated protein kinase
definition: Member of a kinase network in which 'upstream' kinases activate 'downstream' kinases that, in response to phosphorylation, translocate to the nucleus and activate transcription factors.

name: mitophagy
definition: Autophagy-related pathway specific for mitochondria; it can be subdivided into macromitophagy and micromitophagy depending upon the degree of mitophagy.

name: mixed lymphocyte response
definition: T-cell-proliferative response induced by cells expressing allogeneic major histocompatibility complex (MHC) molecules.

name: mixed connective tissue disease
definition: Human autoimmune disease in which the immune system attacks the body, producing symptoms that combine features of polymyositis, systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), and systemic scleroderma, and thus being considered as an overlap syndrome.

name: molecular mimicry
definition: Concept that identity or similarity of epitopes expressed by a pathogen and by a self molecule may lead to production of antibodies reacting to the self-antigen.

name: monocyte
definition: Mononuclear phagocyte found in blood and which is the precursor of the tissue macrophage.

name: monokine
definition: Alternative name for a cytokine produced by monocytes.

name: mononuclear phagocyte system
definition: Network of phagocytic cells throughout the body. System comprising blood monocytes and tissue macrophages.

name: mouse IgE test
definition: Procedure in which serum immunoglobulin E (IgE) levels are measured in mice following topical exposure to a test substance. Substances that cause a significant increase in IgE are considered to be potential respiratory allergens.

name: mouse ear-swelling test
definition: Test for sensitization in which the test substance is applied topically to the ear of a mouse for three consecutive days. The change in ear thickness is then measured following challenge on day 8.

name: mucocutaneous
definition: Pertaining to or affecting the mucous membranes and/or the skin.

name: mucosa
definition: Moist tissue that lines some organs and body cavities, including the nose, mouth, lungs, and digestive tract.

name: mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue
definition: Secondary lymphoid tissue present in the surface mucosa of the respiratory tract and bronchus (BALT), gastrointestinal tract (GALT), nasal passages (NALT), larynx (LALT), conjunctiva (CALT), and genitourinary tract, and in the skin sub-epidermis (SALT).

name: mucosal addressin cell adhesion molecule-1
definition: Protein involved in trafficking of lymphocytes to mucosal endothelium.

name: mucosal tolerance
definition: State of lymphocyte hyporesponsiveness to protein antigens applied across mucosal surfaces by oral or nasal instillation.

name: multiple myeloma
definition: Plasma cell malignancy resulting in high levels of monoclonal immunoglobulin (Ig) in serum and of free light chains (Bence–Jones protein) in urine.

name: multiplex immunoassay
definition: Type of particle immunoassay employing sets of microspheres with various physicochemical features, each labeled with a different antibody. The method allows detection in a single measurement of an array of 100 or more proteins.

name: multipotent progenitor cell
definition: Undifferentiated stem cell, obtained from adult bone marrow or other non-embryonic tissue sources, that possesses the ability to differentiate into a variety of cell types, especially into cells of a closely related family of cells that are expanded in vitro and deposited in master cell banks for 'off-the-shelf' use, with potential hematopoiesis-inducing and immunomodulating activities.

name: murine local lymph node assay
definition: Predictive test of sensitization in which a test substance is applied topically to the skin of mice (usually three times at daily intervals) and the weight of the local draining lymph nodes is measured at six days. Usually lymphoproliferation in the nodes is measured following injection of [\(\ce{^{3}H}\)]thymidine or bromodeoxyuridine.

name: acquired myasthenia gravis
definition: Autoimmune disease characterized by muscle weakness usually affecting ocular and oropharyngeal muscles due to an autoimmune attack against components of the neuromuscular junction (e.g., the nicotinic acetylcholine receptor).

name: myelodysplastic syndrome
definition: Diverse collection of hematological conditions united by ineffective production (or dysplasia) of myeloid blood cells and risk of transformation to acute myelogenous leukemia (AML). Anemia requiring chronic blood transfusion is frequently present.

name: myeloma
definition: Tumor composed of cells derived from hematopoietic cells (see hematopoiesis) of the bone marrow, or from mast cells.

name: myeloid
definition: Referring to the nonlymphocytic groups of white blood cells, including granulocytes, monocytes, and platelets.

name: myeloid stem cell
definition: One of two groups of stem cells produced in the bone marrow. Myeloid stem cells may mature into several types of blood cells, including acidic basophils, eosinophils, erythrocytes, macrophages, megakaryocytes, and neutrophils.

name: myeloid tissue
definition: Tissue within red bone marrow that produces the blood cells. It is found around the blood vessels and contains various cell types that are precursors of the blood cells.

name: myeloma protein
definition: Monoclonal antibody secreted by myeloma cells.

name: myeloperoxidase
definition: Enzyme found in azurophilic granules of neutrophils, the major target of antineutrophil cytoplasmic autoantibody (ANCA).

name: myelopoiesis
definition: Process of formation and development of myeloid blood cells in the bone marrow.

name: myelosuppression
definition: Decrease in myeloid cells, including pancytopenia, anemia, leukopenia, lymphopenia, thrombocytopenia, and other blood dyscrasias.

name: autoimmune myositis
definition: Rare systemic inflammatory myopathy, including primary polymyositis, primary dermatomyositis, myositis associated with malignancy, childhood dermatomyositis, and myositis with multisystem autoimmune disease [e.g., mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD), systemic sclerosis (SSc)].

name: NACHT domain-, leucine-rich repeat (LRR)-, and pyrin (N-terminal homology) domain (PYD)-containing protein 3
definition: NOD-like receptor (NLR), found in certain inflammasomes, that binds to aggregated proteins and the peptides that compose them. Its activation leads to the generation of inflammatory cytokines, such as interleukin (IL)-1, and neurotoxic factors.

name: N-nucleotides
definition: Non-templated nucleotides added to the junctions between antibody and T-cell receptor (TCR) variable (V) gene, diversity (D) gene, and joining (J) gene segments during gene rearrangement.

name: NOD-like receptor
definition: Any of a large family of cytoplasmic proteins containing a nucleotide-binding domain and leucine-rich repeats (LRRs), involved in regulation of inflammation and apoptosis; many family members are thought to function as pattern recognition receptors (PRRs).

name: N-region
definition: Highly variable region on the H-chain of immunoglobulins.

name: naïve lymphocyte
definition: Mature T cell or B cell that has not yet been activated (see lymphocyte activation) by encounter with antigen.

name: natural autoantibodies
definition: Part of the naturally occurring repertoire of polyreactive antibodies that bind to autoantigens with low affinity. They are mainly of immunoglobulin M (IgM) isotype and produced by CD5+ B lymphocytes.

name: natural immunity
definition: Host defense mechanisms that do not require prior exposure to antigen.

name: natural killer cell
definition: Large granular lymphocyte which does not rearrange nor express either immunoglobulin or T-cell receptor (TCR) genes but is able to recognize and destroy certain tumor and virally infected cells in a major histocompatibility complex (MHC) molecule- and antibody-independent manner.

name: natural killer cell activity assay
definition: Immunotoxicity test in which lymphoid tissue or blood that has been treated with a test compound is co-incubated with target cells. The cytotoxic effect on target cells is measured, e.g., with the chromium release assay. It is used under circumstances where differences from untreated cells are attributed to natural killer (NK) cell activity.

name: natural killer T cell
definition: Lymphoid cells with a morphology and granule content intermediate between T cells and natural killer (NK) cells.

name: natural resistance-associated macrophage protein
definition: Iron transporter that plays a critical role in macrophage activation and differentiation.

name: negative selection
definition: Deletion by apoptosis in the thymus of T cells that recognize self-peptides presented by self-major histocompatibility complex (MHC) molecules, thus preventing the development of autoimmune T cells. Negative selection of developing B cells is also thought to occur if they encounter high levels of self-antigen in the bone marrow.

name: neoantigen
definition: Antigen newly expressed on a tumor or virally infected cell, or arising after macromolecule-hapten binding.

name: neonatal tolerance
definition: Tolerance to specific foreign antigens induced by the exposure of a bird or mammal to the foreign antigens during embryonic or neonatal life, depending upon species.

name: autoimmune nephritis
definition: Inflammation of the kidney due to immunological reaction to renal antigens.

name: autoimmune neuropathy
definition: Autoimmune disease of the nervous system.

name: neutralization
definition: Blocking by an antibody of the effects of a virus.

name: neutropenia
definition: Abnormally low concentration of neutrophils in the blood.

name: neutrophil
definition: Granular leukocyte, the major circulating phagocytic polymorphonuclear granulocyte, having a nucleus with three to five lobes and fine cytoplasmic granules stainable by neutral dyes.

name: neutrophil activation
definition: Change in morphology and behavior of a neutrophil resulting from exposure to a cytokine, chemokine, cellular ligand, or soluble factor.

name: nitric oxide
definition: Generic term for nitrogen monoxide species, including nitrosonium ion, nitric oxide radical, etc., that can function in a cell-signaling capacity.

name: nondepleting antibody
definition: Cell surface antibody that does not provoke attack by killer cells and thus does not provoke depletion of a group of cells in the body, usually referring to B cells.

name: non-Hodgkin lymphoma
definition: Any of various malignant lymphomas characterized by the absence of Reed–Sternberg cells and producing symptoms similar to those of Hodgkin disease.

name: non-obese diabetic mouse
definition: Genetically modified mouse with a susceptibility to spontaneous development of automimmune diabetes mellitus type I.

name: non-self
definition: Of, relating to, or designating a cell or tissue that has not been produced by the individual organism.

name: nuclear factor of activated T cells
definition: Transcription factor involved in rapid cell response to stress, such as injury or invading pathogens, and in cell proliferation and survival.

name: nuclear factor kappa-light-chain-enhancer of activated B cells
definition: Protein complex that controls the transcription of genes involved in cytokine production, cellular adhesion, inflammation, and apoptosis.

name: nucleotide-binding oligomerization domain-containing protein 1, 2
definition: Members of a family of human intracellular proteins involved in the detection of invasive bacteria and activation of the $\ce{NF\kappa B}$ transcription factor pathway.

name: nucleotide-binding oligomerization domain-containing protein-like receptor
definition: Cytosolic protein that contains a central nucleotide-binding oligomerization domain, an N-terminal effector-binding domain and C-terminal leucine-rich repeats (LRRs).

name: nude mouse
definition: Mouse that is T-cell-deficient due to a homozygous gene defect (\(nu/nu\)) resulting in the absence of a thymus (and also lack of body hair).

name: null cell
definition: Lymphocyte with neither T- nor B-cell differentiation antigens on its surface.

name: OKT3
definition: Brand name for muromonab-CD3, an immunosuppressant drug given intravenously to reverse acute rejection of transplanted organs, including the heart, kidneys, and liver.

name: oligoclonal
definition: Having a few different clones, or the product of a few different clones.

name: oncofetal antigen
definition: Antigen whose expression is normally restricted to the fetus but which may be expressed during malignancy in adults.

name: opsonization
definition: Coating of antigen with an opsonin to enhance phagocytosis.

name: oral tolerance
definition: Orally induced and immune-mediated non-responsiveness.

name: oral vaccination
definition: Immunization against a pathogen with a vaccine administered by mouth.

name: Ouchterlony technique
definition: Double-radial immunodiffusion procedure for the detection of precipitating antibodies.

name: P-nucleotides
definition: Palindromic nucleotide sequences generated at the junctions between antibody and T-cell receptor (TCR) variable (V), diversity (D), and joining (J) gene segments during gene rearrangement.

name: P-selectin
definition: Cell adhesion molecule expressed on the surface of activated endothelial cells and platelets.

name: pancytopenia
definition: Decrease in the number of red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets.

name: paracortical area
definition: Region of a lymph node enriched in T lymphocytes.

name: paramone
definition: Paracrine agonist.

name: paraneoplastic autoimmune syndrome
definition: Any of several autoimmune diseases that are caused by tumor-induced perturbations of the immune system with damaging effects on various organ systems (e.g. cancer-associated retinopathy, paraneoplastic neurological syndromes, paraneoplastic cutaneous syndromes). In most cases, autoantibodies generated by antitumor immunity are responsible for the tissue injury.

name: paratope
definition: Site in the variable region of an antibody or T-cell receptor (TCR) that binds to an epitope of an antigen.

name: particle immunoassay
definition: Immunoassay in which antibody is bound to the surface of microspheres. After incubation with the antigen-containing biological fluid, and subsequent manipulation, detection is usually performed by flow cytometry.

name: passive cutaneous anaphylaxis test
definition: Assay for allergenicity in which an antibody is injected intradermally into a test animal followed at a later time (anywhere from \(\pu{3}\) to \(\pu{48 h}\)) with an intravenous injection of a mixture of a test antigen and a dye (typically Evans blue). Increased vascular permeability at the site of antigen-antibody reaction is visualized by extravasation of the dye.

name: passive hemagglutination
definition: Method of measuring antibody titer, in which antigen-coated erythrocytes are agglutinated by adding antibody specific for the antigen.

name: passive immunization
definition: Immunization of an individual by the transfer of antibody synthesized in another individual.

name: patch test
definition: Test for allergy that is performed by placing the suspected allergen in direct contact with the skin or mucosa.

name: pathogen-associated molecular pattern
definition: Describing repetitive motifs of molecules such as lipopolysaccharide (LPS), peptidoglycan, lipoteichoic acids, and mannans, which are widely expressed by microbial pathogens but are not present on host tissues. They are therefore utilized by the pattern recognition receptors (PRRs) of the immune system to distinguish pathogens from self-antigens.

name: pattern recognition receptor
definition: Receptor found on many different cell types in the immune system that enables them to recognize pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs). Amongst the large number of different PRRs are the mannose receptor (CD206), macrophage scavenger receptor (CD204), and the toll-like receptors (TLRs).

name: pauci-immune
definition: Referring to vasculitis characterized by relatively little deposition of immunoglobulin (Ig) and complement factors, usually describing a form of glomerulonephritis.

name: pemphigus
definition: Rare, serious autoimmune disease marked by successive outbreaks of blisters, which appear suddenly and disappear, leaving pigmented spots.

name: peptide tetramer
definition: Structure consisting of four identical major histocompatibility complex (MHC)-encoded peptides, presenting four binding sites for biotin attached to the tail of the MHC molecule, and held together by fluorescent streptavidin.

name: peptide vaccine
definition: Preparation of an immunologically active peptide found in a disease-causing organism or substance, or any of their products, which is specially treated for use in vaccination.

name: peptide-binding groove
definition: Structural feature found in major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class I and class II heterodimeric proteins that can bind endogenous peptides.

name: perforin
definition: Molecule produced by cytotoxic T cells and natural killer (NK) cells that, like complement component C9, polymerizes to form a pore in the membrane of the target cell leading to cell death.

name: periarteriolar lymphoid sheath
definition: Lymphoid tissue that forms the white pulp of the spleen.

name: periodontitis
definition: Inflammatory reaction of the tissues surrounding a tooth (periodontium), usually resulting from the extension of gingival inflammation (gingivitis) into the periodontium, and involving inflammation and infection of the ligaments and bones that support the teeth.

name: peripheral blood leukocyte
definition: Leukocyte derived from the peripheral circulatory system.

name: peripheral blood mononuclear cell
definition: Monocyte produced by the bone marrow from hematopoietic stem cell precursors, circulating in the bloodstream for about one to three days before moving into tissues throughout the body.

name: peripheral lymphoid organ
definition: Any of the lymphoid organs (see lymphoid tissue) other than the thymus.

name: autoimmune peripheral neuropathy
definition: Acute or chronic inflammatory neuropathy leading to demyelination and axonal damage of nerves and nerve roots associated with high-titeredautoantibodies against gangliosides [e.g., Guillain–Barré syndrome (GBS), Miller–Fisher syndrome, acute sensory ataxic neuropathy].

name: peripheral tolerance
definition: Specific immunological tolerance occurring outside of the primary lymphoid organs (see lymphoid tissue).

name: pernicious anemia
definition: Disease in which the erythrocytes are abnormally formed, due to an inability to absorb vitamin \({\rm{B}}_{12}\). True pernicious anemia refers specifically to a disorder of atrophied parietal cells leading to absent intrinsic factor, resulting in an inability to absorb \({\rm{B}}_{12}\).

name: pexophagy
definition: Autophagy selective for degradation of peroxisomes, which can be separated into macropexophagy and micropexophagy.

name: Peyer’s patch
definition: Part of the gut-associated lymphoid tissue (GALT) and found as a distinct lymphoid nodule, mainly in the small intestine.

name: phagocyte
definition: Cell, especially of monocyte/macrophage or neutrophil lineage, that is specialized for the engulfment of cellular and particulate matter.

name: phagocytic activity assay
definition: Method of quantifying phagocytosis in which yeast cells, stained with May–Grünwald stain, are incubated with macrophages, and subsequently, after a fixed time, yeast cells engulfed in the macrophages are counted.

name: phagocytosis
definition: Process by which particulate material is endocytosed by a cell.

name: phagolysosome
definition: Intracellular vacuole where killing and digestion of phagocytosed material occurs following the fusion of a phagosome with a lysosome.

name: phagosome
definition: Intracellular vacuole produced following invagination of the cell membrane around phagocytosed material.

name: Philadelphia chromosome
definition: Chromosome resulting from a reciprocal translocation between human chromosomes 9 and 22, most commonly associated with chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML).

name: phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate
definition: Mitogenic phorbol ester that directly stimulates protein kinase C (PKC) and acts as a tumor promoter.

name: phospholipase Cγ
definition: Enzyme that cleaves phosphatidylinositol bisphosphate into diacylglycerol and inositol trisphosphate, leading to the activation of two major cell signaling pathways.

name: photoallergy
definition: Type IV hypersensitivity reaction in which photoactivation of a substance produces a hapten that then acts as a sensitizer.

name: photocontact dermatitis
definition: Type of contact dermatitis arising when substances are transformed into either irritants or allergens upon exposure to light.

name: photosensitivity
definition: Skin reddening due to an abnormal reaction to sunlight, characteristic of systemic autoimmune diseases [e.g., systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD)], and cutaneous and subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus.

name: phototoxicity test
definition: Procedure used to identify the phototoxic potential of a test substance. The substance is administered either systemically or topically on the skin, and light is subsequently shone on the skin to photoexcite the substance.

name: phytohemagglutinin
definition: Plant lectin that acts as a T-cell mitogen.

name: plantibody
definition: Animal antibody (or fragment thereof), expressed in a genetically modified plant.

name: plaque-forming cell
definition: Antibody-secreting plasma cell detected in vitro by its ability to produce a 'plaque' of lysed antigen-sensitized erythrocytes in the presence of complement.

name: plasmablast
definition: Highly proliferative cell that is a developmental intermediate between small B lymphocytes and immunoglobulin (Ig)-secreting mature plasma cells.

name: plasma cell
definition: Terminally differentiated B lymphocyte, with little or no capacity for mitotic division, that actively secretes large amounts of antibody.

name: plasmacytoid dendritic cell
definition: Dendritic cell of distinct lineage, found in blood and peripheral lymphoid tissue, which secretes large amounts of interferon (IFN) upon activation.

name: plasmacytoma
definition: Mass of neoplastic monoclonal plasma cells growing in bone or soft tissue.

name: plasmapheresis
definition: Technique of extracorporeal separation of blood cells from plasma, with return of the cells to the patient.

name: platelet
definition: Small irregular or disc-shaped cell found in large numbers in mammalian blood, essential for blood clotting.

name: platelet-activating factor
definition: Alkyl phospholipid released by a variety of cell types including mast cells and basophils, which has immunoregulatory effects on lymphocytes and monocytes/macrophages, as well as causing platelet aggregation and degranulation.

name: platelet-derived growth factor
definition: Protein synthesized by platelets that is released into the serum during blood clotting.

name: pluripotent stem cell
definition: Self-replicating cell capable of developing into cells and tissues of the three primary embryonic germ layers.

name: pokeweed mitogen
definition: Plant lectin which is a T-cell-dependent B-cell mitogen.

name: polyarteritis nodosa
definition: Systemic disease characterized by widespread inflammation of small and medium-sized arteries in which many of the foci are nodular.

name: polyclonal activator
definition: Substance that induces activation of multiple clones of B lymphocytes or T lymphocytes.

name: autoimmune polyendocrinopathy
definition: Autoimmune disease affecting multiple endocrine organs.

name: poly I:C
definition: Polyinosinic:polycytidylic acid, a synthetic immunostimulant mimicking viral double-stranded RNA.

name: poly ICLC
definition: Polyinosinic:polycytidylic acid, poly-ʟ-lysine, and carboxymethylcellulose (letter roots of the acronym underlined), a synthetic immunostimulant mimicking viral double-stranded RNA.

name: poly-Ig receptor
definition: Receptor molecule that specifically binds J chain-containing polymeric immunoglobulin (Ig), i.e., dimeric secretory immunoglobulin A (IgA) and pentameric immunoglobulin M (IgM), and transports it across mucosal epithelium.

name: polymorphonuclear leukocyte
definition: Mature leukocyte with granular cytoplasm and a segmented and irregularly shaped nucleus.

name: polymyositis
definition: Disorder characterized by inflammation and degeneration of skeletal muscle, causing pain, weakness, and wasting in affected (usually proximal) muscles.

name: popliteal lymph node assay
definition: Test for immunosensitization measuring popliteal lymph node hyperplasia after subcutaneous injection of a test substance into the footpad of the hindpaw of a rodent.

name: positive selection
definition: Selection of those developing T cells in the thymus that are able to recognize self-major histocompatibility complex (MHC) molecules. This occurs by preventing apoptosis in these cells.

name: pre-B cell
definition: Cell in the B-lymphocyte lineage that has rearranged heavy chain but not light chain genes; it expresses surrogate light chains and \(\upmu\) heavy chain at its surface in conjunction with immunoglobulins Ig _012643_ and Ig _012644_. All these molecules comprise the pre-B-cell receptor (pre-BCR).

name: precipitating antibody
definition: Antibody that is capable of reacting with a soluble antigen with the formation of an insoluble antigenantibody complex.

name: precipitin
definition: Precipitate of antibody and multivalent antigen due to the formation of high-molecular-weight complexes.

name: pre-T cell
definition: Cell differentiating into a T lymphocyte in the thymus gland.

name: prick test
definition: Test carried out by placing a drop of a suspected allergenic extract on the skin of the forearm and gently pricking it into the upper layer of skin. Sensitivity to a substance is indicated if the spot swells slightly and becomes red within about \(\pu{15 min}\).

name: primary biliary cirrhosis
definition: Autoimmune liver disease that results in the destruction of bile ducts, leading to fibrosis and cirrhosis.

name: primary immune response
definition: Immune response to the first encounter with an antigen, characterized by slow production of antibody molecules and the priming of lymphoid tissue in readiness for the production of a secondary immune response on subsequent challenge with the same antigen.

name: primary immunization
definition: First introduction of a vaccine into the body for the purposes of inducing immunity.

name: primary lymphoid follicle
definition: Region of a secondary lymphoid organ containing predominantly unstimulated B lymphocytes that develops into a germinal center following antigen stimulation.

name: primary lymphoid organ
definition: Site at which immunocompetent lymphocytes develop, i.e., bone marrow and thymus in mammals.

name: primary myxedema
definition: Atrophic form of diffuse autoimmune thyroiditis.

name: primary sclerosing cholangitis
definition: Chronic, non-bacterial, inflammatory narrowing of the bile ducts.

name: prime
definition: Process of giving an initial sensitization to antigen.

name: professional antigen-presenting cell
definition: Highly efficient antigen-presenting cell (APC), generally referring to dendritic cells, B cells, or macrophages.

name: progressive systemic sclerosis
definition: Systemic autoimmune disease marked by formation of hyalinized and thickened collagenous fibrous tissue, with thickening and adhesion of skin to underlying tissues, especially of the hands and face and vascular alterations.

name: proinflammatory cytokine
definition: Cytokine that initiates or enhances inflammation.

name: proliferation assay
definition: Any test that determines the effect on increase in cell number of a test agent such as a cytokine or mitogen.

name: properdin
definition: Relatively heat-labile, normal serum protein (a euglobulin) that, in the presence of complement component C3 and magnesium ions, is involved in the alternative pathway of complement activation, and acts nonspecifically against Gram-negative bacteria and viruses and may contribute to the lysis of erythrocytes.

name: proteasome
definition: Cytoplasmic and nuclear multiprotein proteolytic complex involved in degradation of excess, damaged, or misfolded proteins.

name: protectin
definition: Member of the Ly-6 family of cell surface molecules that prevents insertion of the membrane attack complex (MAC) into the membrane, thereby protecting cells from complement-induced lysis.

name: protective immunity
definition: Protection against infectious agents conferred by vaccination.

name: protein A
definition: Staphylococcus aureus cell wall protein that binds to the Fc region of immunoglobulin G (IgG).

name: proteinase 3
definition: Multifunctional enzyme of azurophilic granules of neutrophils and monocytes and the major target of antineutrophil cytoplasmic autoantibodies (ANCA).

name: protein G
definition: Streptococcal cell wall protein that binds to the Fc region of immunoglobulin G (IgG), with a wider species specificity than protein A.

name: protein kinase C
definition: Member of a kinase family with broad substrate specificity, activated by calcium, diacylglycerol, and (or) phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA).

name: prozone effect
definition: Loss of immunoprecipitation or agglutination that occurs when antibody concentration is increased to an extent that the antibody is in such excess that it is no longer able to effectively cross-link the antigen. A similar phenomenon may occur in antigen excess.

name: pseudoallergy
definition: Inflammatory or anaphylactic reaction with symptoms similar to an allergy but not involving an antigen-specific immune response, e.g., salicylate intolerance, reaction to contrast reagents.

name: psoriasis
definition: Skin disorder that has a hereditary component and is characterized by erythematous patches covered with silvery scales, especially on the elbows, knees, and scalp.

name: psoriatic
definition: Of, relating to, or associated with psoriasis; affected with psoriasis.

name: purified protein derivative
definition: Partially purified derivative of tuberculin used in the Mantoux test for tuberculosis.

name: purpura
definition: Purple discoloration occurring in patches on the skin, mucus membranes, or organs.

name: pyrogen
definition: Any substance that produces fever.

name: pyrogen test
definition: Any of various tests used to determine whether an agent, usually an infusion or injection fluid, is free of pyrogens.

name: Qa antigen
definition: 'Non-classical' major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class I molecule in mice.

name: radial immunodiffusion
definition: Method for quantifying an antigen by measuring the diameters of circular precipitates around an antigen-spiked cavity in an antibody-containing agar gel.

name: radioallergosorbent test
definition: Solid-phase radioimmunoassay (RIA) for detecting immunoglobulin E (IgE) antibody specific for a particular antigen.

name: radioimmunoconjugate
definition: Biochemical conjugate consisting of an immune-targeting molecule such as an antibody or antibody fragment together with a cytotoxic radionuclide.

name: Raynaud phenomenon
definition: Intermittent bilateral attacks of vasospasm and ischemia of the fingers or toes and sometimes of the ears and nose, marked by a severe pallor and often accompanied by paresthesia and pain.

name: reactive airways dysfunction syndrome
definition: Syndrome characterized by reversible airflow limitation and complicating bronchial hyperresponsiveness induced by acute exposure to high concentrations of non-sensitizer irritant gases.

name: reactive oxygen species
definition: Intermediates in the reduction of molecular dioxygen, \(\ce{O2}\), to water.

name: reagin
definition: Historic term for antibodies of the immunoglobulin E (IgE) class.

name: recall antigen
definition: Substance recognized by memory cells that stimulates rapid (secondary) immune responses, often associated with hypersensitivity.

name: recombinant antibody
definition: Antibody fragment manufactured by use of genetically modified microorganisms.

name: recombination-activating gene
definition: Gene whose products are involved in V(D)J recombination in B cells and T cells. Two such genes that have been identified are RAG-1 and RAG-2.

name: recombination signal sequence
definition: Any conserved heptamer (7-nucleotide)-nonamer (9-nucleotide) sequence, separated by a 12 or 23 base spacer, which occurs 3′ of variable gene segments, 5′ and 3′ of diversity gene segments, and 5′ of joining gene segments, in both immunoglobulin (Ig) and T-cell receptor (TCR) genes. It functions as a recognition sequence for the recombinase enzymes that mediate the gene rearrangement process involved in the generation of lymphocyte antigen receptor diversity.

name: red pulp
definition: Parenchymal tissue of the spleen consisting of cords of cells and sinuses infiltrated with erythrocytes and responsible for removal of aged or damaged erythrocytes.

name: Reed–Sternberg cell
definition: Large transformed lymphocyte, often binucleate, considered pathognomonic of Hodgkin lymphoma.

name: regulated upon activation normal T cell expressed and secreted
definition: Chemokine secreted by T cells and macrophages upon stimulation by mitogens, which acts as a chemoattractant and stimulates eosinophils and basophils.

name: regulatory idiotope
definition: Antibody or T-cell receptor (TCR) idiotope capable of regulating immune responses via interaction with lymphocytes bearing complementary idiotopes (anti-idiotopes).

name: regulatory T cell
definition: T cell that controls the maintenance of normal immune homeostasis. Treg cells are involved in controlling (anergizing or counter-regulating) autoreactive cells that escaped from thymic negative selection.

name: rejection
definition: Immune response leading to destruction of a transplanted organ or tissue.

name: respiratory burst
definition: Generation of cytotoxic superoxide from dioxygen due to increased NADPH oxidase activity, typically occurring in activated neutrophils.

name: respiratory hypersensitivity assay
definition: Test of the ability of a substance to induce hyperreactivity in the airways, typically measured as an increase in the rate of respiration of guinea pigs during inhalation of the substance.

name: reverse immunology
definition: High-throughput procedure where information on potential immunogenic tumor proteins is gained from the amino acid sequences of gene products specifically expressed by the tumor, followed by predicted fitting of putative antigenic peptides to a peptide-binding groove, and finally experimental verification.

name: rheumatic fever
definition: Inflammatory disease that may develop following a streptococcal infection such as strep throat, and may affect the heart, joints, skin, and brain.

name: rheumatoid arthritis
definition: Episodic inflammatory systemic disease with autoimmune pathogenetic mechanisms.

name: rheumatoid factor
definition: Immunoglobulins IgM, IgG, and IgA autoantibodies to the Fc region of IgG.

name: rhinitis
definition: Inflammation of the mucous membrane of the nose.

name: allergic rhinitis
definition: Nasal discharge resulting from an allergic response.

name: rocket electrophoresis
definition: Technique in which a test antigen is electrophoretically driven through an antibody-containing gel. The rocket-shaped tails of precipitation give information on the antigen concentration.

name: rosette
definition: Particles or cells bound to the surface of a lymphocyte (e.g., sheep erythrocytes around a human T cell).

name: scFv
definition: Single-chain molecule composed of the variable (V) regions of an antibody heavy and light chain joined together by a flexible linker.

name: sarcoidosis
definition: Chronic, progressive, generalized granulomatous reticulosis of unknown etiology, involving almost any organ or tissue, including the skin, lungs, lymph nodes, liver, spleen, eyes, and small bones of the hands and feet. It is characterized histologically by the presence in all affected organs or tissues of noncaseating epithelioid cell tubercles.

name: scavenger receptor
definition: Cell surface receptor, for example on phagocytes, which recognizes cells or molecules that require clearance from the body.

name: scleroderma
definition: Chronic progressive autoimmune disease characterized by systemic fibrosis and vascular changes.

name: secondary challenge
definition: Second exposure of primed lymphocytes to a given antigen.

name: secondary immune response
definition: Qualitatively and quantitatively improved immune response that occurs upon the second encounter of primed lymphocytes with a given antigen.

name: secondary lymphoid tissue
definition: Tissue (organ) in which antigen-driven proliferation and differentiation of mature B and T lymphocytes take place following antigen recognition.

name: second set rejection
definition: Accelerated rejection of an allograft in a primed recipient.

name: secretory component
definition: Proteolytic cleavage product of the poly-Ig receptor which remains associated with dimeric immunoglobulin A (IgA) in sero-mucus secretions.

name: secretory immunoglobulin A
definition: Dimeric immunoglobulin A (IgA) found in sero-mucus secretions.

name: selectin
definition: Any member of a family of cell-surface adhesion molecules found on leukocytes and endothelial cells and that bind to sugars on glycoproteins.

name: selective IgA deficiency
definition: Most common form of primary immunodeficiency.

name: self-tolerance
definition: Specific immunological unresponsiveness to a defined autoantigen.

name: sepsis
definition: Spread of bacteria or bacterial products throughout the blood, eliciting a life-threatening, systemic inflammatory reaction.

name: seroconversion
definition: The appearance in the blood serum of detectable antibodies against a specific infectious agent.

name: serology
definition: Study of serum, especially blood serum, frequently used to detect antibodies to microorganisms.

name: serum sickness
definition: Hypersensitive reaction to the administration of a foreign serum, characterized by fever, swelling, skin rash, and enlargement of the lymph nodes.

name: severe combined immunodeficiency
definition: Immunodeficiency affecting both T and B lymphocytes.

name: sheep red blood cell antigen
definition: T-cell-dependent target antigen often used in hemolytic plaque assays of immune responsiveness.

name: signaling lectin
definition: Any member of a large family of lectins that bind sialylated glycans.

name: signal peptide
definition: Any sequence of amino acid residues that, when linked to a newly synthesized protein, identifies it to transport mechanisms that guide the protein to a specific location among the organelles of a eukaryotic cell, or from the cytoplasm to the periplasmic space of prokaryotic cells.

name: signal transducer and activator of transcription
definition: Any member of a family of cytoplasmic proteins that act as second messengers to activate gene transcription in response to cytokines and growth factors.

name: single-chain antibody
definition: Small antibody construct in which the variable fragment (Fv) [see variable (V) region] of a heavy chain is linked via a synthetic peptide to the variable fragment of a light chain.

name: Sjögren syndrome
definition: Chronic inflammation of the lachrymal and salivary glands, often accompanied by rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and the presence of autoantibodies in the blood, occurring chiefly among women.

name: skin immune system
definition: Skin-associated cells that participate in an immune response, including Langerhans cells, dendritic cells, and keratinocytes (mainly responsible for production of cytokines).

name: skin sensitization test
definition: Any test used to study skin hypersensitivity such as the guinea pig maximization test or the Buehler test.

name: skin test
definition: Procedure for evaluating immunity status, involving the introduction of a reagent into or under the skin.

name: slow-reacting substance of anaphylaxis
definition: Group of leukotrienes released by mast cells during anaphylaxis, which induces a prolonged contraction of smooth muscle.

name: small G protein
definition: Any member of a family of monomeric G proteins, with molecular mass typically \(\pu{20\!{-}\! 40 kDa}\), that also bind guanine nucleotides and are involved in signal transduction.

name: small outer capsid protein
definition: Protein from the shell of the bacteriophage T4, commonly used in construction of phage antibody libraries.

name: somatic diversification theory
definition: Theory that very few immunoglobulins (Ig) are inherited, but that extensive antibody diversity arises from mutations in non-reproductive cells.

name: somatic gene conversion
definition: Nonreciprocal exchange of nucleic acid sequences between genes in which part of the donor gene or genes is 'copied' into an acceptor gene, but only the acceptor gene is altered.

name: somatic recombination
definition: Process giving rise to increased antibody diversity by cutting and splicing immunoglobulin (Ig) genes during lymphocyte differentiation.

name: spleen
definition: Largest of the secondary lymphoid organs, composed of white pulp, rich in lymphoid cells, and red pulp, which contains many erythrocytes and macrophages.

name: splenic
definition: Of, pertaining to, connected with, or situated in the spleen.

name: splenocyte
definition: Any splenic cell.

name: split adjuvant technique
definition: Test for allergic contact dermatitis in which guinea pig skin is exposed to repeated applications of a test substance and intradermal injections of complete Freund’s adjuvant are administered separately.

name: spondylitis
definition: Inflammation of the vertebral column.

name: spontaneous autoimmune thyroiditis
definition: Autoimmune thyroiditis (see thyroiditis, autoimmune) that develops spontaneously (without any apparent cause or manipulation) in certain strains of mice and rats (e.g., NOD mice, BB and BUF rats) as well as in other animals (e.g., OS chickens, marmoset monkeys, beagles).

name: Stevens–Johnson syndrome
definition: Allergic reaction, often to a medication (see adverse drug reaction) or infection, characterized by blistering of the skin and ulceration of mucosal membranes.

name: stroma
definition: Supporting tissue of an organ.

name: subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus
definition: Chronic remitting form of dermatitis characterized by severe photosensitivity and Ro/SS-A and La/SS-B autoantibodies.

name: superantigen
definition: Antigen which reacts with all the T cells belonging to a particular T-cell receptor (TCR) variable (V) region family, and which therefore stimulates (or deletes) a much larger number of cells than does conventional antigen.

name: superfamily
definition: Large group of proteins related by structural homology and function. The term also refers to the genes that encode them.

name: suppression
definition: Dominant immunological tolerance, a phenomenon that plays an active role in regulating T-cell and B-cell responses to both foreign antigens and autoantigens.

name: suppressor cell
definition: T cell that suppresses the immune response of B cells and other T cells to an antigen. In more current usage classified as a regulatory T cell.

name: supramolecular adhesion complex
definition: Collection of molecules forming at the contact point of a T cell and an antigen-presenting cell (APC), enriched in T-cell receptor (TCR), adhesion molecules, and signaling molecules.

name: surrogate light chain
definition: Light chain-like structure formed when the proteins encoded by the \({\rm{V}}_{\rm{preB}}\) and \(\uplambda_{5}\) genes associate with each other. It can form immunoglobulin (Ig)-like complexes which are expressed on the surface of pre-B cells at different stages of development.

name: switch sequence
definition: Highly conserved repetitive sequence that mediates class switching in the immunoglobulin (Ig) heavy chain gene locus.

name: sympathetic ophthalmia
definition: Autoimmune injury to one eye that occurs after penetrating injury or surgery to the other eye.

name: syngeneic
definition: Genetically identical, e.g., a fully inbred strain of mice.

name: systemic
definition: 1) Relating to the body as a whole. 2) Occurring at a site in the body remote from the point of contact with a substance.

name: systemic autoimmune disease
definition: Autoimmune disease affecting a number of organs or tissues, or the whole body.

name: systemic lupus erythematosus
definition: Chronic autoimmune disease that is potentially debilitating and sometimes fatal as the immune system attacks the body’s cells and tissues, with inflammation and tissue damage.

name: systemic sclerosis
definition: Fibrosing disease of unclear etiology that affects multiple organ systems.

name: drug-specific T cell
definition: T-memory cell that is specific for a drug allergen.

name: T-cell-dependent antibody response
definition: Immunotoxicity test that evaluates the ability of animals to produce antibodies to a T-dependent antigen [e.g., sheep red blood cells (SRBCs) or keyhole limpet hemocyanin (KLH)].

name: T-cell receptor
definition: Antigen-specific receptor on T cells composed of one set of heterodimeric chains. Two types of TCR heterodimers are known (\(\upalpha/\upbeta\) and \(\upgamma/\updelta\)).

name: T-dependent antigen
definition: Antigen that requires helper T lymphocytes (Th) in order to elicit an antibody response.

name: TdT-dependent dUTP-biotin nick end labeling assay
definition: Method for detecting apoptotic cells in situ based on characteristic DNA fragmentation. It is based on the ability of terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase (TdT) to transfer a labeled deoxyuridine triphosphate to the terminal ends arising from DNA cleavage.

name: Th0 cell
definition: Helper T lymphocyte (Th) with a less restricted cytokine profile than Th1 and Th2 cells.

name: Th1 cell
definition: Helper T lymphocyte (Th) producing mainly interleukin-2 (IL-2), interferon (IFN-$\ce{\upgamma\!}$), and tumor necrosis factor $\ce{\upbeta\!}$ ($\ce{TNF\mbox{-}\upbeta\!}$), and thereby responsible for phagocyte-dependent host responses.

name: Th2 cell
definition: Helper T lymphocyte (Th) in mice producing interleukins IL-4, IL-5, IL-6, IL-9, IL-10, and IL-13.

name: Th3 cell
definition: Helper T lymphocyte (Th) producing and responding to transforming growth factor $\ce{\upbeta\!}$ ($\ce{TGF\mbox{-}\upbeta\!}$) and helping immunoglobulin A (IgA) antibody responses.

name: Th9 cell
definition: Helper T lymphocyte (Th) producing interleukin IL-9, which stimulates mast cells.

name: Th17 cell
definition: Helper T lymphocyte (Th), distinct from Th1 and Th2 cells, that secretes the interleukin IL-17.

name: T-independent antigen
definition: Antigen that is able to elicit an antibody response in the absence of T cells.

name: T lymphocyte
definition: Lymphocyte that matures in the thymus and has the ability to recognize specific peptide antigens through the receptors on its cell surface.

name: Tr1 cell
definition: T lymphocyte that regulates Th1 cell responses. It resembles the regulatory T cell (Treg) and is possibly related to the Th3 cell.

name: tandem conjugate
definition: Molecular construct with two fluorochromes where the first excites the second by its emission.

name: target cell
definition: Cell killed by one of the body’s killer cells, such as a cytotoxic T lymphocyte or natural killer (NK) cell.

name: terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase
definition: Enzyme that inserts non-coded nucleotides at the junctions of V, D, and J gene segments of immunoglobulin (Ig) and T-cell receptor (TCR) locus DNA, thus increasing the diversity of antigen-specific recognition.

name: tetanus toxoid
definition: Detoxified tetanus toxin used to produce active immunity (see active immune response) against tetanus.

name: tetramer staining
definition: Technique used for selective staining of antigen-specific T lymphocytes in vitro or in situ. The antigen is presented to T cells by peptide tetramer constructs of major histocompatibility (MHC) class I molecules. It is also used to isolate antigen-specific T-cell populations for clonal expansion.

name: tertiary lymphoid tissue
definition: Ectopic lymphoid aggregates that accumulate during the process of chronic immune stimulation, and exhibit characteristics usually associated with the secondary lymphoid organs.

name: thromboxane
