definition: Any of several substances (predominantly thromboxanes A2 and B2) synthesized by platelets from arachidonic acid precursor, that cause vasoconstriction of vascular and bronchial smooth muscle and facilitates platelet aggregation.

name: thrush
definition: Oral infection with Candida albicans, often in patients with immunosuppression.

name: thymic
definition: Pertaining to the thymus.

name: thymic atrophy
definition: Involution of the thymus gland leading to a diminished capacity to generate new T cells.

name: thymic education
definition: Process by which T cells, developing in the thymus, are screened for potentially harmful self-reactive T cells (which are removed), while potentially beneficial T cells are promoted.

name: thymoma
definition: Rare, usually benign, tumor arising from tissue of the thymus gland.

name: thymus-dependent antigen
definition: Antigen that requires the participation of T lymphocytes to elicit an immune response in B lymphocytes.

name: thymus-independent antigen
definition: Antigen that does not require the participation of T lymphocytes to elicit an immune response in B cells.

name: thyroglobulin
definition: Glycoprotein secreted by thyroid follicular cells that is a major autoantigen in autoimmune diseases of the thyroid.

name: autoimmune thyroiditis
definition: Inflammatory destruction of the thyroid gland (ranging from a mild focal thyroiditis to extensive lymphocytic infiltration and scarring) often associated with goiter and hypothyroidism.

name: thyroid-stimulating hormone receptor
definition: Main autoantigenic target in patients with Graves disease.

name: thyroid peroxidase
definition: Thyroid enzyme that is a major autoantigen in autoimmune diseases of the thyroid.

name: tissue transglutaminase
definition: Main target of autoantibodies in celiac disease.

name: titer
definition: Reciprocal of the highest dilution of a titration of an antigen with an antibody that gives a measurable effect (e.g., agglutination), and thus an empirical measure of the avidity of an antibody.

name: tolerogen
definition: Antigen used to induce tolerance.

name: toll-like receptor
definition: Member of a family of pattern recognition receptors involved in the detection of structures associated with pathogens or damaged host tissues.

name: toxic epidermal necrolysis
definition: A severe form of Stevens–Johnson syndrome with extensive detachment of the skin, often as a result of an allergic adverse drug reaction.

name: toxic shock syndrome
definition: Systemic reaction produced by the toxin derived from the bacterium Staphylococcus aureus; the toxin acts as a superantigen, which activates a high proportion of CD4+ T lymphocytes to produce cytokines.

name: toxoid
definition: Chemically or physically modified toxin that is no longer harmful but retains immunogenicity.

name: transcytosis
definition: Vesicular transport of macromolecules from one side of a cell to the other, through the cell’s interior.

name: transforming growth factor β
definition: Secreted member of the protein superfamily of the same name that functions in controlling the cell cycle and apoptosis.

name: blood transfusion
definition: Transference of blood or blood-based products from one individual into the circulation of another.

name: transplantation
definition: Grafting solid tissue (e.g., cornea) or organ (e.g., kidney or heart), or cells (particularly bone marrow), from one individual to another.

name: transporters associated with antigen processing
definition: Molecules that carry antigenic peptides from the cytoplasm into the lumen of the endoplasmic reticulum for incorporation into major histocompatibility (MHC) class I molecules.

name: tryptophan
definition: Essential amino acid for humans, and required for T-cell proliferation.

name: tuberculin
definition: Antigen found in extracts of Mycobacteria, used in a skin test for tuberculosis (Mantoux test).

name: tuberculin test
definition: Diagnostic test in which antigens derived from the organism causing tuberculosis (Mycobacterium tuberculosis) are injected subcutaneously; individuals who have been exposed to the organism develop a delayed-type hypersensitivity (DTH) response at the injection site \(\pu{24}\) to \(\pu{48 h}\) later.

name: tumor antigen
definition: Antigen whose expression is associated with tumor cells.

name: tumor immunology
definition: Application of immunology to understanding tumor biology, immune system avoidance by tumors, and immunotherapy directed against tumors.

name: tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte
definition: Mononuclear lymphocyte derived from the inflammatory infiltrate of a solid tumor.

name: tumor necrosis factor
definition: Protein produced and secreted by several of the body’s cell types, including leukocytes.

name: tumor necrosis factor receptor-associated factor
definition: Family of proteins involved in regulating inflammation and apoptosis through interaction with the tumor necrosis factor receptor.

name: tumor rejection antigen
definition: Antigen present specifically on a tumor cell that may target it for destruction by the immune system or for antibody therapy.

name: tumor-specific transplantation antigen
definition: Antigen, present only on a tumor cell, and targetable by the immune system or by antibody therapy in order to destroy the tumor.

name: tyrosine kinase
definition: Any member of a family of enzymes that phosphorylates target proteins on tyrosine residues, thus playing a crucial role in signal transduction.

name: ubiquitin
definition: Highly conserved 76 amino acid peptide abundant in eukaryotic cells. Its covalent attachment to a protein by a ubiquitin ligase complex targets that protein for destruction by the proteasome.

name: unresponsiveness
definition: Inability to respond to an antigenic stimulus.

name: Vα-Jα rearrangement
definition: Preferential partnering of \(\ce{J\upalpha\ gene}\) segments with \(\ce{V\upalpha\ gene}\) segments during rearrangement in the T-cell receptor (TCR) gene, possibly following deletion of the \(\ce{V\updelta\ gene}\) region.

name: V(D)J recombination
definition: Mechanism for generating antigen-specific receptors of T cells and B cells; it involves the joining of V, D, and J gene segments, mediated by the enzyme complex V(D)J recombinase, and products of the recombination-activating genes.

name: vaccination
definition: Immunization with a vaccine against a pathogen.

name: variable gene
definition: Gene, segment(s) of which rearrange together with diversity (D) gene and joining (J) gene segments in order to encode the variable (V) region amino acid sequences of immunoglobulins (Ig) and T-cell receptors (TCRs).

name: variable region
definition: N-terminal portion of an immunoglobulin (Ig) or T-cell receptor (TCR) that contains the antigen-binding region of the molecule. V regions are formed by the recombination of V(D) and J gene segments.

name: vascular addressin
definition: Cell adhesion molecule present on the luminal surface of blood and lymph vessel endothelium, recognized by homing molecules that direct leukocytes to tissues with the appropriate 'address'.

name: vascular cell adhesion molecule
definition: Molecule, expressed on the surface of endothelial cells that functions in the adhesion of lymphocytes, monocytes, eosinophils, and basophils to vascular endothelium to the vascular surface.

name: vasculitis
definition: Group of disorders that share a common underlying problem of inflammation of a blood vessel or vessels.

name: vasoactive amine
definition: Substance containing amino group(s) that increases vascular permeability and smooth muscle contraction.

name: very early activating antigen
definition: Specific antigen expressed on lymphocytes very soon after activation by phorbol myristate acetate (PMA).

name: very late activation antigen
definition: T-cell surface antigen, named for its delayed appearance after T-cell activation; a member of the integrin superfamily involved in cell adhesion.

name: vetoing
definition: Elimination by apoptosis of a self-peptide-major histocompatibility complex (MHC) molecule recognizing lymphocyte by a self-peptide-presenting (veto) cell.

name: warm autoantibody type
definition: Autoantibodies that react optimally at higher temperatures (\(\pu{37^{\circ}C}\)) with surface antigens of erythrocytes. They mediate autoimmune hemolytic anemia.

name: Wegener granulomatosis
definition: Granulomatous inflammation involving the respiratory tract, and necrotizing vasculitis affecting small to medium-sized vessels (e.g., capillaries, venules, arterioles, and arteries).

name: wheal
definition: Circumscribed papule or plaque of edema of the skin, occurring as an urticarial lesion.

name: wheal and flare
definition: Dermatological reaction at a skin site where an antigen is injected into an allergic individual. The reaction is characterized by a 'flare' of erythema and a wheal produced by serum exuding into tissue, causing local edema.

name: white pulp
definition: Collections of lymphocytes in the spleen, responsible for its immune function.

name: Wiskott–Aldrich syndrome
definition: Condition characterized by chronic eczema, chronic suppurative otitis media, anemia, and thrombocytopenic purpura (accompanied by bloody diarrhea); it is an immunodeficiency syndrome transmitted as an X-linked recessive trait, in which there is poor antibody response to polysaccharide antigens and dysfunction of cell-mediated immunity.

name: X-linked agammaglobulinemia
definition: Sex-linked impairment of the ability to produce mature B cells, thus characterized by recurrent infections.

name: X-linked severe combined immunodeficiency
definition: Sex-linked trait carried on the X-chromosome of severe combined immunodeficiency syndrome resulting from nonfunctional B lymphocytes and lack of T lymphocytes and natural killer (NK) lymphocytes, leading to recurrent, persistent, and severe infections.

name: xenogeneic
definition: Exhibiting genetic differences between species.

name: xenograft
definition: Tissue or organ graft between individuals of different species.

name: xenophagy
definition: Autophagy selective for degradation of intracellular bacteria and viruses.

name: Zeta chain-associated protein kinase-70 kDa
definition: T-lymphocyte-specific tyrosine kinase involved in T-lymphocyte activation.

name: zymosan
definition: Crude preparation of yeast cell walls, consisting chiefly of polysaccharide, activating the alternative pathway of the complement system in the presence of properdin and used in the immunoassay of this compound.

name: amphiphile
definition: Substance made up of molecules containing groups that are solvophilic and other groups that are solvophobic with respect to a given solvent.

name: boloamphiphile
definition: Amphiphile, the constituent molecules of which have solvophilic groups at each end of a solvophobic chain.

name: barotropic mesophase
definition: Mesophase formed by varying the pressure at constant temperature.

name: calamitic
definition: Having a rod- or lath-like shape.

name: carceplex
definition: Host-guest complex formed by a carcerand and a completely entrapped guest.

name: carcerand
definition: Host molecule that completely entraps a guest molecule.

name: co-assembly
definition: Self-assembly of two or more self-assembling species that might or might not incorporate a non-assembling component into an ordered structure.

name: coil-to-globule transition
definition: Change in conformation of a macromolecular chain in solution from that of a coil to a relatively compact structure in which the chain has collapsed upon itself in response to an external stimulus.

name: colloidal crystal
definition: Two- or three-dimensional ordered array of molecules or nanoparticles having a dimension roughly between \(\pu{1 nm}\) and \(\pu{1 \upmu m}\) in at least one direction.

name: columnar phase
definition: Cylindrical assembly of molecules within a distinct series of layers in which the axes of the molecules lie in the planes of the layers and are identically aligned and oriented in adjacent layers.

name: core-crosslinked micelle
definition: Core-shell structure formed by self-assembly of amphiphiles and subsequently covalently crosslinked through functionalities in the core.

name: core-shell structure
definition: Molecular entity of spherical, elliptical, or cylindrical symmetry in which the constitution of the interior, the core, differs from that of the external surface, the shell.

name: crystal lattice defect
definition: Interruption to the regular pattern of atomic arrangement in crystal lattices.

name: cubic
definition: Pertaining to assemblies of atoms, molecules, or ions with an overall three-dimensional order of cubic symmetry.

name: cubic mesophase
definition: Mesophase with an overall three-dimensional order of cubic symmetry.

name: director
definition: Local symmetry axis for the singlet, orientational distribution of the molecules of a mesophase.

name: discotic
definition: Having a disc-like shape.

name: discotic mesogen
definition: Mesogen composed of relatively flat, disc- or sheet-shaped molecules.

name: dynamer
definition: Assembly or supramolecular assembly, the components of which are linked through reversible bondings that enable structural reassembly by reshuffling in response to changes in the chemical or physical environment.

name: electroclinic polymer
definition: Polymer with constitutional units that are susceptible to a change in orientation under the influence of an electric field that causes the system to have induced polarity.

name: micro-encapsulation
definition: Confinement of microscopic particles with a host.

name: molecular encapsulation
definition: Confinement of an individual molecule within a larger molecule.

name: external field
definition: Field surrounding a molecular or ionic species emanating from a source external to that species.

name: fluorophilic
definition: Qualifier indicating attraction to fluorous compounds.

name: fluorophilic interaction
definition: Attractive interaction of fluorous structures.

name: fluorophobic
definition: Qualifier indicating repulsion by fluorous compounds.

name: fluorophobic interaction
definition: Repulsive interaction of fluorous and non-fluorous structures.

name: fluorous
definition: Pertaining to the presence of a sufficient number of carbon-fluorine bonds as to cause a substance to be insoluble in water or common organic solvents but soluble in fluorocarbons.

name: foldamer
definition: Polymer or oligomer molecule that adopts a secondary structure stabilized by noncovalent interactions.

name: globule
definition: Conformation of a macromolecule in which the constitutional units collectively arrange into a compact ovoid or spherical shape.

name: globule-to-coil transition
definition: Reverse of a coil-to-globule transition.

name: hemicarceplex
definition: Complex formed by a hemicarcerand and an entrapped guest.

name: hemicarcerand
definition: Host molecule that allows guest molecules to enter and exit its cavities in accordance with a change in the equilibrium conditions.

name: hexagonal mesophase
definition: Columnar mesophase characterized by a hexagonal packing of the molecular column.

name: honeycomb polymer film
definition: Hexagonal array of holes in a polymer film.

name: hydrophilic interaction
definition: Attractive interaction between hydrophilic groups, molecules, or substances.

name: hydrophobic
definition: Qualifier indicating capacity of a molecular entity or of a substituent to interact repulsively with polar molecules, in particular with water or with polar groups.

name: inverse opal
definition: Colloidal crystal of spherical voids with a periodic structure within a solid polymer continuum.

name: lamella
definition: Organized structure extended in two dimensions and of uniform thickness resembling a thin layer, a plate, or a membrane.

name: lamellar block copolymer
definition: Assembly of block copolymer molecules in which like blocks are segregated in lamella.

name: layer-by-layer assembly
definition: Process whereby multilayered structures of molecules or particles of a substance are assembled on a solid substrate by sequential adsorption of monolayers held together by noncovalent interactions.

name: mechanically interlocked molecular architecture
definition: Supramolecular structure in which molecules are linked only as a consequence of their topology.

name: metallomesogen
definition: Mesogen composed of molecules incorporating one or more metal atoms.

name: micellar rod
definition: Rod-like mesogens with the capacity to form micellar aggregates.

name: microstructure
definition: Structure of material in which at least one of the features repeats over distances of the order of micrometers.

name: molecular imprinting
definition: Technique to create templated cavities in polymer matrices with memory of the template molecules to be used in molecular recognition.

name: nanodomain
definition: Region of a self-assembled entity with an equivalent diameter of approximately \(\pu{(1\!-\! 100) nm}\).

name: nanoscopic polymer film
definition: Polymer film that has lateral dimensions in the range of \(\pu{(1\!-\! 100) nm}\).

name: organophilic
definition: Qualifier indicating tendency of a molecular entity or of a pendent group thereof to interact favourably with nonpolar organic solvents.

name: organophilic interaction
definition: Attractive interaction between organophilic molecules or materials.

name: orientation parameter
definition: Order parameter applied to macroscopic assemblies of ordered materials, such as crystal assemblies in fibers.

name: pendent chain
definition: Oligomeric or polymeric offshoot from a macromolecular chain.

name: polymersome
definition: Vesicle with radius ranging from \(\pu{50 nm}\) to greater than \(\pu{5 \upmu m}\) constructed from an amphiphilic synthetic block copolymer.

name: polymolecular
definition: Consisting of many molecules.

name: polyrotaxane
definition: Polymer comprising mechanically interlocked molecular architectures typically of a macromolecule threaded through one or more macrocycles.

name: ditopic receptor
definition: Receptor with two binding sites.

name: rod-coil copolymer
definition: Copolymer the molecules of which consist of rigid and flexible blocks.

name: Scatchard equation
definition: Equation used to calculate the association constant, \(K_{\rm{a}}\), of a ligand with a protein molecule.

name: Scatchard plot
definition: Linear plot of \(r/c\) against \(r\) in accordance with the Scatchard equation.

name: main-chain self-assembly
definition: Inter- or intra-molecular self-assembly of constitutional units within the backbones of polymer molecules.

name: side-chain self-assembly
definition: Inter- or intra-molecular self-assembly of side-chains or constitutional units of polymer molecules.

name: shell-crosslinked micelle
definition: Core-shell structure formed by self-assembly of amphiphiles and subsequently covalently crosslinked through functionalities in the shell.

name: smectic
definition: Pertaining to the arrangement and orientation of molecules in a smectic mesophase.

name: smectic mesophase
definition: Mesophase that has the molecules arranged in layers with a well-defined layer spacing or periodicity.

name: spherand
definition: Macrocyclic compound capable of completely enveloping a cation, having donor atoms (\(\ce{O}\), \(\ce{N}\), \(\ce{S}\)) arranged such that they provide a solvation sphere to the encapsulated cation.

name: π-π stacking
definition: Inter- or intra-molecular alignment of aromatic groups within molecules induced by the interactional overlap of their \(\ce{\uppi\mbox{-}orbitals}\).

name: T-stacking
definition: Orthogonal alignment of constitutional units within molecules that lead to favourable interactions.

name: static self-assembly
definition: Self-assembly at equilibrium.

name: stimuli-responsive polymer
definition: Polymer that responds reversibly to external stimulus or stimuli.

name: solvophilic
definition: Qualifier indicating an affinity for solvents.

name: solvophobic
definition: Qualifier indicating a lack of affinity for solvents.

name: supramolecular association
definition: Self-assembly involving reversible, noncovalent, directional interactions of molecules that result in a high-molecular-mass entity.

name: template polymerization
definition: Polymerization of monomer molecules adsorbed and oriented (a) on a surface, (b) in a polymer lattice, (c) on polymer molecules in solution, or (d) round a metal ion whereby the structure of the polymer chains formed is controlled by the orientation of the monomer molecules.

name: lipid vesicle
definition: Vesicle constructed from a lipid bilayer.

name: artificial
definition: Qualifier for something that is made by human activity, rather than occurring naturally.

name: artificial polymer
definition: Man-made polymer that is not a biopolymer.

name: bioactive
definition: Qualifier for a substance that provokes any response from a living system.

name: bioactivity
definition: Capability of a substance, such as a drug or a vaccine, to provoke a response from a living matter.

name: bioadhesion
definition: Adhesion of cells or tissues to the surface of a material.

name: bioalteration
definition: Cell-mediated chemical modification without main chain scission.

name: biodegradability
definition: Capability of being degraded by biological activity.

name: biodisintegration
definition: Disintegration resulting from the action of cells.

name: biofilm
definition: Aggregate of microorganisms in which cells that are frequently embedded within a self-produced matrix of extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) adhere to each other and/or to a surface.

name: biofragmentation
definition: Fragmentation resulting from the action of cells.

name: biomaterial
definition: Material exploited in contact with living tissues, organisms, or microorganisms.

name: biomineralization
definition: Mineralization caused by cell-mediated phenomena.

name: biostability
definition: Resistance to the deleterious action of living systems that allows preservation of the initial characteristics of a substance.

name: biotic
definition: Pertaining to, or produced by, living cells or organisms.

name: bulk degradation
definition: Homogeneous degradation affecting the volume of a sample.

name: controlled delivery
definition: Supply of a substance according to desired rate and amount over time.

name: degradability
definition: Capability of undergoing degradation.

name: degradable macromolecule
definition: Macromolecule that is able to undergo chain scissions under specific conditions, resulting in a decrease of molar mass.

name: degradable polymer
definition: Polymer in which macromolecules are able to undergo chain scissions, resulting in a decrease of molar mass.

name: degradation
definition: Progressive loss of the performance or of the characteristics of a substance or a device.

name: degradation
definition: Degradation that results in desired changes in the values of in-use properties of the material because of macromolecule cleavage and molar mass decrease.

name: degree of bioassimilation
definition: Mass fraction of a substance that is bioassimilated.

name: degree of biodegradation
definition: Mass fraction of a substance that is biodegraded under specified conditions as measured through specified phenomena or techniques sensitive to mineral and biomass formations.

name: degree of biodisintegration
definition: Mass fraction of a biodisintegrated substance.

name: degree of biofragmentation
definition: Mass fraction of the original material that is biofragmented.

name: degree of biomineralization
definition: Mass fraction of a substance that is biomineralized.

name: degree of degradation
definition: Mass fraction of a polymer that is degraded under specified conditions as measured through a specified phenomenon sensitive to molecular dimensions.

name: degree of disintegration
definition: Mass fraction of the particles of defined size issued from a fragmented substance.

name: degree of fragmentation
definition: Mass fraction of a substance that is fragmented.

name: degree of mineralization
definition: Mass fraction of a substance that is mineralized.

name: depolymerase
definition: Enzyme that is able to catalyse the depolymerization of a biomacromolecule.

name: deterioration
definition: Deleterious alteration of a material in quality, serviceability, or vigor.

name: disintegration
definition: Fragmentation to particles of a defined size.

name: durability
definition: Ability of a material to retain the values of its properties under specified conditions.

name: enzymatic degradation
definition: Degradation caused by the catalytic action of enzymes.

name: erosion
definition: Degradation that occurs at the surface and progresses from it into the bulk.

name: genetic engineering
definition: Process of inserting new genetic information into existing cells in order to modify a specific organism for the purpose of changing its characteristics.

name: maximum degree of biodegradation
definition: Greater value of the degree of biodegradation that can be reached under selected experimental conditions.

name: microcapsule
definition: Hollow microparticle composed of a solid shell surrounding a core-forming space available to permanently or temporarily entrapped substances.

name: microparticle
definition: Particle with dimensions between \(\pu{1E-7}\) and \(\pu{1E-4 m}\).

name: microsphere
definition: Microparticle of spherical shape without membrane or any distinct outer layer.

name: mineralization
definition: Process through which an organic substance becomes impregnated by or turned into inorganic substances.

name: nanocapsule
definition: Hollow nanoparticle composed of a solid shell that surrounds a core-forming space available to entrap substances.

name: nanosphere
definition: Nanoparticle of spherical shape without membrane or any distinct outer layer.

name: plastic
definition: Generic term used in the case of polymeric material that may contain other substances to improve performance and/or reduce costs.

name: solid dispersion
definition: Solid multiphasic mixture with at least one polymer component dominating.

name: stimulus-responsive polymer
definition: Polymer that responds or that is designed to respond to a stimulus like pH, light, heat, etc. change, and provides a predetermined action.

name: sustained delivery
definition: Supply of a substance from a container where it is temporarily entrapped for the sake of achieving a prolonged action.

name: synthetic biopolymer
definition: Copy of a biopolymer man-made using abiotic chemical routes.

name: theoretical degree of biodegradation
definition: Degree of biodegradation that corresponds to conversion of all the organic matter present in an original polymer-based item to minerals and biomass.

name: ultimate biodegradation
definition: Complete breakdown of a compound to either fully oxidized or reduced simple molecules (such as carbon dioxide/methane, nitrate/ammonium, and water).

name: artificial organ
definition: Medical device that replaces, in part or in whole, the function of one of the organs of the body.

name: biomedical
definition: Qualifier for a domain grouping scientific and practical activities related to therapy.

name: bioprosthesis
definition: Implantable prosthesis that consists totally or substantially of nonviable, treated donor tissue.

name: bioresorbability
definition: Ability to be eliminated from an animal or human body through natural pathways.

name: bioresorption
definition: Disappearance of a substance from an organism by processes of metabolism, secretion, or excretion.

name: bone cement
definition: Synthetic, self-curing organic or inorganic material used to fill up a cavity or to create a mechanical fixation.

name: carcinogenicity
definition: Ability or tendency to produce cancer.

name: drug carrier
definition: Macromolecule or polymer used to transport a pharmacologically active compound to be released later on due to an abiotic or biotic process.

name: foreign body reaction
definition: Cellular response of the inflammatory and wound healing processes following introduction of a foreign object in a human or animal body.

name: host response
definition: Reaction of a living system to the presence of a substance or a material.

name: hybrid artificial organ
definition: Artificial organ that is a combination of viable cells and one or more biomaterials.

name: immunogenicity
definition: Ability of a material or substance to elicit a cellular immune response and/or antibody production.

name: implant
definition: Medical device made from one or more biomaterials that is intentionally placed within the body, either totally or partially buried beneath an epithelial surface.

name: macromolecular prodrug
definition: Prodrug in which the temporary chemical entity is a macromolecule.

name: medical device
definition: Instrument, apparatus, implement, machine, contrivance, in vitro reagent, or other similar or related article, including any component, part of accessory, which is intended for use in the diagnosis of disease or other conditions, or in the cure, mitigation, treatment, or prevention of disease in man.

name: pharmaceutical
definition: Qualifier for substances or systems, including polymers, exploited by the pharmaceutical industry.

name: pharmacological
definition: Qualifiers for substances, including macromolecules or polymers, and actions involved in pharmacology.

name: pharmacologically active
definition: Qualifier for a substance that exhibits bioactivity of pharmacological interest.

name: pharmacology
definition: Science of drugs including their origin, composition, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, therapeutic use, and toxicology.

name: prodrug
definition: Compound that undergoes biotransformation before exhibiting pharmacological effects.

name: prosthesis
definition: Device that replaces a limb, organ, or tissue of the body.

name: stealth
definition: Qualifier for a macromolecule, a surface, or a device that is not detected by defense proteins of the complement and the Mononuclear Phagocyte System, especially macrophages, after introduction in parental compartments.

name: targeting
definition: Exploitation of specific or nonspecific interactions to target a particular part of a living system, or a particular type of cells.

name: therapeutic polymer
definition: Polymer aimed at helping therapists in treating diseases or trauma.

name: thrombogenicity
definition: Property of a material (or substance) that induces and/or promotes the formation of a thrombus.

name: tissue engineering
definition: Use of a combination of cells, engineering and materials methods, and suitable biochemical and physico-chemical factors to improve or replace biological functions.

name: transplant
definition: Complete structure, such as an organ that is transferred from a site in a donor to a site in a recipient for the purpose of the reconstruction of the recipient site.

name: aerobic biodegradation
definition: Biodegradation in the presence of molecular oxygen.

name: anaerobic biodegradation
definition: Biodegradation in the absence of oxygen.

name: bioplastic
definition: Biobased polymer derived from the biomass or issued from monomers derived from the biomass and which, at some stage in its processing into finished products, can be shaped by flow.

name: compost
definition: Solid product resulting from the decomposition of organic wastes by fermentation.

name: conditioning film
definition: Film that is rapidly formed on the surface of a solid in contact with a biological system (in the widest sense) that conditions the surface for subsequent interaction with constituents of the biological system.

name: ecotoxicity
definition: Consequence of adverse effects caused by a substance on the environment and on organisms living in it.

name: environmentally degradable polymer
definition: Polymer that can be degraded by the action of the environment, through, for example, air, light, heat, or microorganisms.

name: environmentally friendly
definition: Qualifiers for a substance, device, or process that has minimal deleterious impact on the environment, which is air, water, minerals, living systems, etc.

name: green polymer
definition: Polymer that conforms to the concept of green chemistry.

name: life cycle assessment
definition: Investigation and valuation of the environmental impacts of a given product or service caused or necessitated by its existence.

name: mulching film
definition: Polymer film aimed at covering seeded area in order to protect the growing plants from weeds and cold and preserve humidity.

name: sustainability
definition: Developments that meet the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their needs.

name: waste
definition: Residue left when a compound or a product reaches the end of its initial usefulness.

name: waste management
definition: Control of the collection, treatment and disposal of wastes.

name: macrocyclic component
definition: Molecule that has at least one ring (cycle) large enough to allow it to be threaded onto a linear subchain of another molecule.

name: macromolecular component
definition: Macromolecule that is part of a rotaxane assembly.

name: macromolecular pseudorotaxane
definition: Pseudorotaxane, at least one component of which is a macromolecule.

name: macromolecular rotaxane
definition: Rotaxane, at least one component of which is a macromolecule.

name: main-chain macromolecular rotaxane
definition: Macromolecular rotaxane in which rotaxane constitutional units are exclusively located within the main macromolecular chain.

name: main-chain rotaxane polymer
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecular assemblies that are main-chain macromolecular rotaxanes.

name: molecular shuttle
definition: Rotaxane or pseudorotaxane comprising a threading component upon which is threaded a macrocyclic component that, depending on the conditions, can reside at either a specific recognition site on the threading component or away from any recognition site.

name: pseudorotaxane
definition: Rotaxane-like molecular assembly in which the threading component(s) has(have) ends small enough to permit threading or dethreading of the macrocyclic component(s).

name: pseudorotaxane polymer
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules that are macromolecular pseudorotaxanes.

name: regular macromolecular rotaxane
definition: Macromolecular rotaxane, the structure of which essentially comprises the repetition of a single constitutional unit of the rotaxane type, referred to as the rotaxane constitutional repeating unit, rot-CRU, with all units connected identically with respect to directional sense.

name: rotaxane constitutional repeating unit
definition: Constitutional repeating unit (CRU) that has a rotaxane structure.

name: rotaxane constitutional unit
definition: Constitutional unit (CU) that has a rotaxane structure.

name: rotaxane end-unit
definition: Constitutional unit of a macromolecular rotaxane consisting of an end-group of its macromolecular component and a complementary threading or macrocyclic component.

name: rotaxane monomer
definition: Monomer that is a rotaxane.

name: rotaxane monomeric unit
definition: Monomeric unit (monomer unit, mer) that has a rotaxane structure.

name: rotaxane polymer
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules that are macromolecular rotaxanes.

name: side-chain macromolecular rotaxane
definition: Macromolecular rotaxane in which rotaxane constitutional units are located exclusively in side chains of the macromolecule.

name: side-chain rotaxane polymer
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecular assemblies that are side-chain macromolecular rotaxanes.

name: stopper
definition: Group bulky enough to prevent dethreading of a given macrocyclic component from a threading component or its translocation to another linear section of the threading component.

name: threadable ring
definition: Key part of a macrocyclic component: molecular ring (cycle) large enough to be threaded onto a linear subchain of a threading component.

name: threading component
definition: Molecule with at least one linear section onto which at least one macrocyclic component is threaded.

name: absorbed local spectral photon flux density
definition: Local value of the spectral photon radiance, or spectral photon flux density, defined for a three-dimensional space, often in terms of napierian properties.
synonyms: local spectral photon density absorption rate|local volumetric rate of photon absorption

name: absorbed local spectral radiance
definition: Local value of the spectral radiance, or energy density absorption rate, defined for a three-dimensional space, often in terms of napierian properties.
synonyms: local volumetric rate of energy absorption

name: absorbed radiant density
definition: Monochromatic radiant energy, per time interval (spectral radiance) coming from all directions and absorbed by a system integrated over the whole volume and averaged per volume \(V\), \(\langle L_{\lambda}^{\rm{a}}\left(t \right) \rangle_{V}\).

name: accumulation layer
definition: Subsurface space where the majority carriers accumulate near the surface of a semiconductor because of band bending caused by the surface potential.

name: active state
definition: Electronically excited surface centre, or a surface centre (surface site) with a trapped photogenerated charge carrier that interacts with species at the solid/liquid, liquid/liquid, solid/gas, or liquid/gas interfaces with formation of, e.g., chemisorbed species.

name: active state
definition: Electronically excited surface centre, or a surface centre (surface site) with a trapped photogenerated charge carrier or reactive intermediate that interacts with molecular entities at an interface with the formation of reaction products or intermediates.

name: area-related parameters
definition: Quantities expressed in terms of 'per area' are denoted as area-related parameters.

name: artificial photosynthesis
definition: Photocatalytic production of substances from simple compounds (e.g., \(\ce{H2}\) and \(\ce{O2}\) from water, \(\ce{H2}\) from hydrogen sulfide, etc.) using ultraviolet, visible, or infrared radiation absorbed by chromophoric systems, often included in microheterogeneous media, mimicking the action of antennae and reaction centres in natural photosynthetic organisms.

name: band-to-band recombination
definition: Recombination of charge carriers occurring via a one-step electron transition from the conduction band to the valence band in a semiconductor or insulator.

name: black body
definition: Idealised object absorbing all incident radiant power, regardless of wavelength and transforming it all into heat. No electromagnetic radiation passes through it and none is reflected. A black body is a perfect absorber of radiant energy. Therefore, it is also a perfect emitter of radiation. The wavelength distribution of the radiation of a black body depends only on its temperature and not on its internal nature or structure.

name: black-body-like photocatalytic reactor
definition: Reactor used to determine quantum yields of photoadsorption and photocatalysed reactions when the catalyst is in the form of a powdered layer (or powder dispersion). The incident photons are (nearly) all absorbed by the catalyst, provided that the dispersion layer is sufficiently thick (or the dispersion is sufficiently concentrated).

name: Brunauer–Emmett–Teller surface area
definition: Specific surface area (\(\pu{m2 kg-1}\)) determined from the adsorption isotherm of a gas with the help of the Brunauer, Emmett, and Teller model using the conventional value for the molecular cross-section.

name: catalyst photoactivation
definition: Generation or alteration of the catalytic activity (selectivity) of a substance after its interaction with light.

name: catalytic site
definition: Site at which catalysed chemical transformations take place.

name: catalysed photochemical reaction
definition: Enhancement (alteration) of efficiency of photochemical reactions upon direct excitation of photoactive reactants via an intermediate interaction of these reactants with certain compounds that act as catalysts (promoters) of the appropriate chemical transformations of the reactants.

name: Coekelbergs effect
definition: Adsorption at the surface of a pre-irradiated adsorbent (the photocatalyst) occurring in the dark, after the irradiation in the presence of the photoadsorbate entities is terminated, i.e., after preliminary photoadsorption.

name: colour centres
definition: Lattice defects (typically vacancies) that trap one or more electrons or holes in ionic crystals. They constitute a long-lived deep trap with a low efficiency of trapping of a carrier of the opposite sign.

name: deep energy trap
definition: Trap defined by an energy level (of trapped carriers) within the bandgap energy of a semiconductor or insulator with an energy difference between it and the conduction band (for electrons) or valence band (for holes) much greater than the energy of thermal excitation of the solid at a given temperature.

name: depletion layer
definition: Subsurface space where the majority carriers are forced away owing to band bending caused by the surface potential. (i) The subsurface layer of an n-type semiconductor becomes depleted of electrons, which are the majority carriers, as a consequence of upward band bending. (ii) The subsurface layer of a p-type semiconductor becomes enriched by electrons (depleted of holes) as a consequence of downward band bending.

name: direct bandgap semiconductor
definition: Semiconductor or dielectric materials whose first band-to-band transition occurs from the highest level in the valence band to the lowest level in the conduction band possessing the same electron momentum, i.e., \(\boldsymbol{p}_{\rm{max}} = \boldsymbol{p}_{\rm{min}}\), with \(\boldsymbol{p}_{\rm{max}}\) and \(\boldsymbol{p}_{\rm{min}}\) the momentum vectors of electrons of the highest level in the valence band and the lowest level in the conduction band, respectively.

name: dynamic photoadsorption process
definition: Simultaneous (or synchronous) formation of adsorbed species (adsorbate) via photoadsorption and detachment by photodesorption to yield the same species, both processes occurring under photoexcitation of the solid photocatalyst (adsorbent).

name: effective radiation-catalytic activity
definition: Number of product entities (atoms, molecules, or radicals) generated by each \(\pu{100 eV}\) of radiation incident on the system.

name: electrical double layer
definition: Array of charged species and oriented dipoles existing at a solid-solution interface. The solid may be a metal or a semiconductor. Double refers to the fact that the surface charge and its counter charge at the solution side are included.

name: exciton absorption
definition: Absorption of ultraviolet, visible, or infrared radiation yielding optical information on the excitons in solids. Exciton absorption bands in a spectrum of a semiconductor or insulator are located on the long wavelength side of the fundamental absorption edge.

name: extrinsic absorption
definition: Absorption of ultraviolet, visible, or infrared radiation in semiconductors and insulators corresponding to optical transitions of electrons from defect energy levels (within the bandgap energy) to conduction band levels, or holes to valence band levels (photoionisation of defects), or from the ground state level to excited levels of a given intrinsic defect of any sort.

name: extrinsic defect
definition: Imperfection in a solid semiconductor (or insulator) connected with surface defects of any sort involving extrinsic chemical units in relation to the chemical formula of the solid, particularly adsorbed species of any sort.

name: F centres
definition: Anion vacancies occupied by electrons in semiconductors.

name: Fermi level splitting
definition: Splitting of the Fermi level in irradiated semiconductors and insulators into two Fermi quasi-levels for electrons \(E_{\rm{F}}^{\rm{e}}\) and for holes \(E_{\rm{F}}^{\rm{h}}\), displaced toward the bottom of the conduction band and toward the top of the valence band, respectively.

name: free charge carriers
definition: Applies to free electrons or free holes.

name: free electrons
definition: Photoexcited electrons from the valence band into the conduction band in semiconductors and insulators.

name: fundamental absorption
definition: Absorption of ultraviolet, visible, or infrared radiation in semiconductors and insulators inducing optical transitions of electrons originating exclusively from the valence band to the conduction band to yield free electron-hole pairs and/or exciton absorption bands.

name: fundamental absorption edge
definition: High wavelength limit of the fundamental absorption band in the spectrum of semiconductors and of insulators.

name: heterogeneous photocatalysis
definition: Photocatalysis taking place at the interfacial boundary between two phases (solid/liquid, solid/gas, liquid/gas).

name: heterogeneous radiation catalysis
definition: Radiation catalysis taking place in heterogeneous systems.

name: homogeneous photocatalysis
definition: Photocatalysis taking place in homogeneous systems.

name: homogeneous radiation catalysis
definition: Radiation catalysis taking place in homogeneous systems.

name: indirect bandgap semiconductor
definition: Semiconductor or dielectric materials with a first band-to-band transition from the highest level in the valence band to the lowest level in the conduction band requiring the change of electron momentum, that is \(\boldsymbol{p}_{\rm{max}}  eq \boldsymbol{p}_{\rm{min}}\), where \(\boldsymbol{p}_{\rm{max}}\) and \(\boldsymbol{p}_{\rm{min}}\) are the momentum vectors of electrons of the highest level in the valence band and the lowest level in the conduction band, respectively.

name: in-scattering
definition: Physical phenomenon considering scattered radiative energy from rays in any direction \(\mathit{\Omega}'\) into the direction \(\mathit{\Omega}\) of the rays considered in the radiative transfer equation (RTE).
synonyms: scattering in (into the beam under consideration)

name: interparticle electron transfer
definition: Electron transfer taking place from a photoexcited semiconductor onto another semiconductor (or insulator) in its ground state leading to vectorial (irreversible) charge transfer.

name: intrinsic emission
definition: Band-to-band recombination of electrons and holes (or exciton decay) in a semiconductor or insulator leading to luminescence.

name: intrinsic defects
definition: Imperfections connected with surface point defects (zero-dimensional), linear defects (one-dimensional), or square defects (two-dimensional) not including extrinsic chemical units in relation to the chemical formula of the solid.

name: inversion layer
definition: Layer formed when band bending places the Fermi level on the surface close to the band of the bulk minority charge carriers. This leads to a higher concentration of the minority charge carriers on the surface relative to the concentration of the majority charge carriers, an opposite situation to that in the bulk.

name: local differential absorption
definition: Absorption term in the radiative transfer equation (RTE). Mathematical expression is \[\alpha_{\lambda} (\boldsymbol{x},t) L_{\mathit{\Omega},\lambda} (\boldsymbol{x}/t)\] with \(\alpha_{\lambda} (\boldsymbol{x},t)\) the space- and time-dependent linear napierian absorption coefficient and \(L_{\mathit{\Omega},\lambda} (\boldsymbol{x},t)\) the spectral radiance arriving at position \(x\) and time \(t\) from every possible angular directions \(\mathit{\Omega}\).

name: natural photosynthesis
definition: Production of complex organic substances by higher plants, algae and photosynthesising bacteria from simple compounds (e.g., carbon dioxide and water, hydrogen sulfide, etc.) using ultraviolet, visible, or infrared radiation energy absorbed by, e.g., chlorophyll, chlorophyll-protein complexes, and natural chromoproteins.

name: out-scattering
definition: Physical process by which the incoming electromagnetic radiation is forced to deviate from a straight trajectory by non-uniformities in the medium.
synonyms: scattering out (out of the beam under consideration)

name: phase function
definition: Distribution function representing the fraction of photons scattered from any direction \(\mathit{\Omega}'\) into the direction \(\mathit{\Omega}\) under consideration in the radiative transfer equation (RTE). Dimension one.

name: photoadsorbate
definition: Entity (molecule, atom, or ion) bound to the surface of a solid (semiconductor or insulator) particle (typically to a photoadsorption centre) as the result of photoexcitation of either the solid or the entity (molecule, atom, or ion).

name: photoadsorption area number
definition: Maximum amount of substance photoadsorbed per area on the uniformly irradiated surface of an adsorbent.

name: photoadsorption capacity
definition: Maximal number of entities (molecules, atoms, or ions) per regular surface site that can be photoadsorbed at a uniformly irradiated surface of an adsorbent, \(\theta_{\rm{max}} = N_{\rm{max}}/N^{\rm{ss}}\) where \(N_{\rm{max}}\) is the maximal number of entities photoadsorbed and \(N^{\rm{ss}}\) is the number of surface sites (mainly regular surface sites, i.e., regular lattice ions or atoms; typically, \(N^{\rm{ss}}\) ca. \(\pu{E15 cm-2}\)).

name: photoadsorption centre
definition: Surface site or defect in its active state after photoexcitation capable of photoadsorbing species by a chemical interaction with the adsorbate entities (molecules, atoms, or ions).

name: photoadsorption efficiency
definition: Ratio of the maximal (typically the initial) rate of photoadsorption of entities \(\ce{B}\) (molecules, atoms, or ions) to the integrated incident (superscript 0, zero) photon flux, \(\int_{\lambda_{1}}^{\lambda_{2}} q_{\rm{p},\lambda}^{0}{\rm{d}}\lambda = q_{\rm{p}}^{0} = {\rm{d}}N_{\rm{p}}^{0}/{\rm{d}}t\), in the wavelength range \(\lambda_{1}{-}\lambda_{2}\). Both rates should be measured under otherwise identical conditions (preferably as initial rates) in order to avoid concentration and/or surface area effects.

name: photoadsorption fraction
definition: Number of entities (atoms, molecules or ions) photoadsorbed per regular surface site at a uniformly irradiated surface of an adsorbent.

name: photoadsorption photonic yield
definition: Ratio of the maximal (typically the initial) rate of photoadsorption of entities \(\ce{B}\) (molecules, atoms, or ions) on a surface to the incident (superscript 0, zero) photon flux, \(q_{\rm{p},\lambda}^{0} = {\rm{d}}N_{\rm{p},\lambda}^{0}/{\rm{d}}t\) at a given wavelength. Both rates should be measured under otherwise identical conditions (preferably as initial rates) in order to avoid concentration and/or surface area effects.

name: photoadsorption quantum yield
definition: Ratio of the number of photoadsorbed entities \(\ce{B}\) (molecules, atoms, or ions) on a surface to the number of photons of ultraviolet, visible, or infrared radiation (at a given wavelength \(\lambda\)) absorbed by the system (typically by the adsorbent) during the initial stage of irradiation.

name: photocarrier
definition: Nonequilibrium free electron or free hole generated in a solid by ultraviolet, visible, or infrared absorption and occupying energy levels in the conduction band or the valence band, respectively.

name: photocatalytic active centre
definition: Surface centre, i.e., either a surface defect or a regular surface site, at which a chemical transformation takes place after converting the centre into an active state by a photophysical process, e.g., by photoexcitation.

name: photocatalytic activity
definition: Number of entities (product) formed in a photocatalytic process (alternatively the number of reactant entities disappearing) divided by the number of photons absorbed by the photocatalyst at one single wavelength or within a defined wavelength range. For one wavelength it has the same meaning as quantum yield, whereas within a defined wavelength range it has the same meaning as quantum efficiency.

name: photocatalytic centre
definition: Surface centre, i.e., a surface defect or a regular surface site, in an active or electronically excited state at which a chemical transformation takes place.

name: photocatalytic efficiency
definition: Number of entities (product) formed (alternatively the number of reactant entities disappearing) divided by the number of ultraviolet, visible, or infrared photons incident (prior to absorption) on the system and in a wavelength range \(\lambda_{1}{-}\lambda_{2}\).

name: photocatalytic oxidation
definition: Commonly used to describe the oxidation of pollutants by the action of ultraviolet, visible, or infrared radiation and a catalyst.

name: photocorrosion
definition: Decomposition of the photocatalyst or of the electrodes as a result of a photoinduced reaction.

name: photocurrent
definition: Photogeneration and movement of charge between two electrodes in a photovoltaic cell or a photoelectrochemical cell as a result of photoprocesses induced by light absorption.

name: photodesorption
definition: Desorption induced by the absorption of ultraviolet, visible, or infrared radiation either by the adsorbate or by the adsorbent.

name: photodesorption quantum yield
definition: Number of entities evolving into the medium from a surface divided by the number of photons absorbed at a given wavelength by a solid or by an adsorbed entity treated as a surface extrinsic defect (centre).

name: photoelectrocatalysis
definition: Electrochemically assisted photocatalysis. The role of the photocatalyst is played by a photoelectrode, often a semiconductor.

name: photoelectrode
definition: Electrode capable of initiating electrochemical transformations after absorbing ultraviolet, visible, or infrared radiation.

name: photoelectrosynthesis
definition: Process by which ultraviolet, visible, or infrared radiation is absorbed by a semiconductor, electron transfer occurs at the interface between the semiconductor and a liquid and the output is chemical energy, i.e., radiant energy is stored as chemical energy.

name: photogenerated catalysis
definition: Initiation of chemical transformations through the photochemical formation of molecular species, which (once formed) are catalytically active even without the action of ultraviolet, visible, or infrared radiation.

name: photogenerated charge carrier
definition: Charge carrying entity, especially an electron or a hole, in a semiconductor, produced by the absorption of ultraviolet, visible, or infrared radiation.

name: photoinitiator
definition: Agent initiating certain chemical transformations under the action of ultraviolet, visible, or infrared radiation and consumed therewith.

name: photomineralisation
definition: Complete photodegradation of an organic compound into carbon dioxide and water, and other simple inorganic compounds (depending on the hetero-atom in the compound) upon absorption of ultraviolet, visible, or infrared radiation by the photocatalyst or by the adsorbate.

name: photonic efficiency
definition: Ratio of the rate of the photoreaction measured for a specified time interval (usually the initial conditions) to the rate of incident photons within a defined wavelength interval inside the irradiation window of the reactor.

name: photonic yield
definition: Ratio of the rate of the photoreaction measured for a specified time interval (usually the initial conditions) to the rate of incident photons of monochromatic light inside the irradiation window of the reactor.

name: photonic yield spectrum
definition: Plot of the photonic yield of a given photoprocess, measured at the same photon flux of incident (prior to absorption) light, as a function of a measure of the energy of the photons, i.e., for monochromatic irradiation.

name: photoradiation catalysis
definition: Radiation catalysis under conditions not allowing a distinction between the effect of ultraviolet, visible, or infrared and of ionising radiation as well as the case in which the ionising radiation alone generates emission of chemically active light (e.g., the 'Cherenkov' light emission).

name: photosensitised reaction
definition: Reaction initiated by photosensitisation.

name: photothermocatalysis
definition: Catalysis occurring by the combined action of electronic excitation due to absorption of ultraviolet or visible radiation and thermal energy (infrared radiation or exothermic reactions) including catalytic phenomena.

name: physical pathway
definition: Set of physical processes leading to the relaxation of the electronically excited system without chemical transformations.

name: radiant dose
definition: Radiant energy (\(Q\), SI unit is \(\pu{J}\)) or amount of photons (in \(\pu{mol}\) or the non-SI unit einstein) absorbed per area or volume by an object irradiated during a given exposure time.

name: radiation-activation
definition: Increasing of catalytic activity or alteration of selectivity of a substance after its exposure to high-energy radiation.

name: radiation adsorption
definition: The word combination may be misleading. Usually radiation is absorbed.

name: radiation catalysis
definition: Change in the rate of a chemical reaction under the action of ionising radiation in the presence of a radiation catalyst.

name: radiation catalyst
definition: Substance absorbing ionising radiation and able to produce chemical transformations of the reaction partners, repeatedly producing intermediate transformations and regenerating its chemical composition after each cycle of such interactions.

name: radiation-chemical yield
definition: Number of entities of a product formed (alternatively, the number of entities of a reactant disappearing) generated per \(\pu{100 eV}\) of energy absorbed from ionising radiation.

name: radiation desorption
definition: Desorption from solid or liquid interfaces induced by absorption of radiation by the solid or liquid adsorbent.

name: radiation-generated catalysis
definition: Initiation of chemical transformations through the formation, by absorption of high-energy radiation, of substances that are catalytically active even in the absence of the radiation.

name: radiation-induced adsorption
definition: Adsorption of a molecular entity at solid or liquid interfaces induced by absorption of high-energy radiation by the solid or the liquid adsorbent.

name: radiation sensitisation
definition: Chemical change or physical process occurring in one entity (e.g., biological molecules, cells, and living organisms) as a result of initial absorption of high-energy radiation by the medium in the presence of another entity called the radiation sensitiser.

name: radiation sensitiser
definition: Chemical substance that increases the radiation sensitivity of, in particular, biological molecules, cells and biological organisms.

name: radiation-stimulated diffusion
definition: Increase of diffusion of an adsorbate under the action of ionising radiation absorbed by either the adsorbent and/or the adsorbate.

name: radiation thermal catalysis
definition: Radiation catalysis under the action of large radiation fluxes that simultaneously heat the system as a consequence of absorption of energy from radiationless deactivation.

name: radiative transfer equation
definition: When a photon beam of radiance \(L_{\lambda}\) and angular distribution \(\mathit{\Omega}\) passes along a single direction of propagation through a medium, which is totally absorbing and/or scattering, i.e., the processes occurring are described by the following equation: \[\begin{array} \\ \frac{{\rm{d}}L_{\Omega,\lambda}(\boldsymbol{x},t)}{{\rm{d}}s} + \underbrace{\alpha_{\lambda}(\boldsymbol{x},t) L_{\mathit{\Omega},\lambda}(\boldsymbol{x},t)}_{\rm{adsorption}} + \underbrace{\sigma_{\lambda}(\boldsymbol{x},t) L_{\mathit{\Omega},\lambda}(\boldsymbol{x},t)}_{\rm{out\mbox{-}scattering}} = \\ \underbrace{j_{\lambda}(\boldsymbol{x},t)}_{\rm{emission}} + \underbrace{\frac{\sigma_{\lambda}(\boldsymbol{x},t)}{4\pi}B_{\lambda}(\mathit{\Omega}' \to \mathit{\Omega}) L_{\mathit{\Omega},\lambda}(\boldsymbol{x},t){\rm{d}}\mathit{\Omega}'}_{\rm{in\mbox{-}scattering}} \end{array}\] where \(\frac{{\rm{d}}L_{\Omega,\lambda}(\boldsymbol{x},t)}{{\rm{d}}s}\) is the directional derivative along the direction \(s\) at a point \(\boldsymbol{x}\) in the reaction space of the incident radiance, \(\alpha_{\lambda}(\boldsymbol{x},t)\) is the space- and time-dependent spectral linear napierian absorption coefficient, \(\sigma_{\lambda}(\boldsymbol{x},t)\) is the space- and time-dependent spectral linear napierian scattering coefficient, \(j_{\lambda}(\boldsymbol{x},t)\) represents the spontaneous and/or induced emission, and \(B_{\lambda}\) is the phase function. All quantities are a function of time. The RTE is written for the direction \(s\).

name: rate of generation
definition: Number of carriers (or electron-hole pairs, or excitons) produced per time interval and per volume of a solid photocatalyst particle due to the absorption of light.

name: rate of surface recombination
definition: Decay of carriers at the surface of a solid or interface between different phases, e.g., at the crystal surface.

name: recombination of photocarriers
definition: Two-step transition of an electron from the conduction band to a defect centre and then further to the valence band, or from the defect centre to the valence band (first step) and a subsequent transition of the conduction band electron to the defect centre (second step).

name: recombination centre
definition: Defect in semiconductors and insulators capable of sequential capture of free charge carriers of both signs with high efficiency.

name: regular surface
definition: Perfect surface of a solid without heterogeneity or defect.

name: regular surface site
definition: Zero-dimension site (atom, ion, or interstitial position) at a regular surface.

name: relative photonic efficiency
definition: Ratio of the photonic efficiency (\(\xi\)) of a chemical process to the corresponding photonic efficiency of a standard process under otherwise identical conditions in the same reactor configuration and operation.

name: scattering albedo
definition: Efficiency of scattering, i.e., ratio of scattering coefficient, \(\sigma(\lambda_{\rm{i}})\), to the total attenuance coefficient, \(\beta(\lambda_{\rm{i}})\), at a particular wavelength \(\lambda_{\rm{i}}\).

name: shallow trap
definition: Energy level (of trapped carrier) within the bandgap energy, near the bottom of the conduction band (electron shallow trap) and near the top of the valence band (hole shallow band) at an energy such that \(E_{\rm{trap}} \approx kT\), with \(k\) the Boltzmann constant and \(T\) the thermodynamic temperature.

name: Solonitsyn effect
definition: Adsorption (or reaction) after preliminary irradiation of a photocatalyst in vacuum (or in the absence of reagent).

name: sonophotocatalytic reactor
definition: Reactor in which a hybrid technique combining 'sonochemical' and photocatalytic reactions is used.

name: space charge region
definition: Region formed within a semiconductor in contact with another phase in which there is a band bending that can be upward or downward.

name: specific photoadsorption number
definition: Maximum number of entities (molecules, atoms or radicals) adsorbed as a result of irradiation divided by the surface area and by the mass of adsorbent.

name: specific absorption coefficient
definition: Linear napierian, \(\alpha_{\lambda}^{\ast}\), or linear decadic, \(a_{\lambda}^{\ast}\), absorption coefficient divided by the mass concentration, \(\rho\).
synonyms: specific linear Napierian spectral absorption coefficient|specific linear decadic spectral absorption coefficient|specific spectral absorption coefficient

name: specific napierian attenuance coefficient
definition: Attenuance (napierian), \(D_{\rm{e}}\), divided by the absorption pathlength, \(l\), and the mass concentration, \(\rho\).
synonyms: specific Napierian extinction coefficient|specific Napierian spectral extinction coefficient|specific spectral Napierian attenuance coefficient

name: specific napierian scattering coefficient
definition: Fraction of attenuance (napierian) not due to absorbance, divided by the pathlength, \(l\), within the scattering medium and the mass concentration, \(\rho\).

name: spectral photon irradiance
definition: Derivative of photon irradiance, \(E_{\rm{p}}\), with respect to wavelength, \(\lambda\).

name: spectral photonic yield
definition: Dependence of the photonic yield on the photon energy (wavelength, frequency, or wavenumber) of the radiation for a given photoreaction obtained at a certain incident (prior to absorption) photon irradiance in a given spectral range.

name: spectral quantum yield
definition: Dependence of the quantum yield on the photon energy (wavelength, frequency or wavenumber) of the radiation absorbed by the reactant for a given photoreaction.

name: surface-active site
definition: Surface regular or defect site that can initiate the chemical transformation of reagents.

name: surface recombination
definition: Recombination of charge carriers at a solid surface or at an interface between different phases.

name: thermal bleaching
definition: Loss of absorption by the colour centres because of heating of the solid semiconductor or insulator.

name: thermophotocatalysis
definition: A photocatalytic phenomenon occurring when the system is also heated by the ultraviolet, visible, or infrared radiation.

name: turnover number
definition: Number of times, \(n\), that the overall reaction (the photochemical transformation) goes through a photocatalytic cycle.

name: V centres
definition: Trapped holes in semiconductors.

name: volatile organic chemical/compounds
definition: Term commonly used to designate organic gas-phase pollutants frequently degraded by photocatalytic procedures.

name: absorbance assay
definition: Assay in which response is determined by the detection of light absorption by an assay component.

name: active
definition: Sample that produces a response or signal above a defined threshold at a tested concentration in a single assay or screen.

name: activity distribution
definition: Graphical representation of the number of samples present in each activity range.

name: allosteric site
definition: Binding site on a protein, distinct from the site recognized by an endogenous agonist (i.e., the orthosteric site) in the case of a receptor, or substrate in the case of an enzyme, that when occupied by a ligand effects a conformational change in the protein, thus altering its signaling, catalytic properties, or its capability to interact with other macromolecules.

name: artifact
definition: Observation, effect, or result that is inaccurate because it is produced by the methodology used in scientific investigation or by experimental error.

name: assay validation
definition: Experiments conducted to verify that the output measurements of the assay are consistently reflective of the activity against the target.

name: automated device
definition: Device that performs one or more functions without human intervention by means of direct control or by programmed operations.

name: binding assay
definition: Assay in which the specific physical association or interaction between two molecules (e.g., ligand–receptor, antibody–antigen, protein–protein, ligand–transport protein) is measured.

name: binding isotherm
definition: Graphical representation of the relationship between the amount of ligand that is specifically bound to a receptor per mass of binding material and the amount of free ligand.

name: cell-based assay
definition: Assay in which the response of live cells to a test sample is measured.

name: cell membrane preparation
definition: Preparation from tissue or cells, in which the membranous elements, generally the cell membrane, are enriched in relation to other cellular constituents.

name: cell mortality
definition: Ratio of counted dead cells to the total number of observed cells.

name: cell viability
definition: Ratio of counted live cells to the total number of observed cells.

name: channel blocker
definition: Compound that reduces or eliminates the conductance of an ion channel by impeding the movement of ions through that channel.

name: channel opener
definition: Compound that increases the conductance of an ion channel by a mechanism other than alteration of membrane potential or activation of the cognate receptor.

name: chemotaxis assay
definition: Cell-based assay in which the rate and/or direction of cell migration is measured.

name: combinatorial library
definition: Set of compounds prepared by combinatorial chemistry. It may consist of a collection of pools, or sublibraries. Its composition may be described by the chemset notation.

name: compound collection
definition: Set of chemicals that has been assembled and annotated for easy storage and retrieval and that is available for screening.

name: concentration–response relationship
definition: Association between compound concentration and the resultant magnitude of the continuously graded change produced, in an assay.

name: confirmed hit
definition: Sample that produces activity above the hit threshold in an assay and whose structural identity has been confirmed.

name: counter-screen
definition: Screen in which test samples are assessed against a target for unwanted activity.

name: cytotoxicity assay
definition: Cell-based assay in which damage to cell structure or function caused by a test sample is determined.

name: efficacy
definition: Extent to which a compound activates a receptor to produce a response in an assay under saturating conditions.

name: electrochemiluminescence assay
definition: Assay in which light emitted by electrogenerated luminescence is detected and used to quantify a label, e.g., ruthenium(II) tris-(bipyridine), on one of the two assay binding components.

name: end-point assay
definition: Kinetic assay run for a set constant incubation time. Typically, at the end of the set incubation time, a reagent that stops the reaction is added to allow postponed measurement of the signal.

name: epitope mapping
definition: Identification and localization of the specific regions of protein molecules that are recognized by the immune system.

name: equilibrium assay
definition: Assay in which there is sufficient incubation time for the plateau phase of the signal to be reached and equilibrium has been established between the reactants.

name: equilibrium association constant
definition: Ratio, at equilibrium, of \([\ce{AB}]/[\ce{A}][\ce{B}]\) for the reversible binding interaction of \(\ce{A}\) and \(\ce{B}\) to yield the complex \(\ce{AB}\).

name: equilibrium dissociation constant
definition: Ratio, at equilibrium, of \([\ce{A}][\ce{B}]/[\ce{AB}]\), for the reversible binding interaction of \(\ce{A}\) and \(\ce{B}\) to yield the complex \(\ce{AB}\).

name: flow cytometry assay
definition: Cell-based assay in which the response is dependent on the detection of the phenotype of cells as determined through the light-scattering properties of each cell, and, typically, the fluorescence intensity of a relevant probe.

name: fluorescence correlation assay
definition: Assay in which fluctuations in fluorescence intensity are detected and used to characterize a species that is labeled with a fluorescent probe.

name: fluorescence polarisation
definition: Dimensionless value determined from the fluorescence intensities (\(I\)) measured parallel (\(I_{\Vert}\)) and perpendicular (\(I_{\perp}\)) to the excitation plane: \[p = \frac{I_{\Vert} - I_{\perp}}{I_{\Vert} + I_{\perp}}\]

name: fluorescence polarisation assay
definition: Assay in which the association between an intrinsically fluorescent ligand, or a ligand linked to a fluorescent probe, and a larger macromolecule is detected.

name: fluorescence resonance energy transfer assay
definition: Assay based on the nonradiative energy transfer that occurs when the emission spectrum of a fluorescent donor molecule overlaps with the absorption spectrum of an energy acceptor molecule.

name: functional assay
definition: Assay in which the biological or physiological activity of the target is measured.

name: heterogeneous assay
definition: Assay in which the response is detected only after the physical separation by methods such as filtration or centrifugation of one or more assay components.

name: heterogeneous binding assay
definition: Assay in which one binding component is immobilized to a surface (e.g., cellular membrane, glass, gold, bead, or biopolymer layer) while its binding partner is freely diffusible.

name: high-content screening assay
definition: A cell-based assay that produces multiple biological readouts.

name: high-performance liquid chromatography assay
definition: Assay in which response is determined after the physical separation of assay components using high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) with concurrent detection, usually by monitoring absorbance at an appropriate wavelength.

name: high throughput
definition: Relative term, applied to the generation of a large number of results in a short timeframe (e.g., \(\pu{E5}\) in a week or a month).

name: hit rate
definition: Proportion of hits from a screen that displays confirmed activity beyond a minimum defined level, the hit threshold. It is expressed as a percentage of the number of samples screened.

name: hit threshold
definition: Minimum activity that defines actives in a primary screen.

name: homogeneous assay
definition: Assay in which all reagents and reactants are of a uniform phase (typically, liquid phase) and assay response is detected without the need for physical separation of assay components.

name: homogeneous binding assay
definition: Single-phase system used to qualitatively discriminate between specific and nonspecific interactions or quantitatively determine the concentration of a component part of a mixture.

name: image-based assay
definition: Assay in which image analysis algorithms that determine the compartmentalization of fluorescent probes give topological as well as quantitative information.

name: immobilised metal ion affinity-based fluorescence polarisation assay
definition: Assay in which the interaction between nanoparticles coated with triply charged metal ions and phosphate groups on a substrate that carries a fluorescent tag is detected.

name: inactive
definition: Sample that, at the tested concentration, does not produce a response above the hit threshold in an assay.

name: inverse agonist
definition: Ligand that decreases signaling through a receptor below the level of constitutive activity.

name: kinetic assay
definition: Assay in which the time dependence of the signal intensity is measured. Signal values are typically acquired at several time intervals in order to calculate kinetic parameters.

name: label-free assay
definition: Assay in which there is no requirement to modify one of the interacting components in order to facilitate signal detection.

name: label-free detection
definition: Direct detection of compound activity on a target without the requirement for a labeled reagent.

name: lead identification
definition: Process that is targeted toward the generation of at least one compound series that meets the requirements for progression to lead optimization.

name: lead optimisation
definition: Process in which the drug-like properties of an initial lead or lead series are improved.

name: library
definition: Collection of samples (e.g., chemical compounds, natural products, over-expression library of a microbe) available for screening. Set of compounds produced through combinatorial chemistry or other means that expands around a single core structure.

name: ligand-activated channel
definition: Any ion channel that is gated (i.e., opened or closed) by a ligand.

name: liquid handler
definition: Automated device that accurately and precisely delivers programmed, predefined quantities of liquid to a microplate.

name: luminescence assay
definition: Assay in which response is measured by the detection of light of a nonradiative origin, such as bioluminescence or chemiluminescence.

name: microplate
definition: Any of a number of plates containing a series of wells which may be used for storage or to perform individual assays.

name: microplate standards
definition: Defined footprint, height, flanges, and well positions for 96-, 384-, and 1536-well microplates.

name: miniaturisation
definition: Experimental design aimed at decreasing the reaction volume of an assay and consequently the amount and cost of reagents.

name: module
definition: Individual automated device within a fully automated assay system that usually performs a complete single assay step or procedure.

name: molecular imprinted polymers
definition: Synthetic polymers in which well-defined volume cavities (imprints) created by template molecules mimic a biomolecular specific ligand–receptor interaction.

name: multiplex assay
definition: Assay in which the activity of a single sample against more than one target is measured in a single test.

name: natural product
definition: Complex mixture derived from natural (biological) sources used in screening as a resource for identification of lead compounds. Pure compound of natural (biological) origin (whether obtained by purification of natural mixtures or by laboratory synthesis), as opposed to compounds originating from synthetic chemistry.Note: Typical origins include extracts from microbes and higher organisms from terrestrial or marine environments.

name: negative assay control
definition: Experimental conditions designed to produce the signal reflective of the absence of the process under investigation.

name: noncompetitive binding assay
definition: Assay in which the interaction of a ligand with a receptor is measured without a requirement for added competing agents. It can be homogeneous or heterogeneous.

name: nuclease assay
definition: Method used to determine the presence or quantify the amount of specific target nucleotide sequences.

name: off-rate
definition: Rate of dissociation of the enzyme-substrate (\(\ce{ES}\)) complex to enzyme (\(\ce{E}\)) and substrate (\(\ce{S}\)) or of ligand–receptor (\(\ce{LR}\)) to receptor (\(\ce{R}\)) and ligand (\(\ce{L}\)).

name: on-rate
definition: Rate of formation of the enzyme-substrate (\(\ce{ES}\)) or ligand–receptor (\(\ce{LR}\)) complex.

name: orthosteric site
definition: Binding site recognized by the endogenous agonist of a receptor.

name: partial agonist
definition: Agonist that is unable to induce a maximal receptor response in a given biological assay, regardless of the amount applied.

name: pipettor
definition: Device that aspirates and dispenses liquid (\(\pu{nL}\) to \(\pu{mL}\) range) for the purposes of transferring from a source to destination.

name: plate format
definition: Number and configuration of wells on a microplate.

name: plate gripper
definition: Handling device that positions microplates on a workstation.

name: plate map
definition: Layout of samples and controls configured on a plate during an assay.

name: plate reader
