definition: Automated device that uses optical and/or computer vision techniques to detect biological, chemical, or physical events in samples stored in microplates.

name: plate stacker
definition: Automated device that loads, unloads, and restacks microplates.

name: plate washer
definition: Automated device used to wash the wells of microplates.

name: positive assay control
definition: Experimental conditions designed to produce the signal reflective of maximum biological effect in an assay.

name: potency
definition: Dose of drug required to produce a specific effect of given intensity as compared to a standard reference.

name: primary screen
definition: Initial screen applied to assess the activity of a collection of compounds and identify hits or actives against a biological target of interest.

name: radioligand
definition: Ligand into which a radioisotope has been incorporated as a label.

name: robot
definition: Automated device that performs tasks (i.e., screen functions) that would normally be performed by a human.

name: scheduling software
definition: Computer program used to organize the chronological sequence of experimental methods to be followed to execute an automated high-throughput screening campaign.

name: scintillation proximity assay
definition: Homogeneous assay in which beads incorporated with scintillant emit light in the presence of radiolabeled molecules within the proximity of the bead’s scintillant detection.

name: screen
definition: Execution, analysis, and interpretation of a large number of assays to evaluate the activity of a collection of samples against a target.

name: screen validation
definition: Assay conditions, as determined by assay validation, are performed in the chosen plate format with an acceptable signal to background ratio as described by the Z′ factor.

name: secondary screen
definition: Screen applied to independently confirm actives from the primary screen.

name: selectivity assay
definition: Assay used to determine the relative potency of active or lead compounds toward an alternative target.

name: stably transfected cells
definition: Eukaryotic cells into which recombinant DNA has been introduced and incorporated into the genome, so that the cells replicate the new DNA in a stable fashion.

name: standard error of the mean
definition: Sample standard deviation divided by the square root of the sample size.

name: sublibrary
definition: Portion of a library that is grouped or selected based on similarity of structure or biological effect.

name: surface plasmon resonance assay
definition: Assay in which the binding of a ligand to a target immobilized on the gold surface of a chip is detected by changes in the angle of the light reflected from the surface.

name: targeted library
definition: Library designed, on the basis of preexisting information, to generate enhanced activity or hit rate against a particular biological target or target class.

name: total internal reflection fluorescence
definition: Spectroscopic technique that discriminates between labeled molecules in the homogeneous phase and those interacting with binding partners immobilized at a surface.

name: transiently transfected cells
definition: Eukaryotic cells into which recombinant DNA has been introduced and expressed by cellular transcription, but without incorporation into the stable genome.

name: ultra-high throughput
definition: Relative term, currently applied to the screening of \(\pu{E5}\) test samples in a \(\pu{24\!\mbox{-}h}\) period.

name: voltage-activated channel
definition: Ion channel that is specifically activated, or gated, by the surrounding potential difference across the cell membrane near the channel (or near the cell, neuron, or synapse).

name: workstation
definition: Programmable device used to automate a single operation (such as liquid handling) on a microplate supplied to the device by a robot (automated stacker system or a robotic manipulator).

name: Z factor
definition: Dimensionless statistical parameter that provides a practical assessment of assay performance in the presence of test compounds. \[Z = 1 - 3(\sigma_{\rm{s}} + \sigma_{\rm{c}})/\vert\mu_{\rm{s}} - \mu_{\rm{c}}\vert\] where \(\mu_{\rm{s}}\) denotes the mean of the library sample signal, \(\mu_{\rm{c}}\) the mean of the control signal and \(\sigma_{\rm{s}}\), \(\sigma_{\rm{c}}\) the corresponding standard deviations. \(1 \gt Z \ge 0.5\) generally categorizes an excellent assay.

name: Z′ factor
definition: Dimensionless statistical parameter used extensively in biomolecular screening, and a characteristic of an assay without the intervention of test compounds. It provides a practical index of the quality and reliability of the assay, and can be used as a guide to assay development and optimization. \[Z' = 1 - 3(\sigma_{\rm{c^{+}}} + \sigma_{\rm{c^{-}}})/(\vert\mu_{\rm{c^{+}}} - \mu_{\rm{c^{-}}}\vert)\] where \(\sigma_{\rm{c^{+}}}\) and \(\sigma_{\rm{c^{-}}}\) are the standard deviations of the high and low controls and \(\mu_{\rm{c^{+}}}\) and \(\mu_{\rm{c^{-}}}\) are the means of the high and low controls, respectively. A graphical illustration of the parameters used in the calculation of \(Z'\) is provided below.

name: two-phase model
definition: Model based on the assumption that the polymer sample consists only of domains of a crystalline phase and of an amorphous phase.

name: axial advancement per constitutional repeating unit
definition: Projected length of a constitutional repeating unit (CRU) on the chain axis.

name: directional chain
definition: Polymer chain that may be oriented in two distinguishable, opposite directions along the chain axis.

name: directional stem
definition: Stem of a directional chain.

name: helix pitch
definition: Distance between successive helical windings projected on the chain axis.

name: ideal crystalline chain conformation
definition: Minimum energy conformation of an isolated polymer chain constructed according to the equivalence postulate and approximating the conformation found in a crystalline phase.

name: left-handed helix
definition: Helix in which the continuous helical line, approximating the sequence of bonds along the polymer main chain, winds clockwise moving towards the observer, i.e., seen from the positive axis direction (see the figures in chain identity period).

name: multiple helix
definition: Helical arrangement comprising two or more intertwined helical chains sharing the same axis.

name: right-handed helix
definition: Helix in which the continuous helical line, approximating the sequence of bonds along the polymer main chain, winds anticlockwise moving towards the observer, i.e., seen from the positive axis direction (see the figures in chain identity period).

name: rod group
definition: Symmetry group of a three-dimensional array of atoms, regularly repeating along one direction.

name: rotation per helix residue
definition: Angle of rotation about the chain axis per helix residue.

name: translational chain repeating unit
definition: Smallest structural unit of a polymer chain that is repeated by translation in the crystal lattice along the chain axis.

name: anticlined stems
definition: Stems in a crystal having opposite side-group orientations with respect to the chain axis (see (a) in figure).(a) Pairs of anticlined stems and (b) pairs of isoclined stems of regioregular poly(3-butylthiophene), i.e., poly(3-n-butylthiophene-2,5-diyl). Since regioregular poly(3-n-butylthiophene-2,5-diyl) is also a directional chain, (a) is an example of antidirectional packing of two chains, while (b) is an example of isodirectional packing.

name: antidirectional packing
definition: In a parallel-chain crystal, the crystalline packing of directional stems with opposite chain axis orientations.

name: crystal polymorph
definition: One of the different crystalline phases in which a given substance is able to crystallize.

name: frustration
definition: Feature of crystalline packing characterized by different crystalline arrangements of chain stems at two (or more) sites that would be expected to be equivalent.

name: isochiral stem packing
definition: Crystalline packing of stems having the same helicity.

name: isoclined stems
definition: Stems in a crystal having the same side-group orientation with respect to the chain axis (see figure (b) in anticlined stems).

name: isodirectional packing
definition: In a parallel-chain crystal, the crystalline packing of directional stems with the same chain axis orientation.

name: packing of chain stems
definition: Spatial arrangement of polymer chain stems in a polymer crystal.

name: polymorphic polymer crystal
definition: Polymer crystal formed by domains of different crystal polymorphs of the same polymer.

name: racemic packing
definition: Packing in a polymer crystal in which stems of opposite helicity coexist in equal numbers.

name: symmetry breaking
definition: Vanishing, in a specific crystal polymorph, of selected symmetry elements present in other crystal polymorphs, or in selected minimum energy conformations of isolated molecules of a given substance.

name: orientational disorder
definition: Structural disorder at given crystallographic positions, resulting from the statistical coexistence within crystals of directional stems with opposite orientations.

name: paracrystal
definition: Crystal model characterized by lattice distortions and hence by limited order along given lattice directions.

name: paracrystalline disorder of the first kind
definition: Structural disorder in a paracrystal, resulting from uncorrelated displacements of the atoms around their average positions.

name: paracrystalline disorder of the second kind
definition: Structural disorder in a paracrystal, resulting from permanent atomic displacements from the ordered crystallographic positions.

name: paracrystalline distortion factor
definition: Ratio of the statistical fluctuation \(\Delta a_{ik}\) of a lattice vector \(a_{i}\) along the direction \(a_{k}\) \[g_{ik} = \frac{\Delta a_{ik}}{a_{k}}\]

name: crystalline polymer-inclusion complex
definition: Crystal comprising a polymer guest within a low-molar-mass host.

name: crystalline-polymer molecular complex
definition: Crystalline molecular complex between different polymers.

name: isomorphous polymer co-crystal
definition: Crystal consisting of two or more structurally different polymers, resulting in macromolecular isomorphism.

name: copolymer isomorphism
definition: Macromolecular isomorphism involving copolymers.

name: homopolymer isomorphism
definition: Macromolecular isomorphism involving two homopolymers with different constitutional repeating units.

name: nanoporous polymer crystal
definition: Polymer crystal presenting empty volume elements that can host low-molar-mass guest species.

name: polymer clathrate
definition: Polymer co-crystal in which low-molar-mass guest species are hosted in molecular-sized cages or cavities containing more than one guest molecule.

name: polymer co-crystal
definition: Crystal structure in which at least two substances coexist, one of which is a polymer.
synonyms: polymer mixed crystal|polymer-based crystalline molecular complex

name: irregular adjacent re-entry model
definition: Adjacent re-entry model in which the fold period can vary.

name: regular adjacent re-entry model
definition: Idealized adjacent re-entry model in which the fold periods are assumed to have all the same length.

name: chain-extended crystal
definition: Folded-chain crystal in which each macromolecule makes one, or, at most, a few folds.

name: fold period
definition: Thickness of a lamellar parallel-chain crystal in the direction of its stems.

name: non-parallel-chain crystal
definition: Polymer crystal in which the stems are aligned along two or more different crystallographic directions.

name: solidification model
definition: Model of crystalline polymer formed by lamellar crystallization from the melt, in which some stems of a macromolecule belong to one crystal, whilst other stems of the same macromolecule are in different crystals.

name: amorphous domain
definition: Phase domain consisting of matter in the amorphous state.

name: bundle crystal
definition: Crystal in which the chains predominantly extend from the crystal surface, resulting in a fringed-micelle model morphology.

name: hedrite
definition: Polyhedral aggregate of lamellar crystals resulting in a morphology that resembles that of a polymer single crystal, at least from one viewing direction.

name: lamellar crystal sector
definition: Portion of a lamellar crystal, often bounded by a well-defined crystal face.

name: long period
definition: Average periodicity (repeating distance) of the layers of lamellar crystals in a stacked assembly.

name: polycrystalline polymer
definition: Crystalline polymer in which a large number of polymer crystallites coexist.

name: polymer fibre
definition: Uniaxially oriented polymer filament with macroscopic cylindrical symmetry, in which the average direction of the polymer chain axis coincides with the cylindrical symmetry axis.

name: polymer fibril
definition: Small diameter polymer fiber consisting of a small number of polymer chains.

name: polymer single crystal
definition: Individually distinct polymer crystal whose lattice, at crystallization, is characterized by a single orientation.

name: row structure
definition: Polycrystalline polymer morphology resulting from nucleation of polymer lamellar crystals by multiple fibrillar structures or by macroscopic linear objects such as fibers.

name: dominant lamellae
definition: Lamellar crystals radiating from the center of the spherulite which, by splaying, constitute the initial skeleton of the spherulite.

name: subsidiary lamellae
definition: Lamellar crystals nucleated either epitaxially or incoherently on dominant lamellae.

name: transcrystalline layer
definition: Polycrystalline layer nucleated and shaped by a pre-existing planar surface within or in contact with a polymer melt.

name: twinned polymer crystal
definition: Polymer crystal in which two or more single crystalline domains of the same crystal polymorph, with different lattice orientations, coexist.

name: cellulation
definition: Division of the growth front of individual or groups of dominant lamellae into divergent 'cells', with the impurities and the less crystallizable molecules segregated between the cells and at the spherulite boundaries.

name: confined-spaces crystallisation
definition: Polymer crystallization occurring inside elongated cavities, spheres, galleries, or layers formed by a host material different from the polymer.

name: degree of supercooling
definition: Temperature difference between the equilibrium melting temperature and the temperature of a supercooled melt.

name: heteroepitaxy
definition: Epitaxy between crystals of different substances.

name: homoepitaxy
definition: Epitaxy between crystals of the same substance.

name: isothermal crystallisation
definition: Crystallization taking place at constant temperature.

name: non-isothermal crystallisation
definition: Crystallization taking place under varying temperature conditions.

name: primary nucleus
definition: The smallest crystalline entity, the further growth of which is thermodynamically favored.

name: secondary nucleation
definition: Nucleation of a new molecular layer on a growing crystal face.Note: Secondary nucleation refers to the further growth of an already-existing crystal.

name: self-nucleation
definition: Heterogeneous nucleation by crystals of the same polymer.

name: polymer co-crystallisation
definition: Crystallization, within the same crystal, of a polymer and at least one other component.

name: supercooled melt
definition: Metastable melt of a crystallizable polymer at temperatures below its equilibrium melting temperature \(T^{\circ}_{\rm{m}}\).

name: supercooling
definition: The process of cooling a melt to a temperature below its equilibrium melting point, without crystallization occurring.

name: polymer particle
definition: Particle of polymer of any shape.

name: polymer bead
definition: Sphere of polymer, usually with a diameter in the range from one-tenth to a few millimeters.

name: polymer microparticle
definition: Particle of polymer of any shape with an equivalent diameter from approximately \(\pu{0.1 \upmu m}\) to \(\pu{100 \upmu m}\).

name: polymer microsphere
definition: Polymer microparticle of spherical shape.

name: polymer nanoparticle
definition: Particle of polymer of any shape and an equivalent diameter from approximately \(\pu{1 nm}\) to \(\pu{100 nm}\).

name: polymer nanosphere
definition: Polymer nanoparticle of spherical shape.

name: polymer gel particle
definition: Particle of gel in which the network component is a polymer.

name: gel microparticle
definition: Particle of gel of any shape with an equivalent diameter of approximately \(\pu{0.1 \upmu m}\) to \(\pu{100 \upmu m}\).

name: gel nanoparticle
definition: Particle of gel particle of any shape and an equivalent diameter of approximately \(\pu{1 nm}\) to \(\pu{100 nm}\).

name: polymer network particle
definition: Particle having any shape and composed of a polymer network and possibly species of finite molar mass.

name: artificial latex
definition: Latex obtained by emulsification of a polymer or oligomer solution in a liquid or by emulsification of a liquid polymer or liquid oligomer in a liquid.

name: hybrid latex
definition: Latex comprising a polymer of relatively high molar mass and an oligomer or an alkyd resin, in which there is usually chemical bonding between the two components, formed either during latex synthesis or subsequently after formation of a film from the latex. Latex comprising multicomponent particles that contain both organic and inorganic material phases.

name: inverse latex
definition: Nonaqueous latex in which the dispersed phase comprises hydrophilic polymer usually swollen with water.

name: latex particle
definition: Polymer particle that is present in a latex.

name: natural latex
definition: Latex, the dispersed phase of which is obtained from various plants.

name: synthetic latex
definition: Latex obtained as a product of an emulsion, mini-emulsion, micro-emulsion, or dispersion polymerization.

name: equivalent particle diameter
definition: Diameter of a hypothetical spherical particle of the same composition that, using a given particle-size determination method, would give the same diameter as a substance composed of spherical or nonspherical particles at the same concentration.

name: number-average particle diameter
definition: Calculated using the following equation: \[\left\langle d_{\rm{N}} \right\rangle = \bar d_{\rm{N}} = \frac{\Sigma N_{i} d_{i}}{\Sigma N_{i}}\]

name: surface-average particle diameter
definition: Calculated using the following equation: \[\left\langle {d_{\rm{s}}} \right\rangle = \bar d_{\rm{s}} = \frac{\Sigma {N_{i}} {d_{i}^{3}}}{\Sigma {N_{i}} {d_{i}^{2}}}\]

name: mass-average particle diameter
definition: Calculated using the following equation: \[\left\langle d_{\rm{m}} \right\rangle = \bar d_{\rm{m}} = \frac{\Sigma {N_{i}} {d_{i}^{4}}}{\Sigma {N_{i}} {d_{i}^{3}}}\]

name: z-average particle diameter
definition: Calculated using the following equation: \[\left\langle d_{\rm{z}} \right\rangle = \bar d_{\rm{z}} = \frac{\Sigma N_{i} d_{i}^{5}}{\Sigma N_{i}d_{i}^{4}}\]

name: volume-average particle diameter
definition: Calculated using the following equation: \[\left\langle d_{\rm{v}} \right\rangle = \bar d_{\rm{v}} = \left(\frac{\Sigma N_{i} d_{i}^{3}}{\Sigma N_{i}}\right)^{1/3}\]

name: particle-diameter dispersity
definition: Calculated using the following equation: \[Ɖ_{\rm{d}} = \left\langle d_{\rm{m}} \right\rangle /\!\left\langle d_{\rm{N}} \right\rangle = \bar d_{\rm{m}}/\bar d_{\rm{N}} = \frac{\Sigma N_{i}\Sigma N_{i} d_{i}^{4}}{\Sigma N_{i} d_{i} \Sigma N_{i} d_{i}^{3}}\]

name: homogeneous particle
definition: Particle that is spatially uniform with respect to chemical composition of the constituent polymer(s).

name: multicomponent particle
definition: Inhomogeneous particle consisting of two or more immiscible components.Examples of two-phase particle morphology.

name: core-shell particle
definition: Polymer particle comprising at least two phase domains, one of which (the core) lies within the other(s) that form the polymeric outer layer(s) (the shell(s)).

name: inverted core-shell particle
definition: Core-shell particle in which polymer synthesized in the second stage is located in the core of the particle and polymer constituting the initial seed is located in the shell.

name: multilayered particle
definition: Multicomponent particle made of at least two different polymers, with an inner core of one polymer and with at least two layers of different polymers.

name: occluded particle
definition: Multicomponent particle in which one polymer forms more than one phase domain within a matrix of another polymer.

name: partially engulfed particle
definition: Multicomponent particle in which one or more polymer(s) cover(s) most, but not all, of the particle surface.

name: macroporous particle
definition: Particle containing pores of diameters exceeding about \(\pu{50 nm}\).

name: mesoporous particle
definition: Particle containing pores of diameters between approximately \(\pu{2 \upmu m}\) and \(\pu{50 \upmu m}\).

name: microporous particle
definition: Particle containing pores of diameters not exceeding \(\pu{2 nm}\).

name: dispersed phase
definition: Phase constituted of particles of any size and of any nature dispersed in a continuous phase of a different composition.

name: continuous phase
definition: Phase not interrupted in space

name: dispersion medium
definition: Matrix for the dispersed phase.

name: nonaqueous dispersion
definition: Dispersion in which the continuous phase is nonaqueous.

name: polymer dispersion
definition: Dispersion in which the dispersed phase consists of a polymer.

name: colloid stabiliser
definition: Compound increasing stability of a colloid.

name: polymer colloid
definition: Colloidal dispersion in which at least one of the phases is a polymer, either organic, or inorganic or some combination of the two.

name: polymer emulsion
definition: Emulsion in which the dispersed phase is a liquid polymer or a polymer solution.

name: macro-emulsion
definition: Emulsion in which the particles of the dispersed phase have diameters from approximately \(\pu{1 \upmu m}\) to \(\pu{100 \upmu m}\).

name: mini-emulsion
definition: Emulsion in which the particles of the dispersed phase have diameters in the range from approximately \(\pu{50 nm}\) to \(\pu{1 \upmu m}\).

name: micro-emulsion
definition: Dispersion made of water, oil, and surfactant(s) that is an isotropic and thermodynamically stable system with dispersed domain diameter varying approximately from \(\pu{1 nm}\) to \(\pu{100 nm}\), usually \(\pu{10 nm}\) to \(\pu{50 nm}\).

name: hemi-micelle
definition: Type of micelle that exists in relatively small numbers below the critical micelle concentration.

name: ad-micelle
definition: Surfactant bilayer formed on a charged adsorbing surface.

name: micellar aggregation number
definition: Number of molecules constituting a micelle.

name: micellar charge
definition: Combined charge of the surfactant ions and counterions tightly bound to a micelle.

name: micellar relative molar mass
definition: Mass of a mole of micelles divided by the molar mass constant. The relative molar mass of micelles (mic) is thus \(M_{\rm{r,mic}} = M_{\rm{mic}}/M_{\rm{u}}\).

name: particle number concentration
definition: Number of particles per volume of suspending medium.

name: solids content
definition: Mass fraction of nonvolatile material in a polymer dispersion.

name: polymer content
definition: Mass fraction of polymer in a polymer dispersion.

name: dispersed-phase concentration
definition: Amount concentration of a species within the dispersed phase.
synonyms: dispersed-phase amount concentration|particle-phase amount concentration|particle-phase concentration

name: continuous-phase concentration
definition: Concentration of species within the continuous phase of a dispersion.

name: polymer mass fraction
definition: Mass fraction of polymer within the dispersed phase.

name: emulsion polymerisation
definition: Polymerization whereby monomer(s), initiator, dispersion medium, and possibly colloid stabilizer constitute initially an inhomogeneous system resulting in particles of colloidal dimensions containing the formed polymer.

name: ab initio emulsion polymerisation
definition: Emulsion polymerization in which no seed particles are added.

name: batch emulsion polymerisation
definition: Emulsion polymerization in which all the ingredients are placed in a reactor prior to reaction.

name: continuous emulsion polymerisation
definition: Emulsion polymerization in which all the ingredients are added continuously and the product latex is removed continuously.

name: emulsifier-free emulsion polymerisation
definition: Emulsion polymerization carried out without the addition of a colloid stabilizer.

name: encapsulating emulsion polymerisation
definition: Emulsion polymerization leading to the encapsulation of a solid within polymer particles or liquid polymer droplets.

name: inverse emulsion polymerisation
definition: Emulsion polymerization in a nonaqueous medium in which the dispersed phase is usually an aqueous solution, initially of monomer(s), and finally of polymer.

name: monomer-flooded emulsion polymerisation
definition: Semi-continuous emulsion polymerization in which the monomer(s) is(are) fed to the reactor at a rate that exceeds the rate of polymerization.

name: monomer-starved emulsion polymerisation
definition: Semi-continuous emulsion polymerization in which the polymerization rate is controlled by the feed rate(s) of monomer(s), in such a way that, for most of the process, the polymerization rate equals the monomer(s) feed rate(s).

name: power-feed emulsion polymerisation
definition: Semi-continuous emulsion copolymerization in which the instantaneous composition of the formed copolymer is the same as that of the added monomer mixture(s).

name: seeded emulsion polymerisation
definition: Emulsion polymerization with seed particles are formed in situ or added initially to the polymerizing mixture.

name: semi-continuous emulsion polymerisation
definition: Emulsion polymerization in which some of the ingredients are initially placed in a reactor and the remaining ingredients are added during the polymerization.

name: vesicle polymerisation
definition: Polymerization inside the bilayer of a vesicle leading to formation of polymer inside the bilayer.

name: micro-emulsion polymerisation
definition: Emulsion polymerization in which the starting system is a micro-emulsion and the final latex comprises colloidal particles of polymer dispersed in an aqueous medium.

name: inverse micro-emulsion polymerisation
definition: Emulsion polymerization in which the starting system is a micro-emulsion and the final system is composed of an organic continuous phase with an aqueous polymer solution as the dispersed phase.

name: micellar polymerisation
definition: Polymerization of a polymerizable surfactant in solution above its critical micelle concentration.

name: mini-emulsion polymerisation
definition: Polymerization of a mini-emulsion of monomer in which all of the polymerization occurs within preexisting monomer particles without the formation of new particles.

name: inverse mini-emulsion polymerisation
definition: Emulsion polymerization in which the starting system is a mini-emulsion and the final system is composed of an organic continuous phase with an aqueous polymer solution as the dispersed phase.

name: precipitation polymerisation
definition: Polymerization in which monomer(s), initiator(s) and colloid stabilizer(s) are dissolved in a solvent and this continuous phase that is a nonsolvent for the formed polymer beyond a critical molecular weight.

name: dispersion polymerisation
definition: Precipitation polymerization in which monomer(s), initiator(s), and colloid stabilizer(s) are dissolved in a solvent forming initially a homogeneous system that produces polymer and results in the formation of polymer particles.

name: seeded dispersion polymerisation
definition: Dispersion polymerization in which seed particles are formed in situ or added prior to initiation of the polymerization.

name: precipitation polycondensation
definition: Precipitation polymerization proceeding by polycondensation.

name: dispersion polycondensation
definition: Dispersion polymerization proceeding by polycondensation.

name: precipitation polyaddition
definition: Precipitation polymerization proceeding by polyaddition.

name: dispersion polyaddition
definition: Dispersion polymerization proceeding by polyaddition.

name: suspension polymerisation
definition: Polymerization in which polymer is formed in monomer, or monomer-solvent droplets in a continuous phase that is a nonsolvent for both the monomer and the formed polymer.

name: micro-suspension polymerisation
definition: Suspension polymerization in which the diameter of the monomer droplets is of the order of a few \(\pu{\upmu m}\).

name: average number of radicals per particle
definition: Ratio of the total number of radicals in particles to the number of particles.

name: critical oligomer degree of polymerisation for irreversible entry
definition: Lowest degree of polymerization of aqueous-phase oligomer-radicals needed for irreversible capture by colloidal particles, micelles, or both during a polymerization.

name: critical oligomer degree of polymerisation for precipitation
definition: Lowest degree of polymerization of oligomer-radicals that precipitate from the continuous phase during a polymerization.

name: intervals in emulsion polymerisations
definition: Periods in an emulsion polymerization defined by the formation of polymer particles, and the presence or absence of monomer droplets in the polymerizing mixture.

name: interval 1 in emulsion polymerisation
definition: Period in a batch ab initio emulsion polymerization during which the formation of particles takes place.

name: interval 2 in emulsion polymerisation
definition: Period in an emulsion polymerization during which no new particles are formed and monomer droplets are present.

name: interval 3 in emulsion polymerisation
definition: Period in an emulsion polymerization during which no new particles are formed and no monomer droplets are present.

name: zero-one behaviour
definition: Limiting behaviour in an emulsion, mini-emulsion, or micro-emulsion polymerization during which the entry of a radical into a particle that contains a growing radical results in termination before significant propagation has occurred.

name: compartmentalisation behaviour
definition: Zero-one behaviour wherein radicals are isolated, each being located within a different latex particle.

name: pseudo-bulk behaviour
definition: Behaviour in an emulsion, mini-emulsion, micro-emulsion, suspension, or dispersion polymerization wherein the kinetics are such that the rate equations are the same as those for polymerization in bulk.

name: homogeneous micellisation nucleation
definition: Formation of primary particles as a result of micelle formation from surface-active oligomer radicals formed in a polymerization.

name: micellar nucleation
definition: Formation of primary particles as a result of polymerization within monomer-swollen micelles initiated by the capture of primary radicals or oligomer-radicals.

name: coagulative nucleation
definition: A process combining nucleation by any mechanism with subsequent coagulation being a significant event in formation of colloidally stable particles.

name: phase-transfer event in a dispersed system
definition: Transport of any species (radical, monomer, chain-transfer agent, etc.) from the continuous to the discrete phase and vice-versa.

name: radical entry
definition: Irreversible transport of a radical from the continuous to the dispersed phase.

name: radical entry frequency
definition: Average number of entry events per particle per unit interval of time.

name: radical exit
definition: Reversible or irreversible transport of a radical from the dispersed to the continuous phase.

name: radical exit frequency
definition: Average number of exit events per particle per unit interval of time per radical.

name: primary radical
definition: Radicals formed from an initiator molecule.

name: seed particle
definition: Particle in a polymer colloid that is the locus of subsequent polymerization.

name: surfmer
definition: Monomer with the properties of a surfactant.

name: inisurf
definition: Initiator with the properties of a surfactant.

name: transurf
definition: Chain-transfer agent with the properties of a surfactant.

name: breaking of an emulsion
definition: Formation of a system with separate macrophases from an emulsion.

name: critical coagulation concentration
definition: Minimum concentration of electrolyte at and above which rapid coagulation occurs.

name: heterocoagulation
definition: Coagulation of particles of different kinds or sizes, or both.

name: homocoagulation
definition: Coagulation of colloidal particles of the same size and kind.

name: fast coagulation rate
definition: Rate of coagulation in the absence of any repulsive barrier between particles.

name: fast coagulation rate coefficient
definition: Rate coefficient for fast coagulation.

name: flocculation rate coefficient
definition: Rate coefficient for flocculation.

name: micellisation
definition: Process in which surface-active molecules or ions aggregate into micelles.

name: orthokinetic coagulation
definition: Coagulation due to collisions of particles induced by hydrodynamic motion.

name: particle monolayer
definition: Monolayer of particles deposited at an interface.

name: perikinetic coagulation
definition: Coagulation due to collisions of particles caused by their Brownian motion.

name: slow coagulation rate
definition: Rate of coagulation in presence of repulsive barriers between particles.

name: slow coagulation rate coefficient
definition: Rate coefficient for slow coagulation.

name: stability ratio
definition: Ratio \(W = k_{\rm{fast}}/k_{\rm{slow}}\) or \(W = k_{\rm{fast}}/k_{\rm{floc}}\), for coagulation or flocculation, respectively, with \(k_{\rm{fast}}\), \(k_{\rm{slow}}\), and \(k_{\rm{floc}}\) measured under the same mixing (or hydrodynamic) conditions.

name: colloidally stable system
definition: System in which the particles essentially do not aggregate or sediment.

name: electrostatic stabilisation
definition: Stabilization of a colloid resulting from the mutual repulsion of the electrical double layers surrounding its particles.

name: electrosteric stabilisation
definition: Stabilization of a colloid that has both steric and electrostatic stabilization characteristics.

name: steric stabilisation
definition: Stabilization of a colloid resulting from covering particles with a layer of molecules solvated by the continuous medium.

name: ecotoxicology
definition: Study of the toxic effects of chemical and physical agents on all living organisms, especially on populations and communities within defined ecosystems; it includes transfer pathways of these agents and their interactions with the environment.

name: mutagenicity
definition: Ability of a physical, chemical, or biological agent to induce (or generate) heritable changes (mutations) in the genotype in a cell as a consequence of alterations or loss of genes or chromosomes (or parts thereof).

name: ultrafine particle
definition: Particle in air of aerodynamic diameter \(\pu{\lt 0.1 \upmu m}\).

name: toxicogenetics
definition: Study of the influence of hereditary factors on the effects of potentially toxic substances on individual organisms.

name: reproductive toxicity
definition: Ability of a physical, chemical, or biological agent to induce adverse effects in the reproductive system.

name: reproductive toxicology
definition: Study of the non-heritable adverse effects of substances on male and female reproductive function or capacity and on resultant progeny.

name: risk assessment management process
definition: Global term for the whole process from hazard identification to risk management.

name: risk management
definition: Decision-making process involving considerations of political, social, economic, and engineering factors with relevant risk assessments relating to a potential hazard so as to develop, analyze, and compare regulatory options and to select the optimal regulatory response for safety from that hazard.

name: safety
definition: Reciprocal of risk: practical certainty that injury will not result from a hazard under defined conditions.

name: safety data sheet
definition: Single page giving toxicological and other safety advice, usually associated with a particular preparation, substance, process, use pattern, or exposure scenario.

name: immunotoxicity
definition: Ability of a physical, chemical, or biological agent to induce adverse effects in the immune system.

name: dormant polymer chain
definition: Temporarily deactivated chain carrier.

name: reversible chain deactivation
definition: Deactivation of a chain carrier in a chain polymerisation, reversibly converting the active center into an inactive one and then, within the lifetime of a growing macromolecule, regenerating an active center on the same original chain carrier.

name: degenerate-transfer radical polymerisation
definition: Controlled reversible-deactivation radical polymerization in which the deactivation of the radicals involves degenerative transfer (DT) of a group (or atom).

name: absorbate
definition: Substance that enters and is retained inside a solid or semisolid matrix (absorbent).

name: absorbent
definition: Solid or semisolid matrix that is able to accommodate and retain an absorbate.

name: abundance
definition: Total number of individual organisms in a population, seen over a defined period of time in a certain place.Note: For fish, an estimate of total weight may replace number. Total number of organisms per unit of habitat space seen over a defined period. Amount of an element that exists in nature, usually expressed in relative terms as a percentage of the total amount of all elements in a given medium (e.g., the Earth’s crust). Amount of an isotope of an element that exists in nature, usually expressed in relative terms as a percentage of the total amount of all isotopes of the element.

name: abundant element
definition: Element which is of common occurrence in the Earth’s crust.

name: accessible
definition: Capable of being entered or reached; easy of access; such as one can go to, come into the presence of, reach, or lay hold of; get-at-able.

name: acclimatisation
definition: Processes, including selection and adaptation, by which a population of microorganisms develops the ability to degrade a substance, or develops a tolerance to it. In experimental systems, allowing an organism to adjust to its environment prior to undertaking a study. Modification of biological processes or structures in the maintenance of homeostasis in response to change in some environmental quality such as temperature, salinity, light, radiation, or toxicant concentration. Note: It is an expression of phenotypic plasticity of individuals in response to a sublethal change in some environmental factor.

name: acid precipitation
definition: Rain, fog, snow, sleet, or other particulate matter from the atmosphere with a _000078_ below \(\pu{5.6}\) deposited from the air.

name: acid-volatile sulfide
definition: Soil- and sediment-associated solid-phase sulfides extractable with cold hydrochloric acid.

name: acute
definition: Of short duration, in relation to exposure or effect; the effect usually shows a rapid onset. Note 1: In regulatory toxicology, 'acute' refers to studies where dosing is either single or limited to one day although the total study duration may extend to two weeks to permit appearance of toxicity in susceptible organ systems. Note 2: In aquatic ecotoxicology, exposure of the test organisms is typically continuous and of four days or less. In clinical medicine, sudden and severe, having a rapid onset.

name: acute-to-chronic toxicity ratio
definition: Numerical dimensionless quantity that is the ratio of an acute toxicity test result (e.g., \(\pu{LC_{50}}\)) to a chronic toxicity test result (e.g., maximum acceptable toxicant concentration, MATC) where both are expressed in the same units (e.g., \(\pu{mg L-1}\)). Ideally, the data are for the same chemical species.

name: additive effect
definition: Consequence that follows exposure to two or more physicochemical agents that act jointly but do not interact: the total effect is the simple sum of the effects of separate exposures to the agents under the same conditions.

name: additive index
definition: Quantification of the joint action of toxicants in mixture by adding measures of their toxicity calculated in relation to the toxicity of a reference toxicant.

name: adenylate energy charge
definition: Index reflecting the balance of energy transfer between catabolic and anabolic processes, calculated from the equation \[\rm{AEC} = ([\ce{ATP}] + ½[\ce{ADP})/([\ce{ATP}] + [\ce{ADP}] + [\ce{AMP}])\] where \(\ce{ATP}\), \(\ce{ADP}\), and \(\ce{AMP}\) are the amount concentrations of adenosine tri-, di-, and monophosphate, respectively.

name: adsorption factor
definition: Ratio of the amount of substance adsorbed at the interface of a condensed layer and a liquid or gaseous phase to the total amount of the substance available for adsorption.

name: age class
definition: Group of organisms of the same age within a population.

name: age composition
definition: Distribution of organisms among the various age classes present in the population. The sum of the number of individuals in all age classes equals the population size.

name: age distribution
definition: Composition of a population in terms of how its abundance is distributed across age classes.

name: age-specific death rate
definition: Mean number of deaths as tabulated for a life table interval or for a specific age class in a given year, expressed per \(\pu{1000}\) in that interval or age class.
synonyms: age-specific mortality|age-specific number of individuals dying

name: aggregation error
definition: Error in Bayesian probability analysis of model systems resulting from the use of a single set of parameters to represent a collection of distinct entities, such as individuals, in a population.

name: air pollution tolerance index
definition: Empirical index used to assess the tolerance of individual plants to contaminated air. The numerical value of \(T_{\rm{I}}\) is obtained by combining various quantities according to the recipe \([A (T + P) + R]/10\), where \(A\) is the mass of ascorbic acid divided by the dry mass of a leaf, expressed as \(\pu{mg/g}\), \(T\) is the total mass of chlorophyll divided by the fresh mass, expressed as \(\pu{mg/g}\), \(P\) is the pH of a leaf extract, and \(R\) is the mass of water in the leaf divided by the wet mass, expressed as percent.

name: alga
definition: Any of various chiefly aquatic, eukaryotic, photosynthetic organisms, ranging in size from single-celled forms to the giant kelp.

name: algal bloom
definition: Rapid increase in the abundance of phytoplankton or benthic algae in a given area, often as a result of an increased availability of nutrients or light, or increase in temperature (e.g., the spring bloom).

name: algicide
definition: Substance intended to kill algae.

name: algistatic
definition: Inhibiting algal population growth.

name: allogenic succession
definition: Sequential appearance of species driven by external influences that alter local conditions; e.g., silt deposits changing a marshland to woodland.

name: ambient
definition: Surrounding (applied to environmental media such as air, water, sediment, or soil).

name: ambient monitoring
definition: Continuous or repeated measurement of agents in the environment to evaluate ambient exposure and health risk by comparison with appropriate reference values based on knowledge of the probable relationship between exposure and resultant adverse health effects.

name: anadromous
definition: Showing anadromy.

name: anadromy
definition: Life-history pattern that is characterized by egg incubation and early juvenile development in freshwater, migration to seawater for adult development, and a return to freshwater for spawning.

name: analysis plan
definition: Scheme that defines the exact format and design of the assessment, explicitly states the data needed, and describes the methods and design for analyzing these data.

name: anthropogenic
definition: Caused by or influenced by human activities. Describing a conversion factor used to calculate a dose or concentration affecting a human that has been derived from data obtained with another species, e.g., the rat.

name: antisymmetry
definition: Quality of a population of bilaterally symmetrical individuals in which the difference in measurement of a trait made from the right and left sides of individuals from that population produces a bimodal distribution.

name: arcsine square root transformation
definition: \(\arcsin \sqrt{P}\), where \(P\) is the value of a measured effect, e.g., the proportion of exposed organisms in a population.

name: artificial soil test
definition: Test with earthworms in which the toxicity of a substance by skin and gut uptake is determined by adding the earthworms to an artificial soil made of sand, clay mineral, and peat, containing the substance of concern.

name: artisol test
definition: Test with earthworms in which the toxicity of a substance by skin and gut uptake is determined by placing the worms in an artificial substrate consisting of silica, water, and glass balls, containing the substance of concern.

name: aryl hydrocarbon hydroxylase
definition: Enzyme activity attributed to cytochrome P-450 monooxygenase isoforms and often measured in units of benzo[a]pyrene hydroxylation.

name: as low as reasonably achievable
definition: Describing the situation in which everything practicable is done to reduce risks to the minimum with the approval of the regulatory authorities.

name: assemblage
definition: Set of coexisting populations defined by phylogeny, location, or life style. Assemblages are intermediate between populations and communities.

name: assessment endpoint
definition: Ecological property that is to be protected and the precise parameter to be measured for this property.

name: Association Française de Normalisation test
definition: Commercially available test kit, certified by AFNOR as valid and equivalent to a standardized method.

name: asymptotic threshold concentration
definition: Concentration of a chemical at which some percentage of a population of test organisms is in a state of approximate homeostasis for a prolonged period of time (\(\pu{48 h}\) or more).

name: atmospheric deposition
definition: Process that transfers a chemical from the atmosphere to the Earth’s surface (land, water, or vegetation) by either dry impingement or by transport in rain or snow.

name: aufwuchs
definition: Floral and (or) or faunal communities attached to submerged surfaces in aquatic ecosystems.

name: autogenic succession
definition: Sequential appearance of species driven by processes operating within the community environment (compare allogenic succession), e.g., primary and secondary successions that occur on newly exposed land.

name: autotroph
definition: Organism that is independent of outside sources for organic food materials and manufactures its own organic material from inorganic sources.

name: autotrophic succession
definition: Sequential appearance of species in a location principally involving plants.

name: axenic culture
definition: Growth of organisms of a single species in the absence of cells or living organisms of any other species.

name: baseline toxicity
definition: General, nonspecific, reversible mode of toxic action that can be produced in most living organisms by the presence of sufficient amounts of many organic chemicals.

name: Bayesian
definition: Attributed to Thomas Bayes (1702–1761), English mathematician. The term is used to designate concepts relating to inverse probability, especially Bayes’ theorem, a theorem expressing the probability of one of a number of mutually exclusive events \(H_{\rm{i}}\), given some other event \(E\), in terms of the probabilities of all the \(H_{\rm{i}}\) independently of \(E\) and the probabilities of \(E\) given each \(H_{\rm{i}}\).

name: Bayesian probability
definition: Subjective or objective concept of probability as a 'measure of the state of knowledge'.

name: behavioural teratology
definition: Study of behavioral abnormalities in otherwise apparently normal individuals after exposure in the embryonic state to a substance or physical agent.

name: behavioural toxicology
definition: Study of abnormal behavior produced by exposure to a substance or physical agent.

name: beneficial metal
definition: Non-essential metal which in some form (chemical species) at an appropriate dose can improve health of defined organisms, commonly human beings.

name: benefit
definition: Advantage to, or improvement in condition of, an individual, a population, a species, an assemblage, a community, or an ecosystem.

name: benthic
definition: Living on the bottom of an aquatic system.

name: bioaccessible
definition: Able to come in contact with a living organism and perhaps interact with it with the possibility of absorption into the organism.

name: bioaccumulation
definition: Progressive increase in the amount of a substance in an organism or part of an organism that occurs because the rate of intake from all contributing sources and by all possible routes exceeds the organism’s ability to eliminate the substance from its body.

name: bioaccumulation factor
definition: Ratio of tissue chemical residue to chemical concentration in an external environmental phase (e.g., sediment, water, soil, air, or food). BAF is measured at a steady state in situations where organisms are exposed to multiple sources (e.g., water, sediment, food), unless noted otherwise.

name: bioactivation
definition: Metabolic conversion of a xenobiotic to a more toxic derivative or to one that has more of an effect on living organisms.

name: bioavailable
definition: Able to be absorbed by living organisms.

name: biocenosis
definition: All the interacting organisms living together in a specified habitat.

name: biocide
definition: Substance intended to kill living organisms. Nonagricultural pesticide used to control the severity and incidence of pests or diseases, e.g., algicide, slimicide, or disinfectant for the control of algal, fungal, or bacterial growth.

name: bioconcentration
definition: Process leading to a higher concentration of a substance in an organism than in environmental media to which it is exposed.

name: bioconcentration factor
definition: Measure of the tendency for a substance in water to accumulate in aquatic organisms defined as the ratio of the concentration of the substance of concern in the organism to the concentration in water at equilibrium.

name: lipid-based bioconcentration factor
definition: Ratio of the concentration of the substance of concern in the lipid fraction of the test organism to the concentration in the ambient water.

name: biodiversity
definition: Occurrence of a number of species within a given ecosystem or biome, or the presence of a number of community types in a given area.

name: biodiversity action plan
definition: Internationally recognized program designed to protect and restore biological systems containing threatened species and habitats.

name: biogeochemical cycle
definition: Movement of elements or molecules among organisms and nonliving compartments of the atmosphere, lithosphere, and hydrosphere.

name: biological indicator
definition: Any biological species or group of species whose performance, abundance, or population status is used to determine the health of an environment or ecosystem by systematic monitoring of chemical, physiological, or behavioral changes.

name: biological determinant
definition: Property of living organisms that affects human or environmental health.

name: biomagnification
definition: Sequence of processes by which higher concentrations of a substance are attained in organisms at higher trophic levels. Result of these processes of bioconcentration and bioaccumulation by which tissue concentrations of bioaccumulated chemicals increase as the chemical passes up through two or more trophic levels. Note: Biomagnification occurs in a food chain as a consequence of efficient transfer of a substance from food to consumer accompanied by the lack of, or very slow, excretion or degradation of the substance.

name: biomagnification factor
definition: Ratio of concentrations of a compound at two consecutive trophic levels at steady state. It can also be expressed in terms of a rate constant-based bioaccumulation model \[B = C_{n}/C_{n-1} = \alpha f/k_{\rm{e}}\] where \(\alpha\) is assimilation efficiency, \(f\) is feeding rate, and \(k_{\rm{e}}\) is the first-order elimination constant. \(B\) can be calculated from field data on assumed trophic relations or from laboratory feeding experiments.

name: biomarker of effect
definition: Biomarker that, depending upon the magnitude, can be recognized as associated with an established or possible health impairment or disease.

name: biomarker of exposure
definition: Biomarker that relates exposure to a xenobiotic to the levels of the substance or its metabolite, or of the product of an interaction between the substance and some target molecule or cell, that can be measured in a compartment within an organism.

name: biomarker of susceptibility
definition: Biomarker of an inherent or acquired ability of an organism to respond to exposure to a specific substance.

name: biome
definition: Set of plants and animals that occupy a certain geographic area.

name: biomodification
definition: Alteration of the chemical or physical properties of a substance by the action of living organisms.

name: biomonitor
definition: n. Organism that provides quantitative information on the quality of the environment around it.Note: The ideal substance biomonitor would indicate the presence of a specific pollutant and provide additional information about the amount present. v. To use organisms to monitor pollutants and to deduce possible effects on biota or routes of toxicant exposure to humans.

name: biomonitoring type 1
definition: Determination of community changes along a gradient or among sites differing in levels of pollution.

name: biomonitoring type 2
definition: Determination of bioaccumulation in organisms among sites notionally varying in the level of contamination.

name: biomonitoring type 3
definition: Determination of effects on organisms using tools such as biochemical markers in sentinel species or some measure of diminished fitness or condition of individuals.

name: biomonitoring type 4
definition: Determination of genetically based resistance in populations of contaminated areas.

name: biopesticide
definition: Biological agent with pesticidal activity, e.g., the bacterium Bacillus thuringiensis when used to kill insects.

name: bioremediation
definition: Use of biological organisms such as plants or microbes to aid in removing hazardous substances from an area.

name: biota-sediment accumulation factor
definition: Ratio of lipid-normalized tissue chemical residue to carbon-normalized sediment substance concentration (units of mass lipid/mass organic carbon).

name: biotic index
definition: One of several ranking systems calculated from the presence or abundance of sensitive species relative to tolerant species.

name: biotic ligand
definition: Component of a living organism to which an ion or other substance in aqueous solution can bind, usually with subsequent beneficial or harmful effect on the physiology of the organism.

name: biotic ligand model
definition: Model that integrates the interactions of metals with ligands in water to calculate the speciation (based on hardness, salinity, and presence of other metals) and the concentration of ionic species producing toxicity. The BLM chemically and mathematically models the organism’s target site as ligand(s) competing with nonbiotic ligands, based on the concept that toxicity occurs when a metal-(biotic ligand) complex reaches a critical concentration.

name: biotic score
definition: Weighted measurement of organisms present—the weighted part is determined by each group’s pollution tolerance or intolerance. As pollution increases in a stream, the biotic score value tends to increase.

name: biotope
definition: Habitat shared by many species, most often an area that is uniform in environmental conditions and in its distribution of animal and plant life.

name: bioturbation
definition: Group of processes whereby organisms affect the structure of sediment.

name: biphasic dose–effect model
definition: Model of adverse effect vs. dose relationship that, owing to hormesis, dips down from the control level before increasing with the dose; individuals exposed to low, but nontoxic concentrations are healthier than individuals not exposed to the chemical.Note: Biphasic dose–effect curves occur for any nutrient. Hormesis is a phenomenon associated with compounds that have no nutrient properties. Model of adverse effect vs. dose relationship that changes slope owing to a change in the mechanism of toxic action.Note: This may, e.g., be due to saturation of a transport or metabolic system.

name: birth rate
definition: (in demography) Number of live births in a defined administrative jurisdiction in a calendar year divided by a midyear population of the jurisdiction, with the customary multiplier of \(\pu{1000}\) to produce a whole number rather than a decimal or a fraction. Note: An alternative statistic is total fertility rate, the average number of children born to each woman over the course of her life. In general, the total fertility rate is a better indicator of fertility rates because, unlike the crude birth rate, it is not affected by the age distribution of the population. (in ecology) Number of births, \(B\), in a population of a defined size, \(N\), during a specified time interval \(\Delta t\). The rate is calculated from the formula \[B = \Delta N/\Delta t\] where \(\Delta N\) is the change in the number of births in a limited time period \(\Delta t\).

name: boomerang effect
definition: Delayed damage from earlier environmental contamination.

name: borderline metal ions
definition: Metal ions intermediate in properties between class a and class b metal ions.

name: bottom-up ecotoxicological study
definition: Approach to investigating ecotoxicological effects that starts with a determination of the presence and nature of any adverse effects via responses at the suborganismal (cellular and biochemical) levels of organization rather than via the community and (or) ecosystem levels of organization.

name: Brillouin index
definition: Quantitative value for community species diversity calculated as \[H_{\rm{B}} = (\ln N! - \sum \ln n_{i}!)/N\] where \(N\) is the total number of individuals and \(n_{i}\) is the number of individuals in the \(i^{\rm{th}}\) species.

name: broodstock
definition: Adult fish producing either eggs or sperm.

name: calcinosis
definition: Any pathological condition characterized by the deposition of calcium salts in tissues.

name: calcium sink
definition: Tissue such as arthropod cuticle, bivalve shell, or vertebrate bone that renders calcium or elements with similar biological behavior (such as lead or cadmium) less bioavailable during trophic interactions, thus providing a mechanism for trophic dilution.

name: carrying capacity
definition: Maximum population size expressed as total number of individuals, biomass, or population density that a given unit of habitat is capable of sustaining.

name: catadromous
definition: Describing a species exhibiting catadromy.

name: catadromy
definition: Life-history pattern that is characterized by egg incubation and early juvenile development in seawater, migration to freshwater for adult development, and return to seawater for spawning.

name: catagenesis
definition: Long-term geochemical alteration to organic matter, involving high temperatures and pressures deep below the surface of the Earth.

name: cetaceans
definition: Whales, dolphins, and porpoises, in the order Cetacea.

name: Chapman mechanism
definition: Series of reactions by which ozone is formed in the stratosphere.

name: chemical time bomb
definition: Substance or substances in a component of the environment which are not currently bioavailable but which may become bioavailable at an unknown time in the future with harmful consequences.

name: chloride cell
definition: Specialized cell with a role in ion regulation, characterized by large numbers of mitochondria, an extensive intracellular tubular network and a high concentration of \(\ce{Na+}\)/\(\ce{K+}\) ATPase. This cell is found in salt-secreting glands like the rectal gland of elasmobranchs, the nasal gland of seabirds, and the gills of both seawater and freshwater fish, mainly on the primary lamellae but also on the secondary lamellae.

name: chlorinity
definition: Proportion by mass of dissolved chloride ions in water.

name: chlorofluorocarbon
definition: Carbon-based chemical containing chlorine and fluorine, responsible for ozone depletion in the stratosphere.

name: chronic effect
definition: Consequence that develops slowly and (or) has a long-lasting course: may be applied to an effect which develops rapidly and is long lasting.

name: chlorosis
definition: Loss of green color in plants owing to the lack of production or the destruction of chlorophyll.

name: cladistics
definition: Systematic classification of groups of organisms on the basis of shared characteristics thought to derive from a common ancestor. Also, the study of the branching of evolutionary lines of descent and the relationship between branches.

name: cladogram
definition: Dendrogram illustrating the supposed evolutionary relationships between clades; a diagram showing cladistic relationships.

name: climax community
definition: Community of plants and animals in a steady state due to ecological succession resulting in a composition of the community best adapted to average conditions in the area. The term is sometimes applied to soil development.

name: cold condensation theory
definition: Theory that pollutants with high vapor pressure, e.g., mercury or persistent organic pollutants (POPs), in the air will condense onto soil, water, and biota at cool temperatures. Consequently, the ratios for POP concentrations in the air and on condensed phases decrease as one moves from warmer to cooler climates.

name: cometabolism
definition: Microbial transformation of a compound (that is normally unable to support cell replication) in the requisite presence of a transformable cosubstrate that supports cell replication.

name: community
definition: Assembly of populations of different species of living organisms, usually interdependent on and interacting with each other, within a specified location in space and time.

name: community conditioning hypothesis
definition: Hypothesis that ecological communities retain information about events in their history and will not return to their original state after perturbation.

name: community stability
definition: Tendency of a community to return to its original state after a disturbance (competition, temporarily changing environment, etc.).

name: community resilience
definition: Ability of a community to return to its former state after perturbation.

name: community resistance
definition: Ability of a community to avoid displacement from its present state by a disturbance.

name: community structure
definition: Species present in a community and their relative abundances.

name: compartment
definition: Conceptualized part of the body (organs, tissues, cells, or fluids) considered as an independent system for purposes of modeling and assessment of distribution and clearance of a substance. Part of an ecosystem considered as an independent system for purposes of assessment of uptake, distribution, and dissipation of a substance.

name: competitive exclusion
definition: Outcompetition from a niche of one species by another that uses the available resources of the niche more efficiently, eventually resulting in the exclusion of the outcompeted species.

name: complimentary niches
definition: Niches where coexisting species occupy a similar position along one niche dimension, e.g., altitude, but differ along another, e.g., diet.

name: concentration–response curve
definition: Graph of the relation between exposure concentration and the proportion of individuals in a population responding with a defined effect.

name: conceptual model
definition: Linkage and interrelationship of assessment endpoint(s) and stressors.

name: conceptual model diagram
definition: Figure showing pathways of exposure of organisms and illustrating areas of uncertainty or concern.

name: conceptual site model
definition: Integration of information on contaminants of potential concern (COPCs), ecological resources, evaluated exposure routes, fate and transport mechanisms, evaluated COPC toxicity, identified assessment endpoints, and risk questions and hypotheses, into a description of all that is known and (or) expected about a contaminated site.

name: condition
definition: State of health determining potential for reproduction and growth.

name: condition factor
definition: Parameter used to describe growth in fish. It reflects real growth and nutritional status better than simple measurement of body mass.

name: condition index
definition: Any quantitative measure of the condition in relation to a defined baseline.

name: conservation biology
definition: Science applied to the conservation of genes, populations, species, and ecosystems.

name: conservation ecology
definition: Science of analyzing and protecting the Earth’s biological diversity.

name: contaminant
definition: Minor impurity present in a substance. Extraneous material inadvertently added to a sample prior to or during chemical or biological analysis. In some contexts, as in relation to gas cleaning equipment, used as a synonym for 'pollutant', especially on a small scale. Unintended component in food that may pose a hazard to the consumer. Any undesirable solid, liquid, or gaseous matter occurring, as a result of human activities, in a solid, liquid, or gaseous environmental medium, even without adverse effects being observed.

name: continuous effect
definition: Change that can be measured on a continuum from zero (or even a negative value) to positive values such as growth and reproduction.

name: control
definition: Treatment in a toxicity test that duplicates all the conditions of the exposure treatments but contains no test material, in order to determine the absence of toxicity under basic test conditions (e.g., health of test organisms, quality of dilution water).

name: cooxidation
definition: Cometabolism whereby growing microorganisms oxidize a compound without using either carbon or energy derived from the oxidation of that compound.

name: copepod
definition: Minute marine or freshwater crustacean, usually having six pairs of limbs on the thorax; some are abundant in plankton and others are parasitic on fish, marine mammals, and macro-invertebrates.

name: corrosive
definition: n. Substance having the capability or tendency to cause slow destruction. adj. Gradually destructive; steadily harmful.

name: cost–benefit analysis
definition: Procedure for determining the relationship of the expected benefits of a proposed action to the expected costs in order to decide whether the action provides the best option for the investment of limited resources.

name: cost-effectiveness analysis
definition: Procedure for determining whether the expected beneficial effects of a defined course of action justify the cost when selecting among competing options for the use of limited resources.

name: cough
definition: Abrupt, periodic reversal of water flow over the gills that dislodges and eliminates excess mucus from the gills’ surfaces.

name: critical body residue
definition: Whole-body concentration of a chemical that is associated with a given adverse biological response.

name: critical life-stage testing
definition: Toxicity testing focused on the species life stage thought to be the most sensitive to the toxicant, such as newly hatched individuals.

name: cross-resistance
definition: Condition in which enhanced tolerance to one toxicant also enhances tolerance to another.

name: culture
definition: n. Stock of healthy cells, tissue, microorganisms, or plants raised under well-defined and controlled conditions. v. To maintain a stock of healthy organisms under well-defined and controlled conditions.

name: cumulative dose
definition: Total dose resulting from repeated exposures or continuous exposure over a defined time to a substance or to radiation.

name: cumulative exposure
definition: Total exposure resulting from repeated and continuous exposure over a defined time to a substance or to radiation.

name: Daphnia
definition: Small, mostly planktonic, crustaceans, between \(\pu{0.2 mm}\) and \(\pu{5 mm}\) in length.

name: dead-end metabolite
definition: Substance formed by a microbe’s metabolism of a substrate (most often during cometabolism) that cannot be further metabolized by that organism.

name: death
definition: In assessing population ecology, death of an individual is loss of the ability to reproduce.

name: death
definition: Irreversible cessation of all vital functions of an organism.

name: death rate
definition: Number of deaths \(D\) in a closed population of size \(N\) during a specified time interval, \(\Delta t\). The rate is calculated from the formula \[D = -\Delta N/\Delta t\] where \(\Delta N\) is the change in number of deaths over a specified time period.

name: dechlorinated water
definition: Chlorinated water (usually municipal drinking water) that has been treated to remove chlorine and chlorinated compounds from solution.

name: decomposer
definition: Organism that breaks down dead matter or wastes of other organisms.

name: defoliant
definition: Substance used for removal of leaves by its toxic action on living plants.

name: demographic stochasticity
definition: Variability in population growth rates arising from random differences among individuals in survival and reproduction within a season.

name: demography
definition: Study of populations, especially their age structure and growth rates.

name: density dependence
definition: Variation in characteristics of individuals or of a population produced by changes in the density of the population.

name: deposit feeder
definition: Animal that feeds on particles of matter in the soil or sediment, usually the top soil or sediment where it is filled with organic matter. Feeding takes place either by ingesting soil or sediment or by trapping particles as they fall.

name: depuration
definition: Loss of a substance from an organism owing to elimination and degradation.

name: derived characteristic
definition: Predicted property of a substance that is dependent upon, or is an approximation of, a fundamental property and the prevailing environmental conditions.

name: deterministic
definition: Term applied to effects, of which the extent varies with the dose and for which a threshold is believed to exist.

name: deterministic analysis
definition: Detailed study in which all population and environmental parameters are assumed to be constant and accurately specified.

name: deterministic model
definition: Mathematical model that is fully specified and does not include a stochastic component.

name: detritus
definition: Organic debris from decomposing plants and animals.

name: detrivorous
definition: Describing an organism that survives by eating detritus.

name: developmental reference dose
definition: Reference dose determined for developmental consequences of a single, maternal exposure during development.

name: developmental stability
definition: Potential of an organism to develop into a consistent phenotype in an environment.

name: diatom
definition: Member of a major group of eukaryotic algae, among the most common types of phytoplankton. Unicellular, some form chains or simple colonies. Diatom cells are encased in a frustule, of widely diverse form, made of silica (hydrated silicon dioxide).

name: diffuse source
definition: Release into the environment from multiple sources covering a wide area as opposed to point source.

name: dilution paradigm
definition: Belief that pollution is alleviated by dilution.

name: dilution water
definition: Water used to dilute the test material in an aquatic toxicity test in order to prepare either different concentrations of a test chemical or different percentages of an effluent for the various test treatments.

name: direct ecological effect
definition: Effect where a stressor acts immediately on an ecological component of interest and not through the consequences of effects on other components of the ecosystem.

name: directional asymmetry
definition: Deviation within a population from a mean of zero for the difference between a trait measured from the right and left sides of bilaterally symmetrical individuals from that population.

name: direct toxicity
definition: Toxicity that results from, and is readily attributable to, substances acting at the sites of toxic action in and (or) on the exposed organisms that are exhibiting the adverse biological response in question.

name: discharge
definition: Release of any waste into the environment from a point source.

name: discrimination ratio
definition: Ratio measuring the degree of isotopic discrimination, with a ratio of 1 indicating no discrimination.

name: dispersant
definition: Substance used to disperse liquid spills, e.g., oil spills in water.

name: dissolved organic carbon
definition: Amount concentration of carbon found dissolved in water samples from aquatic systems, measured as total elemental carbon.

name: dissolved oxygen content
definition: Amount concentration of oxygen dissolved in water at a particular temperature and pressure.

name: dissolved organic matter
definition: Analogous to dissolved organic carbon, but refers to the entire organic pool dissolved in water.

name: disturbance
definition: Event that introduces, removes, or redistributes organisms, changing the colonization potential of a given environment.

name: diversity index
definition: Mathematical descriptor of species variation within a community.

name: dose–effect
definition: Relation between dose and the magnitude of a measured biological change.

name: dose–effect curve
definition: Graph of the relation between dose and the magnitude of the biological change produced measured in appropriate units.

name: dose–effect relationship
definition: Association between dose and the resulting magnitude of a continuously graded change, either in an individual or in a population.

name: dose–response curve
definition: Graph of the relation between dose and the proportion of individuals in a population responding with a defined biological effect.

name: dose–response relationship
definition: Association between dose and the incidence of a defined biological effect in an exposed population usually expressed as percentage.

name: drainage basin
definition: Area of land where water from rain or snow melt drains downhill into a body of water, such as a river, lake, dam, estuary, wetland, sea, or ocean.
synonyms: catchment|catchment area|catchment basin|drainage area|river basin|water basin|watershed

name: dynamic energy budget theory
definition: Theory that simple quantitative rules may be applied to define the organization of metabolism of individual organisms.

name: dynamically fragile community
definition: Community that is stable for only a very limited range of environmental characteristics, e.g., a stable and predictable environment with respect to predator–prey ratios or disturbances caused by humans.

name: dynamically robust community
definition: Community that is stable within a wide range of conditions, e.g., in very variable and unpredictable environments.

name: dynamic stability hypothesis
definition: Hypothesis that long food chains are less stable than short food chains.

name: ecology
definition: Branch of biology that studies the interactions between living organisms and all factors (including other organisms) in their environment. Such interactions encompass environmental factors that determine the distributions of living organisms.

name: ecological character
definition: Sum of biological, physical, and chemical components of an ecosystem and their interactions that maintain the ecosystem and its products, functions, and attributes.

name: ecological energetics
definition: Study of the flow of energy within an ecological system from the time the energy enters the living system until it is irretrievably lost from the system as heat.

name: ecological epidemiology
definition: Application of epidemiological methods to determine the cause, incidence, prevalence, and distribution of adverse effects in nonhuman species inhabiting contaminated sites; it is frequently associated with retrospective ecological risk assessment.

name: ecological imbalance
definition: Change in any biological, physical, or chemical components of an ecosystem, or in their interactions, which result in change in ecological character and its functions and attributes.

name: ecological mortality
definition: Toxicant-related diminution of fitness of an individual functioning within an ecosystem that is of a magnitude sufficient to be equivalent to somatic death.

name: ecological parameter
definition: Measurable variable whose value is a determinant of the characteristics of an ecosystem.

name: ecophysiology
definition: Study of physiology and tolerance limits of species that enhances understanding of their distribution in relation to abiotic conditions.

name: ecoregion
definition: Any of a number of regions into which a continent, country, etc., can be divided according to their distinct environmental conditions and habitat types. Large area of land or water with a characteristic, geographically distinct assemblage of natural communities and species comprising a recurring pattern of ecosystems associated with characteristic combinations of soil and landform.Note: The biodiversity of ecosystems in an ecoregion is often distinct from that of other ecoregions.

name: ecosystem
definition: Grouping of organisms (microorganisms, plants, animals) interacting together, with and through their physical and chemical environments, to form a functional entity within a defined environment.

name: ecotone
definition: Area of gradual transition between two or more ecosystems.

name: ecotoxicologically relevant concentration
definition: Concentration of a pesticide (active ingredient, formulations, and relevant metabolites) that is likely to affect a determinable ecological characteristic of an exposed system.
