definition: Poisoning of a predator as a result of eating prey that has accumulated a toxicant as a result of biomagnification through its food chain.

name: secondary substrate metabolism
definition: Microbial growth on a nutrient substrate while transforming another substrate without gaining energetic benefit.

name: secondary succession
definition: Sequential appearance of species following major changes to an established ecosystem.

name: selection components
definition: Components of the life cycle of an individual upon which natural selection can act. They are viability selection, sexual selection, meiotic drive, gametic selection, and fecundity selection.

name: Selyean stress
definition: Syndrome named for Hans Selye (1907–1982) that consists of all the nonspecifically induced changes within a biological system following and during environmental stress.

name: semelparous species
definition: Species that reproduces once.

name: semi-continuous activated sludge test
definition: Test for inherent biodegradability of organic substances in activated sludge by measurement of the decrease in dissolved oxygen content (DOC) in the test system.

name: sentinel species
definition: Feral, caged, or endemic species used in measuring and indicating the level of contamination or effect during a biomonitoring exercise.

name: seston
definition: Minute living organisms and particles of nonliving matter that float in water and contribute to turbidity.

name: sexual selection
definition: Natural selection involving differential mating success of individuals.

name: Shannon–Wiener diversity index
definition: Index based on the assumption that all species are represented in the sample studied and that the sample was obtained randomly, giving the following mathematical relationship: \[H = -\sum \limits_{i=1}^S p_{i} \log p_{i}\] where \(p_{i}\) is the fraction of individuals belonging to the \(i\)-th species and \(S\) is the number of species.

name: Shelford’s law of tolerance
definition: Species’ tolerance(s) along an environmental gradient (or series of environmental gradients) will determine its population distribution and size in the environment.

name: silt
definition: Sediment particles with a grain size between \(\pu{0.004 mm}\) and \(\pu{0.062 mm}\), i.e., coarser than clay particles but finer than sand.

name: Simpson’s diversity index
definition: Dominance index weighted toward the abundance of the most common species, giving the probability of any two individuals drawn at random from an infinitely large community belonging to different species. The bias corrected mathematical form of Simpson’s index is \[D = \sum \limits_{i=1}^{S} p_{i}^{2}\] where \(p_{i}\) is the fraction of all organisms which belong to the \(i\)-th species and \(S\) is the number of species.

name: simulated field studies
definition: Experimental ecosystem that should be: physically confined; self-maintaining; multitrophic; have a duration time exceeding the generation time of the penultimate trophic level present; and of size sufficient to enable pertinent sampling and measurements to be made without seriously influencing the structure and dynamics of the system.

name: soil
definition: Naturally occurring, unconsolidated mineral and (or) organic material at the surface of the Earth that is capable of supporting plant growth. It extends from the surface to \(\pu{15 cm}\) below the depth at which properties produced by soil-forming processes can be detected.

name: solvent drag
definition: Movement of a solute (e.g., a contaminant) along with the bulk movement of the solvent.

name: somatic death
definition: Death of an individual organism.

name: somatic risk
definition: Risk of an adverse effect to the exposed individual associated with genetic damage to somatic cells, e.g., damage leading to cancer.

name: sorbate
definition: Noncommittal term used instead of adsorbate or absorbate when the sorption process is undefined.

name: sorption constant
definition: Quantity describing the distribution of a substance between a solvent and a sorbent, typically water and sediment, at equilibrium, e.g., \[K_{\rm{d}} = [\pu{C(sediment)}]/[\pu{C(water)}]\]

name: source term
definition: Estimate of the total amount released, or the temporal pattern of the rate of release, of a pollutant from a source.

name: Spearman–Karber method
definition: Nonparametric method to estimate the \(\pu{LC_{50}}\), \(\pu{EC_{50}}\), or \(\pu{LD_{50}}\) when it is difficult or unnecessary to assume a specific model for the dose- or concentration effect data.

name: species–area relationship
definition: Common pattern in which the number of species on islands decreases as island area decreases.

name: species assemblage
definition: Operationally defined subset of the entire community.

name: species–deletion stability
definition: Tendency in a model community for the remaining species to remain at locally stable equilibria after a species is made extinct.

name: species differences in sensitivity
definition: Quantitative or qualitative differences of response to the action(s) of a potentially toxic substance on various species of living organisms.

name: species diversity
definition: Heterogeneity of an ecological community, considering both species richness (\(S\)) and species evenness.

name: species evenness
definition: Degree to which the individuals in the community are evenly or uniformly distributed among species.

name: species imbalance
definition: Change in the species numbers or diversity in an ecosystem, or in their interactions, which results in change in ecological character and its functions and attributes.

name: species richness
definition: Total number of species in an ecosystem.

name: species sensitivity distribution
definition: Statistical relationship between exposure concentration and a defined effect derived from a combination of single-species test data to predict concentrations affecting only a certain percentage of the total number of species in a defined community.

name: species-specific sensitivity
definition: Quantitative and qualitative features of response to the action(s) of a potentially toxic substance that are characteristic for a particular species of living organism.

name: specific action concept
definition: Assumption made in radiotracer usage concerning specificity of action of a radionuclide used to trace or quantify the movement of a stable nuclide (e.g., \(\ce{^{14}C}\) for stable \(\ce{C}\)), implying that the radionuclide behaves identically in chemical and biological processes to its nonradioactive analog (e.g., stable \(\ce{C}\)).

name: spiked bioassay approach
definition: Sediment toxicity test method to generate a concentration response model for effects to individuals placed in sediments spiked with different amounts of toxicant.

name: spillover hypothesis
definition: Hypothesis that toxic effects of metals will begin to occur after the metal concentration exceeds the capacity of the amount of metallothionein present to bind the metal. The unbound metals then 'spill over' to interact at sites of adverse action. This is based on the assumption that binding by metallothionein sequesters toxic metals away from sites of action.

name: stable age distribution
definition: Abundance of relative age classes that a population approaches if it is allowed to grow exponentially.

name: stable population
definition: Population with a constant distribution of individuals among the various age classes and a zero growth rate.

name: standard
definition: That which is established as a measure or model to which others of a similar nature should conform.

name: standard
definition: Technical specification, usually in the form of a document available to the public, drawn up with the consensus or general approval of all interests affected by it, based on the consolidated results of science, technology, and experience, aimed at the promotion of optimum community benefits and approved by a body recognized on the national, regional, or international level.

name: static-renewal test
definition: Modified static aquatic toxicity test in which solutions are completely or partially replaced with new solutions at set periods during exposures or in which organisms are periodically transferred to new solutions.
synonyms: batch-replacement test|renewal test|renewed static test|semi-static test|static-replacement test

name: static-toxicity test
definition: Aquatic toxicity test in which the exposure water is not changed during the test.

name: stratification
definition: Process by which materials form or are deposited in layers, as in sedimentary rocks and some igneous rocks. The atmosphere and the ocean also exhibit stratification, with the warmer air or water occupying the upper layers.

name: stratified sampling
definition: Sampling of individual subgroups (strata) of a population after its division into homogeneous strata.

name: stress
definition: Any condition that results in reduced growth of an organism or that prevents an organism from realizing its 'genetic potential'.

name: stressor
definition: Any physical, chemical, or biological factor causing an adverse response on any component of an ecosystem.

name: stress-protein fingerprinting
definition: Proposed use of the patterns of stress-protein induction seen in the field to suggest the particular toxicant inducing the response, after patterns from organisms sampled in the field are compared with those obtained with single-candidate toxicants in the laboratory.

name: stress proteins
definition: Several classes of proteins coded by genes transcriptionally activated by acute stresses, generally serving a protective or adaptive function.

name: stress theory of aging
definition: Theory that stress shortens longevity by accelerating energy expenditure. Selection takes place for resistance to stress, and as an epiphenomenon, individuals resistant to stress will predominate in extreme age classes of a population. The diminution of homeostasis under stress with age should be slowest in individuals with highest longevity.

name: structural diversity
definition: Range of types of physical structure in a community that may provide habitats for species.

name: structure–metabolism relationship
definition: Association between the physicochemical and (or) the structural properties of a substance and its metabolic behavior.

name: Sturm test
definition: Biodegradation test based on the measurement of \(\ce{CO2}\) production.

name: stygobiont
definition: Organism that lives only in groundwater.

name: stygophile
definition: Organism that lives in groundwater and in surface water.

name: subcooled
definition: Term applied to a substance that is a liquid at a temperature lower than the saturation temperature for the existing pressure.

name: subcooled liquid vapour pressure
definition: Vapor pressure of a subcooled liquid.

name: succession
definition: Orderly sequential progression of changes in community composition that occurs during development of new populations in any area, from initial colonization to the attainment of the climax typical of a particular geographic area.

name: supercooled
definition: Term describing a substance that persists as a liquid at a temperature below its freezing point without solidification or crystallization.

name: surrogate organism
definition: Test organism, or population that is cultured under laboratory conditions to serve as a substitute in toxicity testing for indigenous organisms, communities, or populations.

name: surrogate toxicant
definition: Relatively well-studied substance whose properties are assumed to apply to an entire chemically and toxicologically related class.

name: surveillance
definition: Systematic ongoing collection, collation, and analysis of data and the timely dissemination of information to those who need to know in order that action can be taken to initiate investigative or control measures.

name: survival time
definition: Time interval between initial exposure of an organism to a harmful substance and death.

name: survivorship
definition: Proportion of animals surviving between two specified ages.

name: survivorship curve
definition: Graph showing how survivorship from birth varies with age.

name: susceptibility
definition: Condition of an organism or ecological system that makes it more vulnerable to a given exposure than the majority of the population or group of ecological systems to which it belongs.

name: suspension feeder
definition: Animal that feeds by straining suspended matter and food particles from water, typically by passing the water over a specialized structure, such as the baleen of baleen whales.

name: syngenetic
definition: Describing mineral deposits formed at the same time as the enclosing rocks; characterized by or pertaining to a formation contemporaneous with the enclosing or surrounding rock.

name: systematics
definition: Study of the diversity of past and present life forms and of relationships among them through time.

name: taxocene
definition: Taxonomically defined subset of an entire community.

name: taxonomy
definition: Science applied to the allocation of biological names and the rules of naming.

name: teratogenic
definition: Capable of causing nonheritable permanent structural malformations or defects in the offspring of an exposed parent.

name: terrestrial
definition: Relating to land, as distinct from water or air.

name: threshold-effect concentration
definition: Concentration calculated as the geometric mean of no-observed-effect concentration (NOEC) and lowest-observed-effect concentration (LOEC).

name: threshold theory
definition: Theory that, for a given substance, no toxic effect can occur below a defined low dose.

name: tiered testing
definition: Structured approach to assessment of the fate and effects of substances, where a tier of relatively simple tests is used initially to select substances of concern and to define their toxicity. If the information from these tests is inadequate for regulatory decisions, further more complex tests (higher tier tests) may be required. For example, under a tiered structure, testing might progress from acute studies to chronic laboratory studies to field studies.

name: time-independent test
definition: Acute toxicity test with no predetermined temporal endpoint.

name: tolerance index
definition: Quotient of an adequate parameter acquired under treated and control environments, multiplied by \(\pu{100}\), thus: \[\rm{TI} = (\rm{parameter\ treated}/\rm{parameter\ control}) \times 100\]

name: top-down ecotoxicological study
definition: Approach to investigating ecotoxicological effects that starts with a determination of the presence and nature of any adverse effects via responses at community and ecosystem levels of organization rather than the suborganismal levels of organization.

name: total organic carbon
definition: Organic matter content of soil, sediment, or water determined by measurement of organic carbon as the ratio of mass of organic carbon/mass of solid or of water.

name: toxic
definition: Able to cause injury to living organisms as a result of physicochemical interaction.

name: toxic unit
definition: Dose or concentration of a toxicant expressed in units of lethality such as units of \(\pu{LD_{50}}\) or \(\pu{LC_{50}}\).

name: toxicity curve
definition: Curve obtained by plotting the median survival times of a group of test organisms against the concentration of a substance on a logarithmic scale.

name: toxicity equivalency factor
definition: Ratio of the toxicity of a chemical to that of another structurally related chemical (or index compound) chosen as a reference. In risk assessment, ratio of the toxicity of a chemical to that of another structurally related chemical (or index compound) chosen as a reference. Factor used to estimate the toxicity of a complex mixture, commonly a mixture of chlorinated dibenzo-p-dioxins [oxanthrenes], furans, and biphenyls: in this case, TEF is based on relative toxicity to 2,3,7,8-tetrachlorodibenzo-p-dioxin [2,3,7,8-tetrachlorooxanthrene] for which the \(f = 1\).

name: toxicity equivalent
definition: Contribution of a specified component (or components) to the toxicity of a mixture of related substances.

name: toxicity identification and evaluation
definition: Systematic pretreatment (e.g., \(\rm{pH}\) change, filtration, or aeration) of a sample to obtain defined fractions that are subsequently tested for their toxicity. This fractionation is designed to separate out defined substances and thus to identify the agent(s) primarily responsible for lethal or sublethal toxicity of a complex mixture.

name: toxicity value
definition: Factor used to estimate risk. It may be a reference dose or it may be calculated from the following equation: \[T_{\rm{x}} = m\ C\] where \(m\) is the slope of a published dose-effect relationship and \(C\) is the toxicant concentration.

name: trace nutrient
definition: Substance required in very small quantities by a defined organism to maintain health.

name: trade-off
definition: Exchange of one advantageous character for another.

name: trigger values
definition: Criteria applied to results from tests (for fate or effects) which prompt further studies, e.g., moving to the next tier of tests, which are generally more complex.

name: trophic
definition: Relating to nutrition.

name: trophic cascade
definition: Situation arising when predators in a food chain suppress the abundance of their prey, thereby releasing the next lower trophic level from predation (or herbivory if the intermediate trophic level is an herbivore).

name: trophic dilution
definition: Decrease in contaminant concentration as trophic level increases; this results from a net balance of ingestion rate, uptake from food, internal transformation, and elimination processes favoring loss of contaminant that enters the organism via food.

name: trophic level
definition: Position in a food chain, assessed by the number of energy-transfer steps to reach that level.

name: trophic structure
definition: Organization of an ecological community described in terms of energy flow through its various trophic levels.

name: trophic transfer
definition: Transfer of a substance from one trophic level to another.

name: trophic transfer factor
definition: Ratio between the concentration of a compound in a predator and in its prey.

name: turbidity of water
definition: Extent to which the clarity of water is reduced by the presence of suspended or other matter that causes light to be scattered and absorbed rather than transmitted (in straight lines) through the sample.

name: twin-tracer technique
definition: Experimental method for evaluating assimilation that introduces simultaneously a radiotracer of the substance being assimilated and an inert tracer that will not be assimilated, thus providing a basis for evaluating the assimilation.

name: type A organism
definition: Animal or plant living in contact with sediments but unable to ingest particulates.

name: type B organism
definition: Animal or plant living in contact with sediments and capable of ingesting particulates.

name: uncertainty factor
definition: In assay methodology, confidence interval or fiducial limit used to assess the probable precision of an estimate. In toxicology, value used in extrapolation from experimental animals to humans (assuming that humans may be more sensitive) or from selected individuals to the general population.Example: A value applied to the no-observed-effect-level (NOEL) or no-observed-adverse-effect-level (NOAEL) to derive an acceptable daily intake (ADI) or tolerable daily intake (TDI).Note: The NOEL or NOAEL is divided by the value to calculate the ADI or TDI.

name: upstream water
definition: Water in a rivulet, river, or lake that is situated above a defined point, in a direction opposite to that of the current flow.

name: uptake rate constant
definition: First-order one-compartment constant to describe the uptake of a substance by an organism from water.

name: viability selection
definition: Component of the life cycle of an individual in which natural selection can occur through the differential survival of individuals. It begins at the formation of the zygote and continues throughout the life of the individual.

name: vital rates
definition: Measures of how fast vital statistics change in a population (usually expressed per \(\pu{1000}\) individuals).

name: vulnerability
definition: Susceptibility to harm by toxicants.

name: Wahlund effect
definition: Net deficit of heterozygotes when two populations, each in Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium but with different allele frequencies, are mixed and the genotype frequencies quantified in a combined population sample.

name: waldsterben
definition: Widespread and substantial decline in growth and the change in behavior of many softwood and hardwood forest ecosystems in central Europe.

name: waste-water
definition: General term describing effluents, leachate, and elutriates which enter the natural environment.

name: weakest-link incongruity
definition: Questionable extension of the critical life-stage concept (see critical life-stage testing) that protection of the most sensitive life stage will ensure protection of all life stages; it assumes that exposure of field populations to concentrations identified in laboratory testing as causing significant mortality at a critical stage of life will result in significant impact on the field population

name: Weibull model
definition: Dose–response model of the form \[P(d) = \gamma + (1 - \gamma)(1 - e^{-\beta d^{\alpha}})\] where \(P(d)\) is the probability of a tumor (or other response) from lifetime, continuous exposure at dose \(d\) until age \(t\) (when tumor is fatal), \(\alpha\) is a fitted dose parameter (sometimes called the Weibull parameter), \(\beta\) is a fitted dose parameter, and \(\gamma\) is the background response rate.

name: weight composition
definition: Distribution of organisms among the various weight classes present in a population.

name: weight of evidence
definition: (in general) Quantitative, semiquantitative, or qualitative estimate of the degree to which the evidence supports or undermines a given conclusion. (in toxicology) Estimate of the extent to which the available biomedical data support the hypothesis that a substance causes a defined toxic effect such as cancer in humans.

name: Weismannism
definition: Theory of evolution and heredity propounded by the German biologist, August Weismann, especially in regard to the continuity of the germ-plasm and the nontransmission of acquired characteristics.

name: wet deposition
definition: Transfer of chemicals from the atmosphere to the Earth’s surface in atmospheric water precipitation (atmospheric deposition), e.g., rain, snow, or hail, of pollutants that occur in the precipitation, e.g., as a result of Brownian capture, nucleation, dissolution, or impaction.

name: wetland
definition: Area of land consisting of soil that is saturated with moisture, such as a swamp, marsh, or bog.

name: whole-effluent toxicity
definition: Total toxic effect of an effluent measured directly with aquatic organisms in a toxicity test.

name: whole sediment
definition: Sediment and associated interstitial water that have had minimal manipulation.

name: zooplankton
definition: Small floating or weakly swimming animals that drift with water currents and which, with phytoplankton, make up the planktonic food supply upon which almost all oceanic organisms ultimately depend.

name: normal equivalent deviation
definition: Proportion dying in a toxicity test expressed in terms of standard deviations from the mean of a normal curve.

name: absolute bioavailability
definition: Fraction of the administered dose of a drug from a dosage form absorbed intact into the systemic circulation.

name: active transport of drugs
definition: Carriage of a solute across a biological membrane, which requires a suitable carrier and the expenditure of energy.

name: administration
definition: Introduction of a substance to an organism by a defined route.

name: administration of drugs ocular route
definition: Administration of drugs through the eye.

name: administration of drugs oral route
definition: Administration of drugs through the mouth to swallow.

name: administration of drugs parenteral route
definition: Method of introducing substances into an organism, avoiding the gastrointestinal tract.

name: administration of drugs rectal route
definition: Administration of drugs into the rectal cavity or through the rectum.

name: administration of drugs respiratory route
definition: Delivery to the lower respiratory tract in order to obtain a local or systemic effect.

name: administration of drugs topical route
definition: Administration of drugs on surfaces of the body.

name: administration of drugs transdermal route
definition: Introduction of products through unbroken skin by means of a specific drug delivery system (such as a patch containing a semi-solid formulation of the drug) for systemic and/or prolonged drug effect.

name: administration of drugs vaginal route
definition: Introduction of products into the vagina normally for local effect.

name: angle of repose
definition: Characteristic angle of slope formed with the horizontal by the side of a static conical mound of powder.

name: appertisation
definition: Process by which food is rendered free from pathogenic, toxigenic, and spoilage organisms.

name: bioequivalence
definition: Relationship between two preparations of the same drug in the same dosage form that have a similar bioavailability. Dosage forms containing the same drug are said to be bioequivalent if they do not differ significantly in the bioavailability (e.g., AUC, \(c_{\rm{max}}\), \(t_{\rm{max}}\)) of the active constituent/ingredient, when administered in the same dose under similar experimental conditions.

name: biological product
definition: Virus, therapeutic serum, toxin, antitoxin, or analogous product applicable to the prevention, treatment, or cure of diseases or injuries in humans and/or animals.

name: biopharmaceutics
definition: Branch of pharmaceutical science that deals with the fate of drugs in the living system; particularly the release of the drug from its dosage form into a biological medium, its passage across membranes into the systemic circulation, metabolism, and elimination, and the application of this knowledge to obtain the desired therapeutic effect.

name: buccal tablet
definition: Usually a small, flat, and soft tablet, which is designed to be placed inside the cheek to be directly absorbed through the mucosa for systemic effect.

name: bulk density
definition: Characteristic of a powder rather than of individual particles given by the mass of powder occupying a known volume.

name: capsule
definition: Small edible package made usually from gelatin or other materials that can be filled with drugs (solids or liquids) to produce a unit dose, mainly for oral use. Hard capsules consist of two pieces that fit one inside the other which are produced empty and filled in a separate operation, and soft, liquid-filled capsules, which are manufactured and filled in one operation.

name: carrier-mediated drug transport
definition: Transfer of a drug across a membrane by a transporter (often a protein) constituent of the cytosol membrane. Also known as active transport as opposed to passive diffusion/absorption.

name: coating
definition: Technological process consisting of the application of a substance, which forms a layer (e.g., to protect the drug and/or the tablet, to mask taste, to control the rate of drug release (e.g., film coating, sugar coating).

name: compressed tablet
definition: A solid dosage form prepared to a desired shape, usually in large-scale production, by means of high pressure in a punch and die.

name: controlled-release dosage form
definition: Medication, which due to its special technological construction provides for drug release having predefined kinetics (zero order, \(t^{1/2}\), first order, etc.) at a sufficient rate to maintain the desired therapeutic level over an extended period of time.

name: critical moisture content
definition: A stage in the drying of solids, above which the drying rate (derived from the plot of the loss of moisture content against time) is linear, at which the drying rate ceases to be linear, until it reaches the equilibrium moisture content.

name: crossover study
definition: Type of comparative bioavailability study designed in such a way as to take into account differences in bioavailability arising from differences between patients suffering from disease, participating in the study.

name: crystalline
definition: Term that describes a solid of regular shape and the presence of three-dimensional order on the level of atomic dimensions, for a given molecule.

name: delayed-release dosage form
definition: Pharmaceutical preparation that releases the drug(s) at a time other than promptly after administration.

name: deliquescent
definition: Substance that absorbs sufficient moisture from the atmosphere to dissolve itself.

name: depot
definition: Deposit of a drug in a body created by injection or by a similar mode of introduction to form a source of slow release.

name: detergency
definition: Property, which serves as basis for the process whereby surfactants are used for the removal of foreign matter from surfaces (including dirt from clothes or body surfaces).

name: diffusion barrier
definition: Obstacle such as coating or embedding, which acts as a factor controlling the rate of drug release.

name: disperse system
definition: Dosage form in which the active ingredient is insoluble in the carrier; includes aerosols (solids or liquids in gas), suspensions (solids in liquids), emulsions (liquids in liquids), and foams (gas in liquid), or ointments/creams (solid in solid or in semi-solid, or liquid in solid).

name: divided granule
definition: Formulation in which individual doses of a granulated dosage form are separated (e.g., gelatin capsules).

name: divided powder
definition: Powder formulation in which individual doses of a powdered dosage form are separately wrapped (e.g., sachets, envelopes, or gelatin capsules).

name: dosage form
definition: Formulated preparation of molecules/drugs that are rarely if ever suitable for administration to patients without additives.

name: dosage regimen
definition: Dose and dosing interval of a drug.

name: drug delivery system
definition: Sophisticated dosage form, which, by its construction, is able to modify/control the availability of the drug substance to the body by temporal or spatial considerations.

name: drug-eluting stent
definition: Refers to a stent with an active drug that is intended to produce a therapeutic effect (e.g., reduction of restenosis).

name: dusting powder
definition: Usually intended for external use.

name: effervescent tablet
definition: Solid preparation that on contact with water breaks apart by the effect of gas (usually \(\ce{CO2}\)) evolution, resulting commonly from the reaction of hydrogen carbonate with citric or tartaric acid, in order to facilitate dissolution or dispersion of the active ingredient before ingestion.

name: efflorescent
definition: Substance that loses water to form a lower hydrate or becomes anhydrous spontaneously.

name: elixir
definition: Sweet (often colored) dilute alcohol-based, 'hydroalcoholic', liquid used in the compounding of drugs to be taken by mouth in order to improve palatability.

name: embedding
definition: Technological process, which consists of mixing or inclusion of the therapeutic substance with an excipient or their mixtures, typically as a matrix dosage form, in order to change the rate of release.

name: enemas
definition: Solutions (aqueous or oily), emulsions, or suspensions for rectal administration of medicaments for cleansing, diagnostic, or therapeutic purposes.

name: enteric coating
definition: Used on tablets, granules, pellets, and capsules to make them resistant to gastric fluids but designed to disintegrate, disrupt, or dissolve when the preparation enters the duodenum.

name: equilibrium moisture content
definition: Final stage reached after drying of a solid, beyond the critical moisture content.

name: fast-dissolving tablet
definition: A tablet formulation intended for a rapid release of its active agent.

name: formulation
definition: Summary of operations carried out to convert a pharmacologically active compound into a dosage form suitable for administration.

name: gargle
definition: Aqueous solution used for the prevention and treatment of mouth and throat infections.

name: gastric emptying rate
definition: Pace at which a drug along with the stomach content leaves and enters the duodenum.

name: gene therapy
definition: Use of products containing genetic material (e.g., pDNA, antisense DNA, siRNA) to treat a disease or condition, or to modify or manipulate the expression of genetic material or to alter the biological properties of living cells.

name: generic
definition: Drug(s) or formulation(s) of drug(s) or dosage forms, which no longer have patent protection.

name: granules
definition: Powder particles, which have been aggregated to form larger irregular particles, usually of \(\pu{0.5\!{-}\! 2 mm}\) diameter.

name: granulation
definition: Process in which powder particles are made to aggregate to larger particles called granules.

name: hydrate
definition: Crystalline form of a compound in which water molecules are part of the crystal structure.

name: hydrophile-lipophile balance system
definition: Empirical scale (of \(0\!-\!20\)) used to classify surfactants and emulsifying agents.

name: hygroscopicity
definition: Tendency of a substance to absorb water from the atmosphere.

name: immediate-release tablet
definition: Dosage form that releases the drug immediately.

name: inactivation factor
definition: Number that expresses the reduction in the numbers of a microorganism, brought about by a sterilization process.

name: inhalation therapy
definition: Administration of drugs directly to the respiratory tract, mostly by aerosols.

name: injection
definition: Delivery of a generally sterile liquid medication into the body, or a vessel, tissue, or organ via syringe and needle.

name: liniment
definition: Liquid intended for massaging into the skin.

name: loading dose
definition: Initial, typically larger than the maintenance dose of a drug given to a patient at the start of pharmacotherapy.

name: lotion
definition: Solution, emulsion, or suspension to be applied to the skin.

name: lozenge
definition: Tablet, which does not contain a disintegrant and which is sucked to dissolve in the mouth to produce either a local (e.g., antiseptic) or systemic (e.g., vitamins) effect.

name: lubricant
definition: Used as processing aid in tablet and capsule manufacturing, to facilitate the movement of the formulation into the dye and punch and to reduce the energy of compression.

name: matrix formulation
definition: Specific case of drug embedding in insoluble excipients (typically in a polymer) in order to achieve extended release.

name: maximum additive concentration
definition: Maximum concentration of a drug, which will form a clear solution with a given concentration of surfactant.

name: maximum safe concentration
definition: Concentration of a drug in the plasma, above which side effects are likely to occur in a patient.

name: minimum effective plasma concentration
definition: Concentration of a drug that must be achieved in the plasma before any desired therapeutic or pharmacological effect can be obtained.

name: minimum inhibitory concentration
definition: Lowest concentration of an antibacterial drug necessary to inhibit the growth of a microorganism.

name: modified release
definition: Release of a drug from a dosage form that it is not immediate (e.g., sustained release, retarded release, delayed-action preparations, controlled release, extended release, etc.).

name: moistening agents
definition: Usually water or low-molecular-weight alcohols or compounds, used in topical applications and in wet granulation, for the production of tablets.

name: multicompartment formulation
definition: Dosage form (capsule, tablet) comprising several elements (e.g., microspheres or coated pellets) differing in the rate of drug release.

name: multilayer tablet
definition: Consists of several different layers that are compressed on top of each other, to form a single tablet composed of two or more layers.

name: nanoencapsulation
definition: Formation of nanoparticles encapsulating a drug.

name: ointment
definition: Greasy, semi-solid preparation for external application, often anhydrous, containing dissolved or dispersed medicaments.

name: one-compartment model
definition: Kinetic model, where the whole body is thought of as a single compartment in which a substance is distributed rapidly, achieving an equilibrium between blood and tissue immediately.

name: onset of drug action
definition: Time required to achieve the minimum effective plasma concentration following administration of the dosage form.

name: paste
definition: Ointment containing \(\gt \pu{0\%}\) of powder, dispersed in a fatty base.

name: pellet
definition: Very small tablet or pilule. Implantable polymeric matrix. Spherical granule.

name: pelletisation
definition: Process of agglomeration that converts fine powders or granules of bulk drugs and excipients into small, free-flowing, spherical, or semi-spherical units, referred to as pellets.

name: pharmaceutical equivalence
definition: To be pharmaceutically equivalent, the generic and proprietary formulations must (1) contain the same amount of active ingredient; (2) contain the same active ingredient in the same dosage form; (3) be intended for the same route of administration; and (4) generally be labeled for the same conditions of use.

name: pharmaceutics
definition: Science of preparation of drugs, dosage forms, and drug delivery systems taking into account the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of the drug as well as its physical and chemical properties.

name: polymorph
definition: Solid material that exists at least in two different molecular arrangements, i.e., distinctly different crystal species.

name: powder grades
definition: Defined for powders used pharmaceutically, according to particle sizes.

name: powder
definition: Dry solid material consisting of many, usually free flowing, fine particles. Conventionally, the title 'powder' should be restricted to powder mixes for internal use and alternative terms are used for other powdered formulations presented in this way, e.g., dusting powders, which are for external use.

name: preformulation
definition: Exploratory activity that begins early in pharmaceutics, involving studies designed to determine the compatibility of excipients with the active substance for a biopharmaceutical; physicochemical and bioanalytical investigation in support of promising experimental formulations.

name: pseudopolymorph
definition: Different crystalline form(s) of a solvated compound that differ in the identity and/or the stoichiometry of the solvating molecule.

name: repeat action dosage form
definition: Tablet or capsule distinguished from a sustained-release dosage form, by the fact that it releases the medicinal agent, or part of it, at any time other than promptly after administration as opposed to a slow, controlled manner.

name: sieving
definition: Process that differentiates or separates solid particles according to their size using a meshed or perforated device.

name: slugging
definition: Method by which powder particles are compressed into a large tablet, called a slug, which is subsequently dry-screened and compressed into a tablet.

name: solubilising agents
definition: Additives making a substance soluble or more soluble, especially in water.

name: solvate
definition: Crystalline form of a compound in which one or more solvent molecules are part of the crystal structure.

name: spheronisation
definition: Process of making dense, spherical pellets by means of special spheronizing or pelletizing equipment.

name: stent
definition: Scaffold placed into narrowed, diseased vessels (mainly coronary arteries) or a device implanted in a vessel used to help keep it open.

name: sublingual tablets
definition: Usually small, flat, and soft tablets, which are designed to be placed under the tongue to allow direct absorption of the active ingredient through the mucosa for systemic effect.

name: suppositories
definition: Dosage form, semi-solid, used for the administration of drugs via the rectal route, for systemic or local effect. When application is via other routes (e.g., the vaginal route), suppositories are termed differently, inserts, pessaries, etc.

name: sustained release
definition: Dosage form designed to release the drug contained therein at a continuous and controlled rate for a longer period of time that can normally be achieved with its conventional, nonsustained counterpart.
synonyms: extended release|gradual release|long acting|prolonged action|slow release

name: syrup
definition: Liquid preparation of high sugar concentration with or without medicinal and additional flavoring substances.

name: tablet
definition: Solid dosage form compressed into a specific shape containing medicinal substances with or without suitable diluents.

name: tablet coating
definition: Solid layers based typically on cellulose derivatives and may include plasticizers and pigments. They are usually employed for one or more of the following reasons:  Protection of the ingredients (from light or moisture). Masking the bad taste of the drug. Masking possible batchwise differences in the appearance of raw materials and hence allaying possible patient concern over tablets of differing appearance. Coating confers mechanical strength and facilitates handling. Colored coating aids in the rapid identification of a product. Functional film coating is used to impart enteric or controlled-release properties to the tablet.

name: troche
definition: Applied to compressed lozenges. In lay language, lozenge and troche are used interchangeably.

name: acrylic polymer
definition: Polymer prepared from acrylic acid or a derivative of acrylic acid.

name: amino polymer
definition: Polymer prepared by polycondensation of an amino component such as amine or amide with an aldehyde, or by curing reactive oligomers prepared from an amino component and an aldehyde.

name: coumarone-indene polymer
definition: Polymer prepared from a mixture containing 1-benzofuran (formerly coumarone) and indene.

name: epoxy polymer
definition: Polymer prepared by reaction of compounds carrying two or more epoxy groups (reactive epoxides) with curing agents.

name: furan polymer
definition: Polymer prepared from furan or a furan derivative.

name: phenolic polymer
definition: Polymer prepared by the polycondensation of phenols and aldehydes or by curing reactive oligomers prepared from phenols and aldehydes.

name: polybismaleimide
definition: Polymer prepared from a bismaleimide.

name: polycarborane
definition: Polymer prepared from a carborane.

name: polydiene
definition: Polymer prepared from a diene, or a substituted diene, or both in admixture.

name: polyisocyanate
definition: Polymer prepared from an isocyanate.

name: polyisocyanide
definition: Polymer prepared from an isocyanide.

name: polyolefin
definition: Polymer prepared from an olefin.

name: polyvinyl acetal
definition: Polymer prepared by acetalization of poly(vinyl alcohol) with an aldehyde.

name: polyvinyl ester
definition: Polymer prepared from a vinyl ester.

name: polyvinyl ether
definition: Polymer prepared from a vinyl ether.

name: polyvinyl halide
definition: Polymer prepared from a vinyl halide (monohalogenoethene).

name: polyvinyl ketone
definition: Polymer prepared from a vinyl ketone.

name: styrene polymer
definition: Polymer prepared from styrene, or a substituted styrene, or both in admixture.

name: vinyl polymer
definition: Polymer prepared from a monomer containing the vinyl group \(\ce{-CH=CH2}\).

name: vinylidene polymer
definition: Polymer prepared from a monomer containing the ethene-1,1-diyl group \(\gt\!\ce{C=CH2}\), formerly called vinylidene.

name: polyalkenylene
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing exclusively alkene-α,ω-diyl (formerly alkenylene) constitutional repeating units: \[\ce{-[-CH=CH-[CH2]_{m}\bond{-}]_{n}\bond{-}}\]

name: polyalkylene
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing exclusively alkane-α,ω-diyl (formerly alkylene) constitutional repeating units: \[\ce{-[-CR^{1}R^{2}\bond{-}]_{n}\bond{-}}\] where \(\ce{R^1}\) and \(\ce{R^2}\) are each hydrogen, alkyl, or cycloalkyl.

name: polyalkynylene
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing exclusively alkyne-α,ω-diyl (formerly alkynylene) constitutional repeating units: \[\ce{-[-C#C-[CH2]_m\bond{-}]_n\bond{-}}\]

name: polyamide
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing carboxamide groups as linkages in the backbone: \[\ce{-NR-CO\bond{-}}\] where \(\ce{R}\) is hydrogen, alkyl, aryl, or heteroaryl.

name: polyamide acid
definition: Polyamide containing pendent carboxy groups:   where \(\ce{R}\) is a constitutional unit with a connectivity three or higher.

name: polyamine
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing imino groups as linkages in the backbone: \[\ce{-NR\bond{-}}\] where \(\ce{R}\) is hydrogen, alkyl, aryl, or heteroaryl.

name: polyanhydride
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing carboxylic anhydride groupings as linkages in the backbone: \[\ce{-CO-O-CO\bond{-}}\]

name: polybenzothiazole
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing benzothiazole groups in the backbone, such as the groups:

name: polybenzoxazole
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing benzoxazole linkages in the backbone, such as the linkages:

name: polycarbamate
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing carbamate (formerly urethane) or N-substituted carbamate linkages in the backbone: \[\ce{-NR-CO-O\bond{-}}\] where \(\ce{R}\) is hydrogen, alkyl, aryl, heteroaryl, substituted alkyl, substituted aryl, or substituted heteroaryl.

name: polycarbodiimide
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing carbodiimide linkages in the backbone: \[\ce{-N=C=N\bond{-}}\]

name: polycarbonate
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing carbonate linkages in the backbone: \[\ce{-O-CO-O\bond{-}}\]

name: polycarbosilane
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing carbon-silicon linkages in the backbone: \[\ce{-SiR^{1}R^{2}\bond{-}CR^{3}R^{4}\bond{-}}\] where \(\ce{R^1}\), \(\ce{R^2}\), \(\ce{R^3}\), and \(\ce{R^4}\) are each hydrogen, alkyl, aryl, or heteroaryl.

name: polycyanurate
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing 1,3,5-triazine-2,4,6-triyltrioxy constitutional units (formerly cyanurate groups) in the backbone:

name: polyester
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing carboxylic ester linkages in the backbone: \[\ce{-O-CO\bond{-}}\]

name: polyether
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing ether linkages in the backbone: \[\ce{-O\bond{-}}\]

name: polygermane
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing exclusively germanium atoms in the backbone: \[\ce{-[-GeR2\bond{-}]_{n}\bond{-}}\] where \(\ce{R}\) is alkyl, aryl or heteroaryl.

name: polyglutarimide
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing glutarimide rings in the backbone:   where \(\ce{R}\) is hydrogen or alkyl (usually methyl) and \(\ce{R^1}\) is hydrogen, or an alkyl, aryl, or heteroaryl group.

name: polyhydantoin
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing hydantoin (imidazolidine-2,4-dione) rings in the backbone:   where \(\ce{R}\) is hydrogen, or an alkyl, aryl, or heteroaryl group.

name: polyhydrazide
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing hydrazide linkages in the backbone: \[\ce{-CO-NR^1\bond{-}NR^2\bond{-}CO\bond{-}}\] where \(\ce{R^1}\) and \(\ce{R^2}\) are each hydrogen, alkyl, aryl, or heteroaryl.

name: polyimidazole
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing imidazole rings in the backbone:   where \(\ce{R^1}\) and \(\ce{R^2}\) are each hydrogen, or an alkyl or aryl group.

name: polyisocyanurate
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing 2,4,6-trioxo-1,3,5-triazinane-1,3,5-triyl (formerly isocyanurate) rings in the backbone:

name: polyketone
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing keto groups as linkages in the backbone: \[\ce{-CO\bond{-}}\]

name: polymetaloxane
definition: Organometallic polymer composed of macromolecules containing exclusively alternating metal and oxygen atoms in the main chain: \[\ce{-ML_{x}-O\bond{-}}\] where \(\ce{M}\) is a metal atom such as \(\ce{Al}\), \(\ce{Ge}\), \(\ce{Sn}\), or \(\ce{Ti}\), and \(\ce{L}\) is a metal-bonded substituent (ligand).

name: polyoxyalkylene
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing exclusively oxyalkane-α,ω-diyl (formerly oxyalkylene) constitutional repeating units in the backbone: \[\ce{-[-O-Y\bond{-}]_{n}\bond{-}}\] where \(\ce{Y}\) is an alkane-α,ω-diyl (formerly alkylene) or substituted alkane-α,ω-diyl group contributing at least two carbon atoms to the main chain.

name: polyoxyarylene
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing exclusively oxyarenediyl (formerly oxyarylene) constitutional repeating units in the backbone: \[\ce{-[-O-Ar\bond{-}]_{n}\bond{-}}\] where \(\ce{Ar}\) is an arenediyl (formerly arylene), heteroarenediyl (formerly heteroarylene), substituted arenediyl or substituted heteroarenediyl.

name: polyoxymethylene
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing exclusively oxymethylene or substituted oxymethylene constitutional repeating units in the backbone:   where \(\ce{R^1}\) and \(\ce{R^2}\) are each hydrogen, alkyl, aryl, or heteroaryl.

name: polyoxyphenylene
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing exclusively oxyphenylene or ring-substituted oxyphenylene constitutional repeating units in the backbone:   where \(\ce{R^1}\), \(\ce{R^2}\), \(\ce{R^3}\), and \(\ce{R^4}\) are each hydrogen or an alkyl, aryl, or aralkyl group.

name: polyparabanic acid
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing imidazolidine-2,4,5-trione (parabanic acid) rings in the backbone:

name: polyphenylenemethylene
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing exclusively alternating phenylene or substituted phenylene and methylene or substituted methylene constitutional units in the backbone:   where \(\ce{R^1}\), \(\ce{R^2}\), \(\ce{R^3}\), \(\ce{R^4}\), \(\ce{R^5}\), and \(\ce{R^6}\) are each hydrogen, alkyl, aryl, halogen, trialkylsilyl, etc.

name: polyphosphate
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing phosphate constitutional repeating units:   where \(\ce{R}\) is hydrogen, alkyl, aryl, or heteroaryl.

name: polyphosphazene
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing exclusively nitrilophosphanylylidene (formerly phosphazene) constitutional repeating units in the backbone:   where \(\ce{R^1}\) and \(\ce{R^2}\) are each a monovalent group, such as a halogen or an alkoxy group.

name: polypyrrone
definition: Polymer composed of single strand or ladder macromolecules comprising isoindolo[2,1-a]benzimidazole (formerly pyrrone) constitutional repeating units such as:  where \(\ce{Z}\) is a divalent linking group or atom.

name: polyquinoline
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing quinoline moieties in the backbone:

name: polyquinoxaline
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing quinoxaline groups in the backbone:

name: polysilazane
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing exclusively alternating nitrogen and silicon atoms in the backbone: \[\ce{-[-NR^{1}\bond{-}SiR^{2}\!\,R^{3}\bond{-}]_{n}\bond{-}}\] where \(\ce{R^1}\), \(\ce{R^2}\), and \(\ce{R^3}\) are each hydrogen or an alkyl or aryl group.

name: polysiloxane
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing alternating oxygen and silicon atoms in the backbone: \[\ce{-[-O\bond{-}SiR^{1}\!\,R^{2}\bond{-}]_{n}\bond{-}}\] where \(\ce{R^1}\) and \(\ce{R^2}\) are each hydrogen or an alkyl or aryl group.

name: polysilsesquioxane
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing silicon and oxygen atoms in the ratio \(1{:}1.5\) (ideal ratio for infinite macromolecule), which alternate in a hyperbranched or ladder structure such as:   where \(\ce{R}\) is alkyl, aryl, or heteroaryl.

name: polystannane
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing exclusively tin atoms in the backbone: \[\ce{-[-SnR^{1}\!\,R^{2}\bond{-}]_{n}\bond{-}}\] where \(\ce{R^1}\) and \(\ce{R^2}\) are each hydrogen or an alkyl or aryl group.

name: polysulfonamide
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing sulfonamide linkages in the backbone: \[\ce{-SO2-NR\bond{-}}\] where \(\ce{R}\) is hydrogen or an alkyl, aryl, or heteroaryl group.

name: polysulfone
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing sulfonyl linkages in the backbone: \[\ce{-SO2\bond{-}}\]

name: polythioester
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing thiocarboxylate (thioester) linkages in the backbone:\(\ce{-S-CO\bond{-}}\) or \(\ce{-O-CS\bond{-}}\) or \(\ce{-S-CS\bond{-}}\)

name: polythioether
definition: Polymers composed of macromolecules containing thioether (sulfide) linkages in the backbone: \[\ce{-S\bond{-}}\]

name: polytriazine
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing triazine rings in the backbone:

name: polyurea
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules containing ureylene or N-substituted ureylene linkages in the backbone: \[\ce{-NR-CO-NR\bond{-}}\] where \(\ce{R}\) is hydrogen, alkyl, aryl, heteroaryl, substituted alkyl, substituted aryl, or substituted heteroaryl.

name: cardo polymer
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules consisting of a single-strand main chain and many ring units, each having one atom in common with the main chain.

name: catenane polymer
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules consisting of physically catenated macrorings that have no atom in common and cannot be separated unless chemical bonds are broken.

name: helical polymer
definition: Polymer composed of macromolecules that adopt partly or completely a helical conformation.

name: activity coefficient at infinite dilution
definition: For a substance \(\ce{B}\), activity coefficient \(f_{\ce{B}}\) extrapolated to infinite dilution: \[\ln (f_{\ce{B}}^{\infty}) = \lim \limits_{x_{\ce{B}} \to 0} (\frac{\mu_{\ce{B}} - \mu_{\ce{B}}^{\ast}}{RT} - \ln x_{\ce{B}})\]

name: analytical method
definition: Class of experimental procedures for solubility determination in which a saturated solution is prepared and then analyzed to determine composition.

name: aquamolality
definition: For a solute \(\ce{B}\) in a system containing solvent \(\ce{A}\) and a reference solvent \(\ce{C}\), \[m_{\ce{B}}^{(\ce{C})} = m_{\ce{B}} \overline M/M_{\ce{C}}\] where \(m_{\ce{B}}\) is the molality of \(\ce{B}\), \(M_{\ce{C}}\) is the molar mass of a reference component, and \(\overline{M}\) is the average molar mass of a mixed solvent, defined for a system containing two solvents as \[\overline M = x_{ u,\ce{A}} M_{\ce{A}} + (1 - x_{ u,\ce{A}}) M_{\ce{C}}\] the solvent amount fraction of solvent \(\ce{A}\).

name: azeotropic point
definition: For a mixture, temperature and pressure (the azeotropic temperature and pressure) at which the compositions of the liquid and vapor phases become equal (the azeotropic composition), but the intensive properties of the two phases (such as molar volume) are different.

name: binary system
definition: System containing two components.

name: Bunsen coefficient
definition: Volume \(V^{\rm{g}}\) of an amount \(n_{\ce{B}}^{\rm{l}}\) of a gas dissolved at a given standard temperature \(T^{^⦵\!}\) (usually \(\pu{273.15 K}\)) and given standard (partial) pressure \(p_{\ce{B}}^{_{^⦵\!}}\) (\(\pu{1 bar} = \pu{0.1 MPa}\) or, in older literature, \(\pu{1 atm}\)) divided by the volume of the solvent \(V^{\rm{l}}\) containing an amount \(n_{\ce{A}}\) of solvent at temperature \(T\) and the given total pressure \(p^{_{^⦵\!}}\).

name: Clarke–Glew equation
definition: Semi-empirical equation describing the temperature dependence of the standard Gibbs energy of solution, \[\Delta_{\rm{sln}}G^{^⦵\!}(T, p^{_{^⦵\!}})/RT = A_{0} + A_{1}(T_{\rm{ref}}/T) + A_{2}\ln(T/T_{\rm{ref}}) + A_{3}(T/T_{\rm{ref}}) + A_{4}(T/T_{\rm{ref}})^{2} + \ldots\] where the \(A_{i}\) are constants that can be related to thermodynamic quantities (but subject to uncertainty because of statistical correlations among the fitting coefficients) and \(T_{\rm{ref}}\) is a reference temperature.

name: Clarke–Glew–Weiss equation
definition: Clarke–Glew equation with \(T_{\rm{ref}} = \pu{100 K}\).

name: coexistence curve
definition: Boundary of stable phase separation (limits of solubility) in a liquid or solid system of two or more components.

name: conjugate phases
definition: Two phases of variable composition in mutual thermodynamic equilibrium.

name: critical index
definition: Index in the basic equation describing a coexistence curve \[\beta = \lim \limits_{T \to T_{\rm{c}}} \left(\frac{\partial \ln (x'' - x')}{\partial \ln \vert T - T_{\rm{c}}\vert} \right)\] where \(x''\), \(x'\) are the mole fractions of one component in the respective concentrated and dilute phases and \(T_{\rm{c}}\) is the critical solution temperature.

name: data
definition: Experimental results, often numerical.

name: dystectic reaction
definition: Isobaric, reversible melting or dissolution with either complete or partial dissociation on heating of a solid compound, \(\ce{A_{\rm{a}}B_{\rm{b}}}\), formed by components \(\ce{A}\) and \(\ce{B}\) \[\ce{A_{\rm{a}}B_{\rm{b}}(s)  A_{\rm{a}}B_{\rm{b}}(l)  {\rm{a}}A(l) + {\rm{b}}B(l)}\] where the forward arrows indicate the direction of heating.

name: dystonic reaction
definition: Reversible dissolution in an isothermal, isobaric system of three or more components characterized by dissolution and saturation with a stoichiometric compound consisting of two or more of these components. The equilibrium process is, for example, \[\ce{AB.p H2O  A(aq, sat) + B(aq, sat) + p H2O(l)}\]

name: eutectoid reaction
definition: Isothermal reversible reaction of a solid mixture phase \(\upgamma\) which is transformed into two (or more) different solid (pure, binary compound or mixture) phases \(\upalpha\) and \(\upbeta\) during the cooling of a system. In a binary system, \[\ce{\upgamma  \upalpha + \upbeta}\] where the forward arrow indicates the direction of cooling. The equilibrium reaction occurs along the eutectoid line at the eutectoid temperature. At the eutectoid composition, the compositions of the high temperature solid phase and the mechanical mixture of the low-temperature solid phases are equal, and intermediate to the compositions of the pure solid phases \(\upalpha\) and \(\upbeta\). This composition and the eutectoid temperature, which are isobaric invariants of the system, define the eutectoid point.

name: eutonic reaction
definition: Reversible dissolution in a system of three or more components characterized by the composition of a solution that is simultaneously saturated with respect to all (at least two or more) dissolved solutes. The two simultaneous equilibrium processes are, for example, \[\begin{array}{l}\ce{A.p H2O  A{(aq, sat)} + p H2O(l)} \\ \ce{B.q H2O  B{(aq, sat)} + q H2O(l)}\end{array}\]
synonyms: (isothermally and isobarically invariant) reaction of double saturation|isothermally invariant reaction

name: fitting equation
definition: Theoretically based or empirical equation for interpolation of data over a range of temperature, pressure, composition, or other variable.

name: Gibbs–Duhem equation
definition: Equation relating the intensive variables \(T\), \(p\) and the \(C\) chemical potentials \(\mu_{i}\) in a phase \[S{\rm{d}}T - V{\rm{d}}p + \sum \limits_{i=1}^{C} n_{i} {\rm{d}}\mu_{i} = 0\] where \(C\) is the total number of components, \(i\) in a phase.

name: Gibbs energy of transfer
definition: Change in Gibbs energy at a given temperature and pressure for transfer of a substance between two different phases.

name: Gibbs–Konovalov equations
definition: Pair of equations for a binary mixture of components \(\ce{A}\) and \(\ce{B}\) that relate the variables \(T\), \(p\), in one phase of variable composition, \(\upalpha\), to the variables \(T\), \(p\), in a coexisting equilibrium phase of variable composition, \(\upbeta\): \[\begin{array}{c} -\frac{\left(1 - x_{\ce{B}}^{\beta} \right)\Delta_{\alpha}^{\beta} H_{\ce{A}} + x_{\ce{B}}^{\beta} \Delta_{\alpha}^{\beta} H_{\ce{B}}}{T}{\rm{d}}T + \left[\left(1 - x_{\ce{B}}^{\beta} \right)\Delta_{\alpha}^{\beta}V_{\ce{A}} + x_{\ce{B}}^{\beta}\Delta_{\alpha}^{\beta}V_{\ce{B}} \right]{\rm{d}}p +\left(x_{\ce{B}}^{\alpha} - x_{\ce{B}}^{\beta} \right)\left(\frac{\partial^{2} G_{\rm{m}}^{\alpha}}{\partial x_{\ce{B}}^{\alpha 2}} \right)_{T,p} {\rm{d}}x_{\ce{B}}^{\alpha} = 0 \\ -\frac{\left(1 - x_{\ce{B}}^{\alpha} \right)\Delta_{\alpha}^{\beta} H_{\ce{A}} + x_{\ce{B}}^{\alpha} \Delta_{\alpha}^{\beta} H_{\rm{B}}}{T}{\rm{d}}T + \left[\left(1 - x_{\ce{B}}^{\alpha} \right)\Delta_{\alpha}^{\beta}V_{\ce{A}} + x_{\ce{B}}^{\alpha}\Delta_{\alpha}^{\beta}V_{\ce{B}} \right]{\rm{d}}p +\left(x_{\ce{B}}^{\alpha} - x_{\ce{B}}^{\beta} \right)\left(\frac{\partial^{2} G_{\rm{m}}^{\alpha}}{\partial x_{\ce{B}}^{\beta 2}} \right)_{T,p} {\rm{d}}x_{\ce{B}}^{\beta} = 0 \end{array}\] where \(\Delta_{\upalpha}^{\upbeta} H_{\ce{A}} = H_{\ce{A}}^{\upbeta} - H_{\ce{A}}^{\upalpha}\), \(\Delta_{\upalpha}^{\upbeta} V_{\ce{A}} = V_{\ce{A}}^{\upbeta} - V_{\ce{A}}^{\upalpha}\) are the enthalpy and volume of transfer of component \(\ce{A}\) from phase \(\upalpha\) to phase \(\upbeta\), and similarly for component \(\ce{B}\).

name: higher-order system
definition: System containing more than three components.

name: infinite dilution
definition: Limiting composition or other variable in a solution obtained by extrapolating to a value of zero for the variable describing the composition of the solution.

name: infinite miscibility
definition: Property of a system of forming a single phase at all relative proportions of its components.

name: ionic mole fraction
definition: For an ionized salt \(\ce{B}\) in solution, \[x_{+\rm{B}} = \frac{ u_{+\ce{B}}x_{\ce{B}}}{1 + \sum \limits_{i=1}^{s} \left( u_{i} - 1 \right)x_{i}},x_{-\ce{B}} = \frac{ u_{-\ce{B}}x_{+\ce{B}}}{ u_{+\ce{B}}}\] where the summation is over all $s$ solute components \(i\) and \( u_{i} =  u_{+i} +  u_{-i}\) is the sum of the stoichiometric numbers of the ions formed from salt \(i\). For a single solvent \(\ce{A}\) in an ionic solution, \[x'_{\ce{A}} = \frac{x_{\ce{A}}}{1 + \sum \limits_{i=1}^{s} \left( u_{i} - 1 \right)x_{i}}\] Note 1: These are generalizations of terms and are used in formulating fitting equations for solubility of salts, in defining activity coefficients on the mole fraction scale, and in discussing salt effects on solubilities of gases.Note 2: Note that \[\sum \limits_{i=1}^{s} \left(x_{+i} - x_{-i} \right) + x'_{\ce{A}} = 1\]
synonyms: ionic amount fraction|species amount fraction|species mole fraction

name: isopleth
definition: Line joining points of equal composition on a phase diagram.

name: mass ratio
definition: Mass of one constituent \(\ce{A}\) divided by the mass of a second constituent \(\ce{B}\) in the same system. \[\zeta_{\ce{A,B}} = m_{\ce{A}}/m_{\ce{B}}\]

name: mass solubility
definition: Obsolete term for molality of a saturated solution of a gas.

name: metatectic reaction
definition: Isothermal reversible reaction of a solid mixture phase \(\upbeta\) which is transformed into a different solid phase \(\upalpha\) plus a liquid phase \(\ce{l}\) during cooling of a system. For a binary system, \[\ce{\upbeta  \upalpha + 1}\] where the forward arrow indicates the direction of cooling. The equilibrium transformation occurs along the metatectic line characterized by the metatectic temperature. The metatectic composition and temperature, isobaric invariants of the system, define the metatectic point, which lies between the compositions of liquid \(\ce{l}\) and solid phase \(\upalpha\).

name: mole percent
definition: Deprecated term that includes both a quantity and a unit. Replace by mole fraction expressed as percent.

name: mole ratio
definition: Amount of one constituent divided by the amount of a second constituent in the same system. For constituents 1 and 2, \[r_{12} = n_{1}/n_{2}\]

name: mutual solubility
definition: In a system of two or more liquid or solid components, solubility of all components in all phases.

name: non-saturating solute
definition: Solute which forms an unsaturated solution.

name: peritonic reaction
definition: Isothermal, isobaric reversible reaction between two phases, a saturated liquid and a solid, that results, on removal of the solvent component of a ternary system in one new solid phase. For example, \[\ce{l + \upalpha  \upbeta}\] where the forward arrow indicates the direction of removal of the solvent component. The system is in equilibrium along the peritonic line, on which is found the peritonic composition or point, an isothermal, isobaric invariant of the system which lies between the compositions of phases \(\ce{l}\) and \(\upalpha\).

name: permil
definition: One part in a thousand parts.

name: phase diagram
definition: Graphical representation, by use of points, lines, and surfaces, of the phases present at chemical equilibrium in unary, binary, ternary, and higher-order systems containing two or more phases.

name: Poynting correction
definition: Factor used to convert experimentally determined Henry’s law constants at the saturation vapor pressure of the solvent \(\ce{A}\), \(p_{\ce{A}}^{\ast}\), to a reference pressure \(p\) \[\begin{array}{c} I_{\rm{p}} = \int_{p_{\ce{A}}^{\ast}}^p \frac{V_{\ce{B}}^{\infty {\rm{l}}}}{RT}{\rm{d}}p \\ k_{\rm{H},\ce{B}}(p) = k_{\rm{H},\ce{B}}(p^{\ast}) \exp \left[I_{\rm{p}}(p) \right]\end{array}\] is the partial molar volume of liquid \(\ce{B}\) at infinite dilution in solvent \(\ce{A}\). The second equation gives the relation between the two Henry’s law constants.

name: primary data
definition: Data reported in peer-reviewed scientific reports of original research which allow an assessment of data quality.

name: Raoult’s law
definition: Fugacity (\(\tilde{p}_{\ce{B}}\)) of a gaseous component (\(\ce{B}\)) in equilibrium with a liquid or solid mixture containing \(\ce{B}\) is directly proportional to the activity (\(a_{\ce{B}}\)) of the component in the mixture \[\tilde{p}_{\ce{B}} = \tilde{p}_{\ce{B}}^{\ast} f_{\ce{B}} x_{\ce{B}}\] where \(f_{\ce{B}}\) is the activity coefficient of \(\ce{B}\) referenced to Raoult’s law at mole fraction \(x_{\ce{B}}\) and \(\tilde{p}_{\ce{B}}\) is the fugacity of pure \(\ce{B}\).

name: reciprocal salt system
definition: System containing \(n\) ionic species with or without a single solvent. Because of electrical neutrality, the system has \(n\) components in an aqueous system with a single solvent and \(n - 1\) components in a molten salt system.

name: reduced pressure
definition: Pressure divided by the critical pressure.

name: reduced temperature
definition: Temperature divided by the critical temperature.

name: reference data
definition: Data that are critically evaluated and verified, obtained from an identified source, and related to a property of a phenomenon, body, or substance, or a system of components of known composition and structure.

name: retrograde solubility
definition: Solubility that decreases with an increase in conditions such as temperature or added component, where an increase is expected as the usual case. In ternary liquid systems with coexisting phases, where the critical solution point is not a maximum on a ternary diagram, passing from a homogeneous mixture in which the composition of a given component is greater than that of the critical mixture to a heterogeneous mixture and back to a homogeneous mixture by altering the relative amounts of the two other components.

name: saturating solute
definition: Solute that forms a saturated solution.

name: scaling equation
definition: Dimensionless equation representing mutual solubilities in a number of chemically related liquid systems. Each mutual solubility is subtracted from the solubility at the critical solution point, and the temperature is divided by the critical solution temperature.

name: Sechenov equation
definition: Expression of the salt effect that relates the change in solubility of a nonelectrolyte (e.g., gas or organic liquid) to changing ionic strength of aqueous solutions, \[\lg (s_{\rm{o}}/s) = K_{s} I_{s}\] where \(s_{o}\), \(s\) are the solubilities of nonelectrolyte in pure water and saline solution, respectively, \(K_{s}\) the Sechenov parameter (an empirical proportionality constant), and \(I_{s}\) the ionic strength of the saline solution.

name: Sieverts’ law
definition: Solubility of a diatomic gas in a molten metal is proportional to the square root of the partial pressure.

name: solubility constant
definition: Generalization of solubility product to include, for example, undissociated salt or uncharged cation-anion pair as solute, reaction between solution species and the cation or anion of the solid salt, and gas-solution equilibria.

name: solubilisation
definition: Process by which an agent increases the solubility or the rate of dissolution of a solid or liquid solute.Modified from entry 'micellar solubilization' in.

name: solvent mole fraction
definition: Mole or mass fraction of a solvent in a solution containing \(s\) solute constituents (\(i = 1, 2, \ldots, s\)) and \(p\) solvent constituents (\(i = s + 1, s + 2, \ldots, p\)). For a solvent \(\ce{A}\), \[x_{{\rm{v}},{\ce{A}}} = x_{\ce{A}}/\sum \limits_{i=s+1}^{p} x_{i}\] where \[\sum \limits_{i=1}^{p} x_{i} = \sum \limits_{i=1}^{s} x_{i} + \sum \limits_{i=s+1}^{p} x_{i} = 1\] and analogously for \(w_{{\rm{v}},{\ce{A}}}\), where the first and last summations are over all solvent constituents.

name: solvent volume fraction
definition: For a solvent \(\ce{A}\), volume fraction of \(\ce{A}\) divided by the sum of the volume fractions of solvent in a solution containing both \(s\) solutes (\(i = 1, 2, \ldots, s\)) and \(p\) solvents (\(i = s + 1, s + 2, \ldots, p\)) \[\varphi_{{\rm{v}},{\ce{A}}} = \varphi_{\ce{A}}/\sum \limits_{i=s+1}^{p} \varphi_{i}\] where the summation is over the \(p\) solvent components only.

name: standard amount concentration
definition: Chosen value of amount concentration.

name: synthetic method
definition: Class of experimental procedures for solubility determination in which a solution of known composition is prepared. Two major subclasses are recognized. In the isothermal method, one liquid component is titrated with a second liquid component at constant temperature until persistent turbidity is observed (i.e., to the cloud point). In the polythermal method, a mixture of known composition is heated above its solution temperature and monitored visually during cooling until turbidity (the cloud point) is observed.

name: ternary diagram
definition: Triangular plot (usually an equilateral or right-angled triangle) whose vertices represent the pure components of a ternary system at constant temperature and pressure. Any point within the triangle represents the composition in terms of the two independent mole (or mass) fractions. Lines parallel to the sides of the triangle represent constant proportions of the respective components (isopleths).

name: ternary system
definition: System containing three components.

name: tie-line
definition: Straight line connecting compositions of independent coexisting phases in equilibrium on a phase diagram.

name: unary system
definition: System containing one component.

name: unsaturated solution
definition: Solution that has a lower proportion of a solute than one that is in equilibrium with undissolved solute at specified values of temperature and pressure.

name: unsaturation
definition: State of an unsaturated solution.

name: wet residue method
definition: Method for determining composition of a solid phase in a ternary system at constant temperature and pressure by analysis of the total mixture of solid and liquid in equilibrium.

name: Ising model
definition: Theory of coexistence curves or other discontinuities in the properties of phases (such as order-disorder or magnetic transitions) in binary systems, based on a one-, two-, or three-dimensional statistical mechanical nearest-neighbor lattice theory.

name: Jänecke coordinates
definition: Coordinates used mainly in representation of multicomponent phase diagrams that distinguish solutes and a single solvent. The mole or mass fractions of the \(s\) solutes are chosen as the primary composition variables and the mole or mass fraction of solvent as a secondary variable, so that the solute amount (mass) fractions may be represented, for example, in ternary and quaternary systems, as linear (ternary) or planar triangular or square planar (quaternary) diagrams, with the solvent amount or mass fraction along an axis perpendicular to the chosen diagram of solute variables. Quantitatively, \[x_{{\rm{s}},{\ce{B}}} = x_{\ce{B}}/\sum \limits_{i=1}^{s}x_{i}\] where the summation is over the \(s\) solute substances. Note that \(\sum \limits_{i=1}^{s}x_{{\rm{s}},{\ce{B}}} = 1\).

name: Kuenen coefficient
definition: Volume \(V^{\rm{g}}\) of an amount \(n_{\ce{B}}^{\rm{l}}\) of a dissolved gas at a given standard temperature \(T^{^⦵\!}\) (usually \(\pu{273.15 K}\)) and given standard pressure \(p^{_{^⦵\!}}\) (\(\pu{1 bar} = \pu{0.1 MPa}\) or, in older literature, \(\pu{1 atm}\)) divided by the mass \(m^{\rm{l}}\) of the dissolving liquid containing an amount $n_{\ce{A}}$ of solvent at temperature $T$ and the given pressure \(p^{_{^⦵\!}}\).

name: mass percent
definition: Deprecated term that includes both a quantity and a unit. Replace by mass fraction expressed as percent.

name: Ostwald coefficient
definition: Volume \(V^{\rm{g}}\) of an amount \(n_{\ce{B}}^{\rm{l}}\) of a dissolved gas calculated at given temperature \(T\) and pressure \(p\) divided by the volume of the dissolving liquid of volume \(V^{\rm{l}}\) and containing an amount \(n_{\ce{A}}\) of solvent at the same temperature \(T\) and pressure \(p\).

name: acyclic diene metathesis polymerisation
definition: Metathesis polymerization of an acylic diene monomer.

name: apparent rate constant of polymerisation
definition: Measured rate of polymerization divided by the concentration of the reactant (if there is only one) or the product of concentrations of the presumed reactants.

name: auto-acceleration
definition: Increase in the rate of polymerization with increasing conversion of the reactant(s).

name: azeotropic copolymerisation
definition: Binary copolymerization in which the two monomer reactivity ratios, \(r_{12}\) and \(r_{21}\) are not both equal to unity yet the copolymerization forms a copolymer with its molar ratio of monomer units equal to the molar ratio of monomers in the monomer feed.

name: backbiting
definition: Chain transfer from an active center on a macromolecule to another part of the same macromolecule.

name: binary copolymerisation
definition: Copolymerization involving two species of monomer.

name: bulk polymerisation
definition: Polymerization of an undiluted liquid monomer.

name: ceiling temperature
definition: Temperature above which, in a given chain polymerization, polymer of high molar mass is not formed.

name: chain copolymerisation
definition: Chain polymerization in which a copolymer is formed.

name: chain depropagation
definition: Chemical reaction that results in the formation of a monomer molecule at an active center on the terminal unit of a chain carrier and decreases the degree of polymerization of the chain carrier by one.

name: chain-end reactivity ratio
definition: In a binary copolymerization, the ratio of two rate constants defining the relative activity of an active center on a given type of terminal unit of a chain carrier toward one type of monomer, in the two cases where the penultimate unit of the chain carrier is identical to and different from the terminal unit.

name: chain-transfer constant
definition: In a homopolymerization, rate constant for chain transfer, \(k_{\rm{tr}}\), divided by the rate constant for chain propagation, \(k_{\rm{p}}\), i.e., \(C_{\rm{tr}} = k_{\rm{tr}}/k_{\rm{p}}\).

name: comonomer
definition: Monomer used in copolymerization.

name: copolymerisation composition equation
definition: Equation relating the instantaneous composition of a binary copolymer to the monomer reactivity ratios and the ratio of instantaneous monomer concentrations.

name: coupling reaction
definition: Linking of two macromolecules through chemical reaction.

name: cross-propagation
definition: Propagation reaction in a copolymerization in which a chain carrier, bearing at its active end a monomer unit of one kind, reacts with a monomer molecule of another kind.

name: cross-termination
definition: Termination reaction in a copolymerization between two chain carriers with different chemical structures.

name: dead-end polymerisation
definition: Radical polymerization that stops, as a consequence of the depletion of the initiator, before the monomer has reacted fully.

name: degradative chain transfer
definition: Chain transfer reaction that generates a new chain carrier of much lower reactivity than that of the original chain carrier.

name: diffusion-controlled termination
definition: Chain termination in a chain polymerization in which the rate-determining step is a diffusion process.

name: end-capping
definition: Reaction in which end-groups of a desired structure are intentionally formed.

name: enthalpy of polymerisation
definition: Change of enthalpy, in a chain polymerization forming a homopolymer, associated with the conversion of one mole of monomer into polymer under isobaric and isothermal conditions.

name: entropy of polymerisation
definition: Change of entropy, in a chain polymerization forming a homopolymer, associated with the conversion of one mole of monomer into polymer under isobaric and isothermal conditions.

name: floor temperature
definition: Temperature below which, in a given chain polymerization, polymer of high molar mass is not formed.

name: free ion
definition: Ion whose behavior is independent of the influence of a counterion.

name: heat of polymerisation
definition: Heat absorbed or given off from the conversion of a specified amount of monomer into polymer.

name: homopropagation
definition: Addition of a monomer to a chain carrier bearing a terminal group derived from the same monomer species.

name: ideal binary copolymerisation
definition: Binary copolymerization in which the relative rates of incorporation of the two types of monomer into the copolymer are independent of the nature of the monomer unit at the end of a propagating chain.

name: ideal copolymerisation
definition: Copolymerization in which all types of propagating species show the same relative reactivity toward the monomers present.

name: interfacial polycondensation
