definition: Polycondensation involving two monomers separately dissolved in immiscible solvents, forming a twophase system, with polycondensation taking place at (or near) an interface between the two phases.

name: intermolecular chain transfer
definition: Chain transfer from an active center on a macromolecule to a different macromolecule.

name: kinetic-chain length
definition: In a chain polymerization, the rate of chain propagation divided by the sum of the rates of all of the chain-termination processes.

name: monomer reactivity ratios
definition: In binary copolymerization, (a) the ratio (\(r_{12}\)) of the rate constant (\(k_{11}\)) for the homopropagation of monomer \(\rm{M}_{1}\) to the rate constant (\(k_{12}\)) for the cross-propagation of the chain carrier \(\ldots -{\rm{m}}_{1}^{\ast}\) with the monomer \(\rm{M}_{2}\) and (b) the ratio (\(r_{21}\)) of the rate constant (\(k_{22}\)) for the homopropagation of monomer \(\rm{M}_{2}\) to the rate constant for the cross-propagation (\(k_{21}\)) of the chain carrier \(\ldots -{\rm{m}}_{2}^{\ast}\) with monomer \(\rm{M}_{1}\). Thus, \(r_{12} = k_{11}/k_{12}, r_{21} = k_{22}/k_{21}\).

name: monomer reactivity scale
definition: Relative scale defined by the values of the rate constants for the addition of monomers to a reference active center.

name: patterns of reactivity scheme
definition: Method for the prediction of monomer reactivity ratios in binary copolymerization, based exclusively on experimentally determined parameters.

name: penultimate-unit effect
definition: Phenomenon that the penultimate monomer unit preceding the active center on the terminal unit of an active polymer chain affects the reactivity of that active center.

name: primary-radical termination
definition: Termination reaction involving a radical chain carrier and a primary radical.

name: pulsed-laser polymerisation
definition: Polymerization initiated by successive pulses of laser light.

name: Q-e scheme
definition: Empirical equations expressing the monomer reactivity ratios in a binary radical copolymerization, \(r_{12}\) and \(r_{21}\), in terms of the empirical parameters \(Q\) and \(e\) for the two monomers, namely, \(\rm{Q}_{1}\), \(\rm{Q}_{2}\), \(\rm{e}_{1}\), and \(\rm{e}_{2}\), with\(r_{12} = (Q_{1}/Q_{2})\exp [-{e_{1}}(e_{1} - e_{2})]\) and \(r_{21} = (Q_{2}/Q_{1}) \exp [-{e_{2}}(e_{2} - e_{1})]\)

name: radical reactivity scale
definition: Scale of the values of the rate constants for the reaction of radicals with a reference monomer.

name: rate of polymerisation
definition: Rate of consumption of monomers in a chain polymerization, or the rate of consumption of the functional groups in the reaction mixture of a polycondensation or polyaddition.

name: secondary radical
definition: Radical formed by the rearrangement or fragmentation of a primary radical that is capable of initiating a polymerization.

name: self-initiated polymerisation
definition: Polymerization in which initiating species are formed exclusively from the monomer.

name: solid-state polymerisation
definition: Polymerization of a crystalline monomer.

name: spontaneous termination
definition: Chain termination proceeding as a unimolecular process.

name: topochemical polymerisation
definition: Solid-state polymerization, resulting in the formation of a polymer having essentially the same crystal structure as that of the monomer.

name: transamidation
definition: Interchange reaction involving amide groups.

name: transesterification
definition: Interchange reaction involving ester groups.

name: zwitterionic copolymerisation
definition: Copolymerization that is a zwitterionic polymerization.

name: zwitterionic polymerisation
definition: Chain polymerization in which a growing macromolecule bears two ionic chain carriers of opposite signs, at one or both of its ends.

name: cyclic macromolecule
definition: Macromolecule in which the termini of the backbone are connected to form a ring.

name: main ring
definition: Macrocycle in a bridged polycyclic macromolecule or polycyclic macromolecular portion that contains the subunits of highest seniority.

name: path length
definition: Number of polymer main-chain (backbone) atoms between two subunits.

name: polycyclic macromolecule
definition: Molecule that includes more than one macrocycle, all of which have at least one atom in common with another macrocycle.

name: abiotic degradation
definition: Process in which a substance is converted to simpler products by physical or chemical mechanisms.

name: abortifacient
definition: Substance that causes pregnancy to end prematurely and causes an abortion.

name: abuse
definition: Improper use of drugs or other substances.

name: acaricide
definition: Substance intended to kill mites, ticks, or other Acaridae.

name: acceptable residue level
definition: Acceptable concentration of a residue that has been established for an antibiotic found in human or animal foods.

name: acceptable risk
definition: Probability of suffering disease or injury that is considered to be sufficiently small to be 'negligible'.

name: accepted risk
definition: Probability of suffering disease or injury that is accepted by an individual.

name: accidental exposure
definition: Unintended contact with a substance or change in the physical environment (including, e.g., radiation) resulting from an accident.

name: acid dissociation constant
definition: Equilibrium constant for the following reaction of an acid \(\ce{HB}\): \[\begin{gathered} \ce{HB(aq)  H^{+}(aq) + B^{-}(aq)} \\ K_{\rm{a}} = [\ce{H^{+}}][\ce{B^{-}}]/[\ce{HB}]c^{\rm{o}} \end{gathered}\] where \(c^{\rm{o}} = \pu{1 mol L-1}\) is the standard amount concentration and activity coefficients have been neglected.

name: action level
definition: Concentration of a substance in air, soil, water, or other defined medium at which specified emergency counter-measures, such as the seizure and destruction of contaminated materials, evacuation of the local population or closing down the sources of pollution, are to be taken. Concentration of a pollutant in air, soil, water, or other defined medium at which some kind of preventive action (not necessarily of an emergency nature) is to be taken.

name: active ingredient
definition: Component of a mixture responsible for the biological effects of the mixture.

name: active metabolite
definition: Metabolite causing biological and (or) toxicological effects.

name: acute toxicity test
definition: Study in which organisms are observed during only a short part of the life span and in which there is often only a single exposure to the test agent at the beginning of the study.

name: adaptation
definition: Change in an organism, in response to changing conditions of the environment (specifically chemical), which takes place without any irreversible disruptions of the given biological system and without exceeding normal (homeostatic) capacities of its response. Process by which an organism stabilizes its physiological condition after an environmental change.Note: If this process exceeds the homeostatic range, it becomes pathological and results in symptoms of disease (adverse effects).

name: added risk
definition: Difference between the incidence of an adverse effect in a treated group (of organisms or a group of exposed humans) and a control group (of the same organisms or the spontaneous incidence in humans).

name: adverse event
definition: Occurrence that causes an adverse effect.

name: aerodynamic diameter
definition: Diameter of a spherical particle with relative density equal to unity that has the same settling velocity in air as the particle in question.

name: after-effect of a poison
definition: Ability of a poison to produce a change in an organism after cessation of contact.

name: age sensitivity
definition: Quantitative and qualitative age dependence of an effect.

name: air pollution control system
definition: Network of organizations that monitor air pollution. Group of measures or processes used to minimize or prevent air pollution.

name: albuminuria
definition: Presence of albumin, derived from plasma, in the urine.

name: alkylating agent
definition: Substance that introduces an alkyl substituent into a compound.

name: allometric growth
definition: Regular and systematic pattern of growth such that the mass or size of any organ or part of a body can be expressed in relation to the total mass or size of the entire organism according to the allometric equation: \[Y = b{x^{\alpha}}\] where \(Y\) = mass of the organ, \(x\) = mass of the organism, \(\alpha\) = growth coefficient of the organ, and \(b\) is a constant.

name: allometric scaling
definition: Adjustment of data to allow for change in proportion between an organ or organs and other body parts during the growth of an organism. Adjustment of data to allow for differences and make comparisons between species having dissimilar characteristics (e.g., in size, shape, and metabolism).

name: allometry
definition: Measurement of the rate of growth of a part or parts of an organism relative to the growth of the whole organism.

name: allomone
definition: Semiochemical that is produced by an organism inducing a response in an organism of another species that is favorable to the emitter.

name: analytic study
definition: Study designed to examine associations, commonly putative or hypothesized causal relationships.

name: anaplasia
definition: Loss of normal cell differentiation, a feature characteristic of most malignancies.

name: anthracosis
definition: Form of pneumoconiosis caused by accumulation of anthracite carbon deposits in the lungs due to inhalation of smoke or coal dust.

name: anticoagulant
definition: Substance that prevents blood clotting (e.g., warfarin).

name: antidote
definition: Substance capable of specifically counteracting or reducing the effect of a potentially toxic substance in an organism by a relatively specific chemical or pharmacological action.

name: antihistamine
definition: Substance that blocks or counteracts the action of histamine.

name: antimuscarinic
definition: n., Substance inhibiting or preventing the actions of muscarine and muscarine-like agents (e.g., atropine) on the muscarinic acetylcholine receptors. adj., Inhibiting or preventing the actions of muscarine and muscarine-like agents on the muscarinic acetylcholine receptors.

name: antinicotinic
definition: n., Substance inhibiting or preventing the actions of nicotine and nicotine-like agents (e.g., suxamethonium chloride) on the nicotinic acetylcholine receptors. adj., Inhibiting or preventing the actions of nicotine and nicotine-like agents on the nicotinic acetylcholine receptors.

name: antipyretic
definition: Substance that relieves or reduces fever.

name: aphid
definition: Common name for a harmful plant parasite in the family Aphididae, some species of which are vectors of plant virus diseases.

name: aplasia
definition: Lack of development of an organ or tissue, or of the cellular products from an organ or tissue.

name: arboricide
definition: Substance intended to kill trees and shrubs.

name: area source
definition: Widespread origin of emissions.

name: area under the moment curve
definition: Area between a curve and the abscissa (horizontal axis) in a plot of (concentration \(\times\) time) vs. time.

name: argyria
definition: Pathological condition characterized by gray-bluish or black pigmentation of tissues (such as skin, retina, mucous membranes, internal organs) caused by the accumulation of metallic silver, due to reduction of a silver compound which has entered the organism during (prolonged) administration or exposure.

name: arseniasis
definition: Chronic arsenical poisoning.

name: arteriosclerosis
definition: Hardening and thickening of the walls of the arteries.

name: arthralgia
definition: Pain in a joint.

name: arthropathy
definition: Disease of a joint.

name: arthrosis
definition: Joint or articulation.

name: asbestosis
definition: Form of pneumoconiosis caused by inhalation of asbestos fibers.

name: ascaricide
definition: Substance intended to kill roundworms (Ascaridae).

name: asphyxia
definition: Condition resulting from insufficient intake of oxygen.

name: asphyxiant
definition: Substance that blocks the transport or use of oxygen by living organisms.

name: assimilation
definition: Uptake and incorporation of substances by a living organism.

name: asthenia
definition: Weakness; lack or loss of strength.

name: astringent
definition: adj., Causing contraction, usually locally after topical application. n., Substance causing cells to shrink, thus causing tissue contraction or stoppage of secretions and discharges; such substances may be applied to skin to harden and protect it.

name: atherosclerosis
definition: Pathological condition in which there is thickening, hardening, and loss of elasticity of the walls of blood vessels, characterized by a variable combination of changes of the innermost layer consisting of local accumulation of lipids, complex carbohydrates, blood and blood components, fibrous tissue, and calcium deposits. In addition, the outer layer becomes thickened and there is fatty degeneration of the middle layer.

name: attractant
definition: Substance that attracts animals.

name: autophagosome
definition: Membrane-bound body (secondary lysosome) in which parts of the cell are digested.

name: autoxidation
definition: Reaction with dioxygen at moderate temperatures.

name: autoxidation
definition: Apparently spontaneous, usually slow reaction of foodstuff components with dioxygen in an aerobic environment at moderate temperatures.

name: auxotroph
definition: Organism unable to synthesize an organic molecule which is required for its growth: When the compound is given to the organism with the other nutrients it requires, growth of the organism may occur.

name: avicide
definition: Substance intended to kill birds.

name: back-mutation
definition: Process that reverses the effect of a mutation which had inactivated a gene; thus, it restores the wild phenotype.

name: bacterial artificial chromosome
definition: DNA vector into which large DNA fragments can be inserted and cloned in a bacterial host.

name: bactericide
definition: Substance intended to kill bacteria.

name: bagassosis
definition: Lung disease caused by the inhalation of dust from sugar-cane residues.

name: basal lamina
definition: Triple-layered structure on which epithelium sits: It consists of an electron-dense layer (lamina densa) between two electron-transparent layers (lamina lucida). The lamina densa is composed of type IV collagen, and the lamina lucida contains the glycoprotein laminin.

name: Bateman function
definition: Equation expressing the build up and decay in concentration of a substance (usually in plasma) based on first-order uptake and elimination in a one-compartment model, having the form \[C = [fDk_{\rm{a}}/V(k_{\rm{a}} - k_{\rm{e}})] [\exp(-k_{\rm{e}}t) - \exp(-k_{\rm{a}}t)] \]where \(C\) is the concentration and \(D\) the dose of the substance, \(f\) the fraction absorbed, and \(V\) the volume of distribution. \(k_{\rm{a}}\) and \(k_{\rm{e}}\) are the first-order rate constants of uptake and elimination, respectively, and \(t\) is time.

name: benchmark guidance value
definition: Biological monitoring guidance value set at the \(90^{\rm{th}}\) percentile of available biological monitoring results collected from a representative sample of workplaces with good occupational hygiene practices.

name: benchmark response
definition: Response, expressed as an excess of background, at which a benchmark dose or benchmark concentration is set.

name: benign
definition: Of a disease, producing no persisting harmful effects. Tumor that does not invade other tissues (see metastasis ), having lost growth control but not positional control.Note: Such a tumor is not carcinogenic but may cause mechanical damage to adjacent tissues.

name: beryllium disease
definition: Serious and usually permanent lung damage resulting from chronic inhalation of beryllium.

name: biased sample
definition: Any sample that is not a random sample.

name: bilirubin
definition: Orange-yellow pigment, a breakdown product of heme-containing proteins (hemoglobin, myoglobin, cytochromes), which circulates in the blood plasma bound to albumin or as water-soluble glucuronide conjugates, and is excreted in the bile by the liver.

name: bioaccumulation potential
definition: Ability of living organisms to concentrate a substance obtained either directly from the environment or indirectly through its food.

name: biochemical mechanism
definition: Reaction or series of reactions, usually enzyme-catalyzed, associated with a specific physiological event in a living organism.

name: bioelimination
definition: Removal, usually from the aqueous phase, of a test substance in the presence of living organisms by biological processes supplemented by physicochemical reactions.

name: bioinactivation
definition: Metabolic conversion of a xenobiotic to a less toxic derivative.

name: biokinetics
definition: Science of the movements involved in the distribution of substances.

name: biological cycle
definition: Complete circulatory process through which a substance passes in the biosphere. It may involve transport through the various media (air, water, soil), followed by environmental transformation, and carriage through various ecosystems.

name: biological preparation
definition: Compound derived from living organisms and their products for use in medicine or as a pesticide, etc.

name: biological specimen
definition: Organ, tissue (including blood), secretion, or excretion product taken from an organism as a sample reflecting the state of the whole organism. Organism taken as a sample reflecting the state of a population or their environment.

name: biological warfare
definition: Military operations using any organism (bacteria, virus, or other disease-causing organism) or toxin found in nature, to kill, injure, or incapacitate human beings, animals, or plants.

name: biopsy
definition: Excision of a small piece of living tissue for microscopic or biochemical examination; usually performed to establish a diagnosis.

name: biostatic
definition: Adjective applied to a substance that arrests the growth or multiplication of living organisms.

name: biota
definition: All living organisms as a totality.

name: 2,3-bis(sulfanyl)propan-1-ol
definition: Metal chelator that has been used in the treatment of arsenic, antimony, gold, mercury, and lead poisoning.

name: bolus
definition: Single dose of a substance, originally a large pill. Dose of a substance administered by a single rapid intravenous injection. Concentrated mass of food ready to be swallowed.

name: botanical pesticide
definition: Substance with activity against pests, that is produced naturally within a plant and may act as a defense against predators.

name: botulism
definition: Acute food poisoning caused by botulinum toxin produced in food by the bacterium Clostridium botulinum and characterized by muscle weakness and paralysis; disturbances of vision, swallowing, and speech; and a high mortality rate.

name: brady-
definition: Prefix meaning slow as in bradycardia or bradypnoea.

name: bradypnoea
definition: Abnormally slow breathing.

name: breathing zone
definition: Space within a radius of \(\pu{0.5 m}\) from a person’s face.

name: bronchoconstriction
definition: Narrowing of the air passages through the bronchi of the lungs.

name: bronchodilation
definition: Expansion of the air passages through the bronchi of the lungs.

name: bronchospasm
definition: Intermittent violent contraction of the air passages of the lungs.

name: builder
definition: Material that enhances or maintains the cleaning efficiency of a surfactant, in a detergent, principally by inactivating water hardness; complex phosphates (especially sodium tripolyphosphate, i.e., pentasodium triphosphate), sodium carbonate, and sodium silicate are the builders most commonly used.

name: byssinosis
definition: Pneumoconiosis caused by inhalation of dust and associated microbial contaminants and observed in cotton, flax, and hemp workers.

name: bystander exposure
definition: Liability of members of the general public to come in contact with substances arising from operations or processes carried out by other individuals in their vicinity.

name: cacosmia
definition: Imagined perception of vile odors, including coprosmia (smelling feces) and necrosmia (the smell of death).

name: calcification
definition: Form of mineralization in which organic tissue becomes hardened by deposition of calcium salts within its substance.

name: carbonylhemoglobin
definition: Compound that is formed between carbon monoxide and hemoglobin in the blood of animals and humans and is incapable of transporting oxygen.

name: carcinogenicity test
definition: Long-term (chronic) test designed to detect any possible carcinogenic effect of a test substance.

name: cardiotoxic
definition: Chemically harmful to the cells of the heart.

name: carrier-linked prodrug
definition: Compound that contains a temporary linkage between a given active substance and a transient carrier group, the latter producing improved physicochemical or pharmacokinetic properties and easily removable in vivo.

name: carrier substance
definition: Substance that binds to another substance and transfers it from one site to another.

name: case cohort study
definition: Variant of the case control study in which the controls are drawn from the same cohort as the cases but are identified before the cases develop; some of the controls may later become cases.

name: case control study
definition: Study that starts with the identification of persons with the disease (or other outcome variable) of interest, and a suitable control (comparison, reference) group of persons without the disease. The relationship of an attribute to the disease is examined by comparing the diseased and non-diseased with regard to how frequently the attribute is present or, if quantitative, the levels of the attribute, in the two groups.
synonyms: case comparison study|case compeer study|case history study|case referent study|retrospective study

name: catatonia
definition: Behavior marked by excessive and sometimes violent motor activity and excitement, or by generalized inhibition or stupor, that may occur in schizophrenia, mood disorders, or organic brain syndromes.

name: cell cycle
definition: Regulated biochemical steps that cells go through involving DNA replication and cell division, usually depicted as a sequential cyclical series of events.

name: cell-mediated hypersensitivity
definition: State in which an individual reacts with allergic effects caused by the reaction of antigen-specific T-lymphocytes following exposure to a certain substance (allergen) after having been exposed previously to the same substance or chemical group.

name: cell proliferation
definition: Rapid increase in cell number.

name: cell strain
definition: Cells having specific properties or markers derived from a primary culture or cell line.

name: censored data
definition: Sample observations for which the complete distribution is not known.

name: certified reference material
definition: Reference material, accompanied by documentation issued by an authoritative body and referring to valid procedures used to obtain a specified property value with uncertainty and traceability.

name: chain of custody
definition: Sequence of responsibility for a substance from the manufacturer to the distributor, to the user, or to the person(s) ultimately responsible for waste disposal. This term is also used in controlled transmission of samples from collection to analysis, especially of samples of materials used for medico-legal or forensic purposes.

name: chelation therapy
definition: Treatment with a chelating agent to enhance the elimination or reduce the toxicity of a metal ion.

name: chemesthesis
definition: Sensations that arise when chemical compounds activate receptor mechanisms for other effectors, such as light, pain, pressure, and heat, in the eye, skin, nose, mouth, and throat; for example, the burning feeling from chili pepper, the cooling from the menthol in mouthwash, and the stinging feeling of carbonation.

name: chemical conversion
definition: Change from one chemical species to another.

name: chemical safety
definition: Practical certainty that there will be no exposure of organisms to toxic amounts of any substance or group of substances: This implies attaining an acceptably low risk of exposure to potentially toxic substances.

name: chemical warfare
definition: Military operations using the toxic properties of chemical agents to kill, injure, or incapacitate human beings, animals, or plants.

name: chemophobia
definition: Irrational fear of chemicals.

name: chemosis
definition: Chemically induced swelling around the eye caused by edema of the conjunctiva.

name: chemosteriliser
definition: Substance used to sterilize mites, insects, rodents, or other animals.

name: cholinesterase inhibitor
definition: Substance that inhibits the action of acetylcholinesterase (EC 3.1.1.7) and related enzymes which catalyze the hydrolysis of choline esters: Such a substance causes hyperactivity in parasympathetic nerves.

name: chromatin
definition: Stainable complex of DNA and proteins present in the nucleus of a eukaryotic cell.

name: chromosomal aberration
definition: Abnormality of chromosome number or structure.

name: chronic toxicity test
definition: Study in which organisms are observed during the greater part of the life span and in which exposure to the test agent takes place over the whole observation time or a substantial part thereof.

name: chronotoxicology
definition: Study of the influence of biological rhythms on the toxicity of substances or of the influence of a toxicant on biological rhythms.

name: ciguateratoxin poisoning
definition: Serious illness caused by eating carnivorous fish such as snappers and barracuda that have become contaminated by toxins produced by the microalga, Gambierdiscus toxicus; gastrointestinal symptoms may accompany a wide variety of neurological symptoms, including ataxia, vertigo, flaccid paralysis, respiratory arrest, and reversed perception of hot and cold; the neurological symptoms may persist for many years.

name: circadian
definition: Relating to or exhibiting an approximately \(\pu{24\!\mbox{-}h}\) periodicity.

name: circulation of substances
definition: Movement of xenobiotic substances in the environment with air flow, river current, sediment flow, etc.

name: cirrhosis
definition: Liver disease defined by histological examination and characterized by increased fibrous tissue, abnormal morphological and physiological changes such as loss of functional liver cells, and increased resistance to blood flow through the liver (portal hypertension). Chronic interstitial inflammation and fibrosis of an organ.

name: cirrhotic
definition: Describing an organ showing cirrhosis.

name: clastogenesis
definition: Formation (or generation) of chromosomal breaks and (or) consequent gain, loss, or rearrangement of pieces of chromosomes.

name: clinical toxicology
definition: Scientific study involving research, education, prevention, and treatment of diseases caused by substances such as drugs and toxins.

name: clonic
definition: Pertaining to alternate muscular contraction and relaxation in rapid succession.

name: cluster sampling
definition: A method of sampling in which the population is divided into aggregates (or clusters) of items bound together in a certain manner. A sample of these clusters is taken at random, and all the items which constitute them are included in the sample. A sampling method in which each unit selected is a group of persons (all persons in a city block, a family, etc.) rather than an individual.

name: cocarcinogen
definition: Chemical, physical, or biological factor that intensifies the effect of a carcinogen.

name: Codex Alimentarius
definition: Collection of internationally adopted food standards drawn up by the Codex Alimentarius Commission, the principal body implementing the joint FAO/WHO Food Standards Program.

name: cohort
definition: Component of the population born during a particular period and identified by period of birth so that its characteristics (such as causes of death and numbers still living) can be ascertained as it enters successive time and age periods. The term 'cohort' has broadened to describe any designated group of persons followed or traced over a period of time, as in the term cohort study (prospective study).

name: cohort analysis
definition: Tabulation and analysis of morbidity or mortality rates in relationship to the ages of a specific group of people (cohort), identified by their birth period, and followed as they pass through different ages during part or all of their life span. In certain circumstances such as studies of migrant populations, cohort analysis may be performed according to duration of residence in a country rather than year of birth, in order to relate health or mortality experience to duration of exposure.

name: cohort study
definition: Analytic study in epidemiology in which subsets of a defined population can be identified who are, have been, or in the future may be exposed or not exposed, or exposed in different degrees, to a factor or factors hypothesized to influence the probability of occurrence of a given disease or other outcome. The main feature of the method is observation of a large population for a prolonged period (years), with comparison of incidence rates of the given disease in groups that differ in exposure levels.
synonyms: concurrent study|follow-up study|incidence study|longitudinal study|prospective study

name: combined effect of poisons
definition: Simultaneous or successive effect of two or more poisons on the organism by the same route of exposure.

name: comet assay
definition: Means of measuring DNA damage, particularly DNA strand breaks. A cell is embedded in agar and exposed to a DNA-damaging agent. The cell is then permeabilized with a detergent, and an electric field is applied. If the cell’s genomic DNA has been broken into small fragments, these fragments move out of the cell by electrophoresis and form a streak or 'tail' leading away from the cell which looks like a comet.

name: comparative genomics
definition: Study of the relationship of genome structure and function across different biological species.

name: compartmentalise
definition: Separate into compartments.

name: competent authority
definition: In the context of European Community Council Directive 79/831/EEC, the Sixth Amendment to the European Community Council Directive 67/548/EEC relating to the Classification, Packaging and Labeling of Dangerous Substances, official government organization or group receiving and evaluating notifications of new substances.

name: competent bacteria
definition: Culture of bacteria (or yeast) treated in such a way that their ability to take up DNA molecules without transduction or conjugation has been enhanced.

name: complete mineralisation
definition: Complete breakdown of a complex organic compound to carbon dioxide, water, oxides, and oxidative inorganic products such as nitrate or sulfate.

name: comprehensive effect of poisons
definition: Simultaneous or successive effect made on an organism by poisons entering from different media, air, water, or food or through the skin.

name: computational toxicology
definition: Application of mathematical and computer models to predict adverse effects and to better understand the mechanism(s) through which a given chemical causes harm.

name: concentration–effect curve
definition: Graph of the relation between exposure concentration and the magnitude of the resultant biological change.

name: concentration–effect relationship
definition: Association between exposure concentration and the resultant magnitude of the continuously graded change produced, either in an individual or in a population.

name: concurrent validity
definition: Measurement and its criterion refer to the same point in time.

name: confounding
definition: Situation in which the effects of two processes are not distinguishable from one another: The distortion of the apparent effect of an exposure on risk brought about by the association of other factors which can influence the outcome. Relationship between the effects of two or more causal factors as observed in a set of data, such that it is not logically possible to separate the contribution which any single causal factor has made to an effect. Situation in which a measure of the effect of an exposure on risk is distorted because of the association of exposure with other factor(s) which influence the outcome under study.

name: confounding variable
definition: Changing factor that can cause or prevent the outcome of interest, is not an intermediate variable, and is associated with the factor under investigation.

name: conjunctiva
definition: Mucous membrane that covers the eyeball and lines the under-surface of the eyelid.

name: conjunctivitis
definition: Inflammation of the conjunctiva.

name: conservative assessment of risk
definition: Assessment of risk that assumes the worst possible case scenario and therefore gives the highest possible value for risk: Risk management decisions based on this value will maximize safety.

name: construct validity
definition: Extent to which a measurement corresponds to theoretical concepts (constructs) concerning the phenomenon under study; for example, if on theoretical grounds, the phenomenon should change with age, a measurement with construct validity would reflect such a change.

name: contact poison
definition: Chemical that injures the target organism through physical contact and skin absorption rather than through ingestion or inhalation. Pesticide (herbicide) that causes injury to only the plant tissue to which it is applied or which is not appreciably translocated within plants.

name: containment
definition: Process by which possible release, discharge, or spill of a toxic substance during normal use or after an accident is prevented by appropriate action.

name: content validity
definition: Extent to which the measurement incorporates the domain of the phenomenon under study; for example, a measurement of functional health status should embrace activities of daily living, occupational, family, and social functioning, etc.

name: contraindication
definition: Any condition that renders some particular line of treatment improper or undesirable.

name: control group
definition: Selected subjects of study, identified as a rule before a study is done, which comprises humans, animals, or other species who do not have the disease, intervention, procedure, or whatever is being studied, but in all other respects are as nearly identical to the test group as possible.

name: matched control
definition: Control (individual or group or case) selected to be similar to a study individual or group, or case, in specific characteristics: some commonly used matching variables are age, sex, race, and socioeconomic status.

name: core grade
definition: Quality rating, based on standard evaluation criteria established by the U.S. Office of Pesticide Programs regulatory agencies, given to toxicological studies after submission by registrants.

name: count mean diameter
definition: Mean of the diameters of all particles in a population.

name: count median diameter
definition: Calculated diameter in a population of particles in a gas or liquid phase above which there are as many particles with larger diameters as there are particles below it with smaller diameters.

name: crepitations
definition: Abnormal respiratory sounds heard on auscultation of the chest, produced by passage of air through passages which contain secretion or exudate or which are constricted by spasm or a thickening of their walls.

name: criterion
definition: Validated set of data used as a basis for judgment.

name: criterion validity
definition: Extent to which the measurement correlates with an external criterion of the phenomenon under study.

name: critical concentration
definition: Concentration of a substance at and above which adverse functional changes, reversible or irreversible, occur in a cell or an organ.

name: critical dose
definition: Dose of a substance at and above which adverse functional changes, reversible or irreversible, occur in a cell or an organ.

name: critical effect
definition: For deterministic effects, the first adverse effect that appears when the threshold (critical) concentration or dose is reached in the critical organ: Adverse effects with no defined threshold concentration are regarded as critical.

name: critical end-point
definition: Toxic effect used by the USEPA as the basis for a reference dose.

name: critical group
definition: Part of a target population most in need of protection because it is most susceptible to a given toxicant.

name: critical organ
definition: Organ that first attains the critical concentration of a substance and exhibits the critical effect under specified circumstances of exposure and for a given population.

name: critical organ concentration
definition: Mean concentration of a substance in the critical organ at the time the substance reaches its critical concentration in the most sensitive type of cell in the organ.

name: cross-sectional study
definition: Study that examines the relationship between diseases (or other health-related characteristics) and other variables of interest as they exist in a defined population at one particular time.

name: cumulative death rate
definition: Proportion of a defined group that dies within the specified time period (e.g., month, year).

name: cumulative effect
definition: Overall change that occurs after repeated doses of a substance or radiation.

name: cumulative incidence
definition: Number or proportion of individuals in a group who experience the onset of a health-related event during a specified time interval.

name: cumulative incidence rate
definition: Proportion of the cumulative incidence to the total population.

name: cumulative incidence ratio
definition: Value obtained by dividing the cumulative incidence rate in the exposed population by the cumulative incidence rate in the unexposed population.

name: cumulative median lethal dose
definition: Estimate of the total administered amount of a substance that is associated with the death of half a population of animals when the substance is administered repeatedly in doses which are generally fractions of the median lethal dose.

name: cumulative risk
definition: Probability of a common harmful effect associated with concurrent exposure by all relevant pathways and routes of exposure to a group of substances that share a common chemical mechanism of toxicity. Total probability of a harmful effect over time.

name: cyanotoxin
definition: Toxin produced by Cyanobacteria, sometimes called blue–green algae.

name: cyclooxygenase specific inhibitors
definition: Substances, such as aspirin and ibuprofen, that block the activity of cyclooxygenase (COX), an enzyme that is responsible for the formation of prostanoids (including prostaglandins, prostacyclin, and thromboxane); inhibition of COX can provide relief from inflammation and pain.

name: cytochrome P420
definition: Inactive derivative of cytochrome P450 found in microsomal preparations.

name: cytochrome P448
definition: Obsolete term for cytochrome P450 I, A1, and A2, one of the major families of the cytochromes P450 hemoproteins.

name: cytoplasm
definition: Fundamental substance or matrix of the cell (within the plasma membrane) which surrounds the nucleus, endoplasmic reticulum, mitochondria, and other organelles.

name: decipol
definition: Unit of perceived air quality.

name: decompensation
definition: Explicit pathophysiological changes following compensation for adverse effects.

name: decontamination
definition: Process of rendering harmless (by neutralization, elimination, removal, etc.) a potentially toxic substance in the natural environment, laboratory areas, the workplace, other indoor areas, clothes, food, water, sewage, etc.

name: dehydrogenase
definition: Enzyme that catalyzes oxidation of compounds by removing hydrogen.

name: delayed effect
definition: Consequence occurring after a latent period following the end of exposure to a toxic substance or other harmful environmental factor.

name: dental fluorosis
definition: Tooth enamel malformations due to excessive fluoride exposure during dental development.

name: deoxyribonucleic acid cloning
definition: Replication of DNA sequences ligated into a suitable vector in an appropriate host organism.

name: deoxyribonucleic acid repair
definition: Restoration of the molecular structure of DNA after it has been damaged by a chemical or physical agent: This may involve direct DNA damage reversal, base excision repair, nucleotide excision repair, mismatch repair, or double-strand break repair

name: dependence
definition: A psychic craving for a drug or other substance that may or may not be accompanied by a physical dependency. Reliance on a drug or other substance to maintain health.

name: depilatory
definition: Substance causing loss of hair.

name: dermal
definition: Pertaining to the skin.

name: dermal irritation
definition: Skin reaction resulting from a single or multiple exposure to a physical or chemical entity at the same site, characterized by the presence of inflammation; it may result in cell death.

name: descriptive epidemiology
definition: Study of the occurrence of disease or other health-related characteristics in populations, including general observations concerning the relationship of disease to basic characteristics such as age, sex, race, occupation, and social class; it may also be concerned with geographic location. The major characteristics in descriptive epidemiology can be classified under the headings: individuals, time, and place.

name: desquamation
definition: Shedding of an outer layer of skin in scales or shreds.

name: detriment
definition: Estimated measure of the expected harm or loss associated with an adverse event, usually in a manner chosen to facilitate meaningful addition over different events. It is generally the integrated product of arbitrary values of risk and hazard and is often expressed in terms such as costs in U.S. dollars, loss in expected years of life or loss in productivity, and is needed for numerical exercises such as cost-benefit analysis.

name: developmental toxicity
definition: Adverse effects on the developing organism (including structural abnormality, altered growth, or functional deficiency or death) resulting from exposure through conception, gestation (including organogenesis), and postnatally up to the time of sexual maturation.

name: diaphoresis
definition: Profuse perspiration.

name: discharge standard
definition: Maximum amount of a pollutant released from a given source to a specified medium which is acceptable under specified circumstances.

name: discordance
definition: Any difference in a character between individuals due to genetic differences such as may occur in dizygotic twins, or between matched pairs in a case cohort study.

name: disease
definition: Literally, dis-ease, lack of ease; pathological condition that presents a group of symptoms peculiar to it and which establishes the condition as an abnormal entity different from other normal or pathological body states.

name: disposition
definition: Natural tendency shown by an individual or group of individuals, including any tendency to acquisition of specific diseases, often due to hereditary factors. Total of the processes of absorption of a chemical into the circulatory systems, distribution throughout the body, biotransformation, and excretion.

name: dissipation
definition: Reduction in the amount of a pesticide or other compound that has been applied to plants, soil, etc. (used when it is not clear whether this is by mineralization degradation, binding, or leaching).

name: distribution volume
definition: Theoretical volume of a body compartment throughout which a substance is calculated to be distributed.

name: diuresis
definition: Excretion of urine, especially in excess.

name: diuretic
definition: Agent that increases urine production.

name: dominant half life
definition: Half life of a fraction of a substance in a specific organ or compartment if it defines approximately the overall clearance rate for that substance at a specific time point.

name: dominant lethal mutation
definition: Genetic change occurring in a germ cell that does not cause dysfunction of the gamete but which is lethal to the fertilized egg or developing embryo which develops from it.

name: duplicate portion sampling method
definition: Study in which test persons consume their ordinary diet but, for each meal, they prepare for subsequent analysis a duplicate portion of all food as prepared, served, and consumed.

name: duplicate samples
definition: Two samples taken under the same or comparable conditions.

name: dysfunction
definition: Abnormal, impaired, or incomplete functioning of an organism, organ, tissue, or cell.

name: ectoparasiticide
definition: Substance intended to kill parasites living on the exterior of the host.

name: elimination half life
definition: Period taken for the plasma concentration of a substance to decrease by half.

name: eliminator
definition: Substance that contributes to the elimination of a poison from an organism.

name: embryotoxicity
definition: Production by a substance of toxic effects in progeny in the first period of pregnancy between conception and the fetal stage. Any toxic effect on the conceptus as a result of prenatal exposure during the embryonic stages of development: These effects may include malformations and variations, malfunctions, altered growth, prenatal death, and altered postnatal function.

name: embryotropic effect
definition: Change in the embryo and the regulation of its development.

name: emission and exposure control
definition: Technical and administrative procedures and specifications applied for the monitoring, reduction, or elimination of emissions from a source or exposure to a target.

name: endocon
definition: Portion of a conjugated metabolite that is derived from a natural product (such as a sugar, amino acid, or other organic acid) of the metabolizing organism.

name: endoplasmic reticulum
definition: Intracellular complex of membranes in which proteins and lipids, as well as molecules for export, are synthesized and in which the biotransformation reactions of the monooxygenase enzyme systems occur.

name: endothelial
definition: Pertaining to the layer of flat cells lining the inner surface of blood and lymphatic vessels, and the surface lining of serous and synovial membranes.

name: enteritis
definition: Intestinal inflammation.

name: enterohepatic circulation
definition: Cyclical process involving intestinal reabsorption of a substance that has been excreted through the bile, followed by transfer back to the liver, making it available for biliary excretion again.

name: environment
definition: Aggregate, at a given moment, of all external conditions and influences to which a system under study is subjected.

name: environmental damage
definition: Adverse effects to the natural environment.

name: environmental exposure level
definition: Level (concentration or amount or a time integral of either) of a substance to which an organism or other component of the environment is exposed in its natural surroundings.

name: environmental health
definition: Human welfare and its influence by the environment, including technical and administrative measures for improving the human environment from a health point of view.

name: environmental health impact assessment
definition: Estimate of the adverse effects to health or risks likely to follow from a proposed or expected environmental change or development.

name: environmental health criteria documents
definition: Critical publications of IPCS containing reviews of methodologies and existing knowledge—expressed, if possible, in quantitative terms—of selected substances (or groups of substances) on identifiable, immediate, and long-term effects on human health and welfare.

name: environmental hygiene
definition: Practical control measures used to improve the basic environmental conditions affecting human health, for example, clean water supply, human and animal waste disposal, protection of food from biological contamination, and housing conditions, all of which are concerned with the quality of the human environment.

name: environmental medicine
definition: Specialty devoted to the prevention and management of environmentally induced injury, illness, and disability, and the promotion of the health of individuals, families, and communities by ensuring a healthy environment.

name: environmental protection
definition: Actions taken to prevent or minimize adverse effects to the natural environment. Complex of measures including monitoring of environmental pollution, development and practice of environmental protection principles (legal, technical, and hygienic), including risk assessment, risk management, and risk communication.

name: epigastric
definition: Pertaining to the upper-middle region of the abdomen.

name: epileptiform
definition: Occurring in severe or sudden spasms, as in convulsion or epilepsy.

name: epithelioma
definition: Any tumor derived from epithelium.

name: eschar
definition: Slough or dry scab on an area of skin that has been burnt.

name: estimated daily intake
definition: Prediction of the daily intake of a residue of a potentially harmful agent based on the most realistic estimation of the residue levels in food and the best available food consumption data for a specific population: Residue levels are estimated taking into account known uses of the agent, the range of contaminated commodities, the proportion of a commodity treated, and the quantity of home-grown or imported commodities.

name: estimated environmental concentration
definition: Predicted concentration of a substance, typically a pesticide, within an environmental compartment based on estimates of quantities released, discharge patterns, and inherent disposition of the substance (fate and distribution) as well as the nature of the specific receiving ecosystems.

name: estimated exposure concentration
definition: Measured or calculated amount or mass concentration of a substance to which an organism is likely to be exposed, considering exposure by all sources and routes.

name: estimated exposure dose
definition: Measured or calculated dose of a substance to which an organism is likely to be exposed, considering exposure by all sources and routes.

name: estimated maximum daily intake
definition: Prediction of the maximum daily intake of a residue of a potentially harmful agent based on assumptions of average food consumption per person and maximum residues in the edible portion of a commodity, corrected for the reduction or increase in residues resulting from preparation, cooking, or commercial processing.

name: etiology
definition: Science dealing with the cause or origin of disease. In individuals, the cause or origin of disease.

name: eukaryote
definition: Cell or organism with the genetic material packed in a membrane-surrounded structurally discrete nucleus and with well-developed cell organelles.

name: European Inventory of Existing Chemical Substances
definition: List of all substances supplied either singly or as components in preparations to persons in a Member State of the European Community on any occasion between 1 January 1971 and 18 September 1981.

name: excess lifetime risk
definition: Additional or excess risk incurred over the lifetime of an individual by exposure to a toxic substance.

name: exchange transfusion
definition: Method of active artificial elimination of toxicity consisting in complete replacement of blood of the patient by donor blood.

name: excretion rate
definition: Amount of substance and (or) its metabolites that is excreted divided by time of excretion.

name: exocon
definition: Portion of a conjugated metabolite that is derived from the parent molecule.

name: exogenous
definition: Resulting from causes or derived from materials external to an organism.

name: exothelium
definition: Layer of flattened epithelial cells external to an organ or tissue.

name: expected environmental concentration
definition: Calculated concentrations of a substance, typically a pesticide, in various environmental compartments based on calculations using maximum-exposure scenarios.

name: explant
definition: Living tissue removed from its normal environment and transferred to an artificial medium for growth.

name: exposed
definition: Subject to a factor that is under study in the environment, for instance, an environmental hazard.

name: exposed group
definition: People (or other organisms) who have been exposed to a supposed cause of a disease or health state of interest, or possess a characteristic that is a determinant of the health outcome of interest.

name: exposure limit
definition: General term defining an administrative substance concentration or intensity of exposure that should not be exceeded.

name: exposure ratio
definition: In a case control study, value obtained by dividing the rate at which persons in the case group are exposed to a risk factor (or to a protective factor) by the rate at which persons in the control group are exposed to the risk factor (or to the protective factor) of interest.

name: exposure surface
definition: Surface on a target where a substance (e.g., a pesticide) is present.

name: exposure test
definition: Determination of the level, concentration, or uptake of a potentially toxic compound and (or) its metabolite(s) in biological samples from an organism (blood, urine, hair, etc.) and the interpretation of the results to estimate the absorbed dose or degree of environmental pollution; or the measuring of biochemical effects, usually not direct adverse effects of the substance, and relating them to the quantity of substance absorbed, or to its concentration in the environment.

name: external validity
definition: Generalizability of the results of a particular study, beyond the limits of the population actually studied.

name: extracellular space
definition: Volume within a tissue, outside cells, and excluding vascular and lymphatic space.

name: extracellular volume
definition: Volume of fluid outside the cells but within the outer surface of an organism.

name: extraction ratio
definition: Amount of substance extracted from a source divided by the total contained within the source.

name: extra risk
definition: Probability that an agent produces an observed response, as distinguished from the probability that the response is caused by a spontaneous event unrelated to the agent.

name: extraneous residue limit
definition: Refers to a pesticide residue or contaminant arising from environmental sources (including former agricultural uses) other than the use of a pesticide or contaminant substance directly or indirectly on the commodity. It is the maximum concentration of a pesticide residue or contaminant that is recommended by the Codex Alimentarius Commission to be legally permitted or recognized as acceptable in or on food, agricultural commodity, or animal feed.

name: extrapyramidal movement disorders
definition: Involuntary movement disorders mediated by signaling through neurons outside the pyramidal (corticospinal) tract, often describing side effects of psychiatric medications.

name: fertility
definition: Ability to conceive and to produce offspring: For litter-bearing species, the number of offspring per litter is used as a measure of fertility.

name: fertility toxicant
definition: Produces abnormalities of male or female reproductive functions or impairs reproductive capacity.

name: fetotoxicity
definition: Toxicity to the fetus.

name: fibrosis
definition: Abnormal formation of fibrous tissue.

name: fiducial limit
definition: Form of confidence limit given as a stated probability, for example, \(P = \pu{0.95}\).

name: first-order chemical reaction
definition: Chemical reaction where the initial rate is directly proportional to the concentration of one of the reactants. Any process in which a variable decreases with time at a constant fractional amount.

name: fixed dose procedure
definition: Acute toxicity test in which a substance is tested initially at a small number (3 or 4) predefined doses to identify which produces evident toxicity without lethality: The test may be repeated at one or more higher or lower defined discriminating doses to satisfy the criteria.

name: fluorosis
definition: Adverse effects of fluoride, as in dental or skeletal fluorosis.

name: foci
definition: Small groups of cells distinguishable, in appearance or histochemically, from the surrounding tissue: indicative of an early stage of a lesion that may lead to the formation of a neoplastic nodule.

name: food additive
definition: Any substance, not normally consumed as a food by itself and not normally used as a typical ingredient of a given food, whether or not it has nutritive value, that is added intentionally to food for a technological (including organoleptic) purpose in the manufacture, processing, preparation, treatment, packing, packaging, transport, or holding of the food. Addition results, or may be reasonably expected to result (directly or indirectly), in the substance or its byproducts becoming a component of, or otherwise affecting, the characteristics of the food to which it is added.

name: food allergy
definition: Hypersensitivity reaction to substances in the diet to which an individual has previously been sensitized.

name: food intolerance
definition: Physiologically based reproducible, unpleasant (adverse) reaction to a specific food or food ingredient that is not immunologically based.

name: food web
definition: Network of food chains.

name: forced diuresis
definition: Method of stimulating diuresis based on performing hydrational therapy, sometimes with parallel introduction of diuretics, with the aim of achieving increased clearance of a toxic substance in urine.

name: founder effect
definition: Changes in allelic frequencies that occur when a small group is separated from a large population and establishes a colony in a new location.

name: fumigant
definition: Substance that is vaporized in order to kill or repel pests.

name: fungus preparation
definition: Substance obtained from fungi that has an insecticidal effect reflecting the pathogenicity of the fungi for insects.

name: gametocide
definition: Substance intended to kill gametes.

name: gastroenteritis
definition: Inflammation of the stomach and intestine.

name: gastrointestinal
definition: Pertaining to or communicating with the stomach and intestine.

name: gavage
definition: Administration of materials directly into the stomach by esophageal intubation.

name: gene map
definition: Map showing the positions in the genome of genes or other genetic markers, either relative to each other or as a physical map of absolute distances.

name: generally regarded as safe
definition: Phrase used to describe the USFDA philosophy that justifies approval of food additives that may not meet the usual test criteria for safety but have been used extensively and have not demonstrated that they cause any harm to consumers.

name: genetically modified organism
definition: Bacterium, plant, or animal whose DNA has been deliberately altered.

name: genetic polymorphism
definition: Existence of inter-individual differences in DNA sequences coding for one specific gene, giving rise to different functional and (or) morphological traits.

name: genetic susceptibility
definition: Predisposition to a particular disease or sensitivity to a substance due to the presence of a specific allele or combination of alleles in an individual’s genome.

name: genetic toxicology
definition: Study of chemically or physically induced changes to the structure of DNA, including epigenetic phenomena or mutations that may or may not be heritable.

name: germ-free animal
definition: Animal grown under sterile conditions in the period of postnatal development: Such animals are usually obtained by Caesarean operation and kept in special sterile boxes in which there are no viable microorganisms (sterile air, food, and water are supplied).

name: germinal aplasia
definition: Complete failure of gonad development.

name: glomerular
definition: Pertaining to a tuft or cluster, as of a plexus of capillary blood vessels or nerve fibers, especially referring to the capillaries of the glomerular of the kidney.

name: glomerular filtration
definition: Formation of an ultrafiltrate of the blood occurring in the glomerulus of the kidney.

name: glomerular filtration rate
definition: Volume of ultrafiltrate formed in the kidney tubules from the blood passing through the glomerular capillaries divided by time of filtration.

name: glue-sniffing
definition: Inhalation of solvent vapor from plastic cements or other adhesives in order to become intoxicated.

name: gnotobiota
definition: Specifically and entirely known microfauna and microflora of a specially reared laboratory animal.

name: gnotobiote
definition: Specially reared laboratory animal whose microflora and microfauna are specifically known in their entirety.

name: goiter
definition: Noncancerous enlargement of the thyroid gland, visible as a swelling at the front of the neck, that is often associated with iodine deficiency.

name: goitrogen
definition: Any substance (such as thiouracil) that induces the formation of a goiter.

name: gonadotropic
definition: Pertaining to effects on sex glands and on the systems that regulate them.

name: good agricultural practice
definition: Nationally authorized safe uses of pesticides under actual conditions necessary for effective and reliable pest control.

name: graminicide
definition: Pesticide (herbicide) used for the control of weedy grasses (Gramineae).

name: ground treatment of plants
definition: Dusting or spraying of plants with pesticides by hand, by special machines, or by apparatus fixed to tractors or driven by them.

name: guideline for exposure limits
definition: Scientifically judged quantitative value (a concentration or number) of an environmental constituent that ensures aesthetically pleasing air, water, or food and from which no adverse effect is expected concerning noncarcinogenic endpoints, or that gives an acceptably low estimate of lifetime cancer risk from those substances which are proven human carcinogens or carcinogens with at least limited evidence of human carcinogenicity.

name: guideline value
definition: Quantitative measure (a concentration or a number) of a constituent of an environmental medium that ensures aesthetically pleasing air, water, or food and does not result in a significant risk to the user.

name: guides to air quality
definition: Sets of atmospheric concentrations and exposure times that are associated with specific effects of varying degrees of pollution on humans, animals, vegetation, and the environment in general.

name: guides to environmental quality
definition: Sets of concentrations, numbers and exposure times that are associated with the specific effects of factors in environmental media on humans, animals, vegetation, and the environment in general.

name: harmful occupational factor
definition: Component of the work environment, the effect of which on a worker under certain conditions leads to ill health or reduction of working ability.

name: harmful substance
definition: Substance that, following contact with an organism, can cause ill health or adverse effects either at the time of exposure or later in the life of the present and future generations.

name: hazard communication standard
definition: U.S. OSHA standard requiring all employers to inform employees of the hazard of substances in the workplace and the steps necessary to avoid harm.

name: hazardous production factor
definition: Production factor the effect of which on a worker under certain conditions results in injury or some impairment of health.

name: health
definition: State of complete physical, mental, and social well-being, and not merely the absence of disease or infirmity. State of dynamic balance in which an individual’s or a group’s capacity to cope with the circumstances of living is at an optimal level. State characterized by anatomical, physiological, and psychological integrity; ability to perform personally valued family, work, and community roles; ability to deal with physical, biological, psychological, and social stress; a feeling of well-being; and freedom from the risk of disease and untimely death. In ecology, a sustainable steady state in which humans and other living organisms can coexist indefinitely.

name: health advisory level
definition: In the United States, nonregulatory health-based reference level of chemical traces (usually in ppm, i.e., \(\pu{mg L-1}\)) in drinking water at which there are no adverse health risks when ingested over various periods of time.

name: health-based exposure limit
definition: Maximum concentration or intensity of exposure that can be tolerated without significant effect (based on only scientific and not economic evidence concerning exposure levels and associated health effects).

name: health hazard
definition: Any factor or exposure that may adversely affect health.

name: healthy worker effect
definition: Epidemiological phenomenon observed initially in studies of occupational diseases: Workers usually exhibit lower overall disease and death rates than the general population, due to the fact that the old, severely ill, and disabled are ordinarily excluded from employment. Death rates in the general population may be inappropriate for comparison, if this effect is not taken into account.

name: hematemesis
definition: Vomiting of blood.

name: hematotoxicity
definition: Adverse changes in blood caused by exposure to chemicals.

name: hematuria
definition: Presence of blood in the urine.

name: hemochromatosis
definition: Hereditary disorder affecting iron metabolism in which excessive amounts of iron accumulate in the body tissues.

name: hemoglobinuria
definition: Presence of free hemoglobin in the urine.

name: hemolysin
definition: Substance that damages the membrane of erythrocytes causing the release of hemoglobin.

name: hemolysis
definition: Release of hemoglobin from erythrocytes, and its appearance in the plasma.

name: hemoperfusion
definition: Passing blood through a column of charcoal or adsorbent resin for the removal of drugs or toxins.

name: hemosiderin
definition: Insoluble iron(III) hydroxide-based pigment deposited in cells in conditions of iron overload.

name: hepatic
definition: Pertaining to the liver.

name: hepatotoxic
definition: Poisonous to liver cells.

name: herbicide
definition: Substance intended to kill plants.

name: heterozygote
definition: Organism that has different allelic forms of a specified gene on each of a pair of homologous chromosomes or describing the genome of that organism.

name: Hill plot
definition: Graphical method for analyzing binding of a molecule \(\ce{A}\) to a macromolecule \(\ce{P}\) with \(n\) binding sites. A Hill plot of \(\log[\theta/(1 - \theta)]\) vs. \(\log[\ce{A}]\) has a slope of 1 if binding is noncooperative and \(\gt 1\) for cooperative binding, where \(\theta = [\ce{A}]_{\rm{bound}}/n[\ce{P}]_{\rm{total}}\) is the fraction of sites occupied.

name: histogenic origin
definition: Germ cell layer of the embryo from which a given adult tissue develops.

name: histology
definition: Study (usually microscopic) of the anatomy of tissues and their cellular and subcellular structure.

name: histopathology
definition: Microscopic pathological study of the anatomy and cell structure of tissues in disease to reveal abnormal or adverse structural changes.

name: hit-and-run effect
definition: Toxicity that follows a single exposure to a substance.

name: homology
definition: Similarity of anatomical structures in different species because of shared ancestry Similarity of DNA or RNA nucleotide sequences, or of protein amino-acid sequences, supporting the hypothesis that they share a common ancestor.Note: Homology among DNA or RNA nucleotide sequences, or among protein amino-acid sequences, is often concluded on the basis of sequence similarity. In general, if there are almost identical sequences, it is likely that they are homologous. However, it is possible that highly similar sequences were not derived from a common ancestor, i.e., they are similar but not homologous.

name: homozygote
definition: Organism that has the same allelic form of a specified gene on each of a pair of homologous chromosomes or describing the genome of that organism.

name: human ecology
definition: Interrelationship between humans and the entire environment—physical, biological, socioeconomic, and cultural, including the interrelationships between individual humans or groups of humans and other human groups or groups of other species.

name: human equivalent dose
definition: Human dose of an agent that is believed to induce the same magnitude of a toxic effect that the known animal dose has induced.

name: human exposure threshold
definition: Generic value of exposure to a substance, or a group of substances falling within a defined structural class, below which there is expected to be no appreciable risk to human health.

name: hygiene
definition: Science of health and its preservation.

name: hyper-
definition: Prefix meaning above or excessive: when used with the suffix '-emia' refers to blood and with the suffix '-uria' refers to urine, for example, 'hyperbilirubinemia'.

name: hyperemia
definition: Excessive amount of blood in any part of the body.

name: hyperalimentation
definition: Ingestion or administration of nutrients in excess of optimal amounts.

name: hyperbilirubinemia
definition: Excessive concentration of bilirubin in the blood.

name: hypercalcemia
definition: Excessive concentration of calcium in the blood.

name: hyperglycemia
definition: Excessive concentration of glucose in the blood.

name: hyperkalemia
definition: Excessive concentration of potassium in the blood.

name: hypernatremia
definition: Excessive concentration of sodium in the blood.

name: hyperparathyroidism
definition: Abnormally increased parathyroid gland activity that affects, and is affected by, plasma calcium concentration.

name: hypertension
definition: Persistently high blood pressure in the arteries or in a circuit, for example, pulmonary hypertension or hepatic portal hypertension.

name: hypervitaminosis
definition: Condition resulting from the ingestion of an excess of one or more vitamins.

name: hypo-
definition: Prefix meaning under, deficient: when used with the suffix '-emia' refers to blood and with the suffix '-uria' refers to urine, for example, 'hypocalcemia'.

name: hypocalcemia
definition: Abnormally low calcium concentration in the blood.

name: hypokalemia
definition: Abnormally low potassium concentration in the blood.

name: hypomagnesemia
definition: Abnormally low magnesium concentration in the blood.

name: hyponatremia
definition: Abnormally low sodium concentration in the blood.

name: hypovolemic
definition: Pertaining to an abnormally decreased volume of circulating fluid (plasma) in the body.

name: iatrogenic
definition: Any adverse condition resulting from medical treatment.

name: icterus
definition: Excess of bile pigment in the blood and consequent deposition and retention of bile pigment in the skin and the sclera.

name: idiosyncrasy
definition: Genetically based unusually high sensitivity of an organism to the effect of certain substances.

name: immediately-dangerous-to-life-or-health-concentration
definition: According to the U.S. NIOSH, the maximum exposure concentration from which one could escape within \(\pu{30 min}\) without any escape-impairing symptoms or any irreversible health effects.

name: in silico
definition: Phrase applied to data generated and analyzed using computer modeling and information technology.

name: incidence rate
definition: Measure of the frequency at which new events occur in a population.

name: indication
definition: Quantity value provided by a measuring instrument or a measuring system.

name: indirect exposure
definition: Exposure to a substance in a medium or vehicle other than the one originally receiving the substance. Exposure of people to a substance by contact with a person directly exposed.

name: individual protective device
definition: Device for individual use for protection of the whole body, eyes, respiratory pathways, or skin of workers against hazardous and harmful production factors.

name: individual risk
definition: Probability that an individual person will experience an adverse effect.

name: inert chemical
definition: Substance that is not generally reactive.

name: inert ingredient
definition: Any intentionally added ingredient of a mixture that does not contribute to the desired biological effect: This definition does not include impurities and does not imply that the inert ingredient has no biological effects.

name: infusion
definition: Therapeutic introduction of a fluid other than blood, as a (usually saline) solution, into a vein.

name: ingestion
definition: Process of taking food and drink into the body by mouth. Process of taking in particles by a phagocytic cell.

name: inhalation
definition: Act of drawing in of air, vapor, or gas and any suspended particulates into the lung.

name: inherently biodegradable
definition: Class of compounds for which there is unequivocal evidence of biodegradation (primary or ultimate) in any test of biodegradability.

name: intake
definition: Amount of a substance that is taken into the body, regardless of whether or not it is absorbed: The total daily intake is the sum of the daily intake by an individual from food, drinking-water, and inhaled air.

name: integral indicator of toxic effect
definition: Parameter (such as body weight or temperature) characterizing the overall changes in the general state of the organism exposed to a toxic substance.

name: intermittent effect
definition: Biological change that comes and goes at intervals.

name: internal validity
definition: Selection and comparison of index and comparison groups in such a manner that, apart from sampling error, the observed differences between these groups with respect to dependent variables under study may be attributed only to the hypothesized effect under investigation.

name: interpolation
definition: Estimation of a value between two known data points.

name: interpretation
definition: Evaluation of the observations from an investigation or study in order to determine their significance for human health, for the environment or for both.

name: interspecies dose conversion
definition: Process of extrapolating from the doses of one animal species to another, for example, from rodent dose to human equivalent.

name: interstitial fluid
definition: Aqueous solution filling the narrow spaces between cells.

name: interstitial pneumonia
definition: Chronic form of pneumonia involving increase of the interstitial tissue and decrease of the functional lung tissue.

name: intervention study
definition: Epidemiological investigation designed to test a hypothesized cause–effect relationship by intentional change of a supposed causal factor in a population.

name: intestinal reabsorption
definition: Absorption further down the intestinal tract of a substance or substances that have been absorbed before and subsequently excreted into the intestinal tract, usually through the bile.

name: intoxication
definition: Poisoning: pathological process with clinical signs and symptoms caused by a substance of exogenous or endogenous origin. Drunkenness following consumption of beverages containing ethanol or other compounds affecting the central nervous system.

name: intrinsic activity
definition: Maximal stimulatory effect induced by a compound in relation to that of a given reference compound.

name: intrinsic clearance
definition: Volume of plasma or blood from which a substance is completely removed in a period of time under unstressed conditions.

name: intrinsic factor
definition: Specific protein required for the absorption of \(\ce{vitamin B_{12}}\) and secreted by cells in the gastric glands of the stomach.

name: irreversible alteration
definition: Change from normal structure or function that persists or progresses after cessation of exposure of the organism.

name: irritant
definition: n., Substance that causes inflammation following immediate, prolonged, or repeated contact with skin, mucous membrane, or other biological material. Note: A substance capable of causing inflammation on first contact is called a primary irritant. adj., Causing inflammation following immediate, prolonged, or repeated contact with skin, mucous membrane, or other tissues.

name: isotonic
definition: Denoting a liquid exerting the same osmotic pressure or chemical potential of water (water potential) as another liquid with which it is being compared.

name: itai-itai disease
definition: Illness (renal osteomalacia) observed in the Toyama prefecture of Japan, resulting from the ingestion of cadmium-contaminated rice.

name: jaundice
definition: Pathological condition characterized by deposition of bile pigment in the skin and mucous membranes, including the conjunctivae, resulting in yellow appearance of the patient or animal.

name: joint effect
definition: Simultaneous or successive effect of factors of diverse types (chemical, physical, biological) on an organism.

name: kairomone
definition: Semiochemical that is produced by one organism inducing a response in an organism of another species that is unfavorable to the emitter.

name: kinetics
definition: Branch of chemistry concerned with measuring and studying rates of chemical reactions.

name: ketosis
definition: Pathological increase in the production of ketone bodies, for example, following blockage or failure of carbohydrate metabolism.

name: knock-down
definition: Technique used to decrease the expression of a particular gene in a cell or living organism in order to define its function.

name: knock-in
definition: Technique used to express an exogenous gene or to overexpress an endogenous gene in a living organism in order to define its function.

name: knock-out
definition: Technique used to inactivate a particular gene in a living organism in order to define its function.

name: lacrimator
definition: Substance that irritates the eyes and causes the production of tears or increases the flow of tears.

name: larvicide
definition: Substance intended to kill larvae.

name: laryngospasm
definition: Reflex spasmodic closure of the sphincter of the larynx, particularly the glottic sphincter.

name: lassitude
definition: Weakness; exhaustion.

name: lavage
definition: Irrigation or washing out of a hollow organ or cavity such as the stomach, intestines, or lungs.

name: laxative
definition: Substance that causes evacuation of the intestinal contents.

name: lead colic
definition: Chronic intestinal pains and constipation caused by lead poisoning.

name: lesion
