definition: Area of pathologically altered tissue. Injury or wound. Infected patch of skin.

name: life-long exposure
definition: Subjection to a potentially toxic substance during the whole lifetime.

name: limacide
definition: Substance intended to kill mollusks including the gastropod mollusk, Limax.

name: limited evidence
definition: According to the USEPA’s Guidelines for Carcinogen Risk Assessment, 'limited evidence' is a collection of facts and accepted scientific inferences that suggests that an agent may be causing an effect, but this suggestion is not strong enough to be considered established fact.

name: linearised multistage model
definition: Sequence of steps in which (a) a multistage model is fitted to tumor incidence data; (b) the maximum linear term consistent with the data is calculated; (c) the low-dose slope of the dose–response function is equated to the coefficient of the maximum linear term; and (d) the resulting slope is then equated to the upper bound of potency.

name: macroscopic pathology
definition: Study of changes associated with disease that are visible to the naked eye without the need for a microscope.

name: mainstream smoke
definition: Smoke that is inhaled by the smoker.

name: malaise
definition: Vague feeling of bodily discomfort.

name: malignancy
definition: Population of cells showing both uncontrolled growth and a tendency to invade and destroy other tissues.

name: mania
definition: Emotional disorder (mental illness) characterized by an expansive and elated state (euphoria), rapid speech, flight of ideas, decreased need for sleep, distractibility, grandiosity, poor judgment, and increased motor activity.

name: margin of exposure
definition: Ratio of the no-observed-adverse-effect level (NOAEL) to the theoretical or estimated exposure dose (EED) or concentration (EEC).

name: mass mean diameter
definition: Diameter of a spherical particle with a mass equal to the mean mass of all the particles in a population.

name: mass median diameter
definition: Diameter of a spherical particle with the median mass of all the particles in a population.

name: maximum average daily concentration of an atmospheric pollutant
definition: Highest of the average daily concentrations recorded at a definite point of measurement during a certain period of observation.
synonyms: peak daily average concentration of an air pollutant

name: maximum contaminant level
definition: Under the Safe Drinking Water Act (USA), primary MCL is a regulatory concentration for drinking water which takes into account both adverse effects (including sensitive populations) and technological feasibility (including natural background levels): Secondary MCL is a regulatory concentration based on 'welfare', such as taste and staining, rather than health, but also takes into account technical feasibility.

name: maximum exposure limit
definition: Occupational exposure limit legally defined in the United Kingdom under COSHH as the maximum concentration of an airborne substance, averaged over a reference period, to which employees may be exposed by inhalation under any circumstances, and set on the advice of the HSC Advisory Committee on Toxic Substances.

name: maximum residue limit
definition: Maximum contents of a pesticide residue (expressed as \(\pu{mg kg-1}\) fresh weight) recommended by the Codex Alimentarius Commission to be legally permitted in or on food commodities and animal feeds.

name: maximum residue limit for veterinary drugs
definition: Maximum contents of a drug residue (expressed as \(\pu{mg kg-1}\) or \(\pu{\upmu g kg-1}\) fresh weight) recommended by the Codex Alimentarius Commission to be legally permitted or recognized as acceptable in or on food commodities and animal feeds.

name: maximum velocity
definition: In Michaelis–Menten kinetics, the maximum rate of conversion of a substrate when its concentration is not rate-limiting.

name: mercurialism
definition: Chronic poisoning caused by exposure to mercury, often by breathing its vapor but also by skin absorption and, less commonly, by ingestion.

name: mesothelioma
definition: Malignant tumor of the mesothelium of the pleura, pericardium, or peritoneum, that may be caused by exposure to asbestos fibers and some other fibers.

name: metabolic enzymes
definition: Proteins that catalyze chemical transformations of body constituents and, in more common usage, of xenobiotics.

name: metabolic model
definition: Analysis and theoretical reconstruction of the way in which the body deals with a specific substance, showing the proportion of the intake that is absorbed, the proportion that is stored and in what tissues, the rate of breakdown in the body and the subsequent fate of the metabolic products, and the rate at which it is eliminated by different organs as unchanged substance or metabolites.

name: metabolic transformation
definition: Biotransformation of a substance that takes place within a living organism.

name: metastasis
definition: Movement of bacteria or body cells, especially cancer cells, from one part of the body to another, resulting in change in location of a disease or of its symptoms from one part of the body to another. Growth of pathogenic microorganisms or of abnormal cells distant from the site of their origin in the body.

name: methemoglobin
definition: Derivative of hemoglobin that is formed when the iron(II) in the heme porphyrin is oxidized to iron(III); this derivative cannot transport dioxygen.

name: methemoglobinaemia
definition: Presence of methaemoglobin in the blood in greater than normal proportion.

name: methemoglobin-forming substance
definition: Substance capable of oxidizing directly or indirectly the iron(II) in hemoglobin to iron(III) to form methemoglobin.

name: microalbuminuria
definition: Chronic presence of albumin in slight excess in urine.

name: micromercurialism
definition: Early or subclinical effects of exposure to elemental mercury detected at the low exposure levels.

name: microproteinaemia
definition: Chronic presence of microprotein (alpha-1 and beta-2 microglobulin) in blood, indicating proximal renal tubule damage.

name: midstream sampling
definition: Taking an aliquot of a flowing liquid, such as urine, avoiding initial and terminal flow periods which are likely to be unrepresentative.

name: minimal risk level
definition: Estimate of the daily human exposure to a hazardous substance that is likely to be without appreciable risk of adverse noncancer health effects over a specified duration of exposure: This substance-specific estimate is used by ATSDR health assessors to identify contaminants and potential health effects that may be of concern at hazardous waste sites.

name: miscible
definition: Liquid substances capable of mixing without separation into two phases; refers to liquid mixtures.

name: miticide
definition: Substance intended to kill mites.

name: mitochondrion
definition: Eukaryote cytoplasmic organelle that is bounded by an outer membrane and an inner membrane; the inner membrane has folds called cristae that are the center of ATP synthesis in oxidative phosphorylation in the animal cell and supplement ATP synthesis by the chloroplasts in photosynthetic cells.

name: molluskicide
definition: Substance intended to kill mollusks.

name: monooxygenase
definition: Enzyme that catalyzes reactions between an organic compound and molecular oxygen in which one atom of the oxygen molecule is incorporated into the organic compound and one atom is reduced to water; involved in the metabolism of many natural and foreign compounds giving both unreactive products and products of different or increased toxicity from that of the parent compound.

name: morbidity
definition: Any departure, subjective or objective, from a state of physiological or psychological well-being: In this sense, 'sickness', 'illness', and 'morbid condition' are similarly defined and synonymous.

name: morbidity rate
definition: Term (to be avoided) used loosely to refer to incidence or prevalence rates of disease.

name: morbidity survey
definition: Method for the estimation of the prevalence and (or) incidence of a disease or diseases in a population.

name: mortality study
definition: Investigation dealing with death rates or proportion of deaths attributed to specific causes as a measure of response.

name: mucociliary transport
definition: Process of removal of particles from the bronchi of the lungs in a mucus stream moved by cilia, thus contributing to uptake from the gastrointestinal tract.

name: multicompartment model
definition: Product of a compartmental analysis requiring more than two compartments.

name: multifactorial disease
definition: Illness with pathogenesis dependent on complex interplay of genetic and (or) environmental factors.

name: multiple screening
definition: Procedure that has evolved by combining single screening tests, and is the logical corollary of mass screening.

name: multipotent
definition: Of a cell, capable of giving rise to several different kinds of structure or types of cell.

name: multistage cluster sampling
definition: Cluster sampling with more than two stages, each sampling being made on aggregates (or clusters) in which the clusters already obtained by the preceding sampling have been divided.

name: multistage model
definition: Dose–response model for cancer death estimation of the form \[P = 1 - \exp [-(q_{0} + q_{1}d_{1} + q_{2}d_{2} + \ldots + q_{k}d_{k})]\] where \(P\) is the probability of cancer death from a continuous dose rate, \(d_{i}\) , of group (or stage) \(i = 0, 1, 2 \ldots\), the \(q\)’s are constants, and \(k\) is the number of dose groups (or, if less than the number of dose groups, \(k\) is the number of biological stages believed to be required in the carcinogenesis process). With the multistage model, it is assumed that cancer is initiated by cell mutations in a finite series of steps.

name: murine
definition: Of or belonging to the family of rats and mice (Muridae).

name: myalgia
definition: Pain or tenderness in a muscle or group of muscles.

name: myasthenia
definition: Muscular weakness.

name: mycotoxin
definition: Toxin produced by a fungus.

name: nanotoxicology
definition: Scientific discipline involving the study of the actual or potential danger presented by the harmful effects of nanoparticles on living organisms and ecosystems, of the relationship of such harmful effects to exposure, and of the mechanisms of action, diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of intoxications.

name: natriuretic
definition: Substance increasing the rate of excretion of sodium ion in the urine.

name: natural occurrence
definition: Presence of a substance in nature, as distinct from presence resulting from inputs from human activities.

name: negligible risk
definition: Probability of adverse effects occurring that can reasonably be described as trivial. Probability of adverse effects occurring that is so low that it cannot be reduced appreciably by increased regulation or investment of resources.

name: nematicide
definition: Substance intended to kill nematodes.

name: neoplasia
definition: New and abnormal formation of tissue as a tumor or growth by cell proliferation that is faster than normal and continues after the initial stimulus that initiated the proliferation has ceased.

name: nephritis
definition: Inflammation of the kidney, leading to kidney failure, usually accompanied by proteinuria, hematuria, edema, and hypertension.

name: nephropathy
definition: Any disease or abnormality of the kidney.

name: nephrosis
definition: Disease of the kidneys marked by degeneration of renal tubular epithelium.

name: nephrotoxic
definition: Chemically harmful to the cells of the kidney.

name: nitrosative stress
definition: Adverse effects occurring when the generation of reactive nitrogen species in a system exceeds the system’s ability to neutralize and eliminate them; nitrosative stress may lead to nitrosylation reactions that can alter protein structure, thus inhibiting normal function.

name: no-acceptable-daily-intake-allocated
definition: This expression is applicable to a substance for which the available information is not sufficient to establish its safety, or when the specifications for identity and purity are not adequate, or when the available data show that the substance is hazardous and should not be used.

name: nodule
definition: Small node or boss that is solid and can be detected by touch.

name: no-effect dose
definition: Amount of a substance that has no effect on the organism.

name: no-effect level
definition: Maximum dose (of a substance) that produces no detectable changes under defined conditions of exposure.

name: non-bioenvironmental transformation
definition: Change in the chemical or physical nature of a substance occurring as a result of physicochemical conditions and independent of any biological system.

name: nonionising radiation
definition: Electromagnetic radiation of low energy that is not capable of causing ionization.

name: nonoccupational exposure
definition: Environmental exposure outside the workplace to substances that are otherwise associated with particular work environments and (or) activities and processes that occur there.

name: nosocomial
definition: Associated with a hospital or infirmary, especially used of diseases that may result from treatment in such an institution.

name: nutritional table method
definition: Procedure for evaluating the dietary intake of a large number of people.

name: nychthemeral
definition: Relating to or exhibiting a nychthemeron or \(\pu{24\!\mbox{-}h}\) period.

name: objective environment
definition: Actual physical, chemical, and social environment as described by objective measurements, such as noise levels in decibels and concentrations of air pollutants.

name: occupational environment
definition: Surrounding conditions at a workplace.

name: occupational exposure
definition: Experience of substances, intensities of radiation, etc., or other conditions while at work.

name: occupational exposure limit
definition: Regulatory level of exposure to substances, intensities of radiation, etc., or other conditions, specified appropriately in relevant government legislation or related codes of practice.

name: occupational exposure standard
definition: Level of exposure to substances, intensities of radiation, etc., or other conditions considered to represent specified good practice and a realistic criterion for the control of exposure by appropriate plant design, engineering controls, and, if necessary, the addition and use of personal protective clothing. In UK, health-based exposure limit defined under COSHH Regulations as the concentration of any airborne substance, averaged over a reference period, at which, according to current knowledge, there is no evidence that it is likely to be injurious to employees, if they are exposed by inhalation, day after day, to that concentration, and set on the advice of the HSE Advisory Committee on Toxic Substances.

name: occupational hygiene
definition: Identification, assessment, and control of physicochemical and biological factors in the workplace that may affect the health or well-being of those at work and in the surrounding community.

name: occupational medicine
definition: Specialty devoted to the prevention and management of occupational injury, illness, and disability, and the promotion of the health of workers, their families, and their communities.

name: ocular
definition: Pertaining to the eye.

name: odds
definition: Ratio of the probability of occurrence of an event to that of non-occurrence, or the ratio of the probability that something is so, to the probability that it is not so.

name: odds ratio
definition: Quotient obtained by dividing one set of odds by another. The terms 'odds' or 'odds ratio' are defined differently according to the situation under discussion. Consider the following notation for the distribution of a binary exposure and a disease in a population or a sample. \[\begin{array}{l c c} & Exposed & Nonexposed \\ \rm{Disease} & a & b \\ \rm{No\ disease} & c & d \\ \end{array}\] The odds ratio (cross-product ratio) is \(ad/bc\).

name: odor threshold
definition: In principle, the lowest concentration of an odorant in the air that can be detected by a human being.

name: olf
definition: Unit used to measure scent emission of people and objects; one olf is defined as the scent emission of an 'average person', a sitting adult who takes an average of \(\pu{0.7}\) baths per day and whose skin has a total area of \(\pu{1.8 m2}\); the scent emission of an object or person is measured by specially trained personnel comparing it to normed scents.

name: olfactometer
definition: Apparatus for testing the power of the sense of smell.

name: oligozoospermia
definition: Sperm concentration less than a reference value.

name: oliguria
definition: Excretion of a diminished amount of urine in relation to fluid intake.

name: -omics, -omes
definition: Neologism referring to the fields of study in biology ending in the suffix -omics, such as genomics or proteomics: The related neologism -omes are the objects of study of the field such as the genome or proteome, respectively.

name: oncogene
definition: Gene that can cause neoplastic (see neoplasia) transformation of a cell; oncogenes are slightly changed equivalents of normal genes known as proto-oncogenes.

name: oncogenesis
definition: Production or causation of tumors.

name: oncogenic
definition: Capable of producing tumors in animals, either benign (noncancerous) or malignant (cancerous).

name: one-hit model
definition: Dose-response model of the form \[P = 1 - {\rm{e}}^{-bd}\] where \(P\) is the probability of cancer death from a continuous dose rate, \(d\), and \(b\) is a constant.

name: onycholysis
definition: Loosening or detachment of the nail from the nail bed following some destructive process.

name: ophthalmic
definition: Pertaining to the eye.

name: organ dose
definition: Amount of a substance or physical agent (radiation) absorbed by an organ.

name: organelle
definition: Microstructure or separated compartment within a cell that has a specialized function.

name: organic carbon partition coefficient
definition: Measure of the tendency for organic substances to be adsorbed by soil or sediment, expressed as: \[K_{\rm{oc}} = \frac{(\ce{mass adsorbed substance})/(\ce{mass organic carbon})}{(\ce{mass concentration of absorbed substance})}\]

name: osteo-
definition: Prefix meaning pertaining to bone.

name: osteodystrophy
definition: Abnormal development of bone.

name: osteomalacia
definition: Condition marked by softening of the bones (due to impaired mineralization, with excess accumulation of osteoid), with pain, tenderness, muscular weakness, anorexia, and loss of weight, resulting from deficiency of vitamin D and calcium.

name: osteoporosis
definition: Significant decrease in bone mass with increased porosity and increased tendency to fracture.

name: ovicide
definition: Substance intended to kill eggs.

name: para-occupational exposure
definition: Exposure of a worker’s family to substances carried from the workplace to the home. Exposure of visitors to substances in the workplace.

name: parasympathetic
definition: Of, relating to, or affecting the parasympathetic nervous system which stimulates digestive secretions, slows the heart, constricts the pupils of the eyes, and dilates blood vessels.

name: parasympatholytic
definition: Producing effects resembling those caused by interruption of the parasympathetic nerve; also called anticholinergic.

name: parenteral dosage
definition: Method of introducing substances into an organism avoiding the gastrointestinal tract (subcutaneously, intravenously, intramuscularly, etc.).

name: passive smoking
definition: Inhalation of sidestream smoke by people who do not smoke themselves.

name: penetration
definition: Action of entering or passing through a cell membrane. Ability or power to enter or pass through a cell membrane.

name: percutaneous
definition: Through the skin following application on the skin.

name: perfusion
definition: Act of pouring over or through, especially the passage of a fluid through the vessels of a specific organ. Liquid poured over or through an organ or tissue.

name: peritoneal dialysis
definition: Method of artificial detoxication in which a toxic substance from the body is transferred into liquid that is instilled into the peritoneum.

name: permeability coefficient
definition: Quantity defining the permeability of molecules across a cell membrane and expressed as \[P = \frac{KD}{\Delta x}\] where \(K\) is the partition coefficient, \(D\) is the diffusion coefficient, and \(\Delta x\) is the thickness of the cell membrane.

name: permeable
definition: Of a membrane, allowing a given substance to pass through.

name: permissible exposure limit
definition: Recommendation by U.S. OSHA for a time-weighted average concentration that must not be exceeded during any \(\pu{8\!\mbox{-}h}\) work shift of a \(\pu{40\!\mbox{-}h}\) working week.

name: personal monitoring
definition: Type of environmental monitoring in which an individual’s exposure to a substance is measured and evaluated.

name: personal protective device
definition: Equipment (clothing, gloves, hard hat, respirator, etc.) worn by an individual to prevent exposure to a potentially toxic substance.

name: personal sampler
definition: Compact, portable instrument for individual air sampling, measuring, or both, the content of a harmful substance in the respiration zone of a working person.

name: pest
definition: Organism that may harm public health, attacks food and other materials essential to mankind, or otherwise affects human beings adversely.

name: phase III reaction
definition: Further metabolism of conjugated metabolites produced by phase II reactions.

name: phenome
definition: Complete phenotypic description of an organism (by analogy with genome).

name: photo-irritation
definition: Inflammation of the skin caused by exposure to light, especially that due to metabolites formed in the skin by photolysis.

name: phototoxicity
definition: Adverse effects produced by exposure to light energy, especially those produced in the skin.

name: physical map
definition: Map showing how much DNA, measured in base pairs, separates two genes.

name: piscicide
definition: Substance intended to kill fish.

name: placentation
definition: Formation of a placenta in the uterus. Type or structure of a placenta. In botany, arrangement of placentas within the plant ovary.

name: plumbism
definition: Chronic poisoning caused by absorption of lead or lead salts.

name: pneumoconiosis
definition: Usually fibrosis of the lungs that develops owing to (prolonged) inhalation of inorganic or organic dusts.

name: pneumonitis
definition: Inflammation of the lung.

name: point mutation
definition: Change in a single base pair in DNA.

name: poison-bearing
definition: Containing a poison.

name: poisoning
definition: Morbid condition produced by a poison.

name: polyclonal antibody
definition: Antibody produced by a number of different cell types.

name: polydipsia
definition: Chronic excessive thirst.

name: polyuria
definition: Excessive production and discharge of urine.

name: population at risk
definition: Persons who can and may develop an adverse health effect and who are potentially exposed to a substance under study. People already having chronic disease are excluded from the population at risk in studies of the incidence of the adverse effect.

name: population critical concentration
definition: Concentration of a substance in the critical organ at which a specified percentage of the exposed population has reached the individual critical organ concentration.

name: population effect
definition: Absolute number or incidence rate of cases occurring in a group of people.

name: porphyria
definition: Disturbance of porphyrin metabolism characterized by increased formation, accumulation, and excretion of porphyrins and their precursors.

name: porphyrin
definition: Natural pigment containing a fundamental skeleton of four pyrrole nuclei united through the α-positions by four methine groups to form a macrocyclic structure.

name: posology
definition: Pharmacological study of the choice of appropriate dose of a drug in relation to the physiological factors, such as age, that may influence its effect.

name: post-translational modification
definition: Processes by which proteins are biochemically modified within a cell following their synthesis on the ribosomes.

name: practical certainty
definition: Numerically specified low risk of exposure to a potentially toxic substance (e.g., 1 in \(\pu{1000}\)) or socially acceptable low risk of adverse effects from such an exposure applied to decision making in regard to chemical safety.

name: precordial
definition: Pertaining to the region over the heart and lower thorax.

name: predictive validity
definition: Reliability of a measurement expressed in terms of its ability to predict the criterion.

name: predictive value
definition: Percentage of positive results that are true positives or of negative results that are true negatives.

name: premature ovarian failure
definition: Follicular depletion by the age of 35 years.

name: preneoplastic
definition: Before the formation of a tumor.

name: prior informed consent
definition: Concept in law and medicine that states that before one is subjected to a risk, especially a risk of bodily harm, one is entitled to be fully informed well in advance of the nature of that risk in order to make an informed decision about whether to accept it or not.

name: primary protection standard
definition: Accepted maximum level of a pollutant (or its indicator) in the target organism, or some part thereof, or an accepted maximum intake of a pollutant or nuisance into the target under specified circumstances.

name: procarcinogen
definition: Substance that has to be metabolized before it becomes a carcinogen.

name: progression
definition: Increase in the size of a tumor or spread of cancer in the body.

name: prokaryote
definition: Unicellular organism, characterized by the absence of a membrane-enclosed nucleus.

name: pro-pesticide
definition: Substance applied in a form that is not active as a pesticide and which becomes active once it enters an organism and undergoes chemical modification.

name: proportional mortality rate
definition: Proportion of observed deaths from a specified condition in a defined population divided by the proportion of deaths expected from this condition in a standard population, expressed either on an age-specific basis or after age adjustment.

name: proteinuria
definition: Excretion of excessive amounts of protein (derived from blood plasma or kidney tubules) in the urine.

name: pseudo-acceptable daily intake
definition: Intake for a substance derived by applying a thousandfold uncertainty factor to the lowest low-effect level for noncarcinogenic endpoints.

name: pseudoadaptation
definition: Apparent adaptation of an organism to changing conditions of the environment (especially chemical) associated with stresses in biochemical systems that exceed the limits of normal (homeostatic) mechanisms.

name: public health impact assessment
definition: Applying risk assessment to a specific target population of known size, giving as the end product a quantitative statement about the number of people likely to be affected in a particular population.

name: pyrexia
definition: Condition in which the temperature of a human being or mammal is above normal.

name: quantal
definition: Describing a condition that can be expressed only as 'occurring' or 'not occurring', such as death.

name: radiation toxicology
definition: Scientific study involving research, education, prevention, and treatment of diseases caused by ionizing or nonionizing radiation.

name: rate difference
definition: Absolute difference between two rates.

name: ratticide
definition: Substance intended to kill rats.

name: reabsorption
definition: Absorption by a living organism of a substance which it has previously absorbed and then released (e.g., the uptake of a substance from the proximal renal tubule following glomerular filtration).

name: reactive nitrogen species
definition: Radical nitrogen-based molecules that can act to facilitate nitrosylation reactions; reactive nitrogen species include dioxidonitrogen(\(\ce{^{.}}\)) (nitrogen dioxide, nitryl radical) \(\ce{NO^{.}}\), oxidonitrogen(\(\ce{^{.}}\)) (nitrogen monoxide, nitrosyl radical) \(\ce{NO^{.}}\) oxidonitrogen(1+) (nitrosyl cation) \(\ce{NO^{+}}\), hydroxyoxidonitrogen (nitrous acid) \(\ce{HNO2}\), and oxidonitrate(1-) \(\ce{NO^{-}}\).

name: readily biodegradable
definition: Arbitrary classification of substances that have passed certain specified screening tests for ultimate biodegradability; these tests are so stringent that such compounds will be rapidly and completely biodegraded in a wide variety of aerobic environments.

name: recalcitrance
definition: Ability of a substance to remain in a particular environment in an unchanged form.

name: receptor-mediated endocytosis
definition: Endocytosis of a substance and its receptor following receptor binding.

name: recessive gene
definition: Allele which in the heterozygous state is expected to have no effect on the phenotype of the organism which carries it.

name: recommended exposure level
definition: Highest allowable regulatory airborne concentration.

name: reconstitution
definition: Restoration to original form of a substance previously altered for preservation and storage.

name: recycling
definition: Process or method allowing for the recovery of some value from a waste, either as reusable material or as energy.

name: reference concentration
definition: An estimate (with uncertainty spanning perhaps an order of magnitude) of a continuous inhalation exposure to the human population (including sensitive subgroups which include children, asthmatics, and the elderly) that is likely to be without an appreciable risk of deleterious effects during a lifetime.

name: reference distribution
definition: Statistical distribution of reference values.

name: reference individual
definition: Person selected with the use of defined criteria for comparative purposes in a clinical study.

name: reference interval
definition: Area between and including two reference limits, for example, the percentiles \(\pu{2.5}\) and \(\pu{97.5}\).

name: reference limit
definition: Boundary value defined so that a stated fraction of the reference values is less than or exceeds that boundary value with a stated probability.

name: reference population
definition: Group of all reference individuals used to establish criteria against which a population that is being studied can be compared.

name: reference sample group
definition: Selected reference individuals, statistically adequate numerically to represent the reference population.

name: reference value
definition: Quantity value, generally accepted as having a suitably small measurement uncertainty, to be used as a basis for comparison with values of quantities of the same kind.

name: regulatory dose
definition: Term used by the USEPA to describe the expected dose resulting from human exposure to a substance at the level at which it is regulated in the environment.

name: regulatory sequence
definition: DNA sequence to which specific proteins bind to activate or repress the expression of a gene.

name: relative excess risk
definition: Measure that can be used in comparison of adverse reactions to drugs, or other exposures, based solely on the component of risk due to the exposure or drug under investigation, removing the risk due to background exposure experienced by all in the population. The relative excess risk, \(R\), is given by \[R = (R_{1} - R_{0})/(R_{2} - R_{0})\] where \(R_{1}\) is the rate in the population, \(R_{2}\) is the rate in the comparison population, and \(R_{0}\) is the rate in the general population.

name: relative systemic availability
definition: Quantity of metabolizable substance divided by product of quantity of absorbed substance and exposure.

name: remedy
definition: Anything, such as a medicine or therapy, that relieves pain, cures disease, or corrects a disorder.

name: renal plasma flow
definition: Volume of plasma passing through the kidneys in unit time.

name: repellent
definition: Substance used mainly to repel blood-sucking insects in order to protect humans and animals.

name: replicate sampling
definition: Act of taking multiple samples concurrently under comparable conditions.

name: reserve capacity
definition: Physiological or biochemical capacity that may be available to maintain homeostasis when the body or an organism is exposed to an environmental change.

name: reservoir
definition: Storage compartment from which a substance may be released with subsequent biological effects.

name: residual risk
definition: Health risk remaining after risk reduction actions are implemented.

name: residue
definition: Contaminant remaining in an organism or in other material such as food or packaging, following exposure.

name: resorptive effect
definition: Action of a substance after its reabsorption from the gut into the blood.

name: respirable dust
definition: Mass fraction of dust (particles) that penetrates to the unciliated airways of the lung (the alveolar region).

name: retrospective study
definition: Research design used to test etiological hypotheses in which inferences about exposure to the putative causal factor(s) are derived from data relating to characteristics of the persons or organisms under study or to events or experiences in their past.

name: returned effect of poisons
definition: Enhancement of the dose–effect relationship for a poison following repeated exposure to decreasing doses.

name: reverse mutation
definition: Mutation in a mutant allele which makes it capable of producing the nonmutant phenotype; this may result from restoration of the original DNA sequence of the gene or from production of a new DNA sequence which has the same effect.

name: reverse transcription
definition: Process by which an RNA molecule is used as a template to make a single-stranded DNA copy.

name: reversible alteration
definition: Change from normal structure or function, induced by a substance or other agent(s), that returns to normal status or within normal limits after cessation of exposure.

name: rhabdomyolysis
definition: Acute, fulminating, potentially lethal disease of skeletal muscle that causes disintegration of striated muscle fibers as evidenced by myoglobin in the blood and urine.

name: rhonchus
definition: Harsh crepitation in the throat, often resembling snoring.

name: risk associated with a lifetime exposure
definition: Probability of the occurrence of a specified undesirable event following exposure of an individual person from a given population to a specified substance at a defined level for the expected lifetime of the average member of that population.

name: risk aversion
definition: Tendency of an individual person to avoid risk.

name: risk communication
definition: Interpretation and communication of risk assessments in terms that are comprehensible to the general public or to others without specialist knowledge.

name: risk de minimis
definition: Risk that is negligible and too small to be of societal concern (usually assumed to be a probability below \(\pu{E-5}\) or \(\pu{E-6}\)).

name: risk evaluation
definition: Establishment of a qualitative or quantitative relationship between risks and benefits, involving the complex process of determining the significance of the identified hazards and estimated risks to those organisms or people concerned with or affected by them.

name: risk identification
definition: Recognition of a potential hazard and definition of the factors required to assess the probability of exposure of organisms or people to that hazard and of harm resulting from such exposure.

name: risk marker
definition: Attribute that is associated with an increased probability of occurrence of a disease or other specified outcome and that can be used as an indicator of this increased risk.

name: risk monitoring
definition: Process of following up the decisions and actions within risk management in order to check whether the aims of reduced exposure and risk are achieved.

name: risk perception
definition: Subjective perception of the gravity or importance of the risk based on a person’s knowledge of different risks and the moral, economic, and political judgment of their implications.

name: risk phrases
definition: Word groups identifying potential health or environmental hazards required under CPL Directives (European Community); may be incorporated into Safety Data Sheets.

name: risk-specific dose
definition: Amount of exposure corresponding to a specified level of risk.

name: rodenticide
definition: Substance intended to kill rodents.

name: route of exposure
definition: Means by which a toxic agent gains access to an organism by administration through the gastrointestinal tract (ingestion), lungs (inhalation), skin (topical), or by other routes such as intravenous, subcutaneous, intramuscular, or intraperitoneal routes.

name: S9 fraction
definition: Supernatant fraction obtained from an organ (usually liver) homogenate by centrifuging at \(\pu{9000 g}\) for \(\pu{20 min}\) in a suitable medium; this fraction contains cytosol and microsomes.

name: safety pharmacology
definition: Science directed to the discovery, development, and safe therapeutic use of biologically active substances as a result of the identification, monitoring, and characterization of potentially undesirable pharmacodynamic activities of these substances in nonclinical studies.

name: sarcoma
definition: Malignant tumor arising in a connective tissue and composed primarily of anaplastic cells resembling supportive tissue.

name: saturable elimination
definition: Elimination that becomes concentration-independent at a concentration at which the elimination process is functioning maximally.

name: saturnia
definition: Pain in a joint resulting from lead poisoning.

name: saturnism
definition: Intoxication caused by lead.

name: scotoma
definition: Area of diminished or lost vision within the visual field, surrounded by an area of less affected or normal vision.

name: secretion
definition: Process by which a substance such as a hormone or enzyme produced in a cell is passed through a plasma membrane to the outside, for example, the intestinal lumen or the blood (internal secretion).  Solid, liquid, or gaseous material passed from the inside of a cell through a plasma membrane to the outside as a result of cell activity.

name: self-cleaning of water
definition: Water purification by natural biological and physicochemical processes.

name: self-purification of the atmosphere
definition: Purification of the atmosphere from contaminants by natural biological and physicochemical processes.

name: semiochemical
definition: Substance produced by plants or animals, or a synthetic analogue thereof, that evokes a behavioral response in individuals of the producing species or other species (e.g., allomones, kairomones, pheromones, and synomones).

name: semipermeable membrane
definition: Membrane that will preferentially allow certain molecules or ions to pass through it while preventing the passage of others.

name: sensory effect level
definition: Intensity, where the detection threshold level is defined as the lower limit of the perceived intensity range (by convention, the lowest concentration that can be detected in \(\pu{50\%}\) of the cases in which it is present). Quality, where the recognition threshold level is defined as the lowest concentration at which the sensory effect can be recognized correctly in \(\pu{50\%}\) of the cases. Acceptability and annoyance, where the nuisance threshold level is defined as the concentration at which not more than a small proportion of the population, less than \(\pu{5\%}\), experiences annoyance for a small part of the time, less than \(\pu{2\%}\).Note: Since annoyance will be influenced by a number of factors, a nuisance threshold level cannot be set on the basis of concentration alone.

name: short-term exposure limit
definition: Fifteen-minute time-weighted average (TWA) exposure recommended by ACGIH which should not be exceeded at any time during a workday, even if the \(\pu{8 h}\) TWA is within the threshold limit value: time-weighted average, TLV-TWA.

name: side-effect
definition: Action of a drug other than that desired for beneficial pharmacological effect.

name: siderosis
definition: Pneumoconiosis resulting from the inhalation of iron dust. Excess of iron in the urine, blood, or tissues, characterized by hemosiderin granules in urine and iron deposits in tissues.

name: sidestream smoke
definition: Cloud of small particles and gases that is given off from the end of a burning tobacco product (cigarette, pipe, cigar) between puffs and is not directly inhaled by the smoker.

name: sign
definition: Objective evidence of a disease, deformity, or an effect induced by an agent, perceptible to an examining physician.

name: silicosis
definition: Pneumoconiosis resulting from inhalation of silica dust.

name: simulation test
definition: Procedure designed to predict the rate of biodegradation of a compound under relevant environmental conditions.

name: skeletal fluorosis
definition: Osteosclerosis due to fluoride.

name: slimicide
definition: Substance intended to kill slime-producing organisms.

name: slope factor
definition: Value, in inverse concentration or dose units, derived from the slope of a dose-response curve; in practice, limited to carcinogenic effects with the curve assumed to be linear at low concentrations or doses.

name: societal risk
definition: Total probability of harm to a human population including the probability of adverse effects to health of descendants and the probability of disruption resulting from loss of services such as industrial plant or loss of material goods and electricity.

name: soil partition coefficient
definition: Experimental ratio of a substance’s concentration in the soil to that in the aqueous (dissolved) soil phase at equilibrium: It is valid only for the specific concentration and solid/solution ratio of the test.

name: solvent abuse
definition: Deliberate inhalation (or drinking) of volatile solvents, in order to become intoxicated.

name: specific death rate
definition: Death rate computed for a subpopulation of individual organisms or people having a specified characteristic or attribute, and named accordingly.

name: specific pathogen free
definition: Describing an animal removed from its mother under sterile conditions just prior to term and subsequently reared and kept under sterile conditions.

name: spreader
definition: Agent used in some pesticide formulations to extend the even disposition of the active ingredient.

name: stability half life
definition: Time required for the amount of a substance in a formulation to decrease, for any reason, by one-half (\(\pu{50\%}\)).

name: standard morbidity ratio
definition: Ratio of the number of patients with a particular disease observed in a study group or population to the total number of people in the group or population multiplied by \(\pu{100}\).

name: standard mortality ratio
definition: Ratio of the number of deaths observed in the study group or population to the number of deaths that would be expected if the study population had the same specific rates as the standard population, multiplied by \(\pu{100}\).

name: stannosis
definition: Pneumoconiosis resulting from inhalation of tin dust.

name: subchronic
definition: Repeated over a short period, usually about \(\pu{10\%}\) of the life span; an imprecise term used to describe exposures of intermediate duration.

name: subchronic effect
definition: Biological change resulting from an environmental alteration lasting about \(\pu{10\%}\) of the lifetime of the test organism.

name: subchronic toxicity test
definition: Animal experiment serving to study the effects produced by the test substance when administered in repeated doses (or continually in food, drinking water, air) over a period of up to about 90 days.

name: subclinical effect
definition: Biological change with detectable symptoms following exposure to an agent known to cause disease either before symptoms of the disease occur or when they are absent.

name: subfertility
definition: Fertility below the normal range for a given species.

name: subjective environment
definition: Surrounding conditions as perceived by persons living in these conditions.

name: sufficient evidence
definition: According to the USEPA’s Guidelines for Carcinogen Risk Assessment, sufficient evidence is a collection of facts and scientific references that is definite enough to establish that an adverse effect is caused by the agent in question.

name: suggested no-adverse-response level
definition: Maximum dose or concentration that on current understanding is likely to be tolerated by an exposed organism without producing any harm.

name: suicide reaction
definition: Formation of irreversible cleavage complexes (also referred to as 'suicide complexes') leading to cell death.

name: summary sheet
definition: Two-to-four page summary of a risk assessment.

name: summation
definition: Process of addition of separate postsynaptic responses caused by stimuli that are adjacent in time and space.

name: Superfund
definition: Federal authority, established by the U.S. Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA) in 1980, to respond directly to releases or threatened releases (such as from landfills or waste disposal areas) of hazardous substances that may endanger health or welfare.

name: superoxide dismutase
definition: Enzymatic antioxidant that removes the potentially toxic superoxide ion (\(\ce{O2^{-}}\)) by disproportionating it to \(\ce{O2}\) and hydrogen peroxide (\(\ce{H2O2}\)).

name: surrogate
definition: Relatively well studied toxicant whose properties are assumed to apply to an entire chemically and toxicologically related class.

name: susceptible
definition: Describing a group of organisms more vulnerable to a given exposure than the majority of the population to which they belong.

name: sympatholytic
definition: adj., Blocking transmission of impulses from the adrenergic (sympathetic) postganglionic fibers to effector organs or tissues. n., Agent that blocks transmission of impulses from the adrenergic (sympathetic) postganglionic fibers to effector organs or tissues.

name: symptom
definition: Any subjective evidence of a disease or an effect induced by a substance as perceived by the affected subject.

name: symptomatology
definition: General description of all of the signs and symptoms of exposure to a toxicant.

name: synergist
definition: Substance that contributes more than additively to a mutual effect with another substance.

name: synomone
definition: Semiochemical that is produced by one organism inducing a response in an organism of another species that is favorable to both the emitter and the responding organism.

name: synteny
definition: Property of genes which reside on the same chromosome.

name: systematic sample
definition: Subset selected according to some simple rule such as specified date or alphabetic classification.

name: tachy-
definition: Prefix meaning rapid as in tachycardia and tachypnoea.

name: tachypnoea
definition: Abnormally fast breathing.

name: taeniacide
definition: Substance intended to kill tapeworms.

name: target population
definition: Collection of individuals, items, measurements, etc. about which inferences are required: The term is sometimes used to indicate the population from which a sample is drawn and sometimes to denote any reference population about which inferences are needed. Group of persons for whom an intervention is planned.

name: temporary acceptable daily intake
definition: Value for the acceptable daily intake (ADI) proposed for guidance when data are sufficient to conclude that use of the substance is safe over the relatively short period of time required to generate and evaluate further safety data, but are insufficient to conclude that use of the substance is safe over a lifetime.

name: temporary maximum residue limit
definition: Regulatory value established for a specified, limited time when only a temporary acceptable daily intake has been established for the pesticide concerned or, with the existence of an agreed acceptable daily intake, the available residue data are inadequate for firm maximum residue recommendations.

name: testing of chemicals
definition: In toxicology, evaluation of the therapeutic and potentially toxic effects of substances by their application through relevant routes of exposure with appropriate organisms or biological systems so as to relate effects to dose following application. In chemistry, qualitative or quantitative analysis by the application of one or more fixed methods and comparison of the results with established standards.

name: theoretical maximum daily intake
definition: Predicted maximum daily intake of a residue, assuming that it is present at the maximum residue level and that average daily consumption of foods per person is represented by assessed regional diets: It is expressed in milligrams of residue per person per day.

name: therapeutic cloning
definition: Generation and manipulation of stem cells with the objective of deriving cells of a particular organ or tissue to treat a disease.

name: threshold
definition: Dose or exposure concentration below which a defined effect will not occur.

name: threshold limit value–ceiling
definition: As defined by ACGIH, concentration of a potentially toxic substance that should not be exceeded during any part of the working exposure.

name: threshold limit value–short-term exposure limit
definition: As defined by ACGIH, concentration to which it is believed that workers can be exposed continuously for a short period of time without suffering from (1) irritation, (2) chronic or irreversible tissue damage, or (3) narcosis of sufficient degree to increase the likelihood of accidental injury, impair self-rescue or materially reduce work efficiency, and provided that the daily TLV-TWA is not exceeded.

name: threshold limit value–time-weighted average
definition: As defined by ACGIH, time-weighted average concentration for a conventional \(\pu{8\!\mbox{-}h}\) workday and a \(\pu{40\!\mbox{-}h}\) workweek, to which it is believed nearly all workers may be repeatedly exposed, day after day, without adverse effect.

name: threshold of toxicological concern
definition: Human exposure threshold value for a group of chemicals below which there should be no appreciable risk to human health.

name: thyrotoxicosis
definition: Condition resulting from excessive concentrations of thyroid hormones, as in hyperthyroidism, characterized by bulging eyes and rapid heart rate.

name: tidal volume
definition: Quantity of air or test gas that is inhaled and exhaled during one respiratory cycle.

name: time-weighted-average-exposure
definition: Concentration in the exposure medium at each measured time interval multiplied by that time interval and divided by the total time of observation.

name: tissue dose
definition: Amount of a substance or physical agent (radiation) absorbed by a tissue.

name: tolerable daily intake
definition: Estimate of the amount of a potentially harmful substance (e.g., contaminant) in food or drinking water that can be ingested daily over a lifetime without appreciable health risk.

name: tolerable risk
definition: Probability of suffering disease or injury that can, for the time being, be tolerated, taking into account the associated benefits, and assuming that the risk is minimized by appropriate control procedures.

name: tolerable weekly intake
definition: Estimate of the amount of a potentially harmful substance (e.g., a contaminant) in food or drinking water that can be ingested weekly over a lifetime without appreciable health risk.

name: tonic
definition: Characterized by tension, especially muscular tension. Medical preparation that increases or restores normal muscular tension.

name: topical
definition: Applied directly to the surface of the body.

name: torsade de pointes
definition: Potentially lethal form of ventricular tachycardia following chronic abuse of alcohol and mainly due to hypomagnesemia.

name: total diet study
definition: Study designed to establish the pattern of pesticide residue intake by a person consuming a defined diet. Study undertaken to show the range and amount of various foodstuffs in a typical diet or to estimate the total amount of a specific substance in a typical diet.

name: total terminal residue
definition: Summation of levels of all the residues of a defined pesticide in a food.

name: toxemia
definition: Condition in which the blood contains toxins produced by body cells at a local source of infection or derived from the growth of microorganisms. Pregnancy-related condition characterized by high blood pressure, swelling, and fluid retention, and proteins in the urine.

name: toxic dose
definition: Amount of a substance that produces intoxication without lethal outcome.

name: toxicity test
definition: Experimental study of the adverse effects of exposure of a living organism to a substance for a defined duration under defined conditions.

name: toxicogenomics
definition: Scientific subdiscipline that combines toxicology with genomics to determine how an organism’s genetic make-up influences its response to a toxic substance.

name: toxicological data sheet
definition: Document that gives in a uniform manner data relating to the toxicology of a substance, its production and application, properties and methods of identification.

name: toxicometry
definition: Term sometimes used to indicate a combination of investigative methods and techniques for making a quantitative assessment of toxicity and the hazards of potentially toxic substances.

name: toxicophobia
definition: Morbid dread of poisons.

name: toxicophoric group
definition: Structural moiety that upon metabolic activation exerts toxic effects: The presence of a toxicophoric group indicates only potential and not necessarily actual toxicity of a drug or other substances.

name: toxicovigilance
definition: Active process of identification, investigation, and evaluation of various toxic effects in the community with a view to taking measures to reduce or control exposure(s) involving the substance(s) which produces these effects.

name: toxification
definition: Metabolic conversion of a potentially toxic substance to a product that is more toxic.

name: tracer substance
definition: Substance that can be tracked through one or more reactions or systems, often by detecting an incorporated isotope.

name: transcriptome
definition: Total mRNA expressed in a cell or tissue at a given point in time.

name: transcriptomics
definition: Global analysis of gene expression to identify and evaluate changes in synthesis of mRNA after chemical exposure.

name: transformed cell
definition: Cell that has become genetically altered spontaneously or by incorporation of foreign DNA to produce a cell with an extended lifetime in culture.

name: transgene
definition: Gene from one source that has been incorporated into the genome of another organism.

name: treatability
definition: In relation to waste water, the amenability of substances to removal without adversely affecting the normal operation of biological treatment processes (such as a sewage treatment plant).

name: triage
definition: Process for sorting people into groups based on their need for or likely benefit from immediate medical treatment. Note: Triage is used in hospital emergency rooms, on battlefields, and at disaster sites when limited medical resources must be allocated. System used to allocate a scarce commodity, such as food, to those most likely to benefit from it. Process in which things are ranked in terms of importance or priority.

name: trueness
definition: Closeness of agreement between the average of a theoretically infinite number of replicate measured quantity values and a reference quantity value.

name: tubular reabsorption
definition: Transfer of solutes from the renal tubule lumen to the tubular epithelial cell and normally from there to the peritubular fluid.

name: tumorigenic
definition: Able to cause tumors.

name: tumor progression
definition: Sequence of changes by which a benign tumor develops from the initial lesion to a malignant stage.

name: tumor suppressor gene
definition: Gene that serves to protect cells from entering a cancerous state.

name: two-compartment model
definition: Product of compartmental analysis requiring two compartments.

name: ulcer
definition: Defect, often associated with inflammation, occurring locally or at the surface of an organ or tissue owing to sloughing of necrotic tissue.

name: uncertainty
definition: Parameter characterizing the dispersion of the quantity values being attributed to a measurand, based on the information used.

name: unit risk
definition: Upper-bound excess lifetime cancer risk estimated to result from continuous exposure to an agent at a concentration of \(\pu{1 \upmu g L-1}\) in water, or \(\pu{1 \upmu g m-3}\) in air.

name: upper boundary
definition: Estimate of the plausible upper limit to the true value of a quantity.

name: urticaria
definition: Vascular reaction of the skin marked by the transient appearance of smooth, slightly elevated patches (wheals, hives) that are redder or paler than the surrounding skin and often attended by severe itching.

name: vacuole
definition: Membrane-bound cavity within a cell.

name: validity of a measurement
definition: Expression of the degree to which a measurement measures what it purports to measure.

name: validity
definition: Degree to which the inferences drawn, especially generalizations extending beyond the study sample, are warranted when account is taken of the study methods, the representativeness of the study sample, and the nature of the population from which it is drawn.

name: vasodilation
definition: Increase in the caliber of the blood vessels, leading to an increased blood flow.

name: vehicle
definition: Substance(s) used to formulate active ingredients for administration or use.

name: ventilation
definition: Process of supplying a building or room with fresh air. Process of exchange of air between the ambient atmosphere and the lungs. In physiology, the amount of air inhaled per day. Oxygenation of blood.

name: ventricular fibrillation
definition: Irregular heartbeat characterized by uncoordinated contractions of the ventricle.

name: vermicide
definition: Substance intended to kill intestinal worms.

name: vesicant
definition: adj., Producing blisters on the skin. n., Substance that causes blisters on the skin.

name: virtually safe dose
definition: Human exposure over a lifetime to a carcinogen which has been estimated, using mathematical modeling, to result in a very low incidence of cancer, somewhere between zero and a specified incidence (e.g., 1 cancer in \(\pu{1000000}\) exposed people).

name: virucide
definition: Substance used to control viruses.

name: wasting syndrome
definition: Disease marked by weight loss and atrophy of muscular and other connective tissues that is not directly related to a decrease in food and water consumption.

name: water potential
definition: Difference in free energy or chemical potential (per unit molal volume) between pure water and water in cells and solutions.

name: weight-of-evidence for toxicity
definition: Extent to which the available biomedical data support the hypothesis that a substance causes a defined toxic effect such as cancer in humans.

name: working zone
definition: Space measuring up to \(\pu{2 m}\) over the level of the floor or platform that contains a worker’s permanent or temporary station.

name: x-disease
definition: Hyperkeratotic disease in cattle following exposure to chlorinated dibenzo-p-dioxins, naphthalenes, and related compounds.

name: zero-order kinetics
definition: Kinetics of a reaction in which the rate is independent of the concentration(s) of the reactants.

name: zoocide
definition: Substance intended to kill animals.

name: caged compound
definition: Molecular species that can rapidly be converted from inactive into active form by light. Typically, photocaged compounds have a covalently attached group that can be photocleaved by electromagnetic radiation of a specific wavelength.

name: charge-transfer absorption
definition: Electronic absorption corresponding to a charge-transfer transition.

name: cis/trans photoisomerisation
definition: Photoinduced geometric isomerization about a double bond.

name: external quantum efficiency
definition: Efficiency of light emission for solid-state light-emitting devices, such as organic light-emitting devices (OLEDs). Analogous to emission quantum yield.

name: Franck–Condon factor
definition: Squared modulus of the overlap integral between the vibrational wave functions (\(\mathit{\Theta}\)) for the initial (0) and final (\(\rm{e}\)) state of a given electronic transition. \[\left\vert \int \mathit{\Theta} _{\rm{v'}}^{(\rm{e})} \mathit{\Theta} _{\rm{v}}^{(0)} dQ \right\vert^{2}\] where the integration is over all nuclear coordinates.

name: Lippert–Mataga equation
definition: Correlation of the Stokes-shift, \(\Delta \tilde{ u}\), between the absorption and emission maxima, and the orientation polarizability \(f(\varepsilon_{\rm{r}},n)\) of the solvent,\[\Delta \tilde{ u} = 2 \frac{(\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\rm{exc}} - \boldsymbol{\mu}_{\rm{gr}})^{2}}{c h r^{3}} f(\varepsilon_{\rm{r}},n) + {\rm{const.}}\]with \(\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\rm{exc}}\) and \(\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\rm{gr}}\) the excited- and ground-state dipole moments of the dissolved molecule, respectively, \(c\) the speed of light, \(h\) the Planck constant, \(r\) the radius of the cavity in which the solute resides, and \(\varepsilon_{\rm{r}}\) the 'relative static permittivity' (formerly called dielectric constant). The expression of the Stokes shift depends only on the absolute magnitude of the difference between dipole moments and not on the angle between the dipoles. The above equation is sometimes called the Lippert equation. The orientation polarizability is given by\[f(\varepsilon_{\rm{r}},n) = \frac{(\varepsilon_{\rm{r}} - 1)}{(2\varepsilon_{\rm{r}} + 1)} - \frac{(n^{2} - 1)}{(2n^{2} + 1)}\]with \(\varepsilon_{\rm{r}}\) the relative static permittivity and \(n\) the refractive index of the solvent, \(f(\varepsilon_{\rm{r}},n)\) ranges from \(\pu{0.001}\) in cyclohexane to \(\pu{0.320}\) in water.

name: photocaged fluorescent molecules
definition: Caged fluorophores displaying a high fluorescent enhancement after photolysis.

name: photochemical aromatic substitution
definition: Photoinduced substitution in an aromatic compound.

name: aromatic substitution photochemical electrophile-olefin combination
definition: Photosubstitution in electron-rich aromatic compounds, upon reaction with electron-deficient olefins, occurring in polar solvents through an electron-transfer pathway.

name: photochemical nucleophile-olefin combination - aromatic substitution
definition: Photoinduced electron-transfer reaction of an aromatic electron-acceptor in the presence of an olefinic electron donor and a nucleophile, leading to aromatic substitution.

name: aromatic substitution photochemical radical-olefin combination
definition: Regioselective combination of a radical, an olefin, and an arene via a photoinduced electron-transfer pathway.

name: photochirogenesis
definition: Photochemical induction of molecular chirality.

name: photoenolisation
definition: A special case of phototautomerization.

name: photorefractive effect
definition: Photoinduced change in refractive index.

name: photoremovable protecting group
definition: Release of a reactive species by photolysis of a molecular entity. The release may be induced by direct excitation, by triplet sensitization, or by photoinduced electron transfer.

name: photostimulated unimolecular radical nucleophilic substitution
definition: Nucleophilic substitution in a substrate through processes that involve electron transfer steps. The reaction occurs through chain steps. The most extensively used method of initiation is photoinitiation.

name: photosubstitution
definition: Photochemical process leading to a substitution reaction.

name: phototautomerisation
definition: Photoisomerization of the general form \[\ce{G-X-Y=Z [h u] X=Y-Z-G}\]

name: polar driving force
definition: The negative of the standard Gibbs energy change (i.e., \(-\Delta G^{\circ}\)) for outer-sphere electron transfer in polar solvents, where the electrostatic work terms in the expression used for the calculation of the Gibbs energy of photoinduced electron transfer are in general negligibly small.

name: polarisation spectroscopy
definition: In absorption experiments, polarization spectroscopy is performed with polarized light on anisotropic samples.

name: spectral fluence
definition: Derivative of fluence, \(H_{\rm{o}}\), with respect to wavelength, _010366_.

name: genetic epidemiology
definition: Study of the correlations between phenotypic trends and genetic variation across population groups and the application of the results of such a study to control of health problems.

name: risk ratio
definition: Value obtained by dividing the probability of occurrence of a specific effect in one group by the probability of occurrence of the same effect in another group, or the value obtained by dividing the probability of occurrence of one potentially hazardous event by the probability of occurrence of another.

name: toxicity exposure ratio
definition: Ratio of the measure of the effects (e.g., \(\pu{LD_{50}}\), \(\pu{LC_{50}}\), NOEC) to the estimated exposure.

name: bowtie entanglement
definition: Chain entanglement with topology similar to that of a bowtie.

name: acute effect
definition: Effect of finite duration occurring rapidly (usually in the first \(\pu{24 h}\) or up to \(\pu{14 d}\)) following a single dose or short exposure to a substance or radiation.

name: acute exposure
definition: Exposure of short duration.

name: chronic
definition: Long-term (in relation to exposure or effect).

name: chronic exposure
definition: Continued exposures occurring over an extended period of time, or a significant fraction of the test species’ or of the group of individuals’, or of the population’s lifetime.

name: benchmark concentration
definition: Statistical lower CL on the concentration that produces a defined response (called the benchmark response or BMR, usually \(\pu{5\%}\) or \(\pu{100\%}\)) for an adverse effect compared to background, defined as \(\pu{0\%}\).Dose–response curve showing BMC and BMCL (BMC 10 % lower CL).

name: physiologically based pharmacokinetic modeling
definition: Mathematical modeling of kinetic behavior of a substance, based on measured physiological parameters.

name: deterministic effect
definition: Phenomenon committed to a particular outcome determined by fundamental physical principles.

name: stochastic
definition: Pertaining to or arising from chance and hence obeying the laws of probability.

name: effect
definition: Change in biochemistry, morphology, physiology, growth, development, or lifespan of an organism which results in impairment of functional capacity or impairment of capacity to compensate for additional stress or increase in susceptibility to other environmental influences.

name: elimination rate
definition: Derivative with respect to time of the concentration or amount of a substance in the body, or a part thereof, resulting from elimination.

name: local effect
definition: Change occurring at the site of contact between an organism and a toxicant.

name: toxicant
definition: This is the preferred term for a substance that is considered to be toxic under circumstances which are thought likely to happen.

name: medicine
definition: Any drug or remedy.

name: suspension of solid charged particles
definition: Dispersion of solid electrically charged particles, commonly larger in size range than colloidal particles (of approximate diameter range \(\pu{{1}{-}{1000} nm}\)) (dispersed phase), in water or an aqueous solution (continuous, liquid phase).

name: suspension potentiometric cell
definition: Galvanic cell containing, as its essential component, a uniform or combined suspension or one of its separated parts alone, the eqs or sediment.

name: anomalous liquid junction potential
definition: Electrochemical potential that arises at the reference electrode–measurement solution interface when, during a potentiometric measurement, the filling solution of the salt bridge of the reference electrode contacts the charged particles of a suspension.

name: pIon
definition: General mathematical expression form of any ion X activity: \[\rm{p(ion\ X)} = {\rm{pX}} = -\lg {\rm{a_{X}}} = -\lg ({\rm{m_{X}} \gamma_{X}/m^{\circ}})\], analogously to \[\pu{pH} = -\lg {\rm{a_{H}}} = -\lg ({\rm{m_{H}} \gamma_{H}/m^{\circ}})\].

name: suspension pH
definition: Readings on a pH-meter scale obtained for a suspension of soil (in water or electrolyte) by any method for potentiometric pH measurement, performed in a manner analogous to the pH measurement in solutions.

name: bridgehead atom
definition: Atom that is part of two or more rings in a polycyclic molecule and that is separated from another bridgehead atom by bridges all of which contain at least one other atom.

name: unimolecular
definition: Feature of a reaction in which only one molecular entity is involved.

name: initialisation
definition: Process for converting a starting initiator or chain transfer agent into a macro-initiator or macro-chain-transfer agent during reversible-deactivation polymerization (RDP).

name: conjugate
definition: Molecule or compound designed to support, transport, and/or deliver one or several active species in order to take advantage of their specificity.

name: scattering coefficient
definition: Negative Napierian logarithm of the ratio of the intensity of radiation scattered (\(I_{\rm{s}}\)) by a non-absorbing sample to the incident intensity (\(I_{0}\)), divided by the path-length, \(l\). \[s = -\ln(I_{s}/I_{0})/l\]

name: numerical aperture
definition: For an optical fibre, \(n_{\rm{o}}\) sin \(\theta_{\alpha}\), where \(n_{\rm{o}}\) is the refractive index of the exterior medium and \(\theta_{\alpha}\) is the maximum input half angle that can support propagation.

name: molar activity (material)
definition: Activity of a specified radionuclide (\(\ce{R}\)) in a material (\(\ce{M}\)) divided by amount of substance of that material.

name: Nernstian response
definition: Response of an ion-selective electrode according to a local thermodynamic equilibrium, over a given range of activity (or concentration) that follows the Nernst equation.

name: pre-column derivatisation
definition: Technique in chromatography in which the sample is chemically derivatized before entering the column.

name: phase volume ratio
definition: Volume of the mobile phase divided by volume of the stationary phase in a column in counter-current chromatography.

name: total mobile-phase volume in column
definition: Sum of the interparticle volume of the column and intraparticle volume of the column: \(V_{\rm{t}} = V_{0} + V_{\rm{i}}\)

name: retention time
definition: Retention time of a sample component, the molecules of which are smaller than the largest pores of the particles of the stationary phase but larger than the smallest pores.

name: total mobile phase time
definition: Retention time of a sample component the molecules of which are smaller than the smallest pores of the particles of the stationary phase.

name: alveolar period
definition: Phase in lung development beginning in utero (about \(\pu{32}\) to \(\pu{36}\) weeks in the human fetus) and lasting until about eight years of age.

name: osteoblast
definition: Fibroblast-derived bone-forming cell that produces a collagen type-I-rich matrix; this matrix calcifies to become bone.

name: umbilicus
definition: Feature marking the point in the abdominal wall where the umbilical cord entered the fetus.

name: dyspnea
definition: Difficulty in breathing; shortness of breath.

name: neuropeptide
definition: One of a group of small proteins (peptides) that serve as neurotransmitters in the brain, autonomic nervous system and neuroendocrine system.

name: neurotoxic esterase assay
definition: Test in which delayed neuropathy resulting from hydrolytic cleavage of organophosphate esters is studied with measurement of the responsible enzyme activity,

name: photo-induced toxicity
definition: Toxicity of a chemical in the presence of light due to the production of toxic photolysis products.

name: component
definition: Constituent whose amount or concentration can be varied independently in a mixture.

name: constituent
definition: Chemical species present in a system.

name: mixture
definition: Gaseous, liquid, or solid phase containing more than one substance, when all the substances are treated in the same way.

name: α-addition
definition: A chemical reaction resulting in a single reaction product from two or three reacting chemical species, with formation of two new chemical bonds to the same atom in one of the reactant molecular entities. The synonymous term 1/1/addition is also used. For example:  (This particular example can also be viewed as an insertion reaction.). In inorganic chemistry such $\ce{\upalpha\!\mbox{-}addition}$ reactions, generally to a metallic central atom, are known as 'oxidative additions'. $\ce{\upalpha\!\mbox{-}Addition}$ is the reverse of α-elimination or 1/1/elimination.

name: α, β
definition: Stereodescriptors, used in a number of different ways.Relative stereodescriptors used in carbohydrate nomenclature to describe the configuration at the anomeric carbon by relating it to the anomeric reference atom. For simple cases the anomeric reference atom is the same as the configurational reference atom. Thus in $\ce{\upalpha\!{-ᴅ-glucopyranose}}$ the reference atom is $\ce{C-5}$ and the $\ce{OH}$ at $\ce{C-1}$ is on the same side as the $\ce{OH}$ at $\ce{C-5}$ in the Fischer projection.Relative stereodescriptors used by Chemical Abstracts Service to describe the configuration of a cyclic molecule (including suitable polycyclic systems) with several stereogenic centres whereby the $\ce{\upalpha\!}$ side of the reference plane is the side on which the substituent with CIP priority lies at the lowest numbered stereogenic centre. The other side is $\ce{\upbeta\!}$. Absolute stereodescriptors originally devised for steroid nomenclature. However in this sense it is only meaningful if there is an agreed absolute configuration and orientation of the structure so as to define the plane and which way up the molecule is represented. Substituents above the plane of the steroid are described as $\ce{\upbeta\!}$ and are shown as a solid line ( or ); those below the plane are described as $\ce{\upalpha\!}$ and are shown by a broken line ( or ). The extension of this system to tetrapyrroles has been documented and it has been widely used elsewhere.

name: α-cleavage
definition: The fission of a bond originating at an atom which is adjacent to one assumed to bear the charge; the definition of $\ce{\upbeta\!\mbox{-}}$, $\ce{\upgamma\!\mbox{-}}$ cleavage then follows automatically. The process:  would thus be described as $\ce{\upalpha\!\mbox{-}fission}$ of a ketone with expulsion of a radical $\ce{R^{1.}}$ The carbon atoms of the radical $\ce{R^{1.}}$ are called the $\ce{\upalpha\!\mbox{-}}$, $\ce{\upbeta\!\mbox{-}}$, $\ce{\upgamma\!\mbox{-}carbons}$, starting with the atom nearest the functional group.

name: α-decay
definition: Radioactive decay in which an alpha particle is emitted.

name: α-effect
definition: A positive deviation of an $\ce{\upalpha\!\mbox{-}nucleophile}$ (a nucleophile bearing an unshared pair of electrons on an atom adjacent to the nucleophilic site) from a Brønsted-type plot of \(\log k_{\rm{nuc}}\) vs. \({\rm{p}}K_{\rm{a}}\) constructed for a series of related normal nucleophiles. More generally, it is the influence of the atom bearing a lone pair of electrons on the reactivity at the adjacent site.

name: α-elimination
definition: A transformation of the general type:  where the central atom Z is commonly carbon. The reverse reaction is called α-addition.

name: α-oxo carbenes
definition: Synonymous with acyl carbenes.

name: 'A' value
definition: The conformational preference of an equatorial compared to an axial substituent in a monosubstituted cyclohexane. This steric substituent parameter equals \(\Delta _{\rm{r}}G^{\,\unicode{x26ac}}\) in \(\pu{kcal mol-1}\) for the equatorial to axial equilibration on cyclohexane. The values are also known as 'Winstein–Holness' A values.

name: abatement
definition: Action taken to reduce air pollution which involves the use of control equipment or some new process. This refers to a reduction or lessening as opposed to elimination of a type of discharge or pollutant.

name: abeo-
definition: Bond migration, i.e. the formal transfer of one end of a skeletal bond to another position, with a compensating transfer of a hydrogen atom, can be indicated by a prefix of the form '\(x(y\rightarrow z)abeo-\)'. The prefix is compiled as follows: a numeral denoting the stationary (unchanged) end of the migrating bond (x) is followed by parentheses enclosing the locant denoting the original position (y) from which the other end of this bond has migrated, an arrow, and the locant (z) denoting the new position to which the bond has moved. The closing parenthesis is followed by the italicized prefix abeo- (Latin: I go away) to indicate bond migration. The original numbering is retained for the new compound and is used for the numbers x, y and z. It is always necessary to specify the resulting stereochemistry.

name: abiotic
definition: Not associated with living organisms. Synonymous with abiological.

name: abiotic transformation
definition: Process in which a substance in the environment is modified by non-biological mechanisms.

name: absolute activation analysis
definition: A kind of activation analysis in which the elemental concentrations in the material are calculated from known nuclear constants, irradiation and measurement parameters, rather than by comparing with known standards.

name: absolute configuration
definition: The spatial arrangement of the atoms of a chiral molecular entity (or group) and its stereochemical description, e.g., R or S.

name: absolute counting
definition: A measurement under such well-defined conditions that the activity of a sample can be derived directly from the observed counting rate.

name: absolute electrode potential
definition: The electrode potential of a metal measured with respect to a universal reference system (not including any additional metal/solution interface).

name: absolute full energy peak efficiency
definition: Of a radiation spectrometer, the counting efficiency when considering only the events recorded in the full energy peak.

name: absolute lethal concentration
